body.text: mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāraḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> (Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras)

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: prathamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: First chapter (<s>adhikāra</s>)

children.translated_text: The knower of meaning elaborates the meaning through speech and pure words,
out of compassion, being immersed therein, for the suffering people, for the crossing beyond suffering;
showing to beings who are proceeding toward it, with respect to the <s>Dharma</s> taught through the supreme vehicle,
a coherent understanding of meaning, unsurpassed in its scope, having a fivefold nature. || <s>Msa</s> 1.1 ||

body.text: arthajño 'rthavibhāvanāṃ prakurute.........[ityādi] koṣadeśamārabhya ko 'laṃkaroti | arthajñaḥ | kamalaṃkāramalaṃkaroti arthavibhāvanāṃ kurute | kena vācā padaiścāmalaiḥ | amalayā vācetiṣa........[pauryādinā] amalaiḥ padairiti yuktaiḥ sahitairiti vistaraḥ | na hi vinā vācā padavyañjanairartho vibhāvayituṃ śakyata iti | kasmai duḥkhasyottaraṇāya duḥkhitajane kāruṇyatastanmayaḥ | duḥkhitajane yatkāruṇyaṃ tasmātkāruṇyatastanmaya iti kāruṇyamayaḥ | kasyālaṃkāraṃ karoti | dharmasyottamayānadeśitavidheḥ | uttamayānasya deśito vidhiryasmindharme tasya dharmasya | kasminnalaṃkaroti | sattveṣu tadgāmiṣu | nimittasaptamyeṣā.........[mahāyāna]gāmisattvanimittamityarthaḥ | katividhamalaṃkāraṃ karoti | pañcavidham | śliṣṭāmarthagatiṃ niruttaragatāṃ pañcātmikāṃ darśayan | śliṣṭāmiti yuktām | niruttaragatāmityanuttarajñāna[yāna]gatām |
body.translated_text: 'The knower of meaning elaborates the meaning'......... [thus beginning]: starting from the treasury of teaching, who ornaments? The knower of meaning. What ornament does he make? He elaborates the meaning. By what means? Through speech and pure words. 'Pure speech' means......... [through eloquence and such qualities]; 'pure words' means well-arranged, coherent — this is the elaboration. For without speech, that is, without words and syllables, the meaning cannot be elaborated. For whom? 'For the crossing beyond suffering, for the suffering people, out of compassion, being immersed therein.' The compassion that arises toward suffering people — from that compassion, 'immersed therein' means pervaded by compassion. What does he ornament? 'The <s>Dharma</s> taught through the supreme vehicle.' The method taught by the supreme vehicle — that <s>Dharma</s> in which this method is taught. Where does he ornament? 'In beings who are proceeding toward it.' This is a locative of cause......... meaning 'on account of beings proceeding toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.' How many kinds of ornament does he make? Fivefold. 'Showing a coherent understanding of meaning, unsurpassed in its scope, having a fivefold nature.' 'Coherent' means well-connected. 'Unsurpassed in its scope' means pertaining to the unsurpassed knowledge [and vehicle].

body.text: tāmidānīṃ pañcātmikāmarthagatiṃ dvitīyena ślokena darśayati |
body.translated_text: Now he shows that fivefold understanding of meaning by the second verse:

body.text:
ghaṭitamiva suvarṇaṃ vārijaṃ vā vibuddhaṃ
sukṛtamiva subhojyaṃ bhujyamānaṃ kṣudhārtaiḥ |

children.translated_text: like a well-written letter that is understood, like a jewel freed from its casket —

children.text: vivṛta iha sa dharmaḥ prītimagryāṃ dadhāti || Msa_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Dharma</s>, being disclosed here, bestows the highest joy. || <s>Msa</s> 1.2 ||

body.translated_text:
Like gold that has been wrought, or a lotus that has blossomed,
like well-prepared delicious food being eaten by the hungry,

body.text: anena ślokena pañcabhirdṛṣṭāntaiḥ sa hi dharmaḥ pañcavidhamarthamadhikṛtya deśitaḥ sādhyaṃ vyutpādyaṃ cintyamacintyaṃ pariniṣpannaṃ cādhigamārthaṃ pratyātmavedanīyaṃ bodhipakṣasvabhāvam | so 'nena sūtrālaṃkāreṇa vivṛtaḥ prītimagryāṃ dadhāti | yathākramaṃ ghaṭitasuvarṇādivat |
body.translated_text: By this verse, through five similes, that <s>Dharma</s> has been taught with reference to fivefold meaning: that which is to be accomplished, that which is to be learned, that which is to be contemplated, the inconceivable, and the perfectly established — namely, the meaning of realization, that which is to be personally experienced, whose nature is the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>). That <s>Dharma</s>, disclosed by this <s>Sūtrālaṃkāra</s>, bestows the highest joy — respectively, like wrought gold and so forth.

body.text: yadā sa dharmaḥ prakṛtyaiva guṇayuktaḥ kathaṃ so 'laṃkriyata ityasya codyasya parihārārthaṃ tṛtīyaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: When that <s>Dharma</s> is by its very nature endowed with excellent qualities, how can it be ornamented? To address this objection, the third verse:

children.translated_text: Just as a reflection in a mirror, possessing by nature the qualities of adornment,
produces a distinguished delight in people by the power of being seen,
so too the <s>Dharma</s>, though always endowed by nature with the qualities of being well-spoken,
when its meaning is distinguished, produces a special satisfaction in the wise. || <s>Msa</s> 1.3 ||

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati | yathā bimbaṃ bhūṣayā prakṛtyaiva guṇavat ādarśagataṃ darśanavaśādviśiṣṭaṃ prāmodyaṃ janayatyevaṃ sa dharmaḥ subhāṣitaiḥ prakṛtyaiva guṇayukto 'pi satataṃ vibhaktārthastuṣṭiṃ viśiṣṭāṃ janayati | buddhimatāmatastuṣṭiviśeṣotpādanādalaṃkṛta iva bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: What does he show by this? Just as a reflection, possessing by its very nature the qualities of adornment, when placed in a mirror produces a distinguished delight through the power of being seen, so too that <s>Dharma</s>, though always endowed by its very nature with the qualities of being well-spoken, when its meaning is distinguished, produces a special satisfaction — in the wise. Because it produces a special satisfaction in the intelligent, it becomes as if ornamented.

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ tribhiḥ ślokaistasmindharme trividhamanuśaṃsaṃ darśayatyādarotpādanārtham |
body.translated_text: Hereafter, by three verses, he shows three kinds of benefit in that <s>Dharma</s>, for the purpose of generating esteem:

children.translated_text: Just as medicine, pungent when smelled but sweet in taste, so likewise

children.text: dharma[rmo] dvayavyavasthā[stho] vyañjanato 'rtho na ca[rthataśca]jñeyaḥ || Msa_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>, established in both [aspects]: it should be known by its letter and by its meaning [and from its meaning]. || <s>Msa</s> 1.4 ||
Like a king who is difficult to approach, this <s>Dharma</s> is vast, profound, and deep;
but when propitiated, like that [king], it becomes a bestower of the wealth of excellent qualities. || <s>Msa</s> 1.5 ||
Just as a gem of fine quality, though priceless [variant: worthless to], does not please one who is not an appraiser,
so this <s>Dharma</s> does not [please] the unintelligent, but conversely it pleases [the wise] — in the same way. || <s>Msa</s> 1.6 ||

body.text: trividho 'nuśaṃsaḥ | āvaraṇaprahāṇahetutvamauṣadhopamatvena | dvayavyavastha iti vyañjanārthavyavasthaḥ | vibhutvahetutvamabhijñādivaiśeṣikaguṇairśvaryadānādrājopamatvena | āryadha[ja]nopabhogahetutvaṃ ca anartha[rgha]jātyaratnopamatvena | parīkṣakajana āryajano veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The benefit is threefold: being a cause for the removal of obscurations, illustrated by the simile of medicine. 'Established in both' means established in letter and meaning. Being a cause of sovereignty, through special qualities such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges) and other distinguished qualities, illustrated by the simile of a king through the bestowal of lordship. And being a cause for the enjoyment of noble wealth, illustrated by the simile of a priceless [variant: precious] gem of fine quality. 'The appraiser' should be understood as the noble person (<s>ārya</s>).

body.text: naivedaṃ mahāyānaṃ buddhavacanaṃ kutastasyāyamanuśaṃso bhaviṣyatītyatra vipratipannāstasya buddhavacanatvaprasādhanārthaṃ kāraṇavibhājyamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'This <s>Mahāyāna</s> is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s> — whence could this benefit arise from it?' — for those who are thus confused, in order to establish its nature as the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, beginning with a division of reasons, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because of the absence of a prior declaration, because of simultaneous emergence, because it is beyond the range [of ordinary cognition], because of its being established,
because of the absurdity [that would follow] from the presence or absence [of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>], because of being an antidote, and because of a different purport. || <s>Msa</s> 1.7 ||

body.text: ādāvavyākaraṇāt yadyetatsaddharmāntarāyipaścātkenāpyutpāditam | kasmādādau bhagavatā na vyākṛtamanāgatabhaya[bhaṃga]vat | samapravṛtteḥ samakālaṃ ca śrāvakayānena mahāyānasya pravṛttirupalabhyate na paścāditi kathamasyābuddhavacanatvaṃ vijñāyate | agocarānnāyamevamudāro gambhīraśca dharmastārkikāṇāṃ gocaraḥ | tīrthikaśāstreṣu tatprakārānupalambhāditi | nāyamanyairbhāṣito yujyate | ucyamāne 'pi tadanadhimukteḥ | siddherathānyenābhisaṃbudhya bhāṣitaḥ | siddhamasya buddhavacanatvam | sa eva buddho yo 'bhisaṃbudhya evaṃ bhāṣate | bhāvābhāve 'bhāvādyadi mahāyānaṃ kiṃcidasti tasya bhāva[ve] siddhamidaṃ buddhavacanamato 'nyasya mahāyānasyābhāvāt | atha nāsti tasyābhāve śrāvakayānasyāpyabhāvāt | śrāvakayānaṃ buddhavacanaṃ na mahāyānamiti na yujyate vinā buddhayānena buddhānāmanutpādāt | pratipakṣatvāt | bhāvyamānaṃ ca mahāyānaṃ sarvanirvikalpajñānāśrayatvena kleśānāṃ pratipakṣo bhavati tasmād buddhavacanam | rutānyatvāt | na cāsya yathārutamarthastasmānna yathārutārthānusāreṇedamabuddhavacanaṃ veditabyam |
body.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of a prior declaration': if this [<s>Mahāyāna</s>] were an obstacle to the true <s>Dharma</s>, produced later by someone, why was it not declared beforehand by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, as [he declared] a future danger [variant: breach]? 'Because of simultaneous emergence': the emergence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is observed to be simultaneous with the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, not later — so how can its nature as non-<s>buddhavacana</s> be ascertained? 'Because it is beyond the range': this <s>Dharma</s>, so lofty and profound, is not within the range of logicians, since such a type [of teaching] is not found in the treatises of the <s>tīrthikas</s> — so it is not appropriate that this was spoken by others; even if it were spoken [by them], there would be no conviction in it. 'Because of its being established': or else, if it was spoken by another who had attained full awakening, then its nature as <s>buddhavacana</s> is established, for he alone is a <s>Buddha</s> who, having attained full awakening, speaks thus. 'Because of the absurdity from the presence or absence': if the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is something that exists, then its existence [establishes that] this is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, since there is no other <s>Mahāyāna</s>. But if it does not exist, then in its absence, the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> too would be absent. 'The <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is <s>buddhavacana</s> but not the <s>Mahāyāna</s>' — this is not tenable, because without the <s>Buddhayāna</s>, <s>Buddhas</s> would not arise. 'Because of being an antidote': when cultivated, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, by being the basis of all <s>nirvikalpajñāna</s> (non-conceptual knowledge), becomes an antidote to the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — therefore it is <s>buddhavacana</s>. 'Because of a different purport': its meaning is not to be taken literally, therefore it should not be understood as non-<s>buddhavacana</s> by following the literal meaning.

body.text: yaduktamādāvavyākaraṇādityanābhogādetadanāgatāṃ bhagavatā na vyākṛtamiti kasyacit syādata upekṣāyā ayoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: It was said 'because of the absence of a prior declaration' — 'this was not declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as a future [danger] because of inattention' — someone might think thus; therefore, regarding the inappropriateness of indifference, a verse:

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> have direct vision, and are protectors of the teaching;
their knowledge is unobstructed at all times — indifference is not appropriate for them. || <s>Msa</s> 1.8 ||

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati | tribhiḥ kāraṇairanāgatasya mahataḥ śāsanopadravasyopekṣā na yujyate | buddhānāmayatnato jñānapravṛtteḥ pratyakṣacakṣuṣkatayā śāsanarakṣāyāśca[yāṃ ca] yatnavatvāt | anāgatajñānasamarthyācca sarvakālāvyāhatajñānatayeti |
body.translated_text: What does he show by this? By three reasons, indifference toward a great future danger to the teaching is not appropriate: because the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> operates effortlessly, due to their having direct vision; because they are diligent in protecting the teaching; and because of the capacity of their knowledge of the future, their knowledge being unimpeded at all times.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhāvābhāve 'bhāvāditi | etadeva śrāvakayānaṃ mahāyānametenaiva mahābodhiprāptiriti kasyacitsyādataḥ śrāvakayānasya mahāyānatvāyoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: It was said 'because of the absurdity from the presence or absence' — 'this <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> itself is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and <s>Mahābodhi</s> is attained through it alone' — someone might think thus; therefore, regarding the inappropriateness of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> being the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because of incompleteness, because of contradiction, because of being no means, and even so because of the absence of instruction —
this <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> cannot be called the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. || <s>Msa</s> 1.9 ||

body.text: vaikalyātparārthopadeśasya | na hi śrāvakayāne kaścitparārtha upadiṣṭaḥ śrāvakāṇāmātmano nirvidvirāgavimuktimātropāyopadeśāt | na ca svārtha eva pareṣūpadiśyamānaḥ parārtho bhavitumarhati | virodhāt | svārthe hi paro niyujyamānaḥ svārtha eva prayujyate sa ātmana eva parinirvāṇārthaprayukto 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyata iti viruddhametat | na ca śrāvakayānenaiva cirakālaṃ bodhau ghaṭamāno buddho bhavitumarhati | anupāyatvāt | anupāyo hi śrāvakayānaṃ buddhatvasya na cānupāyena ciramapi prayujyamānaḥ prārthitamarthaṃ prāpnoti | śrṛṅgādiva dugdhaṃ na bhasrayā[bhasrāyāḥ] | athānyathāpyatropadiṣṭaṃ yathā bodhisattvena prayoktavyam | tathāpyanupadeśānna śrāvakayānameva mahāyānaṃ bhaviturmahati | na hi sa tādṛśa upadeśa etasminnupalabhyate |
body.translated_text: 'Because of incompleteness' — of instruction for the benefit of others. For in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, no benefit for others is taught, since for <s>Śrāvakas</s>, only the means to their own <s>nirvid</s> (disenchantment), <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), and <s>vimukti</s> (liberation) are instructed. And what is taught for oneself alone, when taught to others, cannot become benefit for others. 'Because of contradiction': for another who is directed to one's own goal engages only in one's own goal — that 'one who is engaged in the goal of one's own <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)' — this is contradictory. And through the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone, one striving for awakening for a long time cannot become a <s>Buddha</s>. 'Because of being no means': for the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is not a means to <s>Buddhahood</s>, and without a [proper] means, even one striving for a long time does not attain the desired goal — like [trying to get] milk from a horn, not from a bellows. But if something else is also taught here as to how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should practice — even so, 'because of the absence of instruction,' the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone cannot be the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For no such instruction is found in it.

body.text: viruddhameva cānyonyaṃ śrāvakayānaṃ mahāyānaṃ cetyanyonyavirodhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> are indeed mutually contradictory — regarding this mutual contradiction, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because of contradiction in disposition, instruction, practice,

children.text: upastambhasya kālasya yat hīnaṃ hīnameva tat || Msa_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: support, and time — what is inferior is indeed inferior. || <s>Msa</s> 1.10 ||

body.text: kathaṃ viruddham | pañcabhirvirodhaiḥ | āśayopadeśaprayogopastambhakālavirodhaiḥ | śrāvakayāne hyātmaparinirvāṇāyaivāśayastadarthamevopadeśastadarthameva prayogaḥ parīttaśca puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasaṃgṛhīta upastambhaḥ, kālena cālpena tadarthaprāptiryāvattribhirapi janmabhiḥ | mahāyāne tu sarvaṃ viparyayeṇa | tasmādanyonyavirodhād yad yānaṃ hīnaṃ hīnameva tat | na tanmahāyānaṃ bhavitumarhati |
body.translated_text: How are they contradictory? Through five contradictions: contradictions of disposition, instruction, practice, support, and time. For in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, the disposition is only for one's own <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, the instruction is only for that purpose, the practice is only for that purpose, the support — the accumulation of merit and knowledge — is limited, and the attainment of that goal is in a short time, even in as few as three lifetimes. But in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, everything is the reverse. Therefore, due to mutual contradiction, whichever vehicle is inferior is indeed inferior — it cannot become the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: buddhavacanasyedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yatsūtre 'vatarati vinaye saṃdṛśyate dharmatāṃ ca na vilomayati | na caivaṃ mahāyānam, sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvopadeśāt | tasmānna buddhavacanamiti kasyacitsyādato lakṣaṇāvirodhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'This is the mark of <s>buddhavacana</s>: that which accords with the <s>Sūtras</s>, is seen in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and does not contradict <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality). But the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is not like this, because it teaches the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore it is not <s>buddhavacana</s>' — someone might think thus; therefore, regarding the non-contradiction with the marks, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because it accords with its own [sūtras], because it is seen in its own <s>Vinaya</s>,
and because of its grandeur and profundity — it is not at all contradictory to <s>dharmatā</s>. || <s>Msa</s> 1.11 ||

body.text: anena ślokena kiṃ darśayati | avataratyevedaṃ svasmin mahāyānasūtre svasya ca kleśasya[kleśaḥ?] vinayaḥ[vinaye]saṃdṛśyate | yo mahāyāne bodhisattvānāṃ kleśaḥ uktaḥ | vikalpakleśā hi bodhisattvāḥ | audāryagāmbhīryalakṣaṇatvācca | na dharmatāṃ vilomayatyathaiva hi dharmatā mahābodhiprāptaye tasmānnāsti lakṣaṇavirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: What does he show by this verse? This indeed accords with its own <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras, and the <s>Vinaya</s> — that is, the discipline of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — is seen in its own [texts]. That which is stated as the affliction of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>: for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have conceptual afflictions (<s>vikalpakleśa</s>). And because its character is grandeur and profundity, it does not contradict <s>dharmatā</s>; for <s>dharmatā</s> is indeed such — for the attainment of <s>Mahābodhi</s>. Therefore there is no contradiction with the marks.

body.text: agocarādityuktamatarstakagocaratvāyoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: It was said 'because it is beyond the range [of reasoning]' — regarding the inappropriateness of it being within the range of logicians, a verse:

children.translated_text: Dependent [on scripture], unstable, non-comprehensive, conventional, and subject to exhaustion —

children.text: bālāśrayo matastarkastasyāto viṣayo na tat || Msa_1.12 ||
children.translated_text: reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) is considered to be the resort of the immature; therefore, this [<s>Dharma</s>] is not its domain. || <s>Msa</s> 1.12 ||

body.text: adṛṣṭasatyāśrayo hi tarkaḥ kaścidāgamaniśrito bhavati | aniyataśca bhavati kālāntareṇānyathāpratyavagamāt | avyāpī ca na sarvajñeyaviṣayaḥ | saṃvṛtisatyaviṣayaśca na paramārthaviṣayaḥ | khedavāṃśca pratibhānaparyādānāt | mahāyānaṃ tu na niśritaṃ yāvadakhedavat | śatasāhasrikādyanekasūtropadeśāt | ato na tarkasya tadviṣayaḥ |
body.translated_text: For reasoning, whose basis is unseen truth, is in some cases dependent on scripture (<s>āgama</s>). It is also unstable, because over time one arrives at a different understanding. It is non-comprehensive, not covering the domain of all that is knowable. It has conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) as its domain, not ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). And it is subject to exhaustion, because of the depletion of insight. But the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is not dependent [on reasoning], and so on up to being free from exhaustion — because of the instruction in numerous sūtras such as the <s>Śatasāhasrikā</s> and others. Therefore, this [<s>Dharma</s>] is not the domain of reasoning.

body.text: anupāyatvāt śrāvakayāne na buddhatvaṃ prāptamityuktam, atha mahāyānaṃ kathamupāyo yukta ityupāyatvayoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: It was said that <s>Buddhahood</s> is not attained in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> because it is no means; now, how is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> a fitting means? Regarding the appropriateness of its being a means, a verse:

children.translated_text: Through grandeur and also through profundity — the ripening [of beings] and non-conceptualization;

children.text: deśanāto dvayasyāsmin sa copāyo niruttare || Msa_1.13 ||
children.translated_text: since there is instruction in both of these herein, this is the means to the unsurpassed [awakening]. || <s>Msa</s> 1.13 ||

body.text: anena ślokena kiṃ darśayati | prabhāvaudāryadeśanayā sattvānāṃ paripākaḥ prabhāvādhimuktito ghaṭanāt | gāmbhīryadeśanayā avikalpanā, ata etasya dvayasyāsmin mahāyāne deśanā | sa copāyo niruttare jñāne, tābhyāṃ yathākramaṃ sattvānāṃ paripācanādātmanaśca buddhadharmaparipākāditi |
body.translated_text: What does he show by this verse? Through the instruction in the grandeur of spiritual power, the ripening of beings — because of engagement through conviction in [the <s>Buddha's</s>] spiritual power. Through the instruction in profundity, non-conceptualization (<s>avikalpanā</s>). Thus there is instruction in both of these in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And this is the means to the unsurpassed knowledge, because through these two, respectively, beings are ripened and one's own <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are brought to maturity.

body.text: ye punarasmāt trasanti tadarthamasthānatrāsādīnave kāraṇatvena ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: For those who are frightened by this, regarding the fact that fear of what is groundless is a cause of harm, a verse:

children.translated_text: That groundless fear of beings causes burning
Because it produces a great mass of demerit over a long period of time,
one without <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), without a virtuous friend, with an uncultivated mind, lacking previous mental merit—

children.text: strasatyasmin dharme patati mahato 'rthādgat iha || Msa_1.14 ||
children.translated_text: such a one fears this <s>dharma</s> and falls away from a great purpose, gone astray here. || Msa_1.14 ||

body.text: trāsāsthāne trāsastadasthānatrāsaḥ | dāhakaraṇo bhavatyapāyeṣu | kiṃ kāraṇam | mahataḥ apuṇyaskandhaprasavasya karaṇāt | kiyantaṃ kālamiti dīrghasamayam | evaṃ paścādādīnavaḥ | yena ca kāraṇena yāvantaṃ ca kālaṃ tat saṃdarśayati | kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇe tu satīti caturvidhaṃ trāsakāraṇaṃ darśayati | gotraṃ cāsya na bhavati sanmitraṃ vā avyutpannamatirvā bhavati mahāyānadharmatāyāṃ pūrvaṃ vānupacitaśubho bhavati | patati mahato 'rthāditi mahābodhisaṃbhārārthāt | aprāptaparihāṇito 'paramādīnavaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: Fear in a place where fear is appropriate is not misplaced fear. It causes burning in the lower realms of existence. For what reason? Because it produces a great mass of demerit. For how long? For a long period of time. Thus the subsequent disadvantage is stated. And he shows the reason why and for how long. But when the cause is present, he shows the fourfold cause of fear: one lacks <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), or lacks a virtuous friend, or has an undeveloped intellect regarding the nature of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> dharma, or has not previously accumulated merit. "Falls away from a great purpose" means from the purpose of accumulating the requisites for great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). He shows a further disadvantage in the loss of what has not yet been attained.

body.text: trāsakāraṇamuktamatrāsakāraṇaṃ vaktavyamityatrāsakāraṇatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having stated the cause of fear, the cause of fearlessness must now be stated; on the ground of fearlessness, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because nothing other than that [i.e., the <s>Mahāyāna</s>] exists [nyasyā?], because of its supreme profundity, because of its systematic method,
because of its variegated exposition, because of its firm and repeated declaration in many ways—
the meaning is not merely according to the letter, and because the state of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) is exceedingly profound,

children.text: na dharme 'smiṃstrāso bhavati viduṣāṃ yonivicayāt || Msa_1.15 ||
children.translated_text: there is no fear regarding this <s>dharma</s> for the wise, due to their thorough investigation of causes. || Msa_1.15 ||

body.text: tadanyānyā[nyasyā?]bhāvāditi tato 'nyasya mahāyānasyābhāvāt | atha śrāvakayānameva mahāyānaṃ syādanyasya śrāvakasya pratyekabuddhasya vābhāvaḥ syāt | sarva eva hi buddhā bhaveyuḥ | paramagahanatvācca | sarvajñajñānamārgasyānugamācca tulyakālapravṛttyā | vicitrasyākhyānāt | vicitraścātra saṃbhā[sā?]ramārga ākhyāyate na kevalaṃ śūnyataiva | tasmāda[ā]bhiprāyikenānena bhavitavyamiti | dhruvakathanayogād, bahumukhādabhīkṣṇaṃ cātra śūnyatā kathyate bahumiśca paryāyaisteṣu teṣu sūtrānteṣu tasmādbhavitavyamatra mahatā prayojanena | anyathā hi satkṛtpratiṣedhamātrakṛtamabhabiṣyaditi | yathākhyānaṃ nārthāt na cāsya yathārutamartho 'smādapi trāso na yuktaḥ | bhagavati ca bhāvātigahanādatigahanaśca buddhānāṃ bhāvo durājñeyastasmānnāsmābhistadajñānāttrasitavyamiti | evaṃ yoniśaḥ pravicayādviduṣāṃ trāso na bhavati |
body.translated_text: "Because nothing other than that [nyasyā?] exists" means because there is no <s>Mahāyāna</s> other than this. Now, if the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone were the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, then there would be no other <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>—all would simply become <s>Buddhas</s>. And because of its supreme profundity. And because of the systematic method of the path to omniscient knowledge, proceeding simultaneously. Because of the variegated exposition—and here the variegated path of discourse is taught, not merely emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) alone; therefore this must be understood as having a deeper intention (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>). Because of the firm and repeated declaration in many ways—emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is declared here repeatedly and through many approaches in the various <s>sūtras</s>, therefore there must be a great purpose here; otherwise it would have been merely a prohibition made with respect. "The meaning is not merely according to the letter"—the meaning of this is not just as it literally sounds, and therefore fear is not justified on this account either. And because the state of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) is exceedingly profound—the state of the <s>Buddhas</s> is exceedingly profound and difficult to comprehend, therefore we should not be frightened on account of our ignorance of it. Thus, through thorough investigation of causes (<s>yoniśaḥ pravicaya</s>), there is no fear for the wise.

body.text: dūrānupraviṣṭajñānagocaratve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the domain of knowledge that has penetrated far within, a verse:

children.text: śrutaṃ niśrityādau prabhavati manaskāra iha yo
children.translated_text: Relying on what has been heard (<s>śruta</s>), first there arises here an attention (<s>manaskāra</s>),
and from that attention arises knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) whose object is the true meaning (<s>tattvārtha</s>);
from that arises the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, and one whose mind delights in that—

children.text: yadā pratyātmaṃ sā kathamasati tasminvyavasitiḥ || Msa_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: when that [understanding] is personal and direct, how can there be certainty that it does not exist? || Msa_1.16 ||

body.text: śrutaṃ niśrityādau manaskāraḥ prabhavati yo yoniśa ityarthaḥ | yoniśo manaskārāttattvārthaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ prabhavati lokottarā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ, tatastatphalasya dharmasya prāptiḥ, tatastasmin prāpte matirvimuktijñānaṃ prādurbhavati | evaṃ yadā pratyātmaṃ sā matirbhavati, kathamasati tasminneṣā vyavasitirniścayo bhavati naivedaṃ buddhavacanamitie |
body.translated_text: "Relying on what has been heard, first attention arises"—the meaning is: that which arises through thorough attention (<s>yoniśaḥ</s>). From thorough attention, knowledge whose object is the true meaning arises—this is the supramundane right view (<s>lokottarā samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). From that comes the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, which is the fruit of that [knowledge]. Then, when that is attained, the understanding (<s>mati</s>)—which is the knowledge of liberation (<s>vimuktijñāna</s>)—manifests. Thus, when that understanding arises as one's own direct experience (<s>pratyātma</s>), how can there be the certainty that concludes "this is definitely not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>"?

body.text: atrāsapadasthānatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the ground of fearlessness, a verse:

children.text: ahaṃ na boddhā na gabhīraboddhā buddhau gabhīraṃ kimatarkagamyam |
children.translated_text: "I cannot understand," "the profound cannot be understood," "why is the profound in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching inaccessible to reasoning?"

children.text: kasmād gabhīrārthavidāṃ ca mokṣa ityetaduttrāsapadaṃ na yuktam || Msa_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: "Why is liberation only for those who understand the profound meaning?"—these grounds for alarm are not justified. || Msa_1.17 ||

body.text: yadi tāvadahamasya na boddhetyuttrāsapadam, tanna yuktam | atha buddho 'pi gambhī[bhī?] rasya padārthasya na boddhā sa kiṃ gabhīraṃ deśayiṣyatītyuttrāsapadam, tadayuktam | atha gambhī[bhī]raṃ kasmādatarkagamyamityuttrāsapadam, tanna yuktam | atha kasmād gabhīrārthavidāmeva mokṣo na tārkikāṇāmityuttrāsapadam, tanna yuktam |
body.translated_text: If the ground for alarm is "I cannot understand this"—that is not justified. Or if the ground for alarm is "even the <s>Buddha</s> cannot understand the profound [bhī?] meaning—then why would he teach the profound?"—that is not justified. Or if the ground for alarm is "why is the profound inaccessible to reasoning?"—that is not justified. Or if the ground for alarm is "why is liberation only for those who understand the profound meaning and not for logicians?"—that is not justified.

body.text: anadhimuktita eva tatsidvau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the establishment [of the Mahāyāna] precisely through the non-faith [of some], a verse:

children.translated_text: For one of inferior faith (<s>hīnādhimukti</s>), of thoroughly inferior disposition (<s>hīna dhātu</s>), surrounded by inferior companions—
if there is no faith in this <s>dharma</s> that is well-taught in its magnificence and profundity, that itself is the proof. || Msa_1.18 ||

body.text: yasya hīnā cādhika[cādhi]muktiḥ, tataśca hīna eva dhātuḥ samudāgata ālayavijñānabhāvanā | hīnaireva sahāyaiḥ samānādhimuktidhātukairyaḥ parivāritastasyāsminnaudāryagāmbhīryasudeśite mahāyānadharme yadyadhimuktirnāsti, ata eva siddhamutkṛṣṭamidaṃ mahāyānamiti |
body.translated_text: One whose faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) is inferior, and from that whose disposition (<s>dhātu</s>) has developed as inferior—the cultivation of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness)—and who is surrounded only by inferior companions of the same disposition and faith: if such a person has no faith in this <s>Mahāyāna</s> dharma that is well-taught in its magnificence and profundity, precisely this proves that this <s>Mahāyāna</s> is supreme.

body.text: aśrutasūtrāntapratikṣepāyoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the impropriety of rejecting <s>sūtras</s> one has not heard, a verse:

children.text: śrutānusāreṇa hi buddhimattāṃ labdhvāśrute yaḥ prakarotyavajñām |
children.translated_text: For one who, having attained intelligence by following what has been heard (<s>śruta</s>), shows contempt for what has not been heard—

children.text: śrute vicitre sati cāprameye śiṣṭe kuto niścayameti mūḍhaḥ || Msa_1.19 ||
children.translated_text: when the heard [teachings] are variegated and immeasurable, how can such a fool arrive at certainty regarding the remainder? || Msa_1.19 ||

body.text: kāmaṃ tāvadadhimuktirna syādaśrutānāṃ tu sūtrāntānāmaviśeṣeṇa pratikṣepo na yuktaḥ | śrutānusāreṇaiva hi buddhimattvaṃ labdhvā yaḥ śruta evāvajñāṃ karoti mūḍhaḥ sa satyevāvaśiṣṭe śrute vicitre cāprameye ca kutaḥ kāraṇānniścayameti na tadbuddhavacanamiti | na hi tasya śrutādanyabdalamasti tasmādaśrutvā pratikṣepo na yuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Granted, there may be no faith, but a wholesale rejection of <s>sūtras</s> that one has not heard is not justified. For one who, having attained intelligence only by following what has been heard, shows contempt for what has been heard—such a fool, when there remain other heard [teachings] that are variegated and immeasurable, on what grounds does he arrive at the certainty that "this is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>"? For he has no basis other than what he has heard; therefore rejection without having heard is not justified.

body.text: yadapi ca śrutaṃ tadyoniśo manasi kartavyaṃ nāyoniśa ityayoniśomanasikārādīnave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Moreover, what has been heard should be attended to thoroughly (<s>yoniśaḥ</s>), not carelessly (<s>ayoniśaḥ</s>); on the disadvantage of careless attention (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: When the meaning is imagined according to the mere letter, one's own conviction undermines one's understanding (<s>buddhi</s>);

children.text: svākhyātatāṃ ca kṣipati kṣatiṃ ca prāpnoti dharme pratighāvatīva[pratīghātameva] || Msa_1.20 ||
children.translated_text: it destroys the quality of being well-taught (<s>svākhyātatā</s>), and one suffers harm with respect to the <s>dharma</s>, as if struck by an obstacle [pratīghātameva]. || Msa_1.20 ||

body.text: svapratyaya iti svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśako, na vijñānāmantikādarthaparyeṣī | hānimupaiti buddheriti yathābhū[ru]tajñānādaprāptiparihānitaḥ | dharmasya ca svākhyātatāṃ pratikṣipati tannidānaṃ cāpuṇyaprabhāvāt kṣatiṃ prāpnoti | dharme ca pratighātamāvaraṇaṃ ca dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyaṃ karmetyayamatrādīnavaḥ |
body.translated_text: "One's own conviction" means one who clings to one's own views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), not one who seeks meaning through the succession of consciousnesses (<s>vijñāna</s>). "Undermines one's understanding" means through failure to attain and loss of knowledge of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>). And one rejects the quality of the <s>dharma</s> being well-taught, and as a result of the demerit arising from that cause, one suffers harm. And the obstacle with respect to the <s>dharma</s>—this is an obstruction, a <s>karma</s> leading to the ruin of the <s>dharma</s>. This is the disadvantage here.

body.text: ayathāvataścā[ayathārutañcā]rthamavijānato 'pi pratighāto na yukta iti pratighātāyoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even for one who does not understand the meaning as it truly is [ayathārutañcā], hostility is not justified; on the impropriety of hostility, a verse:

children.translated_text: Mental defilement that is naturally impure [and directed against what is not according to the letter] is indeed of improper character;

children.text: prāgeva saṃdehagatasya dharme tasmādupekṣaiva varaṃ hyadoṣā || Msa_1.21 ||
children.translated_text: all the more so for one who has arrived at doubt regarding the <s>dharma</s>—therefore equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) alone is better, for it is free from fault. || Msa_1.21 ||

body.text: prakṛtipraduṣṭa iti prakṛtisāvadyaḥ | tasmādupekṣaiva varam | kasmāt | sā hyadoṣā | pratighātastu sadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: "Naturally impure" means blameworthy by its very nature. Therefore equanimity alone is better. Why? Because it is free from fault. But hostility is faulty.

body.text: | mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre mahāyānasiddhyadhikāraḥ prathamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the first chapter on the establishment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (<s>Mahāyānasiddhyadhikāra</s>). ||

body.text: dvitīyo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: The second chapter.

body.text: śaraṇagamanaviśeṣasaṃgrahaślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse summarizing the distinctive features of taking refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>):

children.text: ratnāni yo hi śaraṇapragato 'tra yāne jñeyaḥ sa eva paramaḥ śaraṇa[ṇaṃ] gatānām |
children.translated_text: One who has gone for refuge to the [Three] Jewels (<s>Ratnas</s>) in this vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) should be known as the foremost among those who have taken refuge,

through the fourfold distinguishing characteristic of meaning, differentiated by universality (<s>sarvatraga</s>), acceptance (<s>abhyupagama</s>), realization (<s>adhigama</s>), and mastery (<s>abhibhūti</s>). || Msa_2.1 ||

body.text: sa eva paramaḥ śaraṇaṃ gatānāmiti | kena kāraṇena | caturvidhasvabhāvārthaviśeṣaṇena | caturvidho 'rthaḥ sarvatragābhyupagamādhigamābhibhūtibhedato veditavyaḥ | sarvatragārthaḥ | abhyupagamārthaḥ | adhigamārthaḥ | abhibhavārthaḥ | te punaruttaratra nirdekṣyante |
body.translated_text: "He is the foremost among those who have taken refuge"—for what reason? Through the fourfold distinguishing characteristic of meaning. The fourfold meaning should be understood through the differentiation of universality, acceptance, realization, and mastery: the meaning of universality, the meaning of acceptance, the meaning of realization, and the meaning of mastery. These will be explained further below.

body.text: tathāpyatra śaraṇapragatānāṃ bahuduṣkarakāryatvāt kecinnotsahante | ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, because the task of those who have gone for refuge here is very difficult, some do not have the courage. A verse:

children.text: yasmādādau duṣkara eṣa vyavasāyo duḥsādho 'sau naikasahasrairapi kalpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Since this undertaking is difficult at the outset, since it is hard to accomplish even in many thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
since when accomplished it is of great purpose as a foundation for the welfare of beings—therefore the foremost vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) here is the foremost in its purpose of refuge. || Msa_2.2 ||

body.text: etena tasya śaraṇagamanavyavasāyasya praṇidhānapratipattiviśeṣābhyāṃ yaśohetutvaṃ darśayati | phalaprāptiviśeṣeṇa mahārthatvam |
body.translated_text: By this he shows that the undertaking of taking refuge, through the distinction of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) and practice (<s>pratipatti</s>), is a cause of glory. Through the distinction of attaining the fruit, it is of great purpose.

body.text: pūrvādhikṛte sarvatragārthe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the previously introduced meaning of universality (<s>sarvatragārtha</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: One who has set out to ferry across all beings,
endowed with skill in the vehicle and in knowledge that reaches everywhere,
one who is of a single taste (<s>ekarasa</s>) in both <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and <s>Saṃsāra</s> [in the peace of cessation and in continued existence]—

children.text: jñeyo dhīmāneṣa hi sarvatraga evam || Msa_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: that wise one should be known as truly universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) in this way. || Msa_2.3 ||

body.text: etena caturvidhaṃ sarvatragārthaṃ...........................
body.translated_text: By this the fourfold meaning of universality (<s>sarvatragārtha</s>)...........................

body.text: asāṃketikaṃ dharmatāaprātilambhikaṃ ceti prabhedalakṣaṇā pravṛttiraudārikasūkṣmaprabhedena |
body.translated_text: non-conventional and not apprehending an intrinsic nature of <s>dharmatā</s>—such is the characteristic of engagement, distinguished by its gross and subtle divisions.

body.text: śaraṇapratipattiviśeṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the distinguishing features of the practice of taking refuge, a verse:

children.translated_text: One who has undertaken this taking of refuge, which is of great purpose, attains an immeasurable increase of the multitude of virtues;

children.text: sphurati jagadidaṃ kṛpāśayena prathayati cāpratimaṃ mahā[rya]dharmam || Msa_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: he pervades this world with a mind of compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) and proclaims the incomparable noble <s>dharma</s> (<s>mahāryadharma</s>). || Msa_2.4 ||

body.text: atra śaraṇagamanasthāṃ mahārthatāṃ svaparārthapratipattibhyāṃ darśayati | svārthapratipattiḥ punarbahuprakārāprameyaguṇavṛddhyā | aprameyatvaṃ tarkasaṃkhyākālāprameyatayā veditavyam | na hi sā guṇavṛddhistarkeṇa prameyā na saṃkhyayā na kālenātyantikatvāt | parārthapratipattirāśayataśca karuṇāsphuraṇena prayogataśca mahāyānadharmaprathanena | mahāyānaṃ hi mahāryadṛśāṃ dharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the great purposefulness of the state of having taken refuge, through the practice for one's own benefit and for the benefit of others. The practice for one's own benefit is through the immeasurable increase of virtues of many kinds. Immeasurability should be understood as immeasurability by reasoning, by number, and by time. For that increase of virtues is not measurable by reasoning, nor by number, nor by time, since it is ultimate. The practice for the benefit of others is, in terms of intention (<s>āśaya</s>), through the pervading of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and in terms of application (<s>prayoga</s>), through the proclamation of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> dharma. For the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the dharma of those who possess the noble vision (<s>mahāryadṛś</s>).

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre śaraṇagamanādhikāro dvitīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the second chapter on taking refuge (<s>Śaraṇagamanādhikāra</s>). ||

body.text: tṛtīyo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: The third chapter.

body.text: gotraprabhedasaṃgrahaślokaḥ
body.translated_text: A verse summarizing the divisions of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage):

children.translated_text: The supremacy of beings, the intrinsic nature, the marks, the divisions of <s>gotra</s>,
the disadvantage, the benefit, and the twofold simile—[each] fourfold. || Msa_3.1 ||

body.text: anena gotrasyāstitvamagratvaṃ svabhāvo liṅgaṃ bheda ādīnapravo 'nuśaṃso dvidhaupamyaṃ cetyeṣa prabhedaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ | ete ca prabhedāḥ pratyekaṃ caturvidhāḥ |
body.translated_text: By this are summarized the following divisions of <s>gotra</s>: its existence, its supremacy, its intrinsic nature, its marks, its divisions, its disadvantage, its benefit, and its twofold simile. And each of these divisions is fourfold.

body.text: anena gotrāstitvavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the division of the existence of <s>gotra</s>, a verse:

children.translated_text: Through the differentiation of dispositions (<s>dhātus</s>), of faith (<s>adhimukti</s>), and of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>),
and through the observation of differentiation in fruits (<s>phala</s>), the existence of <s>gotra</s> is established. || Msa_3.2 ||

body.text: nānādhātukatvātsattvānāmaparimāṇo dhātuprabhedo yathoktamakṣarāśisūtre | tasmādevaṃjātīyako 'pi dhātubhedaḥ pratyetavyaḥ iti | asti yānatraye gotrabhedaḥ | adhimuktibhedo 'pi sattvānāmupalabhyate | prathamata eva kasyacit kvacideva yāne 'dhimuktirbhavati | so 'ntareṇa gotrabhedaṃ na syāt | utpāditāyāmapi ca pratyayavaśenādhimuktau pratipattibheda upalabhyate kaścinnirboḍhā bhavati kaścinneti so 'ntareṇa gotraprabhedaṃ na syāt | phalabhedaścopalabhyate hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭā bodhayaḥ | so 'ntareṇa gotrabhedaṃ na syāt bījānurūpatvāt phalasya |
body.translated_text: Because beings are of diverse dispositions (<s>nānādhātuka</s>), there is an immeasurable differentiation of dispositions, as stated in the <s>Akṣarāśisūtra</s>: "Therefore a differentiation of dispositions of this kind should also be acknowledged." Thus there exists a differentiation of <s>gotra</s> in the three vehicles. A differentiation of faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) is also observed among beings: from the very beginning, someone has faith in a particular vehicle only. That would not be so without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>. And even when faith has been generated through conditions, a differentiation in practice is observed—some carry through to awakening and some do not. That would not be so without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>. And a differentiation of fruits is observed—inferior, middling, and superior awakenings (<s>bodhi</s>). That would not be so without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>, because the fruit corresponds to the seed (<s>bīja</s>).

body.text: agratvavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the division of supremacy, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because it is the cause of the excellence, the completeness, the great purposefulness,
and the inexhaustibility of virtue—the supremacy of <s>gotra</s> is established. || Msa_3.3 ||

body.text: atra gotrasya caturvidhena nimittatvenāgratvaṃ darśayati | taddhi gotraṃ kuśalamūlānāmudagratve nimittaṃ, sarvatve, mahārthatve, akṣayatve ca | na hi śrāvakāṇāṃ tathodagrāṇi kuśalamūlāni, na ca sarvāṇi santi, balavaiśāradyādyabhāvāt | na ca mahārthānyaparārthatvāt | na cākṣayāṇyanupadhiśeṣanirvāṇāvasānatvāt |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the supremacy of <s>gotra</s> by its being the cause in a fourfold manner. For that <s>gotra</s> is the cause of the excellence of wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), of their completeness, of their great purposefulness, and of their inexhaustibility. For the wholesome roots of <s>Śrāvakas</s> are not so excellent, nor are they complete, due to the absence of the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and so forth; nor are they of great purpose, because they do not serve the benefit of others; nor are they inexhaustible, because they terminate in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>).

body.text: lakṣaṇavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: On the division of characteristics, a verse:

children.text: prakṛtyā paripuṣṭaṃ ca āśrayaścāśritaṃ ca tat |
children.translated_text: It is by nature and cultivated, and it is both the basis and what is based upon it,
it should be known as both existent and non-existent, for the purpose of producing excellent qualities. || Msa_3.4 ||

body.text: etena caturvidhaṃ gotraṃ darśayati | prakṛtisthaṃ samudānītamāśrayasvabhāvamāśritasvabhāvaṃ ca tadeva yathākramam | tatpunarhetubhāvena sat phalabhāvenāsat guṇottāraṇārthena gotraṃ veditavyaṃ guṇā uttarantyasmādudbhavantīti kṛtvā |
body.translated_text: By this he shows that <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) is fourfold: innate (<s>prakṛtistha</s>), developed (<s>samudānīta</s>), having the nature of a basis, and having the nature of what is based — in that order. Furthermore, <s>gotra</s> should be understood as existent in terms of being a cause, non-existent in terms of being a result, and for the purpose of producing excellent qualities — meaning 'qualities arise from it, they spring forth.'

body.text: liṅgavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of marks:

children.translated_text: Compassion, faith, patience, and from the very first practice,
good conduct even of what is wholesome — these are determined as the marks of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). || Msa_3.5 ||

body.text: caturvidhaṃ liṅgaṃ bodhisattvagotre | ādiprayogata eva kāruṇyaṃ sattveṣu | adhimuktirmahāyānadharme | kṣāntirduṣkaracaryāyāṃ sahiṣṇutārthena | samācāraśca pāramitāmayasya kuśalasyeti |
body.translated_text: There are four marks of the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage: compassion toward beings from the very first practice; faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> teachings; patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) in the sense of endurance of difficult practices; and good conduct consisting of wholesome [deeds] made of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

body.text: prabhedavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of varieties:

children.translated_text: The <s>gotra</s> (lineage) is determined and undetermined, unshakeable and shakeable;
this division of <s>gotra</s> by conditions is fourfold in summary. || Msa_3.6 ||

body.text: samāsena caturvidhaṃ gotraṃ niyatāniyataṃ tadeva yathākramaṃ pratyayairahāryaṃ hāryaṃ ceti |
body.translated_text: In summary, <s>gotra</s> is fourfold: determined and undetermined — which in that order are unshakeable and shakeable by conditions.

body.text: ādīnavavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of disadvantages:

children.translated_text: Habitual practice of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), bad companionship, adversity, and dependence on others —
the disadvantages of <s>gotra</s> should be known as fourfold in summary. || Msa_3.7 ||

body.text: bodhisattvagotre samāsena caturvidha ādīnavo yena gotrastho 'guṇeṣu pravartate | kleśabāhulyam, akalyāṇamitratā, upakaraṇavighātaḥ, pāratantryaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: In the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage, there are four disadvantages in summary, by which one established in the lineage engages in unwholesome qualities: abundance of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), association with unwholesome friends, obstruction of resources, and subjection to others.

body.text: anuśaṃsavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of benefits:

children.translated_text: After a long time, going to the lower realms, and swift liberation there;
experiencing only mild suffering, and with a sense of urgency, maturing beings. || Msa_3.8 ||

body.text: caturvidho bodhisattvasya gotre 'nuśaṃsaḥ | cireṇāpāyān gacchati | kṣipraṃ ca tebhyo mucyate | mṛdukaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ teṣūpapannaḥ pratisaṃvedayate | saṃvignacetāstadupapannāṃśca sattvānkaruṇāyamānaḥ paripācayati |
body.translated_text: There are four benefits in the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage: one goes to the lower realms only after a long time; one is quickly liberated from them; when reborn there, one experiences suffering only mildly; and with an agitated mind, compassionately matures the beings born there.

body.text: mahāsuvarṇagotraupamye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the analogy with a great gold mine:

children.translated_text: It should be known to be like a gold mine, being the basis of immeasurable wholesome [qualities],
and the support of knowledge, purity, and powers. || Msa_3.9 ||

body.text: mahāsuvarṇagotraṃ hi caturvidhasya suvarṇasyāśrayo bhavati | prabhūtasya, prabhāsvarasya, nirmalasya, karmaṇyasya ca | tatsādharmyeṇa bodhisattvagotramaprameyakuśalamūlāśrayaḥ | jñānāśrayaḥ | kleśanairmalyāprāptyāśrayaḥ | abhijñādiprabhāvāśrayaśca | tasmānmahāsuvarṇagotropamaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: For a great gold mine is the basis of four kinds of gold: abundant, lustrous, pure, and workable. By analogy, the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage is the basis of immeasurable wholesome roots; the basis of knowledge; the basis of attaining freedom from afflictions; and the basis of powers such as supernatural abilities (<s>abhijñā</s>). Therefore it should be known as analogous to a great gold mine.

body.text: mahāratnagotraupamye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the analogy with a great jewel mine:

children.translated_text: It should be known to be like a precious jewel mine, because of being a cause of great awakening,
and because of being the support of great knowledge, noble <s>samādhi</s>, and the welfare of great beings. || Msa_3.10 ||

body.text: mahāratnagotraṃ hi caturvidharatnāśrayo bhavati | jātyasya varṇasaṃpannasya saṃsthānasaṃpannasya pramāṇasaṃpannasya ca | tadupamaṃ bodhisattvagotraṃ veditavyam, mahābodhinimittatvāt, mahājñānanimittatvāt, āryasamādhinimittatvāt, cittasya hi saṃsthitiḥ samādhiḥ, mahāsattvaparipākanimittatvācca bahusattvaparipācanāt |
body.translated_text: For a great jewel mine is the basis of four kinds of jewels: of excellent birth, of perfect color, of perfect shape, and of perfect measure. The <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage should be known as analogous to that, because of being a cause of great awakening, because of being a cause of great knowledge, because of being a cause of noble <s>samādhi</s> — for <s>samādhi</s> is the stability of mind — and because of being a cause of maturing many great beings.

body.text: agotrasthavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of those without lineage:

children.translated_text: Someone is exclusively devoted to misconduct; someone has eradicated wholesome qualities;
someone possesses wholesome [qualities] that do not lead to liberation; and another has diminished wholesome qualities, being devoid of the cause. || Msa_3.11 ||

body.text: aparinirvāṇadharmaka etasminnagotrastho 'bhipretaḥ | sa ca samāsato dvividhaḥ | tatkālāparinirvāṇadharmā atyantaṃ ca | tatkālāparinirvāṇadharmā caturvidhaḥ | duścaritaikāntikaḥ, samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ, amokṣabhāgīyakuśalamūlaḥ, hīnakuśalamūlaścāparipūrṇasaṃbhāraḥ | atyantāparinirvāṇadharmā tu hetuhino yasya parinirvāṇagotrameva nāsti |
body.translated_text: Here, by 'one who is of the nature of not attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' is meant one without lineage (<s>agotra</s>). That is of two kinds in summary: one who does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> temporarily, and one who does not at all. The temporarily non-attaining is fourfold: exclusively devoted to misconduct, one whose wholesome roots are cut off, one whose wholesome roots do not lead to liberation, and one whose wholesome roots are deficient with incomplete accumulations. But one who is permanently of the nature of not attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is devoid of the cause — one who simply has no lineage for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: prakṛtiparipuṣṭagotramāhātmye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the greatness of the innate and cultivated lineage:

children.translated_text: Regarding the teaching of the profound and vast, set forth for the benefit of others, the long-lasting Dharma —
even without having known it, faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) arises, vast and capable of commitment;
and at the end, the supreme attainment transcending both — that this occurs for them
should be known as from the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s naturally endowed and cultivated lineage. || Msa_3.12 ||

body.text: yadgābhī[mbhī]ryodāryavādini parahitakriyārthamukte vistīrṇe mahāyānadharme gāmbhīryaudāryārthamajñātvaivādhimuktirvipulā bhavati, pratipattau cotsāhaḥ [cākhedaḥ] saṃpattiścāvasāne mahābodhirdvayagatāyāḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 14

children.text: ) saṃpatteḥ paramā, tatprakṛtyā guṇavataḥ paripuṣṭasya ca bodhisattvagotrasya māhātmyaṃ veditavyam | dvayagatā iti dvaye laukikāḥ śrāvakāśca | parameti viśiṣṭā |
children.translated_text: ) — the greatness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage that is naturally endowed with qualities and cultivated should be understood. 'Transcending both' means: the two are worldly people and <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers). 'Supreme' means: distinguished.

body.translated_text: When the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma is taught — vast, spoken for the purpose of benefiting others, teaching the meaning of the profound and vast — even without having known it, vast faith arises, and enthusiasm for practice [or non-discouragement], and at the end the supreme attainment of great awakening, which is the supreme of the attainment that transcends both (

body.text: phalato gotraviśeṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the distinction of lineage in terms of fruit:

children.translated_text: For the growth of the tree of awakening with vast and excellent qualities, and for the attainment of the cessation of dense suffering and happiness,
because it has as its fruit the activity of happiness for the benefit of self and others, this lineage is supremely rooted. || Msa_3.13 ||

body.text: svaparahitaphalasya bodhivṛkṣasya praśastamūlatvamanena bodhisattvagotraṃ saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: By this, the <s>bodhisattva</s> lineage has been shown to be the excellent root of the tree of awakening, whose fruit is the benefit of self and others.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre gotrādhikārastṛtīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the third chapter on <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) ||

body.text: caturtho 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Fourth chapter:

body.text: cittotpādalakṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the characteristic of the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>):

children.translated_text: Of great enthusiasm, great undertaking, great purpose, and great outcome —
the volition of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, aimed at the benefit of both [self and others], is the generation of the [awakening] mind. || Msa_4.1 ||

body.text: mahotsāhā saṃnāhavīryeṇa gambhīraduṣkaradīrghakālapratipakṣotsa[ttyu]tsahanāt | mahārambhā yathāsaṃnāhaprayogavīryeṇa | mahārthā ātmaparahitādhikārāt | mahodayā mahābodhisamudāgamatvāt | so 'yaṃ trividho guṇaḥ paridīpitaḥ, puruṣakāraguṇo dvābhyāṃ padābhyāmarthakriyāguṇaḥ phalaparigrahaguṇaśca dvābhyām | dvayārthā mahābodhisattvārthakriyālambanatvāt | iti triguṇā dvayālambanā ca catenā cittotpāda ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Of great enthusiasm — through the vigor of determination (<s>saṃnāhavīrya</s>), because of enduring that which is profound, difficult, and long in duration. Of great undertaking — through the vigor of practice corresponding to that determination. Of great purpose — because of the task of benefiting self and others. Of great outcome — because of the attainment of great awakening. These three qualities are illuminated: the quality of effort by the first two phrases, the quality of purposeful activity, and the quality of encompassing the result by the last two. Aimed at the benefit of both — because it has as its object the activity of great awakening and the welfare of beings. Thus the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) is said to have three qualities and two objects.

body.text: cittotpādaprabhede ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the varieties of the generation of the mind:

children.translated_text: The generation of the mind is first that based on faith (<s>adhimokṣa</s>); another is that of pure superior intention;
that which is maturational (<s>vaipākya</s>) is considered to be on the [higher] stages, and likewise that which is free from obscurations. || Msa_4.2 ||

body.text: caturvidho bodhisattvānāṃ cittotpādaḥ | ādhimokṣiko 'dhimukticaryābhūmau | śuddhādhyāśayikaḥ saptasu bhūmiṣu | vaipākiko 'ṣṭamyādiṣu | anāvaraṇiko buddhabhūmau |
body.translated_text: The generation of the mind of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is fourfold: based on faith (<s>ādhimokṣika</s>) on the stage of faith-based practice; of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayika</s>) on the seven stages; maturational (<s>vaipākika</s>) from the eighth stage onward; and free from obscurations (<s>anāvaraṇika</s>) on the Buddha-stage.

body.text: cittotpādaviniścaye cattvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the ascertainment of the generation of the mind:

children.translated_text: It is considered to have compassion as its root, and the constant intention for the welfare of beings;
faith in the Dharma, and having as its object the search for that knowledge. || Msa_4.3 ||
It is progressively aspiring, established in ethical restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvṛti</s>);
the arising of the adversary is the obstacle, and forbearance [overcomes it]. || Msa_4.4 ||
Its benefit is the increase of wholesome [qualities]; for it consists of merit and knowledge.
It is said to always be engaged in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), and it is the way of going forth. || Msa_4.5 ||
Its culmination is the stages; through practice appropriate to each —
the ascertainment of the generation of the mind of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be known. || Msa_4.6 ||

body.text: tathāyaṃ viniścayaḥ | kiṃmūla eṣa catuvirdho bodhisattvānāṃ cittotpādaḥ kimāśayaḥ kimadhimokṣaḥ kimālambanaḥ kiṃyānaḥ kiṃpratiṣṭhaḥ kimādīnavaḥ kimanuśaṃsaḥ kiṃniryāṇaḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 16

children.text: ) kiṃparyavasāna iti | āha | karuṇāmūlaḥ | sadāsattvahitāśayaḥ | mahāyānadharmādhimokṣaḥ | tajjñānaparyeṣṭyākāreṇa tajjñānālambanāt [naḥ] | uttarottaracchandayānaḥ | bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarapratiṣṭhaḥ | paripantha ādīnavaḥ | kaḥ punastatparipantho vipakṣasyānyayānacittasyotthāpanādhivāsanā vā | puṇyajñānamayakuśaladharmavṛddhyanuśaṃsaḥ | sadāpāramitābhyāsaniryāṇaḥ | bhūmiparyavasānaśca pratisvaṃ bhūmiprayogāt | yasyāṃ bhūmau yaḥ prayuktastasya tadbhūmiparyavasānaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) What is its culmination? The answer: Its root is compassion. Its intention is always the welfare of beings. Its faith is in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma. Its object is the knowledge of that, in the form of searching for that knowledge. Its vehicle is progressively aspiring. Its foundation is the <s>bodhisattva</s> ethical restraint. The disadvantage is obstruction. What then is that obstruction? It is the arising or endurance of the opposing mind of another vehicle. Its benefit is the increase of wholesome qualities consisting of merit and knowledge. Its way of going forth is the constant practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>. And its culmination is the stages, through the practice appropriate to each stage — one who is engaged in a particular stage has that stage as the culmination.

body.translated_text: The ascertainment is thus: What is the root of this fourfold generation of the mind of <s>bodhisattvas</s>? What is its intention? What is its faith? What is its object? What is its vehicle? What is its foundation? What is its disadvantage? What is its benefit? What is its way of going forth? (

body.text: samādānasāṃketikacittotpāde ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the conventional and commitment-based generation of the mind:

children.translated_text: Through the power of a friend, through the power of the cause, through the power of the root, through the power of hearing, and through the practice of wholesome [deeds] —
the generation of the mind is said to arise with unstable and stable outcomes, due to the instruction of others. || Msa_4.7 ||

body.text: yo hi parākhyānāccittotpādaḥ paravijñāpanātsa ucyate samādānasāṃketikaḥ | sa punarmitrabalādvā bhavati kalyāṇamitrānurodhāt | hetubalādvā gotrasāmarthyāt | kuśalamūladvātīta[tadgotra]puṣṭitaḥ | śrutabalādvā tatra tatra dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe bahūnāṃ bodhicittotpādāt | śubhābhyāsādvā dṛṣṭa iva dharme satataśravaṇodgrahaṇadhāraṇādibhiḥ | sa punarmitrabalādadṛḍhodayo veditavyaḥ | hetvādibalād dṛḍhodayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The generation of the mind that arises from the instruction of others — from being informed by others — is called conventional and commitment-based (<s>samādānasāṃketika</s>). It occurs through the power of a friend, from following a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>); through the power of the cause, from the capacity of the lineage; through the power of the [wholesome] root, from the cultivation of that [lineage's] root; through the power of hearing, from the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) by many upon hearing various Dharma discourses; or through the practice of wholesome [deeds], as in this very life through constant hearing, memorizing, retaining, and so forth. That which arises through the power of a friend should be known as having an unstable outcome; that which arises through the power of the cause and so forth has a stable outcome.

body.text: pāramārthikacittotpāde sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the ultimate generation of the mind:

children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s> has been well attended upon, and the accumulations of knowledge and merit are well developed,
from the arising of non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpajñāna</s>) regarding phenomena, this [mind] reaches its supreme state. || Msa_4.8 ||

children.text: dharmeṣu ca sattveṣu ca tatkṛtyeṣūttame ca buddhatve |
children.translated_text: Regarding phenomena, regarding beings, regarding their duties, and regarding the supreme <s>Buddhahood</s>,
from the attainment of an equal mind, the distinction of its joy. || Msa_4.9 ||
The nobility of birth in that [state], the enthusiasm, and the purity of intention —

children.text: kauśalyaṃ pariśiṣṭe niryāṇaṃ caiva vijñeyam || Msa_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: the skill in the remainder, and the way of going forth should be known. || Msa_4.10 ||
Born from the seed of faith in the Dharma, from the excellent mother of the <s>pāramitās</s>,

children.text: dhyānamaye sukhagarbhe karuṇā saṃvardhikā dhātrī || Msa_4.11 ||
children.translated_text: in the blissful womb of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), compassion is the nourishing nurse. || Msa_4.11 ||
Nobility should be known from the accomplishment of the ten great vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>);
enthusiasm should be understood from non-discouragement regarding the difficult, long, and excessive [tasks]. || Msa_4.12 ||
From awakening near to enlightenment, and from obtaining knowledge of the means for that,
purity of intention should be known; but skill pertains to other stages. || Msa_4.13 ||
The way of going forth should be known through attention in accordance with the established [truths],
and through the non-conceptualization of the knowledge of the conceptual nature of that very thing. || Msa_4.14 ||

body.text: prathamena ślokenopadeśapratipattyadhigamaviśeṣaiḥ pāramārthikatvaṃ cittotpādasya darśayati | sa ca pāramārthikaścittotpādaḥ pramuditāyāṃ bhūmāviti [pramuditābhūmiḥ] | prāmodyaviśiṣṭatāyāstatra kāraṇaṃ darśayati | tatra dharmeṣu samacittatā dharmanairātmyapratibodhāt | sattveṣu samacittatā ātmaparasamatopagamāt | sattvakṛtyeṣu samacittatā ātmana iva teṣāṃ duḥkhakṣayākāṅkṣaṇāt | buddhatve samacittatā taddharmadhātorātmanyabhedapratibodhāt | tasminneva ca pāramārthikacittotpāde ṣaḍarthā veditavyāḥ | janma audāryamutsāha āśayaśuddhiḥ pariśiṣṭakauśalyaṃ niryāṇaṃ ca | tatra janma bījamātṛgarbhadhātrīviśeṣādveditavyam | audāryaṃ daśamahāpraṇidhānābhinirhārāt | utsāho dīrghakālikaduṣkarākhedāt | āśayaśuddhirāsannabodhijñānāttadupāyajñānalābhācca | pariśiṣṭakauśalyamanyāsu bhūmiṣu kauśalyam | niryāṇaṃ yathāvyavasthānabhūmimanasikāreṇa | kathaṃ manasikāreṇa, tasya bhūmivyavasthānasya kalpanājñānātkalpanāmātrametaditi | tasyaiva ca kalpanājñānasyāvikalpanāt |
body.translated_text: By the first verse, he shows the ultimate nature of the generation of the mind through the distinctions of teaching, practice, and realization. And that ultimate generation of the mind is on the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage. He shows the cause of the distinction of joy there. There, equanimity toward phenomena is from awakening to the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>); equanimity toward beings is from realizing the equality of self and others; equanimity toward the duties of beings is from desiring the cessation of their suffering just as of one's own; equanimity toward <s>Buddhahood</s> is from awakening to the non-difference of that <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in oneself. And in that very ultimate generation of the mind, six aspects should be understood: birth, nobility, enthusiasm, purity of intention, remaining skill, and way of going forth. Among these, birth should be understood from the distinctions of seed, mother, womb, and nurse. Nobility is from the accomplishment of the ten great vows. Enthusiasm is from non-discouragement regarding long-lasting difficult [tasks]. Purity of intention is from knowledge near to awakening and from obtaining knowledge of the means for that. The remaining skill is skill on the other stages. The way of going forth is through attention to the established stages. How through attention? From the knowledge that the conceptual nature of that establishment of stages is mere conceptual construction. And from the non-conceptualization of that very knowledge of conceptual construction.

body.text: aupamyamāhātmye ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the greatness through similes:

children.translated_text: The generation [of the mind] is like the earth; another is like excellent gold;
like the bright crescent moon; another, like fire, should be known as ascending. || Msa_4.15 ||
Furthermore, another is like a great treasure; another is just like a jewel mine;
it should be known as like the ocean; like a diamond; and like the lord of mountains. || Msa_4.16 ||
Like the king of medicines; another should be known as resembling a great friend;
like a wish-fulfilling gem; and another should be known as like the sun. || Msa_4.17 ||
Another is like the sweet song of a <s>gandharva</s> (celestial musician); another should be known as like a king;
like a storehouse; and likewise another is like a great highway. || Msa_4.18 ||
It should be known as like a vehicle; and like a <s>gandharva</s> (celestial musician), arising from the mind;
like the sound of joy; and like the current of a great river. || Msa_4.19 ||
And it is said to be like a cloud — the generation of the mind of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones);

children.text: tasmāttathā guṇāḍhyaṃ cittaṃ muditaiḥ samutpādyam || Msa_4.20 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, such a mind rich in qualities should be generated with joy. || Msa_4.20 ||

body.text: prathamacittotpādo bodhisattvānāṃ pṛthivīsamaḥ sarvabuddhadharmatatsaṃbhāraprasavarasya pratiṣṭhābhūtatvāt | āśayasahagataścittotpādaḥ kalyāṇasuvarṇasadṛśo hitasukhādhyāśayasya vikārābhajanāt | prayogasahagataḥ śuklapakṣanavacandropamaḥ kuśaladharmavṛddhigamanāt | adhyāśayasahagato bahnisadṛśa indhanākaraviśeṣeṇevāgnistasyottarottaraviśeṣādhigamanāt | viśeṣādhigamāśayo hyadhyāśayaḥ | dānapāramitāsahagato mahānidhanopama āmiṣasaṃbhogenāprameyasattvasaṃtarpaṇādakṣayatvācca | śīlapāramitāsahagato ratnākaropamaḥ sarvaguṇaratnānāṃ tataḥ prasavāt | kṣāntipāramitāsahagataḥ sāgaropamaḥ sarvāniṣṭoparipātairakṣobhyatvāt | vīryapāramitāsahagato vajropamo dṛḍhatvādabhedyatayā | dhyānapāramitāsahagataḥ parvatarājopamo niṣkampatvādavikṣepataḥ | prajñāpāramitāsahagato bhaiṣajyarājopamaḥ sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇavyādhipraśamanāt | apramāṇasahagato mahāsuhṛtsaṃnibhaḥ sarvāvasthaṃ satvānupekṣakatvāt | abhijñāsahagataścintāmaṇisadṛśo yathādhimokṣaṃ tatphalasamṛddheḥ | saṃgrahavastusahagato dinakarasadṛśo vineyasasyaparipācanāt | pratisaṃvitsahagato gandharvamadhuraghoṣopamo vineyāvarjakadharmadeśakatvāt | pratiśaraṇasahagato mahārājopamo 'vipraṇāśahetutvāt | puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasahagataḥ koṣṭhāgāropamo bahupuṇyajñānasaṃbhārakoṣasthānatvāt | bodhipakṣasahagato mahārājapathopamaḥ sarvāryapudgalayātānuyatatvāt | śamathavipaśyanāsahagato yānopamaḥ sukhavahanāt | dhāraṇā-pratibhānasahagato gandharvopamaḥ udakadhāraṇākṣayodbhedasādharmyeṇa śrutāśrutadharmārthadhāraṇākṣayodbhedataḥ | dharmoddānasahagata ānandaśabdasadṛśo mokṣakāmānāṃ vineyānāṃ priyaśrāvaṇāt | ekāyanamārgasahagato nadīśro[sro]taḥ samaḥ svarasavāhitvāt | anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhe ekāyanatvaṃ tadbhūmigatānāṃ bodhisattvānāmabhinnakāryakriyātvāt | upāyakauśalyasahagato meghopamaḥ sarvasattvārthakriyātadadhīnatvāttuṣitabhavanavāsādisaṃdarśanataḥ | yathā meghātsarvabhājanalokasaṃpattyaḥ | eṣa ca dvāviṃśatyupamaścittotpāda āryākṣayamatisūtre 'kṣagatānusāreṇānugantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The first generation of the mind of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is like the earth, because it serves as the foundation for the arising of all Buddha-qualities and their accumulations. The generation of the mind accompanied by intention is like excellent gold, because the intention for benefit and happiness does not undergo deterioration. That accompanied by practice is like the bright crescent moon, because it moves toward the increase of wholesome qualities. That accompanied by superior intention is like fire, because just as fire [increases] with the distinction of fuel, so it progressively attains higher distinctions. For superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is the intention for higher attainment. That accompanied by the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is like a great treasure, because it satisfies immeasurable beings with material enjoyment and is inexhaustible. That accompanied by the perfection of moral discipline (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is like a jewel mine, because all the jewels of qualities arise from it. That accompanied by the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is like the ocean, because it is unshakeable by all assaults of the undesirable. That accompanied by the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is like a diamond, because of its firmness and indestructibility. That accompanied by the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is like the king of mountains, because of its immovability and freedom from distraction. That accompanied by the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is like the king of medicines, because it pacifies the disease of all afflictive and cognitive obscurations. That accompanied by the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) resembles a great friend, because it does not neglect beings in any circumstance. That accompanied by supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>) is like a wish-fulfilling gem, because of the accomplishment of results in accordance with [beings'] faith. That accompanied by the means of gathering [disciples] (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) is like the sun, because it ripens the harvest of those to be trained. That accompanied by the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) is like the sweet song of a <s>gandharva</s>, because it teaches the Dharma that attracts those to be trained. That accompanied by the refuges (<s>pratiśaraṇa</s>) is like a great king, because it is a cause of non-destruction. That accompanied by the accumulations of merit and knowledge is like a storehouse, because it is a treasury of vast accumulations of merit and knowledge. That accompanied by the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) is like the great royal highway, because it is traversed and followed by all noble individuals. That accompanied by <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is like a vehicle, because it conveys [one] comfortably. That accompanied by <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) and eloquence is like a <s>gandharva</s> [city], because of the similarity of retaining heard and unheard meanings of the Dharma inexhaustibly, like retaining water that springs forth inexhaustibly. That accompanied by the summary of the Dharma is like the sound of joy, because it is pleasant to hear for those to be trained who desire liberation. That accompanied by the one-way path is like the current of a river, because it flows spontaneously. On the one-way path, upon attaining patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena, there is one-wayness for <s>bodhisattvas</s> on that stage, because their beneficial activity is undifferentiated. That accompanied by skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is like a cloud, because all activity for the welfare of beings is dependent on it, from the display of dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth — just as all the prosperity of the vessel-world comes from clouds. And this <s>cittotpāda</s> (generation of the mind) with twenty-two similes should be understood by following the letter of the noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>.

body.text: cittānutpādaparibhāṣāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the reproach of not generating the mind:

children.translated_text: From the mind aimed at the benefit of others, from obtaining the means for that, from seeing the true nature of the meaning of the great purpose —

children.text: mahārhacittodayavarjitā janāḥ śamaṃ gamiṣyanti vihāya tatsukham || Msa_4.21 ||
children.translated_text: people who are devoid of the arising of such a precious mind will attain peace only by abandoning that happiness. || Msa_4.21 ||

body.text: tena cittotpādena varjitāḥ sattvāścaturvidhaṃ sukhaṃ na labhante yadbodhisattvānāṃ parārthacintanātsukham | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 19

children.text: ) yacca parārthopāyalābhāt | yacca mahābhisaṃdhyarthasaṃdarśanāt gambhīramahāyānasvato[sūtrā]bhiprāyikārthavibodhataḥ | yacca paramatattvasya dharmanairātmyasya saṃdarśanātsukham |
children.translated_text: ) the happiness from obtaining the means for the welfare of others; the happiness from seeing the meaning of the great purpose — that is, from awakening to the intended meaning of the profound <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras; and the happiness from seeing the ultimate reality, the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>).

body.translated_text: Beings who are devoid of that generation of the mind do not obtain fourfold happiness: the happiness that comes from <s>bodhisattvas</s>' thinking of the welfare of others; (

body.text: cittotpādapraśaṃsāyāṃ durgatiparikhedanirbhayatāmupādāya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse in praise of the generation of the mind, with regard to fearlessness regarding distress in the lower realms:

children.translated_text: From the very arising of the excellent mind, the wise one's mind is well-restrained from infinite misdeeds;

children.text: sukhena duḥkhena ca modate sadā śubhī kṛpāluśca vivardhana[yan] dvayam || Msa_4.22 ||
children.translated_text: one always rejoices through happiness and through suffering, being virtuous and compassionate, cultivating both. || Msa_4.22 ||

body.text: tasya cittavarasya sahodayābdodhisattvasya susaṃvṛtaṃ cittaṃ bhavatyanantasattvādhiṣṭhānād duṣkṛtādato 'sya durgatito bhayaṃ na bhavati | sa ca dvayaṃ vardhayan śubhaṃ ca karma-kṛpāṃ ca nityaṃ ca śubhī bhavati kṛpāluśca tena sadā modate | sukhenāpi śubhitvāt | duḥkhenāpi parārthakriyānimittena kṛpālutvāt | ato 'sya bahukarttavyatāparikhedādapi bhayaṃ na bhavati |
body.translated_text: From the very arising of that excellent mind, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s mind is well-restrained from misdeeds due to the commitment to infinite beings — therefore there is no fear of the lower realms. And cultivating both — virtue and compassion — one is always virtuous and always compassionate, and therefore always rejoices: through happiness, because of being virtuous; through suffering, because of being compassionate on account of the activity for others' welfare. Therefore, there is no fear even from the weariness of having much to do.

body.text: akaraṇasaṃvaralābhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on obtaining the restraint of non-action [in evil]:

children.translated_text: When one who is indifferent to one's own body and life undergoes supreme exertion for the benefit of others,

children.text: paropaghātena tathāvidhaḥ kathaṃ sa duṣkṛte karmaṇi saṃpravartsyati || Msa_4.23 ||
children.translated_text: how could such a one, through harm to others, engage in evil deeds? || Msa_4.23 ||

body.text: asya piṇḍārtho yasya para eva priyataro nātmā parārthaṃ svaśarīrajīvite nirapekṣatvāt | sa kathamātmārthaṃ paropaghātena duṣkṛte karmaṇi pravartsyatīti |
body.translated_text: The summary meaning of this: For one to whom others are dearer than oneself, due to indifference to one's own body and life for the sake of others — how would such a one engage in evil deeds through harm to others for one's own sake?

body.text: cittāvyāvṛttau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the non-reversal of the mind:

children.translated_text: Seeing all phenomena as illusion-like, and rebirths as like a pleasure-garden excursion,

children.text: kleśācca duḥkhācca bibheti nāsau saṃpattikāle 'tha vipattikāle || Msa_4.24 ||
