children.translated_text: that one fears neither afflictions nor suffering, whether in times of prosperity or adversity. || Msa_4.24 ||

children.text: svakā guṇāḥ sattvahitācca modaḥ saṃcintyajanmarddhivikurvitaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: One's own qualities and delight in the welfare of beings, intentional birth, supernatural transformation,
adornment, nourishment, the highest ground, play and delight — these belong to those whose nature is constant compassion. || Msa_4.25 ||

body.text: māyopamasarvadharmekṣaṇātsa bodhisattvaḥ saṃpattikāle kleśebhyo na vibheti | udyānayātropamopapattīkṣaṇāt vipattikāle duḥkhānna bibheti | tasya kuto bhayābdodhicittaṃ vyāvartiṣyate | api ca svaguṇā maṇḍanaṃ bodhisattvānām | parahitātprītirbhojanam | saṃcintyopapattirudyānabhūmiḥ | ṛddhivikurvitaṃ krīḍāratirbodhisattvānāmevāsti | nābodhisattvānām | teṣāṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ vyāvartiṣyate |
body.translated_text: Because of seeing all phenomena as illusion-like, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not fear afflictions in times of prosperity. Because of seeing rebirths as like a pleasure-garden excursion, one does not fear suffering in times of adversity. From what fear would the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) be reversed? Moreover, one's own qualities are the adornment of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Delight from the welfare of others is nourishment. Intentional rebirth is the pleasure-ground. Supernatural transformation is play and delight — these belong only to <s>bodhisattvas</s>, not to non-<s>bodhisattvas</s>. How would their mind be reversed?

body.text: duḥkhatrāsapratiṣedhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the refutation of fear of suffering:

children.translated_text: For one who is striving for the benefit of others, whose nature is compassion, even <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) becomes delightful.

children.text: kutaḥ punastrasyati tādṛśo bhavan parāśrayairduḥkhasamudbhavairbhave || Msa_4.26 ||
children.translated_text: How then would such a one be frightened in worldly existence by sufferings that arise from dependence on others? || Msa_4.26 ||

body.text: api ca yasya parārthamudyogavataḥ karuṇātmakatvādavīcirapi ramyaḥ sa kathaṃ parārthanimittairduḥkhotpādairbhave punastrāsamāpatsyate | yato 'sya duḥkhāttrāsaḥ syāccittasya vyāvṛttirbhavati |
body.translated_text: Moreover, for one who is striving for the benefit of others, for whom even <s>Avīci</s> is delightful because of having compassion as one's nature — how would such a one be frightened again by the arising of sufferings in worldly existence that are occasioned by the welfare of others? Since fear of suffering would cause the reversal of the mind.

body.text: sattvopekṣāpratiṣedhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the refutation of neglecting beings:

children.translated_text: For one whose self is constantly heated by the teacher of great compassion, whose mind is scorched by the sufferings of others,

children.text: parasya kṛtye samupasthite punaḥ paraiḥ samādāpanato 'tilajjanā || Msa_4.27 ||
children.translated_text: when the duty toward others has arisen, to be prompted to it by others would be deeply shameful. || Msa_4.27 ||

body.text: yasya mahākaruṇācāryeṇa nityoṣitaḥ ātmā paraduḥkhaiśca duḥkhitaṃ cetastasyotpanne parārthaṃ karaṇīye yadi paraiḥ kalyāṇamitraiḥ samādāpanā kartavyā bhavati atilajjanā |
body.translated_text: For one whose self is constantly heated by the teacher of great compassion, and whose mind is distressed by the sufferings of others — when a duty for the welfare of others has arisen, if prompting by other spiritual friends is necessary, that is deeply shameful.

body.text: kauśīdyaparibhāṣāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the reproach of laziness:

children.translated_text: Having placed the lofty burden of beings upon one's head, the foremost being does not shine while proceeding slackly;
being excessively bound by the various bonds of self and others, one should exert effort a hundredfold. || Msa_4.28 ||

body.text: śirasi mahāntaṃ sattvabhāraṃ vinidhāya bodhisattvaḥ śithilaṃ parākramamāṇo na śobhate | śataguṇaṃ hi sa vīryaṃ kartumarhati śrāvakavīryāt tathā hi svaparabandhanairvividhairatyarthaṃ baddhaḥ kleśakarmajanmasvabhāvaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Having placed the great burden of beings upon one's head, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not shine while exerting oneself slackly. For one should make effort a hundredfold greater than the effort of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), since one is excessively bound by the various bonds of self and others — those having the nature of afflictions, actions, and births.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre cittotpādādhikāraścaturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fourth chapter on the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) ||

body.text: pañcamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Fifth chapter:

body.text: pratipattilakṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the characteristic of practice:

children.translated_text: Having a great basis, great undertaking, and the nature of the arising of great fruit —
the practice of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) is accepted [as having] always great giving, great forbearance, and the activity of accomplishing great purposes. || Msa_5.1 ||

body.text: tatra mahāśrayā cittotpādāśrayatvāt | mahārambhā svaparārthārambhāt | mahāphalodayā mahābodhiphalatvāt | ata eva yathākramaṃ mahādānā sarvasattvopādānāt | mahādhivāsanā sarvaduḥkhādhivāsanāt | mahārthasaṃpādanakṛtyakārikā vipulasattvārthasaṃpādanāt |
body.translated_text: Among these: having a great basis, because of being based on the generation of the mind; great undertaking, because of undertaking the welfare of self and others; having the arising of great fruit, because of having great awakening as its fruit. Hence, in that order: great giving, because of the adoption of all beings; great forbearance, because of enduring all suffering; and the activity of accomplishing great purposes, because of accomplishing the vast welfare of beings.

body.text: svaparārthanirviśeṣatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the non-difference of the welfare of self and others:

children.translated_text: Having attained an attitude equal to oneself toward others, or having attained a desire [to regard] others as more excellent than oneself,

children.text: tathātmano 'nyārthaviśiṣṭasaṃjñinaḥ svakārthatā kā katamā parārthatā || Msa_5.2 ||
children.translated_text: for one who perceives the welfare of others as more distinguished than one's own — what is self-interest and what is the interest of others? || Msa_5.2 ||

body.text: paratrātmasamānacittatāṃ labdhvādhimuktito vā sāṃketikacittotpādalābhe jñānato vā pāramārthikacittotpādalābhe | ātmato vā punaḥ paratra viśiṣṭatarāmiṣṭatāṃ labdhvā tenaiva ca kāraṇenātmanaḥ parārthe viśiṣṭasaṃjñino bodhisattvasya kaḥ svārthaḥ parārtho vā | nirviśeṣaṃ hi tasyobhayamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having attained an attitude equal to oneself toward others — either through faith, in the attainment of the conventional generation of the mind, or through knowledge, in the attainment of the ultimate generation of the mind. Or furthermore, having attained the desire to regard others as more excellent than oneself — for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who, for that very reason, perceives the welfare of others as more distinguished than one's own, what is self-interest or the interest of others? For both are without distinction for such a one — this is the meaning.

body.text: parārthaviśeṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the distinction of the welfare of others:

children.text: paratra loko na tathātinirdayaḥ pravartate tāpanakarmaṇāripau |
children.translated_text: In the world, even an enemy does not proceed so exceedingly cruelly with the act of tormenting toward a foe,

children.text: yathā parārthaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhatāpane kṛpātmakaḥ svātmani saṃpravartate || Msa_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: as the compassionate one proceeds toward oneself in the intense torment of suffering for the sake of others. || Msa_5.3 ||

body.text: yathā svātmanaḥ parārtho viśiṣyate tatsādhayati parārthamātmano 'tyarthaṃ saṃtāpanāt |
body.translated_text: That the welfare of others is more distinguished than one's own self-interest — this he establishes: because of exceedingly tormenting oneself for the sake of others.

body.text: parārthapratipattivibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the classification of the practice for the welfare of others:

children.translated_text: For those established in inferior, middling, and superior spiritual dispositions: excellent teaching, attraction, and introduction;
training in the meaning, ripening in the wholesome, and likewise instruction, stability, wisdom, and liberation. || Msa_5.4 ||
Likewise, the attainment of distinguished qualities, noble birth, prediction, and consecration;

children.text: tathāgatajñānamanuttaraṃ padaṃ parārtha eṣa tryadhiko daśātmakaḥ || Msa_5.5 ||
children.translated_text: the unsurpassed knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the supreme state — this welfare of others is tenfold plus three. || Msa_5.5 ||

body.text: trividhe sattvanikāye hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭagotrastheḥ trayodaśavidho bodhisattvasya parārthaḥ | sudeśanānuśāsanyādeśanāpratihāryābhyām | āvarjanā ṛddhiprātihāyerṇa | avatāraṇā śāsanābhyupagamanāt | vinītirarthe 'vatīrṇānāṃ saṃśayacchedanam | paripācanā kuśale | avavādaścittasthitiḥ prajñāvimuktiḥ, abhijñādibhirviśeṣakairguṇaiḥ samudāgamaḥ | tathāgatakule janma, aṣṭabhyāṃ bhūmau vyākaraṇaṃ daśamyāmabhiṣekaśca | saha tathāgatajñānenetyeṣa triṣu gotrastheṣu yathāyogaṃ trayodaśavidhaḥ parārtho bodhisattvasya |
body.translated_text: For three types of sentient beings — those established in inferior, middling, and distinguished spiritual lineages — the welfare of others performed by the <s>bodhisattva</s> is thirteenfold: excellent teaching through instruction and miraculous display; attraction through supernatural powers; introduction through acceptance of the teaching; training consists in the removal of doubts for those who have entered; ripening in wholesome qualities; instruction, mental stability, wisdom, and liberation; the attainment of distinguished qualities through supernatural knowledges and other special qualities; birth in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; prediction on the eighth stage, and consecration on the tenth — together with the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, this thirteenfold welfare of others performed by the <s>bodhisattva</s> applies to those established in the three lineages in their respective ways.

body.text: parārthapratipattisaṃpattau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the accomplishment of the practice for the welfare of others:

children.translated_text: Teaching that is suited to beings and not contrary, and that is without pride, without possessiveness, discerning,

children.text: kṣamā ca dāntā ca sudūragākṣayā jinātmajānāṃ pratipattiruttamā || Msa_5.6 ||
children.translated_text: patient, self-controlled, far-reaching, and inexhaustible — this is the supreme practice of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_5.6 ||

body.text: yathāsau parārthapatipattiḥ saṃpannā bhavati tathā saṃdarśayati | kathaṃ cāsau saṃpannā bhavati | yadi gotrasthajanānurūpāviparītā ca deśanā bhavati | anunnatā cāvarjanā | amamā cāvatāraṇā | na ṛddhayā manyate na cāvatāritānsattvānmamāyati | vicakṣaṇā cārthe vinītipratipattirbhavati | kṣamā ca śubhe paripācanāpratipattiḥ | dāntā cāvavādādipratipattiḥ | na hyadānto 'vavādādiṣu pareṣāṃ samarthaḥ | sudūragā ca kulodayādipratipattiḥ | na hyadūragatayā pratipattyā kulodayādayaḥ pareṣāṃ kartuṃ śakyāḥ | sarvā caiṣā, parārthapratipattirbodhisattvānāmakṣayā bhavatyabhyupagatasattvākṣayatvādato 'pi saṃpannā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: He shows how that practice for the welfare of others becomes accomplished. And how does it become accomplished? When the teaching is suited to those established in the lineages and is not contrary; when the attraction is without pride; when the introduction is without possessiveness — one does not take pride in supernatural powers, nor does one regard as 'mine' the beings who have been introduced; when the practice of training in the meaning is discerning; when the practice of ripening in the wholesome is patient; when the practice of instruction and so forth is self-controlled — for indeed, one who is not self-controlled is not capable of giving instruction and the like to others; when the practice of noble birth and so forth is far-reaching — for indeed, without a far-reaching practice, noble birth and the rest cannot be accomplished for others. And all this practice for the welfare of others of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is inexhaustible, because beings whom they have undertaken [to help] are inexhaustible — thus it should be understood as accomplished from this [perspective] as well.

body.text: pratipattiviśeṣaṇe dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the distinction of practice:

children.text: mahābhaye kāmijanaḥ pravartate cale viparyāsasukhe bhavapriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The one who craves sense-pleasures engages in great danger; the one who loves existence [delights] in the unstable, perverted happiness of becoming;

children.text: pratisvamādhipraśame śamapriyaḥ sadā tu sarvādhiga[śa]me kṛpātmakaḥ || Msa_5.7 ||
children.translated_text: the one who loves peace [seeks] the individual pacification of one's own afflictions; but the one whose nature is compassion [seeks] always the complete pacification of all. || Msa_5.7 ||

children.text: jano vimūḍhaḥ svasukhārthamudyataḥ sadā tadaprāpya paraiti duḥkhatām |
children.translated_text: The deluded person, always striving for one's own happiness, never attaining it, goes to suffering;

children.text: sadā tu dhīro hi parārthamudyato dvayārthamādhāya paraiti nirvṛtim || Msa_5.8 ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one, always striving for the welfare of others, having accomplished both purposes, goes to bliss. || Msa_5.8 ||

body.text: tatra kāmānāṃ mahābhayatvaṃ bahukāyikacaitasikaduḥkhadurgatigamanahetutvāt | calaṃ viparyāsasukhaṃ rūpārūpyabhavapriyāṇāmanityatvātparamārthaduḥkhatvācca saṃskāraduḥkhatayā | ādhayaḥ kleśā veditavyā duḥkhādhānāt | vimūḍho janaḥ sadā svasukhārthaṃ pratipannaḥ sukhaṃ nāpnoti duḥkhamevāpnoti | bodhisattvastu parārthaṃ pratipannaḥ svaparārthaṃ saṃpādya nirvṛtisukhaṃ prāpnotyayamasyāparaḥ pratipattiviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, sense-pleasures are of great danger because they are the cause of much physical and mental suffering and of going to lower rebirths. The unstable, perverted happiness of those who love the realms of form and formlessness is impermanent and ultimately suffering through the suffering of formations. Afflictions (<s>ādhi</s>) should be understood as <s>kleśas</s> (mental defilements), because they impose suffering. The deluded person, always engaged in the pursuit of one's own happiness, does not attain happiness but attains only suffering. But the <s>bodhisattva</s>, engaged in the welfare of others, having accomplished the welfare of both self and others, attains the bliss of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) — this is another distinction of practice.

body.text: gocarapariṇāmane ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the transformation of the domain [of experience]:

children.text: yathā yathā hyakṣavicitragocare pravartate cāragato jinātmajaḥ |
children.translated_text: In whatever way the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, engaged in conduct, operates in the varied domain of the senses,

children.text: tathā tathā yuktasamānatāpadairhitāyā sattveṣvabhisaṃskaroti tat || Msa_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: in that very way, through appropriate and corresponding expressions, he performs what is beneficial for beings. || Msa_5.9 ||

body.text: yena yena prakāreṇa cakṣurādīndriyagocare vicitre bodhisattvaḥ pravartate | īryāpathavyāpāracāre vartamānastena tena prakāreṇa saṃbaddhasādṛśyavacanairhitārthaṃ sattveṣu tatsarvamabhisaṃskaroti | yathā gocarapariśuddhisūtre vistareṇa nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: In whatever manner the <s>bodhisattva</s> operates in the varied domain of the senses such as sight and so on — while engaged in the conduct of the postures and activities — in that very manner, through connected and analogous expressions for beneficial purposes, he performs all that toward beings. As has been taught extensively in the <s>Gocarapariśuddhisūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Purification of the Domain).

body.text: sattveṣvakṣāntipratiṣedhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the prohibition of impatience toward beings:

children.translated_text: The wise one does not become hostile toward people whose minds are always made unfree by their faults,

children.text: akāmakāreṇa hi viprapattayo jane bhavantīti kṛpāvivṛddhitaḥ || Msa_5.10 ||
children.translated_text: for transgressions among people occur involuntarily — thus, from the growth of compassion. || Msa_5.10 ||

body.text: sadā kleśairasvatantrīkṛtacetane jane na saṃdoṣamupaiti bodhisattvaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam | akāmakāreṇaiṣāṃ vipratipattayo bhavantīti viditvā karuṇāvṛddhigamanāt |
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> does not become hostile toward people whose minds are always made unfree by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Why? Because, knowing that their transgressions occur involuntarily, compassion increases.

body.text: pratipattimāhātmye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the greatness of practice:

children.translated_text: This very practice, overcoming all the realms and destinies of existence,
following supreme peace, increasing with manifold groups of qualities, always embracing the world with compassionate intention. || Msa_5.11 ||

body.text: caturvidhaṃ māhātmyaṃ saṃdarśayati | abhibhavamāhātmyaṃ sakalaṃ bhavatrayaṃ gatiṃ ca pañcavidhāmabhibhūyagamanāt | yathoktaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ, rūpaṃ cetsubhūta[te] bhāvo 'bhaviṣyannābhāvo nedaṃ mahāyānaṃ sadevamānuṣāsuralokamabhibhūya niryāsyatīti vistaraḥ | nirvṛtimāhātmyamapratiṣṭhanirvāṇānugatatvāt | guṇavṛddhimāhātmyaṃ sattvāparityāgamāhātmyaṃ ceti |
body.translated_text: He shows the fourfold greatness: the greatness of overcoming — because of overcoming the entire three realms of existence and the five destinies; as stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: '<s>Subhūti</s>, if form were a real entity or a non-entity, this <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth overcoming the world of gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>' — and so on in detail. The greatness of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) — because of following the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The greatness of the increase of qualities. And the greatness of not abandoning beings.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre pratipattyadhikāraḥ pañcamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fifth chapter on practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) ||

body.text: ṣaṣṭho 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Sixth chapter:

body.text: paramārthalakṣaṇavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the analysis of the characteristic of ultimate reality:

children.text: na sanna cāsanna tathā na cānyathā na jāyate vyeti na cā[nā]vahīyate |
children.translated_text: It is neither existent nor non-existent, nor otherwise; it neither arises nor ceases, nor diminishes;

children.text: na vardhate nāpi viśudhyate punarviśudhyate tatparamārthalakṣaṇam || Msa_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: it neither increases nor is purified, yet it is purified — that is the characteristic of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). || Msa_6.1 ||

body.text: advayārtho hi paramārthaḥ | tamadvayārthaṃ pañcabhirākāraiḥ saṃdarśayati | na satparikalpitaparatantralakṣaṇābhyāṃ, na cāsatpariniṣpannalakṣaṇena | na tathā parikalpitaparatantrābhyāṃ pariniṣpannasyaikatvābhāvāt | na cānyathā tābhyamevānyatvābhāvāt | na jāyate na ca vyetyanabhisaṃskṛtatvāddharmadhātoḥ | na hīyate na ca vardhate saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣayornirodhotpāde tad[thā]vasthatvāt | na viśudhyati prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭatvāt na ca na viśudhyati āgantukopakleśavigamāt | ityetatpañcavibhamadvayalakṣaṇaṃ paramārthalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: For the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) is the meaning of non-duality (<s>advaya</s>). He shows that meaning of non-duality through five aspects: it is not existent — through the characteristics of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>); it is not non-existent — through the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>); it is not the same as those [the imagined and dependent] — because of the absence of identity of the perfected with the imagined and the dependent; it is not otherwise — because of the absence of difference from them as well; it neither arises nor ceases — because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) is unconditioned; it neither diminishes nor increases — because in the decline and arising of the defilement and purification aspects, it remains the same; it is not purified — because it is by nature undefiled; yet it is not not purified — because of the removal of adventitious defilements. Thus, this characteristic of ultimate reality should be understood as the characteristic of non-duality with five divisions.

body.text: ātmadṛṣṭiviparyāsapratiṣedhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the refutation of the perversion of the view of self:

children.text: na cātmadṛṣṭiḥ svayamātmalakṣaṇā na cāpi duḥsaṃsthitatā vilakṣaṇā |
children.translated_text: The view of self is not itself of the nature of a self, nor is the ill-constituted [basis of the self-view] of a different nature;

children.text: dvayānna cānyad bhrama eṣata[tū]ditastataśca mokṣo bhramamātrasaṃkṣayaḥ || Msa_6.2 ||
children.translated_text: and apart from these two there is no other [self] — this delusion has arisen [from them], and therefore liberation is merely the cessation of delusion. || Msa_6.2 ||

body.text: na tāvadātmadṛṣṭirevātmalakṣaṇā | nāpi duḥsaṃsthitatā | tathā hi sā vilakṣaṇā ātmalakṣaṇātparikalpitāt | sā punaḥ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ kleśadauṣṭhulyaprabhāvitatvāt | nāpyato dvayādanyadātmalakṣaṇamupapadyate | tasmānnāstyātmā | bhrama eṣa tūtpanno yeyamātmadṛṣṭistasmādeva cātmābhāvonmokṣo 'pi bhramamātrasaṃkṣayo veditavyaḥ, na tu kaścinmuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: The view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) itself is not of the nature of a self. Nor is the ill-constituted [basis] — for it is of a different nature from the imagined self-nature. And that [ill-constituted basis] is the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>), because they are produced through the potency of the defilements' dysfunction. Nor is any other self-nature established apart from these two. Therefore, the self does not exist. This delusion has arisen — namely this view of self — and therefore liberation, which is the absence of self, should be understood as merely the cessation of delusion, not that anyone is actually liberated.

body.text: viparyāsaparibhāṣāyāṃ dvau ślaukau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the explanation of perversion:

children.text: kathaṃ jano vibhramamātrāmāśritaḥ paraiti duḥkhaprakṛtiṃ na saṃtatām |
children.translated_text: How does a person, relying merely on delusion, not go beyond the continuous nature of suffering?

children.text: avedako vedaka eva duḥkhito na duḥkhito dharmamayo na tanmayaḥ || Msa_6.3 ||
children.translated_text: Not knowing, yet being one who experiences, one is afflicted by suffering; not afflicted by suffering, being composed of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), yet not composed of that [self]. || Msa_6.3 ||
How can a person, regarding things that arise from dependent origination, which operate before one's very eyes, resort to the view that they are caused by another?
What kind of darkness is this, whereby one who does not see [reality] perceives the existent and the non-existent? || Msa_6.4 ||

body.text: kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ loko bhrāntimātramātmadarśanaṃ niḥśritya satatānubaddhaṃ duḥkhasvabhāvaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ na paśyati | avedako jñānena tasyā duḥkhaprakṛteḥ | vedako 'nubhavena (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 25

children.text: ) duḥkhasyā[sya] duḥkhito duḥkhasyāprahīṇatvāt | na duḥkhiuto duḥkhayuktasyātmano 'satvāt | dharmamayo dharmamātratvāt pudgalanairātmyena | na ca dharmamayo dharmanairātmyena | yadā ca loko bhāvānāṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyakṣaṃ paśyati taṃ taṃ pratyayaṃ pratītya te te bhāvā bhavantīti | tatkathametāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ śrayate 'nyakāritaṃ darśanādikaṃ na pratītyasamutpannamiti | katamo 'yamīdṛśastamaḥ prakāro lokasya yadvidyamānaṃ pratītyasamutpādamavipaśyannavidyamānamātmānaṃ nirīkṣate | śakyaṃ hi nāma tamasā vidyamānamadraṣṭuṃ syānna tvavidyamānaṃ draṣṭhumiti |
children.translated_text: ) suffering, one is afflicted — because suffering is not abandoned; yet not [truly] afflicted — because of the non-existence of a self that possesses suffering; composed of <s>dharmas</s> — because of being mere phenomena, through the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>); yet not composed of <s>dharmas</s> — through the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>). And when the world directly perceives the dependent origination of things — that those various things arise in dependence on those various conditions — how then does it resort to this view that seeing and the like are caused by another and are not dependently arisen? What kind of darkness is this of the world, whereby not seeing the existing dependent origination, it perceives a non-existing self? For it is possible that due to darkness one might not see what exists, but it should not be that one sees what does not exist.

body.translated_text: How indeed does this world, relying on the view of self which is merely delusion, not see the constantly bound suffering-nature of conditioned formations? Not knowing through wisdom that nature of suffering; yet being one who experiences (

body.text: asatyātmani śamajanmayoge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the connection of cessation and birth when the self is non-existent:

children.text: ta cāntaraṃ kiṃcana vidyate 'nayoḥ sadarthavṛttyā śamajanmanoriha |
children.translated_text: There is no difference whatsoever between these two — cessation and birth — when considered in terms of ultimate reality;

children.text: tathāpi janmakṣayato vidhīyate śamasya lābhaḥ śubhakarmakāriṇām || Msa_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: yet the attainment of cessation is accomplished through the cessation of birth for those who perform wholesome actions. || Msa_6.5 ||

body.text: na cāsti saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ kiṃcinnānākaraṇaṃ paramārthavṛttyā nairātmyasya samatayā | tathāpi janmakṣayānmokṣaprāptirbhavatyeva śubhakarmakāriṇāṃ ye mokṣamārgaṃ bhāvayanti | viparyāsaparibhāṣāṃ kṛtvā-
body.translated_text: There is no distinguishing factor whatsoever between <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) from the standpoint of ultimate reality, because of the equality of selflessness. Yet, the attainment of liberation through the cessation of birth does occur for those who perform wholesome actions — those who cultivate the path of liberation. Having explained the perversion —

body.text: tatpratipakṣapāramārthikajñānapraveśe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on entry into the ultimate knowledge that is the antidote to that:

children.text: saṃbhṛtya saṃbhāramanantapāraṃ jñānasya puṇyasya ca bodhisattvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having accumulated the boundless accumulations of knowledge and merit, the <s>bodhisattva</s>,
through well-established certainty from contemplation of phenomena, goes beyond the conceptual proliferations to the apprehension of meaning. || Msa_6.6 ||

children.text: arthānsa vijñāya ca jalpamātrān saṃtiṣṭhate tannibhacittamātre |
children.translated_text: And having understood those meanings as mere conceptual designations, one abides in mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), which resembles that;
and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) becomes directly perceived — being free from the characteristic of duality. || Msa_6.7 ||

children.text: nāstīti cittātparametya buddhyā cittasya nāstitvamupaiti tasmāt |
children.translated_text: Having transcended mind with the understanding 'it does not exist,' therefore the non-existence of mind is realized;
having realized the non-existence of both [subject and object], the wise one abides in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, which is the domain of that [non-dual knowledge]. || Msa_6.8 ||
Through the power of the non-conceptual knowledge of the wise one, which always follows everywhere,

children.text: tadāśrayo gahvaradoṣasaṃcayo mahāgadeneva viṣaṃ nirasyate || Msa_6.9 ||
children.translated_text: the accumulation of deep faults — the support of that [ignorance] — is expelled, as poison is [expelled] by a great antidote. || Msa_6.9 ||

body.text: ekena saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāratvaṃ dharmacintāsuviniśri[ści]tatvaṃ samādhi[dhiṃ]niśrityabhāvanānmanojalpācca teṣāṃ dharmāṇāmarthaprakhyānāvagamāttatpraveśaṃ darśayati | asaṃkhyeyaprabhedakālaṃ pāramasya (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 26

children.text: ) paripūraṇamityanantapāram | dvitīyena manojalpamātrānarthānviditvā tadābhāse cittamātre 'vasthānamiyaṃ bodhisattvasya nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthā | tataḥ pareṇa dharmadhātoḥ pratyakṣato['va?] gamane dvayalakṣaṇena viyukto grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇena | iyaṃ darśanamārgāvasthā | tṛtīyena yathāsau dharmadhātuḥ pratyakṣatāmeti tad darśayati | kathaṃ cāsau dharmadhātuḥ pratyakṣatāmeti | cittādanyadālambanaṃ grāhyaṃ nāstītyavagamya buddhyā tasyāpi cittamātrasya nāstitvāvagamanaṃ grāhya[ā]bhāve grāhakābhāvāt | dvaye cāsya [dvayasyāsya?] nāstitvaṃ viditvā dharmadhātāvavasthānamatadgatirgrāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇābhyāṃ rahitaṃ evaṃ dharmadhātuḥ pratyakṣatāmeti | caturthena bhāvanāmārgāvasthāyāmāśrayaparivartanāt pāramārthikajñānapraveśaṃ darśayati | sadā sarvatra samatānugatenāvikalpajñānabalena yatra tatsamatānugataṃ paratantre svabhāve tadāśrayasya dūrānupraviṣṭasya doṣasaṃcasya dauṣṭhulyalakṣaṇasya mahāgadeneva viṣasya nirasanāt |
children.translated_text: ) the fulfillment [of bodhisattva practice] is without limit. By the second [verse], having understood that mental fabrication alone is without purpose, the abiding in mind-only in its appearance — this is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s stage of penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). Then, by what follows, in the direct realization of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), one is separated from the characteristic of duality — the characteristic of grasped and grasper. This is the stage of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). By the third [verse], he shows how that <s>dharmadhātu</s> is directly realized. And how is that <s>dharmadhātu</s> directly realized? By understanding that there is no apprehended object (<s>grāhya</s>) apart from mind, and then by the intellect's understanding of the non-existence of that mind-only itself — since in the absence of the apprehended, the apprehender is also absent. And having understood the non-existence of both, the abiding in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is free from the characteristics of grasped and grasper — thus the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is directly realized. By the fourth [verse], he shows the entry into ultimate knowledge (<s>pāramārthikajñāna</s>) through the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivartana</s>) on the stage of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). Through the power of non-conceptual knowledge (<s>avikalpajñāna</s>) that follows equality everywhere at all times — in the dependent nature (<s>paratantra svabhāva</s>) where that equality is followed, there is the removal of the deeply embedded mass of faults, having the characteristic of afflictive obstruction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), like a great disease of poison, from the basis (<s>āśraya</s>).

body.translated_text: With one [verse], he shows entry into that through having accumulated the accumulations, through well-established certainty in the contemplation of phenomena, relying on <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) for cultivation, and through understanding the manifestation of the meaning of those phenomena beyond conceptual proliferation. The [accumulation spans] a duration of innumerable divisions (

body.text: paramārthajñānamāhātmye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the greatness of ultimate knowledge (<s>paramārthajñāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Well-established in the excellent Dharma laid down by the <s>Muni</s> (Sage), having directed the intellect to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> together with its root,
understanding all recollection and cognition to be mere conceptual construction, the steadfast one swiftly crosses to the far shore of the ocean of qualities. || Msa_6.10 ||

body.text: buddhavihite sudharme suvyavasthāpite sa paramārthajñānapraviṣṭo bodhisattvaḥ saṃpiṇḍitadharmālambanasya mūlacittasya dharmadhātau matimupanividhāya yā smṛtirūpalabhyate tāṃ sarvāṃ smṛtipravṛttiṃ kalpanāmātrāmavagacchatyevaṃ guṇārṇavasya pāraṃbuddhatvamāśu vrajatītyetatparamārthajñānasya māhātmyam |
body.translated_text: That <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered ultimate knowledge, well-established in the excellent Dharma taught by the <s>Buddha</s>, having directed the intellect to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — the root consciousness that has the collected dharmas as its object — understands all that recollection which is obtained, all that activity of recollection, as mere conceptual construction. Thus one swiftly reaches the far shore of the ocean of qualities, which is Buddhahood — this is the greatness of ultimate knowledge.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre tattvādhikāraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixth chapter on reality (<s>tattvādhikāra</s>) ||

body.text: saptamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Seventh chapter:

body.text: prabhāvalakṣaṇavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the analysis of the characteristic of supernatural power (<s>prabhāva</s>):

children.translated_text: Knowledge of birth, speech, mind, wholesome and unwholesome [actions], their abodes, [and] the state of liberation — indirectly,

children.text: jñānaṃ hi sarvatragasaprabhedeṣvavyāhataṃ dhīragataḥ prabhāvaḥ || Msa_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: this knowledge, unobstructed in all domains with their divisions, is the supernatural power of the steadfast one. || Msa_7.1 ||

body.text: pareṣāmupapattau jñānaṃ cyutopapādābhijñā | vāci jñānaṃ divyaśrotrābhijñāyāṃ[yayā] vācaṃ tatra gatvopapannā bhāṣante | citte jñānaṃ cetaḥ paryāyābhijñā | pūrvaśubhāśubhādhāne jñānaṃ pūrvanivāsābhijñā | yatra vineyāstiṣṭhanti tatsthānagamanajñānaṃ ṛddhiviṣayābhijñā | niḥsaraṇe jñānamāsravakṣayābhijñā, yathā sattvā upapattito niḥsarantīti | eṣu ṣaṭsvartheṣu sarvatra laukadhātau saprabhedeṣu padāparokṣamavyāhataṃ jñānaṃ sa prabhāvo bodhisattvānāṃ ṣaḍabhijñāsaṃgṛhītaḥ | prabhāvalakṣaṇavibhāge svabhāvārthaṃ uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Knowledge regarding the birth of others is the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) of death and rebirth (<s>cyutopapāda</s>). Knowledge of speech is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), by which one [knows] the speech spoken by those who have gone and been reborn there. Knowledge of mind is the <s>abhijñā</s> of reading others' thoughts (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>). Knowledge of previous wholesome and unwholesome [karmic] deposits is the <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>). Knowledge of traveling to the place where those to be trained abide is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the domain of miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>). Knowledge of liberation is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) — that is, how beings are liberated from rebirth. Regarding these six objects, knowledge that is direct, unobstructed everywhere in all world-realms with their divisions — that is the supernatural power of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). In the analysis of the characteristic of supernatural power, the meaning of its intrinsic nature has been stated.

body.text: hetvarthamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the meaning of the cause:

children.translated_text: Having attained the supremely purified fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), through the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge,
through mental application according to proper arrangement, one reaches the supreme accomplishment of supernatural power. || Msa_7.2 ||

body.text: yena niśrayeṇa yena jñānena yena manasikāreṇa tasya prabhāvasya samudāgamastatsaṃdarśayati |
body.translated_text: He shows by what support, by what knowledge, and by what mental application the attainment of that supernatural power comes about.

body.text: phalārthamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the meaning of the fruit:

children.translated_text: By the noble, divine, incomparable, and <s>Brāhma</s> abodes, one always dwells magnificently;

children.text: buddhāṃśca satvāṃśca sa dikṣu gatvā saṃmānayatyānayate viśuddhim || Msa_7.3 ||
children.translated_text: and having gone to the <s>Buddhas</s> and beings in the [ten] directions, one honors [the Buddhas] and brings about purification [of beings]. || Msa_7.3 ||

body.text: trividhaṃ phalamasya prabhāvasya saṃdarśayati | ātmana āryādisukhavihāramatulyaṃ cotkṛṣṭaṃ ca lokadhātvantareṣu gatvā buddhānāṃ pūjanaṃ sattvānāṃ viśodhanaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: He shows the threefold fruit of this supernatural power: for oneself, the incomparable and supreme happiness of abiding in the noble and other [meditative states]; and having gone to other world-realms, the worship of <s>Buddhas</s> and the purification of beings.

body.text: karmārthaṃ ṣaḍvidhamārabhya catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses beginning with the sixfold meaning of action:

body.text: darśanakarma saṃdarśanakarma cārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the action of seeing and the action of displaying:

children.translated_text: One sees all world-realms with their beings, with their evolution and dissolution, as illusion-like;

children.text: saṃdarśayatyeva ca tānyatheṣṭaṃ vaśī vicitrairapi sa prakāraiḥ || Msa_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: and that master displays them just as desired, by various means as well. || Msa_7.4 ||

body.text: svayaṃ ca sarvalokadhātūnāṃ sasattvānāṃ savivartasaṃvartānāṃ māyopamatvadarśanāt | pareṣāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ tatsaṃdarśanāt | anyaiśca vicitraiḥ kampanajvalanādiprakāraiḥ | daśavaśitālābhāt | yathā daśabhūmike 'ṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau nirdiṣṭāḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of seeing all world-realms with their beings, with their evolution and involution, as illusion-like; because of displaying them to others as desired; and by other various means such as causing trembling and blazing; because of obtaining the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>) — as taught in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s> on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage).

body.text: raśmikarmārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the action of light-rays:

children.translated_text: By the emission of light-rays, one causes those greatly suffering in the lower realms to be reborn in heaven;
causing the palaces of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue to tremble brilliantly, one terrifies [them] together with <s>Māra</s>. || Msa_7.5 ||

body.text: dvividhaṃ raśmikarma saṃdarśayati | apāyopapannānāṃ ca prasādaṃ janayitvā svargopapādanam | mārabhavanānāṃ ca samārakāṇāṃ kampanodvejanam |
body.translated_text: He shows the twofold action of light-rays: generating faith in those reborn in the lower realms and causing their rebirth in heaven; and causing disturbance and alarm in <s>Māra</s>'s abodes together with <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: vikrīḍanakarma cārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the action of miraculous display (<s>vikrīḍana</s>):

children.translated_text: One displays immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>-sport in the midst of the foremost assembly;
and through supreme emanations (<s>nirmita</s>) with their purposeful births, one carries out the welfare of beings at all times. || Msa_7.6 ||

body.text: aprameyasamādhivikrīḍitasaṃdarśanāt buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalamadhye trividhena nirmāṇena sadā sattvārthakaraṇācca | trividhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ śilpakarmasthānanirmāṇam | vineyavaśenayatheṣṭopapattinirmāṇam | uttamanirmāṇaṃ ca tuṣitabhavanavāsādikam |
body.translated_text: Because of displaying immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>-sport in the midst of the <s>Buddha</s>'s assembly, and because of always accomplishing the welfare of beings through threefold emanation. The threefold emanation is: emanation of craft and skill in action; emanation of birth at will according to the disposition of those to be trained; and the supreme emanation, such as dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth.

body.text: kṣetrapariśuddhikarma ārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the action of purifying the [Buddha-]field:

children.translated_text: Through the mastery of knowledge, one attains the purification of the field for displaying it as desired;
and by causing the name of <s>Buddha</s> to be heard in [realms] where the name of <s>Buddha</s> does not exist, one transfers [beings] to another realm. || Msa_7.7 ||

body.text: dvividhapāpaviśodhanayā | bhājanapariśodhanayā jñānavaśitvādyatheṣṭaṃ sphaṭikavaidūryādimayabuddhakṣetrasaṃdarśanataḥ | sattvapariśodhanayā ca buddhanāmavirahiteṣu lokadhātuṣūpapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhanāmasaṃśrāvaṇayā prasādaṃ grāhayitvā tadavirahiteṣu lokadhātuṣūpapādanāt |
body.translated_text: Through the twofold purification of evil: by the purification of the vessel-world, through the mastery of knowledge, displaying as desired Buddha-fields made of crystal, <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and so forth; and by the purification of beings — causing beings reborn in world-realms devoid of the name of <s>Buddha</s> to hear the name of <s>Buddha</s>, generating faith in them, and causing their rebirth in world-realms that are not devoid of it.

body.text: yogārthamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the meaning of yoga (practice):

children.text: śakto bhavatyeva ca sattvapāke saṃjātapakṣaḥ śakuniryathaiva |
children.translated_text: One becomes capable indeed in the ripening of beings, just as a bird whose wings have grown;
one receives supreme praise from the <s>Buddha</s> and becomes one whose words are accepted by beings. || Msa_7.8 ||

body.text: trividhaṃ yogaṃ pradarśayati | sattvaparipācanaśaktiyogaṃ praśaṃsāyogamādeyavākyatāyogaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: He shows the threefold yoga: the yoga of the power to ripen beings, the yoga of [receiving] praise, and the yoga of being one whose words are accepted.

body.text: vṛttyarthamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the meaning of mode of operation (<s>vṛtti</s>):

children.text: ṣaḍdhāpyabhijñā trividhā ca vidyā aṣṭau vimokṣābhibhuvastathāṣṭau |
children.translated_text: The six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the three <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), the eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery),

children.text: daśāpi kṛtsnāyatanānyameyāḥ samādhayo dhīragataḥ prabhāvaḥ || Msa_7.9 ||
children.translated_text: the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases), and immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) — [these constitute] the supernatural power of the steadfast one. || Msa_7.9 ||

body.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ prabhedairbodhisattvasya prabhāvo vartate | abhijñāvidyāvimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanāpramāṇasamādhiprabhedaiḥ |
body.translated_text: The supernatural power of the <s>bodhisattva</s> operates through six divisions: the divisions of <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery), <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases), and immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations).

body.text: evaṃ ṣaḍarthena vibhāgalakṣaṇena prabhāvaṃ darśayitvā tanmāhātmyodbhāvanārthaṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus shown supernatural power through the analytical characteristic of sixfold meaning, a verse for the purpose of demonstrating its greatness:

children.text: sa hi paramavaśitvalabdhabuddhirjagadavaśaṃ svavaśe vidhāya nityam |
children.translated_text: For that one who has attained supreme mastery of wisdom, having always brought the world, which is not under its own control, under one's own control,
delighting solely in performing the welfare of others, the steadfast one moves through existences like a lion. || Msa_7.10 ||

body.text: trividhaṃ māhātmyaṃ darśayati | vaśitāmāhātmyaṃ svayaṃ paramajñānavaśitvaprāptyā kleśāsvavaśasya jagataḥ svavaśe sthāpanāt | abhiratimāhātmyaṃ sadā parahitakriyaikārāmatvāt | bhavanirbhayatāmāhātmyaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: He shows the threefold greatness: the greatness of mastery, by placing the world — which is under the power of afflictions and not under its own control — under one's own control, through one's own attainment of supreme knowledge-mastery; the greatness of delight, through always having sole delight in performing the welfare of others; and the greatness of fearlessness in existences.

body.text: || prabhāvādhikāraḥ mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre saptamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || The chapter on supernatural power (<s>prabhāvādhikāra</s>), the seventh in the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> ||

body.text: aṣṭamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Eighth chapter:

body.text: bodhisattvaparipāke saṃgrahaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A summary verse on the ripening of <s>bodhisattvas</s>:

children.text: rūciḥ prasādaḥ praśamo 'nukampanā kṣamātha medhā prabalatvameva ca |
children.translated_text: Inclination, faith, tranquility, compassion, patience, intelligence, strength,

children.text: ahāryatāṅgaiḥ samupetatā bhṛśaṃ jinātmaje tatparipākalakṣaṇam || Msa_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the quality of being unshakeable, being endowed with these limbs — in the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, this is the characteristic of ripening. || Msa_8.1 ||

body.text: rūcirmahāyānadeśanādharme, prasādastaddeśike, praśamaḥ kleśānām, anukampā sattveṣu, kṣamā duṣkaracaryāyāṃ, medhā grahaṇadhāraṇaprativedheṣu, prabalatvamadhigame, ahāryatā māraparapravādibhiḥ, prāhāṇikāṅgaiḥ samanvāgatatvam | bhṛśamiti rūcyādīnāmadhimātratvaṃ darśayati | eṣa samāsena bodhisattvānāṃ navaprakāra ātmaparipāko veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Inclination (<s>rūci</s>) is toward the Dharma of <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching; faith (<s>prasāda</s>) is in the teacher of that; tranquility (<s>praśama</s>) is of the afflictions; compassion (<s>anukampā</s>) is toward beings; patience (<s>kṣamā</s>) is in difficult practice; intelligence (<s>medhā</s>) is in apprehension, retention, and penetration; strength (<s>prabalatva</s>) is in realization; being unshakeable (<s>ahāryatā</s>) is by <s>Māra</s> and proponents of other doctrines; being endowed with the limbs of abandonment. 'Exceedingly' indicates the superlative degree of inclination and the rest. This, in summary, should be understood as the ninefold self-ripening of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: rūciparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of inclination:

children.translated_text: The triad beginning with good friendship, intense vigor, the collection of the supreme and ultimate excellent Dharma —
in the compassionate one's great embrace of the true Dharma, this is considered the proper characteristic of ripening. || Msa_8.2 ||

body.text: sumitratāditrayaṃ satpuruṣasaṃsevā saddharmaśravaṇaṃ yoniśomanasikāraśca | ugravīryatā adhimātro vīryārambhaḥ | parārdhaniṣṭhā sarvācintyasthānanirvicikitsatā | uttamadharmasaṃgraho mahāyānadharmarakṣā, tatpratipannānāmupadravebhyo rakṣaṇāt |
body.translated_text: The triad beginning with good friendship (<s>sumitratā</s>) is: association with good persons, hearing the true Dharma, and proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>). Intense vigor (<s>ugravīryatā</s>) is the superlative exertion of effort. The ultimate end (<s>parārdhaniṣṭhā</s>) is freedom from doubt regarding all inconceivable states. The collection of the supreme Dharma is the protection of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma — because of protecting those who practice it from calamities.

body.text: bodhisattvasya mahāyānadharmaparigrahamadhikṛtyedaṃ rūciparipākalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam | yena kāraṇena paripacyate sumitratāditrayeṇa | yaśca tasyāḥ paripāka ugravīryaparārdhaniṣṭhāyuktaḥ svabhāvaḥ | yatkarma cottamadharmasaṃgrahakaraṇāttadetena paridīṣitam |
body.translated_text: This ripening of inclination should be understood with reference to the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s embrace of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma: the cause by which one is ripened — the triad beginning with good friendship; the intrinsic nature of that ripening, which is endowed with intense vigor and the ultimate end; and the action — because of performing the collection of the supreme Dharma — this has been illuminated by this [verse].

body.text: prasādaparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of faith:

children.translated_text: Knowledge of qualities, swiftness in attaining <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), experience of its fruit, and the imperviousness of the mind —

children.text: jīnātmaje śāstari saṃprapattaye mataṃ hi samyakparipākalakṣaṇam || Msa_8.3 ||
children.translated_text: in the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, with regard to devotion to the teacher, this is considered the proper characteristic of ripening. || Msa_8.3 ||

body.text: tatparipāko 'pi kāraṇataḥ svabhāvataḥ karmataśca paridīpitaḥ | guṇajñatā ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgata iti vistareṇa kāraṇam | avetyaprabhāva[sāda]lābhādabhedyacittatā svabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Its ripening too is illuminated from the standpoint of cause, intrinsic nature, and action: 'knowledge of qualities' — that is, [knowing] that the Blessed One is the <s>Tathāgata</s> and so forth in detail — is the cause; the imperviousness of mind through obtaining irreversible faith is the intrinsic nature;

body.text: āśusamādhilābhastatphalasya cābhijñādikasya pratyanubhavanaṃ karma |
body.translated_text: swiftness in attaining <s>samādhi</s> and the experience of its fruit such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and so forth — this is the action.

body.text: praśamaparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of tranquility:

children.translated_text: Good restraint [of the senses], avoidance of afflicted discursive thoughts, freedom from obstacles, and delight in wholesome [states] —
in the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, for the removal of afflictions, this is considered the proper characteristic of ripening. || Msa_8.4 ||

body.text: kleśavinodanā bodhisattvasya praśamaḥ | tatparipāko 'pi kāraṇataḥ svabhāvataḥ karmataśca paridīpitaḥ | indriyāṇāṃ smṛtisaṃprajanyābhyāṃ susaṃvṛtiḥ kāraṇam | kliṣṭavitarkavarjanā svabhāvaḥ | pratipakṣabhāvanāyāṃ nirantarāyatvaṃ kuśalābhirāmatā ca karma |
body.translated_text: The removal of afflictions is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s tranquility (<s>praśama</s>). Its ripening too is illuminated from the standpoint of cause, intrinsic nature, and action: good restraint of the faculties through mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) is the cause; avoidance of afflicted discursive thoughts is the intrinsic nature; freedom from obstacles in the cultivation of the antidote, and delight in wholesome [states] — this is the action.

body.text: kṛpāparipākalakṣaṇamadhikṛtya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the characteristic of the ripening of compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>):

children.text: kṛpā prakṛtyā paraduḥkhadarśanaṃ nihīnacittasya ca saṃpravarjanam |
children.translated_text: Compassion by nature, seeing the suffering of others, and the avoidance of the attitude of the inferior [vehicle],
progress toward distinction, and supremacy among beings — this is the characteristic of the ripening of compassion toward others. || Msa_8.5 ||

body.text: svaprakṛtyā ca gotreṇa paraduḥkhadarśanena nihīnayānaparivarjanatayā ca paripacyata itikāraṇam | viśeṣagāmitvaṃ paripākavṛddhigamanāt svabhāvaḥ | sarvalokaśreṣṭhātmabhāvatā karma avinivartanīyabhūmau |
body.translated_text: One is ripened by one's own nature — that is, by one's spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) — by seeing the suffering of others, and by the avoidance of the inferior vehicle — this is the cause. Progress toward distinction, due to the growth of ripening, is the intrinsic nature. Supremacy of being in all the world is the action, on the stage of non-regression (<s>avinivartanīyabhūmi</s>).

body.text: kṣāntiparipākalakṣaṇamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the characteristic of the ripening of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>):

children.translated_text: Fortitude by nature, cultivation through analytical reflection, constant endurance of intense suffering from cold and the like,
progress toward distinction and delight in wholesome [states] — this is considered the characteristic of the ripening of patience. || Msa_8.6 ||

body.text: dhṛtiḥ sahanaṃ kṣāntiriti paryāyāḥ tatatparipāke gotraṃ pratisaṃkhyānaṃ bhāvanā ca kāraṇam | tīvrāṇāṃ śītādiduḥkhānāmadhivāsanāsvabhāvaḥ | kṣamasya viśeṣagāmitvaṃ kuśalābhirāmatā ca karma |
body.translated_text: Fortitude, endurance, and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) are synonyms. In that ripening, the lineage (<s>gotra</s>), analytical reflection, and cultivation are the causes. Its essential nature is the tolerance of intense sufferings such as cold and the like. The function of the patient one is the attainment of distinction and delight in wholesome qualities.

body.text: medhāparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of intelligence (<s>medhā</s>):

children.translated_text: Purity of fruition, non-loss of what has been heard and so forth, penetration into the meanings of well-spoken and ill-spoken [words],

children.text: smṛtermahābuddhyudaye ca yogyatā sumedhatāyāḥ paripākalakṣaṇam || Msa_8.7 ||
children.translated_text: and capacity for the arising of great wisdom through mindfulness — these are the characteristics of the ripening of intelligence (<s>medhā</s>). || Msa_8.7 ||

body.text: tatra medhānukūlā vipākaviśuddhiḥ kāraṇam | śrutacintitabhāvitacirakṛtacirabhāṣitānāmasaṃmoṣatā subhāṣitadurbhāṣitārthasupraviṣṭatā ca smṛtermedhāparipākasvabhāvaḥ | lokottaraprajñotpādanayogyatā karma |
body.translated_text: Therein, the purity of fruition that is conducive to intelligence is the cause. The non-loss of what has been heard, reflected upon, cultivated, long practiced, and long discussed, and the thorough penetration into the meanings of well-spoken and ill-spoken [words] through mindfulness — these are the essential nature of the ripening of intelligence. The capacity for producing supramundane wisdom is its function.

body.text: balavatvapratilambhaparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of the attainment of strength:

children.translated_text: Nourishment of the two bases through the two wholesome [accumulations], supreme capacity of the basis for the arising of the fruit,
fulfillment of aspirations, and becoming the foremost in the world — these are the characteristics of the ripening of the attainment of strength. || Msa_8.8 ||

body.text: tatra puṇyajñānadvayena tasya puṇyajñānadvayasya bījapuṣṭatā tatparipāke kāraṇam | adhigamaṃ pratyāśrayayogyatā tatparipākasvabhāvaḥ | manorathasaṃpattirjagadagrabhūtatā ca karma |
body.translated_text: Therein, the nourishment of the seeds of the two — merit and knowledge — through the two [accumulations of] merit and knowledge is the cause in that ripening. The capacity of the basis for the attainment is the essential nature of that ripening. The fulfillment of aspirations and becoming the foremost in the world are its functions.

body.text: ahāryatāparipākamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the ripening of invincibility:

children.translated_text: A disposition for the investigation of reasoning in the true Dharma, the attainment of distinction, the refutation of opposing positions,

children.text: punaḥ sadā māranirantarāyatā ahāryatāyāḥ paripākalakṣaṇam || Msa_8.9 ||
children.translated_text: and furthermore, the constant freedom from obstruction by <s>Māra</s> — these are the characteristics of the ripening of invincibility. || Msa_8.9 ||

body.text: tatparipākasya saddharme yuktivicāraṇākṛta āśayaḥ kāraṇam | māranirantarāyatā svabhāvo yadā māro na punaḥ śankotyantarāyaṃ kartum | viśeṣādhigamaḥ parapakṣadūṣaṇaṃ ca karma |
body.translated_text: For that ripening, the disposition formed by the investigation of reasoning in the true Dharma is the cause. Freedom from obstruction by <s>Māra</s> is the essential nature — when <s>Māra</s> can no longer create obstacles. The attainment of distinction and the refutation of opposing positions are its functions.

body.text: prāhāṇikāṅgasamanvāgamaparipākamadhikṛtya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse concerning the ripening of the possession of the factors of abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>):

children.translated_text: The accumulation of wholesome qualities, then the capacity of the basis for exertion, delight in eminent wholesome qualities through seclusion —

children.text: jinātmaje hyaṅgasamanvaye punarmataṃ hi samyakparipākalakṣaṇam || Msa_8.10 ||
children.translated_text: for a son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the possession of these factors is considered the characteristic of the proper ripening. || Msa_8.10 ||

body.text: tatparipākasya kāraṇaṃ kuśalamūlopacayaḥ | āśrayasya vīryārambhakṣamatvaṃ svabhāvaḥ | vivekotkṛṣṭatā kuśalābhirāmatā ca karma |
body.translated_text: For that ripening, the cause is the accumulation of wholesome roots. The essential nature is the capacity of the basis for the undertaking of vigor. Eminence in seclusion and delight in wholesome qualities are its functions.

body.text: navavidhātmaparipākamāhātmyamārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the greatness of the ninefold self-ripening:

children.translated_text: Thus, one whose self is enriched by the nine categories, having attained the capacity for ripening others,
one whose self is constantly developed through wholesome qualities, always becomes the foremost kinsman of the world. || Msa_8.11 ||

body.text: dvividhaṃ tanmāhātmyam | paraparipāke pratiśaraṇatvam | satataṃ dharmakāyavṛddhiśca | tata eva jagato 'grabandhubhūtaḥ |
body.translated_text: The greatness of that is twofold: being a refuge for the ripening of others, and the constant growth of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body). And thereby one becomes the foremost kinsman of the world.

body.text: sattvaparipākavibhāge ekādaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Eleven verses on the classification of the ripening of beings:

children.text: vraṇe 'pi bhojye paripāka iṣyate yathaiva tatsrāvaṇabhogayogyatā |
children.translated_text: Just as ripening is recognized both in a wound and in food — as the capacity for draining and for enjoyment respectively —
so too in this basis [of beings], the pacification of the two opposing aspects, and the enjoyment of the wholesome counteracting aspect, [constitute ripening]. || Msa_8.12 ||

body.text: anena paripākasvabhāvaṃ darśayati | yathā vraṇasya srāvaṇayogyatā paripākaḥ | bhojanasya ca bhogayogyatā | evaṃ sattvānāmāśraye vraṇabhojanasthānīye srāvaṇasthānīyaṃ vipakṣaśamanam | bhogasthānīyaśca pratipakṣopabhogaḥ | tadyogyatā āśrayasya paripāka iti | vipakṣapratipakṣāvatra pakṣadvayaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: By this he shows the essential nature of ripening. Just as ripening of a wound is its readiness for draining, and of food its readiness for enjoyment, so too for beings, in the basis that corresponds to wound and food, the pacification of the opposing factor corresponds to draining, and the enjoyment of the counteracting factor corresponds to eating. The readiness of the basis for that is ripening. Herein, the two aspects should be understood as the opposing factor and the counteracting factor.

body.text: dvitīyaślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The second verse:

children.translated_text: Ripening is called 'thorough ripening' (<s>vipācanā</s>), and also 'complete ripening' (<s>paripācanā</s>), and 'conforming ripening' (<s>anupācanā</s>),

children.text: supācanā[cā]pyadhipācanā matā nipācanotpācananā ca dehiṣu || Msa_8.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'excellent ripening' (<s>supācanā</s>), 'superior ripening' (<s>adhipācanā</s>), 'perpetual ripening' (<s>nipācanā</s>), and 'progressive ripening' (<s>utpācanā</s>) among beings. || Msa_8.13 ||

body.text: anena paripākaprabhedaṃ darśayati | kleśavigamena pācananā [pācanā?] vipācanā | sarvato yānatrayeṇa pācanā paripācanā | bāhyaparipākaviśiṣṭatvāt prakṛṣṭā pācanā prapācanā | yathāvineyadharmadeśanāttadanurūpā pācanā anupācanā | satkṛtya pācanā supācanā | adhigamena pācanā adhipācanā aviparītārthena | nityā pācanā nipācanā aparihāṇīyārthena | krameṇottarottarapācanā utpācanā | ityayamaṣṭaprakāraḥ pariparipākaprabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this he shows the classification of ripening. Ripening through the removal of defilements is <s>vipācanā</s> (thorough ripening). Ripening by all means through the three vehicles is <s>paripācanā</s> (complete ripening). Ripening that is distinguished from external ripening, being eminent, is <s>prapācanā</s> (excellent initial ripening). Ripening that conforms to beings to be trained through teaching the Dharma appropriate to them is <s>anupācanā</s> (conforming ripening). Ripening done with respect is <s>supācanā</s> (excellent ripening). Ripening through attainment, in the sense of non-perversion, is <s>adhipācanā</s> (superior ripening). Perpetual ripening, in the sense of non-decline, is <s>nipācanā</s>. Progressive ripening, each stage surpassing the next, is <s>utpācanā</s>. Thus this is the eightfold classification of ripening.

body.text: tṛtīyacaturthau ślokau |
body.translated_text: The third and fourth verses:

children.translated_text: The way in which a son of the <s>Jinas</s>, established with a beneficial intention, ripens all the world —

children.text: tathā na mātā na pitā na bandhavaḥ suteṣu bandhuṣvapi suvyavasthitāḥ || Msa_8.14 ||
children.translated_text: in that way, neither a mother, nor a father, nor relatives are established even toward their children and kinsmen. || Msa_8.14 ||

children.text: tathājano nātmani vatsalo mataḥ kuto 'pi susnigdhaparāśraye jane |
children.translated_text: Likewise, a person is not considered as affectionate toward oneself as

children.text: yathā kṛpātmā parasattvavatsalo hite sukhe caiva niyojanānmataḥ || Msa_8.15 ||
children.translated_text: the compassionate one is considered affectionate toward other beings, through engaging them in what is beneficial and happy. || Msa_8.15 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ kiṃ darśayati | yādṛśenāśayena bodhisattvaḥ sattvānparipācayati tamāśayaṃ darśayati | mātāpitṛbāndhavāśayaviśiṣṭaṃ lokātmavātsalyaviśiṣṭaṃ ca hitasukhasaṃyojanāt | ātmavatsalastu loka ātmānaṃ hite ca sukhe ca saṃniyojayati |
body.translated_text: What does he show by these two? He shows the intention with which the <s>bodhisattva</s> ripens beings — an intention surpassing that of mother, father, and relatives, and surpassing the world's self-affection, through engaging [beings] in what is beneficial and happy. But the world, being self-affectionate, engages only oneself in what is beneficial and happy.

body.text: avaśiṣṭaiḥ ślokairyena prayogeṇa sattvānparipācayati taṃ pāramitā pratipattyā saṃdarśayati |
body.translated_text: With the remaining verses, he shows the means by which one ripens beings, demonstrating through the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections):

body.text: yādṛśena dānena yathā sattvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of giving by which one ripens beings:

children.text: na bodhisattvasya śarīrabhogayoḥ pareṣvadeyaṃ punarasti sarvathā |
children.translated_text: For the <s>bodhisattva</s>, there is absolutely nothing in one's body or enjoyments that cannot be given to others;

children.text: anugraheṇa dvividhena pācayan paraṃ samairdānaguṇairna tṛpyate || Msa_8.16 ||
children.translated_text: ripening others through twofold benefit, one is never satisfied with equal qualities of giving. || Msa_8.16 ||

body.text: trividhena dānena pācayati | sarvasvaśarīrabhogadānena aviṣamadānena atṛptidānena ca | kathaṃ paripācayati dṛṣṭadharmasaṃparāyānugraheṇa | avighātenecchāparipūrṇāt [pūraṇāt] | anāgatena [tena] ca saṃgṛhya kuśalapratiṣṭhāpanāt |
body.translated_text: One ripens through threefold giving: giving of all possessions including one's body and enjoyments, impartial giving, and insatiable giving. How does one ripen? Through twofold benefit — in the present life and in the future. [In the present], through non-harm and the fulfillment of wishes. And [in the future], by gathering [beings] and establishing them in wholesome qualities.

body.text: yādṛśena śīlena yathā satvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of moral discipline by which one ripens beings:

children.translated_text: Always by nature exceedingly non-violent, oneself delighting [in virtue] and vigilant, establishing others therein,
performing twofold successive benefit for others, ripening them through the qualities of fruition and natural outflow. || Msa_8.17 ||

body.text: pañcavidhena śīlena | dhruvaśīlena prakṛtiśīlena paripūrṇaśīlenādhyaviṃhiṃsakatvāt | paripūrṇo hyavihiṃsako 'dhyavihiṃsako daśakuśalakarmapathaparipūritaḥ | yathoktaṃ dvitīyāyāṃ bhūmau | adhigamaśīlena svayaṃratatayā nirantarāskhalitaśīlena cāpramattatayā | kathaṃ ca (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 35

children.text: ) paripācayati | śīle saṃniveśanāt | dvidhānugrahakriyayā dṛṣṭadharme saṃparāye ca | saṃparāyānugrahaṃ pareṣu vipākaniṣyandaguṇābhyāṃ paraṃparayā karoti | tadvipākaniṣyandayoranyonyānukūlyenāvyavacchedāt |
children.translated_text: ) does one ripen? Through establishing [others] in moral discipline. Through performing twofold benefit — in the present life and in the future. One performs successive benefit for others in the future through the qualities of fruition (<s>vipāka</s>) and natural outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) — because of the uninterrupted mutual concordance of those two, fruition and natural outflow.

body.translated_text: Through fivefold moral discipline: constant discipline, natural discipline, and perfect discipline — because of being exceedingly non-violent. For one who is perfectly non-violent has fulfilled the ten wholesome courses of action, as stated regarding the second <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). Through the discipline of attainment, being self-delighting; and through the discipline of uninterrupted and unfailing conduct, being vigilant. And how (

body.text: yādṛśyā kṣāntyā yathā sattvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of patience by which one ripens beings:

children.translated_text: The wise one, having the thought of benefiting one who does harm, enduring even severe transgressions,
through skillful intentions and endurance of offenses, causes the offenders to undertake wholesome [conduct]. || Msa_8.18 ||

body.text: apakāriṇi pare upakāribuddhyā pragāḍhāpakāramarṣaṇakṣāntyā paripācayati | upakāribuddhitvaṃ punaḥ kṣāntipāramitāparipūryānukūlyavṛttitā veditavyam | kathaṃ paripācayati | dṛṣṭadharmānugraheṇa cāpakāramarṣaṇāt | saṃparāyānugraheṇa copāyajñastairapakāramarṣaṇairāvarjyāpakāriṇāṃ kuśale samādāpanāt |
body.translated_text: One ripens by enduring with the thought of benefiting one who does harm, through the patience of forbearing severe offenses. The thought of benefiting should be understood as the conduct of favorable disposition through the fulfillment of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>). How does one ripen? Through benefit in the present life — by enduring offenses. And through benefit in the future — by skillfully attracting offenders through those very acts of enduring offenses, and causing them to undertake wholesome [conduct].

body.text: yādṛśena vīryeṇa yathā sattvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of vigor by which one ripens beings:

children.text: punaḥ sa yatnaṃ paramaṃ samāśrito na khidyate kalpasahasrakoṭibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having undertaken the supreme effort, the son of the <s>Jinas</s> is not wearied even by billions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: jinātmajaḥ sa[ttva]gaṇaṃ prapācayanparaikacittasya śubhasya kāraṇāt || Msa_8.19 ||
children.translated_text: ripening the multitude of beings, for the sake of even a single wholesome thought in another. || Msa_8.19 ||

body.text: adhimātradīrghakālākhede vīryeṇa dīrghakālākheditvamanantasattvaparipācanāt | paraikacittasya kuśalasyārthe kalpasahasrakoṭibhirakhedāt | ata evoktaṃ bhavati yathā paripācayati | kuśalacittasaṃniyojanāt dṛṣṭadharmasaṃparāyānugraheṇeti |
body.translated_text: Through vigor of supreme and prolonged unwearied [effort] — the prolonged unwearied nature is due to ripening infinite beings. Through unwearied effort over billions of <s>kalpas</s> for the sake of even a single wholesome thought in another. Thus it is stated how one ripens — through engaging [beings] in wholesome thoughts, by benefit in both the present life and the future.

body.text: yādṛśena dhyānena yathā sattvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of meditation by which one ripens beings:

children.translated_text: Having attained supreme mastery over the mind, one attracts others to this teaching,

children.text: nihatya sarvāmavamānakāmatāṃ śubhena saṃvardhayate ca taṃ punaḥ || Msa_8.20 ||
children.translated_text: having destroyed all desire for contempt, and one further develops that [being] through wholesome [qualities]. || Msa_8.20 ||

body.text: prāptānuttaravaśitvena dhyānena nirāmiṣeṇa ca nihatasarvāvamānābhilāṣeṇa paripācayati | buddhaśāsane parasyāvarjanādāvarjitasya ca kuśaladharmasaṃvardhanāt paripācayati |
body.translated_text: One ripens through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) in which one has attained supreme mastery, which is free from material attachment, and in which all desire for contempt has been destroyed. One ripens by attracting others to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>, and by developing the one who has been attracted in wholesome qualities.

body.text: yādṛśyā prajñayā yathā sattvānparipācayati tadārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse beginning with the kind of wisdom by which one ripens beings:

children.text: sa tattvabhāvārthanaye suniścitaḥ karoti sattvānsuvinīta saṃśayān |
children.translated_text: Well-established in the method of understanding the nature of reality and its meaning, one removes the doubts of beings who are well-trained,

children.text: tataśca te tajjinaśāsanādarād vivardhayante svaparaṃ guṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ || Msa_8.21 ||
children.translated_text: and then they, out of respect for the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>, develop both themselves and others through excellent qualities. || Msa_8.21 ||

body.text: sa bodhisattvastattvārthanaye cābhiprāyārthanaye ca suviniścitayā prajñayā paripācayati | kathaṃ paripācayati sattvānāṃ saṃśayavinayanāt | tataśca śāsanabahumānātteṣāmātmaparaguṇasaṃvardhakatvena |
body.translated_text: That <s>bodhisattva</s> ripens through wisdom that is well-established in the method of the meaning of reality and the method of the intended meaning. How does one ripen? Through removing the doubts of beings. And then, through their respect for the teaching, they develop the qualities of self and others.

body.text: niya[ga]mena ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse of summary:

children.text: iti sugatigatau śubhatraye vā jagadakhilaṃ kṛpayā sa bodhisattvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, with compassion, trains the entire world toward the attainment of good destinies or in the three wholesome [vehicles],
through subtle, supreme, and middling modes, proceeding in accordance with the nature of the world. || Msa_8.22 ||

body.text: anena yatra ca vinayati, sugatigamane yānatraye vā | yacca vinayati, jagadakhilam | yena ca vinayati, kṛpayā | yaśca vinayati bodhisattvaḥ | yādṛśaiśca paripācanaprakārai tanuparamavimadhyamaprakāraiḥ | yāvantaṃ ca kālaṃ, tatparidīpanāt samāsena paripākamāhātmyaṃ darśayati | tatra tanuḥ prakāro 'dhimukticaryābhūmau bodhisattvasya paramo 'ṣṭāmyādiṣu vimadhyamaḥ saptasu veditavyaḥ | yāvallokasya bhāvastatsamānayā gatyā atyantamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this [he shows]: where one trains — in going to good destinies or in the three vehicles. What one trains — the entire world. By what means one trains — by compassion. Who trains — the <s>bodhisattva</s>. And through what kinds of ripening modes — through subtle, supreme, and middling modes. And for how long — he shows the greatness of ripening in summary by illuminating that. Therein, the subtle mode belongs to the <s>bodhisattva</s> on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); the supreme belongs to the eighth stage and above; and the middling should be understood as belonging to the seven [intermediate stages]. For as long as the world exists — proceeding by the corresponding course — that is, forever: this is the meaning.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre paripākādhikāro 'ṣṭamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eighth chapter on ripening (<s>paripāka</s>) ||

body.text: navamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Ninth chapter:

body.text: sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dvau ślokau | tṛtīyastayoreva nirdeśabhūtaḥ |

children.translated_text: Through immeasurable hundreds of difficult deeds, through immeasurable accumulations of wholesome [qualities],
through immeasurable time, and through the exhaustion of immeasurable obscurations — || Msa_9.1 ||

body.translated_text: Two verses on omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). The third is an exposition of those very two.

children.translated_text: the attainment of omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), free from all obscurations,
is revealed like a jewel casket — this is declared to be Buddhahood (<s>buddhatva</s>). || Msa_9.2 ||
Having performed wondrous difficult deeds, having accumulated all wholesome [qualities] through hundreds of exertions,
through the great and supreme duration of <s>kalpas</s>, through the exhaustion of all obscurations,
through the uprooting of the subtle obscuration that has pervaded the stages — Buddhahood,

children.text: ratnānāmiva sā prabhāvamahatāṃ peṭā samuddhāti[ṭi?]tā || Msa_9.3 ||
children.translated_text: like a casket of greatly powerful jewels, is revealed. || Msa_9.3 ||

body.text: samudāgamataḥ svabhāvata aupamyataśca buddhatvamudbhāvitam | yāvadbhirduṣkaraśatairyāvadbhiḥ kuśalasaṃbhārairyāvatā kālena yāvataḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇasya prahāṇātsamudāgacchati, ayaṃ samudāgamaḥ | sarvākārajñatāvāptiḥ sarvāvaraṇanirmalā svabhāvaḥ | vivṛtāratnapeṭā tadaupamyam |
body.translated_text: Buddhahood is set forth in terms of attainment, essential nature, and simile. Through however many hundreds of difficult deeds, through however many accumulations of wholesome qualities, through however much time, and through the abandonment of however many obscurations of afflictions and knowables it is attained — this is the attainment. The attainment of omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), free from all obscurations, is the essential nature. The revealed jewel casket is the simile.

body.text: tasyaiva buddhatvasyādvayalakṣaṇe sānubhāve dvau lokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the non-dual characteristic and its power of that very Buddhahood:

children.text: sarvadharmāśca buddhatvaṃ dharmo naiva ca kaścana |
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are Buddhahood, yet no single <s>dharma</s> whatsoever [is Buddhahood].

children.text: śukladharmamayaṃ tacca na ca taistannirūpyate || Msa_9.4 ||
children.translated_text: and it is composed of wholesome qualities, yet it cannot be defined by those [qualities]. || Msa_9.4 ||
Because it is the cause of the jewel of Dharma, it is considered like a jewel-mine;
because it is the cause of wholesome harvest, it is considered like a [rain-]cloud. || Msa_9.5 ||

body.text: sarvadharmāśca buddhatvaṃ, tathatāyā abhinnatvāttadviśuddhiprabhāvitatvācca | buddhatvasya na ca kaściddharmo 'sti | parikalpitena dharmasvabhāvena śukladharmamayaṃ ca buddhatvaṃ, pāramitādināṃ kuśalānāṃ tadbhāvena parivṛtteḥ | na ca taistannirdiśyate pāramitādīnāṃ pāramitādibhāvenāpariniṣpatteridamadvayalakṣaṇam | ratnākarameghopamatvamanubhāvaḥ, deśanādharmaratnānāṃ tatprabhavatvāt, kuśalasasyānāṃ ca vineyasaṃtānakṣetreṣu |
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are Buddhahood, because of the non-difference of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and because it is made manifest through the purification of that [suchness]. Yet there is no [separate] dharma that constitutes Buddhahood. Buddhahood is composed of wholesome qualities through the imagined nature of dharmas (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), because the wholesome [qualities] such as the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are transformed into that [Buddhahood]. Yet it cannot be defined by those — because the <s>pāramitās</s> and the rest are not perfectly accomplished (<s>apariniṣpatti</s>) as <s>pāramitās</s> and so forth — this is the characteristic of non-duality. Being like a jewel-mine and a cloud is the influence (<s>anubhāva</s>), because it is the source of the jewels of Dharma-teaching, and [the source] of wholesome harvests in the field-continua of those to be trained.

children.translated_text: Buddhahood is all dharmas taken together, or alternatively, it is devoid of all dharmas;
because it is the cause of the greatly extensive jewel of Dharma, it resembles a jewel-mine (<s>dharmaratnākara</s>);
because it is the cause of the greatly extensive production of wholesome harvest for beings, it is like a cloud,
from the giving of the greatly extensive, well-dispensed, and inexhaustible rain-water of Dharma upon beings. || Msa_9.6 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena ślokena tamevārthaṃ nirdiśati | sumahataḥ pratatasya dharmaratnasya prodbhūtenimittatvādratnākarābham, bhūtānāṃ mahataḥ śuklasasyaprasavahetutvānmeghabhūtam | mahataḥ suvihitasyākṣayasya dharmāmbuvarṣasya dānāt prajāsvityayamatra padavigraho veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this third verse, he explains that very same meaning: because it is the cause of the arising of the greatly extensive jewel of Dharma, it resembles a jewel-mine; because it is the cause of the production of a great wholesome harvest for beings, it is like a cloud. The word-analysis here should be understood as: 'from the giving of the great, well-dispensed, and inexhaustible rain-water of Dharma upon beings.'

body.text: tasyaiva buddhatvasya śaraṇatvānuttarye pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the unsurpassable nature of that very Buddhahood as refuge:

children.translated_text: For Buddhahood is always protection from the entire host of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>),
from all evil conduct, and from birth and death as well. || Msa_9.7 ||

body.text: anena saṃkṣepataḥ kleśakarmajanmasaṃkleśaparitrāṇārthena śaraṇatvaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this [verse], he shows in summary the nature of being a refuge for the purpose of protection from the defilement of afflictions, actions, and birth.

children.translated_text: From all calamities, from the lower realms, from wrong methods,
from the belief in a self-existing body (<s>satkāya</s>), and from the inferior vehicle — therefore it is the supreme refuge. || Msa_9.8 ||
