body.text: anena dvitiyenopadravādiparitrāṇādvistareṇa | tatra sarvopadravaparitrāṇatvaṃ yad buddhānubhāvena andhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante, badhirāḥ śrotaṃ, vikṣiptacittāḥ svasthacittamītayaḥ śāmyantītyevamādi | apāyaparitrāṇatvaṃ buddhaprabhayā tadgatānāṃ mokṣaṇāt, tadagamane ca pratiṣṭhāpanāt | anupāyaparitrāṇatvaṃ tīrthikadṛṣṭivyutthāpanāt | satkāyaparitrāṇatvaṃ yānadvayena parinirvāpaṇāt |
body.translated_text: By this second [verse], in detail, [he shows protection] from calamities and so forth: protection from all calamities — by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the blind obtain eyes, the deaf obtain hearing, those with disturbed minds obtain sound minds, and calamities are pacified, and so forth. Protection from the lower realms — by the light of the <s>Buddha</s>, those who have gone there are liberated and are established in non-going there. Protection from wrong methods — by causing those holding the views of non-Buddhist schools (<s>tīrthika</s>) to rise above them. Protection from the belief in a self-existing body — by bringing about <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) through the two vehicles.

body.text: hīnayānaparitrāṇatvamaniyatagotrāṇāṃ mahāyānaikāyanīkaraṇāt |

children.translated_text: That supreme Buddhahood is accepted as an incomparable refuge —
a protection against birth, death, all afflictions, and evil deeds;
a vehicle of complete protection for those beset by various fears,
for those who possess extensive and various means of removing suffering in the lower realms. || Msa_9.9 ||

body.translated_text: Protection from the inferior vehicle — by bringing those of indeterminate spiritual lineage (<s>aniyatagotra</s>) into the single course of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: anena tṛtīyena tasyaiva śaraṇatvasyānupamaśreṣṭhasya cānuttaryaṃ tenaivārthena darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows the unsurpassable nature of that very refuge, which is incomparable and supreme, by that very meaning.

children.text: bauddhairdharmairyacca susaṃpūrṇaśarīraṃ yatsaddharme vetti ca sattvānpravinetum |
children.translated_text: Because the body is well-endowed with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, because one knows how to train beings in the true Dharma,

children.text: yātaṃ pāraṃ yatkṛpayā sarvajagatsu tad buddhatvaṃ śreṣṭhamihatyaṃ[heṣṭaṃ] śaraṇānām || Msa_9.10 ||
children.translated_text: because one has gone to the far shore [of existence] through compassion for all beings — that Buddhahood is the supreme among refuges here. || Msa_9.10 ||

body.text: anena caturthena yaiḥ kāraṇaistattathānuttaraṃ śaraṇaṃ bhavati tatsaṃdarśayati | bauddhairdharmairbalavaiśāradyādibhiḥ susaṃpūrṇasvabhāvatvāt svārthaniṣṭhāmadhikṛtya saddharmasattvavinayopāyajñānāt karuṇāpāragamanācca parārthaniṣṭhāmadhikṛtya |
body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the reasons by which it becomes thus an unsurpassable refuge: because of the well-perfected intrinsic nature through <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the powers (<s>bala</s>) and fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) — with reference to the fulfillment of self-interest; because of the knowledge of the means to train beings in the true Dharma, and because of having gone to the far shore of compassion — with reference to the fulfillment of the welfare of others.

children.translated_text: For all beings at all times, Buddhahood is a great refuge,
regarded as [effective] in the removal of all misfortune and in the attainment of prosperity. || Msa_9.11 ||

body.text: anena pañcamena ślokena yāvantaṃ kālaṃ yāvatāṃ sattvānāṃ yatrārthe śaraṇaṃ bhavati tatsamāsena darśayati | yatrārthe iti sarvavyasanavyāvṛttau saṃpattyabhyudaye ca |
body.translated_text: By this fifth verse, he shows in summary for how long, for how many beings, and for what purpose it serves as refuge: 'for what purpose' means in the removal of all misfortune and in the attainment of prosperity.

body.text: āśrayaparāvṛttau ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>):

children.translated_text: The seed of the activities of affliction-obscuration and knowledge-obscuration (<s>kleśajñeyāvaraṇa</s>), which has constantly followed [beings] since beginningless time —
when in that [Buddhahood] it has gone to destruction through all the supremely extensive modes of abandonment,
Buddhahood is the otherness-attainment of the basis, endowed with the foremost and excellent qualities of wholesome dharmas —
the attainment of that comes from the supremely pure knowledge-path, whose object is the vast non-conceptual [realm]. || Msa_9.12 ||

body.text: anena vipakṣabījaviyogataḥ pratipakṣasaṃpattiyogataścāśrayaparivṛttiḥ paridīpitā | yathā ca tatprāptirdvividhamārgalābhāt | suviśuddhalokottarajñānamārgalābhāt | tatpṛṣṭhalabdhānantajñeyaviṣayajñānamārgalābhācca | utkṛṣṭakālamityanādikālaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this [verse], the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) is illuminated through separation from the seed of the adverse factor and through conjunction with the accomplishment of the antidote. And how that attainment [comes about] — through obtaining a twofold path: through obtaining the supremely pure supramundane knowledge-path, and through obtaining the path of knowledge whose object is the boundless knowable [realm], which is subsequently attained. 'Since beginningless time' means for a time without beginning.

body.text: suvipulaiḥ sarvahāniprakārairiti bhūmiprakāraiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Through all the supremely extensive modes of abandonment' means through the modes of the [ten] stages (<s>bhūmi</s>).

children.translated_text: And abiding in that [state], the <s>Tathāgata</s> looks down upon the world as if standing on the king of great mountains;

children.text: śamābhirāmaṃ karūṇāyate janamaghā[bhavā]bhirāme 'nyajane tu kā kathā || Msa_9.13 ||
children.translated_text: one who delights in tranquility feels compassion for beings, and what need be said of those who delight in the evils of existence? || Msa_9.13 ||

body.text: anena dvitīyenānyāśrayaparāvṛttibhyastadviśeṣaṃ darśayati | tatstho hi mahācalendrastha iva dūrāntaranikṛṣṭaṃ lokaṃ paśyati |
body.translated_text: By this second [verse], he shows the distinction from other transformations of the basis: for one abiding in that [state], like one standing on the king of great mountains, sees the world far below and distant.

body.text: dṛṣṭvā ca karūṇāyate śrāvakapratyekabuddhānapi prāgeva tadanyān |
body.translated_text: And having seen, one feels compassion — even for <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), how much more for others.

children.translated_text: Activity, elevation, non-activity, the basis, cessation, perpetual activity, duality and non-duality,

children.text: samāviśiṣṭā api sarvagātmikā tathāgatānāṃ parivṛttiriṣyate || Msa_9.14 ||
children.translated_text: both equal and distinguished, and having the nature of all-pervasiveness — such is regarded as the transformation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || Msa_9.14 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena taddaśaprabhedaṃdarśayati | sā hi tathāgatānāṃ parivṛttiḥ parārthavṛttiriti pravṛttiḥ | sarvadharmaviśiṣṭatvāduṣkṛṣṭā vṛttirityudvṛttiḥ | saṃkleśahetāvavṛttiḥ | āśraya iti yo 'sau parivṛttyāśrayastaṃ darśayati | saṃkleśānnivṛttito nivṛttiḥ | ātyantikatvādāyatā vṛttirityāvṛttiḥ | abhisaṃbodhiparinirvāṇadarśanavṛttyā dvayā vṛttiḥ | saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhitatvātsaṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtatvenādvayā vṛttiḥ | vimuktisāmānyena śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamā vṛttiḥ | balavaiśāradyādibhiḥ buddhadharmairasamatvādviśiṣṭā vṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows the tenfold division of that: for that transformation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), since it functions for the welfare of others; it is elevation (<s>udvṛtti</s>), since its functioning is distinguished from all dharmas; it is non-activity (<s>avṛtti</s>) with regard to the cause of defilement; 'the basis' indicates the basis of that transformation; it is cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), since it has ceased from defilement; it is perpetual activity (<s>āvṛtti</s>), since its functioning is permanent and extended; it has a dual functioning through the display of perfect awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhi</s>) and <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation); it has a non-dual functioning, since it is not established in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being neither conditioned nor unconditioned; it has a functioning equal [to that of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas] through the commonality of liberation; and it has a distinguished functioning, since it is unequalled through the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the powers (<s>bala</s>) and fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>);

body.text: sarvayānopadeśagatatvātsarvagatāvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: it has an all-pervasive functioning, since it extends to the instruction of all vehicles.

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ sarvagataṃ sadāmataṃ tathaiva tatsarvagataṃ sadāmatam |
children.translated_text: Just as space is regarded as all-pervading at all times, so too is that [Buddhahood] regarded as all-pervading at all times;

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ rūpagaṇeṣu sarvagaṃ tathaiva tatsattvagaṇeṣu sarvagam || Msa_9.15 ||
children.translated_text: just as space pervades all groups of forms, so too does that [Buddhahood] pervade all groups of beings. || Msa_9.15 ||

body.text: anena caturthena tatsvabhāvasya buddhatvasya sarvagatatvaṃ darśayati | ākāśasādharmyeṇauddeśanirdeśataḥ pūrvāparārdhābhyām | sattvagaṇeṣu sarvagatatvaṃ buddhatvasyātmatvena sarvasattvopagamane pariniṣpattito veditavyam |
body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the all-pervasiveness of Buddhahood, whose nature is that — by analogy with space, through indication and detailed explanation, by means of the first and second halves. The all-pervasiveness among groups of beings should be understood as Buddhahood being perfectly accomplished in approaching all beings as their self.

children.translated_text: Just as, when a water-vessel is broken, the reflection of the moon is not seen,

children.text: tathā duṣṭeṣu sattveṣu buddhabimbaṃ na dṛśyate || Msa_9.16 ||
children.translated_text: so too, in beings who are corrupted, the reflection of the <s>Buddha</s> is not seen. || Msa_9.16 ||

body.text: anena pañcamena sarvagatatve 'pyabhājanabhūteṣu sattveṣu abuddhabimbadarśanaṃ dṛṣṭāntena sādhayati |
body.translated_text: By this fifth [verse], he establishes through an analogy that even though [Buddhahood] is all-pervasive, the reflection of the <s>Buddha</s> is not seen in beings who are not [suitable] vessels.

children.translated_text: Just as fire blazes in one place and is extinguished in another,
so too with regard to <s>Buddhas</s>, one should understand the appearance and disappearance [of their manifestation]. || Msa_9.17 ||

body.text: anena ṣaṣṭhena buddhavineyeṣu satsubuddhotpādāttaddarśanaṃ | vinīteṣu parinirvāṇāttadadarśanaṃ agnijvalanaśamanasādharmyeṇa sādhayati |
body.translated_text: By this sixth [verse], he establishes through the analogy of the blazing and extinguishing of fire that when there are beings to be trained by the <s>Buddha</s>, there is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> and [hence] seeing; and when they have been trained, there is <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and [hence] non-seeing.

body.text: anābhogāpratiprasrabdhabuddhakāryatve catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the effortless and unrelenting <s>Buddha</s>-activity:

children.translated_text: Just as sound might arise from musical instruments that are not being played,

children.text: tathā jine vinābhogaṃ deśanāyāḥ samudbhavaḥ || Msa_9.18 ||
children.translated_text: so too, in the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), the arising of teaching occurs without effort. || Msa_9.18 ||
Just as a jewel displays [its radiance] without effort, by its own nature,
so too, in <s>Buddhas</s>, the display of [their] activity occurs without effort. || Msa_9.19 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāmanābhogena buddhakāryaṃ sādhayatyaghaṭitatūryaśabdamaṇiprabhāva[sa]sādharmyeṇa |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he establishes <s>Buddha</s>-activity without effort, by analogy with the sound of unplayed instruments and the radiance of a jewel.

children.translated_text: Just as in space, activities in the world are seen without interruption,
so too, in the undefiled element (<s>anāsrava dhātu</s>), the activities of the <s>Jina</s> are without interruption. || Msa_9.20 ||
Just as in space, there is always the decline and rise of activities,
so too, in the undefiled element, there is the arising and passing of <s>Buddha</s>-activity. || Msa_9.21 ||

body.text: ābhyāmapyapratiprasrabdhabuddhakāryatvaṃ buddhakṛtyasyāvicchedāt | ākāśa iva lokakriyāṇāmavicchede 'pi cānyānyakriyodayavyayastathaiva |
body.translated_text: By these [two verses] as well, [he establishes] the unrelenting nature of <s>Buddha</s>-activity, because <s>Buddha</s>-activity is without interruption — just as worldly activities in space are without interruption, yet there is the arising and passing of various activities, so it is likewise.

body.text: anāsravadhātugāmbhīrye ṣoḍaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Sixteen verses on the depth of the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>):

children.translated_text: Although undifferentiated in sequence, and purified of all obscurations,

children.text: naśuddhā nāpi cāśuddhā tathatā buddhatā matā || Msa_9.22 ||
children.translated_text: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is regarded as Buddhahood — neither pure nor impure. || Msa_9.22 ||

body.text: paurvāparyeṇa[ā]viśiṣṭatvānna śuddhā | paścātsarvāvaraṇanirmalatvānnāśuddhā malavigamāt |
body.translated_text: It is not pure, because it is undifferentiated in temporal sequence; it is not impure, because afterward it is free from all obscurations, due to the removal of stains.

children.translated_text: In the purified <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), through <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) and the attainment of the path,
<s>Buddhas</s>, having obtained a pure self, have attained the greatness of the self. || Msa_9.23 ||

body.text: tatra cānāsrave dhātau buddhānāṃ paramātmā nirdiśyate | kiṃ kāraṇam | agranairātmyātmakatvāt | agraṃ nairātmyaṃ viśuddhā tathatā sā ca buddhānāmātmā svabhāvārthena tasyāṃ viśuddhāyāmagraṃ nairātmyamātmānaṃ buddhā labhante śuddham | ataḥ śuddhātmalābhitvāt buddhā ātmamāhātmyaṃ prāptā ityanenābhisaṃdhinā buddhānāmanāsrave dhātau paramātmā vyavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, in the undefiled element, the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s> is taught. For what reason? Because it has the nature of the supreme selflessness (<s>agranairātmya</s>). The supreme selflessness is the purified <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and that is the self of the <s>Buddhas</s> in the sense of intrinsic nature. In that purified [suchness], the <s>Buddhas</s> obtain the supreme selflessness as a pure self. Therefore, because of obtaining a pure self, the <s>Buddhas</s> have attained the greatness of the self — with this intention, the supreme self of the <s>Buddhas</s> is established in the undefiled element.

children.text: na bhāvo nāpi cābhāvo buddhatvaṃ tena kathyate |
children.translated_text: Buddhahood is said to be neither existence nor non-existence;
therefore, regarding the question about the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the method of the undeclared (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is regarded [as appropriate]. || Msa_9.24 ||

body.text: tenaiva kāraṇena buddhatvaṃ na bhāva ucyate | pudgaladharmābhāvalakṣaṇatvāttadātmakatvācca buddhatvasya | nābhāva ucyate tathatālakṣaṇabhāvāt | ato buddhasya bhāvābhāvapraśne, bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇānna bhavatītyevamādiravyākṛtanayomataḥ |
body.translated_text: For that very reason, Buddhahood is not called existence — because it has the characteristic of the absence of person and dharmas, and because Buddhahood has that as its nature. Nor is it called non-existence — because of having the nature characterized by <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Therefore, regarding the question of the existence or non-existence of the <s>Buddha</s> — 'Does the <s>Tathāgata</s> exist after death or not?' and so forth — the method of the undeclared (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is regarded [as appropriate].

children.translated_text: Just as the cessation of burning in metal and [the cessation] of visual impairment (<s>timira</s>) in vision —

children.text: cittajñāne tathā bauddhe bhāvābhāvo na śasyate || Msa_9.25 ||
children.translated_text: so too in the mind-knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>, neither existence nor non-existence is commended. || Msa_9.25 ||

body.text: yathā ca lohe dāhaśāntirdarśane ca timirameta[?]sya śāntirna bhāvo dāhatimirayorabhāvalakṣaṇāt | nābhāvaḥ śāntilakṣaṇena bhāvāt | evaṃ buddhānāṃ cittajñāne ca dāhatimirasthānīyayo rāgāvidyayoḥ śāntirna bhāvaḥ śasyate tadabhāvaprabhāvitatvāccetaḥ prajñāvimuktyā nābhāvastena tena vimuktilakṣaṇena bhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Just as the cessation of burning in metal and the cessation of visual impairment in vision are not existence — because burning and visual impairment have the characteristic of non-existence; nor are they non-existence — because they have existence characterized by cessation. So too, in the mind-knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the cessation of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), which correspond to burning and visual impairment, is not commended as existence — because the mind is made manifest by the absence of those, through wisdom-liberation (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>); nor as non-existence — because it has existence characterized by that very liberation.

children.text: buddhānāmamale dhātau naikatā bahutā na ca |
children.translated_text: In the stainless element of the <s>Buddhas</s>, there is neither oneness nor multiplicity,
because of bodilessness like space, yet following previous bodies. || Msa_9.26 ||

body.text: buddhānāmanāsravadhātau naikatvaṃ pūrvadehānusāreṇa | na bahutvaṃ dehābhāvādākāśavat |
body.translated_text: In the undefiled element of the <s>Buddhas</s>, there is no oneness — in accordance with previous bodies; and no multiplicity — because of the absence of body, like space.

children.translated_text: With respect to <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the powers (<s>bala</s>) and so forth, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is like a jewel-mine;
with respect to the wholesome harvests of the world, it is regarded as like a great cloud. || Msa_9.27 ||
Because of being well-filled with merit and knowledge, it is regarded as like the full moon;
and because of producing the light of knowledge, it is regarded as like the great sun. || Msa_9.28 ||

body.text: etau ratnākarameghopamatve pūrṇacandramahādityopamatve ca ślokau gatārthau |
body.translated_text: These two verses on the likeness to a jewel-mine and cloud, and the likeness to the full moon and great sun, have their meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Just as immeasurable rays, unmixed [with darkness],
in the orb of the sun always function with a single purpose and illuminate the world, || Msa_9.29 ||
Likewise, in the uncontaminated realm (anāsrava dhātu), the immeasurability of the Buddhas,
their mixed single-function activity in actions, and the delightful nature of their knowledge-light. || Msa_9.30 ||

body.text: ekena vyāmiśraraśmyekakāryasyopamatayā sādhāraṇakarmatāṃ darśayati | raśmīnāmekakāryatvaṃ pācanaśoṣaṇasamānakāryatvādveditavyaṃ | dvitīyenānāsrave dhātau miśraikakāryatvaṃ nirmāṇādikṛtyeṣu |
body.translated_text: With the first [half-verse], by the analogy of mixed rays having a single function, he shows their common activity. The single-function nature of rays should be understood from their having the same activity of ripening and drying. With the second [half-verse], [he shows] the mixed single-function nature in the uncontaminated realm in actions such as emanation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) and so forth.

children.translated_text: Just as from the emission of a single ray, all rays issue forth
from the sun, so too should the issuing forth of the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> be understood. || Msa_9.31 ||

body.text: ekakāle sarvaraśmiviniḥsṛtyā sa ca [saha?]buddhānāmekakāle jñānapravṛttiṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By the simultaneous issuing forth of all rays, he shows the simultaneous operation of knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.translated_text: Just as in the operation of the sun's rays there is no sense of 'mine',

children.text: tathaiva buddhajñānānāṃ vṛttau nāsti mamāyitam || Msa_9.32 ||
children.translated_text: so too in the operation of the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge there is no sense of 'mine'. || Msa_9.32 ||
Just as the world is illuminated by rays emitted from a single sun,

children.text: sakṛt jñeyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ buddhajñānaiḥ prabhāsyate || Msa_9.33 ||
children.translated_text: so too all that is to be known is illuminated at once by the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge. || Msa_9.33 ||

body.text: mamatvābhāve jagajjñeyaprabhāsena[sane] ca yathākramaṃ ślokau gatārthau |
body.translated_text: The two verses are self-explanatory regarding the absence of possessiveness and the illumination of the world of knowable objects, respectively.

children.translated_text: Just as the obscuration of the sun's rays by clouds and so forth is recognized,
so too the obstruction of the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge is the corruption of beings. || Msa_9.34 ||

body.text: yathā raśmīnāṃ meghādyāvaraṇamaprabhāsena | tathā buddhajñānānāmāvaraṇaṃ sattvānāmā[ma]bhājanatvena duṣṭatā pañcakaṣāyātyutsadatayā |
body.translated_text: Just as the obscuration of rays by clouds and the like is [shown] by non-illumination, so too the obstruction of the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge is the corruption of beings through their being unworthy vessels, due to the excessive prevalence of the five degenerations (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>).

children.translated_text: Just as due to dust, cloth has variegated or unvariegated coloring,
so too due to [prior karmic] penetration, in liberation there is variegated or unvariegated knowledge. || Msa_9.35 ||

body.text: yathā pāṃśuviśeṣeṇa vastre raṅgavicitratā kvacidavicitratā | tathaiva pūrvapraṇidhānacaryābalādhānaviśeṣād buddhānāṃ vimuktau jñānavicitratā bhavati |
body.translated_text: Just as due to a particular [quality of] dust, cloth has variegated or unvariegated coloring, so too due to the particular prior aspirations, practice, and accumulated power, the <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge in liberation becomes variegated;

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ vimuktāvavicitratā |
body.translated_text: for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, in liberation there is non-variegation.

children.translated_text: The profundity in the undefiled realm, in characteristics, abode, and action —
this has been stated regarding the <s>Buddhas</s>; [it is like] painting space with colors. || Msa_9.36 ||

body.text: etadanāsravadhātau buddhānāṃ trividhaṃ gāmbhīryamevamuttam | lakṣaṇagāmbhīryaṃ caturbhiḥ ślokaiḥ | sthānagāmbhīryaṃpañcamenaikatvapṛthaktvābhyāmasthitatvāt | karmagāmbhīryaṃ daśabhiḥ | tatpunarlakṣaṇagāmbhīryaṃ viśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ paramātmalakṣaṇamavyākṛtalakṣaṇaṃ vimuktilakṣaṇaṃ cārabhyoktam | karmagāmbhīryaṃ bodhipakṣādiratnāśrayatvakarma sattvaparipācanakarma niṣṭhāgamanakarma dharmadeśanākarma nirmāṇādikṛtyakarma jñānapravṛttikarma avikalpanakarma citrākārajñānakarma jñānāpravṛttikarma vimuktisāmānyajñānaviśeṣakarma cārabhyoktam | seyamanāsrave dhātau niṣprapañcatvādākāśopame gāmbhīryaprabhedadeśanā yathā raṅgairākāśacitraṇī veditavyā |
body.translated_text: This threefold profundity of the <s>Buddhas</s> in the uncontaminated realm has thus been stated. The profundity of characteristics [is shown] by four verses. The profundity of abode [is shown] by the fifth, because it does not abide in either unity or multiplicity. The profundity of action [is shown] by ten [verses]. Furthermore, the profundity of characteristics is explained beginning with the characteristic of purity, the characteristic of supreme self, the characteristic of being unobstructed, and the characteristic of liberation. The profundity of action is explained beginning with the action of being a jewel-repository of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) and so forth, the action of ripening beings, the action of reaching the ultimate goal, the action of teaching the Dharma, the action of functions such as emanation, the action of knowledge-operation, the action of non-conceptualization, the action of variegated-form knowledge, the action of non-operation of knowledge, and the action of the particular knowledge common to liberation. This teaching of the divisions of profundity in the uncontaminated realm — being free from conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>) and thus like space — should be understood as painting space with colors.

children.translated_text: <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) of all [beings], though undifferentiated, having reached purity,
is <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood; therefore all embodied beings have that as their embryo (<s>tathāgatagarbha</s>). || Msa_9.37 ||

body.text: sarveṣāṃ nirviśiṣṭā tathatā taddhiśuddhisvabhāvaśca tathāgataḥ | ataḥ sarve sattvāstathāgatagarbhā ityucyate |
body.translated_text: The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all [beings] is undifferentiated, and its purity-nature is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore all beings are said to possess <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> (the embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>).

children.translated_text: On the classification of sovereignty (<s>vibhutva</s>), eleven verses:
By the sovereignty of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, the worldly [sovereignty] is surpassed;
by the [sovereignty of those on] the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, the sovereignty of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> is surpassed, in comparison with the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. || Msa_9.38 ||
The sovereignty of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> does not attain even a fraction of that;
the sovereignty of <s>Tathāgatas</s> does not attain even a fraction of that. || Msa_9.39 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ tāvad dvābhyāṃ prabhāvotkarṣaviśeṣeṇa buddhānāṃ vibhutvaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By these two [verses], he first shows the sovereignty of the <s>Buddhas</s> by the distinction of surpassing excellence of supernatural power.

children.translated_text: The sovereignty of the <s>Buddhas</s> is held to be immeasurable and inconceivable —

children.text: yasya yatra yathā yāvatkāle yasminpravartate || Msa_9.40 ||
children.translated_text: for whom, where, how, how much, and at what time it operates. || Msa_9.40 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena prakāraprabhedagāmbhīryaviśeṣābhyāṃ kathamaprameyaṃ kathaṃ vā cintyamityāha | yasya pudgalasyārthe tatpravarttate yatra lokadhātau yathā tādṛśaiḥ prakārairyāvadalpaṃ vā bahu vā yasminkāle |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he explains how it is immeasurable and how it is inconceivable through the distinction of the profundity of the varieties of modes: for what person it operates, in what world-realm, by what kinds of modes, how much — whether little or much — and at what time.

body.text: avaśiṣṭaiḥ ślokaiḥ mano[parā]vṛttibhedena vibhutvabhedaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: With the remaining verses, he shows the classification of sovereignty through the classification of transformation (<s>parāvṛtti</s>).

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained
in the operation regarding all objects of all [faculties], upon the arising of twelve hundred qualities. || Msa_9.41 ||

body.text: pañcendriyaparāvṛttau dvividhaṃ vibhutvaṃ paramaṃ labhyate | sarveṣāṃ pañcānāmindriyāṇāṃ sarvapañcārthavṛttau | tatra pratyekaṃ dvādaśaguṇaśatotpattau |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of the five faculties, a twofold supreme sovereignty is attained: in the operation of all five faculties regarding all five [types of] objects; and therein, upon the arising of twelve hundred qualities for each [faculty].

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of mind too, supreme sovereignty is attained
in knowledge that follows sovereignty — non-conceptual and perfectly pure. || Msa_9.42 ||

body.text: manasaḥ parāvṛttau vibhutvānucare nirvikalpe suviśuddhe jñāne paramaṃ vibhutvaṃ labhyate | yena sahitaṃ sarvaṃ vibhutvajñānaṃ pravartate |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of mind, supreme sovereignty is attained in knowledge that follows sovereignty — non-conceptual and perfectly pure — with which all sovereign knowledge operates.

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of apprehension and purpose, supreme sovereignty is attained
in the purification of the [Buddha-]field, for displaying enjoyments as desired. || Msa_9.43 ||

body.text: arthaparāvṛttau udgrahaparāvṛttau ca kṣetraviśuddhivibhutvaṃ paramaṃ labhyate yena yathākāmaṃ bhogasaṃdarśanaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of purpose and through the transformation of apprehension, supreme sovereignty of field-purification is attained, by which one displays enjoyments as desired.

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained
in the unobstructed [operation] at all times of all knowledge-actions. || Msa_9.44 ||

body.text: vikalpaparāvṛttau sarveṣāṃ jñānānāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca sarvakālamavyāghāte paramaṃ vibhutvaṃ labhyate |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of conceptualization, supreme sovereignty is attained in the unobstructed [operation] at all times of all knowledges and actions.

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of the basis (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained —
the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s> in the immovable [and] undefiled stage. || Msa_9.45 ||

body.text: pratiṣṭhāparāvṛttāvapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ vibhutvaṃ labhyate | buddhānāmanāsravedhātau |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of the basis, supreme sovereignty of non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> is attained — of the <s>Buddhas</s> in the uncontaminated realm.

children.translated_text: Through the transformation of sexual union (<s>maithuna</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained
in the blissful abode of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and in seeing the defilement of wives. || Msa_9.46 ||

body.text: maithunasya parāvṛttau dvayorbuddhasukhavihāre ca dārāsaṃkleśadarśane ca |
body.translated_text: Through the transformation of sexual union, a twofold [sovereignty is attained]: in the blissful abode of the <s>Buddhas</s> and in seeing the defilement of wives.

children.translated_text: Through the reversal of the perception of space (<s>ākāśasaṃjñā</s>), supreme sovereignty is attained
in the fulfillment of intended purposes and in the manifestation of movement and form. || Msa_9.47 ||

body.text: ākāśasaṃjñāvyāvṛttau dvayoreva cintitārthasamṛddhau ca yena gaganagarbho bhavati | gatirūpavibhāvena ca yatheṣṭagamanādāśavaśī[kāśī]karaṇācca |
body.translated_text: Through the reversal of the perception of space, a twofold [sovereignty] indeed [is attained]: in the fulfillment of intended purposes, by which one becomes a 'womb of space' (<s>gaganagarbha</s>); and in the manifestation of movement and form, through going wherever one wishes and mastering visibility.

children.translated_text: Thus, through immeasurable transformation, immeasurable sovereignty is recognized,
with inconceivable performance of actions by the <s>Buddhas</s> in the undefiled basis. || Msa_9.48 ||

body.text: ityanena mukhenāprameyā parāvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, by this method, the transformation is immeasurable.

body.text: tatra cāprameyaṃ vibhutvamacintyakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ buddhānāmanāsrave dhātau veditavyam |
body.translated_text: And therein, the immeasurable sovereignty and inconceivable performance of actions should be understood as [pertaining to] the <s>Buddhas</s> in the uncontaminated realm.

body.text: tasyaiva buddhasya sattvaparipākanimittatve sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: On the instrumentality of that very <s>Buddha</s> for the ripening of beings, seven verses:

children.text: śubhe bṛddho loko vrajati suviśuddhau paramatāṃ
children.translated_text: When the world, grown in virtue, proceeds to the supremacy of perfect purity,
and when, without having begun in virtue, it proceeds to the supremacy of growth in virtue;

children.text: vrajatyevaṃ loko diśi diśi jinānāṃ sukathitai-
children.translated_text: thus the world proceeds in every direction through the well-spoken [teachings] of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) —

children.text: rapakvaḥ pakvo vā [na] ca punaraśeṣaṃ dhruvamiha || Msa_9.49 ||
children.translated_text: whether unripened or ripened — yet not entirely and definitively here. || Msa_9.49 ||

body.text: anena yādṛśasya paripākasya nimittaṃ bhavati taddarśayati | upacitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca vimuktau paramatāyāmanupacitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca kuśalamūlopacaye | apakvaḥ śubhavṛddhau paramatāṃ vrajana[n] pākaṃ vrajati pakvaḥ suviśuddhau paramatāṃ vrajati | evaṃ ca nityakālaṃ vrajati na ca niḥśeṣaṃ lokasyānantatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows what serves as the cause of what kind of ripening. For those with accumulated roots of merit, [the cause serves] for supremacy in liberation; for those without accumulated roots of merit, [it serves] for the accumulation of roots of merit. The unripened one, proceeding to the supremacy of growth in virtue, attains ripening; the ripened one proceeds to the supremacy of perfect purity. And thus it proceeds perpetually, yet not entirely, because of the infinity of the world.

children.translated_text: Having thus performed a practice [attained with difficulty], wonderful due to the conjunction of supreme qualities,
the eternal great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>), which is assuredly the refuge of those without refuge —
that which the resolute ones attain everywhere, always, at all times,
that is a wonder in the world; yet due to well-ordered practice, it is also not a wonder. || Msa_9.50 ||

body.text: anena dvitīyena paripavkānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ paripākasyāścaryaṃ nāścaryaṃ lakṣaṇam | sadā sarvasamayamiti nityaṃ nirantaraṃ ca tadanubhūya[rūpa]mārgacaraṇaṃ suvidhicaraṇam |
body.translated_text: By this second [verse], the wonder and non-wonder is the characteristic of the ripening of the ripened <s>bodhisattvas</s>. 'Always at all times' means perpetually and without interruption; experiencing that is well-ordered path-practice (<s>suvidhicaraṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: Somewhere he displays the wheel of the Dharma (<s>dharmacakra</s>) through hundreds of varied approaches;
somewhere [he shows] birth and disappearance, and elsewhere various conduct among people;
somewhere complete awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), and elsewhere <s>nirvāṇa</s>, repeatedly —

children.text: na ca sthānāttasmādvicalati sa sarvaṃ ca kurute || Msa_9.51 ||
children.translated_text: yet he does not move from that abode, and he does all this. || Msa_9.51 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena yugapadbahumukhaparipācanopāyaprayoge nimittatvaṃ darśayati | yathā yatrasthaḥ sattvān vinayati | vicitrā janacarī jātakabhedena | na ca sthānāccalatītyanāsravāddhātoḥ |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows the instrumentality in the application of the simultaneous method of ripening through many approaches. He trains beings wherever he is stationed. 'Various conduct among people' refers to the division of former-life stories (<s>jātaka</s>). 'He does not move from that abode' — that is, from the uncontaminated realm.

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> do not have such [thoughts as] 'this one is ripened by me' or 'this

children.text: pācyo 'yaṃ dehī api ca adhunāpācyata iti |
children.translated_text: embodied being is not to be ripened' or 'this one is now being ripened';
yet without [deliberate] conditioning, beings proceed
toward wholesome dharmas perpetually, in every direction, universally, through the three vehicles (<s>yānatraya</s>). || Msa_9.52 ||

body.text: anena caturthena tatparipākaprayoganimittatvamanabhisaṃskāreṇa darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the instrumentality of that ripening-application without deliberate conditioning (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>).

body.text: trayamukhamiti yānatrayeṇa |
body.translated_text: 'Through the three approaches' means through the three vehicles.

children.translated_text: Just as the sun, with its extended, clear, and radiant beams,
produces the ripening of crops in every direction universally,
so too the sun of the Dharma (<s>dharmārka</s>), with its rays of the qualities of the method of pacification (<s>praśama</s>),

children.text: prapākaṃ sasyānāṃ diśi diśi samantātprakurūte || Msa_9.53 ||
children.translated_text: produces the ripening of [the] crops [of beings] in every direction universally. || Msa_9.53 ||

body.text: anena pañcamenānabhisaṃskāraparipācanadṛṣṭāntaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this fifth [verse], he shows the illustration of ripening without deliberate conditioning.

children.translated_text: Just as from a single lamp there arises a great multitude of lamps,
immeasurable and innumerable, yet that [original lamp] does not thereby diminish;
so too from a single <s>Buddha</s>, there arises a great multitude of ripenings,

children.text: 'prameyo 'saṃkhyeyo na ca sa punareti[punarupaiti] vyayamataḥ || Msa_9.54 ||
children.translated_text: immeasurable and innumerable, yet that [<s>Buddha</s>] does not thereby diminish. || Msa_9.54 ||

body.text: anena ṣaṣṭhena paraṃparayā paripācanam |
body.translated_text: By this sixth [verse], [he shows] successive ripening.

children.text: yathā toyaistṛptiṃ vrajati na mahāsāgara iva
children.translated_text: Just as the great ocean does not reach satiety with waters,

children.text: na vṛddhiṃ vā yāti pratataviṣadāmbu praviśanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: nor does it increase when clear waters enter continuously,
so too the realm of the <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>bauddha dhātu</s>), with the continuous entry of purifications,

children.text: rnatṛptiṃ vṛddhiṃ vā vrajati paramāścaryamiha tat || Msa_9.55 ||
children.translated_text: neither reaches satiety nor increases — this is a supreme wonder here. || Msa_9.55 ||

body.text: anena saptamena paripavkānāṃ vimuktipraveśe samudrodāharaṇena dharmadhātoratṛptiṃ cāvakāśadānādavṛddhiṃ dhyānā[cāna]dhikatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this seventh [verse], with the illustration of the ocean regarding the entry into liberation of the ripened ones, [he shows] the non-satiety of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> due to granting space, and its non-increase due to there being nothing further to add.

body.text: dharmadhātuviśuddhau catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: On the purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, four verses:

children.translated_text: Having the characteristic of the purity of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all dharmas through the removal of the two [obscurations], and
having the characteristic of mastery and inexhaustibility of the object, knowledge, and their basis. || Msa_9.56 ||

body.text: eṣa svabhāvārthamārabhyaikaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is one verse concerning the meaning of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).

children.translated_text: It has the characteristic of the purity of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all dharmas from the two obscurations of affliction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and cognitive [obscuration] (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>),
and it has the characteristic of inexhaustibility and mastery of the object, its basis, and the knowledge of it.
The cultivation of <s>tathatā</s>-knowledge in all respects is the accomplishment;
the conferral of the twofold [benefit] upon all beings in every way, with inexhaustibility, is the fruit. || Msa_9.57 ||

body.text: eṣa hetvarthaṃ phalārthaṃ cārabhya dvitīyaḥ ślokaḥ | sarvatastathatājñānabhāvanā dharmadhātuviśuddhihetuḥ | sarvata iti sarvadharmaparyāyamukhaiḥ | sarvasattvānāṃ sarvathā hitasukhadvayādhānākṣayatā phalam |
body.translated_text: This is the second verse concerning the meaning of cause and fruit. The cultivation of <s>tathatā</s>-knowledge in all respects is the cause of the purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. 'In all respects' means through all approaches of the Dharma. The inexhaustible conferral of the twofold benefit and happiness upon all beings in every way is the fruit.

children.translated_text: Having the action of the application of means through emanations of body, speech, and mind,
endowed with immeasurable twofold gateways of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic retention). || Msa_9.58 ||

body.text: eṣa karmārthaṃ yogārthaṃ cārabhya tṛtīyaḥ ślokaḥ | trividhaṃ kāyādinirmāṇaṃ karma samādhidhāraṇīmukhābhyāṃ dvayena cāprameyeṇa puṇyajñānasaṃbhāreṇa samanvāgamo yogaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the third verse, beginning with the purpose of action and the purpose of yoga. The threefold emanation of body and so forth is the action. The possession of the two immeasurable accumulations of merit and knowledge through the two means of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) is the yoga.

children.translated_text: Having distinct functions through the essential nature body (<s>svabhāvakāya</s>), the Dharma body, the enjoyment body (<s>saṃbhogakāya</s>), and the emanation body (<s>nirmāṇakāya</s>),
this purified <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) is declared to be [the body] of the <s>Buddhas</s>. || Msa_9.59 ||

body.text: eṣa vṛttyarthamārabhya caturthaḥ ślokaḥ | svābhāvikasāṃbhogikanairmāṇikakāyavṛttyā bhinnavṛttikaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fourth verse, beginning with the purpose of function. It has distinct functions through the functions of the essential nature body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>), the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>), and the emanation body (<s>nairmāṇikakāya</s>).

body.text: buddhakāyavibhāge saptaślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the classification of the Buddha bodies:

children.translated_text: The essential nature body, then the enjoyment body, and the other — the emanation body;

children.text: kāyabhedā hi buddhānāṃ prathamastu dvayāśrayaḥ || Msa_9.60 ||
children.translated_text: these are indeed the divisions of the bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and the first is the basis of the [other] two. || Msa_9.60 ||

body.text: trividhaḥ kāyo buddhānām | svābhāviko dharmakāya āśrayaparāvṛttilakṣaṇaḥ | sāṃbhogiko yena parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu dharmasaṃbhogaṃ karoti | nairmāṇiko yena nirmāṇena sattvārthaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: The body of the <s>Buddhas</s> is threefold: the essential nature body is the <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma body), characterized by the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>). The enjoyment body is that by which one engages in the enjoyment of the Dharma in the assemblies. The emanation body is that by which one accomplishes the welfare of beings through emanation.

children.translated_text: The enjoyment body is differentiated in all realms by its retinues,
by fields, by names, by bodies, and by the activities of Dharma enjoyment. || Msa_9.61 ||

body.text: tatra sāṃbhogikaḥ sarvalokadhātuṣu parṣanmaṇḍalabuddhakṣetranāmaśarīradharmasaṃbhogakriyābhirbhinnaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the enjoyment body is differentiated in all world-realms by assemblies, Buddha-fields, names, physical forms, and the activities of Dharma enjoyment.

children.text: samaḥ sūkṣmaśca tacchiṣṭaḥ[cchilaṣṭaḥ] kāyaḥ svābhāviko mataḥ |
children.translated_text: The essential nature body is considered to be equal and subtle, and connected with that [enjoyment body];
it is the cause of the splendor of the enjoyment [body], for the display of enjoyment as desired. || Msa_9.62 ||

body.text: svābhāvikaḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ samo nirviśiṣṭatayā | sūkṣmo durjñānatayā | tena saṃbhogikena kāyena saṃbaddhaḥ saṃbhogavibhutve ca heturyatheṣṭaṃ bhogadarśanāya |
body.translated_text: The essential nature body is equal for all <s>Buddhas</s>, being without distinction. It is subtle, being difficult to know. It is connected with that enjoyment body, and is the cause of the splendor of enjoyment, for the display of enjoyment as desired.

children.translated_text: The immeasurable emanation of <s>Buddhas</s> is considered the emanation body;
the complete accomplishment of both purposes, in all its aspects, is established in the two [bodies]. || Msa_9.63 ||

body.text: nairmāṇikastu kāyo buddhānāmaprameyaprabhedaṃ buddhanirmāṇaṃ sāṃbhogikaḥ svārthasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ | nairmāṇikaḥ parārthasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ | evaṃ dvayārthasaṃpattiryathākramaṃ dvayoḥ pratiṣṭhitā sāṃbhogike ca kāye nairmāṇike ca |
body.translated_text: The emanation body of the <s>Buddhas</s> is the Buddha-emanation of immeasurable varieties. The enjoyment body is characterized by the accomplishment of self-benefit. The emanation body is characterized by the accomplishment of the benefit of others. Thus, the accomplishment of both purposes is established, respectively, in the two — the enjoyment body and the emanation body.

children.translated_text: Through the displays of crafts, birth, great awakening, and perpetual <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
this emanation body of the <s>Buddha</s> is a great skillful means for liberation. || Msa_9.64 ||

body.text: sa punarnirmāṇakāyaḥ sadā vineyārthaṃ śilpasya vīṇāvādanādibhiḥ | janmanaścābhisaṃbodheśca nirvāṇasya ca darśanairvimocane mahopāyatvātparārthasaṃpattilakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: That emanation body, always for the benefit of those to be trained, through the displays of crafts such as playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and so forth, of birth, of perfect awakening, and of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — should be understood as characterized by the accomplishment of the benefit of others, being a great skillful means for liberation.

children.translated_text: The totality of the bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be understood through the three bodies;
the welfare of self and others, together with its basis, is shown by the three bodies. || Msa_9.65 ||

body.text: tribhiśca kāyairbuddhānāṃ sarvakāyasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ | ebhistribhiḥ kāyaiḥ sāśrayaḥ svaparārtho nidarśitaḥ | dvayoḥ svaparārthaprabhāvitatvāt dvayośca tadāśritatvādyathā pūrvamuktam |
body.translated_text: The totality of all the bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be understood through the three bodies. By these three bodies, the welfare of self and others, together with its basis, is shown — because both [bodies of enjoyment and emanation] are produced for the welfare of self and others, and because both are based on that [essential nature body], as was stated before.

children.translated_text: They are considered equal in basis, in intention, and in action;
and in those [three bodies], eternity is [established] through nature, through non-cessation, and through continuity. || Msa_9.66 ||

body.text: te ca trayaḥ kāyāḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ yathākramaṃ tribhirnirviśeṣāḥ, āśrayeṇa dharmadhātorabhinnatvāt, āśayena pṛthagbuddhāśayasyābhāvāt | karmaṇā ca sādhāraṇakarmakatvāt | teṣu ca triṣu kāyeṣu yathākramaṃ trividhā nityatā veditavyā yena nityakāyāstathāgatā ucyante | prakṛtyā nityatā svābhāvikasya svabhāvena nityatvāt | asraṃsanena sāṃbhogikasya dharmasaṃbhogāvicchedāt | prabandhena nairmāṇikasyāntarvyaye[rdhāya]punaḥ punarnirmāṇadarśanāt |
body.translated_text: Those three bodies are without distinction for all <s>Buddhas</s> in three ways respectively: in basis, because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is undifferentiated; in intention, because there is no separate Buddha-intention; and in action, because their activity is shared. And in those three bodies, threefold eternity should be understood respectively, by which the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are said to have eternal bodies: eternity by nature belongs to the essential nature body, because it is eternal by its own nature; eternity by non-cessation belongs to the enjoyment body, because of the uninterrupted enjoyment of the Dharma; eternity by continuity belongs to the emanation body, because of the repeated display of emanation after passing away.

body.text: buddhajñānavibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Ten verses on the classification of Buddha knowledge:

children.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge (<s>ādarśajñāna</s>) is immovable; the three [other] knowledges are based upon it —
namely, the knowledge of equality (<s>samatājñāna</s>), the knowledge of discernment (<s>pratyavekṣājñāna</s>), and the knowledge of duty-accomplishment (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>). || Msa_9.67 ||

body.text: caturvidhaṃ buddhānāṃ jñānamādarśajñānaṃ samatājñānaṃ pratyavekṣājñānaṃ kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānaṃ ca | ādarśajñānamacalaṃ trīṇī jñānāni tadāśritāni calāni |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> is fourfold: mirror-like knowledge (<s>ādarśajñāna</s>), knowledge of equality (<s>samatājñāna</s>), knowledge of discernment (<s>pratyavekṣājñāna</s>), and knowledge of duty-accomplishment (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>). Mirror-like knowledge is immovable; the three [other] knowledges are based upon it and are movable.

children.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge is unlimited, ever-present,

children.text: sarvajñeyeṣvasaṃmūḍhaṃ na ca teṣvāmukhaṃ sadā || Msa_9.68 ||
children.translated_text: unconfused regarding all knowables, and yet never turned toward them. || Msa_9.68 ||

body.text: ādarśajñānamamaparicchinnaṃ deśataḥ sadānugaṃ kālataḥ | saervajñeyeṣvasaṃmūḍhaṃ sadāvaraṇavigamāt, na ca teṣvāmukhamanākāratvāt |
body.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge is unlimited in scope, ever-present in time, unconfused regarding all knowables because of the permanent removal of obscurations, and yet never turned toward them because of being without particular cognized forms.

children.translated_text: Because it is the cause of all knowledges, it resembles the form of a great knowledge;
and there is the enjoyment-Buddhahood, because of the arising of the reflections of knowledge in it. || Msa_9.69 ||

body.text: teṣāṃ ca samatādijñānānāṃ sarvaprakārāṇāṃ hetutvātsarvajñānānāmākaropam | saṃbhogabuddhatvatajjñānapratibimbodayācca tadādarśajñānāmityucyate |
body.translated_text: Because it is the cause of all those knowledges of equality and so forth, in all their forms, it resembles the form of all knowledges. And it is called mirror-like knowledge because of the enjoyment-Buddhahood and the arising of the reflections of those knowledges in it.

children.translated_text: The knowledge of equality toward beings, purified through cultivation, is immaculate;
the knowledge of equality is considered to be established in non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || Msa_9.70 ||

body.text: yabdodhisattvenābhisamayakāleṣu [sattveṣu] samatājñānaṃ pratilabdhaṃ tadbhāvanāśuddhito bodhiprāptasyāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇe niviṣṭaṃ samatājñānamiṣyate |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of equality that the <s>bodhisattva</s> obtained at the time of realization toward beings — that, purified through cultivation upon attaining awakening, is the knowledge of equality that is considered to be established in the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: Through great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), it is considered to be ever-present at all times,
and it displays Buddha-images in accordance with the faith of beings. || Msa_9.71 ||

body.text: mahāmaitrīkaruṇābhyāṃ sarvakālānugaṃ yathādhimokṣaṃ ca sattvānāṃ buddhabimbanidarśakam | yataḥ kecitsattvāstathāgataṃ nīlavarṇaṃ paśyanti kecitpītavarṇamityevamādi |
body.translated_text: Through great loving-kindness and compassion, it is ever-present at all times and displays Buddha-images in accordance with the faith of beings. For some beings see the <s>Tathāgata</s> as blue-colored, some see him as yellow-colored, and so forth.

children.translated_text: The knowledge of discernment is always unobstructed regarding knowables,
and it is like a treasury of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions) and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). || Msa_9.72 ||
In the assembly, it displays all splendors,
it cuts through all doubts, and it causes the great Dharma to rain down. || Msa_9.73 ||

body.text: pratyavekṣaṇakaṃ jñānaṃ yathāślokam |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of discernment is as stated in the verses.

children.translated_text: The knowledge of duty-accomplishment, through emanations in all realms,
manifold, immeasurable, and inconceivable, accomplishes the welfare of all beings. || Msa_9.74 ||

body.text: kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānaṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu nirmāṇairnānāprakārairaprameyairacintyaiśca sarvasattvārthakam |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of duty-accomplishment accomplishes the welfare of all beings in all world-realms through emanations of various kinds, immeasurable and inconceivable.

children.translated_text: Through the divisions of the accomplishment of duties, in number and in fields, always,

children.text: acintyaṃ buddhanirmāṇaṃ vijñeyaṃ tacca sarvathā || Msa_9.75 ||
children.translated_text: the emanation of the <s>Buddha</s> should be known as inconceivable, and that in every way. || Msa_9.75 ||

body.text: tacca buddhanirmāṇaṃ sadā sarvathā cācintyaṃ veditavyaṃ | kṛtyakriyābhedataḥ saṃkhyāta [taḥ] kṣetrataśca |
body.translated_text: That Buddha-emanation should be understood as always inconceivable in every way — in the divisions of the performance of duties, in number, and in fields.

children.translated_text: From retention, from an equal mind, from the correct illumination of the Dharma,
and from the accomplishment of duties — the arising of the four knowledges [is established]. || Msa_9.76 ||

body.text: tatra dhāraṇāt śrutānāṃ dharmāṇām | samacittatā sarvasattveṣvātmaparasamatayā | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, from the retention of the <s>dharmas</s> that have been heard. The equal mind is the equality of self and other toward all beings. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: buddhānekatvāpṛthaktveślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the non-unity and non-separateness of <s>Buddhas</s>:

children.translated_text: Because of the difference of lineages, because of non-futility, because of completeness, and also because of beginninglessness,
there is not a single Buddhahood; and there is multiplicity in the undefiled basis. || Msa_9.77 ||

body.text: eka eva buddha ityetanneṣyate | kiṃ kāraṇam | gotrabhedāt | anantā hi buddhagotrāḥ sattvāḥ | tatraika evābhisaṃbuddho nānye 'bhisaṃmotsyanta iti kuta etat | puṇyajñānasaṃbhāravaiyarthyaṃ ca syādanyeṣāṃ bodhisattvānāmanabhisaṃbodhānna ca yuktaṃ vaiyarthyam | tasmādavaiyarthyādapi naika eva buddhaḥ sattvārthakriyāsākalyaṃ ca na syāt | buddhasya buddhatve kasyacidapratiṣṭhāpanādetacca na yuktam | na ca kaścidādibuddho 'sti vinā saṃbhāreṇa buddhatvāyogādvinā cānyena buddhena saṃsthānā [saṃbhārā]yogādityanāditvādapyeko buddhau na yuktaḥ | bahutvamapi neṣyate buddhānāṃ dharmakāyasyābhedādanāsrave dhātau |
body.translated_text: That there is only one <s>Buddha</s> — this is not accepted. Why? Because of the difference of lineages — for beings of the Buddha-lineage are infinite. If only one among them were to attain perfect awakening and the others were not to attain it — how could that be? And there would be futility of the accumulations of merit and knowledge for the other <s>bodhisattvas</s> who would not attain awakening — and futility is not reasonable. Therefore, because of non-futility as well, there is not a single <s>Buddha</s>. And the completeness of the activity of benefiting beings would not exist — for it is not reasonable that the <s>Buddha</s>, upon attaining Buddhahood, would not establish someone [in it]. Nor is there a first <s>Buddha</s>, because Buddhahood is not possible without the accumulations, and the accumulations are not possible without another <s>Buddha</s> [who inspires them] — thus, because of beginninglessness as well, a single <s>Buddha</s> is not reasonable. Multiplicity too is not accepted for <s>Buddhas</s>, because of the non-differentiation of the <s>dharmakāya</s> in the undefiled realm.

body.text: buddhatvopāyapraveśe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on entry into the means of [attaining] Buddhahood:

children.translated_text: That very non-existence [of the imagined nature] is the supreme existence;
and the complete non-apprehension [of the imagined] is considered the supreme apprehension. || Msa_9.78 ||

body.text: yā parikalpitena svabhāvenāvidyamānatā saiva paramā vidyamānatā pariniṣpannena svabhāvena | yaśca sarvathānupalambhaḥ parikalpitasya svabhāvasya sa eva parama upalambhaḥ pariniṣpanna svabhāvasya |
body.translated_text: The non-existence through the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>) is itself the supreme existence through the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>). And the complete non-apprehension of the imagined nature is itself the supreme apprehension of the perfected nature.

children.translated_text: The supreme cultivation is the endeavor of those who do not perceive cultivation;

children.text: pratilambhaḥ paraśceṣṭaḥ pratilambhaṃ na paśyatām || Msa_9.79 ||
children.translated_text: and the supreme attainment is the endeavor of those who do not perceive attainment. || Msa_9.79 ||

body.text: saiva paramā bhāvanā yo bhāvanāyā anupalambhaḥ | sa eva paramaḥ pratilambho yaḥ pratilambhānupalambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: That very [state] is the supreme cultivation which is the non-apprehension of cultivation. That very [state] is the supreme attainment which is the non-apprehension of attainment.

children.translated_text: For those who perceive the gravity, the long time, the sign, and the effort of oneself —
for such conceited <s>bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is declared to be far away. || Msa_9.80 ||

body.text: ye ca gurutvaṃ buddhatvaṃ paśyanti adbhutadharmayuktam | dīrghaṃ ca kālaṃ paśyanti tatsamudāgamāya | nimittaṃ ca paśyanti cittālambanam | ātmanaśca vīryaṃ vayamārabdhavīryā buddhatvaṃ prāpsyāma iti |
body.translated_text: Those who perceive the gravity of Buddhahood as endowed with wondrous qualities, and who perceive the long time for its attainment, and who perceive the sign — the mental object — and who perceive their own effort, thinking 'We who have undertaken effort will attain Buddhahood' —

body.text: teṣāmevaṃmānināṃ bodhisattvānāmaupalambhikatvāt dūre bodhirnirūpyate |
body.translated_text: for such conceited <s>bodhisattvas</s>, because of their apprehending, awakening is declared to be far away.

children.translated_text: For those who perceive that all this as described is merely conceptualization,
for such non-conceptualizing <s>bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is declared to be attained. || Msa_9.81 ||

body.text: kalyanāmātraṃ tvetatsarvamiti paśyatāṃ tasyāpi kalpanāmātrasyāvikalpanādakalpabodhisattvānāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāvasthāyāmarthataḥ prāptaiva bodhirityucyate |
body.translated_text: But for those who perceive that all this is merely conceptualization, and who do not even conceptualize that mere conceptualization — for such non-conceptualizing <s>bodhisattvas</s>, at the stage of attaining patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>), awakening is said to be virtually attained.

body.text: buddhānāmanyonyanai[nyai]kakāryatve catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the non-unity of action among <s>Buddhas</s>:

children.translated_text: Rivers with separate courses and separate waters, with little water, performing separate functions,
enjoyable for only small creatures dwelling in water — [such are rivers] before entering the ocean. || Msa_9.82 ||
And having entered the ocean, they all become of one course and one great water,
mixed, performing one function, and always greatly enjoyable for the multitudes of creatures dwelling in water. || Msa_9.83 ||
The wise ones with separate bases and separate understandings, with little realization, performing separate individual functions,
enjoyable for only limited beings — [such they are] before entering Buddhahood. || Msa_9.84 ||
And having entered Buddhahood, they all become of one basis and one great realization,

children.text: miśraikakāryāśca mahopabhogyāḥ sadā mahāsattvagaṇasya te hi || Msa_9.85 ||
children.translated_text: mixed, performing one function, and always greatly enjoyable for the multitudes of great beings. || Msa_9.85 ||

body.text: tatra bhinnāśrayā nadyaḥ svabhājanabhedāt | kṛtyapṛthaktvakāryāḥ pṛthaktvena kṛtyakaraṇāt | tanūpabhogyā ityalpānāmupabhogyāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, rivers with separate courses — because of the difference of their own vessels. Performing separate functions — because of performing functions separately. Enjoyable for only small [beings] — meaning enjoyable for few. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: buddhatvaprotsāhane ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the encouragement to [attain] Buddhahood:

children.translated_text: Thus, because of the incomparable practice of pure virtues, because of the <s>Buddha</s> stage being the cause of benefit and happiness,
and because it produces wholesome, supreme, and inexhaustible happiness — one of virtuous mind is worthy of attaining the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). || Msa_9.86 ||

body.text: nirūpamasukladharmayogāt svārthasaṃpattitaḥ | hitasukhahetutvācca buddhatvasya parārthasaṃpattiḥ | anavadyotkṛṣṭākṣayasukhākaratvācca sukhavihāro viśeṣataḥ | buddhimānahīnabodhicittamādātuṃ tatpraṇidhānaparigrahāt |
body.translated_text: Because of the incomparable practice of pure virtues — this is the accomplishment of self-benefit. Because Buddhahood is the cause of benefit and happiness — this is the accomplishment of the benefit of others. And because of producing blameless, eminent, and inexhaustible happiness — this is the special comfortable abiding. The intelligent one should adopt the <s>bodhicitta</s> through the embrace of that aspiration.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre bodhyadhikāro navamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the ninth chapter on awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) ||

body.text:
daśamodhikāraḥ
uddānam |
body.translated_text: Tenth chapter. Synopsis:

children.text: ādiḥ siddhiḥ śaraṇaṃ gotraṃ citte tathaiva cotpādaḥ |
children.translated_text: The beginning, the accomplishment, the refuge, the lineage, and likewise in the mind, the generation [of the awakening mind];
the welfare of self and others, the meaning of reality, power, ripening, and awakening. || Msa_10.1 ||

body.text:
eṣa ca bodhyadhikāra ādimārabhya yāvat bodhipaṭalānusāreṇānugantavyaḥ |
adhimuktiprabhedalakṣaṇavibhāge ślokau |
body.translated_text:
This chapter on awakening should be followed from the beginning up to the chapter on awakening itself.
Two verses on the analysis of the classification and characteristics of faith (<s>adhimukti</s>):

children.text: jātā-jātā grāhikā grāhyabhūtā mitrādāttā svātmato bhrāntikā ca |
children.translated_text: Arisen and not-yet-arisen, apprehending and that which is apprehended, received from a spiritual friend and [arising] from oneself, erroneous and

children.text: abhrāntānyā āmukhā naiva cānyā ghoṣācārā caiṣikā cekṣikā ca || Msa_10.2 ||
children.translated_text: non-erroneous, proximate and not proximate, proceeding from hearing, investigative, and contemplative. || Msa_10.2 ||

body.text: jātā atītapratyutpannā | ajātā anāgatā | grāhikā ādhyātmikā[kī] yayālambanamadhimucyate | grāhyabhūtā bāhyā yānā[mā] lambanatvenādhimucyate | mitrādāttā audārikī | svātmataḥ sūkṣmā | bhrāntikā hīnā viparītādhimokṣāt | abhrāntikā praśāntā [praṇītā] | āmukhā antike samavahitapratyayatvāt | anāmukhā dūre viparyayāt | ghoṣācārā śrutamayī | eṣikā cintāmayī | īkṣikā bhāvanāmayī pratyavekṣaṇāt |
body.translated_text: Arisen means past and present. Not-yet-arisen means future. Apprehending means internal — that by which one is convinced of the object. That which is apprehended means external — that which is taken as the object of conviction. Received from a [spiritual] friend means coarse. [Arising] from oneself means subtle. Erroneous means inferior, due to perverted conviction. Non-erroneous means excellent. Proximate means near, because of being produced by an immediate condition. Not proximate means distant, due to the opposite. Proceeding from hearing means born of hearing (<s>śrutamayī</s>). Investigative means born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī</s>). Contemplative means born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī</s>), because of [direct] examination.

children.translated_text: Vulnerable, mixed with opposing factors, and unmixed; inferior and exalted; obstructed and unobstructed;

children.text: yuktāyuktā saṃbhṛtāsaṃbhṛtā ca gāḍhaṃ viṣṭā dūragā cādhimuktiḥ || Msa_10.3 ||
children.translated_text: engaged and disengaged; equipped and unequipped; deeply entered and far-reaching — such is faith (<s>adhimukti</s>). || Msa_10.3 ||

body.text: hāryā mṛdvī | vyavakīrṇā madhyā | avyavakīrṇā vipakṣairadhimātrā | hinānyayāne | udārāmahāyāne | āvṛtā sāvaraṇā viśeṣagamanāya | anāvṛtā nirāvaraṇā | yuktā sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogāt | ayuktā tadvirahitā | saṃbhṛtādhigamayogyā | asaṃbhṛtā viparyayāt | gāḍhaṃ viṣṭā bhūmipraviṣṭā | dūragā pariśiṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu |
body.translated_text: Vulnerable means weak. Mixed [with opposing factors] means middling. Unmixed with opposing factors means intense. Inferior means in the lesser vehicle. Exalted means in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Obstructed means with obscurations, for the purpose of attaining distinction. Unobstructed means without obscurations. Engaged means through continuous and respectful application. Disengaged means devoid of that. Equipped means ready for attainment. Unequipped means the opposite. Deeply entered means having entered a [<s>bodhisattva</s>] stage. Far-reaching means on the remaining stages.

body.text: adhimuktiparipanthe trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the obstacles to faith:

children.translated_text: Inattentiveness, laziness, confusion in practice,
bad companions, weakness in wholesome [roots], and improper mental engagement. || Msa_10.4 ||

body.text: jātāyā amanasikārabāhulyaṃ paripanthaḥ | ajātāyāḥ kauśīdyam, grāhyagrāhakabhūtāyā yogavibhramaḥ, tathaivābhiniveśāt | mitrādāttāyāḥ kumitram, viparītagrāhaṇāt | svātmato 'dhimukteḥ kuśalamūladaurbalyam | abhrāntāyā ayoniśo amanasikāraḥ [manasikāraḥ] paripanthastadvirodhitvāt |
body.translated_text: For the arisen [faith], inattentiveness is the obstacle. For the not-yet-arisen, laziness. For the apprehending and the apprehended, confusion in practice — because of clinging to them. For that received from a friend, a bad companion — because of receiving wrongly. For the faith [arising] from oneself, weakness of wholesome roots. For the non-erroneous, improper mental engagement is the obstacle, because it is contrary to it.

children.translated_text: Heedlessness and little learning, and contentment with mere hearing and little reflection,
and conceit from mere calm, and likewise lack of familiarity are considered [obstacles]. || Msa_10.5 ||

body.text: āmukhāyāḥ pramādaḥ, tasyā apramādakṛtatvāt | ghoṣācārāyā alpaśrutatvam, nītārthasūtrāntāśravaṇāt | eṣikāyāḥ śrutamātrasaṃtuṣṭatvamalpacintāsaṃtuṣṭatvaṃ ca | īkṣikāyāścintāmātrasaṃtuṣṭatvaṃ śamathamātrābhimānaśca | hāryāvyavakīrṇayoraparijayaḥ paripanthaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the proximate [faith], heedlessness — because it is produced by diligence. For that proceeding from hearing, little learning — from not hearing sūtras of definitive meaning. For the investigative, contentment with mere hearing and contentment with little reflection. For the contemplative, contentment with mere reflection and conceit from mere <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). For the vulnerable and the mixed, lack of familiarity is the obstacle.

children.translated_text: Non-alarm and alarm, obstruction and disengagement,
and lack of equipment — these should be known as obstacles to faith. || Msa_10.6 ||

body.text: hīnāyā anudvegaḥ saṃsārāt | udārāyā udvegaḥ anāvṛtāyāścāvṛtiḥ | yuktāyā ayuktatā | saṃbhṛtāyā asaṃbhṛtiḥ paripanthaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the inferior [faith], non-alarm from <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the exalted, alarm. For the unobstructed, obstruction. For the engaged, disengagement. For the equipped, lack of equipment is the obstacle.

body.text: adhimuktāvanuśaṃse pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the benefits of faith:

children.translated_text: Great merit, freedom from remorse, happiness of mind, great comfort,

children.text: avipraṇāśaḥ sthairyaṃ na viśeṣagamanaṃ tathā || Msa_10.7 ||
children.translated_text: non-destruction, stability, and likewise attainment of distinction. || Msa_10.7 ||
And realization of the Dharma, and the supreme attainment of the welfare of self and others,
and swift attainment of supernatural knowledge — these are the benefits of faith. || Msa_10.8 ||

body.text: jātāyāṃ pratyutpannāyāṃ puṇyaṃ mahat | atītāyāmakaukṛtyamavipratisārāt | grāhikāyāṃ grāhyabhūtāyāṃ ca mahatsaumanasyaṃ samādhiyogāt | kalyāṇamitrajanitāyāmavipraṇāśaḥ | svayamadhimuktau sthairyam | bhrā[abhrā]ntikāyāmāmukhāyāṃ śrutamayādikāyāṃ ca yāvat madhyāyāṃ viśeṣagamanam | adhimātrāyāṃ dharmābhisamayaḥ | hīnāyāṃ svārthaprāptiḥ | udārāyāṃ parārthaprāptiḥ paramā | anāvṛtayuktasaṃbhṛtādiṣu śuklapakṣāsu kṣiprābhijñatvamanuśaṃsaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the arisen, present [faith], there is great merit. For the past, freedom from remorse — because of absence of regret. For the apprehending and apprehended, great happiness of mind — from the practice of <s>samādhi</s>. For that generated by a good friend, non-destruction. For self-generated faith, stability. For the non-erroneous, proximate, and those born of hearing and so forth, up to the middling, attainment of distinction. For the intense, realization of the Dharma. For the inferior, attainment of self-benefit. For the exalted, the supreme attainment of the benefit of others. For the unobstructed, engaged, equipped, and so forth — those on the wholesome side — swift attainment of supernatural knowledge is the benefit.

children.translated_text: For the desirous, that [faith] is like a dog; for the meditative, it resembles a tortoise;

children.text: bhṛtyopamā svārthināṃ sā rājaprakhyā parārthinām || Msa_10.9 ||
children.translated_text: for the self-interested, it is like a servant; for the altruistic, it resembles a king. || Msa_10.9 ||

body.text: yatha śvā duḥkhārtaḥ satatamavitṛptaḥ kṣudhitako yathā kūrmaścāsau jalavivarake saṃkucitakaḥ | yathā bhṛtyo nityamupacakitamūrtirvicarati | yathā rājā ājñāviṣaye vaśa[cakra?]vartī viharati |
body.translated_text: Just as a dog, afflicted by suffering, is constantly unsatisfied and hungry; just as a tortoise contracts in a pool of water; just as a servant always moves about with a frightened demeanor; just as a king rules over the domain of his command —

children.translated_text: so too, for those engaged in the purposes of the desirous, the stable, the self-interested, and those working for others,
the distinction should be known through the various kinds of faith always;
having properly understood the supremacy of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,

children.text: bhṛśaṃ tasmin dhīraḥ satatamiha tābheva vṛṇuyāt || Msa_10.10 ||
children.translated_text: the wise one should always ardently choose it through those very [qualities]. || Msa_10.10 ||

body.text: api khalu kāmināmadhimuktiḥ śvasadṛśī laukikasamādhigatānāṃ kūrmaprakhyāsvārthavatāṃ bhṛtyopamā | rājaprakhyā parārthavatām | etamevārthaṃ pareṇopapādya mahāyānādhimuktau samādāpayati |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the faith of the desirous is like a dog; of those who have attained worldly <s>samādhi</s>, it resembles a tortoise; of the self-interested, it is like a servant; of the altruistic, it resembles a king. Having established this very meaning through this [analysis], he encourages faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: adhimuktilayapratiṣedhe ślokāḥ[kaḥ] |
body.translated_text: A verse on the prohibition of the decline of faith:

children.translated_text: Beings who are human attain perfect awakening at every moment;

children.text: aprameyā yataḥ sattvā layaṃ nāto 'dhivāsayet || Msa_10.11 ||
children.translated_text: since beings are immeasurable, therefore one should not acquiesce in decline. || Msa_10.11 ||

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇairlayo na yuktaḥ | yato manuṣa[ṣya]bhūtā bodhiṃ prāpnuvanti | nityaṃ prāpnuvanti | aprameyāśca prāpnuvanti |
body.translated_text: For three reasons, decline is not reasonable: because those who are human attain awakening, because they always attain it, and because immeasurable [beings] attain it.

body.text: adhimuktipuṇyaviśeṣaṇe dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the distinction of the merit of faith:

children.text: yathā puṇyaṃ prasavate pareṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dadat |
children.translated_text: Just as merit is produced for one who gives food to others,

children.text: na tu svayaṃ sa bhuñjānastathā puṇyamahodayaḥ || Msa_10.12 ||
children.translated_text: but not for one who eats it oneself — such is the great arising of merit. || Msa_10.12 ||
The merit stated in the sūtras is obtained from the Dharma taught based on the welfare of others,
but it is not obtained from the Dharma taught based on self-interest. || Msa_10.13 ||

body.text: yathā bhojanaṃ dadataḥ puṇyamutpadyate parārthādhikārāt | na tu svayaṃ bhuñjānasya svārthādhikārāt | evaṃ parārthāśrayadeśitāt mahāyānadharmātteṣu teṣu [mahāyāna] sūtreṣūktaḥ puṇyodayo mahāṃllabhyate | na tu svārthāśrayadeśitāt śrāvakayānadharmāt |
body.translated_text: Just as merit arises for one who gives food, because of the concern for the welfare of others, but not for one who eats it oneself, because of the concern for self-interest — so too, the great arising of merit stated in those <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras is obtained from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma taught based on the welfare of others, but not from the Dharma of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Vehicle of Hearers) taught based on self-interest.

body.text: adhimuktiphalaparigrahe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on embracing the fruit of faith:

children.text: iti vipulagatau mahogha[mahārya]dharme janiya [parijanayan?] sadā matimānmahādhimuktim |
children.translated_text: Thus, the intelligent one, always generating great faith in the vast and noble Dharma of extensive scope,
attains the increase of vast and constant merit, and the greatness of self through incomparable qualities. || Msa_10.14 ||

body.text: yatra yādṛśyādhimuktyā yo yatphalaṃ parigṛhṇāti | vistīrṇe mahāyānadharme 'pari[hā]ṇī[parijananī?] yayodārādhimuktyā matimān trividhaṃ phalaṃ parigṛhṇāti | vipulapuṇyavṛddhiṃ tasyā evādhimuktervṛddhiṃ taddhetukāṃ cātulyaguṇamahātmatāṃ buddhatvam |
body.translated_text: Concerning where, through what kind of faith, one embraces what fruit: the intelligent one, through exalted faith in the extensive <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma that is non-declining, embraces a threefold fruit — the increase of vast merit, the increase of that very faith because of it, and the incomparable greatness of self through qualities, which is Buddhahood.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre adhimuktyadhikāro daśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the tenth chapter on faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) ||

body.text: ekādaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Eleventh chapter:

body.text: dharmaparyeṣṭyadhikāre ālambanaparyeṣṭau catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the search for the object in the chapter on the search for the Dharma (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>):

children.translated_text: The three <s>piṭakas</s> (baskets), or the two in terms of grouping, are deemed established by nine reasons;
through impression, awakening, calming, and penetration — they liberate. || Msa_11.1 ||

body.text: piṭakatrayaṃ sūtravinayābhidharmāḥ | tadeva trayaṃ hīnayānāgra[mahā?]yānabhedena dvayaṃ bhavati | śrāvapiṭakaṃbodhisattvapiṭakaṃ ca | tatpunastrayaṃ dvayaṃ vā [ca?]kenārthena piṭakamityāha | saṃgrahataḥ sarvajñeyārthasaṃgrahādveditavyam | kena kāraṇena trayam | navabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ, vicikitsāpratipakṣeṇa sūtram, yo yatrārthe saṃśayitastasya tanniścayārthaṃ deśanāt | antadvayānuyogapratipakṣeṇa vinayaḥ sāvadyaparibhogapratiṣedhataḥ kāmasukhallikānuyogāntasya, anavadyaparibhogānujñānata ātmaklamathānuyogāntasya | svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarṣapratipakṣeṇābhidharmo 'viparītadharmalakṣaṇābhidyotanāt |
body.translated_text: The three <s>piṭakas</s> are the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s>. Those very three, through the division into the lesser vehicle and the great vehicle, become two: the <s>Śrāvakapiṭaka</s> and the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>. Why are those three, or two, called <s>piṭakas</s>? He says: in terms of grouping — because they comprehend the meaning of all knowables. For what reason are there three? By nine reasons: the <s>Sūtra</s> as the antidote to doubt — because it teaches for the purpose of resolving the doubt of whoever is doubtful about any meaning. The <s>Vinaya</s> as the antidote to adherence to the two extremes — through the prohibition of blameworthy enjoyment, [it is the antidote] to the extreme of devotion to sensual pleasure; and through the permission of blameless enjoyment, [it is the antidote] to the extreme of devotion to self-mortification. The <s>Abhidharma</s> as the antidote to clinging to self-views — because it illuminates the non-perverted characteristics of phenomena.

body.text: punaḥ śikṣātrayadeśanā sūtreṇa adhiśīlādhicittasaṃpādanatā vinayena śīlavato 'vipratisārādavipratisāreṇa[dikrameṇa] samādhilābhāt | adhiprajñāsaṃpādanābhidharmeṇāviparītārthapravicayāt | punardharmārthadeśanā sūtreṇa | dharmārthamippattirvinayena kleśavinayasaṃyuktasya tayoḥ prativedhāt | dharmārthasāṃkathyaviniścayakauśalyamabhidharmeṇeti |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through the <s>Sūtra</s>, the teaching of the threefold training; through the <s>Vinaya</s>, the accomplishment of higher moral discipline and higher mind — because for the morally disciplined, from the absence of remorse, through the successive stages, there is the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>; through the <s>Abhidharma</s>, the accomplishment of higher wisdom — because of the non-perverted analysis of meaning. Furthermore, through the <s>Sūtra</s>, the teaching of the Dharma and its meaning; through the <s>Vinaya</s>, the attainment of the Dharma and its meaning — because of the penetration of both, being connected with the training in [removal of] afflictions; through the <s>Abhidharma</s>, skill in the determination of the discussion of the Dharma and its meaning.

body.text: ebhirnavabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ piṭakatrayamiṣṭam | tacca saṃsārādvimocanārtham | kathaṃ punastadvimocayati | vāsanabodhanaśamanaprativedhaistadvimocayati | śrūtena cittavāsanataḥ | cintayā bodhanataḥ | bhāvanayā śamathena śamanataḥ | vipaśyanayā prativedhataḥ |
body.translated_text: By these nine reasons, the three <s>piṭakas</s> are deemed established. And they are for the purpose of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. How then do they liberate? Through impression, awakening, calming, and penetration, they liberate: through hearing, by impressing the mind; through reflection, by awakening; through meditation, through <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), by calming; through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), by penetration.

children.translated_text: The <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Abhidharma</s>, and <s>Vinaya</s> are considered to have fourfold meaning in summary;
through knowledge of them, the wise one attains omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). || Msa_11.2 ||

body.text: te ca sūtravinayabhidharmāḥ pratyekaṃ caturvidhārthāḥ samāsatasteṣāṃ jñānābdodhisattvaḥ sarvajñatāṃ prāpnoti | śrāvakastvekasyā api gāthāyā arthamājñāyāstravakṣayaṃprāpnoti |
