body.translated_text: Those <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s> each have fourfold meaning in summary. Through knowledge of them, the <s>bodhisattva</s> attains omniscience. But the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer), having understood the meaning of even a single <s>gāthā</s> (verse), attains the exhaustion of the outflows.

children.translated_text: The <s>Sūtra</s> [has its fourfold meaning] through basis, characteristic, phenomena, and indication of meaning;
and the <s>Abhidharma</s> through facing [<s>nirvāṇa</s>], through repetition, through overcoming, and through approach. || Msa_11.3 ||

body.text: kathaṃ pratyekaṃ caturvidhārthaḥ | āśrayalakṣaṇadharmārthasūcanātsūtram | tatrāśrayo yatra deśe deśitaṃ yena yasmai ca | lakṣaṇaṃ saṃvṛttisatyalakṣaṇaṃ paramārthasatyalakṣaṇaṃ ca | dharmāḥ skandhāyatanadhātvāhārapratītyasamutpādādayaḥ | artho 'nusaṃdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: How does each have fourfold meaning? The <s>Sūtra</s> through basis, characteristic, phenomena, and indication of meaning. Therein, the basis is where, in what place it was taught, by whom, and to whom. The characteristic is the characteristic of conventional truth and the characteristic of ultimate truth. The phenomena are the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), nutriments (<s>āhāra</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), and so forth. The meaning is the intended purport.

body.text: abhimukhatvādabhīkṣṇatvādabhibhavanādabhigamanāccābhidharmo veditavyaḥ | nirvāṇābhimukho dharmo 'bhidharmaḥ satyabodhipakṣavimokṣamu[su?]khādideśanāt | abhīkṣṇaṃ dharmo 'bhidharma ekaikasya dharmasya rūpyarūpisanidarśanādiprabhedena bahulanirdeśāt | abhibhavatītyabhidharmaḥ parapravādābhibhavanādvivādādhikaraṇādibhiḥ | abhigamyate sūtrārtha etenetyabhidharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Abhidharma</s> should be understood through facing, repetition, overcoming, and approach. The <s>dharma</s> that faces <s>nirvāṇa</s> is <s>abhidharma</s> — because of the teaching of truths, factors of awakening, liberations, and the like. The <s>dharma</s> [taught] repeatedly is <s>abhidharma</s> — because of the extensive exposition of each single <s>dharma</s> through the divisions of material, immaterial, with indication, and so forth. That which overcomes is <s>abhidharma</s> — because of overcoming the doctrines of others through debates, arbitrations, and the like. That by which the meaning of the sūtras is approached is <s>abhidharma</s>.

children.translated_text: The nature of <s>Vinaya</s> [is established] through offense, arising, restoration, and emergence;
and through persons, designations, divisions, and determinations. || Msa_11.4 ||

body.text: āpattitaḥ samutthānato vyutthānato nisāraṇataśca veditavyaḥ | tatrāpattiḥ pañcāpattinikāyāḥ | samutthānamāpattīnāmajñānātpramādāt kleśaprācuryādanādarācca | vyutthānamāśayato na daṇḍakarmataḥ | niḥsaraṇaṃ saptavidham | pratideśanā, abhyupagamaḥ śikṣādattakādīnām, daṇḍakarmaṇaḥ[ṇām] | samavadyotaḥ [samavadhātaḥ], prajñapte śikṣāpade punaḥ paryāyeṇa a[ṇānu] jñānāt, prasrabdhiḥ samagreṇa saṃghena śikṣāpadasya pratiprasrambhaṇāt | āśrayaparivṛttirbhikṣubhikṣuṇyoḥ strīpuruṣavyañjanaparivartanādasādhāraṇā ve[ce]dāpattiḥ | bhūtapratyavekṣā dharmoddānāka[kā]raiḥ pratyavekṣāvaśeṣaḥ | dharmatāpratilambhaśca satyadarśanena kṣudrānukṣudrāpannā[ttya]bhāve dharma [tā]pratilambhāt | punaścaturvidhenārthena vinayo vaiditavyaḥ | pudgalato yamāgamya śikṣā prajñapyate | prajñaptito yadārocite pudgalāparādhe śāstā saṃnipātya saṃgha[saṃghaṃ?] śikṣāṃ prajñāpayati | pravibhāgato yaḥ prajñapte śikṣāpade taduddeśasya vibhāgaḥ | viniścayataśca tatrāpattiḥ kathaṃ bhavatyanāpattirveti nirdhāraṇāt |
body.translated_text: This should be understood from the standpoint of offenses (<s>āpatti</s>), their arising (<s>samutthāna</s>), emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>), and their expiation (<s>niḥsaraṇa</s>). Therein, offenses are of five classes of offenses (<s>pañcāpattinikāya</s>). The arising of offenses is from ignorance, heedlessness, abundance of afflictions, and disrespect. Emergence is from intention, not from punitive action. Expiation is sevenfold: confession (<s>pratideśanā</s>); acceptance — as in the case of those who have undertaken the training rules (<s>śikṣādattaka</s>) and the like; punitive action; reconciliation — through the permission being granted again in turn for a promulgated training rule; relaxation — through the relaxation of a training rule by the complete <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community); transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) — the uncommon offense of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) through the change of female and male characteristics; and examination of reality — the remainder of examination through the method of the summary of Dharma (<s>dharmoddāna</s>); and attainment of the nature of reality — through the direct seeing of the [four noble] truths, the attainment of the nature of reality when there is no [further] falling into minor and trivial [offenses]. Furthermore, the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline) should be understood through a fourfold purpose: from the standpoint of the person — the person on account of whom the training rule is promulgated; from the standpoint of promulgation — when, upon the report of a person's offense, the Teacher convenes the <s>Saṃgha</s> and promulgates the training rule; from the standpoint of analysis — the analysis of the recitation of a promulgated training rule; and from the standpoint of determination — the ascertainment of how an offense arises and how there is non-offense.

body.text: ālambanalābhaparyeṣṭau trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the search for the object-support and its attainment:

children.translated_text: The Dharma is regarded as the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) — internal and external;
the attainment of both [internal and external]
is through the meaning of duality, and [the attainment] of both [as tathatā] is through non-apprehension. || Msa_11.5 ||

body.text: dharmālambanaṃ yo deśitaḥ kāyādikañcādhyātmikaṃ
body.translated_text: The Dharma object-support that is taught — the internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) such as the body and the rest, the external, and both the internal-external. Therein, the internal, such as the body and the rest, constitutes the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>); the external constitutes the grasped (<s>grāhya</s>); the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of both of these constitutes the dual [object-support]

body.text: bāhyamādhyātmikabāhyañca | tatra grāhakabhūtaṃ kāyādikamādhyātmikaṃ grāhyabhūtaṃ bāhyaṃ tayoreva tathatā dvayam | tatra dvayorādhyātmikabāhyayorālambanayordvayārthena lābho yathākramam | yadi grāhyārthadgrāhakārthamabhinnaṃ paśyati grāhakārthācca grāhyārtham, dvayasya punaḥ samastasyādhyātmikabāhyālambanasya tathatāyā lābhastayorevadvayoranupalambhādveditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: . Therein, the attainment of both internal and external object-supports is through the meaning of duality, respectively — if one sees the grasped-object as not different from the grasper-object, and the grasper-object [as not different] from the grasped-object. The attainment of the <s>tathatā</s> of both combined — the internal-external object-support — should be understood as through the non-apprehension of both of those.

children.translated_text: Through mental discourse (<s>manojalpa</s>), because of the retention by one who has faith in the meaning as stated;

children.text: arthakhyānasya jalpācca nāmni sthānācca cetasaḥ || Msa_11.6 ||
children.translated_text: because of the discourse about the meaning-appearance, and because of the mind's abiding in the name; || Msa_11.6 ||
the attainment of the Dharma object-support occurs through three knowledges — arising from hearing and the rest;
and the threefold attainment of the object-support, as previously stated, is dependent on that. || Msa_11.7 ||

body.text: dharmālambanalābhaḥ punastribhirjñānairbhavati śrutacintābhāvanāmayaiḥ | tatra samāhitena cetasā manojalpairyathoktārthaprasannasya tatpradhāraṇāt | śrutamayena jñānena tallābhaḥ, manojalpairiti saṃkalpaiḥ | prasannasyetyadhimuktasya niścitasya | pradhāraṇāditi pravicayāt | jalpādarthakhyānasya pradhāraṇāccintāmayena tallābhaḥ | yadi manojalpādevāyamarthaḥ khyātīti paśyati nānyanmanojalpādyathoktaṃ dvayālambanalābhe | cittasya nāmni sthānāt bhāvanāmayena jñānena tallābho veditavyo dvayānupalambhādyathoktaṃ dvayālambanalābhe | ata eva ca sa pūrvoktastrividhālambanalābho dharmālambanalābhasaṃniśrito veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The attainment of the Dharma object-support occurs through three knowledges: those arising from hearing (<s>śruta</s>), reflection (<s>cintā</s>), and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Therein, with a concentrated mind, through mental discourse, because of the retention by one who has faith in the meaning as stated — the attainment occurs through knowledge arising from hearing. 'Mental discourse' means conceptual thoughts; 'of one who has faith' means one who is convinced and determined; 'retention' means investigation. Through the discourse about the meaning-appearance, the attainment occurs through knowledge arising from reflection — if one sees that this meaning appears only through mental discourse and not otherwise, as stated for the attainment of the dual object-support. Because of the mind's abiding in the name, the attainment should be understood as through knowledge arising from cultivation, due to the non-apprehension of duality, as stated for the attainment of the dual object-support. And for this very reason, the threefold attainment of the object-support as previously stated should be understood as dependent on the attainment of the Dharma object-support.

body.text: manasikāraparyeṣṭau pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the search for mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>):

children.translated_text: One is determined by the three realms; another is duty-accomplishing; another is based on [either] constricted or [unconstricted] support;
another instills conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>); another produces intense zeal (<s>chanda</s>). || Msa_11.8 ||
Based on either inferior or complete [samādhi], it is twofold — with discourse and without discourse;
conjoined with knowledge, and having the nature of the prerequisite of yoga (<s>yogopaniṣad</s>). || Msa_11.9 ||
It has combined object-supports and also separate object-supports;

children.text: pañcadhā saptadha caiva parijñā pañcadhāsya ca || Msa_11.10 ||
children.translated_text: it is fivefold and sevenfold, and its full comprehension (<s>parijñā</s>) is also fivefold. || Msa_11.10 ||
Four and thirty-seven aspects belong to the cultivation [stage];
it has the nature of the two paths, twofold benefit, and is receptive. || Msa_11.11 ||
It is applied and self-mastering, limited and vast in nature —

children.text: yogināṃ hi manaskāra eṣa sarvātmako mataḥ || Msa_11.12 ||
children.translated_text: this mental attention of <s>yogins</s> is regarded as all-encompassing. || Msa_11.12 ||

body.text: aṣṭādaśavidho manaskāraḥ | dhātuniyataḥ kṛtyakara āśrayavibhakto 'dhimuktiniveśakaścchandajanakaḥ samādhisaṃniśrito jñānasaṃprayuktaḥ saṃbhinnālambano vibhinnālambanaḥ parijñāniyato bhāvanākārapraviṣṭaḥ śamathavipaśyanāmārgasvabhāvo 'nuśaṃsamanaskāraḥ pratīcchakaḥ prāyogikamanaskāro vaśavartimanaskāraḥ parīttamanaskāro vipulamanaskāraśca | tatra dhātuniyato yaḥ śrāvakādigotraniyataḥ | kṛtyakaro yaḥ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya | āśrayavibhakto yaḥ sasaṃvādhagṛhasthāśrayo 'saṃbādhapravrajitāśrayaśca | adhimuktiniveśako yo buddhānusmṛtisahagataḥ | (

mātrāvitarkāvicārasahagataśca | jñānasaṃprayukto yo yogopaniṣadyogasahagataḥ, sa punaryathākramaṃ śrutacintāmayo bhāvanāmayaśca | saṃbhinnālambanaḥ pañcavidhaḥ children.translated_text: ) Generating zeal means accompanied by confidence in that. Dependent on <s>samādhi</s> means accompanied by the preliminary and root <s>samādhis</s> — accompanied by initial and sustained application of thought (<s>savitarkasavicāra</s>), without initial application but with sustained application (<s>nirvitarkasavicāra</s>), and without either. These are to be understood respectively in the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>). Conjoined with knowledge means accompanied by the yoga that is the prerequisite of yoga (<s>yogopaniṣadyoga</s>), which in turn is respectively that arising from hearing, reflection, and cultivation. Having combined object-supports is fivefold: having as object-support [texts of the type] <s>sūtra</s>, <s>uddāna</s> (summary), <s>gāthā</s> (verse), <s>nipāta</s> (minor text), up to what is memorized, and up to what is taught. Having separate object-supports is sevenfold: having name as object-support, having word (<s>pada</s>) as object-support, having syllable (<s>vyañjana</s>) as object-support, having the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) as object-support, having the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) as object-support, having material phenomena (<s>rūpidharma</s>) as object-support, and having immaterial phenomena (<s>arūpidharma</s>) as object-support. Therein, having material phenomena as object-support means having the body as object-support; having immaterial phenomena as object-support means having feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and mental factors (<s>dharma</s>) as object-support. Determined by full comprehension means concerning the object to be fully comprehended, the meaning to be fully comprehended, the full comprehension itself, the fruit of full comprehension, and its experience. Therein, the object to be fully comprehended is suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>); the meaning to be fully comprehended is its impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and selflessness; full comprehension is the path; the fruit of full comprehension is liberation; its experience is the knowledge-and-vision of liberation. Entered into the aspects of cultivation is the cultivation of four aspects and thirty-seven aspects. Therein, the cultivation of four aspects is: cultivation of the aspect of the selflessness of persons, cultivation of the aspect of the selflessness of phenomena, cultivation of the aspect of seeing, and cultivation of the aspect of knowledge. The cultivation of thirty-seven aspects: cultivation of the aspect of the unattractive, suffering, impermanence, and selflessness — in the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>); cultivation of the aspects of attainment, familiarization, driving out, and antidote — in the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>); cultivation of mental attention as antidote to discontent — when generating zeal; cultivation of mental attention as antidote to distraction and doubt — when one strives and initiates vigor, respectively; cultivation of the <s>samādhi</s>-aspect as antidote to agitation — when one steadies the mind; cultivation of the <s>samādhi</s>-aspect as antidote to dullness — when one uplifts the mind. These should be understood respectively in the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>). For one whose mind is settled, cultivation of the aspect of confidence in supramundane accomplishment — just as the cultivation of the aspect of confidence, so too the cultivation of the aspects of resolve, non-forgetfulness of dharmas, stability of mind, and investigation — in the [five spiritual] faculties (<s>indriya</s>). These same five, with their adverse factors inscribed, [apply] to the [five] powers (<s>bala</s>). Cultivation of the aspect of the manifestation of awakening — and therein the cultivation of the aspects of investigation, vigor, joy, pliancy, stability of mind, and equanimity — in the seven factors of awakening (<s>saṃbodhyaṅga</s>). Cultivation of the aspects of the attainment of certainty, the guarding of the preparatory ground, the accomplishment of the transcendent, entry into morality beloved by the noble ones, the erasure of habitual conduct-patterns, the practice of the path obtained through previous cultivation, non-forgetfulness of the sign of the stability of dharmas, and the transformation of the basis through abiding in signlessness — in the limbs of the path (<s>mārgāṅga</s>). Regarding the paths of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) cultivation, there is no [separate] exposition. The mental attention on benefits is twofold: the removal of afflictive obstruction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) and the removal of the sign of [wrong] views. The receptive [mental attention] is one that, in the stream of Dharma, accepts instruction from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Applied mental attention is fivefold, in the domain of <s>samādhi</s>: the applied [attention] of discerning enumeration, by which one discerns the enumeration of names, words, and syllables in <s>sūtras</s> and the rest; (

children.text: ) vṛttyupalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena dvividhāṃ vṛttimupalakṣayate parimāṇavṛttiṃ ca vyañjanānāmaparimāṇavṛttiṃ ca nāmapadayoḥ | parikalpopalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena dvayamupādāya dvayaparikalpamupalakṣayate | nāmaparikalpamupādāyārthaparikalpamarthaparikalpamupādāya nāmaparikalpamaparikalpamakṣaram | kramopalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena nāmagrahaṇapūrvikāmarthagrahaṇapravṛttimupalakṣayate | prativedhaprāyogikaśca | sa punarekādaśavidho veditavya, āgantukatvaprativedhataḥ, saṃprakhyānanimittaprativedhataḥ, arthānupalambhaprativedhataḥ, upalambhānupalambhaprativedhataḥ, dharmadhātuprativedhataḥ pudgalanairātmyaprativedhataḥ, dharma nairātmyaprativedhataḥ, hīnāśayaprativedhataḥ, udāramāhātmyāśayaprativedhataḥ yathādhigamadharmavyavasthānaprativedhataḥ, vyavasthāpitadharmaprativedhataśca | vaśavartimanaskārastrividhaḥ, kleśāvaraṇasuviśuddhaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇasuviśuddhaḥ, guṇābhinirhārasuviśuddhaśca |
children.translated_text: ) the applied [attention] of discerning mode of operation, by which one discerns the twofold mode of operation — the finite mode of operation of syllables and the infinite mode of operation of names and words; the applied [attention] of discerning conceptualization, by which one discerns the dual conceptualization based on duality — the conceptualization of meaning based on name-conceptualization, and the conceptualization of name based on meaning-conceptualization, while the syllable is non-conceptualized; the applied [attention] of discerning sequence, by which one discerns the operation of meaning-apprehension preceded by name-apprehension; and the applied [attention] of penetration. This [last] should be understood as elevenfold: penetration of the adventitious nature [of defilements]; penetration of the sign of discernment; penetration of the non-apprehension of meaning; penetration of the non-apprehension of apprehension; penetration of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality); penetration of the selflessness of persons; penetration of the selflessness of phenomena; penetration of the inferior disposition; penetration of the disposition of noble greatness; penetration of the establishment of dharmas according to realization; and penetration of the established dharmas. The self-mastering mental attention is threefold: well-purified from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>); well-purified from both the obscuration of afflictions and the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>); and well-purified in the production of qualities.

body.translated_text: Mental attention is of eighteen kinds: determined by the [three] realms (<s>dhātu</s>); duty-accomplishing; distinguished by support; instilling conviction; generating zeal; dependent on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); conjoined with knowledge; having combined object-supports; having separate object-supports; determined by full comprehension; entered into the aspects of cultivation; having the nature of the paths of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); mental attention on the benefits; receptive; applied mental attention; self-mastering mental attention; limited mental attention; and vast mental attention. Therein, determined by the [three] realms means determined by the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others. Duty-accomplishing means that of one who has accumulated the accumulations. Distinguished by support means based on the constricted support of a householder or the unconstricted support of one gone forth [into monastic life]. Instilling conviction means accompanied by the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>). (

body.text: dharmatattvaparyeṣṭau dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the search for the reality of phenomena (<s>dharmatattva</s>):

children.text: tattvaṃ yatsatataṃ dvayena rahitaṃ, bhrānteśca saṃniśrayaḥ,
children.translated_text: That which is always devoid of duality, and which is the basis of delusion,
which cannot in any way be expressed in words, and which has the nature of non-elaboration (<s>aprapañca</s>),

children.text: jñeyaṃ heyamatho viśodhyamamalaṃ yacca prakṛtyā matam |
children.translated_text: which is to be known, to be abandoned, to be purified, and which is regarded as stainless by nature,
whose purification from afflictions is regarded as similar to space, gold, and water — || Msa_11.13 ||

body.text: satataṃ dvayena rahitaṃ tattvaṃ, parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇenātyantamasattvāt | bhrānteḥ saṃniśrayaḥ paratantrastena tatparikalpanāt | anabhilāpyamaprapañcātmakaṃ ca pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ | tatra prathamaṃ tattvaṃ parijñeyaṃ dvitīyaṃ praheyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ viśodhyaṃ cāgantukamalādviśuddhaṃ ca prakṛtyā, yasya prakṛtyā viśuddhasyākāśasuvarṇavārisadṛśī kleśādviśuddhiḥ | na hyākāśādīni prakṛtyā aśuddhāni na cāgantukamalāpagamādeṣāṃ viśuddhirneṣyata iti |
body.translated_text: the reality (<s>tattva</s>) always devoid of duality is the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), because of the utter non-existence of the characteristics of grasped and grasper. The basis of delusion is the dependent nature (<s>paratantra</s>), because of the conceptualization of that [duality] in it. The inexpressible, having the nature of non-elaboration, is the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>). Therein, the first reality is to be fully known; the second is to be abandoned; the third is to be purified — purified from adventitious stains and stainless by nature. Its purification from afflictions, being pure by nature, is similar to space, gold, and water — for space and the rest are not impure by nature, yet their purification from adventitious stains is not denied.

children.translated_text: Therefore, there exists nothing whatsoever in the world that is other [than this reality],
and the entire world is confused in understanding regarding that;
how has this mode of the delusion of the world become so entrenched?
who, being attached to what is unreal, abandons the real entirely. || Msa_11.14 ||

body.text: na khalu tasmādevaṃlakṣaṇāddharmadhātoḥ kiṃcidanyalloke vidyate dharmatāyā dharmasyābhinnatvāt | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Indeed, apart from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas) having such a characteristic, nothing else exists in the world, since the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>) is not different from dharmas. The rest is self-explanatory.

body.text: tattve māyopamaparyeṣṭau pañcadaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: On the search for the truth through the illusion-like inquiry, fifteen verses:

children.translated_text: Just as there is <s>māyā</s> (illusion), so <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization) is declared;
just as the product of <s>māyā</s>, so the delusion of duality is declared. || Msa_11.15 ||

body.text: yathā māyā yantra [mantra]parigṛhītaṃ bhrāntinimittaṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭādikam tathābhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantraḥ svabhāvo [svabhāvākāro] veditavyaḥ | yathā māyākṛtaṃ tasyāṃ māyāyāṃ hastyaśvasuvarṇādyākṛtistadbhāvena pratibhāsitā, tathā tasminnabhūtaparikalpe dvayabhrāntirgrāhyagrāhakatvenapratibhāsitā parikalpitasvabhāvākārā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: Just as <s>māyā</s> — that is, the material such as wood and clods of earth seized by a mantra, which serves as the basis for delusion — so <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> should be understood as the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) nature-aspect. Just as the product of <s>māyā</s> — that is, the appearance of forms such as elephants, horses, gold, and so forth manifested as if real in that illusion — so in that unreal conceptualization, the delusion of duality, manifested as apprehended and apprehender, should be understood as the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) nature-aspect.

children.translated_text: Just as in that [illusion] there is no reality of that [appearance], so ultimate truth is held;
just as there is apprehension of that, so conventional truth is [understood]. || Msa_11.16 ||

body.text: yathā[']tasminna tadbhāvo māyākṛte hastitvādyabhāvastathā tasminparatantre paramārtha iṣyate parikalpitasya dvayalakṣaṇasyābhāvaḥ | yathā tasya māyākṛtasya hastyādibhāvenopalabdhiḥ, tathābhūtaparikalpasya saṃvṛtisatyatopalabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as in the product of <s>māyā</s> there is no reality of elephant-nature and so forth, so in the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent nature), ultimate truth is held to be the absence of the imagined dual characteristic. Just as there is apprehension of the product of <s>māyā</s> as having elephant-nature and so forth, so the apprehension of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization) is [its] conventional truth.

children.translated_text: Just as in the absence of that [illusion], the manifestation of its cause is obtained,
so through the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), [the manifestation] of unreal conceptualization is obtained. || Msa_11.17 ||

body.text: yathā māyākṛtasyābhāve tasya nimittasya kāṣṭhādikasya vyaktirbhūtārthopalabhyate, tathāśrayaparāvṛttau dvayabhrāntyabhāvādabhūtaparikalpasya bhūto 'rtha upalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Just as in the absence of the product of <s>māyā</s>, the genuine reality of its cause — the wood and the like — is apprehended, so through the transformation of the basis, due to the absence of the delusion of duality, the genuine reality of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> is apprehended.

children.translated_text: Just as the world, undeluded regarding that cause, moves about freely,
so through transformation, the noble one (<s>ārya</s>), unconfused, becomes one who moves freely. || Msa_11.18 ||

body.text: yathā tannimitte kāṣṭhādāvabhrānto lokaḥ kāmataścarati svatantraḥ tathā'śrayaparāvṛttāvaparyasta āryaḥ kāmacāri bhavati svatantraḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the world, undeluded regarding that cause — the wood and the like — moves about freely, being autonomous, so through the transformation of the basis, the noble one (<s>ārya</s>), unconfused, becomes one who moves freely, being autonomous.

children.translated_text: The appearance of that exists therein, yet the reality of that does not exist;
therefore both existence and non-existence are established in <s>māyā</s> and the like. || Msa_11.19 ||

body.text: eṣa śloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: This verse is self-explanatory.

children.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca |
children.translated_text: The existent is not therein merely non-existent, nor is the non-existent merely existent;
and the non-differentiation of existence and non-existence is established in <s>māyā</s> and the like. || Msa_11.20 ||

body.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvo yastadākṛtibhāvo nāsau na bhāvaḥ | nābhāvo bhāva eva ca yo hastitvādyabhāvo nāsau na [?]bhāvaḥ | tayośca bhāvābhāvayoraviśeṣo māyādiṣu vidhīyate | ya eva hi tatra tadākṛtibhāvaḥ, sa eva hastitvādyabhāvaḥ | ya eva hastitvādyabhāvaḥ sa eva tadākṛtibhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The existent is not therein merely non-existent — that which is the existence of that appearance is not non-existent. The non-existent is not merely existent — that which is the absence of elephant-nature and so forth is not [truly] existent. And the non-differentiation of these two — existence and non-existence — is established in <s>māyā</s> and the like. For that very existence of the appearance therein is itself the absence of elephant-nature and so forth; and that very absence of elephant-nature and so forth is itself the existence of the appearance.

children.translated_text: Likewise, the appearance of duality exists herein, yet the reality of that does not exist;
therefore both existence and non-existence are established in form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. || Msa_11.21 ||

body.text: tathātrābhūtaparikalpe dvayābhāsatāsti dvayabhāvaśca nāsti | tasmādastitvanāstitvaṃ rūpādiṣu vidhīyate 'bhūtaparikalpasvabhāveṣu |
body.translated_text: Likewise, herein in <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>, the appearance of duality exists, but the reality of duality does not exist. Therefore both existence and non-existence are established in form and the like, which have the nature of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>.

children.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca |
children.translated_text: The existent is not therein merely non-existent, nor is the non-existent merely existent;
and the non-differentiation of existence and non-existence is established in form and the like. || Msa_11.22 ||

body.text: na bhāvastatra cābhāvaḥ | yā dvayābhāsatā | nābhāvo bhāva eva ca | yā dvayatānāstitā | bhāvābhāvāviśeṣaśca rūpādiṣu vidhīyate | ya eva hi dvayābhāsatāyā bhāvaḥ sa eva dvayasyābhāva iti |
body.translated_text: The existent is not therein merely non-existent — [this refers to] the appearance of duality. The non-existent is not merely existent — [this refers to] the non-existence of duality. And the non-differentiation of existence and non-existence is established in form and the like. For that very existence of the appearance of duality is itself the non-existence of duality.

children.translated_text: It is held for the purpose of rejecting both superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>),
and also for the purpose of rejecting [going by] the inferior vehicle. || Msa_11.23 ||

body.text: kimarthaṃ punarayaṃ bhāvābhāvayoraikāntikatvamaviśeṣaśceṣyate | yathākramam | samāropāpavādābha[ntaḥ?]pratiṣedhārthamiṣyate, hīnayānagamanapratiṣedhārthaṃ ca | abhāvasya hyabhāvatvaṃ viditvā samāropaṃ na karoti | bhāvasya bhāvatvaṃ viditvāpavādaṃ na karoti | tayoścāviśeṣaṃ viditvā na bhāvādudvijate tasmānna hinayānena niryāti |
body.translated_text: For what purpose then is this non-absoluteness and non-differentiation of existence and non-existence held? In due order: it is held for the purpose of rejecting superimposition and denial, and for the purpose of rejecting going by the inferior vehicle. For knowing the non-existence of the non-existent, one does not superimpose. Knowing the existence of the existent, one does not deny. And knowing the non-differentiation of the two, one is not repelled by existence, and therefore does not depart by the inferior vehicle.

children.translated_text: The cause of delusion and the delusion [itself] are held to be material cognition (<s>rūpavijñapti</s>);
and the immaterial cognition would not exist due to the non-existence [of the material], nor would the other. || Msa_11.24 ||

body.text: rūpabhrānteryā nimittavijñaptiḥ sā rūpavijñaptiriṣyate rūpākhyā | sā tu rūpabhrāntirarūpiṇī vijñaptiḥ | abhāvādrūpavijñapteritarāpi na syādarūpiṇī vijñaptiḥ | kāeraṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: The cognition that is the cause of material delusion is held to be material cognition, called 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>). But that material delusion is an immaterial cognition. Due to the non-existence of material cognition, the other — the immaterial cognition — would also not exist, because of the absence of the cause.

children.translated_text: Two things are illustrated from the delusion of grasping the appearance of an illusory elephant;

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate || Msa_11.25 ||
children.translated_text: just as duality does not exist therein, yet duality is indeed apprehended. || Msa_11.25 ||
Two things are illustrated from the delusion of grasping a reflection and a chain;

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate || Msa_11.26 ||
children.translated_text: just as duality does not exist therein, yet duality is indeed apprehended. || Msa_11.26 ||

body.text: māyāhastyākṛtigrāhya[ha]bhrantito dvayamudāhṛtam | grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ ca, tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate | pratibimbaṃ[ba?] saṃkalikāṃ ca manasikurvataḥ tadgrāhabhrānterdvayamudāhṛtaṃ pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: From the delusion of grasping the appearance of an illusory elephant, two things are illustrated — the apprehended and the apprehender — just as duality does not exist therein, yet duality is indeed apprehended. For one who mentally attends to a reflection and a chain, from the delusion of grasping them, two things are illustrated, as before.

children.translated_text: Thus, because of such existence, because of such non-existence, and because of the non-differentiation of existence and non-existence,

children.text: sadasanto 'tha māyābhā ye dharmā bhrāntilakṣaṇāḥ || Msa_11.27 ||
children.translated_text: dharmas characterized by delusion are both existent and non-existent, and resemble <s>māyā</s> (illusion). || Msa_11.27 ||

body.text: ye dharmā bhrāntilakṣaṇā vipakṣasvabhāvāste sadasanto māyopamāśca | kiṃ kāraṇam | santastathābhāvādabhūtaparikalpatvena | asantastathābhāvāt grāhyagrāhakatvena | tayośca bhāvābhāvayoraviśiṣṭatvāt santo 'pyasanto 'pi māyāpi caivaṃlakṣaṇā sta[ta?]smānmāyopamāḥ |
body.translated_text: Those dharmas characterized by delusion, having the nature of affliction (<s>vipakṣa</s>), are both existent and non-existent, and resemble <s>māyā</s>. Why? They are existent because of such existence — as <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization). They are non-existent because of such non-existence — as apprehended and apprehender. And because of the non-differentiation of these two — existence and non-existence — they are both existent and non-existent, and <s>māyā</s> too has such a characteristic; therefore they resemble <s>māyā</s>.

children.translated_text: Because of such existence, because of such non-existence, and because of such non-existence [in another sense], they are without [fixed] characteristics;

children.text: māyopamāśca nirdiṣṭā ye dharmāḥ prātipakṣikāḥ || Msa_11.28 ||
children.translated_text: the antidotal dharmas too are declared to be illusion-like. || Msa_11.28 ||

body.text: ye 'pi prātipakṣikā dharmā buddhenopadiṣṭāḥ smṛtyupasthānādayaste 'pyalakṣaṇā māyāśca nirdiṣṭāḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam | tathābhāvādyathā bālairgṛhyante | tathābhāvādyathā deśitāḥ | tathābhāvādyathā saṃdarśitā buddhena garbhāvakramaṇajanmābhiniṣkramaṇābhisaṃbodhyādayaḥ | evamalakṣaṇā avidyamānāśca khyānti tasmānmāyopamāḥ |
body.translated_text: Even the antidotal dharmas taught by the <s>Buddha</s> — such as the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and the like — are also without [fixed] characteristics and are declared to be like <s>māyā</s>. Why? Because of such non-existence as they are grasped by the childish. Because of such non-existence as they were taught. Because of such non-existence as was demonstrated by the <s>Buddha</s> — entry into the womb, birth, renunciation, complete awakening, and so forth. Thus they are without characteristics and appear as non-existent; therefore they resemble <s>māyā</s>.

children.translated_text: Just as a <s>māyā</s>-king is defeated by another <s>māyā</s>-king,

children.text: ye sarvadharmān paśyanti nirmārāste jinātmajāḥ || Msa_11.29 ||
children.translated_text: those who see all dharmas [in this way] are sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), free from <s>Māra</s>. || Msa_11.29 ||

body.text: ye prātipakṣikā dharmāste māyārājasthānīyāḥ saṃkleśaprahāṇe vyavadānādhipattyāt | ye 'pi sāṃkleśikā dharmāste 'pi rājasthānīyāḥ saṃkleśanirvṛttāvādhipatyāt | atastaiḥ prātipakṣikaiḥ saṃkleśaparājayo māyā [?] rājñeva rājñaḥ parājayo draṣṭavyaḥ | tajjñānācca bodhisattvā nirmārā bhavanti ubhayapakṣe |
body.translated_text: The antidotal dharmas occupy the place of a <s>māyā</s>-king, because of their sovereignty in the abandonment of affliction and purification. The afflictive dharmas too occupy the place of a [<s>māyā</s>-]king, because of their sovereignty in the production of affliction. Therefore, the defeat of affliction by the antidotal [dharmas] should be seen as the defeat of a king by a <s>māyā</s>-king. And from knowing this, <s>bodhisattvas</s> become free from <s>Māra</s> with respect to both sides.

body.text: aupamyārthe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the meaning of the analogy:

children.translated_text: Resembling <s>māyā</s>, dreams, mirages, and reflections, like echoes,
resembling reflections in water and the moon in water, like emanations again —

children.text: ṣaṭ ṣaṭ dvau ca punaśca ṣaṭ dvayamatā ekaikaśaśca trayaḥ
children.translated_text: six, six, and two, then again six, two — thus recognized — and one, one, and three:

children.text: saṃskārāḥ khalu tatra tatra kathitā buddhairvibuddhottamaiḥ || Msa_11.30 ||
children.translated_text: conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) have indeed been described there and there by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the best among the awakened. || Msa_11.30 ||

body.text: yattūktaṃ bhagavatā māyopamā dharmā yāvannirmāṇopamā iti | tatra māyopamā dharmāḥ ṣaḍādhyātmikānyāyatanāni | asatyātmajīvāditve tathā prakhyānāt | svapnopamāḥ ṣaṭ bāhyānyāyatanāni tadupabhogasyāvastukatvāt | marīcikopamau dvau dharmau cittaṃ caitasikāśca bhrāntikaratvāt | pratibimbopamāḥ punaḥ ṣaḍevādhyātmikānyāyatanāni pūrvakarmapratibimbatvāt | pratibhāsopamāḥ ṣaḍeva bāhyānyāyatanānyādhyātmikānāmāyatanānāṃ chāyābhūtatvāt tadādhipatyotpattitaḥ | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 63

children.text: ) ṣaṭ dvayaṃ matāḥ ṣaṭ dvayamatāḥ | pratiśrutkopamā deśanādharmāḥ | udakacandrabimbopamāḥ samādhisaṃniśritā dharmāḥ samādherūdakasthānīyatvādacchatayā | nirmāṇopamāḥ saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahe 'saṃkliṣṭasarvakriyāprayogatvāt |
children.translated_text: 'Six, two — thus recognized; six.' Echo-like are the dharmas of teaching. Water-moon-reflection-like are dharmas associated with <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), because <s>samādhi</s> occupies the place of water, through its clarity. Emanation-like [are dharmas] in the deliberate assumption of existence-birth, because of the engagement in all activities without affliction.

body.translated_text: What the Blessed One said — 'dharmas are like <s>māyā</s>, up to like emanation' — therein: dharmas resembling <s>māyā</s> are the six internal sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), because of appearing as if having self-nature and life-nature when such do not exist. Dream-like are the six external sense-bases, because the enjoyment of them is without substance. Mirage-like are the two — mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) — because they produce delusion. Reflection-like are again the six internal sense-bases, because they are reflections of prior <s>karma</s>. Echo-like are the six external sense-bases, because they are shadows of the internal sense-bases, arising under their dominion.

body.text: jñeyaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the search for the knowable:

children.text: abhūtakalpo na bhūto nābhūto 'kalpa eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Abhūtakalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization) — neither real nor unreal, and also <s>akalpa</s> (non-conceptualization) —

children.text: na kalpo nāpi cākalpaḥ sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ nirucyate || Msa_11.31 ||
children.translated_text: neither conceptualization nor non-conceptualization: all that is knowable is declared [thus]. || Msa_11.31 ||

body.text: abhūtakalpo yo na lokottarajñānānukūlaḥ kalpaḥ, na bhūto nābhūto yastadanukūlo yāvannirvedhabhāgīyaḥ | akalpastathatā lokottaraṃ ca jñānam | na kalpo nāpi cākalpo lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ laukikaṃ jñānam | etāvacca sarvaṃ jñeyam |
body.translated_text: <s>Abhūtakalpa</s> — the conceptualization that does not accord with supramundane knowledge — is neither real nor unreal, [while] that which accords with it, up to the factors conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), [is also such]. <s>Akalpa</s> (non-conceptualization) is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and supramundane knowledge. Neither conceptualization nor non-conceptualization is the worldly knowledge obtained subsequent to the supramundane. And this constitutes all that is knowable.

body.text: saṃkleśavyavadānaparyeṣṭau ślokadvayam |
body.translated_text: On the search regarding affliction and purification, two verses:

children.translated_text: From their own basis (<s>dhātu</s>), appearing as duality, with the operation of ignorance and afflictions,
conceptualizations arise, devoid of the substance of duality. || Msa_11.32 ||

body.text: svadhātuta iti bhāvāṅgā [svabījā?]dālayavijñānataḥ | dvayābhāsā iti grāhyagrāhakābhāsāḥ | sahāvidyayā kleśaiśca vṛttireṣāṃ ta ime sāvidyākleśavṛttayaḥ | dvayadravyavivarjitā iti grāhyadravyeṇa grāhakadravyeṇa ca | evaṃ kleśaḥ paryeṣitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'From their own basis' means from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), as the seed. 'Appearing as duality' means appearing as apprehended and apprehender. 'With the operation of ignorance and afflictions' — those whose operation is with ignorance and afflictions are called <s>sāvidyākleśavṛtti</s>. 'Devoid of the substance of duality' means [devoid] of the substance of the apprehended and the substance of the apprehender. Thus should affliction be investigated.

children.translated_text: The attainment of a special object [of meditation], through abiding in one's own basis and practice —

children.text: ta eva hyadvayābhāsā vartante carmakāṇḍavat || Msa_11.33 ||
children.translated_text: those very [conceptualizations], now appearing without duality, operate like leather or a bamboo shaft. || Msa_11.33 ||

body.text: ālambanaviśeṣāptiriti yo dharmālambanalābhaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ | svadhātusthānayogata iti svadhāturvikalpānāṃ tathatā tatra sthānaṃ nāmni sthānāccetasaḥ | yogata ityabhyāsāt | bhāvanāmārgeṇa ta eva vikalpā advayābhāsā vartante parāvṛttāśrayasya | carmavat kāṇḍavacca | yathā hi svaratvāpagamāttadeva carma mṛdu bhavati | agnisaṃtāpanayā tadeva kāṇḍaṃ ṛju bhavati | evaṃ śamathavipaśyanābhāvanābhyāṃ cetaḥ prajñāvimuktilābhe parāvṛttāśrayasya ta eva vikalpā na punardvayābhāsāḥ pravartante | ityeva [vaṃ?] vyavadānaṃ paryeṣitavyam |
body.translated_text: 'The attainment of a special object' refers to the previously mentioned attainment of the dharma-object. 'Through abiding in one's own basis and practice' — the basis of conceptualizations is their own <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); abiding therein means through the mind's abiding in the name. 'And practice' means through repeated cultivation. Through the path of cultivation, those very conceptualizations operate appearing without duality, for one whose basis has been transformed. Like leather and like a bamboo shaft: just as leather itself becomes soft through the removal of its rigidity, and just as that very bamboo shaft becomes straight through heating with fire, so too through the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), for one whose basis has been transformed, those very conceptualizations no longer operate appearing as duality, upon attaining wisdom-liberation. Thus should purification be investigated.

body.text: vijñaptimātratāparyeṣṭau dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the search for consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: Mind (<s>citta</s>) appears as duality and is held to appear as passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like;

children.text: śraddhādyābhāsaṃ na tadanyo dharmaḥ kliṣṭakuśalo 'sti || Msa_11.34 ||
children.translated_text: it likewise appears as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the like — no dharma, afflicted or wholesome, other than that exists. || Msa_11.34 ||

body.text: cittamātrameva dvayapratibhāsamiṣyate grāhyapratibhāsaṃ grāhakapratibhāsaṃ ca | tathā rāgādikleśābhāsaṃ tadeveṣyate | śraddhādikuśaladharmābhāsaṃ vā | na tu tadābhāsādanyaḥ kliṣṭo dharmo 'sti rāgādilakṣaṇaḥ kuśalo vā śraddhādilakṣaṇaḥ | yathā dvayapratibhāsādanyo na dvayalakṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Mind alone is held to appear as duality — as the appearance of the apprehended and the appearance of the apprehender. Likewise, it is held to appear as the afflictions such as passion and the like; or as the appearance of wholesome dharmas such as faith and the like. But no afflicted dharma other than that appearance exists, having the characteristic of passion and the like, nor any wholesome [dharma] having the characteristic of faith and the like — just as no [entity] having the characteristic of duality exists apart from the appearance of duality.

children.translated_text: Thus mind operates with variegated appearances and variegated forms;

children.text: tathābhāsobhāvābhāvo na tu dharmāṇāṃ mataḥ || Msa_11.35 ||
children.translated_text: but the existence or non-existence of [those] appearances is not considered [to be the existence or non-existence] of dharmas. || Msa_11.35 ||

body.text: tatra cittameva vastutacci[ści]trābhāsaṃ pravartate | paryāyeṇa rāgābhāsaṃ vā dveṣābhāsaṃ vā | tadanyadharmābhāsaṃ vā | citrākāraṃ ca yugapat śraddhādyākāram | bhāso bhāvābhāvaḥ kliṣṭakuśalāvasthe cetasi | na tu dharmāṇāṃ [kliṣṭānāṃ?] kuśalānāṃ [vā?] tatpratibhāsavyatirekeṇa tallakṣaṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, mind itself — being the real substance — operates with variegated appearances: appearing alternately as passion, or as hatred, or as the appearance of any other dharma; and with variegated forms simultaneously, such as the forms of faith and the like. The appearance is the existence or non-existence [of dharmas] in the afflicted and wholesome states of mind. But [this is] not of the dharmas [themselves] — of the afflicted or the wholesome — because apart from that appearance, their characteristic does not exist.

body.text: lakṣaṇaparyeṣṭau ślokā aṣṭau | ekanoddeśaḥ śeṣairnirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Eight verses on the search for characteristics. One [verse] is a summary; the rest are the exposition.

children.text: lakṣyaṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ caiva lakṣaṇā ca prabhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: The characterized (<s>lakṣya</s>), the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and the characterization (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), in terms of their divisions,
have been illuminated by the perfectly awakened ones for the benefit of beings. || Msa_11.36 ||

body.text: anenoddeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the summary.

children.translated_text: The mind together with [wrong] views, and therein the states and the unchanging —
this is the characterized (<s>lakṣya</s>) in brief, but in terms of divisions it is immeasurable. || Msa_11.37 ||

body.text: tatra cittaṃ vijñānaṃ rūpaṃ ca | dṛṣṭiścaitasikā dharmāḥ | tatrāvasthā cittaviprayuktā varmāḥ | avikāritā asaṃskṛtamākāśādikaṃ tadvijñapternityaṃ tathāpravṛtteḥ | ityetat samāsena pañcavidhaṃ lakṣyaṃ prabhedenāpramāṇam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the mind is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) and <s>rūpa</s> (form). The views are the mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>). Therein, the states are the factors dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta dharmas</s>). The unchanging is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), such as space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like — because of the eternal non-occurrence of its cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>). Thus, in brief, the characterized is fivefold, but in terms of divisions it is immeasurable.

body.text:
yathājalpārthasaṃjñāyā nimittaṃ tasya vāsanā |
tasmādapyarthavikhyānaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ || Msa_11. || 38 ||
body.translated_text:
The conception of an object according to verbal expression, the sign of that, and its latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>),
and from that also the appearance of the object — this is the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>). || Msa_11.38 ||

body.text: lakṣaṇaṃ samāsena trividhaṃ parikalpitādilakṣaṇam | tatra parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ yathā jalpārthasaṃjñāyā nimittaṃ tasya jalpasya vāsanā tasmācca vāsanādyo 'rthaḥ khyāti avyavahārakuśalānāṃ vināpi yathājalpārthasaṃjñayā | tatra yathābhilāpamarthasaṃjñā caitasikī yathājalpārthasaṃjñā | tasyā yadālambanaṃ tannimittamevaṃ [va] yacca parikalpyate yataśca kāraṇādvāsana[nā]tastadubhayaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇamatrābhipretam |
body.translated_text: The characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is threefold in brief, being the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and so forth. Therein, the imagined characteristic is threefold: the conception of an object according to verbal expression, the sign of that verbal expression, and its latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>), and from that impression the object that appears — even for those unskilled in convention, without the conception of an object according to verbal expression. Therein, the conception of an object in accordance with utterance is a mental factor — the conception of an object according to verbal expression. Whatever is the object of that conception is its sign, and likewise what is imagined, and the latent impression from which as a cause — both of those are the imagined characteristic intended here.

children.text: yathā nāmārthamarthasya nāmnaḥ prakhyānatā ca yā |
children.translated_text: As name and object, and the appearance of the object as the name
and of the name [as the object] — the basis of unreal imagination is indeed the imagined characteristic. || Msa_11.39 ||

body.text: aparaparyāyo yathā nāma cārthaśca yathānāmārthamarthasya nāmnaśca prakhyānatā yathā nāmārthaprakhyānatā | yadi yathā nāmārthaḥ khyāti yathārthaṃ vā nāma ityetadabhūtaparikalpālambanaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ etāvaddhi parikalpyate yaduta nāma vā artho veti |
body.translated_text: An alternative formulation: as name and object — the object as conforming to the name, and the appearance of the name as conforming to the object. If the object appears as conforming to the name, or the name as conforming to the object — this, being the object of unreal imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>), is the imagined characteristic. For only this much is imagined: namely, either name or object.

children.translated_text: Appearing as three kinds of threefold [manifestation], having the characteristic of the apprehended and the apprehender —
unreal imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is indeed the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). || Msa_11.40 ||

body.text: trividhastrividhaścābhāso 'syeti trividhatrividhābhāsaḥ | tatra trividhābhāsaḥ padābhāso 'rthābhāso dehābhāsaśca | punastrividhābhāso manaudgrahavikalpābhāsaḥ | mano yat kliṣṭaṃ sarvadā | udgrahaḥ pañca vijñānakāyāḥ | vikalpo manovijñānam | tatra prathamatri[mastri-?] vidhābhāso grāhyalakṣaṇaḥ | dvitīyo grāhakalakṣaṇaḥ | ityayamabhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantrasya lakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: 'Having the appearance of three kinds of threefold' means having threefold and threefold appearances. Therein, the threefold appearance is: appearance of words, appearance of objects, and appearance of body. Again, the threefold appearance is: appearance of mind (<s>manas</s>), apprehension (<s>udgraha</s>), and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>). The mind is that which is always afflicted (<s>kliṣṭa</s>). Apprehension is the five groups of consciousness (<s>vijñānakāya</s>). Conceptualization is <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness). Therein, the first threefold appearance has the characteristic of the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>). The second has the characteristic of the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>). Thus, this unreal imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>).

children.translated_text: The non-existence of [imagined] existence and the existence of that non-existence, the equality of existence and non-existence,
and the nature of being unquiescent yet quiescent, and non-conceptual — this is the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). || Msa_11.41 ||

body.text: pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ punastathatā sā hyabhāvatā ca, sarvadharmāṇāṃ parikalpitānā [nāṃ?] bhāvatā ca tadabhāvatvena bhāvāt | bhāvābhāvasamānatā ca tayorbhāvābhāvayorabhinnatvāt | aśāntā cāgantukairupakleśaiḥ, śāntā ca prakṛtipariśuddhatvāt | avikalpā ca vikalpāgocaratvāt niṣprapañcatayā | etena trividhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tathatāyāḥ paridīpitaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ kle[saṃ]śavyavadānalakṣaṇamavikalpalakṣaṇaṃ ca uktaṃ trividhaṃ lakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: The characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). For it is the non-existence of all imagined phenomena, and the existence of that very non-existence — because it exists as the non-existence of those. It is the equality of existence and non-existence — because those two, existence and non-existence, are undifferentiated. It is unquiescent due to adventitious defilements, yet quiescent due to being pure by nature. And it is non-conceptual because it is beyond the range of conceptualization, being free from conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>). By this, the threefold characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> has been illuminated: its own characteristic, the characteristic of defilement and purification, and the characteristic of non-conceptualization — thus the threefold characteristic has been stated.

children.translated_text: Taking the outflow-Dharma as object, proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>),

children.text: cittasya dhātau sthānaṃ ca sadasattārthapaśyanā || Msa_11.42 ||
children.translated_text: the mind's abiding in the element (<s>dhātu</s>), and the seeing of objects as existent and non-existent. || Msa_11.42 ||

body.text: lakṣaṇā punaḥ pañcavidhā yogabhūmiḥ | ādhāra ādhānamādarśa āloka āśrayaśca | tatrādhāro niṣpa[ṣya]ndadharmo yo buddhenādhigamo deśitaḥ sa tasyādhigamasya niṣpa[ṣya]ndaḥ | ādhānaṃ yoniśo manaskāraḥ | ādarśaḥ cittasya dhātau sthānaṃ samādhiryadetatpūrvaṃ nāmni sthānamuktam | ālokaḥ sadasattvenārthadarśanaṃ lokottarā prajñā, tathā[tayā] sacca sato yathābhūtaṃ paśyatyasaccāsataḥ |
body.translated_text: The characterization (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is the fivefold <s>yogabhūmi</s> (ground of practice): support (<s>ādhāra</s>), placement (<s>ādhāna</s>), mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>), light (<s>āloka</s>), and basis (<s>āśraya</s>). Therein, the support is the outflow-Dharma (<s>niṣyandadharma</s>) — that which has been taught by the <s>Buddha</s> as his realization, which is the outflow of that realization. The placement is proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). The mirror is the mind's abiding in the element (<s>dhātu</s>) — <s>samādhi</s>, which was previously called 'abiding in name.' The light is the seeing of objects as existent and non-existent — supramundane wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); by that, one sees the existent as it truly is, and the non-existent as non-existent.

body.text: āśraya āśrayaparāvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: The basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>).

children.translated_text: The attainment of equality therein — the noble lineage (<s>āryagotra</s>) is indeed pure,
equal, distinguished, neither deficient nor excessive — thus is the characterization considered. || Msa_11.43 ||

body.text: samatāgamanamanāsravadhātau āryagotre tadanyairāryaiḥ | tacca nirmalamāryagotraṃ buddhānām | samaṃ vimuktisamatā śrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ | viśiṣṭaṃ pañcabhirviśeṣaiḥ | viśuddhiviśeṣeṇa savāsanakleśaviśuddhitaḥ | pariśuddhiviśeṣeṇa kṣetrapariśuddhitaḥ | kāyaviśeṣaṇa dharmakāyatayā | saṃbhogaviśeṣeṇa parṣanmaṇḍaleṣvavicchinnadharmasaṃbhogapravartanataḥ | karmaviśeṣeṇa ca tuṣitabhavanavāsādinirmāṇaiḥ sattvārthakriyānuṣṭhānataḥ | na ca tasyonatvaṃ saṃkleśapakṣanirodhe nādhikatvaṃ vyavadānapakṣotpāda ityeṣā pañcavidhā yogabhūmirlakṣaṇā | tayā hi tallakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca lakṣyate |
body.translated_text: The attainment of equality in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), in the noble lineage (<s>āryagotra</s>), with other noble ones. And that pure noble lineage of the <s>Buddhas</s> is: equal — in the equality of liberation with <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones). Distinguished — by five distinctions: by the distinction of purification, through purification of afflictions together with their latent impressions; by the distinction of complete purification, through the purification of [Buddha-]fields; by the distinction of body, through having the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body); by the distinction of enjoyment, through the uninterrupted turning of the enjoyment of the Dharma in the assemblies; and by the distinction of activity, through accomplishing the welfare of beings by emanations such as dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and the like. And it has no deficiency in the cessation of the side of defilement, nor excess in the arising of the side of purification. This is the fivefold <s>yogabhūmi</s> as characterization. For by that, the characterized, the characteristic, and [the characterization itself] are characterized.

body.text: vimuktiparyeṣṭau ṣaṭślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the search for liberation (<s>vimukti</s>).

children.translated_text: The transformation of the appearances of words, objects, and body — the undefiled
element (<s>dhātu</s>) from the transformation of the seed — and that is the all-pervading basis. || Msa_11.44 ||

body.text: bījaparāvṛtterityālayavijñānaparāvṛttitaḥ | padārthadehanirbhāsānāṃ vijñānānāṃ parāvṛttiranāsravo dhāturvimuktiḥ | sa ca sarvatragāśrayaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagataḥ |
body.translated_text: 'From the transformation of the seed' means from the transformation of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). The transformation of the consciousnesses that appear as words, objects, and body — the undefiled element is liberation. And that is the all-pervading basis, pertaining to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> [as well].

children.translated_text: Fourfold mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) from the cessation of mind (<s>manas</s>), apprehension (<s>udgraha</s>),

children.text: vikalpasyāvikalpe hi kṣetre jñāne 'tha karmaṇi || Msa_11.45 ||
children.translated_text: and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) — in the non-conceptual, in the field, in knowledge, and in action. || Msa_11.45 ||

body.text: manasaścodgrahasya ca vikalpasya cāvṛtteḥ parāvṛtterityarthaḥ | caturdhā vaśitā bhavati yathākramamavikalpe kṣetre jñānakarmaṇośca |
body.translated_text: 'Of mind, apprehension, and conceptualization' — from the cessation, meaning the transformation, [comes] fourfold mastery, respectively in the non-conceptual, the field, and in knowledge and action.

children.translated_text: In the three stages beginning with the Immovable (<s>Acalā</s>), that fourfold mastery [is distributed];
two [masteries] in one [stage], and one each in the other [two stages] — thus mastery is considered. || Msa_11.46 ||

body.text: sā ceyamacalādibhūmitraye caturdhā vaśitā veditavyā | ekasyāmacalāyāṃ bhūmau dvividhā | avikalpe na [?] cānabhisaṃskāranirvikalpatvāt | kṣetre ca buddhakṣetrapariśodhanāt | tadanyasyāṃ bhūmāvekai[vai]kā vaśitā sādhumatyāṃ jñānavaśitā pratisaṃvidviśeṣalābhāt | dharmameghāyāṃ karmaṇyabhijñākarmaṇāmavyāghātāt |
body.translated_text: This fourfold mastery should be understood in the three stages beginning with the <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). In one stage, the <s>Acalā</s>, there is twofold [mastery]: in the non-conceptual — because of being spontaneously non-conceptual without deliberate effort; and in the field — because of the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. In one other stage, the <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), there is mastery of knowledge — because of attaining the distinction of the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges). In the <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma), there is mastery of action — because of the unobstructed [exercise] of supernatural actions (<s>abhijñā</s>).

children.translated_text: Having understood the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) pertaining to existence,

children.text: samaṃ tacca jñātvā praviśati sa tattvaṃ grahaṇataḥ |
children.translated_text: the wise one, knowing that to be equal, enters reality through [mere] apprehension.

children.text: tatastatra sthānānmanasa iha na khyāti tadapi
children.translated_text: Then, from abiding therein, even that does not appear to the mind;

children.text: tadakhyānaṃ muktiḥ parama upalambhasya vigamaḥ || Msa_11.47 ||
children.translated_text: that non-appearance is liberation — the supreme cessation of apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>). || Msa_11.47 ||

body.text: aparo vimuktiparyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Another formulation of liberation:

body.text: dvividhaṃ nairātmyaṃ viditvā bhavatrayagataṃ bodhisattvaḥ samaṃ tacca jñātvā dvividhanairātmyaṃ parikalpitapudgalābhāvāt parikalpitadharmābhāvāt, na tu sarva thaivābhāvataḥ | tattvaṃ praviśati vijñaptimātratāṃ grahaṇato grahaṇamātrametaditi | tatastatra tattvavijñaptimātrasthānānmanasastadapi tattvaṃ na khyāti vijñaptimātram | tadakhyānaṃ muktiḥ parama upalambhasya yo vigamaḥ pudgaladharmayoranupalambhāt |
body.translated_text: Having understood the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) pertaining to the three realms of existence, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, knowing that to be equal — the twofold selflessness through the non-existence of the imagined person (<s>pudgala</s>) and the non-existence of imagined phenomena (<s>dharma</s>), but not through the complete non-existence of everything — enters reality, which is mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), through [mere] apprehension, [thinking] 'this is nothing but apprehension.' Then, from abiding in that reality of mere cognition, even that reality does not appear to the mind as mere cognition. That non-appearance is liberation — the supreme cessation of apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>), through the non-apprehension of both person and phenomena.

children.translated_text: Based on the support, from the accumulation [of merit and wisdom], when the placement is present, one sees mere name;

children.text: paśyati hi nāmamātraṃ tatpaśyaṃstacca naiva paśyati bhūyaḥ || Msa_11.48 ||
children.translated_text: one indeed sees mere name, and seeing that, one no longer sees even that. || Msa_11.48 ||

body.text: apara[raḥ]paryāyaḥ ādhāra iti śrutau saṃbhārāditi saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya pūrvasaṃbhāralābhāt | ādhāne satīti yoniśomanaskāre nāmamātraṃ paśyannityabhilāpamātramartharahitaṃ | paśyati hi nāmamātramiti vijñaptimātraṃ nāma arūpiṇaścatvāraḥ skandhā iti kṛtvā tatpaśyaṃstadapi bhūyo naiva paśyatyarthābhāve tadvijñaptyadarśanādityayamanupalambho vimuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: Another formulation: 'support' means in scripture (<s>śruti</s>); 'from the accumulation' means for one who has accumulated the accumulations, through obtaining the prior accumulations. 'When the placement is present' means when there is proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>), 'seeing mere name' means [seeing] mere verbal designation, devoid of [real] object. 'One indeed sees mere name' means mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), considering that the four immaterial aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) are called 'name.' 'Seeing that, one no longer sees even that' — because in the absence of the object, that cognition too is not seen. This non-apprehension is liberation.

children.translated_text: This mind, always endowed with dysfunction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), bound by the view of self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>),
operates [in existence]; but cessation is considered [to come] from its abiding within itself. || Msa_11.49 ||

body.text: apara[raḥ] prakāraḥ cittametatsadauṣṭhulyaṃ pravartate janmasu | ātmadarśanapāśitamiti dauṣṭhulyakāraṇaṃ darśayati | dvividhenātmadarśanena pāśitam ataḥ sadauṣṭhulyamiti | nivṛttistu tadadhyātmasthiteriti tasya cittasya citta evāvasthānādālambanānupalambhataḥ |
body.translated_text: Another mode: this mind, always endowed with dysfunction, operates in births. 'Bound by the view of self' shows the cause of the dysfunction — it is bound by the twofold view of self; therefore it is always endowed with dysfunction. 'But cessation is from its abiding within itself' — from the mind's resting in mind itself, through the non-apprehension of objects.

body.text: niḥsvabhāvatāparyeṣṭau ślokadvayam |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the search for non-self-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>).

children.translated_text: Because of non-existence by itself, because of non-abiding in its own nature,
and because of the non-existence of that as apprehended — non-self-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) is maintained. || Msa_11.50 ||

body.text: svayamabhāvānniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyayādhīnatvāt | svenātmanābhāvānniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ niruddhānāṃ punastenā [svenā?]tmanānutpatteḥ | svabhāva[ve] 'navasthitatvānniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ kṣaṇikatvādityetattrividhaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvam saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatrayānugaṃ veditavyam | grāhavattadabhāvācca niḥsvabhāvatvam | tadabhāvāditi svābhāvāt | yathā bālānāṃ svabhāvagrāho nityasukhaśucyātto[tmā] vānyena vā parikalpitalakṣaṇena tathāsau svabhāvo nāsti tasmādapi niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ dharmāṇāmiṣyate | ..........
body.translated_text: Non-self-nature of phenomena is because of dependence on conditions — [they do] not [exist] by themselves. Non-self-nature is because of the non-arising again with that same nature when [phenomena have] ceased — [they do] not [abide] in their own nature. Non-self-nature is because of momentariness — [they do] not abide in [their own] nature. This threefold non-self-nature should be understood as following the three characteristics of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). And non-self-nature is because of the non-existence of that which is apprehended — 'the non-existence of that' means the non-existence of self-nature. Just as the self-nature grasped by the childish — [as] permanent, pleasant, pure, or self, or by another imagined characteristic — such a self-nature does not exist; therefore too the non-self-nature of phenomena is maintained. ..........

body.text:
niḥsvabhāvatayā siddhā uttarottaraniśrayāḥ |
anutpannā niroddhādiśāntaprakṛtinirvṛtāḥ || Msa_11.51 ||
body.translated_text:
Established through non-self-nature, depending on each successively:
unborn, unceased, primordially quiescent, and extinguished by nature. || Msa_11.51 ||

body.text: siddhā
body.translated_text: Non-arising and the rest are [established]

body.text: niḥsvabhāvatayānutpādādayaḥ | yo hi niḥsvabhāvaḥ so 'nutpannaḥ, yo 'nutpannaḥ so 'nirūddhaḥ, yo 'nirūddhaḥ sa ādiśāntaḥ ya ādiśāntaḥ sa prakṛtiparinirvṛta ityevamuttarottaraniśrayairebhirniḥsvabhāvatā[di]bhirniḥsvabhāvatayānutpādādayaḥ siddhā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: through non-self-nature. For that which has no self-nature is unborn; that which is unborn is unceased; that which is unceased is primordially quiescent; that which is primordially quiescent is extinguished by nature (<s>prakṛtiparinirvṛta</s>). Thus, through these [qualities] depending on each successively — non-self-nature and the rest — non-arising and the other [qualities] are established through non-self-nature.

body.text: anutpattidharmakṣāntiparyeṣṭāvāryā |
body.translated_text: A verse on the search for patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (<s>anutpattidharmakṣānti</s>):

children.translated_text: In the beginning, in reality, in otherness, in own-characteristic, in self [nature], in becoming otherwise,
in defilement, and in distinction — patience regarding non-arising phenomena is declared. || Msa_11.52 ||

body.text: aṣṭāsvanutpattidharmeṣu kṣāntiranutpattikadharmakṣāntiḥ | ādau saṃsārasya, na hi tasyādyutpattirasti | tattve 'nyatve ca pūrvapaścimānāṃ, na hi saṃsāre teṣāmeva dharmāṇāmutpattiḥ, ye pūrvamutpannāstadbhāvenānutpatteḥ | na cānyeṣām, apūrvaprakārānutpatteḥ | svalakṣaṇe parikalpitasya svabhāvasya, na hi tasya kadācidutpattiḥ | svayamanutpattau paratantrasya | anyathābhāve pariniṣpannasya na hi tadanyathābhāvasyotpattirasti | saṃkleśe prahīṇe, na hi kṣayajñānalābhinaḥ saṃkleśasyotpattiṃ punaḥ paśyanti | viśeṣe buddhadharmakāyānām, na hi teṣāṃ viśeṣotpattirasti | ityeteṣvanutpattidharmeṣu kṣāntiranutpattidharmoktā |
body.translated_text: Patience regarding eight aspects of non-arising is the patience regarding non-arising phenomena (<s>anutpattidharmakṣānti</s>). In the beginning of <s>saṃsāra</s> — for it has no initial arising. In reality and otherness of the former and later — for in <s>saṃsāra</s>, those very phenomena that arose before do not arise [again] in that same form, because of not arising as those; nor do others arise, because of not arising in an unprecedented manner. In the own-characteristic of the imagined self-nature — for that never arises at any time. In the self [nature] of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) — [it does] not arise by itself. In the becoming otherwise of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) — for the arising of its becoming otherwise does not exist. In defilement, when abandoned — for those who have attained the knowledge of destruction do not see the arising of defilement again. In the distinction of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> — for there is no arising of distinction in those. In these aspects of non-arising, the patience is declared as patience regarding non-arising phenomena.

body.text: ekayānatāparyeṣṭau sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the search for the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Because of the equality of the Dharma, selflessness, and liberation; because of the differentiation of lineage (<s>gotra</s>);
because of the attainment of the twofold intention; and because of emanation and the final point — [there is] one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>). || Msa_11.53 ||

body.text: dharmatulyatvādekayānatā, śrāvakādīnāṃ dharmadhātorabhinnatvāt yātavyaṃ yānamiti kṛtvā | nairātmyasya tulyatvādekayānatā, śrāvakādīnāmātmābhāvatāsāmānyādyātā yānamiti kṛtvā | vimuktitulyatvādekayānatā, yāti yānamiti kṛtvā | gotrabhedādekayānatā | aniyataśrāvakagotrāṇāṃ mahāyānena niryāṇāt yānti tena yānamiti kṛtvā | dvyāśayāpte rekayānatā | buddhānāṃ ca sarvasattveṣvātmāśayaprāpteḥ, śrāvakāṇāṃ ca tadgotraniyatānāṃ pūrvaṃ bodhisaṃbhāracaritādanā[nāmā]tmani buddhāśayaprāpterabhinnasaṃtānādhimokṣalābhato buddhānubhāvena tathāgatānugrahaviśeṣapradeśalābhāya ityekatvāśayalābhenaikatvād buddhatacchrāvakāṇāmekayānatā | nirmāṇādekayānatā, yathoktamanekaśatakṛtvo 'haṃ śrāvakayānena parinirvṛta iti vineyānāmarthe tathā nirmāṇasaṃdarśanāt | paryantādapyekayānatā yataḥ pareṇa yātavyaṃ nāsti tadyānamiti kṛtvā | buddhatvamekayānam, evaṃ tatratatra sūtre tena tanābhiprāyeṇaikayānatā veditavyā, na tu yānatrayaṃ nāsti |
body.translated_text: The one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>) is due to the equality of <s>Dharma</s>, since for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of phenomena) is undifferentiated — considering 'that which is traveled is the vehicle.' The one vehicle is due to the equality of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), since for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others the non-existence of self (<s>ātman</s>) is common — considering 'that which is gone to is the vehicle.' The one vehicle is due to the equality of liberation — considering 'one goes by the vehicle.' The one vehicle is due to the differentiation of lineage (<s>gotra</s>), since those of indeterminate <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage attain final deliverance through the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — considering 'they go by that vehicle.' The one vehicle is due to the attainment of the twofold intention: both the <s>Buddhas</s>' attainment of the intention regarding self in all beings, and the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of determinate lineage having previously practiced the accumulations of awakening, thereby attaining the <s>Buddha</s>'s intention in themselves — through obtaining the faith of an undifferentiated continuum, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, for the purpose of obtaining the special domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s grace — thus, through obtaining the intention of oneness, the one vehicle pertains to <s>Buddhas</s> and their <s>Śrāvakas</s>. The one vehicle is due to emanation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>), as stated: 'I have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> hundreds of times' — because of showing such emanations for the benefit of those to be trained. The one vehicle is also due to the final point, since beyond that there is nothing to be traveled — considering 'that vehicle is Buddhahood.' Thus, in various sūtras, with various intentions, the one vehicle should be understood; but it is not the case that the three vehicles do not exist.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punastena tenābhiprāyeṇaikayānatā buddhairdeśitā |
body.translated_text: For what purpose, then, has the one vehicle been taught by the <s>Buddhas</s> with various intentions?

children.translated_text: For the purpose of attracting some and for the restraining of others,
the one vehicle has been taught by the perfectly awakened ones for those who are indeterminate. || Msa_11.54 ||

body.text: ākarṣaṇārthamekeṣāmiti ye śrāvakagotrā aniyatāḥ | anyeṣāṃ ca saṃdhāraṇāya, ye bodhisattvagotrā aniyatāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of attracting some' refers to those of <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage who are indeterminate. 'And for the restraining of others' refers to those of <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage who are indeterminate.

children.translated_text: The indeterminate <s>Śrāvaka</s> is twofold: based on the vehicle of one who has seen the truth and one who has not seen the truth;
the one who has seen the truth is either free from passion or not free from passion, and the latter is of mild [capacity]. || Msa_11.55 ||

body.text: śrāvakaḥ punaraniyato dvividho veditavyaḥ | dṛṣṭārthayānaśca yo dṛṣṭasatyo mahāyānena niryāti, adṛṣṭārthayānaśca yo na dṛṣṭasatyo mahāyānena niryāti | dṛṣṭārthaḥ punarvītarāgaścāvītarāgaśca kāmebhyaḥ | asau ca mṛdurdhandhagatiko veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The indeterminate <s>Śrāvaka</s> should be understood as twofold: one of the vehicle who has seen the truth — who, having seen the truths, attains final deliverance through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; and one of the vehicle who has not seen the truth — who, not having seen the truths, attains final deliverance through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The one who has seen the truth is again either free from passion or not free from passion regarding sensual desires. And the latter should be understood as of mild [capacity], of slow progress.

body.text: yo dṛṣṭārtho dvividha uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: The one who has seen the truth has been stated to be twofold:

children.translated_text: Both of them, through the maturation of the attained noble path in [future] existences,
are endowed with an inconceivably maturing rebirth. || Msa_11.56 ||

body.text: tau ca dṛṣṭārthau labdhasyāryamārgasya bhaveṣu pariṇāmanāt acintyapariṇāmikyā upapattyā samanvāgatau veditavyau | acintyo hi tasyāryamārgasya pariṇāma upapattau tasmādacintyapariṇāmikī |
body.translated_text: Both those who have seen the truth should be understood as endowed with an inconceivably maturing rebirth, through the maturation of the attained noble path in [future] existences. For the maturation of that noble path in rebirth is inconceivable; therefore [the rebirth is called] 'inconceivably maturing.'

children.translated_text: One, by the power of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), takes rebirth;
the other, by the force of the practice of non-returning (<s>anāgāmitā</s>), accomplishes [it] through emanations. || Msa_11.57 ||

body.text: tayoścaikaḥ praṇidhānavaśādupapattiṃ gṛhṇāti yatheṣṭaṃ yo na vītarāgaḥ | eko 'nāgāmitāyogabalena nirmāṇaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Of those two, one takes rebirth as desired by the power of aspiration — the one who is not free from passion. The other, by the force of the practice of non-returning, [accomplishes it] through emanations.

children.translated_text: Because of their delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, both are considered of slow progress,
due to the repeated arising of their own [<s>Śrāvaka</s>] mind. || Msa_11.58 ||

body.text: tau ca nirvāṇābhiratatvādubhāvapi dhandhagatikau matau ciratareṇābhisaṃbodhataḥ | svasya śrāvakacittasya nirvitsahagatasyābhīkṣṇaṃ samudācārāt |
body.translated_text: Both of them, because of their delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, are considered of slow progress — because of [their] very long time to full awakening, due to the frequent arising of their own <s>Śrāvaka</s> mind accompanied by disenchantment.

children.translated_text: That one who has not accomplished his purpose, born in a time without a <s>Buddha</s>, strives for <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation),
desiring emanation, and relying on that, attains supreme awakening. || Msa_11.59 ||

body.text: yaḥ punarasāvavītarāgo dṛṣṭasatyaḥ so 'kṛtārthaḥ śaikṣo bhavan buddharahite kāle jāto dhyānārthamudyato bhavati nirmāṇārthī | tacca nirmāṇamāśritya krameṇa parāṃ bodhiṃ prāpnoti | tamavasthātrayasthaṃ saṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā śrīmālāsūtre | śrāvako bhūtvā pratyekabuddho bhavati punaśca buddha iti | agnidṛṣṭānte[na] ca yadā ca pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭasatyāvasthā[stho] yadā buddharahite kāle svayaṃ dhyānamutpādya janmakāyaṃ tyaktvā nirmāṇakāyaṃ gṛhṇāti yadā ca parāṃ bodhiṃ prāpnotīti |
body.translated_text: The one who is not free from passion and has seen the truths — he, being a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) who has not accomplished his purpose, born in a time without a <s>Buddha</s>, strives for <s>dhyāna</s>, desiring emanation. And relying on that emanation, he gradually attains supreme awakening. Referring to him in these three states, the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the <s>Śrīmālā Sūtra</s>: 'Having been a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, he becomes a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and then again a <s>Buddha</s>.' And by the analogy of fire: when he is first in the state of having seen the truths, when in a time without a <s>Buddha</s> he himself generates <s>dhyāna</s> and, abandoning the birth-body, takes an emanation-body, and when he attains supreme awakening.

body.text: vidyāsthānaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the search for the fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>):

children.text: vidyāsthāne pañcavidhe yogamakṛtvā sarvajñatvaṃ naiti kathaṃcitparamāryaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without practicing in the five fields of knowledge, the supreme noble one can in no way attain omniscience;

children.text: ityanyeṣāṃ nigrahaṇānugrahaṇāya svājñārthaṃ vā tatra karotyeva sa yogam || Msa_11.60 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, for the purpose of subduing others, benefiting them, or [gaining] one's own knowledge, he indeed practices therein. || Msa_11.60 ||

body.text: pañcavidhaṃ vidyāsthānam | adhyātmavidyā hetuvidyā śabdavidyā cikitsāvidyā śilpakarmasthānavidyā ca | tadyadarthaṃ bodhisattvena paryeṣitavyaṃ taddarśayati | sarvajñatvaprāptyarthamabhedena sarvam | bhedena punarhetuvidyāṃ śabdavidyāṃ ca paryeṣate nigrahārthamanyeṣāṃ tadanadhimuktānām | cikitsāvidyāṃ śilpakarmasthānavidyāṃ cānyeṣāmanugrahārthaṃ tadarthikānām | adhyātmavidyāṃ svayamājñārtham |
body.translated_text: The five fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>) are: inner knowledge (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), logic (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>). He shows the purpose for which they should be sought by the <s>bodhisattva</s>: for the attainment of omniscience — all of them without distinction. In terms of distinction, however, he seeks logic and grammar for the purpose of subduing others who lack faith in them. He seeks medicine and arts and crafts for the benefit of others who desire them. He seeks inner knowledge for the purpose of his own realization.

body.text: dhātupuṣṭiparyeṣṭau trayodaśa ślokāḥ | pāramitāparipūraṇārthaṃ ye pāramitāpratisaṃyuktā evaṃ manasikārā dhātupuṣṭaye bhavanti ta etābhirgāthābhirdeśitāḥ |
