body.translated_text: Thirteen verses on the search for the nourishment of the element (<s>dhātupuṣṭi</s>). The mental engagements connected with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), which serve to nourish the element for the purpose of fulfilling the <s>pāramitās</s>, are taught through these verses.

children.translated_text: Satisfaction in obtaining the cause, reliance and its recollection,
desire for a shared fruit, and conviction according to awakening. || Msa_11.61 ||

body.text: te punarhetūpalabdhituṣṭiumanasikārāt yāvadagratvātmāvadhāraṇamanasikāraḥ | tatra hetūpalabdhituṣṭimanasikāra ādita eva tāvat | gotrastho bodhisattvaḥ svātmani pāramitānāṃ gotraṃ paśyan hetūpalabdhituṣṭyā pāramitādhātupuṣṭiṃ karoti | gotrastho 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayatītyato 'nantaraṃ niśrayatadanusmṛtimanasikāraḥ | sa hi bodhisattvaḥ svātmani pāramitānāṃ saṃniśrayabhūtaṃ bodhicittaṃ samanupaśyannevaṃ manasikaroti niyatametāḥ pāramitāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti | tathā hyasmākaṃ bodhicittaṃ saṃvidyate iti | utpāditabodhicittasya pāramitābhiḥ svaparārthaprayoge sādharaṇaphalecchāmanasikāra, āsāṃ pāramitānāṃ parasādhāraṇaṃ vā phalaṃ bhavatvanyathā vā mā bhūdityabhisaṃskaraṇāt | svaparārthaṃ prayujyamāno 'saṃkleśopāyaṃ tattvārthaṃ pratividhyatītyato 'nantaraṃ yathābodhādhimucyanāmanasikāraḥ | evaṃ sarvatrānukamo veditavyaḥ | yathā buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ pāramitā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante 'bhisaṃbudhyante ca tathāhamadhimucye ityabhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: These [mental engagements] range from the mental engagement of satisfaction in obtaining the cause to the mental engagement of ascertaining oneself as foremost. Therein, first of all, the mental engagement of satisfaction in obtaining the cause: the <s>bodhisattva</s>, established in the lineage (<s>gotra</s>), seeing in himself the lineage of the <s>pāramitās</s>, nourishes the element of the <s>pāramitās</s> through satisfaction in obtaining the cause. Since one established in the lineage generates the mind of supreme perfect awakening — immediately after that comes the mental engagement of reliance and its recollection. For that <s>bodhisattva</s>, seeing in himself the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) that serves as the basis for the <s>pāramitās</s>, engages mentally thus: 'Certainly these <s>pāramitās</s> will reach fulfillment, for our <s>bodhicitta</s> is present.' For one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, in the practice of benefiting self and others through the <s>pāramitās</s>, [comes] the mental engagement of desire for a shared fruit — through the intention: 'May the fruit of these <s>pāramitās</s> be shared with others, or even if not, let it be.' While engaged in benefiting self and others, one penetrates the ultimate reality through the means free from defilement — immediately after that comes the mental engagement of conviction according to awakening. Thus the sequence should be understood throughout. Through the intention: 'Just as the <s>pāramitās</s> have been fully realized by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, will be realized, and are being realized — so do I aspire.'

children.translated_text: Through fourfold power, delight, determination in the face of weariness,
and fourfold practice regarding the adversary and the antidote. || Msa_11.62 ||

body.text: anubhāvaprīyaṇāmanasikāraścaturvidhānubhāvadarśanaprīyaṇā, caturvidhānubhāvo vipakṣaprahāṇaṃ, saṃbhāraparipākaḥ, svaparānugraha, āyatyāṃ vipākaphalaniḥṣyandaphaladānatā ca | sattvasvabuddhadharmaparipākamārabhyākhedaniścayamanasikāraḥ, sarvasattvavipratipattibhiḥ sarvaduḥkhāpattipātaiścākhedaniścayābhisaṃskaraṇāt paramabodhiprāptaye | vipakṣe pattipakṣe ca caturvidhapratipattimanasikāraḥ | dānādivipakṣāṇāṃ ca mātsaryādīnāṃ pratideśanā, pratipakṣāṇāṃ ca dānādīnāmanumodanā, tadadhipateyadharmadeśanārthaṃ ca buddhādhyeṣaṇā | tāsāṃ ca bodhau pariṇāmanā |
body.translated_text: The mental engagement of delight in power is delight from seeing fourfold power. The fourfold power is: abandonment of adversaries, maturation of accumulations, benefiting self and others, and in the future, the giving of the fruits of maturation and outflow-fruits. The mental engagement of determination in the face of weariness — beginning with the maturation of beings, one's own [nature], and <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — is the intention of unwavering determination in the face of all the errors of beings, all the calamities of suffering, for the attainment of supreme awakening. The mental engagement of fourfold practice regarding the adversary and the antidote: confession of the adversaries of generosity and the rest, such as miserliness and the like; rejoicing in the antidotes of generosity and the like; supplication to the <s>Buddhas</s> for the purpose of teaching the Dharma that governs these; and dedication of those to awakening.

children.text: prasādaḥ saṃpratīkṣā ca dānacchandaḥ paratra ca |
children.translated_text: Faith, acceptance, desire to give, and regarding others,
armor, aspiration, and the mental engagement of rejoicing. || Msa_11.63 ||

body.text: adhimuktibalādhānatāmārabhya pāramitādhipateyadharmārthe ca prasādamanasikāraḥ | dharmaparyeṣṭimārabhya saṃpratīcchanamanasikārastasyaiva dharmasyāprativahanayogena parigrahaṇatayā | da[de]śanāmārabhya dānacchandamanasikāro dharmasyārthasya ca prakāśanārthaṃ pareṣām | pratipattimārabhya saṃnāhamanasikāro dānādiparipūriye saṃnahanāt | praṇidhānamanasikārastatparipūriprāptaye[pratyaye] samavadhānārthaṃ | abhinandamanasikāro 'ho bata dānādipratipattyā samyak saṃpādayeyamityabhinandanāt | eta eva trayo manasikārā avavādānuśāsanyāṃ yojayitavyāḥ | upāyopasaṃhitakarmamanasikāraḥ saṃkalpaiḥ sarvaprakāradānādiprayogamanasikaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: Beginning with the undertaking of the power of aspiration, the mental engagement of faith in the Dharma that governs the <s>pāramitās</s>. Beginning with the search for the Dharma, the mental engagement of acceptance — through embracing that very Dharma by the method of not relinquishing it. Beginning with teaching, the mental engagement of desire to give — for the purpose of illuminating the Dharma and its meaning to others. Beginning with practice, the mental engagement of armor — from girding oneself for the fulfillment of generosity and the rest. The mental engagement of aspiration — for the purpose of establishing the conditions for attaining that fulfillment. The mental engagement of rejoicing — from the delight: 'Oh, may I properly accomplish [this] through the practice of generosity and the rest!' These same three mental engagements should be applied to instruction and guidance. The mental engagement of action endowed with skillful means — from mentally engaging in the practice of generosity and the rest in every manner through [wholesome] intentions.

children.translated_text: Constant eagerness in obtaining the capacity, sixfold endeavor in generosity and the rest,
and regarding maturation, worship, service, and compassion. || Msa_11.64 ||

body.text: autsukyamanasikāraścaturvidhaḥ | śaktilābhe ca dānādau ṣaḍvidhe dānadāne yāvat prajñādāne | evaṃ śīlādiṣu ṣaḍvidheṣu | pāramitābhireva saṃgrahavastuprayogeṇa sattvaparipāke | pūjāyāṃ ca dānena lābhasatkārapūjayā | śeṣābhiśca pratipattipūjayā |
body.translated_text: The mental engagement of eagerness is fourfold: in obtaining the capacity, and in the sixfold [practice] of generosity and the rest — from the giving of generosity up to the giving of wisdom, and similarly in the sixfold [practice] of moral discipline and the rest. In the maturation of beings through the practice of the means of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) by means of the <s>pāramitās</s> themselves. In worship — through generosity, by worship of gain, honor, and reverence; and through the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>], by worship through practice.

body.text: aviparītapāramitopadeśāpa[rtha]ñcakalyāṇamitrasevāyāmautsukyamanasikāro veditavyaḥ | anukampāmanasikāraścaturbhirapramāṇairdānādyupasaṃhāreṇa maitrāyataḥ | mātsaryādisamavadhānena sattveṣu karuṇāyataḥ | dānādisamanvāgateṣu muditāyataḥ | tadasaṃkleśādhimokṣataśca upekṣāyataḥ
body.translated_text: The mental engagement of eagerness should be understood regarding the service of a good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who gives non-erroneous instruction in the <s>pāramitās</s>. The mental engagement of compassion is through the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) combined with generosity and the rest: from <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) — through removing miserliness and the like regarding beings; from <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) — through establishing [the conditions for the cessation of] miserliness and the like in beings; from <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) — regarding those endowed with generosity and the rest; and from <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) — through the aspiration for non-defilement regarding those.

children.text: akṛte kukṛte lajjā kaukṛtyaṃ viṣaye ratiḥ |
children.translated_text: Shame regarding what is not done and what is badly done, remorse, delight in the object,
the perception of the enemy regarding weariness, and the intention of composition and promulgation. || Msa_11.65 ||

body.text: hīdharmamārabhya lajjāmanaskāraḥ, akṛteṣu vā dānādiṣvaparipūrṇamithyākṛteṣu vā lajjā, lajjāyamānaśca pravṛttinivṛttyarthamanānuṣaṅgikaṃ kaukṛtyāyate | dhṛtimārabhya ratimanaskāro dānādyālambane 'vikṣepataścittasya dhāraṇāt | akhedamanaskāro dānādiprayogaparikhede śatrusaṃjñākaraṇāt | racanācchandamanaskāraḥ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaśāsraracanābhisaṃskaraṇāt | lokajñatāmārabhya udbhāvanāmanaskārastasyaiva śāstrasya loke yathābhājanamudbhāvanābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: Beginning with the sense of moral conscience (<s>hrī</s>), the mental engagement of shame — shame regarding generosity and the rest that are not done or that are not fully and wrongly done; and one who feels shame generates remorse for the purpose of engaging and refraining, without attachment. Beginning with steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), the mental engagement of delight — from the mind's focused attention on the object of generosity and the rest without distraction. The mental engagement of non-weariness — from perceiving as an enemy the fatigue in the practice of generosity and the rest. The mental engagement of desire for composition — from the intention of composing treatises (<s>śāstra</s>) connected with the <s>pāramitās</s>. Beginning with knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>), the mental engagement of promulgation — from the intention of promulgating that very treatise in the world according to [people's] capacity.

children.translated_text: Generosity and the rest are the refuge for awakening, not <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and the like,

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca pratisaṃvedanād [?]dvayoḥ || Msa_11.66 ||
children.translated_text: through the experience of the faults and virtues of both. || Msa_11.66 ||

body.text: pratisaraṇamanaskāro bodhiprāptaye dānādīnāṃ pratisaraṇānneśvarādīnām, pratisaṃvinmanaskāro mātsaryadānādi vipakṣapratipakṣayordoṣaguṇapratisaṃvedanāt |
body.translated_text: The mental engagement of refuge — for the attainment of awakening, relying on generosity and the rest, not on <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. The mental engagement of experience — from experiencing the faults and virtues of the adversary and the antidote, [namely] miserliness and generosity and the like.

children.translated_text: Recollection with joy regarding the accumulation, and the seeing of its great purpose,
desire for practice in the non-conceptual, and upon the arrival of its condition, steadfastness therein. || Msa_11.67 ||

body.text: cayānusmaraṇaprītimanaskāro dānādyupacaye puṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayasaṃdarśanāt | māhārthyasaṃdarśanamanaskāro dānādīnāṃ bodhipakṣe bhāvārthena mahābodhiprāptyarthasaṃdarśanāt | abhilāṣamanaskāraḥ sa punaścaturvidhaḥ | yogābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ śamathavipaśyanāyogabhāvanābhilāṣāt | avikalpābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ pāramitāparipūraṇārthamupāyakauśalyābhilāṣāt | dhṛtyabhilāṣamanaskāraḥ pāramitādhipateyadharmārthadhāraṇābhilāṣāt | pratyayābhigamābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ samyak praṇidhānābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of recollecting the joy of accumulation is from seeing the accumulation of the accumulations of merit and knowledge through giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest. The mental attention of displaying great purpose is from displaying the purpose of attaining great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) through the meaning of existence in the factors of awakening for giving and the rest. The mental attention of aspiration is further fourfold: the mental attention of aspiration for yoga — from the aspiration for the cultivation of the yoga of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); the mental attention of aspiration for non-conceptuality — from the aspiration for skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) for the purpose of fulfilling the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); the mental attention of aspiration for retention — from the aspiration for retaining the dominant dharmas of the <s>pāramitās</s> and their meaning; and the mental attention of aspiration for the approach to conditions — from the conditioning of correct aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).

children.translated_text: The display of capacity for the overcoming of sevenfold false grasping,

children.text: āścaryaṃ cāpyanāścaryaṃ saṃjñā caiva caturvidhā || Msa_11.68 ||
children.translated_text: and the wondrous and the non-wondrous, and fourfold perception — || Msa_11.68 ||

body.text: saptaprakārāsadgrāhavyutthānaśaktidarśanamanaskāraḥ | saptavidho 'sadgrāhaḥ | asati sadgrāhaḥ, doṣavati guṇavatvagrāhaḥ, guṇavatyaguṇavatvagrāhaḥ, sarvasaṃskāreṣu ca nityasukhāsadgrāhau, sarvadharmeṣu cātmāsadgrāhaḥ, nirvāṇe cāśāntāsadgrāhaḥ | yasya pratipakṣeṇa śūnyatā [di]samādhitrayaṃ dharmoddānacatuṣṭayaṃ ca deśyate | āścarye caturvidhasaṃjñāmanaskāraḥ | pāramitāsūdārasaṃjñā, āyatattvasaṃjñā, pratikāranirapekṣasaṃjñā, vipākanirapekṣasaṃjñā ca | anāścarye 'pi caturvidha[saṃjñā]manaskāraḥ | caturvidhamanāścaryamaudarya āyatatve ca sati pāramitānāṃ buddhatvaphalābhinirvartanāt | asminneva ca dvaye sati svaparasamacittāvasthāpanāt [vasthāpanā?]tadviśiṣṭebhyaśca (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 73

children.text: ) śaru[śakrā]dibhyaḥ pūjādilābhe sati pratikāranirapekṣatā ..... [sarvalokebhyo viśiṣṭaśarīrabhoga]lābhe satyapi vipākanirapekṣatā |
children.translated_text: ) given the obtaining of worship and the like from <s>Śakra</s> and others who are distinguished [in these respects], the disregard for reciprocation ..... [and given the obtaining of a body and enjoyments] distinguished from all worlds, the disregard for karmic fruition.

body.translated_text: The mental attention of the display of capacity for overcoming sevenfold false grasping: sevenfold false grasping consists of — grasping something as existent when it does not exist; grasping what has faults as having qualities; grasping what has qualities as lacking qualities; and in all conditioned things, the false graspings of permanence and pleasure; in all dharmas, the false grasping of self; and in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the false grasping of non-quiescence. As the antidote to these, the three concentrations on emptiness [and the rest] and the fourfold summary of the Dharma (<s>dharmoddāna</s>) are taught. The mental attention of perception regarding the wondrous is fourfold: the perception of magnificence regarding the <s>pāramitās</s>; the perception of their vastness; the perception of disregard for reciprocation; and the perception of disregard for karmic fruition. And the mental attention of perception regarding the non-wondrous is also fourfold: the fourfold non-wonder [arises because], given the magnificence and vastness of the <s>pāramitās</s>, the production of Buddhahood as their fruit [is not surprising]; and given these two, [it is not surprising that] one establishes oneself and others in equality of mind, and (

children.translated_text: Equality toward all beings, and a magnanimous view,
hope for the reciprocal qualities of others, and uninterrupted [practice] — || Msa_11.69 ||

body.text: samatāmanaskāraḥ sarvasattveṣu dānādibhiḥ samatāpravṛttyabhisaṃskaraṇāt | mahātmadṛṣṭimanaskāraḥ sarvasattvopakāratayā pāramitāsaṃdarśanāt | pratyaya[pratyupa]kārāśaṃsanamanaskāro dānādiguṇapravṛttyā parebhyaḥ | āśāstimanaskāraḥ sattveṣu tristhānāśaṃsanāt pāramitānāṃ bodhisattvabhūminiṣṭhāyā buddhabhūminiṣṭhāyāḥ sattvāva[rthāca]raṇāśaṃsanācca | nirantaramanaskāro dānādibhirabadhya[ndhya]kālakaraṇābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of equality is through the conditioning of equal activity toward all beings through giving and the rest. The mental attention of magnanimous view is through seeing the <s>pāramitās</s> as benefiting all beings. The mental attention of hoping for reciprocal benefit is through the activity of qualities such as giving toward others. The mental attention of aspiration is through aspiring for beings in three ways — aspiring for the <s>pāramitās</s>' culmination in the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages, in the <s>Buddha</s> stage, and aspiring for the welfare of beings. The mental attention of uninterruptedness is through the conditioning of making time unfailing through giving and the rest.

children.translated_text: From practicing in accordance with what the <s>Buddha</s> has taught, from the intention of those not yet established,
from the decrease and increase of that in beings — displeasure and rejoicing. || Msa_11.70 ||

body.text: samyakprayogamanaskāro 'viparītānuṣṭhānādarvāgasthānamanasikaraṇāt | anāmodamanaskāro dānādibhirhīyamāneṣu | pramodamanaskāro dānādibhirvardhamāneṣu sattveṣu |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of correct application is from non-erroneous practice and from the mental attention toward those not yet established. The mental attention of displeasure is toward beings who are declining in giving and the rest. The mental attention of rejoicing is toward beings who are increasing in giving and the rest.

children.translated_text: Neither aversion toward the counterpart [practice] and the genuine practice,
nor the mental attention of acquiescence; aspiration regarding the certain and the determined — || Msa_11.71 ||

body.text: arūcimanaskāraḥ pāramitāprativarṇikābhāvanāyām | rūcimanaskāro bhūtāyām | anadhivāsanāmanaskāro mātsaryādivipakṣavinayanābhisaṃskāraṇāt | spṛhāmanaskāro dvividhaḥ pāramitāparipūrivyākaraṇalābhaspṛhāmanaskāraḥ pāramitāniyatabhūmyavasthālābhaspṛhāmanaskāraśca |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of aversion is toward the non-genuine practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>. The mental attention of non-aversion is toward the genuine [practice]. The mental attention of non-acquiescence is from the conditioning of subduing the adverse factors such as miserliness. The mental attention of aspiration is twofold: the mental attention of aspiration for obtaining the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s>, and the mental attention of aspiration for obtaining the determined stage of the <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: Activity from seeing the future, intention, seeing with equality,
and through activity in the supreme dharmas, the ascertainment of supremacy of self — || Msa_11.72 ||

body.text: āyatyāṃ darśanādvṛttimanaskāro yātvā[yāṃ yāṃ] gatiṃ gatvā bodhisattvena satāvaśya karaṇīyatābhisaṃskāraṇāt | dānādīnāṃ samatekṣaṇāmanaskārastadanyairbodhisattvaiḥ sahātmanaḥ pāramitāsātatyakaraṇādhimokṣārtham | agratvātmāvadhāraṇamanaskāraḥ pāramitāgradharmapravṛttyā svātmanaḥ pradhānabhāvasaṃdarśanāt |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of activity from seeing the future is from the conditioning that a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having gone to whatever destiny, necessarily has duties to perform. The mental attention of seeing with equality regarding giving and the rest is for the purpose of conviction in the continuity of one's own <s>pāramitā</s>-practice together with other <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The mental attention of the ascertainment of supremacy of self is from displaying oneself as foremost through the activity of the supreme dharmas of the <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: These wholesome mental attentions pertaining to the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections)

children.text: sarvadā bodhisattvānāṃ dhātupuṣṭau bhavanti hi || Msa_11.73 ||
children.translated_text: exist always for <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the nourishment of the element (<s>dhātu</s>). || Msa_11.73 ||

body.text: iti nigamanaśloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the concluding verse has its meaning already explained.

body.text: dharmaparyeṣṭibhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the divisions of the search for Dharma (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>):

children.translated_text: Through nourishment and superior intention, the great search is accepted for the steadfast;

children.text: savivāsā hyavivāsā tathaiva vaibhutvikī teṣām || Msa_11.74 ||
children.translated_text: it is with dwelling, without dwelling, and likewise of the nature of sovereignty — for them. || Msa_11.74 ||
It is without body, with [newly] obtained body, and with fully developed body — for <s>bodhisattvas</s>;
with great pride, subtle pride, and through emanation — the search is regarded [thus]. || Msa_11.75 ||

body.text: trayodaśavidhā paryeṣṭiḥ | puṣṭitaḥ śrutādhimuktipuṣṭyā | adhyāśayato dharmamukhastrotasā | mahatī citta[vibhu]tvalābhinām | sabiprabāsā prathamā | avipravāsā dvitīyā | vaibhutvikī tṛtīyā | akāyā śrutacintāmayī dharmakāyarahitatvāt | sakāyā bhāvanāmayī adhimukticaryābhūmo | laghu[labdha]kāyā saptasu bhūmiṣu | paripūrṇakāyā śeṣāsu | bahumānādhimukticaryābhūmau | sūkṣmamānā saptasu | nirmāṇā śeṣāsu |
body.translated_text: The search is of thirteen kinds: through nourishment — through the nourishment of faith based on what has been heard. Through superior intention — through the stream of the gateway of Dharma. Great — for those who have obtained vastness of mind. With dwelling — the first [type]. Without dwelling — the second. Of the nature of sovereignty — the third. Without body — that arising from hearing and reflection, because of being devoid of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. With body — that arising from cultivation, on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>). With [newly] obtained body — on the seven stages. With fully developed body — on the remaining [three stages]. With great pride — on the stage of devoted conduct. With subtle pride — on the seven [stages]. Through emanation — on the remaining [stages].

body.text: dharmahetutvaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the search for the cause-nature of Dharma:

children.translated_text: In the realm of form and the formless realm, the Dharma is the cause of [excellent] characteristics; likewise in [the cause of] health,
in sovereignty through the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and in the imperishability of that — for the steadfast. || Msa_11.76 ||

body.text: rūpe lakṣaṇaheturdharmaḥ | arūpe ārogyahetuḥ kleśavyādhipraśamanāt | aiśvaryaheturabhijñābhistadakṣayatvahetuścānupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pyanupacchedāt | ata evoktaṃ brahmaparipṛcchāsūtre | caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā dharmaṃ paryeṣante | ratnasaṃjñayā durlabhārthena bhaiṣajyasaṃjñayā kleśavyādhipraśamanārthena arthasaṃjñayā avipraṇāśārthena nirvāṇasaṃjñayā sarvaduḥkhapraśamanārthena | ratnabhūtāni hi lakṣaṇāni śobhākaratvādatastaddhetutvāddharmaratnasaṃjñā | ārogyahetutvādbhaiṣajyasaṃjñā | abhijñaiścaryahetutvādarthasaṃjñā | tadakṣayahetutvānnirvāṇasaṃjñākṣayanirbhayatārthena |
body.translated_text: In the realm of form, the Dharma is the cause of [the Buddha's excellent physical] characteristics. In the formless realm, it is the cause of health — through the pacification of the disease of afflictions. It is the cause of sovereignty through the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). And it is the cause of their imperishability — because there is no interruption even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>). Therefore it is said in the <s>Brahmaparipṛcchāsūtra</s>: '<s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four dharmas search for the Dharma — with the perception of a jewel, for the purpose of [obtaining] something rare; with the perception of medicine, for the purpose of pacifying the disease of afflictions; with the perception of wealth, for the purpose of non-destruction; and with the perception of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, for the purpose of pacifying all suffering.' For the [excellent bodily] characteristics are like jewels, because of producing beauty; therefore, because [the Dharma] is their cause, [there is] the perception of a Dharma-jewel. Because of being the cause of health, [there is] the perception of medicine. Because of being the cause of the sovereignty of the <s>abhijñās</s>, [there is] the perception of wealth. Because of being the cause of their imperishability, [there is] the perception of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — in the sense of fearlessness regarding cessation.

body.text: vikalpaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the search regarding conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>):

children.translated_text: The conceptualizations of non-existence, existence, superimposition, deprecation, oneness, diversity, own-characteristic, distinction,
and attachment to name as corresponding to the object, and attachment to object as corresponding to the name — are to be avoided by the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_11.77 ||

body.text: daśavidhavikalpo bodhisattvena parivarjanīyaḥ | abhāvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | prajñāpāramitāyāmiha bodhisattvo bodhisattva eva sanniti | bhāvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 75

children.text: ) bodhisattvaṃ na samanupaśyatītyevamādi | adhyāropavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | rūpaṃ śāriputra svabhāvena śūnyamiti | apavādavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | na śūnyatayeti | ekatvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | yā rūpasya śūnyatā na tadrūpamiti | nānātvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | na cānyatra śūnyatāyā rūpaṃ rūpameva śūnyatā śūnyataiva rūpamiti | svalakṣaṇavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | nāmamātramidaṃ yadidaṃ rūpamiti | viśeṣavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | rūpasya hi notpādo na nirodho na saṃkleśo na vyavadānamiti | yathānāmārthābhiniveśavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | kṛtrimaṃ nāmetyevamādi | yathārthanāmābhiniveśavikalpaśca yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | tāni bodhisattvaḥ sarvanāmāni na samanupaśyatyasamanupaśyannābhiniviśate yathārthatayetyabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) 'One does not perceive the <s>bodhisattva</s>' and so forth. The conceptualization of superimposition — as the antidote to which it says: 'Form, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of its own nature.' The conceptualization of deprecation — as the antidote to which it says: 'Not by emptiness.' The conceptualization of oneness — as the antidote to which it says: 'That which is the emptiness of form is not that form.' The conceptualization of diversity — as the antidote to which it says: 'Nor is form other than emptiness; form itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is form.' The conceptualization of own-characteristic — as the antidote to which it says: 'This which is called form is a mere name.' The conceptualization of distinction — as the antidote to which it says: 'Form has no arising, no cessation, no defilement, no purification.' The conceptualization of attachment to name as corresponding to the object — as the antidote to which it says: 'The name is artificial' and so forth. And the conceptualization of attachment to object as corresponding to the name — as the antidote to which it says: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s> does not perceive all those names; not perceiving them, one does not attach to them as corresponding to the object' — this is the intended meaning.

body.translated_text: Tenfold conceptualization is to be avoided by the <s>bodhisattva</s>: the conceptualization of non-existence — as the antidote to which [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] says: 'In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is indeed a <s>bodhisattva</s>.' The conceptualization of existence — as the antidote to which it says: (

children.translated_text: Thus, having attained good understanding with intense effort, the reality of dharmas sought through duality —

children.text: pratiśaraṇamataḥ sadā prajānāṃ bhavati guṇaiḥ sa samudravatprapūrṇaḥ || Msa_11.78 ||
children.translated_text: one becomes a refuge for beings always, filled with qualities like the ocean. || Msa_11.78 ||

body.text: anena nigamanaślokena paryeṣṭimāhātmyaṃ trividhaṃ darśayati | upāyamāhātmyamugravīryatayā saṃvṛttiparamārthasatyadharmatāparyeṣaṇataśca tattvaṃ satyamityarthaḥ | parārthamāhātmyaṃ pratiśaraṇībhāvāt prajānām | svārthamāhātmyaṃ ca guṇaiḥ samudravat prapūrṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this concluding verse, he shows the threefold greatness of the search: the greatness of means — through intense vigor and the search for the reality of the Dharma of conventional and ultimate truth, 'reality' meaning truth. The greatness of the welfare of others — through becoming a refuge for beings. And the greatness of self-interest — through being filled with qualities like the ocean.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre dharmaparyeṣṭyadhikāra ekādaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eleventh chapter on the search for Dharma (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>) ||

body.text: dvādaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Twelfth chapter:

body.text: dharmadeśanāyāṃ mātsaryapratiṣedhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the prohibition of miserliness in Dharma-teaching:

children.translated_text: The steadfast, with joyful minds, constantly relinquish their lives and possessions — which are hard-won and without essence —
to suffering beings through the loftiest forms of giving;
how much more so the noble Dharma, which repeatedly benefits beings in every way,

children.text: kṛcchre naivopalabdhaṃ bhṛśamavasṛjatāṃ vṛddhigaṃ cāvyayaṃ ca || Msa_12.1 ||
children.translated_text: and which, when abundantly given, increases and is inexhaustible — [how much more should it not be given?] || Msa_12.1 ||

body.text: kṛcchralabdhānapyasārān kṣayitvā[t]prāṇān bhogāṃśca bodhisattvā duḥkhitebhyaḥ kāruṇyāt satatasamudārairvisargairutsṛjanti prāgeva dharmaṃ yo naiva kṛcchreṇa vā bhṛśamapi vāvasṛjatāṃ vṛddhiṃ gacchati na kṣayaṃ |
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, out of compassion, constantly give up to suffering beings — through the most magnificent acts of relinquishment — their lives and possessions, though hard-won and without essence due to their perishability. How much more should they give the Dharma, which, even when given abundantly and profusely, grows and does not diminish!

body.text: dharma nairarthakyasārthakye ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the purposefulness and meaningfulness of the Dharma:

body.text: dharmo naiva ca deśito bhagavatā pratyātmavedyo yata

children.text: ākṛṣṭā janatā ca yukta[yukti]vihitairdharmaiḥ svakīṃ dharmatāṃ
children.translated_text: yet beings are drawn by dharmas established through reasoning to their own true nature —
in the vast and pure opening of the mouth of [the Buddha's] own peace, which is shared and inexhaustible,
they are brought [to liberation] by the compassionate ones who are like great pythons (<s>ajagara</s>). || Msa_12.2 ||

body.translated_text: The Dharma has not truly been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), since it is to be personally experienced;

body.text: tatra buddhā ajagaropamāsteṣāṃ svaśānti[śānte?]rāsyapuṭaṃ dharmakāyaḥ | viśuddhivipulaṃ savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhitaḥ | sādhāraṇaṃ sarvabuddhaiḥ akṣayamātyantikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Buddhas</s> are like great pythons; the opening of their mouths, which is their own peace, is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. It is vast in purity — because of purification from the obscurations of afflictions and the knowable together with their latent impressions. It is shared by all <s>Buddhas</s>. It is inexhaustible — because of being ultimate.

children.text: tasmānnaiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā bhāvanā yogināṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, the cultivation of <s>yogins</s> is indeed not purposeless;

children.text: tasmānnaiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā deśanā saugatī |
children.translated_text: therefore, the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) is indeed not purposeless.
If the meaning were seen from mere hearing, cultivation would be purposeless;
if one could enter cultivation without having heard, teaching would be purposeless. || Msa_12.3 ||

body.text: tasmānna nirarthikā yogināṃ bhāvanā bhavati pratyātmavedyasya dharmasya tadvaśenābhigamāt | na nirarthikā deśanā bhavati yuktivihitairdharmaiḥ svadharmatāyāṃ janatākarṣaṇāt | yathā punarbhāvanā sārthikā bhaveddeśanā vā tat ślokārdhena darśayati | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the cultivation of <s>yogins</s> is not purposeless — because of the realization of the personally-experienced Dharma through that [cultivation]. The teaching is not purposeless — because of drawing beings to their own true nature through dharmas established by reasoning. And the half-verse shows how cultivation becomes purposeful or how teaching [becomes purposeful]: the rest has its meaning already explained.

body.text: deśanāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the divisions of teaching:

children.translated_text: From scripture (<s>āgama</s>), from realization (<s>adhigama</s>), from sovereignty — the teaching of the supreme beings;
from the mouth, from form, from all [things] like space, the utterance also ...... || Msa_12.4 ||

body.text: tatra vibhutvato yā mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ | sarvato rūpādyā vṛkṣavāditrādibhyo 'pi niścarati | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, from sovereignty — that of those who have entered the great stages (<s>bhūmi</s>). From all things such as form and the rest — [teaching] that issues forth even from trees, musical instruments, and the like. The rest has its meaning already explained.

body.text: deśanāsaṃpatau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the excellence of teaching:

children.translated_text: Clear, doubt-removing, acceptable, truth-showing, and twofold —
this excellent teaching of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be known. || Msa_12.5 ||

body.text: ayaṃ catuṣkārthanirdeśena ślokaḥ | yaduktaṃ brahmaparipṛcchāyāṃ | catrubhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahādharmadānaṃ vitaranti saddharmaparigrahaṇatayā ātmanaḥ prajñottāpanatayā satpurūṣakarmakaraṇatayā saṃkleśavyavadānasaṃdeśanatayā ca | ekena hi bāhuśrutyādviṣadā deśanā bhavati | dvitīyena mahāprājñatvāt | saṃśayajahā pareṣāṃ saṃśayacchedāt |
body.translated_text: This is a verse explaining the meaning of the fourfold [quality]. As stated in the <s>Brahmaparipṛcchā</s>: '<s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four dharmas bestow the great gift of Dharma — through embracing the true Dharma, through sharpening their own wisdom, through performing the deeds of good persons, and through demonstrating defilement and purification.' For by the first, the teaching is clear, due to great learning. By the second, [there is] great wisdom — and it removes the doubts of others, through cutting their doubts.

body.text: tṛtīyenānavadyakarmattvādādeyā | caturthena tattvadarśikā dvividhā saṃkleśalakṣaṇasya ca tattvasya vyavadānalakṣaṇasya ca dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ satyābhyām |
body.translated_text: By the third, it is acceptable, due to blameless conduct. By the fourth, it shows truth in two ways — the truth of the characteristic of defilement and the truth of the characteristic of purification, through two and two truths respectively.

children.text: madhurā madavyapetā na ca khinnā deśanāgrasattvānāṃ |
children.translated_text: Sweet, free from intoxication, unwearied — the teaching of the supreme beings;
clear, variegated, well-reasoned, accessible, free from material gain, and all-pervading. || Msa_12.6 ||

body.text: asmindvitīye śloke madhurā pareṇākṣiptasyāparūṣavacanāt | madavyapetā stutau siddhau vā madānanugamanāt | akhinnā akilāsikatvāt | sphuṭā nirācāryamuṣṭitvāt kṛtsnadeśanataḥ | citrā apunaruktatvāt | yuktā pramāṇāviruddhatvāt | gamikāpratītapadavyañjanatvāt | nirāmiṣā prasannādhikārānadhi[rthi]katvāt | sarvatragā yānatrayagatatvāt |
body.translated_text: In this second verse: 'sweet' — because of gentle speech when challenged by others. 'Free from intoxication' — because of not succumbing to intoxication when praised or successful. 'Unwearied' — because of being indefatigable. 'Clear' — because of having no teacher's closed fist, teaching everything completely. 'Variegated' — because of non-repetition. 'Well-reasoned' — because of being non-contradictory with the means of valid knowledge. 'Accessible' — because of having well-known words and syllables. 'Free from material gain' — because of not being motivated by gain, honor, or glory. 'All-pervading' — because of pertaining to all three vehicles.

body.text: vāksaṃpattau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the excellence of speech:

children.text: adīnā madhurā sūktā pratītā viṣadā tathā [vāgjinātmaje] |
children.translated_text: Undepressed, sweet, well-spoken, intelligible, clear —
appropriate, free from material gain, measured, and lucid
— [such is the speech] of the son of the <s>Jina</s>. || Msa_12.7 ||

body.text: adīnā paurī parṣatpūraṇāt | madhurā valguḥ | sūktā vispaṣṭā sunirūktākṣaratvāt | pratītā vijñeyā pratītābhidhānatvāt | yathārhā śravaṇīyā vineyānurūpatvāt | anāmiṣā aniḥśrita[tā]lābhasatkārāloke[raśloke] | pratatā[pramitā] apratikūlā parimitāyāmakhedāt | viṣadā aparyāttā |
body.translated_text: 'Undepressed' — urbane, because of filling the assembly. 'Sweet' — melodious. 'Well-spoken' — distinct, because of clearly articulated syllables. 'Intelligible' — comprehensible, because of using well-known expressions. 'Appropriate' — worth hearing, because of being suited to those to be trained. 'Free from material gain' — independent of gain, honor, and fame. 'Measured' — agreeable, because of not being tiresome due to limited length. 'Lucid' — unimpeded.

body.text: vyañjanasaṃpattau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the excellence of phrasing:

children.translated_text: Through synopsis, through exposition, through conformity with the vehicles, through refinement,
through intelligibility, through appropriateness, through leading to liberation, and through conduciveness. || Msa_12.8 ||

body.text: yuktaiḥ padavyañjanairūddeśātpramāṇāvirodhena | sahitairnirdeśāduddeśāvirodhena | yānānulomanādānulomikairyānatrayāvirodhena | ślākṣṇyāda[dā]nucchavikairakaṣṭaśabdatayā | prātītyādaupayikaiḥ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: MSA_Bagchi 78]

children.text: ) pratītārthatayā cārthopagamanāt | yāthārhātpratirūpairvineyānurūpatayā | nairyāṇyātpradakṣiṇairnirvāṇādhikāratayā | ānukūlyānnipakasyāṅgasaṃbhāraiḥ śaikṣasyāryāṣṭāṅgamārgānukūlyāt |
children.translated_text: Through intelligibility — with appropriate [expressions], because of leading to the comprehension of meaning through clear meaning. Through appropriateness — with fitting [expressions], by being suited to those to be trained. Through leading to liberation — with auspicious [expressions], because of being directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Through conduciveness — with the limbs of a prudent one's assemblage, because of conformity with the noble eightfold path of a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>).

body.translated_text: With well-arranged words and syllables — through synopsis, by non-contradiction with valid knowledge. With coherent [phrasing] — through exposition, by non-contradiction with the synopsis. Through conformity with the vehicles — with conforming [expressions], by non-contradiction with the three vehicles. Through refinement — with smooth [expressions], by the absence of harsh words.

children.translated_text: This excellence of phrasing of the supreme beings should be understood in all respects;
it is sixty-limbed and inconceivable — the voice of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) is indeed infinite. || Msa_12.9 ||

body.text: ṣaṣṭyaṅgī sācintyā yā guhyakādhipatinirdeśe buddhasya ṣaṣṭyākārā vāg nirdiṣṭā | punaraparaṃ śāntamate tathāgatasya ṣaṣṭyākāropetā vāg niścarati snigdhā ca mṛdukā ca manojñā ca manoramā ca śuddhā ceti vistaraḥ | tatra snigdhā sattvādhātukuśalamūlopastambhikatvāt | mṛdukā dṛṣṭa eva dharme sukhasaṃsparśatvāt | manojñā svarthatvāt | manoramā suvyañjanatvāt | śuddhā nirūttaralokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhatvāt | vimalā sarvakleśānuśayavāsanāvisaṃyuktatvāt | prabhāsvarā pratītapadavyañjanatvāt | valguḥ sarvatīrthyakumatidṛṣṭividhātabalaguṇayuktatvāt | śravaṇīyā pratipattinairyāṇikatvāt | anantā[anelā] sarvaparapravādibhiranāchedyatvāt | kalā rañjikatvāt | vinītā rāgādipratipakṣatvāt | akarkaśā śikṣāprajñaptisukhopāyatvāt | aparūṣā tadvyatikramasaṃpanniḥsaraṇopadeśakatvāt | suvinītā yānatrayanayopadeśikatvāt | karṇasukhā vikṣepapratipakṣatvāt | kāyaprahṇādanakarī samādhyābāhakatvāt | cittaudvilyakarī vipaśyanāprāmodyāvāhaphalakatvāt | hṛdayasaṃtuṣṭikarī saṃśayacchedikatvāt | prītisukhasaṃjananī mithyāniścayāpakarṣikatvāt | niḥparidāhā pratipattāvavipratisāratvāt | ājñeyā saṃpannaśrutamayajñānāśrayatvāt | vijñeyā saṃpannacintāmayajñānāśrayatvāt | viṣpaṣṭā anācāryamuṣṭidharmavihitatvāt | premaṇīyānuprāptasvakārthānāṃ premakaratvāt | abhinandanīyānanuprāptasvakārthānāṃ spṛhaṇīyatvāt | ājñāpanīyā acintyadharmasamyagdarśikatvāt | vijñāpanīyā cintyadharmasamyagdeśikatvāt | yuktā pramāṇāvirūddhatvāt | sahitā yathārhavineyadeśikatvāt | punarūktadoṣajahā avandhyatvāt | siṃhasvaravegā sarvatīrthyasaṃtrāsakatvāt | nāgasvaraśabdā udāratvāt | meghasvaraghoṣā gambhīratvāt | nāgendrarutā ādeyatvāt | kinnarasaṃgītighoṣā madhuratvāt | kalaviṅkasvararūtaravitābhī[tī]kṣṇabhaṅguratvāt | brahmasvararutaravitā dūraṃgamatvāt | jīvaṃjīvakasvararutaravitā sarvasiddhipūrvaṃgamamaṅgalatvāt | devendramadhuranirghoṣā anatikramaṇīyatvāt | dundubhisvarā sarvamārapratyarthikavijayapūrvaṃgamatvāt | anunnatā stutyasaṃkliṣṭatvāt | anavanatā nindāsaṃkliṣṭatvāt | sarvaśabdānupraviṣṭā sarvavyākaraṇasarvākāralakṣaṇānupraviṣṭatvāt | apaśabdavigatā smṛtisaṃpramoṣe tadaniścaraṇatvāt | avikalā vineyakṛtyasarvakālapratyupasthitatvāt | alīnā lābhasatkārāniśritatvāt | adīnā sāvadyāpagatvāt | pramuditā akheditvāt | prasṛtā sarvavidyāsthānakauśalyānugatatvāt | akhilā[sakhilā] sattvānāṃ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: MSA_Bagchi 79]

children.text: ) tatsakalārthasaṃpādakatvāt | saritā prabandhānupacchinnatvāt | lalitā vicitrākārapratyupasthānatvāt | sarvasvarapūraṇī ekasvaranaikaśabdavijñaptipratyupasthāpanatvāt | sarvasattvendriyasaṃtoṣaṇī ekānekārthavijñaptipratyupasthānatvāt | aninditā yathāpratijñatvāt | acañcalā āgamitakālaprayuktatvāt | acapalā atvaramāṇavihitatvāt | sarvaparṣadanuravitā durāntikaparṣattulyaśravaṇatvāt | sarvākāravaropetā sarvalaukikārthadṛṣṭāntadharmapariṇāmikatvāt |
children.translated_text: because of accomplishing the complete welfare of beings. 'Continuous' — because of uninterrupted continuity. 'Graceful' — because of presenting manifold forms. 'Filling all sounds' — because of establishing the cognition of many words through a single sound. 'Satisfying the faculties of all beings' — because of establishing the cognition of one and many meanings. 'Blameless' — because of [acting] in accordance with one's promises. 'Unshaken' — because of being delivered in accordance with the time stated. 'Unhurried' — because of being delivered without haste. 'Resounding in all assemblies' — because of being heard equally by those near and far in the assembly. 'Endowed with the excellence of all forms' — because of transforming all worldly objects and analogies into the Dharma.

body.translated_text: It is sixty-limbed and inconceivable — as in the exposition of the <s>Guhyakādhipati</s> (Lord of Secret Beings), where the sixty aspects of the <s>Buddha</s>'s speech are described. And furthermore, in the <s>Śāntamati</s> [Sūtra]: 'The speech of the <s>Tathāgata</s> issues forth endowed with sixty aspects — smooth, soft, pleasing, delightful, pure,' and so on in detail. Therein: 'smooth' — because it nurtures the wholesome roots of beings in [various] realms. 'Soft' — because it gives pleasurable contact in this very life. 'Pleasing' — because it conveys one's own meaning well. 'Delightful' — because of excellent phrasing. 'Pure' — because it is obtained as the afterglow of the unsurpassed supramundane [wisdom]. 'Stainless' — because it is free from the latent impressions of all affliction-tendencies. 'Radiant' — because of having well-known words and syllables. 'Melodious' — because it possesses the power of qualities that destroy the views of wrong doctrines of all non-Buddhist teachers. 'Worth hearing' — because its practice leads to liberation. 'Inviolable' — because it cannot be refuted by any opponents. 'Resonant' — because it gives delight. 'Disciplined' — because it is the antidote to passion and the rest. 'Not harsh' — because its skillful means of precept-instruction are pleasant. 'Not rough' — because it instructs in the escape from the fall of transgressing those [precepts]. 'Well-disciplined' — because it instructs in the methods of the three vehicles. 'Pleasing to the ear' — because it is the antidote to distraction. 'Producing bodily ease' — because it invites <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). 'Producing mental elation' — because it brings the fruit of joy through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). 'Producing satisfaction of the heart' — because it cuts doubt. 'Generating joy and happiness' — because it removes wrong certainty. 'Without burning' — because of non-regret in practice. 'To be known' — because it is the basis of accomplished knowledge born of hearing. 'To be understood' — because it is the basis of accomplished knowledge born of reflection. 'Distinct' — because it is delivered without a teacher's closed fist regarding the Dharma. 'Endearing' — because it produces affection in those who have attained their own purpose. 'To be rejoiced in' — because it produces longing in those who have not yet attained their own purpose. 'Producing comprehension' — because it shows the inconceivable dharmas correctly. 'Producing understanding' — because it teaches the conceivable dharmas correctly. 'Well-reasoned' — because of non-contradiction with valid knowledge. 'Coherent' — because it teaches appropriately to those to be trained. 'Free from the fault of repetition' — because of being never in vain. 'With the force of a lion's roar' — because it terrifies all non-Buddhist teachers. 'With the sound of an elephant' — because of being majestic. 'With the rumble of a cloud' — because of being profound. 'With the cry of the king of serpents' — because of being authoritative. 'With the song of <s>Kinnaras</s>' — because of being sweet. 'With the call of a cuckoo (<s>kalaviṅka</s>)' — because of being keen and tremulous. 'With the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>' — because of reaching far. 'With the call of a <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> bird' — because of being the auspicious forerunner of all accomplishments. 'With the sweet sound of <s>Indra</s>' — because of being not to be transgressed. 'With the sound of a drum' — because of being the forerunner of victory over all <s>Māra</s>-adversaries. 'Without exaltation' — because of being undefiled by praise. 'Without depression' — because of being undefiled by blame. 'Penetrating all sounds' — because of entering into all grammatical forms and all modal characteristics. 'Free from incorrect speech' — because of not issuing from those who have lost mindfulness. 'Complete' — because of being present at all times for the duties of those to be trained. 'Unshrunken' — because of being independent of gain and honor. 'Undepressed' — because of being free from the blameworthy. 'Joyful' — because of being unwearied. 'Flowing' — because it follows expertise in all fields of knowledge. 'Comprehensive' —

body.text: deśanāmāhātmye catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the greatness of teaching:

children.translated_text: With speech and well-arranged phrases, through synopsis, analysis, and the cutting of doubt,
following expansion — [teaching] to those of sudden understanding and those of detailed understanding. || Msa_12.10 ||

body.text: ākhyāti vācā | prajñāpayati padaiḥ suyuktaiḥ | prasthāpayati vibhājayati vivṛṇoti yathākramamuddeśavibhāgasaṃśayacchedaiḥ | uttānīkaroti uttānīkaraṇaṃ bahulīkārānugatā deśanā niścayabalādhānārthaṃ | deśayatyuddhaṭitajñeṣu | saṃprakāśayati vipañcitajñeṣu |
body.translated_text: He declares — through speech. He designates — through well-arranged phrases. He sets forth, analyzes, and elucidates — through synopsis, analysis, and the cutting of doubt, respectively. He makes clear — and the teaching that follows expansion is for the purpose of establishing the power of certainty. He teaches — to those of sudden understanding. He fully illuminates — to those of detailed understanding.

children.text: śuddhā trimaṇḍalena hiteyaṃ deśanā hi buddhānāṃ |
children.translated_text: Pure through the three spheres, this teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> is indeed beneficial;
but it should be known as free from eight faults. || Msa_12.11 ||

body.text: śuddhā trimaṇḍaleneti | yena ca deśayati vācā padaiśca | yathā coddeśādiprakāraiḥ | yeṣu coddhaṭitavipañcitajñeṣu | eṣaiva ca deśanā punaraṣṭadoṣavivarjitā veditavyā yathākramam |
body.translated_text: 'Pure through the three spheres' — by what one teaches: speech and phrases; how one teaches: through the modes of synopsis and so forth; and to whom: to those of sudden and detailed understanding. And this same teaching should be known as free from eight faults, in order.

children.translated_text: Laziness, incomprehension, not providing opportunity, impreciseness,
failure to cut doubt, and failure to firmly establish its removal. || Msa_12.12 ||

body.text: te punaraṣṭau doṣāḥ | kauśīdyamanavasaṃbodhaḥ avakāśasyākaraṇaṃ anītārthatvaṃ saṃdehasyācchedanā tadvigamasyādṛḍhīkaraṇaṃ niścayaśyetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: These eight faults are: laziness, incomprehension, not providing opportunity, impreciseness of meaning, failure to cut doubt, and failure to firmly establish the removal of that [doubt] — meaning failure to establish certainty.

children.text: khedo 'tha matsaritvaṃ doṣā hyete matā kathāyāṃ hi |
children.translated_text: Weariness, and stinginess — these are considered faults in discourse;
in their absence, the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> becomes unsurpassed. || Msa_12.13 ||

body.text: khedo yenābhīkṣṇaṃ na deśayet | matsaritvaṃ [matsaritvaṃ] cākṛtsnaprakāśanāt | arthasaṃpattau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Weariness — on account of which one does not teach frequently. And stinginess — due to not revealing everything fully. Two verses on the excellence of meaning:

children.translated_text: This Dharma is excellent, being the cause of devotion, satisfaction, and understanding,
having twofold meaning, easily grasped, and declaring the holy life endowed with four qualities. || Msa_12.14 ||
Not shared with others, solely complete in destroying the afflictions of the three realms,
pure by nature and [also] pure from [the removal of] stains — this holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is deemed to have four qualities. || Msa_12.15 ||

body.text: caturguṇabrahmacaryasaṃprakāśako dharmaḥ | ādimadhyaparyavasānakalyāṇo yathākramaṃ śrutacintābhāvanābhirbhaktituṣṭibuddhihetutvāt | tatra bhaktiradhimuktiḥ saṃpratyayaḥ tuṣṭiḥ prāmodyaṃ (

children.translated_text: [page reference: MSA_Bagchi 80]

children.text: ) yuktinidhyānācchakyaprāptitāṃ viditvā | buddhiḥ samāhitacittasya yathābhūtajñānaṃ | dvividhārtha ityataḥ svarthaḥ saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyayogāt | sugrāhya ityataḥ suvyañjanaḥ pratītapadavyañjanatvāt | caturguṇaṃ brahmacaryam | kevalaṃ paraisādhāraṇātvāt paripūrṇaṃ tridhātukleśaprahāṇaparipūraṇāt | pariśuddhaṃ svabhāvaviśuddhito 'nāsravatvāt | paryavadātaṃ malaviśuddhitaḥ saṃtānaviśuddhyā kṣīṇāsravāṇām |
children.translated_text: from knowing, through reasoning and contemplation, the attainability [of the goal]. Understanding is the knowledge of things as they truly are, of one whose mind is concentrated. 'Having twofold meaning' — therefore meaningful in itself, through the connection with conventional and ultimate truth. 'Easily grasped' — therefore well-phrased, because of having well-known words and syllables. The holy life endowed with four qualities: sole — because of not being shared with others. Complete — because of fulfilling the abandonment of the afflictions of the three realms. Completely pure — pure by nature, because of being undefiled. Thoroughly pure — pure from [the removal of] stains, through the purification of the continuum of those whose outflows are exhausted.

body.translated_text: The Dharma that illuminates the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) endowed with four qualities: excellent at the beginning, middle, and end — because of being the cause of devotion, satisfaction, and understanding, respectively, through hearing, reflection, and meditation. Therein, devotion is aspiration — conviction. Satisfaction is joy —

body.text: abhisaṃdhivibhāge ślokadvayam |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of hidden intention (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>):

children.translated_text: The hidden intention of introduction, and another hidden intention regarding characteristics,
the hidden intention of antidote, and the hidden intention regarding transformation. || Msa_12.16 ||
Regarding <s>Śrāvakas</s>, regarding the [three] natures, regarding the discipline of faults, and likewise
regarding the profundity of expression — this fourfold hidden intention. || Msa_12.17 ||

body.text: caturvidho 'bhisaṃdhirdeśanāyāṃ buddhasya veditavyaḥ | avatāraṇābhisaṃdhirlakṣaṇābhisaṃdhiḥ pratipakṣābhisaṃdhiḥ pariṇāmanābhisaṃdhiśca | tatrāvatāraṇābhisaṃdhiḥ śrāvakeṣu draṣṭavyaḥ | śāsanāvatāraṇārthamanutrāsāya rūpādyastitvadeśanāt | lakṣaṇābhisaṃdhistriṣu parikalpitādisvabhāveṣu draṣṭavyo niḥsvabhāvānutpannādisarvadharmadeśanāt | pratipakṣābhisaṃdhirdoṣāṇāṃ vinaye draṣṭavyo yathāṣṭāvaraṇapratipakṣāgrayānasaṃbhāṣāsānuśaṃse[saṃ] gāthādvayaṃ vakṣyati | pariṇāmanābhisaṃdhirabhidhānagāmbhīrye draṣṭavyo yathāha |
body.translated_text: The fourfold hidden intention (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching should be understood: the hidden intention of introduction, the hidden intention of characteristics, the hidden intention of antidote, and the hidden intention of transformation. Therein, the hidden intention of introduction should be seen regarding <s>Śrāvakas</s> — from the teaching that form and the rest exist, in order not to frighten [them], for the purpose of introducing [them] into the teaching. The hidden intention of characteristics should be seen regarding the three natures beginning with the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) — from the teaching that all dharmas have no self-nature, are unborn, and so forth. The hidden intention of antidote should be seen regarding the discipline of faults — as will be stated in two verses concerning the praises of the foremost vehicle as the antidote to the eight obscurations. The hidden intention of transformation should be seen regarding the profundity of expression — as stated:

body.text: asāre sāramatayo viparyāse ca susthitāḥ |

children.text: kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭā labhante bodhimuttamāṃ || Msa_12.iti |
children.translated_text: and who are thoroughly afflicted by afflictions — they attain supreme awakening. || thus in Msa_12 ||

body.translated_text: Those whose minds find essence in what is without essence, and who are well established in error,

body.text: ayamatrābhisaṃdhiḥ | asāre sāramataya ityavikṣepe yeṣāṃ sārabuddhiḥ pradhānabuddhirvikṣepo hi visāraścetasaḥ | viparyāse ca susthitā iti nityasukhaśucyātmagrāhaviparyayeṇānityādike viparyāse susthitā aparihāṇitaḥ | kleśena ca sa saṃkliṣṭā iti dīrghaduṣkaravyāyāmaśrameṇātyarthaṃ parikliṣṭāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the hidden intention here. 'Those whose minds find essence in what is without essence' — in non-distraction, those for whom the essential thought, the primary thought, [is non-distraction], for distraction is the dispersal of the mind. 'Well established in error' — through the reversal of grasping at permanence, happiness, purity, and self, they are well established in error [i.e., in what the world calls error] regarding impermanence and the rest, from the standpoint of non-deterioration. 'Thoroughly afflicted by afflictions' — they are greatly afflicted by the fatigue of long and difficult exertion.

body.text: abhiprāyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of intention (<s>abhiprāya</s>):

children.translated_text: To be understood in the sense of equality, in the sense of another [meaning],
and the fourfold intention regarding the disposition of the person. || Msa_12.18 ||

body.text: caturvidho 'bhiprāyaḥ | sata[ma]tābhiprāyo yadāha | ahameva sa tasminsamaye vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūvamityaviśiṣṭadharmakāyatvāt | arthāntarābhiprāyo yadāha | niḥ svabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā anutpannāityevamādi ayathārūtārthatvāt | kālantarābhiprāyo yadāha | ye (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 81

children.text: ) sukhāvatyāṃ praṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti te tatropapatsyanta iti kālāntareṇetyabhiprāyaḥ | pudgalāśayābhiprāyo yattadeva kuśalamūlaṃ kasyacitpraśaṃsate kasyacidvigarhate 'lpamātrasaṃtuṣṭasya vaipulyasaṃgrahāt mahāyānasūtrāntasānuśaṃsaṃ gāthādvayamupādāyāha |
children.translated_text: ) will make aspiration [to be reborn] in <s>Sukhāvatī</s> will be reborn there' — the intention being 'at another time.' The intention regarding the disposition of the person (<s>pudgalāśayābhiprāya</s>) — when [the <s>Buddha</s>] praises that very same root of merit for one person and criticizes it for another, who is content with merely a little — to draw [the latter] toward the comprehensive collection [of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>]. He states two verses showing the benefits of [retaining] <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras:

body.translated_text: The intention is fourfold: the intention of equality (<s>samatābhiprāya</s>) — when [the <s>Buddha</s>] says: 'I myself at that time was <s>Vipaśvī</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One' — because of the non-differentiation of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. The intention of another meaning (<s>arthāntarābhiprāya</s>) — when he says: 'All dharmas are without self-nature, unborn' and so forth — because the meaning is not as literally stated. The intention of another time (<s>kālāntarābhiprāya</s>) — when he says: 'Those who (

children.translated_text: Disrespect toward the <s>Buddha</s> and the Dharma, laziness, contentment with merely a little,

children.text: rāge māne caritaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ cāniyatabhedaḥ || Msa_12.19 ||
children.translated_text: conduct in passion, in pride, remorse, and the division of the undetermined — || Msa_12.19 ||
these are the obscurations of beings; the antidote is the teaching of the supreme vehicle;
from that, the abandonment of all faults of obstruction occurs for them. || Msa_12.20 ||
Whoever applies oneself to the retention of the two verses, whether by letter or by meaning,

children.text: sa hi daśavidhamanuśaṃsaṃ labhate sattvottamo dhīmān || Msa_12.21 ||
children.translated_text: that supreme being, endowed with wisdom, obtains tenfold benefit. || Msa_12.21 ||

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ ca dhātupuṣṭiṃ prāmodyaṃ cottamaṃ maraṇakāle |
children.translated_text: Complete nourishment of the element (<s>dhātu</s>), and supreme joy at the time of death,

children.text: janma ca yathābhikāmaṃ jātismaratāṃ ca sarvatra || Msa_12.22 ||
children.translated_text: birth as desired, and the recollection of past lives everywhere; || Msa_12.22 ||
meeting with <s>Buddhas</s>, hearing from them the supreme vehicle,

children.text: adhimuktiṃ saha buddhyā dvayamukhatāmāśubodhiṃ ca || Msa_12.23 ||
children.translated_text: conviction together with understanding, access to two gateways, and swift awakening. || Msa_12.23 ||

body.text: buddhe dharme 'vajñeti pañca gāthāḥ | tatrāniyatabhedo bodhisattvānāmaniyatānāṃ mahāyānādbhedaḥ | agrayānasaṃbhāṣā yā mahāyānadeśanā | buddhe 'vajñāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | ahameva sa tena kālena vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūvamiti | dharme 'vajñāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | iyato gaṃgānadīvālikāsamānabuddhānparyupāsya mahāyāne 'vabodha utpadyata iti | kauśīdyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | ye sukhāvatyāṃ praṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti te tatropapatsyanta iti | vimalacandraprabhasya ca tathāgatasya nāmadheyagrahaṇamātreṇa niyato bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti | alpamātrasaṃtuṣṭyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān kvaciddānādi vivarṇayati anyatra varṇitavān | rāgacaritasya cāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān buddhakṣetravibhūtiṃ varṇayati | mānacaritasyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān kasyacid buddhasyādhikāṃ saṃpattiṃ varṇayati | kaukṛtyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | ye buddhabodhisattveṣva[ṣvapa]kāraṃ kariṣyanti te sarve svargopagā bhaviṣyantīti | aniyatabhedasyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ buddhatve vyākaraṇadeśanā ekayānadeśanā ca | kṛtsnadhātupuṣṭiḥ sarvamahāyānādhiṣṭhānāya dhātupuṣṭistadāvaraṇavigamāt sarvatra mahāyāne 'dhimuktilābhataḥ | dvayamukhatā samādhimukhatā dhāraṇīmukhatā ca | dṛṣṭe dharme dvividho 'nuśaṃsaḥ sāṃparāyike 'ṣṭavidhaḥ krameṇottarottaraviśeṣalābhādveditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The five verses beginning with 'disrespect toward the <s>Buddha</s> and the Dharma': therein, the division of the undetermined (<s>aniyatabheda</s>) is the separation of undetermined <s>bodhisattvas</s> from the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The teaching of the supreme vehicle is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching. The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of disrespect toward the <s>Buddha</s>: 'I myself at that time was <s>Vipaśvī</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.' The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of disrespect toward the Dharma: 'Having attended upon <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, awakening in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> arises.' The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of laziness: 'Those who will make aspiration [to be reborn] in <s>Sukhāvatī</s> will be reborn there;' and 'By merely taking up the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalacandraprabha</s>, one becomes determined for unsurpassed perfect awakening.' The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of contentment with merely a little: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> disparages giving and the like in one place and praises them elsewhere. The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of conduct in passion: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> describes the splendors of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of conduct in pride: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> describes the greater wealth of some [other] <s>Buddha</s>. The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of remorse: 'Those who will harm <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> will all become heaven-bound.' The antidote-teaching for the obscuration of the division of the undetermined: the teaching of the prediction of Buddhahood for the great <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), and the teaching of the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>). Complete nourishment of the element means the nourishment of the element for the support of the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through the removal of those obscurations and the attainment of conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in all respects. Access to two gateways means the gateway of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the gateway of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention). The benefit in the present life is twofold; in the next life it is eightfold — to be understood as the successive attainment of progressively superior distinctions.

body.text: deśanānuśaṃseślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the benefit of teaching:

children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is easy-going, tireless, compassionate, of widespread renown, and endowed with knowledge of proper method,

children.text: bhavati sukathiko hi bodhisattvastapati jane kathitairyathaiva sūryaḥ || Msa_12.24 ||
children.translated_text: becomes a skilled teacher, and blazes among beings like the sun with teachings. || Msa_12.24 ||

body.text: pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sukathikatvaṃ | sūryavatpratapanaṃ cānuśaṃsaḥ | lokāvarjanato bahumatatvāt | pañca kāraṇāni sukathikatvasya yenāviparītaṃ darśayati abhīkṣṇaṃ nirāmiṣacitta ādeyavākyavineyānurūpaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Skilled teacherhood is due to five causes; and blazing like the sun is the benefit — because of winning over the world and being highly esteemed. The five causes of skilled teacherhood are: showing without error, frequently, with a selfless mind, with acceptable speech, and in a manner appropriate to those being trained.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre deśanādhikāro dvādaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the twelfth chapter on teaching (<s>deśanādhikāra</s>) ||

body.text: trayodaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Thirteenth chapter:

body.text: pratipattivibhāge ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the division of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>):

children.translated_text: Having understood the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of person and phenomena, the wise one
should avoid the false and the correct regarding duality, through the threefold [concentrations]. || Msa_13.1 ||

body.text: yathārthamājñāya dharmamājñāya dharmānudharmapratipanno bhavati sāmīcīpratipanno 'nudharmacārī tatsaṃdarśayati | tatra dvidhā pudgaladharma nairātmyajñānaṃ grāhyagrāhakābhāvataḥ | dvayamithyātvasamyakttvaṃ vivarjyaṃ trayaṃ | abhāve ca śūnyatāsamādhiḥ parikalpitasya svabhāvasya | bhāve cāpraṇīhitānimittau paratantraniṣpannayoḥ svabhāvayoḥ | etatsamādhitrayaṃ laukikaṃ na mithyātvaṃ lokottarajñānāvāhanāt | na samyaktvamalokottaratvāt |
body.translated_text: Having understood the meaning correctly, having understood the Dharma, one becomes one who practices in conformity with the Dharma, one who practices properly, one who conducts oneself in accordance with the Dharma — this he shows. Therein, the twofold knowledge of the selflessness of person and phenomena is through the absence of the grasped and the grasper. The threefold [concentrations] by which the false and the correct regarding duality are to be avoided: in the non-existence [of the imagined nature], the <s>śūnyatā-samādhi</s> (concentration on emptiness) regarding the imagined self-nature; in the existence [of the dependent and perfected natures], the <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishless) and <s>ānimitta</s> (signless) [concentrations] regarding the self-natures of the dependent and perfected. This threefold <s>samādhi</s> is mundane — it is not false because it leads to supramundane knowledge; it is not correct because it is not supramundane.

children.translated_text: The knower of meaning knows the kernel-like nature of all dharmas;
for the abandonment of contentment with mere hearing, one is therefore called a knower of Dharma. || Msa_13.2 ||

body.text: evamarthajñaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sūtrādīnāṃ kolopamatāṃ jānāti | śrutamātrasaṃtuṣṭiprahāṇāya tena dharmajño bhavati |
body.translated_text: Thus the knower of meaning knows the kernel-like nature of all dharmas such as sūtras and the rest. For the abandonment of contentment with mere hearing, one thereby becomes a knower of Dharma.

children.translated_text: Having penetrated duality with worldly knowledge,
one practices in conformity with the Dharma for the perfection of that knowledge. || Msa_13.3 ||

body.text: etena dvividhena pārthagjanenārthadharmajñānena dvayaṃ nairātmyabhāvaṃ pratividhya yathākramaṃ [nairātmyaṃ tathā pratividhya yathoktaṃ] tasya jñānasya pariniṣpattyarthaṃ pratipadyate | evamanudharmaṃ pratipadyate |
body.translated_text: Having penetrated duality — the existence of selflessness — with this twofold worldly knowledge of meaning and Dharma, in proper order [having penetrated selflessness as stated], one practices for the purpose of the perfection of that knowledge. Thus one practices in conformity with the Dharma.

children.translated_text: Then one obtains supramundane, unsurpassed knowledge,
on the first stage, equal with all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of that nature. || Msa_13.4 ||

body.text: tato jñānaṃ sa labhate lokottaramanuttaramiti | viśiṣṭatarayānābhāvāt | ādibhūmau pramuditāyāṃ bhūmau samaṃ sarvairbodhisattvaistadātmabhiriti tadbhūmikairevaṃ sāmīcīpratipanno bhavati tadbhūmikabodhisattvasamatayā |
body.translated_text: 'Then one obtains supramundane, unsurpassed knowledge' — because there is no higher vehicle. On the first stage, the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage, 'equal with all <s>bodhisattvas</s> of that nature' means those of that very stage — thus one becomes one who practices properly, through equality with the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of that stage.

children.translated_text: Having accomplished the complete destruction of the afflictions to be abandoned through seeing and knowing,
one applies oneself to cultivation for the abandonment of the obscuration of the knowable. || Msa_13.5 ||

body.text: śloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The verse has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Through knowledge conjoined with the conceptualization of establishment [in stages],
one thus conducts oneself in conformity with the Dharma on the remaining stages. || Msa_13.6 ||

body.text: śeṣeṇānudharmacāritvaṃ darśayati | vyavasthānāvikalpeneti bhūmivyavasthānajñānenāvikalpena ca | sahacāriṇetyanusaṃbaddhacāriṇā anyonyanairantaryeṇa | etena ślokadvayenānudharmacāritvaṃ darśitaṃ |
body.translated_text: With the remaining [verse], he shows the conduct in conformity with the Dharma: 'through the conceptualization of establishment' means through the knowledge of establishment in the stages, and non-conceptual [knowledge]; 'conjoined' means progressing in an uninterrupted manner, one with the other. By these two verses, the conduct in conformity with the Dharma has been shown.

body.text: pratipattāvapramādakriyāyāṃ catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the action of diligence (<s>apramāda</s>) in practice:

children.translated_text: Easily obtainable [requisites], self-established, with good terrain, with good companions,

children.text: suyogo guṇavān deśo yatra dhīmān prapadyate || Msa_13.7 ||
children.translated_text: with good practice, a place endowed with qualities — where the wise one practices. || Msa_13.7 ||

body.text: caturbhiścakrairapramādakriyāṃ darśayati pratirūpadeśavāsādibhiḥ | tatrānena ślokena pratirūpadeśavāsaṃ darśayati | sulābhaścīvarapiṇḍapātādīnāṃ jīvitapariṣkārāṇāmakṛcchreṇa lābhāt | svadhiṣṭhāno durjanairdasyuprabhṛtibhiranadhiṣṭhitatvāt | subhūmirārogyabhūmitvāt | susahāyakaḥ sabhāgaśīladṛṣṭisahāyakatvāt | suyogo divālpākīrṇābhilāpakatvāt rātrau cālpaśabdādikatvāt |
body.translated_text: He shows the action of diligence through four wheels, beginning with dwelling in a suitable place. With this verse, he shows dwelling in a suitable place: easily obtainable — because of the effortless obtaining of requisites of life such as robes and alms-food; self-established — because of not being occupied by wicked persons such as bandits; with good terrain — because of being a region conducive to health; with good companions — because of having companions of similar moral conduct and views; with good practice — because of having few crowds and conversations during the day, and little noise and the like at night.

children.translated_text: Learned, one who has seen the truth, eloquent, compassionate,

children.text: akhinno bodhisattvaśca jñeyaḥ satpurūṣo mahān || Msa_13.8 ||
children.translated_text: and untiring — such a <s>bodhisattva</s> should be known as a great good person. || Msa_13.8 ||

body.text: anena dvitīyena satpurūṣaṃ darśayati | āgamādhigamavākkaraṇanirāmiṣacittākilāsitvaguṇayogāt |
body.translated_text: By this second [verse], he shows the good person — through the qualities of scriptural learning (<s>āgama</s>), realization (<s>adhigama</s>), skill in speech, selfless mind, and tirelessness.

children.translated_text: [Having] one's own object-support, well-accumulated [provisions], proper cultivation itself, as taught,
and with proper application of the means of liberation — this is the proper self-endeavor. || Msa_13.9 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena yoniśomanaskārasaṃgṛhītamātmanaḥ samyakpraṇīdhānatāṃ darśayati | saddharmālambanatayā susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāratayā śamathādinimittānāṃ kālena kālaṃ bhāvanātayā alpamātrāsaṃtuṣṭitayā satyuttarakaraṇīye sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogatayā ca |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows one's own proper endeavor, which is comprised of proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>): through having the true Dharma as the object-support; through having well-accumulated accumulations; through the timely cultivation of the signs of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and the rest; through non-contentment with merely a little; and through continuous and earnest application when there is more that needs to be done.

children.translated_text: The cause of delight, of obtaining the [right] moment, and also of health,
of <s>samādhi</s>, and of investigation — is indeed the making of merit in the past. || Msa_13.10 ||

body.text: anena caturthena pūrvakṛtapuṇyatāṃ pañcavidhena hetutvena darśayati | ratihetutvena yataḥ pratirūpadeśavāse 'bhiramate | kṣaṇopapattihetutvena yataḥ satpurūṣāyāśrayaṃ labhate | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 85

children.text: ) ārogyasamādhiprajñāhetutvena ca yata ātmanaḥ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ sampadyate |
children.translated_text: ) and as the cause of health, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom — because one's own proper endeavor is accomplished.

body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the making of merit in the past through its fivefold causality: as the cause of delight — because one delights in dwelling in a suitable place; as the cause of obtaining the [right] moment — because one obtains the support of a good person; (

body.text: kleśata eva kleśaniḥsaraṇe ślokāstrayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the escape from afflictions through the afflictions themselves:

children.translated_text: Since no dharma exists that is released from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality),
therefore passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest are regarded by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the escape from those [afflictions]. || Msa_13.11 ||

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhagavatā | nāhamanyatra rāgādrāgasya niḥsaraṇaṃ vadāmyevaṃ dveṣānmohāditi | tatrābhisaṃdhiṃ darśayati | yasmāddharmadhātuvinirmukto dharmo nāsti dharmatāvyatirekeṇa dharmābhāvāt | tasmādrāgādidharmatāpi rāgādyākhyāṃ labhate sa ca niḥsaraṇaṃ rāgādīnāmityevaṃ tatrābhisaṃdhirveditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: What was stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I do not speak of an escape from passion other than through passion, and likewise from hatred, from delusion' — herein he shows the intention. Since no dharma exists apart from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — because of the non-existence of dharmas apart from their true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) — therefore the true nature of passion and the rest also obtains the designation of passion and the rest, and that [true nature] is the escape from passion and the rest — thus the intention therein should be understood.

children.translated_text: Since no dharma exists that is released from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,

children.text: tasmātsaṃkleśanirdeśe sa saṃvid[saṃdhira] dhīmatāṃ mataḥ || Msa_13.12 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, in the teaching about defilement, that [hidden] intention of the wise is recognized. || Msa_13.12 ||

body.text: yaduktaṃ | avidyā ca bodhiścaikamiti | tatrāpi sakleśanirdeśe sa evābhisaṃdhiḥ | avidyā bodhidharmatā syāttadupacārāt |
body.translated_text: What was stated: 'Ignorance and awakening are one' — therein too, in the teaching about defilement, that very same intention [applies]: ignorance would be the true nature of awakening (<s>bodhidharmatā</s>), through metaphorical usage.

children.translated_text: Since one properly practices with respect to those very passions and the rest,
one is thereby liberated from them; therefore the escape from them is from those [very afflictions]. || Msa_13.13 ||

body.text: tāneva rāgādīnyoniśaḥ pratipadyamānastebhyo vimucyate tasmātparijñātāsta eva teṣāṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ bhavatītyayamatrābhisaṃdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Properly practicing with respect to those very passions and the rest, one is liberated from them; therefore, when they are fully known (<s>parijñāta</s>), those very [afflictions] become the escape from them — this is the intention here.

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhamanasikāraparivarjane ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the avoidance of the mental attention of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones):

children.translated_text: Indeed, for the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, intense suffering is no hindrance,
even through dwelling in the hells, for the sake of beings — somehow;
but the various wholesome conceptualizations in the inferior vehicle, prompted by the qualities and defects
of quiescence and existence, are the [real] hindrances for the wise. || Msa_13.14 ||
Indeed, dwelling in the hells does not at any time
create an obstacle for the wise to the stainless and vast awakening;
but the conceptualization of another vehicle, which is supremely cool for one's own benefit,
creates an obstacle even to the abode of supreme bliss. || Msa_13.15 ||

body.text: anayoḥ ślokayorekasya dvitīyaḥ sādhakaḥ | ubhau gatārthau |
body.translated_text: Of these two verses, the second proves [the point of] the first. Both have their meaning already explained.

body.text: niḥsvabhāvatāprakṛtipariśuddhitrāsapratiṣedhe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the refutation of fear regarding non-self-nature and natural purity:

children.translated_text: The non-existence and apprehension of dharmas, purification free from defilement —
these should be known as like illusion and the rest, and likewise as like space. || Msa_13.16 ||

children.text: yathaiva citre vidhivadvicitrite natonnataṃ nāsti ca dṛśyate 'tha ca |
children.translated_text: Just as in a painting properly executed with various [colors], there is no elevation or depression, yet they are seen;

children.text: abhūtakalpe 'pi tathaiva sarvathā dvayaṃ sadā nāsti sa dṛśyate 'tha ca || Msa_13.17 ||
children.translated_text: so too in unreal imagination (<s>abhūtakalpa</s>), in every respect, duality never exists, yet it is always seen. || Msa_13.17 ||

children.text: yathaiva toye luti[ṭi]te prasādite na jāyate sā punaracchatānyataḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as when turbid water is clarified, the clarity does not arise from elsewhere;

children.text: malāpakarṣastu sa tatra kevalaḥ svacittaśuddhau vidhireṣa eva hi || Msa_13.18 ||
children.translated_text: rather, it is merely the removal of impurities therein — this is indeed the method for the purification of one's own mind. || Msa_13.18 ||

children.text: mataṃ ca cittaṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ sadā tadāgantukadoṣadūṣitaṃ |
children.translated_text: The mind is considered to be luminous by nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>), [yet] it is always defiled by adventitious faults;

children.text: na dharmatācittamṛte 'nyacetasaḥ prabhāsvaratvaṃ prakṛtau vidhīyate || Msa_13.19 ||
children.translated_text: apart from the <s>dharmatā</s>-mind (the mind as suchness), no luminosity of nature is established for any other mind. || Msa_13.19 ||
