body.text: dharmābhāvaśca dharmopalabdhiśceti trāsasthānaṃ niḥsaṃkleśatā ca dharmadhātoḥ prakṛtyā viśuddhatā ca paścāditi trāsasthānaṃ bālānāṃ | tadyathākramaṃ māyādisādṛśyenākāśasādṛśyena ca prasādhayaṃstatastrāsaṃ pratiṣedhayati | tathā citre natonnatasādṛśyena luti[ṭi]taprasāditatoyasādṛśyena ca yathākramaṃ | caturthena ślokena toyasādharmyaṃ citte pratipādayati | yathā toyaṃ prakṛtyā prasannamāgantukena tu kāluṣyeṇa luti[ṭi]taṃ bhavatyevaṃ cittaṃ prakṛtyā prabhāsvaraṃ matamāgantukaistu dauṣairdūṣitamiti | na ca dharmatācittādṛte 'nyasya cetasaḥ paratantralakṣaṇasya prakṛtiprabhāsvaratvaṃ vidhīyate | tasmāccittatathataivātra cittaṃ veditavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: The absence of phenomena and the perception of phenomena — these are grounds for alarm. The freedom from affliction of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena), its purity by nature, and its subsequent [purity] — these are grounds for alarm for the childish. He refutes that alarm, in order, by the simile of illusion and such, by the simile of space, by the simile of the unevenness in a painting, and by the simile of turbid and clear water, respectively. With the fourth verse, he demonstrates the similarity of water to the mind: just as water is by nature clear, but becomes turbid through adventitious defilements, so the mind is considered to be luminous by nature, but defiled by adventitious faults. And apart from the <s>dharmatā</s>-mind, no luminosity of nature is established for any other mind having the character of <s>paratantra</s> (the dependent). Therefore, the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of mind alone is to be understood here as "mind."

body.text: rāgajāpattipratiṣedhe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the refutation of the offense born of passion (<s>rāga</s>):

children.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva's</s> love for beings is great, penetrating to the marrow,
as toward an only child; therefore it is considered always beneficial. || Msa_13.20 ||
Because of acting for the benefit of beings, one does not incur the offense born of passion;

children.text: dveṣo virudyate tvasya sarvasattveṣu satpathā[sarvathā] || Msa_13.21 ||
children.translated_text: rather, hatred is opposed to this [love] toward all beings in every way. || Msa_13.21 ||
Just as a dove, exceedingly tender toward her young, embraces her natural offspring and remains,

children.text: tathāvidhāyāṃ pratigho virudhyate suteṣu tadvatsakṛpe 'pi dehiṣu || Msa_13.22 ||
children.translated_text: so aversion is opposed in one of such nature toward beings, as toward children, even in one who is compassionate. || Msa_13.22 ||
Since there is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), a hostile mind is thereby opposed;
since there is peace, a mind of misfortune is thereby opposed;
since there is [giving of] benefit, a deceitful mind is thereby opposed;

children.text: lhādo yataḥ pratibhayaṃ na[ca] tato viruddhaṃ || Msa_13.23 ||
children.translated_text: since there is joy, fear is thereby opposed. || Msa_13.23 ||

body.text: yatsattveṣu bodhisattvasya prema so 'tra rāgo 'bhipretastatkṛtāmāpattiṃ teṣāṃ pratiṣedhayati | sattvahitakriyāhetutvāt | kapotīmudāharati tabdahurāgatvāt apatyasnehādhimātratayā (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 87

children.text: ) sakṛpe bodhisattve dehiṣu sattveṣu pratigho virudhyate | bodhisattvānāṃ sattveṣu maitrī bhavati vyasanaśāntiḥ arthadānaṃ lhādaśca prītyutpādāt | yata ime maitryādayastata eva pratighacittaṃ viruddhaṃ | tatpūrvakāṇi ca vyasanacittādīni |
children.translated_text: In a compassionate <s>bodhisattva</s>, aversion toward living beings is opposed. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have loving-kindness toward beings, the calming of misfortune, the giving of benefit, and joy — through the generation of delight. Since these — loving-kindness and so forth — exist, hostile thoughts are opposed; and [so too are] thoughts of misfortune and the rest, which are preceded by them.

body.translated_text: The love that a <s>bodhisattva</s> has for beings — that is what is meant by passion (<s>rāga</s>) here. He refutes the offense caused by it, because it is the cause of benefiting beings. He gives the example of a dove, because of the extremity of its affection for its young.

body.text: pratipattibhede pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the distinction of practice:

children.translated_text: As a sick person toward good medicine, so one practices regarding <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: āture ca yathā vaidyaḥ sattveṣu pratipadyate || Msa_13.24 ||
children.translated_text: and as a physician toward the sick, so one practices regarding beings. || Msa_13.24 ||
As toward an unfinished servant, so one practices regarding oneself;

children.text: vaṇigyathā punaḥ paṇye kāmeṣu pratipadyate || Msa_13.25 ||
children.translated_text: and as a merchant toward merchandise, so one practices regarding sense-pleasures. || Msa_13.25 ||
Just as a dyer toward a garment, so one practices regarding action (<s>karma</s>);

children.text: pitā yathā sute bāle sattvāheṭhe prapadyate || Msa_13.26 ||
children.translated_text: as a father toward a young child, so one approaches a being who does no harm. || Msa_13.26 ||
One desiring fire toward the lower fire-stick, so one practices regarding perseverance;
one who is trustworthy toward what is unfinished, so one approaches the higher mind. || Msa_13.27 ||
Like a magician regarding what is to be known, so one practices with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>);

children.text: pratipattiryathā yasmin bodhisattvasya sā matā || Msa_13.28 ||
children.translated_text: how the <s>bodhisattva's</s> practice is in each — that is so considered. || Msa_13.28 ||

body.text: yathā yasminpratipadyate tadabhidyotayati | yatheti subhaiṣajyādiṣvivāturādayaḥ | yatreti saṃsārādiṣu pratisaṃkhyāya saṃsāraniṣevaṇāt | kāruṇyena kleśāturasattvāparityāgāt | svapraṇihitatvacittakaraṇāt | dānādipāramitābhiśca yathākramaṃ bhogavṛddhinayanāt | kāyādikarmapariśodhanāt | sattvāpakārākopāt | kuśalabhāvanānirantarābhiyogāt | samādhyanāsvādanāt | jñeyāviparyāsācca |
body.translated_text: He illuminates how one practices in each: "as" refers to the sick person and so forth with respect to good medicine and so forth. "Wherein" refers to <s>saṃsāra</s> and the rest: by deliberately engaging in <s>saṃsāra</s> with full understanding; by not abandoning beings afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) through compassion; by disciplining one's own mind; and by leading to the increase of wealth through the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of giving and so forth, respectively; by purifying actions of body and so forth; by not being angered at harm done by beings; by uninterrupted application to the cultivation of wholesome states; by not relishing <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); and by not being confused regarding what is to be known.

body.text: pratipattitrimaṇḍalapariśuddhau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>) of practice:

children.translated_text: Thus, one of perpetually noble and vigorous effort, well-engaged in the ripening and purification of the two,

children.text: paramavimalanirvikalpaguddhyā vrajati sa siddhimanuttamāṃ krameṇa || Msa_13.29 ||
children.translated_text: advances gradually to the unsurpassed attainment, through the supremely pure and non-conceptual awakening. || Msa_13.29 ||

body.text: iti nirvikalpena dharma nairātmyajñānena pratipattuḥ pratipattavyasya pratipatteścāvikalpanā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhirveditavyā | dvayaparipācanaśodhaneṣu [su]yukta iti sattvānāmātmanaśca |
body.translated_text: Thus, the non-conceptualization of the practitioner, of what is to be practiced, and of the practice itself, through the non-conceptual knowledge of <s>dharmanairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena), should be understood as the purity of the three spheres. "Well-engaged in the ripening and purification of the two" means of beings and of oneself.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre pratipattyadhikārastrayodaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the thirteenth chapter on practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) ||

body.text: caturdaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Fourteenth chapter:

body.text: avavādānuśāsanīvibhāge ślokā ekapañcāśat |
body.translated_text: In the division of instruction and guidance (<s>avavādānuśāsanī</s>), fifty-one verses:

children.translated_text: Having emerged from incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), constantly increasing one's faith (<s>adhimukti</s>),
complete with wholesome dharmas, like the ocean with waters — || Msa_14.1 ||

body.text: adhimuktiṃ vivardhayannityadhimātrāvasthānayanāt | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: "Constantly increasing one's faith" — because of always leading to a state of intense [faith]. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Thus, the child of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), having accumulated the accumulations [of merit and knowledge], pure from the beginning,
well-learned and with a fit mind, engages in meditation. || Msa_14.2 ||

body.text: ādiśuddho bodhisattvasaṃvarapariśodhanānmahāyāne dṛṣṭiṛjju[ju]karaṇāccāviparītārthagrahaṇataḥ | suvijño bahuśrutatvāt | kalpa[lya]citto vinivaraṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: "Pure from the beginning" — from the purification of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vows and from making one's views straight in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through the non-perverted apprehension of meaning. "Well-learned" — because of being greatly learned. "With a fit mind" — because of being free from the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: Then, in the stream of the Dharma, one receives instruction from the <s>Buddhas</s>,
vast, for the sake of attaining the fullness of the knowledge of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). || Msa_14.3 ||

body.text: śloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The verse has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Then, regarding the Dharma such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest, which illuminate the meaning of non-duality,
the ascetic should first bind the mind to the name of <s>sūtras</s> and the rest. || Msa_14.4 ||
Then one should proceed gradually through the divisions of words,
and one should investigate their meanings, personally and thoroughly. || Msa_14.5 ||

body.text: avadhṛtya ca tānarthāndharme saṃkalayetpunaḥ

children.translated_text: then one should make an aspiration for the realization of those meanings. || Msa_14.6 ||

body.translated_text: Having ascertained those meanings, one should again compile them in the Dharma;

body.text: sūtrageyādike dharme yatsūtrādināma daśabhūmikamityevamādi tatra cittaṃ prathamato badhnīyāt | ebhistribhiḥ ślokaiḥ ṣaṭ cittānyupadiṣṭāni | mūlacittamanucaracittaṃ vicāraṇācittamavadhāraṇācittaṃ saṃkalanacittamāśāsticittaṃ ca | tatra mūlacittaṃ yatsūtrādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nāmālambanaṃ | avavādaṃ śrutvā svayaṃ vā kalpayitvā | tadyathānityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmyaṃ ya yoniśo na cetyādi | anucaracittaṃ yena sūtrādīnāṃ nāmata ālambitānāṃ padaprabhedamanugacchati | vicāraṇācittaṃ yenārthaṃ vyañjanaṃ ca vicārayati | tatrārthaṃ caturbhirākārairvicārayati gaṇanayā tulanayā mīmāṃsayā pratyavekṣaṇayā ca | tatra gaṇanā saṃgrahaṇaṃ tadyathā rūpaṃ daśāyatanānyekasya ca pradeśo vedanā ṣaḍ vedanākāyā ityevamādi | tulanā saṃkhyāvato (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 89

children.text: ) dharmasya śamalakṣa[ṇa?]grahaṇamanādhyāropānapavādataḥ | mīmāṃsā pramāṇaparīkṣa | pratyavekṣaṇāgaṇitatulitamīmāṃsitasyārthasyāvalokanaṃ | vyañjanaṃ dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ vicārayati | sārthatathā[yā] ca samastānāṃ vyañjanānāṃ nirarthatayā ca vyastānāṃ | avadhāraṇācittaṃ yena yathānucaritaṃ vicāritaṃ vā tannimittamavadhārayati | saṃkalanacittaṃ tadyathā vicāritamarthaṃ mūlacitte saṃkṣipyaparipiṇḍitākāraṃ vartate | āśāsticittaṃ yadarthaṃ prayukto bhavati samā[dhyarthaṃ vā?] tatparipūryarthaṃ vā śrāmaṇyaphalārthaṃ vā bhūmipraveśārthaṃ vā viśeṣagamanārthaṃ vā tacchandasahagataṃ vartate | cittameva hyālambanapratibhāsaṃ vartate na cittādanyadālambanamastīti jānato vā cittamātramajānato vā cittamevālambanaṃ nānyat | iti ṣaḍvidhaṃ cittamālambanaṃ vyavasthāpyate |
children.translated_text: phenomenon that has been enumerated, without superimposition or deprecation. Critical examination is testing by means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Review is the contemplation of a meaning that has been enumerated, compared, and critically examined. One investigates expression in two ways: through the meaningfulness of all expressions taken together, and through the meaninglessness of individual [expressions] taken separately. The ascertaining-mind is that by which one ascertains the sign of what has been attended to or investigated. The compiling-mind is that which, having condensed the investigated meaning in the root-mind, operates in a consolidated form. The aspiration-mind is that for the purpose of which one strives — whether for the purpose of <s>samādhi</s>, or for the fulfillment of that, or for the fruits of the ascetic life, or for entering a stage, or for attaining distinction — and it operates accompanied by desire. For the mind itself operates with the appearance of its object — whether one who knows that no object exists apart from the mind, or one who does not know — in either case, the mind alone is the object and nothing else. Thus the sixfold mind is established as the object.

body.translated_text: Regarding the Dharma such as sūtras, recitations, and the rest — such names of sūtras as 'the Ten Stages' (<s>Daśabhūmika</s>) and so forth — one should first bind the mind thereto. By these three verses, six [types of] mind are taught: the root-mind (<s>mūlacitta</s>), the attendant-mind (<s>anucaracitta</s>), the investigating-mind (<s>vicāraṇācitta</s>), the ascertaining-mind (<s>avadhāraṇācitta</s>), the compiling-mind (<s>saṃkalanacitta</s>), and the aspiration-mind (<s>āśāsticitta</s>). Therein, the root-mind is that which takes the names of dharmas such as sūtras as its object — having heard instruction or having conceived it oneself — such as 'impermanent, suffering, empty, non-self, which is properly attended to' and so forth. The attendant-mind is that by which one follows the word-divisions of the sūtras and the rest that have been taken as objects by name. The investigating-mind is that by which one investigates meaning and expression. Therein, one investigates meaning in four ways: by enumeration, by comparison, by critical examination, and by review. Therein, enumeration is classification — such as 'form is ten sense-bases and a portion of one'; 'feeling is six classes of feeling' and so forth. Comparison is the apprehension of the tranquility-characteristic of a

children.translated_text: One should seek and examine through mental discourse in succession,
and also investigate through mental attentions that are discourse-free and of a single flavor. || Msa_14.7 ||
The path of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) should be known as the condensed Dharma-name;
the path of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) should be known as the investigation of its meanings. || Msa_14.8 ||
The path of the union (<s>yuganaddha</s>) of both should also be known; and again, regarding that condensed [object],
one should apprehend the contracted mind and calm the agitated one. || Msa_14.9 ||

body.text: śa[sa]maprāptamupekṣeta tasminnālambane punaḥ

children.translated_text: one should then engage with continuity and with earnestness, and then apply [the mind] to everything. || Msa_14.10 ||

body.translated_text: One should regard with equanimity the mind that has attained tranquility, and regarding that very object,

body.text: ebhiścaturbhiḥ ślokairekādaśa manaskārā upadiṣṭāḥ | savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ | avitarko vicāramātraḥ | avitarko 'vicāraḥ | śamathamanaskāraḥ | vipaśyanā manaskāraḥ | yuganaddhamanaskāraḥ | [pragrahanimittamanaskāraḥ] śamathanimittamanaskāraḥ | upekṣānimitta manaskāraḥ | sātatyamanaskāraḥ | satkṛtyamanaskāraśca |
body.translated_text: By these four verses, eleven mental attentions are taught: with initial application (<s>savitarka</s>); with sustained application (<s>savicāra</s>); without initial application, with sustained application alone; without initial or sustained application; the mental attention of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding); the mental attention of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); the mental attention of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>); the mental attention of the sign of apprehension; the mental attention of the sign of calming; the mental attention of the sign of equanimity; the mental attention of continuity; and the mental attention of earnestness.

children.translated_text: Having bound the mind to the object, one should not scatter its current;
recognizing distraction quickly, one should redirect [the mind] to that [object] again. || Msa_14.11 ||
One should gather the mind inwardly, progressively, the wise one;
then one should tame the mind, from seeing the qualities of <s>samādhi</s>. || Msa_14.12 ||
One should calm aversion toward it, from seeing the faults of distraction;
likewise, one should calm covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and other [hindrances] that have arisen. || Msa_14.13 ||
Then one obtains the effortful [concentration] of mind, and the spontaneously flowing one;
the ascetic obtains the effortless [concentration] through the repeated practice of that. || Msa_14.14 ||

body.text: ebhiścaturbhiḥ ślokairnavākārayā cittasthityā sthityupāya upadiṣṭaḥ | cittaṃ sthāpayati saṃsthāpayati avasthāpayati upasthāpayati damayati śamayati vyupaśamayatyekotīkaroti cittaṃ samādaghātīti navākārāḥ |
body.translated_text: By these four verses, the method of abiding through the ninefold stages of mental abiding is taught: one fixes the mind (<s>sthāpayati</s>), re-fixes it (<s>saṃsthāpayati</s>), places it close (<s>avasthāpayati</s>), closely places it (<s>upasthāpayati</s>), tames it (<s>damayati</s>), calms it (<s>śamayati</s>), thoroughly calms it (<s>vyupaśamayati</s>), makes it one-pointed (<s>ekotīkaroti</s>), and places it in equipoise (<s>samādadhāti</s>) — these are the nine stages.

children.text: tataḥ sa tanukāṃ labdhvā praśrabdhiṃ kāyacetasoḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained a subtle <s>praśrabdhi</s> (pliancy) of body and mind,
one should be known as possessing [proper] mental attention, and one further increases that. || Msa_14.15 ||
By the far-reaching development, one obtains the primary stage of abiding;
purifying that for the sake of the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), one attains the supreme workability. || Msa_14.16 ||
Through the production of <s>abhijñās</s> in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one goes to the world-realms,
for the purpose of worshipping immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> and for the purpose of hearing [the Dharma]. || Msa_14.17 ||
Having attended upon immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> through incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
one attains the supreme workability of mind, through that attendance. || Msa_14.18 ||

body.text: iti karmaṇyatāṃ parāṃ dhyāne iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ | kalpairameyagairityaprameyasaṃkhyāgataiḥ | śeṣameṣāṃ ślokānāṃ gatārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, 'the supreme workability' should be connected with 'in <s>dhyāna</s>.' 'Through incalculable <s>kalpas</s>' means through those gone to an immeasurable number. The rest of these verses has its meaning already explained.

children.text: tato 'nuśaṃsāna labhate pañca śuddhaiḥ sa pūrvagān |
children.translated_text: Then one obtains, through the preceding pure [stages], five benefits;

children.text: viśuddhibhājanatvaṃ ca tato yāti niruttaraṃ || Msa_14.19 ||
children.translated_text: and then one reaches the unsurpassed state of being a vessel of purity. || Msa_14.19 ||
For one's entire body of coarseness melts away at every moment,

children.text: āpūryate ca praśrabdhyā kāyacittaṃ samantataḥ || Msa_14.20 ||
children.translated_text: and body and mind are filled completely with <s>praśrabdhi</s> (pliancy). || Msa_14.20 ||
One knows the unlimited appearance of all phenomena everywhere,
and one perceives the unimagined signs in purification. || Msa_14.21 ||

children.text: prapūrau ca viśuddhau ca dharmakāyasya sarvathā |
children.translated_text: for the fulfillment and purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> in every way,
the wise one constantly undertakes such a gathering of causes. || Msa_14.22 ||

body.text: tataḥ śuddheḥ pūrvaṃgamānpañcānuśaṃsān labhate | śuddheriti śuddhyāśayabhūmeḥ | teṣāṃ ca lābhādviśuddhibhājanatvaṃ prāpnoti | nirūttaraṃ yānānantaryāt[nuttaryāt] | prapūrau ca viśuddhau ca dharmakāyasyeti daśamyāṃ bhūmau paripūrirbuddhabhūmau viśuddhiḥ | eteṣāṃ pañcānāmanuśaṃsānāṃ trayaḥ śamathapakṣā dvau vipaśyanāpakṣau veditavyau | ato yāvallaukikaḥ samudāgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then one obtains the five benefits that precede purification. 'Of purification' means of the stage of pure intention (<s>śuddhāśayabhūmi</s>). And from obtaining these, one reaches the state of being a vessel for purification. 'Unsurpassed' — because of the unsurpassedness of the vehicle. 'For the fulfillment and purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>' — fulfillment is on the tenth stage, purification is on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. Of these five benefits, three belong to the side of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and two to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Thus far is the worldly attainment.

children.translated_text: Then that <s>bodhisattva</s>, being in such a state, concentrated,
does not perceive any objects freed from mental discourse (<s>manojalpā</s>). || Msa_14.23 ||
For the purpose of increasing the light of Dharma, one undertakes firm vigor;
and through the increase of the light of Dharma, one abides in mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). || Msa_14.24 ||
Then one perceives that all objects are merely appearances in mind;
at that time, the distraction toward the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) is abandoned. || Msa_14.25 ||
Then the distraction toward the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) alone remains for that one;

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiṃ ca spṛśatyāśu tadā punaḥ || Msa_14.26 ||
children.translated_text: and then again one swiftly touches the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>). || Msa_14.26 ||

body.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyāni | tathābhūto bodhisattvaḥ samāhitacitto manojalpādvinirmuktān sarvadharmānna paśyati svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇākhyānmanojalpamātrameva khyāti | sāsyoṣmagatāvasthā | ayaṃ sa āloko yamadhikṛtyoktaṃ kṣāranadyām | āloka iti dharmanidhyānakṣānteretadadhivacanamiti | sa tasyaiva dharmālokasya vivṛdhdyarthamāsthitakriyayā dṛḍhaṃ vīryamārabhate | sāsya mūrdhāvasthā | dharmālokavivṛdhdyā ca cittamātre 'vatiṣṭhate | cittametaditi prativedhāt | tataścitta eva sarvārthapratibhāsatvaṃ paśyati | na cittādanyamarthaṃ | tadā cāsya grāhyavikṣepaḥ prahīno bhavati | grāhakavikṣepaḥ kevalo 'vaśiṣyate | sāsya kṣāntyavasthā | tadā ca kṣipramānantaryasamādhiṃ spṛśati | sāsya laukikāgradharmāvasthā | kena kāraṇena sa ānantarya ucyate |
body.translated_text: From here onward are the factors conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). The <s>bodhisattva</s> in such a state, with concentrated mind, does not perceive all dharmas as freed from mental discourse — only mental discourse itself, consisting of specific and general characteristics, appears. That is the stage of heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>). This is the light referred to in the <s>Kṣāranadī</s> [sūtra]: 'light' is a designation for the patient acceptance of the contemplation of dharmas (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>). For the purpose of increasing that very light of Dharma, one undertakes firm vigor through sustained practice. That is the stage of the summit (<s>mūrdha</s>). Through the increase of the light of Dharma, one abides in mind-only — 'this is mind' — from penetration. Then one perceives the nature of all objects as mere appearances in mind itself — not any object other than mind. At that time, the distraction toward the apprehended is abandoned; the distraction toward the apprehender alone remains. That is the stage of patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>). Then one swiftly touches the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>. That is the stage of the supreme worldly dharma (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). For what reason is it called 'uninterrupted'?

children.translated_text: Because the distraction toward the apprehender ceases immediately after that;
these, beginning with heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>), should be known in due order. || Msa_14.27 ||

body.text: ityetānyuṣmagatādīni nirvedhabhāgīyāni |
body.translated_text: Thus these, beginning with heat, are the factors conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>).

children.translated_text: Disjoined from the dual grasping, supramundane, unsurpassed,

children.text: nirvikalpaṃ malāpetaṃ jñānaṃ sa labhate punaḥ || Msa_14.28 ||
children.translated_text: non-conceptual, free from defilements — that knowledge one then attains. || Msa_14.28 ||

body.text: ataḥ pareṇa darśanamārgāvasthā | dvayagrāhavisaṃyuktaṃ grāhyagrāhagrāhakagrāhavisaṃyogāt | anuttaraṃ yānānantaryeṇa[nuttaryeṇa] | nirvikalpaṃ grāhyagrāhakavikalpavisaṃyogāt | malāpetaṃ darśanajñe[he]yakleśaprahāṇāt | etena virajo vigatamalamityuktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: From this point onward is the stage of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). 'Disjoined from dual grasping' — because of the disjunction from grasping at the apprehended and grasping at the apprehender. 'Unsurpassed' — because of the unsurpassedness of the vehicle. 'Non-conceptual' — because of the disjunction from the conceptualization of apprehended and apprehender. 'Free from defilements' — because of the abandonment of the afflictions and cognitive obscurations to be abandoned by seeing. By this, what is stated is 'dustless and free from stain.'

children.translated_text: That is regarded as the first transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>);

children.text: ameyaiścāsya sā kalpaiḥ suviśuddhiṃ nigacchati || Msa_14.29 ||
children.translated_text: and through immeasurable eons, it reaches complete purification. || Msa_14.29 ||

body.text: śloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The verse is self-explanatory.

children.translated_text: Having then penetrated the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
one attains the constant equal-mindedness toward all beings as toward oneself. || Msa_14.30 ||
Regarding selflessness, regarding the meaning of suffering, regarding activity, regarding non-retaliation,
one is equal-minded toward beings, just like the other sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_14.31 ||

body.text: dharmanairātmyena ca dharmasamatāṃ pratividhya sarvasattveṣu sadā ātmasamacittatāṃ prattilabhate | pañcavidhayā samatayā | nairātmyasamatayā duḥkhasamatayā svaparasaṃtāneṣu nairātmyaduḥkhatayoraviśeṣāt | kṛtyasamatayā svaparaduḥkhaprahāṇakāmatāsāmānyāt | niṣpratikārasamatayā | ātmana iva parataḥ pratikārānabhinandanāt | tadanyabodhisattvasamatayā ca yathā tairabhisamitaṃ tathābhisamayāt |
body.translated_text: Having penetrated the equality of dharmas through the selflessness of dharmas, one attains the constant equal-mindedness toward all beings as toward oneself, through a fivefold equality: through the equality of selflessness and the equality of suffering — because there is no difference between selflessness and suffering in one's own and others' continua. Through the equality of activity — because of the commonality of the desire to abandon one's own and others' suffering. Through the equality of non-retaliation — because, just as for oneself, one does not rejoice in retaliation from others. And through the equality with other <s>bodhisattvas</s> — because one realizes just as they have realized.

children.translated_text: The conditioned phenomena of self in the three realms, arising from unreal conceptualization,
one sees with knowledge that is perfectly pure and non-dual in meaning. || Msa_14.32 ||

body.text: sa traidhātukātmasaṃskārānabhūtaparikalpanāmātrānpaśyati | suviśuddhena jñānena lokottaratvāt | advayārthenetyagrāhyagrāhakārthena |
body.translated_text: One sees the conditioned phenomena of self in the three realms as mere unreal conceptualization — with perfectly pure knowledge, because of its supramundane nature; and 'non-dual in meaning' means with the meaning of non-apprehended and non-apprehender.

children.translated_text: The existence of the absence of that [duality], liberated from what is abandoned through seeing —

children.text: labdhvā darśanamārgo hi tadā tena nirūcyate || Msa_14.33 ||
children.translated_text: having attained this, the path of seeing is then declared thereby. || Msa_14.33 ||

body.text: tasya grāhyagrāhakābhāvasya bhāvaṃ dharmadhātūndarśanaprahātavyaiḥ kleśairvimuktaṃ paśyati |
body.translated_text: One sees the existence of the absence of the apprehended and apprehender — the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — liberated from the afflictions to be abandoned through seeing.

children.translated_text: Having known the emptiness of non-existence, and likewise the emptiness of such existence,

children.text: prakṛtyā śūnyatāṃ jñātvā śūnyajña iti kathyate || Msa_14.34 ||
children.translated_text: and having known the emptiness by nature — one is called a knower of emptiness. || Msa_14.34 ||

body.text: sa ca bodhisattvaḥ śūnyajña ityucyate | trividhaśūnyatājñānāt | abhāvaśūnyatā parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ svena lakṣaṇenābhāvāt | tathābhāvasya śūnyatā paratantrasya sa hi na tathābhāvo yathā kalpyate svena lakṣaṇena bhāvaḥ | prakṛtiśūnyatā pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ śūnyatāsvabhāvatvāt |
body.translated_text: And that <s>bodhisattva</s> is called a knower of emptiness, from the knowledge of threefold emptiness. The emptiness of non-existence is the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>) — because of the non-existence of its own characteristic. The emptiness of such existence is of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) — for it does not exist in the way it is conceptualized, [yet] it exists through its own characteristic. The emptiness by nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) is the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>) — because its intrinsic nature is emptiness.

children.translated_text: The signless state (<s>animitta</s>) is to be known, and the cessation of conceptualizations;
and unreal conceptualization — that is indeed [the domain] of the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). || Msa_14.35 ||

body.text: animittapadaṃ jñeyaṃ vikalpānāṃ ca saṃkṣayaḥ | abhūtaparikalpastadapraṇidhānasya padamālambanamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The signless state is to be known, and the cessation of conceptualizations. Unreal conceptualization is the domain — the object — of the wishless state. This is the meaning.

children.text: tena darśanamārgeṇa saha lābhaḥ sadā mataḥ |
children.translated_text: Together with that path of seeing, the attainment is always recognized
of all the varied factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), for the son of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_14.36 ||

body.text: tena darśanamārgeṇa saha bodhisattvasya sarveṣāṃ bodhipakṣāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābho veditavyaḥ smṛtyupasthānādīnāṃ |
body.translated_text: Together with that path of seeing, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s attainment of all the dharmas that are factors conducive to awakening — the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and the rest — should be understood.

children.translated_text: Understanding the world as mere conditioning (<s>saṃskāramātra</s>), selfless, and merely an outgrowth of suffering,

children.text: vihāya yānarthamayātmadṛṣṭiḥ mahātmadṛṣṭiṃ śrayate mahārthā || Msa_14.37 ||
children.translated_text: abandoning the self-view that is purposeless and harmful, one resorts to the great self-view that has great purpose. || Msa_14.37 ||
One who has a self-view without [ordinary] self-view, and who is deeply pained even without [personal] suffering,

children.text: sarvārthakartā na ca kārakāṅkṣī yathātmanaḥ svātmahitāni kṛtvā || Msa_14.38 ||
children.translated_text: who accomplishes all purposes yet does not seek an agent — as if having done beneficial things for one's own self. || Msa_14.38 ||

children.text: yo muktacittaḥ parayā vimuktyā baddhaśca gāḍhāyatabandhanena |
children.translated_text: One whose mind is liberated with the supreme liberation, yet who is bound with a firm and extensive bond,

children.text: duḥkhasya paryantamapaśyamānaḥ prayujyate caiva karoti caiva || Msa_14.39 ||
children.translated_text: not seeing the end of suffering, one engages and acts. || Msa_14.39 ||
The world is unable to bear its own suffering; how much less the accumulated suffering of others?

children.text: janmaikamālokayate[gataṃ] tvacinto viparyayāttasya tu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_14.40 ||
children.translated_text: It looks at a single birth [and recoils]; but the <s>bodhisattva</s>, through the reverse [attitude], [acts with] inconceivable [courage]. || Msa_14.40 ||

children.text: yatprema yā vatsalatā prayogaḥ sattveṣvakhedaśca jinātmajānāṃ |
children.translated_text: The love, the tenderness, the effort, and the unwearied [devotion] toward beings of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: āścaryametatparamaṃ bhaveṣu na caiva sattvātmasamānabhāvāt || Msa_14.41 ||
children.translated_text: this is a supreme wonder in the worlds, yet it is also not a wonder, because of [their] equal regard for beings as for themselves. || Msa_14.41 ||

body.text: ebhiḥ pañcabhiḥ ślokairdarśanamārgalābhino bodhisattvasya māhātmyodbhāvanam | anarthamayātmadṛṣṭiryā kliṣṭā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ | mahātmadṛṣṭiriti mahārthā yā sarvasattveṣvātmasamacittalābhātmadṛṣṭiḥ | sā hi sarvasattvārthakriṃyāhetutvāt mahārthā | vinātmadṛṣṭyā anarthamayyātmadṛṣṭirmahārthā yā vināpi duḥkhena svasaṃtānajena suduḥkhitā sarvasattvasaṃtānajena | yo vimuktacitto darśanaprahātavyebhyaḥ parayā vimuktyānuttareṇa yānena | baddhaśca gāḍhāyatabandhanena sarvasattvasāṃntānikena duḥkhasya paryantaṃ na paśyati sva[sattva]dhātoranantatvādākāśavat prayujyate ca duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai sattvānāṃ karoti caiva tāma[arthaṃ] prameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ | viparyayāttasya tu bodhisattvaḥ sa hi saṃpiṇḍitasarvasattvaduḥkhaṃ yāvallokagatamudvoḍhuṃ samarthaḥ | yā sattveṣu bodhisattvasya priyatā yā ca hitasukhaiṣitā yaśca tadarthaṃ prayogo yaścitta[yaścatat]prayuktasyākheda etatsarvamāścaryaṃ paramaṃ lokeṣu | na caivāścaryaṃ sattvānāmātmasamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: By these five verses, the greatness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained the path of seeing is displayed. 'The self-view that is purposeless and harmful' is the afflicted view of the transitory collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). 'The great self-view' means one of great purpose — the self-view consisting of the equal-mindedness toward all beings gained toward all beings; it is of great purpose because it is the cause of accomplishing the welfare of all beings. 'Without self-view' — the harmful self-view of great purpose; 'without suffering' in one's own continuum, yet deeply pained by the suffering in the continua of all beings. 'Whose mind is liberated' from what is to be abandoned through seeing, 'with the supreme liberation' through the unsurpassed vehicle. 'Yet bound with a firm and extensive bond' — the suffering in the continua of all beings — one does not see the end of suffering, because of the infinity of the realm of beings like space; one engages in making an end of suffering for beings, and one acts for immeasurable beings. 'Through the reverse [attitude] of the <s>bodhisattva</s>' — for one is able to bear the accumulated suffering of all beings throughout the world. The love toward beings, the tenderness seeking their welfare and happiness, the effort for that purpose, and the unwearied [devotion] of one so engaged — all this is a supreme wonder in the worlds; yet it is also not a wonder, because of the equal regard for beings as for oneself.

children.translated_text: Then, on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), on the remaining stages,
one engages in the cultivation of the twofold knowledge here. || Msa_14.42 ||
The non-conceptual knowledge is that which purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas;
the other — the knowledge of 'as-it-is establishment' — ripens beings. || Msa_14.43 ||
The culmination of cultivation [occurs] upon the completion of the second incalculable [eon];
reaching the final cultivation, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is consecrated (<s>abhiṣikta</s>). || Msa_14.44 ||
Attaining the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), which is unbreakable by conceptualizations,
and the ultimate transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), purified of all obscurations, || Msa_14.45 ||
one attains omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), the unsurpassed state,
abiding wherein one proceeds for the welfare of all beings. || Msa_14.46 ||

body.text: ebhirbhāvanāmārgaḥ paridīpitaḥ dvividhaṃ jñānaṃ | nirvikalpaṃ ca yenātmano buddhadharmān viśodhayati | yathāvyavasthānaṃ ca lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ laukikaṃ yena sattvānparipācayati | asaṃkhyeyadvayasya samāptau paścimāṃ bhāvanāmāgamyāvasānagatāmabhiṣikto vajropamaṃ samādhiṃ labhate | vikalpānuśayābhedyārthena vajropamaḥ | tato niṣṭhāgatāmāśrayaparāvṛttiṃ labhate sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇanirmalāṃ | sarvākārajñatāṃ cānuttarapadaṃ yatrastho yāvatsaṃsāramabhisaṃbodhinirvāṇasaṃdarśanādibhiḥ sattvānāṃ hitāya pratipadyate |
body.translated_text: By these [verses], the path of cultivation is illuminated. The twofold knowledge: non-conceptual, by which one purifies one's own <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas; and the knowledge of 'as-it-is establishment' — the worldly [knowledge] obtained subsequent to the supramundane — by which one ripens beings. Upon the completion of the second incalculable [eon], reaching the final cultivation at its conclusion, the consecrated one attains the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>. 'Diamond-like' in the sense of being unbreakable by the latent dispositions of conceptualization. Then one attains the ultimate transformation of the basis, purified of all obscurations of afflictions and the knowable. And omniscience — the unsurpassed state — abiding wherein, throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>, one proceeds for the welfare of beings through the display of awakening, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and so forth.

children.text: kathaṃ tathā durlabhadarśane munau bhavenmahārthaṃ na hi nityadarśanaṃ |
children.translated_text: How could one who has a rare vision of the <s>Muni</s> not [benefit greatly], for there is no constant seeing [of him]?
One whose mind is always greatly nourished by the torrents of faith born from incomparable hearing — || Msa_14.47 ||

children.text: a[pra]codyamānaḥ satataṃ ca saṃmukhaṃ tathāgatairdharmasu[mu]khe vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: constantly urged and standing face to face, established in the gateway of the Dharma by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: nigṛhya keśeṣviva doṣagahvarāt nikṛṣya bodhau ca balānniveśyate || Msa_14.48 ||
children.translated_text: seized as if by the hair from the pit of faults, dragged out and forcefully established in awakening. || Msa_14.48 ||
Having surpassed the entire world in every way through perfectly pure visions and non-conceptual awakenings,

children.text: mahāndhakāraṃ vidhamayya bhāsate jaganmahāditya ivātyudārataḥ || Msa_14.49 ||
children.translated_text: dispelling the great darkness, one shines like a great sun over the world, with supreme magnificence. || Msa_14.49 ||

body.text: ebhistribhiḥ ślokairavavādamāhātmyaṃ darśayati | yo hi dharmamukhaśrotasyavavādaṃ labhate tasya nityaṃ buddhadarśanaṃ bhavati | tataścāsamaṃ dharmaśravaṇaṃ | yato 'syātyarthaṃ prasādaḥ prasādavegairāpyāyitacetasastannityadarśanaṃ buddhānāṃ mahārthaṃ bhavati | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: By these three verses, the greatness of instruction is shown. For one who receives instruction from one standing at the gateway of the Dharma-hearing, there is constant seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>. From that, incomparable hearing of the Dharma. Because of the extreme faith arising thereby, with torrents of faith nourishing the mind, that constant seeing of the <s>Buddhas</s> becomes of great purpose. The rest is self-explanatory.

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> constantly give due praise to one who is properly engaged in self-interest;
criticism to one engaged in jealousy; [they show] dharmas of every kind that are favorable to obstacles — regarding stability and investigation —
the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) display, as is proper, to the foremost beings,

children.text: yān varjyāsevya yoge bhavati vipulatā saugate śāsane 'smim || Msa_14.50 ||
children.translated_text: by avoiding and cultivating which, there is vastness in this teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). || Msa_14.50 ||

body.text: caturvidhāmanuśāsanīmetena ślokena darśayati | adhiśīlamadhikṛtya samyaksvārthaprayukte bodhisattve praśaṃsāvidhānataḥ | adhicittamadhiprajñaṃ cādhikṛtya sthitivicayapare tadantarāyāṇāṃ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 95

children.text: ) tadanukūlānāṃ ca sarvaprakārāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ deśanataḥ | yānvarjyāsevyetyantarāyānanukūlāṃśca yathākramaṃ | yoga iti śamathavipaśyanābhāvanāyāṃ |
children.translated_text: ) and through the teaching of all kinds of dharmas favorable to those [obstacles]. 'What is to be avoided and what is to be cultivated' [refers to] the obstacles and the favorable factors, respectively. 'Yoga' means in the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).

body.translated_text: By this verse, the fourfold instruction is shown. With regard to higher moral discipline, [there is] the giving of praise to the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is properly engaged in self-interest. With regard to higher mind and higher wisdom, regarding stability and investigation, the obstacles to those —

children.text: iti satataśubhācayaprapūrṇaḥ suvipulametya sa cetasaḥ samādhiṃ |
children.translated_text: Thus, filled with the constant accumulation of wholesome [qualities], having attained the supremely vast <s>samādhi</s> of the mind,
constantly receiving the great instruction of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage), the foremost being goes to the far shore of the ocean of qualities. || Msa_14.51 ||

body.text: nigamanaśloko gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The concluding verse has its meaning already explained.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre avavādānuśāsanyadhikāraścaturdaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fourteenth chapter on instruction and admonition (<s>avavādānuśāsanī</s>) ||

body.text: pañcadaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Fifteenth chapter:

body.text: uddānam
body.translated_text: Synopsis:

body.text: adhimukterbahulatā dharmaparyeṣṭideśane

children.translated_text: practice, likewise proper instruction and admonition. || Msa_15.1 ||

body.translated_text: Conviction, abundance, the search for Dharma, teaching,

body.text: upāyasahitakarmavibhāge catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the division of action accompanied by skillful means (<s>upāya</s>):

children.translated_text: Just as the earth is the support of forests, bodies, mountains, and rivers on all sides,

children.text: tathaiva dānādiśubhasya sarvato budheṣu karma trividhaṃ nirucyate || Msa_15.2 ||
children.translated_text: so too, in the wise ones, the threefold action is declared [as the basis] of all wholesomeness such as giving and the rest. || Msa_15.2 ||

body.text: anena ślokena samutthānopāyaṃ darśayati | sarvaprakārasya dānādiśubhasya pāramitābodhipakṣādikasya karmatrayasamutthitatvāt | budheṣviti bodhisattveṣu | vanādigrahaṇamupabhojyā sthirasthiravastunidarśanārtham |
body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows the means of arising: because all kinds of wholesomeness such as giving and the rest — the <s>pāramitās</s>, factors conducive to awakening, and so forth — arise from the three kinds of action. 'In the wise ones' means in <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The mention of forests and the rest is to illustrate enjoyable and stable/unstable things.

children.translated_text: For those whose selves are exerted in difficult deeds of various forms, accumulated over many <s>kalpas</s> (eons),

children.text: na kāyavākcittamayasya karmaṇo jinātmajānāṃ bhavatīha saṃnatiḥ || Msa_15.3 ||
children.translated_text: there is no weariness regarding the action of body, speech, and mind for the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_15.3 ||
Just as one who seeks one's own welfare would protect one's own body from poison, weapons, and great fire, from the enemy,
so the son of the <s>Jinas</s> would protect the threefold action from the inferior vehicle in its various forms. || Msa_15.4 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ vyutthānopāyaṃ darśayati | mahāyānakhedānyayānapātavyutthānādyathākramaṃ | saṃnatiḥ kheda ityarthaḥ | viṣādisādharmyaṃ hīnayānapratisaṃyuktasya karmaṇo hīnayānacittapariṇāmanāt mahāyāne kuśalamūlasamucchedanāt anutpannakuśalamūlānutpādāya | utpanna kuśalamūla[sa?]sya dhvaṃsanāt | buddhatvasaṃpatprāptivibandhanācca |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he shows the means of rising above [obstacles]: through rising above the weariness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and the falling into another vehicle, respectively. 'Weariness' means discouragement. The analogy with poison and the rest [applies] to action connected with the inferior vehicle — because through the mental dedication toward the inferior vehicle, the roots of merit in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> are completely cut off, because unarisen roots of merit are prevented from arising, because arisen roots of merit are destroyed, and because the attainment of the prosperity of Buddhahood is obstructed.

children.text: na karmiṇaḥ karma na karmaṇaḥ kriyāṃ sadāvikalpaḥ samudīkṣate tridhā |
children.translated_text: Always non-conceptual, one does not regard the doer of action, the action, or the deed — in three ways;

children.text: tato 'sya tatkarma viśuddhipāragaṃ bhavatyanantaṃ tadupāyasaṃgrahāt || Msa_15.5 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, that action of one's becomes infinitely pure to the far shore, through the embrace of that means. || Msa_15.5 ||

body.text: anena ślokena caturthena viśuddhyupāyaṃ karmaṇo darśayati | maṇḍalapariśuddhitaḥ kartṛkarmakriyāṇāmanupalambhāt | anantamityakṣayam |
body.translated_text: By this fourth verse, he shows the means of purification of action: through the purity of the maṇḍala — from the non-apprehension of agent, action, and deed. 'Infinite' means inexhaustible.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra upāyasahitakarmādhikāraḥ pañcadaśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fifteenth chapter on action accompanied by skillful means (<s>upāyasahitakarma</s>) ||

body.text: ṣoḍaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Sixteenth chapter:

body.text: pāramitāprabhedasaṃgrahe uddānaślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A synopsis verse on the comprehensive analysis of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections):

children.translated_text: Their enumeration, then their characteristics, the sequence, the etymology, the cultivation and their qualities,

children.text: prabhedanaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ vipakṣo jñeyo guṇo 'nyonyaviniścayaśca || Msa_16.1 ||
children.translated_text: the division, the comprehensive collection, the adverse factors, the qualities [in detail], and the mutual determination — should be known. || Msa_16.1 ||

body.text: saṃkhyāvibhāge ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the division of enumeration:

children.translated_text: Prosperity of enjoyments, personal existence, attendants, and undertakings; higher attainment;
freedom from the power of afflictions; and always non-error in duties — || Msa_16.2 ||

body.text: iti prathamaḥ | tatra catasṛbhiḥ pāramitābhiścaturvidho 'bhyudayaḥ | dānena bhogasaṃpat | śīlenātmabhāvasaṃpat | kṣāntyā paricārasaṃpat | tathā hi tadāsevanādāyatyād[tyāṃ] bahujanasupriyo bhavati | vīryeṇārambhasaṃpat sarvakarmāntasaṃpattitaḥ | pañcamyā kleśāvaśagatvaṃ dhyānena kleśaviṣkambhanāt | ṣaṣṭhyā kṛtyeṣvaviparyāsaḥ sarvakāryayathābhūtaparijñānāt | ityabhyudayaḥ tatra cāsaṃkleśamaviparītakṛtyārambhaṃ cādhikṛtya ṣaṭ pāramitā vyavasthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the first [reason]. Therein, through four <s>pāramitās</s>, there is fourfold higher attainment (<s>abhyudaya</s>): through giving (<s>dāna</s>), prosperity of enjoyments; through moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), prosperity of personal existence; through patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), prosperity of attendants — for indeed, through its cultivation, one becomes well-loved by many people in future [lives]; through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), prosperity of undertakings — because of the accomplishment of all enterprises. Through the fifth [pāramitā], freedom from the power of afflictions — because <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) suppresses the afflictions. Through the sixth, non-error in duties — because of the true knowledge of all tasks as they really are. Thus [the reason of] higher attainment: regarding both freedom from defilement and non-erroneous undertaking of duties, the six <s>pāramitās</s> are established.

children.translated_text: Well-engaged in the welfare of beings, one accomplishes [it] through relinquishment, non-harm, and forbearance of harm;
through causal basis, stability, and liberation, one practices self-interest in every way. || Msa_16.3 ||

body.text: iti dvitīyaḥ | sattvārtheṣu samyakprayukto bodhisattvastisṛbhirdānaśīlakṣāntipāramitābhiryathākramaṃ tyāgenānupaghātenopaghātamarṣaṇena ca sattvārthaṃ kurute | tisṛbhiḥ sanidānatayā [sanidānayā] cittasthityā vimuktyā ca sarvaprakāramātmārthaṃ carati | vīryaṃ niśritya yathākramaṃ dhyānaprajñābhyāsa[ma]samāhitasya cittasya samavadhānāt samāhitasya mocanāt | iti parārthamātmārthaṃ cārabhya ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the second [reason]. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, properly engaged in the welfare of beings, accomplishes the welfare of beings through the three <s>pāramitās</s> of giving, moral discipline, and patience — in order, through relinquishment, non-harm, and forbearance of harm. Through the [other] three, one practices self-interest in every way — through causal basis, stability of mind, and liberation. Relying on vigor, in order: through the settling of an unsettled mind by <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>, and through the liberating of a settled [mind]. Thus, for the purpose of others' welfare and self-interest, [there are] six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: Through non-obstruction, non-harm, forbearance of harm, tirelessness in activity,

children.text: āvarjanaiḥ sulapitaiḥ parārtha ātmārthaṃ etasmāt || Msa_16.4 ||
children.translated_text: winning over [beings], and well-spoken [words] — [there is] the welfare of others [and] self-interest therefrom. || Msa_16.4 ||

body.text: iti tṛtīyaḥ | dānādibhirbodhisattvasya sakalaḥ parārtho bhavati | yathākramaṃ pareṣāmupakaraṇāvidhātaiḥ | aviheṭhaiḥ viheṭhanāmarṣaṇaiḥ | sāhāyya kriyāsvakhedaiḥ ṛddhyādiprabhāvāvarjanaiḥ subhāṣitasulapitaiśca saṃśayacchedanāt | etasmātparārthāt bodhisattvasyātmārtho bhavati | parākāryasvakāryatvānmahābodhiprāptitaśca | iti sakalaparārthādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |

children.translated_text: Intense non-attachment to enjoyments, gravity toward the two [trainings], tirelessness,
and non-conceptual yoga — all of this together constitutes the supreme vehicle. || Msa_16.5 ||

body.translated_text: This is the third [reason]. Through giving and the rest, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s complete welfare of others comes about: in order — through the non-withholding of resources from others; through non-harm and forbearance of harm; through tirelessness in acts of assistance; through winning over by the power of supernatural attainments and the like; and through well-spoken, good words — from the cutting of doubts. From this welfare of others, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s self-interest arises — because the welfare of others is one's own duty, and because of the attainment of great awakening. Thus, because of [encompassing] the complete welfare of others, [there are] six <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.text: iti caturthaḥ | dānena bodhisattvasya bhogeṣvabhi[ṣvanabhi]ratirnirapekṣatvāt | śīlasamādānena bodhisattvaśikṣāsu tīvrā gurutā | kṣāntyā vīryeṇa cākhedo dvaye yathākramaṃ duḥkhe ca sattvāsattvakṛte kuśalaprayoge ca | dhyānaprajñāyāṃ[bhyāṃ] nirvikalpo yogaḥ śamathavipaśyanāsaṃgṛhītaḥ | etāvacca samasta [mahāyānam iti?] mahāyānasaṃgrahādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fourth [reason]. Through giving, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s non-attachment to enjoyments — because of indifference. Through the undertaking of moral discipline, intense gravity toward the trainings of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Through patience and vigor, tirelessness regarding the two, respectively — suffering caused by beings and non-beings, and the wholesome endeavor. Through <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>, non-conceptual yoga, comprised of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). And this much constitutes the totality [of the Mahāyāna] — thus, because of [encompassing] the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s>, [there are] six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: In [freedom from] attachment to sense-objects, another path; in the control of their obtainment and distraction;
in the non-abandoning of beings and their growth; in the purification of obscurations — another. || Msa_16.6 ||

body.text: iti pañcamaḥ | tatra dānaṃ viṣayeṣvasaktimārgastyāgābhyāsena tatsaktivigamāt | śīlaṃ tadāptivikṣepasaṃyameṣu bhikṣusaṃvarasthasya viṣayaprāptaye sarvakarmāntavikṣepāṇāmapravṛtteḥ | kṣāntiḥ sattvānutsarge sarvo[vā]pakāraduḥkhānudvegāt | vīryaṃ kuśalavivardhana ārabdhavīryasya tadbuddhigamanāt | dhyānaṃ prajñā cāvaraṇaviśodhaneṣu mārgastābhyāṃ kleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśodhanāt | mārga ityupāyaḥ | evaṃ sarvākāramārgādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fifth [reason]. Therein, giving is the path to non-attachment to sense-objects — because through the practice of relinquishment, attachment to those is removed. Moral discipline [is the path] to the control of their obtainment and distraction — because for one established in the monastic code (<s>bhikṣusaṃvara</s>), all distracting enterprises for the obtainment of sense-objects do not operate. Patience [is the path] to the non-abandoning of beings — because of non-agitation from the suffering of harm from all [beings]. Vigor [is the path] to the growth of the wholesome — because for one who has initiated vigor, understanding progresses toward that. <s>Dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s> are the path to the purification of obscurations — because through those two, the obscurations of afflictions and the knowable are purified. 'Path' means method. Thus, because of [encompassing] the complete method of the path, [there are] six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.text: śikṣātrayamadhikṛtya ca ṣaṣṭ pāramitā jinaiḥ samākhyātāḥ |
children.translated_text: And with reference to the three trainings, six <s>pāramitās</s> have been declared by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors);
the first three [pertain to] the first [training] in two ways; one [pertains] to each of the latter two. || Msa_16.7 ||

body.text: iti ṣaṣṭhaḥ | tatrādyā adhiśīlaṃ śikṣā tisraḥ pāramitāḥ sasaṃbhārasaparivāragrahaṇāt | dānena hi bhoganirapekṣaḥ śīlaṃ samādatte samāttaṃ ca kṣāntyā rakṣatyākruṣṭāpratyākrośanādibhiḥ | dvidhetyadhicittamadhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣā sā antena dvayena saṃgṛhītā yathākramaṃ dhyānena prajñayā ca | tisṛṣvapi śikṣāsvekā vīryapāramitā veditavyā | sarvāsāṃ vīryasahāyatvāt | lakṣaṇavibhāge ślokāḥ ṣaṭ |
body.translated_text: This is the sixth [reason]. Therein, the first is the training in higher moral discipline (<s>adhiśīla</s>) — three <s>pāramitās</s>, because it includes its accumulations and accompaniments. For through giving, being indifferent to enjoyments, one undertakes moral discipline; and through patience, one protects that which has been undertaken — by not retaliating when insulted, and so forth. 'In two ways' means the trainings in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>) — these are comprised by the latter two, respectively, by <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>. And the one <s>pāramitā</s> — vigor — should be understood as pertaining to all three trainings, because vigor accompanies all of them. Six verses on the division of characteristics:

children.text: dānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Giving is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.8 ||

body.text: bodhisattvānāṃ dānaṃ caturvidhalakṣaṇaṃ | vipakṣahīnaṃ tā[mā]tsaryasya prahīṇatvāt | nirvikalpajñānasahagataṃ dharma nairātmyaprativedhayogāt sarvecchāparipūrakaṃ yo yadicchati tasmai tasya dānāt | sattvaparipācakaṃ tredhā dānena sattvān saṃgṛhya triṣu yāneṣu yathābhavyaniyojanāt |
body.translated_text: The giving of <s>bodhisattvas</s> has a fourfold characteristic: it is free from the adverse factor — because miserliness has been abandoned; accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge — because of penetration of the selflessness of phenomena; it fulfills all wishes — because it gives to each what each desires; and it ripens beings in three ways — because, having gathered beings through giving, it establishes them in the three vehicles according to their capacity.

children.text: śīlaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Moral discipline is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.9 ||
Patience is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.10 ||

children.text: vīryaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Vigor is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.11 ||

children.text: dhyānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Meditation is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.12 ||

children.text: prajñā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Wisdom is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfills all wishes, and ripens beings in three ways. || Msa_16.13 ||

body.text: yathā dānalakṣaṇaṃ caturvidhamevaṃ śīlādīnāṃ veditavyam | eṣāṃ tu vipakṣā dauḥśīlyaṃ krodhaḥ kauśīdyaṃ vikṣepo dauṣprajñyaṃ yathākramaṃ | sarvecchāparipūrakatvaṃ śīlādibhiḥ pareṣāṃ sarvakāyavāksaṃyamāparādhamarṣaṇasāhāyyamanorathasaṃśayacchedanecchāparipūraṇāt | sattvaparipācakatvaṃ śīlādibhirāvarjya triṣu yāneṣu paripācanāt |
body.translated_text: Just as the characteristic of giving is fourfold, so it should be understood for moral discipline and the rest. Their adverse factors, in order, are: bad conduct, anger, laziness, distraction, and poor wisdom. The fulfillment of all wishes through moral discipline and the rest: by [providing] complete restraint of body and speech, forbearance of harm, assistance, [fulfillment of] mental desires, and the cutting of doubts for others, respectively. The ripening of beings through moral discipline and the rest: by winning over [beings] through each, and ripening [them] in the three vehicles.

body.text: anukramavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of sequence:

children.translated_text: Because each succeeding one arises from dependence on the preceding, the teaching is in that order;
also because of the [preceding being] inferior and [the succeeding being] the basis for excellence, and because of [moving from] coarse to subtle. || Msa_16.14 ||

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇaisteṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ krameṇa nirdeśaḥ | pūrvasaṃniśrayeṇottarasyotpatteḥ | bhoganirapekṣo hi śīlaṃ samātte śīlavān kṣamo bhavati kṣamāvān vīryamārabhate ārabdhavīryaḥ samādhimutpādayati samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | pūrvasya ca hīnatvāt uttarasyotkarṣasthānatvāt | hīnaṃ hi dānamutkṛṣṭaṃ śīlamevaṃ yāvaddhīnaṃ dhyānamutkṛṣṭā prajñeti | pūrvasya caudārikatvāduttarasyasūkṣmatvāt | audārikaṃ hi dānaṃ supraveśatvāt sukaratvācca | sūkṣmaṃ jñīlaṃ tato duṣpraveśatvād duṣkaratvācca | evaṃ yāvadaudārikaṃ dhyānaṃ sūkṣmā prajñeti |
body.translated_text: For three reasons, the teaching of giving and the rest is in sequence: because each succeeding one arises from dependence on the preceding — for one indifferent to enjoyments undertakes moral discipline; one who is morally disciplined becomes patient; one who is patient initiates vigor; one who has initiated vigor produces <s>samādhi</s>; and one whose mind is concentrated knows as it truly is. And because the preceding is inferior and the succeeding is the basis for excellence — for giving is inferior, moral discipline is more excellent, and so on until meditation is inferior and wisdom is more excellent. And because the preceding is coarse and the succeeding is subtle — for giving is coarse, because it is easy to enter and easy to do; moral discipline is subtle compared to that, because it is difficult to enter and difficult to do; and so on until meditation is coarse and wisdom is subtle.

body.text: nirvacanavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of etymology:

children.translated_text: From the removal of poverty, from the obtaining of coolness, from the exhaustion of anger,
from yoking to the best, from the holding of the mind within, and from the knowledge of ultimate reality — the names [are derived]. || Msa_16.15 ||

body.text: dāridyamapanayatīti dānaṃ | śaityaṃ lambhayatīti śīlaṃ tadvato viṣayanimittakleśaparidāhābhāvāt | kṣayaḥ kruddheriti kṣāntistayā krodhakṣayāt | vareṇa yojayatīti vīryaṃ kuśaladharmayojanāt | dhārayatyadhyātmaṃ mana iti dhyānaṃ | paramārtha[rthaṃ] jānātyanayeti prajñā |
body.translated_text: <s>Dāna</s> (giving) — because it removes poverty. <s>Śīla</s> (moral discipline) — because it produces coolness, for one who possesses it has no burning from the afflictions caused by sense-objects. <s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) — because it is the exhaustion (<s>kṣaya</s>) of anger (<s>kruddhi</s>), since anger is exhausted by it. <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) — because it yokes to the best (<s>vara</s>), through the yoking to wholesome dharmas. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) — because it holds (<s>dhārayati</s>) the mind within (<s>adhyātma</s>). <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) — because by it one knows (<s>jānāti</s>) the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>).

body.text: bhāvanāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of cultivation:

children.translated_text: The cultivation is spoken of as depending on the support, mental attention, disposition,

children.text: upāyaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ ca sarvāsāmeva kathyate || Msa_16.16 ||
children.translated_text: skillful means, and sovereignty — for all of them. || Msa_16.16 ||

body.text: pañcavidhā pāramitābhāvanā | upadhisaṃniśritā | tatropadhisaṃniśritā caturākārā hetusaṃniśritā yo gotrabalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ | vipākasaṃniśritā ca ātmabhāvasaṃpattibalena | praṇidhānasaṃniśritā yaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānabalena | pratisaṃkhyānasaṃniśratā yaḥ prajñābalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ | manasikārasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā caturākārā | adhimuktimanaskāreṇa sarvapāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ sūtrāntamadhimucyamānasya | āsvādanāmanaskāreṇa labdhāḥ pāramitā āsvādayato guṇasaṃdarśayogena | anumodanāmanaskāreṇa sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ dānādikamanumodamānasya | abhinandanāmanaskāreṇātmanaḥ sattvānāṃ cānāgataṃ pāramitāviśeṣamabhinandamānasya | āśayasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā ṣaḍākārā | atṛptāśayena vipulāśayena muditāśayena upakārāśayena nirlepāśayena kalyāṇāśayena ca | tatra bodhisattvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayo yadbodhisattva ekasattvasyaikakṣaṇe gaṃgānadībālukāsamān lokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇān kṛtvā pratipādayet | gaṃgānadībālikāsamāṃścātmabhāvān | evaṃ ca pratikṣaṇaṃ gaṃgānadīvālikāsamānkalpānpratipādayet | yathā caikasya sattvasyaivaṃ yāvān sattvadhāturanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācayitavyastamanena paryāyeṇa pratipādayet | atṛpta eva bodhisattvasya dānāśaya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayaḥ | na ca bodhisattva evaṃrūpāṃ dānaparaṃparāṃ kṣaṇamātramapi hāpayati | na vicchinattyā bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāditi | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne vipulāśaya iti | muditataraśca bodhisattvo bhavati tānsattvāndānena tathānugṛhṇan | na tveva te satvāstena dānenānugṛhyamāṇā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne muditāśayaḥ | upakārakatarāṃśca sa bodhisattvastānsattvānātmanaḥ samanupaśyati | yeṣāṃ tathā dānenopakaroti nātmānaṃ | teṣāmanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyupastambhatāmupādāya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne upakārāśayaḥ | na ca bodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu tathā vipulamapi dānamayaṃ puṇyamabhisaṃskṛtya pratikāreṇa vā artho[rthī] bhavati vipākena vā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirlepāśayaḥ | yadbodhisattvastathā vipulasyāpi dānaskandhasya vipākaṃ satveṣvabhinandati nātmanaḥ | sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ ca kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ kalyāṇāśayaḥ | tatra bodhisattvasya (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 101

children.text:
) śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāmatṛptāśayaḥ | yadvodhisattvo gaṃgānadībālikāsameṣvātmabhāveṣu gaṃgānadībālikāsamakalpāyuṣpramāṇeṣu sarvopakaraṇanirantaravighātī trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāvagnipratipūrṇe caturvidhamīryāpathaṃ kalpayannekaṃ śīlapāramitākṣaṇaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitākṣaṇaṃ bhāvayedetena paryāyeṇa yāvāṃśchīlaskandho yāvān ca prajñāskandho yenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate śīlaskandhaṃ yāvatprajñāskandhaṃ bhāvayedatṛpta eva bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāmāśayo yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāmāśaya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāmatṛptāśayo yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāmatṛptāśayaḥ | yadbodhisattvastāṃ śīlapāramitābhāvanāparaṃparāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāparaṃparāmābodhimaṇḍaniṣadanānna sraṃsayati na vicchinatti iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ vipulāśayaḥ | children.translated_text: insatiable disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom is as follows: if a <s>bodhisattva</s>, in personal existences as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with lifespans measured in eons as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, constantly afflicted by all adversities in a great trichiliocosm filled with fire, maintaining the four modes of deportment, were to cultivate one moment of the perfection of moral discipline up to one moment of the perfection of wisdom — in this manner, however vast the aggregate of moral discipline up to the aggregate of wisdom by which one fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening, were to cultivate such an aggregate of moral discipline up to an aggregate of wisdom — still the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom would be insatiable. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not let the succession of the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom lapse, does not interrupt it until sitting at the seat of awakening. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vast disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> is exceedingly joyful when thus benefiting beings through the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, not those beings being benefited. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s joyful disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> regards those beings as more beneficial to oneself — those whom one benefits through the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom — not oneself, because of their serving as supports for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s beneficent disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated even such vast merit consisting of the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, neither desires reciprocation nor fruition. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s untainted disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. Therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> rejoices in the fruition of the aggregate of merit consisting of the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom among beings alone, not for oneself; and making it shared by all beings, dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. [Fourth,] the cultivation dependent on skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is threefold: through non-conceptual knowledge, by way of the examination of the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>). For that skillful means serves to accomplish all mental attentions. [Fifth,] the cultivation dependent on sovereignty (<s>vibhutva</s>) is threefold: through sovereignty of body, sovereignty of conduct, and sovereignty of teaching. Therein, sovereignty of body — in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, two bodies should be seen: the natural body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>) and the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>). Sovereignty of conduct — the emanation body (<s>nairmāṇikakāya</s>) should be seen, by which one displays all forms of conduct as companions in Dharma to all beings. Sovereignty of teaching — unobstructedness in the teaching of all aspects of the six <s>pāramitās</s>. On the comprehensive collection of divisions, twelve verses. For each of giving and the rest, there are six meaning-divisions.
MSA_Bagchi 102
The six meanings are: intrinsic nature, cause, fruit, action, yoga, and mode of operation.

body.translated_text: The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> is fivefold. [First,] dependent on the support (<s>upadhi</s>): therein, the support-dependent cultivation is fourfold — dependent on the cause: the practice and cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of one's spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>); dependent on the fruition: through the power of the prosperity of one's personal existence; dependent on aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): through the power of former aspirations; and dependent on analytical reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>): the practice and cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of wisdom. [Second,] the cultivation dependent on mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>) is fourfold: through the mental attention of conviction (<s>adhimuktimanaskāra</s>) — for one who has conviction in the sūtras connected with all <s>pāramitās</s>; through the mental attention of savoring (<s>āsvādanamanaskāra</s>) — for one who savors the attained <s>pāramitās</s> through the method of displaying their qualities; through the mental attention of rejoicing (<s>anumodanāmanaskāra</s>) — for one who rejoices in the giving and the rest of all beings in all world-realms; through the mental attention of delight (<s>abhinandanāmanaskāra</s>) — for one who delights in the future distinction of the <s>pāramitās</s> for oneself and for beings. [Third,] the cultivation dependent on disposition (<s>āśaya</s>) is sixfold: with an insatiable disposition, a vast disposition, a joyful disposition, a beneficent disposition, an untainted disposition, and a wholesome disposition. Therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable disposition regarding giving is as follows: if a <s>bodhisattva</s>, for a single being, at a single moment, were to fill world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges) with the seven precious substances and give them away, and give away personal existences as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and at every moment give thus for eons as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and just as for one being, so for as many beings as constitute the realm of beings to be ripened toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — were to give in this manner — still the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s disposition regarding giving would be insatiable. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable disposition regarding giving. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not let this succession of giving lapse even for a moment, does not interrupt it until sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vast disposition regarding giving. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> is exceedingly joyful when thus benefiting those beings through giving, not those beings being benefited by that giving. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s joyful disposition regarding giving. And that <s>bodhisattva</s> regards those beings as more beneficial to oneself — those to whom one thus gives — not oneself [as the benefactor], because of their serving as supports for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s beneficent disposition regarding giving. And the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated even such vast merit consisting of giving toward beings, neither desires reciprocation nor [craves] fruition. Such a disposition is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s untainted disposition in the cultivation of the perfection of giving. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> rejoices in the fruition of even such a vast aggregate of giving among beings, not for oneself; and making it shared by all beings, dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening. body.text: tatra dānaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the division of giving, two verses:

children.translated_text: The giving away of material things, with volition (<s>cetanā</s>) ascertained as its root;
prosperity of enjoyments and prosperity of personal existence, fulfilling the benefit of both — || Msa_16.17 ||
that [giving], accompanied by non-miserliness, in the visible world [provides] material goods and fearlessness;
having thus understood giving, the wise one should undertake it. || Msa_16.18 ||

body.text: arthapratipādanaṃ pratigrāhakeṣu dānasya svabhāvaḥ | alobhādisahajā cetanā hetuḥ | bhogasaṃpattirātmabhāvasaṃpattiścāyurādisaṃgṛhītā phalaṃ pañcasthānasūtravat | svaparānugraho mahābodhisaṃbhāraparipūriśca karma | amātsaryayogo amatsariṣu vartate | dṛṣṭadharmāmiṣābhayapradānaprabhedena ceti vṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: The giving away of material things to recipients is the intrinsic nature of giving. Volition conjoined with non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>) and the like is the cause. Prosperity of enjoyments and prosperity of personal existence — comprising longevity and the rest — is the fruit, as in the <s>Pañcasthānasūtra</s>. The benefit of self and others, and the fulfillment of the provisions for great awakening, is the action. The yoga of non-miserliness — it operates among those who are not miserly. And its mode of operation is through the division of giving material goods (<s>āmiṣa</s>) and fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>) in the present life.

body.text: śīlaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the division of moral discipline, two verses:

children.translated_text: Having six limbs, culminating in calm, bestowing abode in fortunate destinies,
a foundation, peaceful, fearless, endowed with the accumulation of merit — || Msa_16.19 ||
obtained through convention and through the nature of dharmas, it exists in those established in restraint;
having thus understood moral discipline, the wise one should undertake it. || Msa_16.20 ||

body.text: ṣaḍaṅgamiti svabhāvaḥ | ṣaḍaṅgīti śīlavān viharati yāvatsamādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣviti | śamabhāvāntamiti hetuḥ | nirvāṇābhiprāyeṇa samādānāt | sugatisthitidāyakamiti phalaṃ | śīlena sugatigamanāt | avipratisārādikrameṇa cittasthitilābhācca | pratiṣṭhāśāntanirbhītamiti karma | śīlaṃ hi sarvaguṇānāṃ pratiṣṭhā bhavati | kleśaparidāhaśāntyā ca śāntaṃ | prāṇātipātādipratyayānāṃ ca bhayāvadyavairāṇāmaprasavānnirbhītaṃ | puṇyasaṃbhārasaṃyutamiti yogaḥ sarvakālaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarmasamāva[ca]raṇāt | saṃketadharmatālabdhaṃ saṃvarastheṣu vidyata iti vṛttistatra saṃketalabdhaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ | dharmatāpratilabdhaṃ dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītameṣāsya prabhedavṛttiḥ trividhena prabhedena vartanāt | saṃvarastheṣu vidyata ityācā[dhā]ravṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Having six limbs' is the intrinsic nature. 'Six-limbed' means one lives morally disciplined, up to 'undertaking the training in the training-rules.' 'Culminating in calm' is the cause — because of the undertaking with the intention of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Bestowing abode in fortunate destinies' is the fruit — because through moral discipline one goes to fortunate destinies; and because through the sequence beginning with freedom from remorse, one attains stability of mind. 'A foundation, peaceful, fearless' is the action. For moral discipline serves as the foundation of all qualities. Through the pacification of the burning of afflictions, it is peaceful. And through the non-production of fears, punishments, and enmities that are the results of killing and the like, it is fearless. 'Endowed with the accumulation of merit' is the yoga — because at all times it is engaged through bodily, verbal, and mental action. 'Obtained through convention and through the nature of dharmas, it exists in those established in restraint' is the mode of operation. Therein, obtained through convention is that comprised by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation) restraint. Obtained through the nature of dharmas is that comprised by the restraints of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>). This is its operation through division — because it operates through a threefold division. 'It exists in those established in restraint' is its operation through its locus.

body.text: kṣāntiprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the division of patience, two verses:

children.translated_text: Forbearance, endurance, and understanding — [arising] from compassion, from reliance on the Dharma,
declared to have five benefits, and producing the welfare of both — || Msa_16.21 ||
that [patience], endowed with ascetic power and intensity, is considered threefold among those [who possess it];
having thus understood patience, the wise one should undertake it. || Msa_16.22 ||

body.text: marṣādhivāsajñānamiti trividhāyāḥ kṣānteḥ svabhāvaḥ | apakāramarṣaṇakṣāntermarṣaṇaṃ marṣa iti kṛtvā | duḥkhādhivāsakṣānterdharmanidhyānakṣānteśca yathākramaṃ | kārūṇyāddharmasaṃśrayāditi hetuḥ | dharmasaṃśrayaḥ punaḥ | śīlasamādānaṃ śrutaparyavāptiśca | pañcānuśaṃsamākhyātamiti phalaṃ | yathoktaṃ sūtre | pañcānuśaṃsāḥ kṣāntau | na vairabahulo bhavati | na bhedabahulo bhavati | sukhasaumanasyabahulo bhavati | avipratisārī kālaṃ karoti | kāyasya ca bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate iti | dvayorarthakaraṃ ca taditi marṣādhivāsanamityadhikṛtaṃ idaṃ karma | yathoktam |
body.translated_text: 'Forbearance, endurance, and understanding' is the intrinsic nature of the threefold patience. The forbearance of harm (<s>apakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s>) — 'forbearance' in the sense of enduring. The patient endurance of suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsakṣānti</s>) and the patient acceptance of the contemplation of dharmas (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>), respectively.
