'From compassion, from reliance on the Dharma' is the cause. 'Reliance on the Dharma,' furthermore, [means] the undertaking of moral discipline and the acquisition of learning. 'Declared to have five benefits' is the fruit. As stated in the sūtra: 'Five benefits of patience: one is not full of enmity; one is not full of discord; one is full of happiness and mental ease; one dies without regret; and upon the dissolution of the body, one is reborn among the gods in a fortunate heavenly realm.' 'Producing the welfare of both' — this action refers specifically to forbearance and endurance. As stated:

children.text: dvayorarthaṃ sa kurūte ātmanaśca parasya ca |
children.translated_text: 'One produces the welfare of both — of oneself and of the other —

children.text: yaḥ paraṃ kupitaṃ jñātvā svayaṃ tatropaśāmyati || iti ||
children.translated_text: who, knowing the other to be angry, remains calm in response.'

body.text: tapaḥ prābalyasaṃyuktamiti yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | kṣāntiḥ paramaṃ tapa iti | teṣu tadityādhāravṛttiḥ kṣamiṣu tadvṛtteḥ | trividhaṃ matamiti prabhedavṛttistrividhakṣāntiprabhedena yathoktaṃ prāk |
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with ascetic power and intensity' is the yoga. As stated: 'Patience is the supreme austerity.' 'Among those' is its operation through locus — because it operates among the patient. 'Considered threefold' is its operation through division — through the threefold division of patience, as previously stated.

body.text: vīryaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the division of vigor, two verses:

children.translated_text: Enthusiasm for the wholesome, properly established in faith and aspiration,
and in the growth of qualities beginning with mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), counteracting the afflictions — || Msa_16.23 ||
that [vigor], endowed with qualities of non-attachment and the like, is sevenfold among those [who possess it];
having thus understood vigor, the wise one should undertake it. || Msa_16.24 ||

body.text: utsāhaḥ kuśale samyagiti svabhāvaḥ | kuśala iti tadanyakṛtyotsāhavyudāsātha[rthaṃ] samyagityanyatīrthikamokṣārthotsāhavyudāsārthaṃ | śraddhācchandapratiṣṭhita iti hetuḥ śraddadhāno hyatīva[hyarthiko] vīryamārabhati | smṛtyādiguṇavṛddhāviti phalam | ārabdhavīryasya smṛtisamādhyādiguṇodbhavāt | saṃkleśaprātipakṣika iti karma | yathoktam | ārabdhavīryastu sukhaṃ viharatyavyavakīrṇaḥ pāpakairakuśalairdharmairiti | alobhādiguṇopeta iti yogaḥ | teṣvityārabdhavīryeṣu iyamādhāravṛttiḥ | saptavidha iti prabhedavṛttiḥ | sa punaradhiśīlādi śikṣātraye kāyikaṃ cetasikaṃ ca sātatyena satkṛtya ca yadvīryam |
body.translated_text: Exertion in the wholesome correctly — this is the essential nature. 'In the wholesome' — to exclude exertion in other tasks. 'Correctly' — to exclude exertion for the purpose of liberation according to other religious systems. 'Established in faith and aspiration' — this is the cause, for one who has faith exerts vigor with great dedication. 'In the increase of qualities beginning with mindfulness' — this is the fruit, because of the arising of qualities such as mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, and the like for one who has initiated vigor. 'Being the antidote to defilement' — this is the function. As stated: 'One who has initiated vigor dwells happily, unmixed with evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' 'Endowed with qualities of non-attachment and the rest' — this is the yoga. 'In those' means in those who have initiated vigor — this is the foundational function. 'Sevenfold' — this is the classification function. It is further the vigor that pertains to the threefold training of higher moral discipline and the rest, both physical and mental, with continuity and with respect.

body.text: dhyānaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the classification of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation):

children.translated_text: The stability of the mind internally, established in mindfulness and vigor,
yielding mastery over happy rebirth, supernatural knowledge, and [meditative] states. || Msa_16.25 ||

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ pramukhaṃ teṣu vidyate trividhaśca saḥ |
children.translated_text: It is the foremost among <s>dharmas</s>; it exists in those [who possess it]; and it is threefold —
having thus understood <s>dhyāna</s>, the wise one should cultivate it. || Msa_16.26 ||

body.text: sthitiścetasa adhyātmamiti svabhāvaḥ | smṛtivīryapratiṣṭhitamiti hetuḥ | ālambanāsaṃpramoṣe sati vīryaṃ niśritya samāpattyabhinirhārāt | sukhopapattaye iti phalaṃ dhyānasyāvyābādhopapattiphalatvāt | abhijñāvihāravaśavartakamiti karma | dhyānenābhijñāvaśavartanāt | āryadivyabrāhmavihāravaśavartanācca | dharmāṇāṃ pramukhamiti prāmukhyena yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | samādhipramukhāḥ sarvadharmā iti | teṣu vidyata iti dhyāyiṣviyamādhāravṛttiḥ | triviśca sa iti savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ avitarko vicāramātraḥ | avitarko avicāraḥ | punaḥ prītisahagataḥ | sātasahagataḥ | upekṣāsahagataśca | iyaṃ prabhedavṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The stability of the mind internally' — this is the essential nature. 'Established in mindfulness and vigor' — this is the cause, because, when there is non-forgetfulness of the object, and relying on vigor, one accomplishes the attainments. 'Yielding happy rebirth' — this is the fruit, because <s>dhyāna</s> has as its fruit rebirth free from affliction. 'Yielding mastery over supernatural knowledge and [meditative] states' — this is the function, because through <s>dhyāna</s>, one gains mastery over the supernatural knowledges, and mastery over the noble, divine, and <s>Brahmā</s> abidings. 'The foremost among <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the yoga, in the sense of preeminence. As stated: 'All <s>dharmas</s> have <s>samādhi</s> as foremost.' 'It exists in those' means in those who meditate — this is the foundational function. 'And it is threefold' — this is the classification function: with initial thought and sustained thought, without initial thought but with sustained thought only, and without initial thought and without sustained thought. Again: accompanied by joy, accompanied by bliss, and accompanied by equanimity.

body.text: prajñāprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the classification of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom):

children.translated_text: The correct analysis of knowables, established in mental equipoise,
for the purpose of complete liberation from defilement, with the livelihood of wisdom and excellent teaching. || Msa_16.27 ||
It is the highest among <s>dharmas</s>; it exists in those [who possess it]; and it is threefold —
having thus understood <s>prajñā</s>, the wise one should cultivate it. || Msa_16.28 ||

body.text: samyak pravicayo jñeya iti svabhāvaḥ | samyagiti na mithyā jñeya iti laukikakṛtyasamyakpravicayavyudāsārthaṃ | samādhānapratiṣṭhita iti hetuḥ | samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | yasmātsuvimokṣāya saṃkleśāditi phalaṃ | tena hi saṃkleśātsu vimokṣo bhavati | laukikahīnalokottaramahālokottareṇa pravicayena | prajñājīvasudeśana iti prajñājīvaḥ sudeśanā cāsya karma | tena hyanuttara[raḥ] prajñājīvakānāṃ jīvati | samyag dharmaṃ deśayatīti | dharmāṇāmuttara ityuttaratvena yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | prajñottarāḥ sarvadharmā iti | teṣu vidyate trividhaśca sa iti vṛttiḥ | prājñeṣu vartanāt trividhena ca prabhedena | laukiko hīnalokottaro mahālokottaraśca | uktaḥ pratyekaṃ dīnādīnāṃ ṣaḍarthaprabhedena prabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The correct analysis of knowables' — this is the essential nature. 'Correct' means not false; 'of knowables' — to exclude the correct analysis of worldly tasks. 'Established in mental equipoise' — this is the cause, for one whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are. 'For the purpose of complete liberation from defilement' — this is the fruit, for through it there is complete liberation from defilement — through worldly, inferior supramundane, and great supramundane analysis. 'With the livelihood of wisdom and excellent teaching' — these are its functions: the livelihood of wisdom and excellent teaching. For through it, one lives the unsurpassed livelihood of those who live by wisdom, and teaches the Dharma correctly. 'The highest among <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the yoga, in the sense of being highest. As stated: 'All <s>dharmas</s> have <s>prajñā</s> as highest.' 'It exists in those, and it is threefold' — this is the function: functioning among the wise, and with threefold classification — worldly, inferior supramundane, and great supramundane. The classification of each of giving and the rest through the sixfold division of meaning has been stated.

body.text: saṃgrahavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of comprehensive collection:

children.translated_text: All pure <s>dharmas</s> should be known as [pertaining to] the dispersed, the concentrated, and both,

children.text: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ pāramitābhyāṃ parigṛhītāḥ || Msa_16.29 ||
children.translated_text: each comprehended by two <s>pāramitās</s>. || Msa_16.29 ||

body.text: sarve śuklā dharmā dānādidharmāḥ | tatra vikṣiptā dvābhyāṃ pāramitābhyāṃ saṃgṛhītāḥ prathamābhyāṃ dānasamādānaśīlayorasamāhitatvāt | samāhitā dvābhyāṃ paścimābhyāṃ dhyānayathābhūtaprajñayoḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 105

children.text: ) samāhitatvāt | ubhaye dvābhyāṃ kṣāntivīryābhyāṃ | tayoḥ samāhitāsamāhitatvāt |
children.translated_text: ) because they pertain to the concentrated [state]. Both [dispersed and concentrated] are comprehended by the two — patience and vigor — because those two pertain to both concentrated and non-concentrated [states].

body.translated_text: All pure <s>dharmas</s> are the <s>dharmas</s> of giving and the rest. Therein, the dispersed are comprehended by the first two <s>pāramitās</s> — giving and the undertaking of moral discipline — because they pertain to the non-concentrated [state]. The concentrated are comprehended by the last two — <s>dhyāna</s> and wisdom of things as they truly are — (

body.text: vipakṣavibhāge ślokāḥ ṣaṭ |
body.translated_text: Six verses on the division of adverse factors:

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca dānaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the giving [of <s>bodhisattvas</s>]

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.30 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the giving] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.30 ||

body.text: saptavidhā saktirdānasya vipakṣaḥ | bhogasaktiḥ vilambanasaktiḥ tanmātrasaṃtuṣṭisaktiḥ pakṣapātasaktiḥ[?] pratikārasaktiḥ vipākasaktiḥ | vipakṣasaktistu tadvipakṣalābhānuśayāsamuddhātāt | vikṣepasaktiśca | sa punarvikṣepo dvividhaḥ | manasikāravikṣepaśca hīnayānaspṛhaṇāt | vikalpavikṣepaśca dāyakapratigrāhakadānavikalpanāt | ataḥ saptavidhasaktimuktatvāt saptakṛtvo dānasyāsaktatvamuktam |
body.translated_text: There are seven kinds of attachment that are the adverse factors of giving: attachment to enjoyments, attachment to delay, attachment to mere contentment with that [little giving], attachment to partiality, attachment to reciprocation, attachment to fruition. Attachment to the adverse factor — because the latent tendency to that adverse factor has not been uprooted. And attachment through distraction. That distraction is further twofold: distraction of mental attention — from aspiring to the lesser vehicle; and distraction of conceptualization — from conceptualizing the giver, the recipient, and the gift. Therefore, because it is free from sevenfold attachment, the non-attachment of giving has been stated seven times.

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca śīlaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the moral discipline [of <s>bodhisattvas</s>]

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.31 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the moral discipline] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.31 ||

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā saktikā na kṣāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached — the patience

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.32 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the patience] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.32 ||

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva ca na vīryaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the vigor [of <s>bodhisattvas</s>]

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.33 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the vigor] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.33 ||

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktameva na ca dhyānaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the <s>dhyāna</s> [of <s>bodhisattvas</s>]

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.34 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the <s>dhyāna</s>] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.34 ||

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā saktikā na ca prajñā |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached — the <s>prajñā</s>

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā bodhisattvānām || Msa_16.35 ||
children.translated_text: is not attached, not attached, not attached — [the <s>prajñā</s>] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_16.35 ||

body.text: yathā dānāsaktirūktā evaṃ śīle yāvatprajñāyāṃ veditavyā | atra tu viśeṣabhogasaktiparivartena dauḥśīlyādyāsāktirveditavyā vipakṣasaktistadvipakṣānuśayā samuddhātanāt | vikalpavikṣepaśca yathāyogaṃ trimaṇḍalaparikalpanāt | guṇavibhāge trayoviṃśatiḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the non-attachment of giving has been stated, so it should be understood for moral discipline through to wisdom. But here, the specific [difference]: in place of attachment to enjoyments, attachment to bad conduct and the rest should be understood. Attachment to the adverse factor — because the latent tendency to that adverse factor has not been uprooted. And distraction of conceptualization — from the conceptualization of the triple sphere, as appropriate. Twenty-three verses on the division of qualities:

children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have always given up even their own lives, having met one who is in need,

children.text: kāruṇyātparato na ca pratikṛtirneṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prārthitaṃ |
children.translated_text: out of compassion for others, and no reciprocation is desired, nor is any fruit sought;

children.text: dānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā |
children.translated_text: and by that very giving, all people have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;

children.text: dānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'jñayaṃ sthāpitam || Msa_16.36 ||
children.translated_text: and giving, through the embrace of [non-conceptual] knowledge, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.36 ||

body.text: iti subodhaḥ padārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the meaning of the words is easily understood.

body.text:
āttaṃ buddhasutairyamodyamamayaṃ śīlatrayaṃ sarvadā
svargo nābhimataḥ sametya ca punaḥ saktirna tatrāhitā |

children.text: śīlenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā |
children.translated_text: and by that very moral discipline, all people have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;

children.text: śīlaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || Msa_16.37 ||
children.translated_text: and moral discipline, through the embrace of [non-conceptual] knowledge, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.37 ||

body.translated_text:
The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have always undertaken the threefold moral discipline, consisting of restraint and effort;
heaven is not desired, and having obtained it, no attachment to it is produced;

body.text: trividhaṃ śīlaṃ | saṃgharaśīlaṃ | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ | sattvārthakriyāśīlaṃ ca | ekātmakam[eṣāmekaṃ] yamasvabhāvaṃ | dve udyamasvabhāve |
body.translated_text: The threefold moral discipline is: the moral discipline of restraint (<s>saṃvaraśīla</s>), the moral discipline of accumulating wholesome qualities (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s>), and the moral discipline of benefiting beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s>). One of these has the nature of restraint; the [other] two have the nature of effort.

children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have endured what is extremely difficult to endure, even all the harm from people,
not for the sake of heaven, not from attachment, not from fear, and not in expectation of a favor;
and by that unsurpassed patience, all beings have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;
and patience, through the embrace of [non-conceptual] knowledge, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.38 ||

body.text: iti | jñāntyānuttarayā ceti duḥkhādhivāsanakṣāntyā ca parāpakāramarṣaṇakṣāntyā ca yathākramam |
body.translated_text: 'And by that unsurpassed patience' — that is, the patience of enduring suffering and the patience of forbearing harm from others, in that order.

children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have exerted incomparable vigor, consisting of armor and application,

children.text: hantuṃ kleśagaṇaṃ svato 'pi parata prāptaṃ ca bodhiṃ parāṃ |
children.translated_text: to destroy the host of afflictions, both from oneself and from others, and have attained supreme awakening;

children.text: vīryeṇaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā |
children.translated_text: and by that very vigor, all people have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;

children.text: vīryaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || Msa_16.39 ||
children.translated_text: and vigor, through the embrace of [non-conceptual] knowledge, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.39 ||

body.text: iti | saṃnāhavīryaṃ prayogavīryaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: That is, the vigor of armor and the vigor of application.

children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have accomplished <s>dhyāna</s>, abundant in <s>samādhi</s>, in every way;
having dwelt in the most excellent meditative bliss, out of compassion they have resorted to rebirth in the lower [realms];

children.text: dhyānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā |
children.translated_text: and by that very <s>dhyāna</s>, all people have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;

children.text: dhyānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punarloke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || Msa_16.40 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>dhyāna</s>, through the embrace of [non-conceptual] knowledge, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.40 ||

body.text: iti | samādhibahulamiti anantabodhisattvasamādhisaṃgṛhītam |
body.translated_text: 'Abundant in <s>samādhi</s>' means comprehended by the innumerable <s>samādhis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

children.text: jñātaṃ buddhasutaiḥ satattvamakhilaṃ jñeyaṃ ca yatsarvathā
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have known all reality and all that is knowable, in every way;

children.text: saktirnaiva ca nirvṛttau prajanitā buddhaiḥ[ddheḥ] kutaḥ saṃvṛttau |
children.translated_text: no attachment to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been produced — how much less to conventional [reality];

children.text: jñānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā |
children.translated_text: and by that very knowledge, all people have been planted in the three [types of] awakening;
and knowledge, through the embrace of beings, has been established in the world as imperishable. || Msa_16.41 ||

body.text: iti | satattvaṃ parmārthasaṃgṛhītaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ pudgaladharma nairātmyaṃ | jñeyaṃ ca yatsarvathetyanantasvasaṃketādilakṣaṇabhedabhinnaṃ yadajñe[yajjñe] (yadaparaṃjñeyaṃ) | dānādīnāṃ nirvikalpajñānaparigraheṇākṣayatvaṃ nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pi tadakṣayāt | jñānasya punaḥ sattvaparigraheṇa karuṇayā sattvānāmaparityāgāt | eṣāṃ punaḥ ṣaṇāṃ ślokānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ saptamena ślokena nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Reality' is comprehended by ultimate reality — the general characteristic of the selflessness of persons and phenomena. 'And all that is knowable, in every way' — what is knowable, differentiated by infinite conventional designations and other characteristic distinctions. The imperishability of giving and the rest through the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge [applies] even in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder — because they are imperishable even there. But for knowledge, [imperishability is] through the embrace of beings, through compassion, through not abandoning beings. The summary meaning of these six verses is indicated by the seventh verse:

children.translated_text: Generosity, freedom from self-interest, great purpose, and imperishability —

children.text: dānādīnāṃ samastaṃ hi jñeyaṃ guṇacatuṣṭayam || Msa_16.42 ||
children.translated_text: these should be known as the fourfold quality of giving and the rest, in their entirety. || Msa_16.42 ||

body.text: iti | tatradānādīnāṃ prathamena pādenodāratā paridīpitā | dvitīyena nirāmipatā | tṛtīyena mahārthatā mahataḥ sattvārthasya saṃpādanāt | caturthenākṣayatā ityeṣāṃ guṇacatuṣṭayamebhiḥ ślokairveditavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the generosity of giving and the rest has been illuminated by the first quarter-verse. Freedom from self-interest by the second. Great purpose by the third — because of accomplishing the great welfare of beings. Imperishability by the fourth. Thus, this fourfold quality should be understood through these verses.

children.translated_text: The satisfaction of seeing, filling the wishes, and the longing of the suppliant —

children.text: abhibhavati sa tāṃ dātā kṛpālurādhikyayogena || Msa_16.43 ||
children.translated_text: the giver, being compassionate, surpasses all that through the excess of his engagement. || Msa_16.43 ||

body.text: yācanake hi jane dāyakadarśanāttataśca yathepsitaṃ labdhvā manorathaparipūraṇādyā tuṣṭirūtpadyate | atuṣṭiścādarśanādaparipūraṇācca | āśāstiśca yā taddarśane manorathaparipūraṇe ca | sā bodhisattvasyādhikotpadyate sarvakālaṃ yācanakadarśanāttanmanorathaparipūraṇācca | adarśanādaparipūraṇāccātuṣṭiḥ | ato dātā kṛpālustāṃ sarvamabhibhavatyādhikyayogāt |
body.translated_text: For when the suppliant sees the giver, and then having obtained what is desired, the satisfaction that arises from the fulfillment of wishes; and the dissatisfaction from not seeing [the giver] and from non-fulfillment; and the longing that arises for seeing [the giver] and for the fulfillment of wishes — all that arises to a greater degree in the <s>bodhisattva</s>, at all times, from seeing the suppliant and from fulfilling their wishes, and dissatisfaction from not seeing [them] and from non-fulfillment. Therefore, the giver who is compassionate surpasses all that through the excess of his engagement.

children.translated_text: Lives, enjoyments, and wives — because of the compassion of one who always gives up [these] to beings,

children.text: āmodate nikāmaṃ tadviratiṃ pālayenna katham || Msa_16.44 ||
children.translated_text: one rejoices abundantly — how could one not guard abstinence from [taking] those? || Msa_16.44 ||

body.text: tebhyo viratiṃ tadviratiṃ parakīyebhyaḥ prāṇabhogadārebhyaḥ | etena trividhātkāyaduścaritādviratiśīlaguṇaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: 'Abstinence from those' means abstinence from the lives, enjoyments, and wives belonging to others. By this, he shows the quality of the moral discipline of abstaining from the threefold bodily misconduct.

children.translated_text: Without regard [for oneself], with an equal mind, without fear, giving everything, for the sake of compassion —
how would a noble one speak falsehood to harm others? || Msa_16.45 ||

body.text: etena mṛṣāvādādviratiguṇaṃ darśayati | ātmahetormṛṣāvāda ucyeta kāyajīvitāpekṣayā | parahetorvā priyajanapremnā | bhayena vā rājādibhayāt | āmiṣakiṃcitkahetorvā lābhārthaṃ | bodhisattvaśca svakāyajīvitanirapekṣaḥ | samacittaśca sarvasattveṣvātmasamacittatayā | nirbhayaśca pañcabhayasamatikrāntatvāt | sarvapradaścārthibhyaḥ sarvasattvaparityāgāt | sa kena hetunā mṛṣāvādaṃ brūyāt |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the quality of abstaining from false speech. False speech could be spoken for one's own sake — out of regard for one's body and life; or for others' sake — out of affection for beloved persons; or out of fear — from fear of kings and the like; or for the sake of some material gain — for profit. But the <s>bodhisattva</s> is without regard for his own body and life; has an equal mind toward all beings — through the equality of self with all beings; is without fear — having transcended the five fears; and gives everything to those in need — through the relinquishment of [attachment to] all beings. For what reason then would he speak falsehood?

children.translated_text: One whose desires are well-restrained, who is compassionate, and who is extremely afraid of causing suffering to others —
well-engaged in the discipline of beings, far removed from the threefold fault of speech. || Msa_16.46 ||

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣu samaṃ hitakāmaḥ sa kathaṃ pareṣāṃ mitrabhedārthaṃ paiśunyaṃ kariṣyatīti | sukṛpaśca paraduḥkhāpanayābhiprāyāt | paraduḥkhotpādane cātyarthaṃ bhīrūḥ sa (

children.translated_text: [page reference: MSA_Bagchi 108]

children.text: ) kathaṃ pareṣāṃ duḥkhotpādanārthaṃ parūṣaṃ vakṣyati | sattvānāṃ vinaye samyakprayuktaḥ sa kathaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpaṃ kariṣyati tasmādasau sūvidūre trividhavāgdoṣāt paiśunyātpārūṣyātsaṃbhinnapralāpācca |
children.translated_text: how could he speak harsh words for the purpose of producing suffering in others? Being properly engaged in the discipline of beings — how could he engage in idle talk? Therefore he is far removed from the threefold fault of speech: slander, harsh speech, and idle talk.

body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s>, equally desiring the welfare of all beings — how could he engage in slander for the purpose of dividing the friends of others? And being compassionate, with the intention of removing others' suffering, and being exceedingly timid regarding the production of others' suffering — he

children.translated_text: Giving everything, compassionate, and well-skilled in dependent arising of dharmas —
how could he entertain in his mind affliction of any kind? || Msa_16.47 ||

body.text: abhidhyā vyāpādo mithyādṛṣṭirvā yathākramaṃ | eṣa dauḥśīlyapratipakṣadharmaviśeṣayogācchīlaviśuddhigū[gu?]ṇo bodhisattvānāṃ veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Covetousness, malice, or wrong views, respectively. This distinction in the qualities of the purification of moral discipline, through the special connection with dharmas that are the antidote to misconduct, should be understood for <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

children.translated_text: The perception of benefit, delight in the harmful one, the perception of others' welfare — always in suffering,

children.text: labhate yadā kṛpāluḥ kṣamitavyaṃ ... [kiṃ kutastasya] || Msa_16.48 ||
children.translated_text: when the compassionate one obtains [these] — what is there for him to be patient about, and from what [cause]? || Msa_16.48 ||

body.text: apakāriṇi hi kṣamitavyaṃ bhavati | tatra ca bodhisattva apakārisajñāṃ labhate kṣāntisaṃbhāranimittatvāt duḥkhañca kṣamitavyaṃ bhavati | tatra ca parahitahetubhūte duḥkhe bodhisattvaḥ sadā modaṃ labhate tasya kutaḥ kiṃ kṣamitavyaṃ
body.translated_text: For there is something to be patient about in the harmful one. But therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> obtains the perception of benefit in the harmful one, since he is the occasion for the accumulation of patience. And there is suffering to be patient about. But therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> always obtains delight in suffering that is the cause of others' welfare. What then is there for him to be patient about?

body.text: | yasya nāpakārisaṃjñā pravartate na duḥkhasaṃjñā |
body.translated_text: — for whom neither the perception of a harmful one arises nor the perception of suffering.

children.translated_text: Because of the disappearance of the perception of self and other, because of love for others always greater than for oneself,
because of the practice of what is difficult to do — for the compassionate one, vigor is not difficult. || Msa_16.49 ||

body.text: sakṛpo bodhisattvaḥ | tatra sakṛpe yatparārthaṃ duṣkaracaraṇādvīryaṃ tadduṣkaraṃ ca suduṣkaraṃ ca kathamaduṣkaraṃ | paratra parasaṃjñāpagamāt | svato 'dhikatarācca sarvadā pareṣu snehāt | kathaṃ suduṣkaraṃ | yadevaṃ parasaṃjñāpagataṃ ca svatodhikatarasnehaṃ ca tadvīryam |
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> is compassionate. For the compassionate one, the vigor that consists in the practice of what is difficult to do for the sake of others — that is both difficult and exceedingly difficult. How then is it not difficult? Because of the disappearance of the perception of others [as separate], and because of love for others that is always greater than for oneself. How then is it exceedingly difficult? Because that very vigor is devoid of the perception of others [as separate] and possesses love greater than for oneself.

children.text: alpasukhaṃ hyātmasukhaṃ līnaṃ parihāṇikaṃ kṣayi samohaṃ |
children.translated_text: Of little happiness, self-oriented happiness, contracted, deteriorating, perishable, and deluded —
such is the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) considered for [those of] three [types]; for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, it is the reverse. || Msa_16.50 ||

body.text: alpasukhaṃ dhyānaṃ laukikānāmātmasukhaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ | līnaṃ laukikānāṃ satkāye śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ ca nirvāṇe | parihāṇikaṃ laukikānāṃ kṣayi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nirūpadhiśeṣanirvāṇe tatkṣayāt | samohaṃ sarveṣāṃ yathāyogakliṣṭākliṣṭena mohena | bodhisattvānāṃ punardhyāna bahusukhamātmaparasukhamalīnamaparihāṇikamakṣayyasamohaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Meditation is of little happiness for worldly beings; of self-oriented happiness for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Contracted — for worldly beings in the personal aggregates (<s>satkāya</s>); for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Deteriorating — for worldly beings; perishable — for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), because of the perishing of that. Deluded — for all, through afflicted and non-afflicted delusion as appropriate. But the meditation of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is of much happiness, of happiness for both self and others, uncontracted, non-deteriorating, imperishable, and free from delusion.

children.translated_text: Just as knowledge in darkness by flashes of lightning — so is the knowledge of the three [types];
but like the rays of the sun, the knowledge of the compassionate ones is incomparable. || Msa_16.51 ||

body.text: yathā hastāmoṣaistamasi jñānaṃ parīttaviṣayamapratyakṣamavyaktaṃ ca tathā pṛthagjanānāṃ | yathāvacarake[gahavarake] dīpairjñānaṃ prādeśikaṃ pratyakṣaṃ nātinirmalaṃ tathā śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ ca | yathā dinakarakiraṇairjñānaṃ samantātpratyakṣaṃ sunirmalaṃ ca tathā bodhisattvānāṃ | ata eva tadatulyam |
body.translated_text: Just as knowledge by flashes of lightning in darkness is of limited scope, indirect, and unclear — so is the knowledge of ordinary persons. Just as knowledge by lamps in a room is localized, direct but not very clear — so is the knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as knowledge by the rays of the sun is everywhere, direct, and perfectly clear — so is the knowledge of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore that [knowledge] is incomparable.

children.translated_text: Giving is considered supreme through the basis, the substance, the sign, the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam || Msa_16.52 ||
children.translated_text: the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance. || Msa_16.52 ||

body.text: tatrāśrayo bodhisattvaḥ | vastu āmiṣadānasyādhyātmikaṃ vastu paramam | abhayadānasthāpāyasaṃsārabhītebhyastu tadabhayaṃ | dharmadānasya mahāyānaṃ | nimittaṃ karuṇā | pariṇāmanā tena mahābodhiphalaprārthanā | hetuḥ pūrvadānapāramitābhyāsavāsanā | jñānaṃ nirvikalpaṃ yena trimaṇḍalapariśuddhaṃ dānaṃ dadāti dātṛdeyapratigrāhakrāvikalpanāt | kṣetraṃ pañcavidham | arthī duḥkhito niḥpratisaraṇo duścaritacārī guṇavāṃśca | caturṇāmuttaraṃ kṣetraṃ paraṃ | tadabhāve pañcamaṃ | niśrayastrividho yaṃ niśritya dadāti | adhimuktirmanasikāraḥ samādhiśca | adhimuktiryathā bhāvanāvibhāge 'dhimuktimanaskāra uktaḥ | manaskāro yathā tatraivāsvādanābhinandana[naumodanābhi] manaskāra uktaḥ | samādhirgaganagañjādiryathā tatraiva vibhutvamuktaṃ | evamāśrayādiparasamayo dānaṃ paramaṃ | so 'yaṃ cāpadeśo veditavyaḥ | yaśca dadāti yacca yena ca yasmai ca yataśca yasya ca parigraheṇa yatra ca yāvatprakāraṃ taddānam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the basis is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. The substance — for the gift of material things, the supreme substance is the internal [body]. For the gift of fearlessness — that fearlessness to those frightened by evil destinies and <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the gift of Dharma — the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The sign is compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). The dedication is the aspiration for the fruit of great awakening through that [giving]. The cause is the latent impression from the prior practice of the <s>pāramitā</s> of giving. Knowledge is non-conceptual [knowledge], by which one gives with the purity of the three spheres — from the non-conceptualization of giver, gift, and recipient. The field is fivefold: the needy, the suffering, the unprotected, the wrongdoer, and the virtuous. For the first four, the supreme field is the latter [i.e., the more pitiful]; in their absence, the fifth. The reliance is threefold — that upon which one relies when giving: aspiration, mental attention, and <s>samādhi</s>. Aspiration is as stated in the section on cultivation as the mental attention of aspiration. Mental attention is as stated there as the mental attention of savoring and rejoicing. <s>Samādhi</s> is such as the <s>Gaganagañja</s> and the like, as the power [of meditation] is stated there. Thus, giving that is supreme in basis and the rest [is supreme]. And this designation should be understood: who gives, what [is given], by what [means], to whom, from what [cause], with whose acceptance, where, and in what manner — that is giving.

children.translated_text: Moral discipline is considered supreme through the basis, the substance,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam || Msa_16.53 ||
children.translated_text: the sign, the dedication, the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance. || Msa_16.53 ||
[Patience is considered supreme through the basis, the substance, the sign, the dedication,
the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance.
Vigor is considered supreme through the basis, the substance, the sign, the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca paraṃ matam || Msa_16.54 ||
children.translated_text: the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance. || Msa_16.54 ||
Meditation is considered supreme through the basis, the substance, the sign, the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrāniśrayācca paraṃ matam || Msa_16.55 ||
children.translated_text: the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance. || Msa_16.55 ||
Wisdom is considered supreme through the basis, the substance, the sign, the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrānniśrayācca parā matā || Msa_16.56 ||
children.translated_text: the cause, knowledge, the field, and the reliance. || Msa_16.56 ||]

body.text: śīlasya paramaṃ vastu bodhisattvasaṃvaraḥ | kṣānteḥ prāṇāpahāriṇau hīnadurbalau | vīryasya pāramitābhāvanā tadvipakṣaprahāṇaṃ ca | dhyānasya bodhisattvasamādhayaḥ | prajñāyāstathatā | sarveṣāṃ śīlādīnāṃ kṣetraṃ mahāyānaṃ | śeṣaṃ pūrvabaddheditavyam |
body.translated_text: The supreme substance of moral discipline is the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow (<s>bodhisattvasaṃvara</s>). Of patience — [patience toward] those who are weak and inferior and who take one's life. Of vigor — the cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> and the abandonment of their adversaries. Of meditation — the <s>samādhis</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Of wisdom — <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). The field for all — moral discipline and the rest — is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The rest should be understood as before.

children.translated_text: Even if giving brought happiness to only a single being and caused hardship to oneself for many <s>kalpas</s>,
it would still be dear to <s>bodhisattvas</s> — how much more so when the reverse [is the case]! || Msa_16.57 ||

body.text: yadi bodhisattvānāṃ dānamekasyaiva sattvasya sukhadaṃ syādātmanaśca bahukalpavighātakṛta | tathāpi tatteṣāṃ priyaṃ syātkaruṇāviśeṣātkiṃ punaryadanekasattvasukhaṃ ca bhavatyātmanaśca bahukalpānugrahakṛt |

children.text: yadarthamicchanti dhanāni dehinastadeva dhīrā visṛjanti dehiṣu |
children.translated_text: That for the sake of which embodied beings desire wealth — that very thing the wise ones release to [other] embodied beings;

children.text: śarīrahetordhanamiṣyate janaistadeva dhīraḥ śataśo visṛjyate || Msa_16.58 ||
children.translated_text: wealth is desired by people for the sake of the body — that very [body] the wise one releases a hundredfold. || Msa_16.58 ||

body.translated_text: If the giving of <s>bodhisattvas</s> were to bring happiness to only a single being and cause hardship to oneself for many <s>kalpas</s>, even then it would be dear to them, because of their special compassion. How much more so when it brings happiness to many beings and produces benefit to oneself for many <s>kalpas</s>!

body.text: atra pūrvārdhamuttarārdhe vyākhyātam |
body.translated_text: Here, the first half is explained by the second half.

children.text: śarīramevotsṛjato na duḥkhyate yadā manaḥ kā draviṇe 'vare kathā |
children.translated_text: When the mind does not suffer even while giving up the body itself, what need to speak of inferior possessions?

children.text: tadasya lokottaramiti yanmudaṃ sa tena tattasya taduttaraṃ punaḥ || Msa_16.59 ||
children.translated_text: That this joy of his is supramundane — and furthermore, that [joy] which is superior to that very [supramundane joy]. || Msa_16.59 ||

body.text: atra śarīramevotsṛjato yadā mano na duḥkhyate tadasya lokottaramiti saṃdarśitaṃ | eti yanmudaṃ sa tena duḥkhena tattasya taduttaramiti tasmāllokottarāduttaram |
body.translated_text: Here, 'when the mind does not suffer while giving up the body itself — that [state] of his is supramundane' is demonstrated. 'And furthermore, the joy that he experiences through that suffering — that is superior to that' — therefore superior to the supramundane.

children.translated_text: Even one who is in need does not find satisfaction with desired gifts obtained in the wished-for manner;

children.text: sarvāstidānena yatheha dhīmān tuṣṭiṃ vrajatyarthijanasya tuṣṭyā || Msa_16.60 ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one here attains satisfaction through giving everything — through the satisfaction of the needy person. || Msa_16.60 ||

body.text: iṣṭanikāmalabdhairityabhipretaparyāptalabdhaiḥ | sarvāstidāneneti yāvatsvajīvitadānena |
body.translated_text: 'Desired gifts obtained in the wished-for manner' means those obtained as desired and in full measure. 'Through giving everything' means up to the giving of one's own life.

children.translated_text: One whose enjoyments are complete does not regard oneself as wealthy in the same way a beggar does;
but the wise one, even though destitute from giving everything, regards oneself as wealthy. || Msa_16.61 ||
Even after obtaining very abundant wealth, the needy person does not appreciate
the benefit from the giver, because of [focusing on] the gain;
but having properly satisfied the needy through excellent gifts,
the wise one conceives a great perception of benefit toward them. || Msa_16.62 ||

body.text: karuṇāviśeṣād | gatārthau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Because of the distinction of compassion. The meaning of the [following] verses is clear.

children.translated_text: Embodied beings, freed from grief and sound in form,
take and enjoy the abundant wealth of that one,
just as from a fruit-laden tree of enjoyment on the roadside —
such a tree of abundant enjoyment and generous giving is none other than the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_16.63 ||

body.text: pravisṛtiratibhogaścāsyeti pravisṛtiratibhogī sa ca nānyo bodhisattvādveditavyaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: 'Tree of abundant enjoyment and generous giving' — one who is a tree of abundant enjoyment and generous giving is none other than the <s>bodhisattva</s>. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Vigor should be fully understood through the divisions of preeminence, its cause, action,
kind, basis, and the antidote to the four bonds — thus it has been declared. || Msa_16.64 ||

body.text: ṣaḍvidhena prabhedena vīryaṃ parijñeyaṃ | prādhānyabhedena | tatkāraṇabhedena | [karmabhedena] prakārabhedena | āśrayabhedena | caturvibandhapratipakṣabhedena ca | asyoddeśasyottaraiḥ | ślokairnirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Vigor should be fully understood through sixfold division: by the division of preeminence, by the division of its cause, [by the division of action,] by the division of kind, by the division of basis, and by the division of the antidote to the four bonds. The exposition of this synopsis follows in the subsequent verses.

children.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ śuklagaṇasya madhye tanniśritastasya yato 'nulābhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Vigor is supreme among the host of wholesome [dharmas], since relying on it, one obtains them;

children.text: vīryeṇa sadyaḥ susukho vihāro lokottarā lokagatā ca siddhiḥ || Msa_16.65 ||
children.translated_text: through vigor, there is immediately a most happy dwelling, and both supramundane and worldly accomplishment. || Msa_16.65 ||

body.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ śuklagaṇasya madhye iti sarvakuśaladharmaprādhānyaṃ vīryasya nirdiṣṭaṃ | tanniśritastasya yato 'nulābha iti prādhānyakāraṇaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ | yasmādvīryāśritaḥ sarvakuśaladharmalābhaḥ | vīryeṇa sadyaḥ susukho vihāro lokottarā lokagatā ca siddhiriti karma nirdiṣṭaṃ vīryeṇa hi dṛṣṭadharme paramaḥ sukhavihāraḥ | sarvā ca lokottarā siddhirlaukikī ca kriyate |
body.translated_text: 'Vigor is supreme among the host of wholesome [dharmas]' — the preeminence of vigor among all wholesome dharmas has been declared. 'Since relying on it, one obtains them' — the cause of that preeminence has been declared, since the obtaining of all wholesome dharmas depends on vigor. 'Through vigor, there is immediately a most happy dwelling, and both supramundane and worldly accomplishment' — the action [of vigor] has been declared, for through vigor there is the supreme happy dwelling in this very life, and all supramundane and worldly accomplishment is achieved.

children.translated_text: Through vigor, the desired enjoyments of existence are obtained; through vigor, one attains powerful purification;

children.text: vīryeṇa satkāyamatītya muktā vīryeṇa bodhiṃ paramāṃ vibuddhāḥ || Msa_16.66 ||
children.translated_text: through vigor, having transcended the personal aggregates (<s>satkāya</s>), one is liberated; through vigor, one is awakened to supreme awakening. || Msa_16.66 ||

body.text: iti | paryāyadvāreṇa [paryāyāntareṇa] vīryasya karma nirdiṣṭaṃ | laukikalokottarasiddhibhedāt | tatra prabalā laukikī siddhiranātyantikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, the action of vigor has been declared in another manner, through the division of worldly and supramundane accomplishment. Therein, the powerful [accomplishment] is the worldly accomplishment, because of being non-ultimate.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, vigor is considered [as that of] decline and increase, [as that which is] dominant in liberation, [as that] of the favorable side and the adverse side, [as that which has] entered reality,

children.text: tattve praviṣṭaṃ parivartakaṃ ca vīryaṃ mahārthaṃ ca niruktamanyata || Msa_16.67 ||
children.translated_text: and [as that which] transforms — and vigor is declared as of great purpose by others. || Msa_16.67 ||
First is the armor-vigor, then the vigor of application, properly exerted,
unshrunken, unshakeable, and the vigor of non-complacency — the <s>Buddhas</s> declare all these kinds. || Msa_16.68 ||

body.text: ityeṣa prakārabhedaḥ | tatra hānivivṛddhivīryaṃ samyakprahāṇeṣu [dvayorakuśaladharmahānayeapi?] ca dvayoḥ kuśaladharmābhivṛddhaye | mokṣādhipaṃ vīryamindriyeṣu | mokṣādhipattyārthena yasmādindriyāṇi | pakṣavipakṣaṃ baleṣu vipakṣānavamṛdyārthena yasmādbalāni | tattve praviṣṭaṃ bodhyaṅgeṣu darśanamārge tadvya1sthāpanāt | parivarttakaṃ mārgāṅgeṣu bhāvanāmārge 'ntasyā[tasyā]śrayaparivṛttihetutvāt | (

children.translated_text: [page reference: MSA_Bagchi 112]

children.text: ) mahārthaṃ vīryaṃ pāramitāsvabhāvaṃ svaparārthādhikārāt | saṃnāhavīryaṃ prayogāya saṃnahyataḥ | prayogavīryaṃ tathā prayogataḥ | alīnavīryamudāre 'pyadhigantavye layābhāvataḥ | akṣobhyavīryaṃ śītaloṣṇādibhirduḥkhairavikopanataḥ | asaṃtuṣṭivīryamalpenādhigamenāsaṃtuṣṭitaḥ | ebhireva saṃnāhavīryādibhiḥ sūtre | sthāmavān vīryavānutsāhī dṛḍhaparākramo anikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvityucyate yathākramam |
children.translated_text: The vigor of great purpose has the nature of a <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection), because of the undertaking of self-interest and others' interest. The armor-vigor is that of one who girds oneself for endeavor. The vigor of endeavor is from that very endeavor. The non-sinking vigor is from the absence of languor even when what is to be attained is vast. The unshakeable vigor is from not being disturbed by sufferings such as cold, heat, and the like. The vigor of non-contentment is from not being content with a small measure of attainment. By these very [types] — armor-vigor and so forth — it is said in the sūtra: 'One who is strong, vigorous, enthusiastic, of firm exertion, and who does not lay down the burden regarding wholesome dharmas' — in that order.

body.translated_text: This is the division of kinds. Therein, the vigor of decline and increase is regarding the four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) — for the decline of the two unwholesome dharmas and for the increase of the two wholesome dharmas. The vigor dominant in liberation is regarding the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) — because the faculties serve the purpose of dominance over liberation. The vigor of the favorable side and adverse side is regarding the powers (<s>bala</s>) — because the powers serve the purpose of not being crushed by the adverse side. That which has entered reality is regarding the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), on the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), because of establishing [reality] thereby. That which transforms is regarding the limbs of the path (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), because of being the cause of the final transformation of the basis.

children.translated_text: Inferior, middling, and superior vigor is another [division], depending on those engaged in the three vehicles;
through the connection of contracted, supremely exalted intention and understanding, vigor is considered of small purpose and great purpose. || Msa_16.69 ||

body.text: atrāśrayaprabhedena vīryabhedo nirdiṣṭaḥ | yānatraye prayukto yo janastadāśrayeṇa yathākramaṃ nikṛṣṭamadhyottamaṃ vīryaṃ veditavyaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | līnātyudārāśayabuddhiyogāt | līno hi buddhyāśayo yānadvaye prayuktānāṃ kevalātmārthādhikārāt | atyudāro mahāyāne prayuktānāṃ parārthādhikārāt | ata eva yathākramaṃ vīryaṃ tadalpārthaṃ mahārthamiva[ṣṭam] svārthādhikārācca [svaparārthādhikaraṇatvācca |]
body.translated_text: Here, the division of vigor is indicated by the division of its support. Depending on those engaged in the three vehicles, vigor should be understood as inferior, middling, and superior, respectively. Why? Because of the connection of contracted, supremely exalted intention and understanding. For the intention-understanding of those engaged in the two [lesser] vehicles is contracted, because of the undertaking of self-interest alone. That of those engaged in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is supremely exalted, because of the undertaking of others' interest. For this very reason, vigor is considered of small purpose and great purpose, respectively — because of the undertaking of self-interest and the undertaking of both self-interest and others' interest.

children.translated_text: One who has vigor is not defeated by enjoyments;
one who has vigor is not defeated by afflictions;
one who has vigor is not defeated by weariness;
one who has vigor is not defeated by [meager] attainment. || Msa_16.70 ||

body.text: ityayaṃ caturvibandhapratipakṣabhedaḥ | caturvidho dānādīnāṃ vibandho yena dānādiṣu na pravartate | bhogasaktistadāgrahataḥ | kleśasaktistatparibhogādhyavasānataḥ | khedo dānādiṣu prayogābhiyogaparikhedataḥ | prāptiralpamātradānādisaṃtuṣṭitaḥ | tatpratipakṣabhede naitaccaturvidhaṃ vīryamuktam |
body.translated_text: This is the division of the antidotes to the fourfold obstacle. The fourfold obstacle to giving and the rest is that by which one does not engage in giving and so forth. Attachment to enjoyments — from clinging to them. Attachment to afflictions — from the resolution to indulge in their enjoyment. Weariness — from fatigue in the exertion of effort in giving and the rest. [Contentment with meager] attainment — from contentment with a mere small amount of giving and the rest. In the division of their antidotes, this fourfold vigor is stated.

body.text: anyonyaviniścayavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of mutual determination:

children.translated_text: Through mutual inclusion, through subdivision, through dharmas, and through causes —

children.text: ṣaṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ viniścayaḥ sarvathā jñeyaḥ || Msa_16.71 ||
children.translated_text: the determination of the six <s>pāramitās</s> should be known in every way. || Msa_16.71 ||

body.text: anyonyasaṃgrahato viniścayaḥ | abhayapradānena śīlakṣāntisaṃgraho yasmāttābhyāmabhayaṃ dadāti | dharmadānena dhyānaprajñayoryasmāttābhyāṃ dharmaṃ dadāti | ubhābhyāṃ vīryasya yasmāttenobhayaṃ dadāti | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakeṇa śīlena sarveṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ saṃgrahaḥ | evaṃ kṣāntyādibhiranyonyasaṃgraho yathāyogaṃ yojyaḥ | prabhedato viniścayaḥ | dānaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ dānadānaṃ śīladānaṃ yāvatprajñādānaṃ | parasaṃtāneṣu śīlādiniveśanāt | dharmato viniścayaḥ | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 113

children.text: ) ye sūtrādayo yeṣu dānādiṣvartheṣu saṃdṛśyante | ye ca dānādayo yeṣu sūtrādiṣu dharmeṣu saṃdṛśyante | teṣāṃ parasparaṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ | nimittato viniścayaḥ | dānaṃ śīlādīnāṃ nimittaṃ bhavati | bhoganirapekṣasya śīlādiṣu pravṛtteḥ | śīlamapi dānādīnāṃ | bhikṣusaṃvarasamādānaṃ sarvasvaparigrahatyāgācchīlapratiṣṭhitasya ca kṣāntyādiyogāt | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlasamādānaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ nimittaṃ | evaṃ kṣāntyādīnāmanyonyanimittabhāvo yathā yojyaḥ [yogaṃ] saṃgrahavastuvibhāge sapta ślokāḥ | catvāri saṃgrahavastūni | dānaṃ priyavāditā arthacaryā samānārthatā | tatra |
children.translated_text: Whichever sūtras and the rest are seen concerning whichever meanings of giving and so forth, and whichever [aspects of] giving and the rest are seen in whichever sūtras and other dharmas — their mutual inclusion should be understood. Determination through causes: giving becomes the cause of moral discipline and the rest — because for one indifferent to enjoyments, there is engagement in moral discipline and the rest. Moral discipline also [is the cause] of giving and the rest — because the undertaking of the monastic code (<s>bhikṣusaṃvara</s>) involves the renunciation of all possessions, and because one established in moral discipline engages in patience and the rest. And the undertaking of the moral discipline of encompassing wholesome dharmas is the cause of all — giving and the rest. Likewise, the mutual causal relationship of patience and the rest should be applied accordingly. Seven verses on the division of the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). The four means of attraction are: giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and acting in accord.

body.translated_text: Determination through mutual inclusion: through the giving of fearlessness, moral discipline and patience are included — because through those two one gives fearlessness. Through the giving of Dharma, meditation and wisdom [are included] — because through those two one gives the Dharma. Through both [types of giving], vigor [is included] — because through it one gives both. Through moral discipline, which encompasses wholesome dharmas, all [the rest] — giving and so forth — are included. Likewise, mutual inclusion through patience and the rest should be applied as appropriate. Determination through subdivision: giving is sixfold — the giving of giving, the giving of moral discipline, up to the giving of wisdom — because of establishing moral discipline and the rest in the continua of others. Determination through dharmas:

children.translated_text: Giving equally, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and acting in accord —
this is considered [to consist of] the teaching thereof, undertaking [it], and conforming one's own conduct [to it]. || Msa_16.72 ||

body.text: dānaṃ samamiṣyate yathā pāramitāsu priyākhyānaṃ taddeśanā | arthacaryā tatsamādāpanā tacchabdena pāramitānāṃ grahaṇātpāramitādeśanā pāramitāsamādāpanetyarthaḥ | samānārthatā yatra paraṃ samādāpayati tatra svayamanuvṛttiḥ | kimarthaṃ punaretāni catvāri saṃgrahavastūnīṣyante | eṣa hi pareṣāṃ |
body.translated_text: Giving is considered equal as in the <s>pāramitās</s>. Kind speech is the teaching thereof. Beneficial conduct is causing [others] to undertake it — by the word 'that,' the <s>pāramitās</s> are meant, so the meaning is: the teaching of the <s>pāramitās</s> and causing [others] to undertake the <s>pāramitās</s>. Acting in accord is one's own conformity to that in which one causes others to undertake. For what purpose are these four means of attraction held?

children.translated_text: A means that is beneficent, a means that attracts, a means that sets in motion,
and one that conforms — these should be known from the four means of attraction. || Msa_16.73 ||

body.text: dānamanugrāhaka upāyaḥ | āmiṣadānena kāyikānugrahotpādanāt priyavāditā grāhakaḥ | avyutpannasaṃdigdhārthagrāhaṇāt | arthacaryā pravartakaḥ | kuśale pravartanāt | samānārthatānuvartakaḥ | yathāvāditathākāriṇaṃ hi samādāpakaṃ viditvā yatra kuśale tena pravartitāḥ pare bhavanti tadanuvartante |
body.translated_text: Giving is the beneficent means — because through material giving, bodily well-being is produced. Kind speech is the attracting means — because of the apprehension [of meaning] by those who are uninstructed or doubtful. Beneficial conduct is the means that sets in motion — because of setting [beings] in motion toward the wholesome. Acting in accord is the conforming means — for knowing the instructor to act as he speaks, others become inclined to follow [the path] toward whatever wholesome [activity] he has set them in motion.

children.translated_text: Through the first, one becomes a vessel; through the second, there is conviction;
through the third, practice; and through the fourth, purification. || Msa_16.74 ||

body.text: āmiṣadānena bhājanībhavati dharmasya vidheyatāpatteḥ | priyavāditayā taṃ dharmamadhimucyate tadarthavyutpādanasaṃśayacchedanataḥ | arthacaryayā pratipadyate yathādharmaṃ | samānārthatayā tāṃ pratipattiṃ viśodhayati dīrghakālānuṣṭhānād | idaṃ saṃgrahavastūnāṃ karma |
body.translated_text: Through material giving, one becomes a vessel of the Dharma — because of the attainment of receptivity. Through kind speech, one develops conviction in that Dharma — from the explanation of its meaning and the cutting of doubt. Through beneficial conduct, one practices according to the Dharma. Through acting in accord, one purifies that practice — through long-term observance. This is the function of the means of attraction.

children.translated_text: The fourfold nature of the means of attraction is considered from twofold attraction —
through material and through Dharma; through Dharma also as object. || Msa_16.75 ||

body.text: yadapyanyatsaṃgrahavastudvayamuktaṃ bhagavatā āmiṣasaṃgraho dharmasaṃgrahaśca | tābhyāmetānyeva catvāri saṃgrahavastūni saṃgṛhītāni |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has also spoken of another twofold means of attraction: material attraction and Dharma-attraction. By those two, these very four means of attraction are encompassed.

body.text: āmiṣasaṃgraheṇa prathame | dharmasaṃgraheṇāvaśiṣṭāni | tāni punastrividhena dharmeṇa | ālambanadharmeṇa pratipattidharmeṇa tadviśuddhidharmeṇa ca yathākramam |
body.translated_text: By material attraction, the first [means]. By Dharma-attraction, the remaining ones. And those again [are encompassed] by threefold Dharma: the Dharma as object, the Dharma as practice, and the Dharma as purification of that, respectively.

children.translated_text: The attraction is inferior, middling, and superior; and mostly barren, fruitful,

children.text: abandhyaḥ sarvathā caiva jñeyo hyākārabhedataḥ || Msa_16.76 ||
children.translated_text: and fruitful in every way — this should be known from the division of aspects. || Msa_16.76 ||

body.text: eṣa saṃgrahasya prakārabhedaḥ | tatra hīnamadhyottamaḥ saṃgraho bodhisattvānāṃ yānatrayaprayukteṣu veditavyo yathākramaṃ | prāyeṇa vandhyo 'dhimukticaryābhūmau | prāyeṇābandhyo bhūmipraviṣṭānām | avandhyaḥ sarvathā aṣṭāmyādiṣu bhūmiṣu sattvārthasyāvaśyaṃ saṃpādanāt |
body.translated_text: This is the division of types of attraction. Therein, inferior, middling, and superior attraction of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood with respect to those engaged in the three vehicles, respectively. Mostly barren — on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>). Mostly fruitful — for those who have entered the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>). Fruitful in every way — on the eighth and subsequent stages, because of the certain accomplishment of the welfare of beings.

children.translated_text: This method is relied upon by those engaged in attracting assemblies;
and it is praised as the easy means for the accomplishment of all purposes for all. || Msa_16.77 ||

body.text: ye kecitparṣatkarṣaṇe prayuktāḥ sarvaistairayamevopāyaḥ samāśrito yaduta catvāri saṃgrahavastūni | tathā hi sarvārthasiddhaye sarveṣāṃ sukhaścaiṣa upāyaḥ praśasyate buddhaiḥ |
body.translated_text: All those engaged in attracting assemblies rely upon this very method — namely, the four means of attraction. For it is praised by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the easy means for the accomplishment of all purposes for all.

children.translated_text: Those who have been attracted, those who will be attracted, and those who are being attracted now —

children.text: sarve ta evaṃ tasmācca vartma tatsattvapācane || Msa_16.78 ||
children.translated_text: all are [attracted] thus; therefore this is the path for the ripening of beings. || Msa_16.78 ||

body.text: etena lokatraye 'pi sarvasattvānāṃ paripācane caturṇāṃ saṃgrahavastūnāmekāyanamārgatvaṃ darśayati | anyamārgābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows that the four means of attraction are the one-way path for the ripening of all beings in the three worlds — because there is no other path.

children.translated_text: Thus, one whose understanding is constantly free from attachment to enjoyments, who has reached the far shore of tranquility, effort, and exertion, who is firmly established,

children.text: bhavaviṣayanimittanirvikalpo bhavati sa sattvagaṇasya saṃgṛhītā || Msa_16.79 ||
children.translated_text: who is non-conceptual regarding the signs of existence and sense-objects — such a one becomes the attractor of the multitude of beings. || Msa_16.79 ||

body.text: etena yathoktāsu ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu sthitasya bodhisattvasya saṃgrahavastuprayogaṃ darśayati svaparārthasaṃpādanāt pāramitābhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiśca yathākramam |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the engagement in the means of attraction by a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the six <s>pāramitās</s> as described — through the accomplishment of self-interest and others' interest by the <s>pāramitās</s> and the means of attraction, respectively.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre pāramitādhikāraḥ [ṣoḍaśaḥ] samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixteenth chapter on the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) is completed ||

body.text: saptadaśo 'dhikāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Seventeenth chapter:

body.text: buddhapūjāvibhāge sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the division of worship of the <s>Buddha</s>:

children.translated_text: Worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> is [performed] in their presence and in their absence, with robes and the like,
by one whose mind is deeply serene, for the fulfillment of the two accumulations [of merit and knowledge]. || Msa_17.1 ||
For [ensuring] that one's Buddha-birth be fruitful, through the power of one's <s>praṇidhāna</s> (aspiration),
and through the non-apprehension of the three [spheres] — [thus] is the worship of the <s>Buddha</s> accomplished. || Msa_17.2 ||
Another [worship] is for the ripening of immeasurable beings,
and yet another is from material support and from the mind, from conviction and from the treasury [of aspiration]. || Msa_17.3 ||
Another is from compassion and forbearance, from practice,
and from the apprehension of the real, from awakening, and from liberation — such is its nature. || Msa_17.4 ||

body.text: ityebhiścaturbhiḥ ślokaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus by these four verses:

children.translated_text: Worship is shown from the support, from the substance, from the cause, from the dedication,
from the motive, from knowledge, from the field, and from the basis. || Msa_17.5 ||

body.text: veditavyā | tatrāśrayaḥ samakṣaparokṣā buddhāḥ | vastu cīvarādayaḥ | nimittaṃ pragāḍhaprasādasahagataṃ cittaṃ | pariṇāmanā puṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūraye | heturabandhyo me buddhotpādaḥ syāditi pūrvapraṇidhānaṃ | jñānaṃ nirvikalpaṃ pūjakapūjyapūjānupalambhataḥ | kṣetramaprameyāḥ sattvāḥ | tatparipācanāya taistatprayojatā[nā]t teṣu tadropaṇataḥ | niśraya upadhiścittaṃ ca | tatropadhiṃ niśritya pūjācīvarādibhiścittaṃ niśrityāsvādanānumodanābhinandanamanaskāraiḥ | ta [ya]thoktaiścādhimuktyādibhiryaduta mahāyānadharmādhimuktitaḥ bodhicittotpādataḥ | praṇidhānameva hi nidhānamatroktaṃ ślokavattvā[bandhā]nurodhāt | sattvānukampanataḥ | duṣkaracaryā duḥkhakṣamaṇataḥ pāramitāsamudācārataḥ | yoniśo dharmamanasikārataḥ | sa hyaviparyayastattvādvastvābhogaḥ | samyagdṛṣṭito darśanamārge | sa hi yathābhūtāvabodhādvastvavabodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: This should be understood. Therein, the support is the <s>Buddhas</s>, present and absent. The substance is robes and the like. The cause is the mind accompanied by deep faith. The dedication is for the fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and knowledge. The motive is the previous aspiration that 'may my Buddha-birth be fruitful.' The knowledge is non-conceptual — from the non-apprehension of worshipper, worshipped, and worship. The field is immeasurable beings — for the sake of ripening them, because one motivates them toward that and plants [the seeds] in them. The basis is material support and the mind. Therein, relying on material support, worship is [performed] with robes and the like; relying on the mind, through relishing, rejoicing, appreciation, and mental attention. And through the aforementioned conviction and so forth — namely, from conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma, from the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). Aspiration itself is called 'treasury' here, in accordance with the verse structure. From compassion for beings; from the endurance of difficult practices and suffering; from the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>; from proper mental attention to the Dharma — for that is the non-perverted apprehension of the real, because of its truth; from right view on the path of seeing — for that is the awakening to the real, because of awakening as it truly is.

body.text: vimuktitaḥ kleśavimokṣācchrāvakāṇāṃ | tathātvato mahābodhiprāpterityayaṃ pūjāyāḥ prakārabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: From liberation — from the liberation from afflictions of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers). From its suchness — from the attainment of great awakening. This is the division of types of worship.

children.translated_text: From the cause and from the fruit, through oneself and through others,
and from gain and honor, and [worship] of practice — it is twofold. || Msa_17.6 ||

children.text: parīttā mahatī pūjā samānāmānikā ca sā |
children.translated_text: Small and great worship, that which is equal and unequal in honor,
from endeavor and from destination, and from aspiration — it is so considered. || Msa_17.7 ||

body.text: ityayamarthā[dhvā]dibhedenāparaḥ prakārabhedaḥ | tatrātītā hetuḥ pratyutpannā phalaṃ pratyutpannā heturanāgatā phalamityevaṃ hetuphalato 'tītānāgatapratyutpannā veditavyā | ātmanetyādhyātmikī parairiti bāhyā | lābhasatkārato audārikī | pratipattitaḥ sūkṣmā | parīttā hīnā mahatī praṇītā | punaḥ samānā hīnā nirmānā praṇītā trimaṇḍalāvikalpanāt | kālāntaraprayojyā dūre | tatkālaprayojyāntike | punarvichinnāyāṃ gatau dūre | samanantarāyāmantike | punaryāṃ pūjāmāyatyāṃ prayojayituṃ praṇidadhāti sā dūre yāṃ praṇihitaḥ kartuṃ sāntike | katamā punarbuddhapūjā paramā veditavyetyāha |
body.translated_text: This is another division of types by [distinctions of] time and the like. Therein, the past is the cause, the present is the fruit; the present is the cause, the future is the fruit — thus, from cause and fruit, the past, future, and present should be understood. Through oneself — internal. Through others — external. From gain and honor — gross. From practice — subtle. Small — inferior. Great — exalted. Furthermore, equal means inferior, unequal means exalted — because of the non-conceptualization of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍala</s>). That to be performed at a later time — distant. That to be performed at the present time — near. Furthermore, in an interrupted course — distant. In an immediately subsequent one — near. Furthermore, the worship that one aspires to perform in the future — that is distant; the worship that one has aspired to and now performs — that is near. And what is the supreme worship of the <s>Buddha</s> to be understood? He says:

children.text: buddheṣu pūjā paramā svacittāt dharmādhimuktyāśayato vibhutvāt |
children.translated_text: The supreme worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> is from one's own mind, from conviction in the Dharma, from the vastness of one's intention,
through the embrace of the method of non-conceptualization, and from the establishment in the single task of all. || Msa_17.8 ||

body.text: ityebhiḥ pañcabhirākāraiḥ svacittapūjā buddheṣu paramā veditavyā | yaduta pūjopasaṃhitamahāyānadharmādhimuktitaḥ | āśayato navabhirāśayaiḥ | āsvādanānumodanābhinandanāśayaiḥ | atṛptavipulamuditopakaranirlepakalyāṇāśayaiśca ye pāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ | vibhutvato gaganagañjādisamādhibhiḥ | nirvikalpajñānopāyaparigrahataḥ | sarvamahābodhisattvaikakāryatvapraveśataśca miśropamiśrakāryatvāt |
body.translated_text: Through these five aspects, the supreme worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> from one's own mind should be understood: namely, from conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma accompanied by worship; from disposition — through the nine dispositions of savoring, rejoicing, and delight, and the insatiable, vast, joyful, beneficent, untainted, and wholesome dispositions that were taught regarding the cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s>; from sovereignty — through <s>samādhis</s> such as the <s>Gaganagañja</s> and others; from the embrace of the method of non-conceptual knowledge; and from entering into the single task of all great <s>bodhisattvas</s> — because of the mixed and semi-mixed nature of the task.

body.text: kalyāṇamitrasevāvibhāge sapta ślokāḥ | tatrārdhapañcamaiḥ ślokaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the division of the service of a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitrasevā</s>). Therein, by four and a half verses:

children.translated_text: Service is demonstrated from the support, from the substance, from the motive, from the dedication,
from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the reliance. || Msa_17.9 ||
One should rely on a friend who is disciplined, calm, and pacified, superior in qualities, energetic, rich in scriptural learning,

children.text: prabuddhatatvaṃ vacasābhyupetaṃ kṛpātmakaṃ khedavivarjitaṃ ca || Msa_17.10 ||
children.translated_text: awakened to reality, endowed with eloquence, compassionate in nature, and free from weariness. || Msa_17.10 ||

body.text: ityevaṃguṇamitraṃ sevāyā āśrayaḥ | dāntaṃ śīlayogādindriyadamena | śāntaṃ samādhiyogādadhyātmaṃ cetaḥ śamathena | upaśāntaṃ prayogā[prajñāyogā] (prajñātvā)dupasthitakleśopaśamanataḥ | guṇairadhikaṃ na samaṃ vā nyūnaṃ vā | sodyamaṃ nodasīnaṃ parārthe | āgamāḍhyaṃ nālpaśrutaṃ | prabuddhatatvaṃ tatvādhigamāt | vacasābhyupetaṃ vākkaraṇenopetaṃ | kṛpātmakaṃ nirāmiṣacittatvāt | khedavivarjitaṃ sātatyasatkṛtyadharmadeśanāt |
body.translated_text: Such a friend possessing these qualities is the support of service. 'Disciplined' — through the taming of the faculties by the yoga of moral discipline. 'Calm' — through the calming of the mind within by the yoga of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). 'Pacified' — through the pacification of the manifest afflictions by the yoga of wisdom. 'Superior in qualities' — not equal or inferior. 'Energetic' — not indolent regarding the welfare of others. 'Rich in scriptural learning' — not of little learning. 'Awakened to reality' — from the realization of truth. 'Endowed with eloquence' — possessing the skill of speech. 'Compassionate in nature' — because of having a mind free from [desire for] material goods. 'Free from weariness' — from continuous and respectful teaching of the Dharma.

body.text: satkāralābhaiḥ paricaryayā ca seveta mitraṃ pratipattitaśca |
body.translated_text: One should serve the friend through honor and material offerings, through attendance, and through practice.

body.text: iti | sevāyā[va]stu |
body.translated_text: This is the substance of service.

body.text: dharme tathājñāśaya eva dhīmān mitraṃ pragacchetsamaye nataśca || Msa_17.11 ||
body.translated_text: The wise one should approach the friend with the desire to learn in the Dharma, at the proper time, and with humility. || Msa_17.11 ||

body.text: iti trividhaṃ nimittaṃ | ājñātukāmatā | kālajñatā | nirmānatā ca |
body.translated_text: This is the threefold motive: the desire to understand, knowledge of the right time, and humility.

body.text: satkāralābheṣu gataspṛho 'sau prapattaye taṃ pariṇāmayecca |
body.translated_text: Free from craving for honor and material gain, one should dedicate that [service] to practice.

body.text: iti pariṇāmanā pratipattyarthaṃ sevanānna lābhasatkārārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: This is the dedication — service for the purpose of practice, not for the purpose of material gain and honor.

body.text: yathānuśiṣṭapratipattitaśca saṃrādhayeccittamato 'sya dhīraḥ || Msa_17.12 ||
body.translated_text: The resolute one should then please the mind [of the friend] through practice in accordance with instruction. || Msa_17.12 ||

body.text: iti | yathānuśiṣṭapratipattiḥ sevāhetuḥ | tayā taccittārādhanāt |
body.translated_text: Practice in accordance with instruction is the cause of service — because thereby the mind [of the friend] is pleased.

body.text: yānatraye kauśalametya buddhyā svasyaiva yānasya yateta siddhau |
body.translated_text: Having attained skill in the three vehicles through wisdom, one should strive for the accomplishment of one's own vehicle;

body.text: iti yānatrayakauśalāt jñānaṃ |
body.translated_text: from skill in the three vehicles — this is the knowledge.

body.text: sattvānameyānparipācanāya kṣetrasya śuddhasya ca sādhanāya || Msa_17.13 ||
body.translated_text: for the ripening of immeasurable beings and for the accomplishment of a pure [Buddha-]field. || Msa_17.13 ||

body.text: iti dvividhaṃ kṣetraṃ tatsevāyāḥ | aprameyāśca sattvāḥ pariśuddhaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ | dharmaṃ śrutvā yeṣu pratiṣṭhāpanāt | yatra ca sthitena |
body.translated_text: This is the twofold field of that service: immeasurable beings and the purified <s>Buddha</s>-field — those in whom [beings] are established after hearing the Dharma, and that in which one is stationed.

body.text: dharmeṣu dāyādaguṇena yukto naivāmiṣeṇa pravasetsa mitram |
body.translated_text: Endowed with the quality of being an heir to the Dharma, not to material goods, one should approach that friend.

body.text: iti niśrayaḥ sevāyāḥ | dharmadāyādatāṃ niśritya kalyāṇamitraṃ seveta | nāmiṣadāyādatāṃ | ata ūrdhvamadhyardhena ślokena prakārabhedaḥ sevāyā veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the reliance of service. One should serve a spiritual friend relying on Dharma-inheritance, not on material inheritance. From here onward, by one and a half verses, the division of types of service should be understood.

body.text: hetoḥ phalāddharmamukhānuyānātseveta mitraṃ bahitaśca dhīmān || Msa_17.14 ||
body.translated_text: From the cause, from the fruit, from following the gateway of Dharma, and from the external — the wise one should serve the friend; || Msa_17.14 ||

body.text: śrutaśravāccetasi yogataśca samānanirmānamano 'nuyogāt |
body.translated_text: from hearing and from listening, from the yoga in the mind, and from the pursuit of equal humility of mind.

body.text: hetoḥ phalādityatītādibhedataḥ pūrvavat dharmamukhānuyānātseveta mitraṃ bahitaśca dhīmānityādhyātmikabāhyabhedaḥ | dharmamukhastroto hi dharmamukhānuyānaṃ bahirdhā bahitaḥ śrutaśravāccetasi yogataścetyaudārikasūkṣmabhedaḥ | śravaṇaṃ hyaudārikaṃ cintanabhāvanaṃ sūkṣmaṃṃ | tadeva cetasi yogaḥ | samānanirmānamano 'nuyogāditi hīnapraṇītabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'From the cause and from the fruit' is the division by past and the rest, as before. 'From following the gateway of Dharma, the wise one should serve the friend from the external' — this is the division of internal and external. The stream of the gateway of Dharma is the following of the gateway of Dharma; externally is from the external. 'From hearing and from listening, and from the yoga in the mind' — this is the division of gross and subtle. For hearing is gross; reflection and cultivation are subtle. 'Yoga in the mind' itself is that. 'From the pursuit of equal humility of mind' — this is the division of inferior and excellent.

body.text: gatiprayogapraṇidhānataśca kalyāṇamitraṃ hi bhajeta dhīmān || Msa_17.15 ||
body.translated_text: From the destination, the method, and the aspiration — the wise one should indeed serve a spiritual friend. || Msa_17.15 ||

body.text: iti dūrāntikabhedaḥ pūrvavadyojayitavyaḥ | katamā punaḥ paramā seveti saptamaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the division of distant and near, to be applied as before. Now, what is the supreme service? The seventh verse:

children.translated_text: The supreme service of a good friend is from one's own mind, from conviction in the Dharma, from disposition, through sovereignty,
through the embrace of the method of non-conceptualization, and from establishment in the single task of all. || Msa_17.16 ||

body.text: iti pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: As before.

body.text: apramāṇavibhāge dvādaśaślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Twelve verses on the division of the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>):

children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes (<s>brāhmavihāra</s>), free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
operating with a threefold object, and ripening beings — for the resolute. || Msa_17.17 ||

body.text: brāhmyā vihārāścatvāryapramāṇāni | maitrī karuṇā muditopekṣā ca | te punarbodhisattve caturlakṣaṇā veditavyāḥ | vipakṣahānitaḥ | pratipakṣaviśeṣayogataḥ | vṛttiviśeṣatastrividhālambanavṛttitvāt | tathā hi te sattvālambanā dharmālambanāśca[dharmālambanā anālambanāśca] | karmaviśeṣataśca | sattvaparipācakatvāt | sattvadharmālambanāt | punaḥ katamasmin sattvanikāye dharme vā pravartante | anālambanāśca katamasminnālambane |
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes are the four immeasurables: <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). Furthermore, for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, they should be understood as having a fourfold characteristic: from the absence of the adverse factor; from the conjunction with a special antidote; from the distinctive mode of operation — because of operating with a threefold object; and from the distinctive action — because of ripening beings. The threefold object is: beings, dharmas, and the objectless. In which class of beings, or regarding which dharma, do they operate? And regarding what object are they objectless?

children.text: saukhyārthini duḥkhārte sukhite kliṣṭe ca te pravartante |
children.translated_text: They operate regarding those who desire happiness, those afflicted by suffering, those who are happy, and those who are defiled;

children.text: taddeśite ca dharme tattathatāyāṃ ca dhīrāṇām || Msa_17.18 ||
children.translated_text: and regarding the Dharma taught concerning that, and regarding the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of that — for the resolute. || Msa_17.18 ||

body.text: sattvālambanāḥ sukhārthini yāvat kliṣṭe sattvanikāye pravartante | tathā hi maitrī sattveṣu sukhasaṃyogākārā | karuṇā duḥkhaviyogākārā | muditā sukhaviyogākārā | upekṣāsu vedanāsu teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ niḥkleśatopasaṃhārākārā | dharmālambanāstaddeśite dharme | yatra te vihārā deśitāḥ | anālambanāstattathatāyāṃ | te hyavikalpatvādanālambanā ivetyanālambanāḥ | api khalu |
body.translated_text: With beings as object, they operate regarding the class of beings from those desiring happiness up to those who are defiled. Thus: <s>maitrī</s> toward beings has the aspect of conjoining with happiness. <s>Karuṇā</s> has the aspect of separating from suffering. <s>Muditā</s> has the aspect of [not] separating from happiness. <s>Upekṣā</s> has the aspect of withdrawing those beings from [neutral] feelings toward freedom from affliction. With dharmas as object — regarding the Dharma taught concerning that, [i.e.,] where those abodes were taught. Objectless — regarding the <s>tathatā</s> of that. For being non-conceptual, they are as if objectless, and thus are objectless. Moreover:

children.translated_text: Because of having that <s>tathatā</s> as its meaning, from the attainment of [the] patient acceptance [of non-arising dharmas], from purification,
from twofold action, and from the exhaustion of afflictions — <s>maitrī</s> is objectless. || Msa_17.19 ||

body.text: ebhiścaturbhiḥ kāraṇairanālambanā maitrī veditavyā | tathatālambanatvāt | anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhenāṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau | dhātupuṣṭyā tadviśuddhitaḥ | karmadvayataśca | yā maitrī niṣpandena kāyakarmaṇā [vākkarmaṇā?] ca? saṃgṛhītā kleśakṣayataśca | tathā hi kleśa ālambanamuktaṃ | manomayānāṃ granthānāṃ prahāṇāducchidyate ālambanamiti vacanāt |
