body.translated_text: By these four reasons, objectless <s>maitrī</s> should be understood: because of having <s>tathatā</s> as its object; from the attainment of the patient acceptance of non-arising dharmas (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) on the eighth stage; from the purification [thereof] through the nourishment of the element (<s>dhātupuṣṭi</s>); from twofold action — the <s>maitrī</s> that is comprised of effortless bodily and verbal action; and from the exhaustion of afflictions. For indeed, it is said that the affliction is the released object — from the statement that the object is cut off through the abandonment of the mental fetters.

body.text: te niścalāśca calāśca kṛpaṇairāsvāditā na ca jñeyāḥ |
body.translated_text: They are immovable and movable; [when] savored by the wretched, they should not be known [as such].

body.text: te ca brāhmyā vihārāścaturvidhā veditavyāḥ | tatra calā hānabhāgīyāḥ parihāṇīyatvāt | acalāḥ sthitiviśeṣabhāgīyā aparihāṇīyatvāt | āsvāditāḥ kliṣṭāḥ anāsvāditā akliṣṭāḥ | kṛpaṇairiti sukhalolairanudāracittaiḥ | eṣa brāhmyavihārāṇāṃ hānabhāgīyādiprakārabhedaḥ | teṣu punaḥ |
body.translated_text: And those <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes should be understood as fourfold. Therein, the movable are those on the side of decline — because of being subject to regression. The immovable are those on the side of stability and distinction — because of being not subject to regression. The savored are the afflicted; the unsavored are the unafflicted. 'By the wretched' means by those who are fond of happiness, who have ignoble minds. This is the division of types of the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes into the side of decline and so forth. Regarding those, furthermore:

body.text: acaleṣu bodhisattvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ saktivigateṣu || Msa_17.20 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established in those that are immovable, free from attachment — || Msa_17.20 ||

body.text: na caleṣu nāpyāsvāditeṣu |
body.translated_text: not in the movable nor in the savored.

children.translated_text: Those that are unconcentrated in nature, soft, middling, belonging to a lower stage,

children.text: hīnāśayāḥ samānā hīnāste hyanyathā tvadhikāḥ || Msa_17.21 ||
children.translated_text: of inferior disposition, equal, inferior — but otherwise, they are superior. || Msa_17.21 ||

body.text: eṣa mṛdvadhimātratābhedaḥ | tatra ṣaḍvidhā mṛdukā asamāhitasvabhāvāḥ | sarve samāhitā api | ye mṛdumadhyāḥ | hīnabhūmikā ye 'pi uttarāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimapekṣya | hīnāśayā api | śrāvakādīnāṃ samānā api | ye 'nutpattikadharmakṣāntirahitā hīnāste mṛdukā ityarthaḥ | anyathā tvadhikā iti yathoktaviparyayeṇādhimātratā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: This is the division of soft, middling, and intense. Therein, the soft are sixfold: unconcentrated in nature — even all the concentrated ones; those that are soft and middling; those belonging to a lower stage — in comparison with the higher <s>bodhisattva</s> stages; those of inferior disposition also; those equal to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like also; those lacking the patient acceptance of non-arising dharmas — these are inferior, meaning soft. 'Otherwise, superior' — the intense should be understood by the reverse of what has been stated.

children.translated_text: When the wise one who has dwelt in the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes is born in the realm of desire,
one fulfills the provisions and ripens beings through that. || Msa_17.22 ||
And everywhere one is never separated from the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes, and free from their adverse factor;

children.text: tatpratyayairapi bhṛśairna yāti vikṛtiṃ pramatto 'pi || Msa_17.23 ||
children.translated_text: even with intense conditions for that [adverse factor], one does not undergo deterioration, even when heedless. || Msa_17.23 ||

body.text: hetuphalaliṅgabhedaḥ | tatra brāhmyairvihṛto vihārairiti hetuḥ | kāmiṣu sattveṣu saṃjāyata iti vipākaphalaṃ | saṃbhārānpūrayatyadhipatiphalaṃ | sattvānparipācayatīti puruṣakāraphalaṃ | sarvatra cāvirahito brāhmyairvihārairjāyata iti niṣpandaphalaṃ | rahitaśca tadvipakṣeṇeti visaṃyogaphalaṃ | bhṛśairapi tatpratyayairavikṛtigamanaṃ liṅgaṃ | pramatto 'pītyasaṃmukhībhūte 'pi pratipakṣe | anyeścaturbhiḥ ślokairguṇadoṣabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the division of cause, fruit, and sign. Therein, 'having dwelt in the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes' is the cause. 'Being born among beings of the desire realm' is the ripened fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>). 'Fulfilling the provisions' is the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>). 'Ripening beings' is the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>). 'Everywhere never separated from the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes when born' is the outflow fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>). 'Free from their adverse factor' is the fruit of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). 'Not undergoing deterioration even with intense conditions' is the sign. 'Even when heedless' means even when the antidote has not been brought face to face. By the next four verses, the division of faults and qualities:

children.translated_text: Through ill-will and harmfulness, through aversion, ill-will, and sensual desire,

children.text: yukto hi bodhisattvo bahuvidhamādīnavaṃ spṛśati || Msa_17.24 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>bodhisattva</s>, [if] endowed [with these], incurs faults of many kinds. || Msa_17.24 ||

body.text: iti doṣaḥ | brāhmyavihārābhāve tadvipakṣayogāt | tatra vyāpādādayo maitryādīnāṃ yathākramaṃ vipakṣāḥ | vyāpādakāmarāgāvupekṣāyāḥ | kathaṃ bahuvidhādīnavaṃ spṛśatītyāha |
body.translated_text: These are the faults — in the absence of the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes, from the conjunction with their adverse factors. Therein, ill-will and the rest are the adverse factors of <s>maitrī</s> and the rest in due order. Ill-will and sensual desire are [the adverse factors] of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). How does one incur faults of many kinds? He says:

children.translated_text: Through the afflictions, one harms oneself; one harms beings; one damages moral discipline;
one suffers distress, loss of gain, and is deprived of protection, and [deprived] of the teacher. || Msa_17.25 ||
One becomes the subject of censure, loses fame, and in future lives is born in unfavorable conditions;
one loses both the attained and unattained [wholesome dharmas]; and one experiences great mental suffering. || Msa_17.26 ||

body.text: tatra prathamaistribhiḥ padairātmavyābādhāya cetayate paravyābādhāyobhayavyābādhāyetyetamādīnavaṃ darśayati | savilekhādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ padairdṛṣṭadhārmikamavadyaṃ prasavatīti darśayati | kathaṃ ca prasavati | ātmāsyāpavadate | pare 'pi devatā api | śāstāpyanye 'pi vijñāḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 120

children.text: ) sabrahmacāriṇo dharmatayā vigarhante | digvidikṣu cāsya pāpako 'varṇaśabdaśloko niścaratītyevaṃ savilekho yāvadayaśasvītyeanena yathākramaṃ darśayati | śeṣaistribhiḥ padairyathākramaṃ sāṃparāyikaṃ dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikamavadyaṃ prasavati | tajjaṃ caitasikaṃ duḥkha[khaṃ] daurmanasya prati saṃvedayata ityetadādīnavaṃ darśayati |
children.translated_text: fellow practitioners in accordance with the Dharma also censure. And the evil reputation and ill-repute spread in the cardinal and intermediate directions — thus, from 'distress' up to 'loses fame,' he shows [this] in order. With the remaining three terms, he shows respectively: one produces faults in future lives; one produces faults in both the present and future; and one experiences the mental suffering born of that — namely, dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, with the first three terms, he shows this fault: one intends harm to oneself, harm to others, and harm to both. With the six terms beginning with 'distress,' he shows that one produces faults in the present life. How does one produce them? Oneself condemns oneself. Others also, deities also. The teacher also; other wise persons also,

children.text: ete sarve doṣā maitryādiṣu susthitasya na bhavanti |
children.translated_text: All these faults do not occur for one well-established in <s>maitrī</s> and the rest;

children.text: akliṣṭaḥ saṃsāraṃ sattvārthaṃ no ca saṃtyajati || Msa_17.27 ||
children.translated_text: unafflicted, one does not abandon <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings. || Msa_17.27 ||

body.text: iti | brāhmavihārayoge tri[dvi]vidhaṃ guṇaṃ darśayati | yathoktadoṣābhāvam akliṣṭasya sattvahetoḥ saṃsārāparityāgaṃ |
body.translated_text: He shows the twofold quality in the conjunction with the <s>Brahmā</s>-abodes: the absence of the aforementioned faults, and the non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings while being unafflicted.

children.translated_text: Not even regarding their only children do all beings possess such
a volition of <s>maitrī</s> and the rest toward beings as the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> do. || Msa_17.28 ||

body.text: ityete[na?] ca bodhisattvamaitrādīnāṃ tīvratāṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the intensity of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>maitrī</s> and the rest.

body.text: karūṇāvibhāge tadālambanaprabhedamārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: On the division of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), beginning with the division of its objects, two verses:

children.translated_text: Those who are ablaze, those under the power of enemies, those seized by suffering, those shrouded in darkness,
those who have mounted a difficult path, those bound with great fetters, || Msa_17.29 ||
those overcome by great poison of food, those who are fickle, those who have lost the path,
those who have set out on a wrong path, beings who are weak — toward these one has compassion. || Msa_17.30 ||

body.text: tatra pradīptāḥ kāmarāgeṇa kāmasugvabhaktāḥ | śatruvaśagā mārakṛtāntarāyāḥ kuśale 'prayuktāḥ duḥkhākrāntāḥ duḥkhā[bhi?]bhūtā narakādiṣu | tamovṛtā aurabhrikādayo duścaritaikāntikāḥ | karmavipākasaṃmūḍhatvāt | durgamārgasamārūḍhā aparinirvāṇadharmāṇaḥ saṃsāravartmātyantānupacchedāt | mahābandhanasaṃyutā anyatīrthyāḥ[rthya]mokṣasaṃprasthitā nānākudṛṣṭigāḍhabandhanabaddhatvāt | mahāśanaviṣākrāntalolāḥ samāpattisukhasaktāḥ | teṣāṃ hi tat kliṣṭaṃ samāpattisukhaṃ | yathā mṛṣṭamaśanaṃ viṣākrāntaṃ | tataḥ pracyāvanāt | mārgapraṇaṣṭakā abhimānikā mokṣamārgabhrāntatvāt | utpathaprasthitā hīnayānaprayuktā aniyatāḥ | durbalā aparipūrṇasaṃbhārā bodhisattvāḥ | ityete daśavidhāḥ satvā bodhisattvakaruṇāyā ālambanam |
body.translated_text: Therein: those ablaze — devoted to sense-desire pleasures, burning with the fire of passion. Those under the power of enemies — obstructed by <s>Māra</s>, not engaged in wholesome [activities]. Those overwhelmed by suffering — overcome by suffering in the hells and so forth. Those enveloped in darkness — those devoted exclusively to misconduct, such as butchers and the like — because of their confusion about the ripening of actions. Those who have entered a dangerous path — those of the nature of non-final-<s>nirvāṇa</s>, because of the absolute non-cessation of the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Those bound by great bondage — followers of other religious systems who have set out for liberation, because of being tightly bound by the bondage of various wrong views. Those overcome by great poisoned food — those attached to the bliss of meditative attainments, who are greedy. For their bliss of attainment is defiled, just as delicious food is when pervaded by poison — because of falling from it. Those who have lost the path — those with conceit, because of their confusion about the path of liberation. Those who have set out on a wrong path — those of indeterminate [lineage] engaged in the lesser vehicle. Those who are weak — <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have not completed the accumulations. These tenfold beings are the object of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s compassion.

body.text: pañcaphalasaṃdarśane karuṇāyāḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on showing the five fruits of compassion:

children.translated_text: Removing affliction, being the seed of supreme awakening, bringing happiness, the cause of what is desired,

children.text: svabhāvadaṃ dharmamupāśritasya bodhirna dūre jinātmajasya || Msa_17.31 ||
children.translated_text: and bestowing [its own] nature — awakening is not far for the son of the <s>Jinas</s> who has relied upon that. || Msa_17.31 ||

body.text: tataḥ heṭhāpahatvena tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇādvisaṃyogaphalaṃ darśayati | uttamabodhibījatvenādhipatiphalaṃ | parātmanoryathākramaṃ sukhāvahatāya[pa]katvena puruṣakāraphalaṃ | iṣṭahetutvena vipākaphalaṃ | svabhāvadatvena niṣpandaphalamāyatyāṃ viśiṣṭakaruṇāphaladānāt | evaṃ pañcavidhāṃ karuṇāmāśritya buddhatvamadūre veditavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thereby, through removing affliction — by the abandonment of harm to the opposing factors — he shows the fruit of disconnection. Through being the seed of supreme awakening — the predominant fruit. Through bringing happiness and removing [suffering] to others and oneself respectively — the fruit of human effort. Through being the cause of what is desired — the fruit of fruition. Through bestowing [its own] nature — the fruit of natural outflow, because of giving the fruit of distinguished compassion in the future. Thus, having relied upon the fivefold compassion, Buddhahood should be understood as not far away.

body.text: apratiṣṭhitasaṃsāranirvāṇatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the non-abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>:

children.text: vijñāya saṃsāragataṃ samagraṃ duḥkhātmakaṃ caiva nirātmakaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Having understood all that pertains to <s>saṃsāra</s> as of the nature of suffering and as without self,

children.text: nodvegamāyāti na cāpi doṣaiḥ prabādhyate kāruṇiko 'grabuddhiḥ || Msa_17.32 ||
children.translated_text: the compassionate one of supreme wisdom neither becomes alarmed nor is afflicted by faults. || Msa_17.32 ||

body.text: sarvaṃ saṃsāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ parijñāya bodhisattvo nodvegamāyāti kāruṇikatvāt | na doṣairbādhyate 'grabuddhitvāt | evaṃ nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhito bhavati na saṃsāre yathākramaṃ | saṃsāraparijñāne ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having fully understood all of <s>saṃsāra</s> as it truly is, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not become alarmed, because of being compassionate. Nor is one afflicted by faults, because of being of supreme wisdom. Thus, one is established in <s>nirvāṇa</s> [yet] not in <s>saṃsāra</s>, respectively. A verse on the full understanding of <s>saṃsāra</s>:

children.text: duḥkhātmakaṃ lokamavekṣamāṇo duḥkhāyate vetti ca tadyathāvat |
children.translated_text: Observing the world as of the nature of suffering, one feels compassion and understands it as it truly is,

children.text: tasyābhyupāyaṃ parivarjane ca na khedamāyātyapi vā kṛpāluḥ || Msa_17.33 ||
children.translated_text: and the compassionate one does not become weary regarding the means for its elimination. || Msa_17.33 ||

body.text: duḥkhāyata iti karuṇāyate | vetti ca tadyathāvaditi duḥkhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ tasya ca duḥkhasya parivarjane 'bhyupāyaṃ | vetti yenāsya duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate | etena jānannapi saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ tatparityāgopāyaṃ ca na khedamāpadyate bodhisattvaḥ karuṇāviśeṣāditi pradarśayati |
body.translated_text: 'Feels compassion' means is compassionate. 'Understands it as it truly is' — understands suffering as it truly is, and the means for the elimination of that suffering — that by which this suffering is ceased. By this he demonstrates that even though the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> as it truly is and the means for its abandonment, one does not become weary — because of the special quality of compassion.

body.text: karūṇāprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the classification of compassion:

children.text: kṛpā prakṛtyā pratisaṃkhyayā ca pūrvaṃ tadabhyāsavidhānayogāt |
children.translated_text: Compassion is by nature, by analytical reflection, by the practice of its prior cultivation,

children.text: vipakṣahīnā ca viśuddhilābhāt caturvidheyaṃ karuṇātmakānāṃ || Msa_17.34 ||
children.translated_text: and free from the opposing factor through the attainment of purity — fourfold is this [compassion] of those whose nature is compassion. || Msa_17.34 ||

body.text: seyaṃ yathākramaṃ gotraviśeṣataḥ guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇataḥ | janmāntaraparibhāvanataḥ | vairāgyalābhataśca veditavyāḥ | tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇe sati viśuddhilābhata iti vairāgyalābhataḥ |
body.translated_text: These should be understood respectively as arising from: the distinction of lineage; the examination of qualities and faults; the cultivation over past lives; and the attainment of dispassion — 'through the attainment of purity, being free from the opposing factor' means through the attainment of dispassion, when harm to the opposing factor has been abandoned.

children.text: na sā kṛpā yā na samā sadā vā nādhyāśayādvā pratipattito vā |
children.translated_text: That compassion is not [true] compassion which is not equal, or not constant, or not from superior intention, or not from practice,

children.text: vairāgyato nānupalambhato vā na bodhisattvo hyakṛpastathā yaḥ || Msa_17.35 ||
children.translated_text: or not from dispassion, or not from non-apprehension — for a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is thus without compassion does not exist. || Msa_17.35 ||

body.text: tatra samā sukhitādiṣu yatkiṃcidveditamidamatra duḥkhasyeti viditvā | sadā nirūpadhiśeṣanirvāṇe tadakṣayāt | adhyāśayādbhūmipraviṣṭānāmātmaparasamatāśayalābhāt | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 122

) From practice — through the activity of rescuing from suffering. From dispassion — through the abandonment of harm to the opposing factor. From non-apprehension — through the attainment of patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, equal — toward those who are happy and so forth, knowing 'even here there is this [suffering]' and perceiving it. Constant — because of its imperishability even in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. From superior intention — because of the attainment of the intention of equality of self and other for those who have entered the stages. (

body.text: karuṇāvṛkṣapratibimbake pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the simile of the tree of compassion:

children.translated_text: Compassion, patience, reflection, aspiration, birth, and the ripening of beings —
this great tree of compassion has these as its root and so forth, with flowers, leaves, and fruit at the end. || Msa_17.36 ||

body.text: ityeṣa mūlaskandhaśākhāpatrapuṣpaphalāvasthaḥ karuṇāvṛkṣo veditavyaḥ | etasya karuṇā mūlaṃ | kṣāntiḥ skandhaḥ | sattvārthacintā śākhā | praṇidhānaṃ śobhaneṣu janmasu patrāṇi | śobhanaṃ janma puṣpaṃ | sattvaparipākaḥ phalaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, this tree of compassion should be understood as having the stages of root, trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit. Compassion is its root. Patience is its trunk. Reflection on the welfare of beings is its branches. Aspirations for beautiful births are its leaves. Beautiful birth is its flower. The ripening of beings is its fruit.

children.text: mūlaṃ karuṇā na bhaved duṣkaracaryāsahiṣṇutā na bhavet |
children.translated_text: If compassion were not the root, there would be no tolerance of difficult conduct;
and the wise one, unable to bear suffering, would never reflect on the welfare of beings. || Msa_17.37 ||
And one devoid of the understanding of reflection would not make aspirations for births in wholesome [states];
and one who does not follow through with wholesome birth would never ripen beings. || Msa_17.38 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ pūrvottaraprasavasādharmyātkaruṇādīnāṃ mūlādibhāvaṃ sādhayati |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he establishes the status of root and so forth for compassion and the rest, through the analogy of the successive production of the earlier and the later.

children.translated_text: The watering of the [tree of] compassion is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>); from it, abundant nourishment through the joy of [relieving] suffering;
the growth of the branches, lucid, should be known as [arising] from proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). || Msa_17.39 ||
The shedding and receiving of leaves — the non-interruption of the continuity of aspirations;
from the accomplishment of the twofold condition, the flower is fruitful, and hence the fruit as well. || Msa_17.40 ||

body.text: etābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ vṛkṣamūlasekādisādharmyaṃ karuṇāvṛkṣasya darśayati | karuṇā hi mūlavṛkṣā[mūlamityuktā] | tasyāḥ seko maitrī tayā tadāpyāyanāt | maitracitto hi paraduḥkhena duḥkhāyate | tataśca karuṇodbhava[karuṇāto yad]duḥkhamutpadyate bodhisattvasyasvā[sattvā]rthaprayuktasya tatra saukhyotpādādvipulapuṣṭiḥ kṣāntipuṣṭirityarthaḥ | sā hi skandha ityuktā | skandhaśca vipulaḥ | yoniśomanaskārād bahuvidhā mahāyāne śākhāvṛddhiḥ | cintā hi śākhetyuktā | pūrvāparanirodhotpādakrameṇa praṇidhānasaṃtānasyānucchedāt | parṇatyāgādānasādharmyaṃ praṇīdhānānāṃ veditavyam | ādhyātmikapratyayasiddhitaḥ svasaṃtānaparipākātpuṣpamiva janmābandhyaṃ veditavyam | bāhyapratyayasiddhitaḥ parasaṃtānaparipākāt phalabhūtaḥ sattvaparipāko ['bandhyo?] veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, he shows the similarity of the tree of compassion to the watering of a real tree-root and so forth. For compassion has been called the root. Its watering is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), because it nourishes it. For one who has a loving mind is distressed by the suffering of others. And from the suffering that arises for the <s>bodhisattva</s> engaged in the welfare of beings through compassion, there is abundant nourishment through the production of joy — the nourishment of patience, is the meaning, for that has been called the trunk, and the trunk is abundant. From proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>), the manifold growth of branches in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — for reflection has been called the branches. Because of the non-interruption of the continuity of aspirations, through the sequence of the cessation and arising of earlier and later [aspirations], the analogy of the shedding and receiving of leaves should be understood for the aspirations. From the accomplishment of the internal condition — the ripening of one's own continuum — birth, like a flower, should be understood as fruitful. From the accomplishment of the external condition — the ripening of others' continuums — the ripening of beings, which is the fruit, should be understood as [likewise] fruitful.

body.text: karuṇānuśaṃse ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the benefit of compassion:

children.text: kaḥ kurvīta na karuṇāṃ sattveṣu mahākṛpāguṇakareṣu |
children.translated_text: Who would not practice compassion toward beings, [who are] producers of the quality of great compassion?

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi saukhyamatulaṃ bhavati yadeṣāṃ kṛpājanitaṃ || Msa_17.41 ||
children.translated_text: For even in suffering, the incomparable happiness that is born of their compassion arises for them. || Msa_17.41 ||

body.text: atra mahākaruṇāguṇa uttarārdhena saṃdarśitaḥ | śeṣo gatārthaḥ | karuṇāniḥsaṅgatāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the quality of great compassion has been shown by the second half. The rest is self-evident. A verse on the non-attachment of compassion:

children.text: āviṣṭānāṃ kṛpayā na tiṣṭhati manaḥ śame kṛpālūnāṃ |
children.translated_text: For those pervaded by compassion — the compassionate ones — the mind does not rest in peace;

children.text: kuta eva lokasaukhye svajīvite vā bhavetsnehaḥ || Msa_17.42 ||
children.translated_text: how then could there be attachment to worldly happiness or to one's own life? || Msa_17.42 ||

body.text: sarvasya hi lokasya laukike saukhye svajīvite ca snehaḥ | tatrāpi ca niḥsnehānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sarvaduḥkhopaśame nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhitaṃ manaḥ | bodhisattvānāṃ tu karuṇāviṣṭatvānnirvāṇe 'pi mano na pratiṣṭhitaṃ | kuta eva tayoḥ sneho bhaviṣyati | karuṇāsnehavaiśeṣye trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: For all the world has attachment to worldly happiness and to one's own life. And even for those who are without attachment to these — the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) — the mind rests in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the cessation of all suffering. But for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, because of being pervaded by compassion, the mind does not rest even in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How then would there be attachment to those two? Three verses on the distinction of the affection of compassion:

children.text: sneho na vidyate 'sau yo niravadyo na laukiko yaśca |
children.translated_text: That affection does not exist which is blameless and not worldly;
the affection of compassion among the wise is blameless and transcends the world. || Msa_17.43 ||

body.text: mātāpitṛprabhṛtīnāṃ hi tṛṣṇāmayaḥ snehaḥ sāvadyaḥ | laukikakarūṇāvihāriṇāṃ niravadyo 'pi laukikaḥ | bodhisattvānāṃ tu karūṇāmayaḥ | sneho niravadyaśca laukikātikrāntaśca | kathaṃ ca punarniravadya ityāha |
body.translated_text: For the affection of mothers, fathers, and others, being of the nature of craving, is blameworthy. The [affection] of those who dwell in worldly compassion, though blameless, is worldly. But the affection of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, being of the nature of compassion, is both blameless and transcends the world. And how is it blameless? He says:

children.translated_text: The world is situated in the great flood of suffering and in the great darkness of ignorance —

children.text: uddhartuṃ ya upāyaḥ kathamiva na syātsa niravadyaḥ || Msa_17.44 ||
children.translated_text: how could the means to rescue [it] not be blameless? || Msa_17.44 ||

body.text: duḥkhamahaugha ajñānamahāndhakāre ceti yojyaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | kathaṃ lokātikrānta ityāha |
body.translated_text: 'In the great flood of suffering and the great darkness of ignorance' should be construed together. The rest is self-evident. How does it transcend the world? He says:

children.translated_text: That affection does not exist among the <s>Arhats</s> in the world, nor among the solitary-awakened <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: prāgeva tadanyeṣāṃ kathamiva lokottaro na syāt || Msa_17.45 ||
children.translated_text: much less among others — how could it not be supramundane? || Msa_17.45 ||

body.text: pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ buddhāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: 'Solitary-awakened <s>Buddhas</s>' means <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: trāsābhinandananimittatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the cause of terror and delight:

children.translated_text: The suffering that arises for <s>bodhisattvas</s> through compassion in the absence of [actual] suffering —

children.text: saṃtrāsayati tadādau spṛṣṭaṃ tvabhinandayati gāḍhaṃ || Msa_17.46 ||
children.translated_text: that terrifies in the beginning, but when deeply touched, it brings delight. || Msa_17.46 ||

body.text: duḥkhābhāve iti duḥkhābhāvo nimittaṃ sattveṣu karuṇayā bodhisattvānāṃ yad duḥkhamutpadyate tadādau saṃtrāsayati adhimukticaryābhūmau | ātmaparasamatayā duḥkhasya yathābhūtamaspṛṣṭatvāt | spṛṣṭaṃ tu śuddhādhyāśayabhūmāvabhinandayatyevetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'In the absence of suffering' means the absence of suffering [in oneself] is the cause — the suffering that arises for <s>bodhisattvas</s> through compassion toward beings terrifies in the beginning, on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), because, through the equality of self and other, suffering has not been truly touched. But when truly touched, on the stage of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>), it brings delight — this is the meaning.

body.text: karuṇāduḥkhena sukhābhibhave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the overcoming of all happiness by the suffering of compassion:

children.text: kimataḥ paramāścaryaṃ yad duḥkhaṃ saukhyamabhibhavati sarvaṃ |
children.translated_text: What is more wonderful than this — that suffering overcomes all happiness,

children.text: kṛpayā janitaṃ laukyaṃ yena vimukto api kṛtārthaḥ || Msa_17.47 ||
children.translated_text: born of compassion, worldly [happiness], by which even a liberated one is accomplished? || Msa_17.47 ||

body.text: nāsyata āścaryataraṃ yad duḥkhameva karuṇājanitaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tathā sukhaṃ bhavati | yatsarvaṃ laukikaṃ sukhamabhibhavati | yena sukhena vimuktā arhanto 'pi kṛtārthāḥ prāgevānye |
body.translated_text: There is nothing more wonderful than this: that the very suffering born of compassion for <s>bodhisattvas</s> becomes such happiness that it overcomes all worldly happiness — the happiness by which even the liberated <s>Arhats</s> are accomplished, much less others.

body.text: kṛpākṛtadānānuśaṃse ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the benefit of giving accompanied by compassion:

children.text: kṛpayā sahitaṃ dānaṃ yaddānasukhaṃ karoti dhīrāṇāṃ |
children.translated_text: The happiness that the giving accompanied by compassion produces for the wise —
the [happiness] of the three realms produced by enjoyments does not touch a fraction of that happiness. || Msa_17.48 ||

body.text: yacca traidhātukaṃ sukhamupabhogai kṛtaṃ na tatsukhaṃ tasya sukhasya kalāṃ spṛśatītyayamuttarārdhasyārthaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: The happiness of the three realms produced by enjoyments does not touch a fraction of that happiness — this is the meaning of the second half. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: kṛpayā duḥkhābhyupagame ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the acceptance of suffering through compassion:

children.text: duḥkhamayaṃ saṃsāraṃ yatkṛpayā na tyajati sattvārthaṃ |
children.translated_text: That one does not abandon, through compassion, the <s>saṃsāra</s> that is composed of suffering, for the welfare of beings —
what suffering would those who are compassionate not accept for the benefit of others? || Msa_17.49 ||

body.text: sarvaṃ hi duḥkhaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhe 'ntarbhūtaṃ | tasyābhyupagamāt sarvaṃ duḥkhamabhyupagataṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: For all suffering is included within the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. By accepting that, all suffering is accepted.

body.text: tatra tatphalavṛddhau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the growth of its fruits therein:

children.translated_text: Compassion, giving, and enjoyments — for the compassionate one, these always increase;
and from this, the happiness born of affection, benefit, and their capacity [arises]. || Msa_17.50 ||

body.text: trayaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajanmasu vardhate karūṇāyogāt | karūṇā tadabhyāsāt | dānaṃ karuṇāvaśāt | bhogāśca dānavaśāt | tasmācca trayātphalaṃ trividhaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati | snehajanitaṃ karuṇātaḥ | sattvānugrahajanitaṃ dānāt | tadanugrahakriyāśaktikṛtaṃ bhogebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Three things increase for <s>bodhisattvas</s> in all births through the practice of compassion: compassion — through its repeated cultivation; giving — through the force of compassion; and enjoyments — through the force of giving. And from this threefold [increase], a threefold happiness, which is the fruit, arises: born of affection — from compassion; born of benefiting beings — from giving; and produced by the capacity for that beneficent activity — from enjoyments.

body.text: dānaprotsāhanāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the encouragement to give:

children.text: vardhe ca vardhayāmi ca dāne paripācayāmi sukhayāmi |
children.translated_text: 'I increase and cause increase, in giving I ripen and make happy,

children.text: ākarṣāmi nayāmi ca karuṇā sannānpravadatīva || Msa_17.51 ||
children.translated_text: I attract and lead' — compassion speaks thus, as it were, to those devoted [to it]. || Msa_17.51 ||

body.text: dāne sannāniti saṃbandhanīyaṃ | ṣaḍbhirguṇairdānai 'vasannān bodhisattvānkaruṇā protsahayatīva | svabhāvavṛddhyā | bhogaistadvardhanayā | dānena sattvaparipācanayā | dātuśca sukhotpādanāt | mahābodhisaṃbhārasyānyasyā[saṃbhārasyā]karṣaṇāt | mahābodhisamīpanayanācca |
body.translated_text: 'Devoted to giving' should be construed. Through six qualities, compassion encourages, as it were, <s>bodhisattvas</s> devoted to giving: through the growth of its own nature; through the increase of enjoyments by it; through the ripening of beings by giving; and through the production of happiness for the giver; through the attraction of the other accumulations of great awakening; and through leading near to great awakening.

body.text: parasaukhyena sukhā[nu?]bhave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the experience of happiness through the happiness of others:

children.text: duḥkhe duḥkhī kṛpayā sukhānyanādhāya kena sukhitaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: Suffering in suffering through compassion, not placing [emphasis on] one's own happiness — by what then would one be happy?
one makes oneself happy by establishing the happiness of others through compassion. || Msa_17.52 ||

body.text: karuṇayā bodhisattvaḥ paraduḥkhairduḥkhitaḥ sattveṣvanādhāya sukhaṃ kathaṃ sukhitaḥ syāt | tasmātpareṣu sukhamādhāya bodhisatva ātmānameva sukhayatīti veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Since the <s>bodhisattva</s>, pained by the suffering of others through compassion, cannot be happy without establishing happiness among beings — therefore it should be understood that by establishing happiness in others, the <s>bodhisattva</s> makes oneself happy.

body.text: kṛpayā dānasamanuśāstau ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: On the instruction regarding giving through compassion, six verses:

children.text: svaṃ dānaṃ kāruṇikaḥ śāstīva sadaiva niḥsvasukhakāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The compassionate one instructs regarding one's own giving, always desiring the happiness of the destitute, as follows:

children.text: bhogaiḥ sukhaya paraṃ vā māmapyayutasaukhyam || Msa_17.53 ||
children.translated_text: 'Make the other happy with enjoyments, or [give] even me, whose happiness is inseparable [from theirs].' || Msa_17.53 ||

body.text: na hi kāruṇikasya vinā parasukhenāsti sukhaṃ | tasyāyutasaukhyatvādvaudhisattvastena vinā[tma?]no dānasya phalaṃ sukhaṃ necchati |
body.translated_text: For the compassionate one, there is no happiness without the happiness of others, since [the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s] happiness is inseparable [from others']. The <s>bodhisattva</s> does not desire the fruit of giving — namely happiness — without that [others' happiness].

children.text: saphalaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ tanme sattveṣu tatsukhasukhena |
children.translated_text: 'The giving I have given is fruitful in beings; through the happiness of their happiness,

children.text: phala teṣveva nikāmaṃ yadi me kartavyatā te 'sti || Msa_17.54 ||
children.translated_text: may it bear fruit in them abundantly, if I have any duty [toward them].' || Msa_17.54 ||

body.text: dānaṃ dadatā dānaṃ ca dānaphalaṃ ca tanmayā sattveṣu dattaṃ | tatsukhameva me sukhaṃ yasmāt | atasteṣveva yāvatphalitavyaṃ tāvatphaleti loṭ | bodhisattvaḥ karūṇayā dānamanuśāsti |
body.translated_text: 'The giving I gave — both the giving and its fruit — I have given to beings. Their happiness alone is my happiness.' Therefore, 'may it bear fruit in them for as long as it should bear fruit' — [this is an] optative. The <s>bodhisattva</s> instructs regarding giving through compassion.

children.translated_text: 'For the giver who is averse to enjoyments, enjoyments approach in greater abundance and beauty;

children.text: na hi tatsukhaṃ mataṃ me dāne pāraṃparo 'smi yataḥ || Msa_17.55 ||
children.translated_text: yet that is not regarded as happiness by me, since I am devoted to the continuation of giving.' || Msa_17.55 ||

body.text: bhogavimukhasya dāturbhogā bahutarāścopatiṣṭhante | śobhanatarāśca | dharma taiveyaṃ cittasyodārataratvāt | na hi tatsukhaṃ mataṃ me yad bhogāstathopatiṣṭhante | yasmādahaṃ dāne pāraṃparastatprabandhakāmatvānnasukhe |
body.translated_text: For the giver who is averse to enjoyments, enjoyments present themselves in greater abundance and greater beauty. This is the very nature of dharmas, because the mind is more generous. 'Yet that is not regarded as happiness by me' — the fact that enjoyments so present themselves — 'since I am devoted to the continuation of giving, not to happiness.'

children.translated_text: '[O giving,] in that you compassionately watch over me constantly when I relinquish everything,

children.text: nanu te tena jñeyaṃ na matphalenārthitāsyeti || Msa_17.56 ||
children.translated_text: know this well from that: I have no desire for your fruit.' || Msa_17.56 ||

body.text: yo 'haṃ dānaphalaṃ sarvameva karuṇayā nityaṃ parityajāmi nanvata eva veditavyaṃ nāsti me dānaphalenārthitvamiti bodhisattvo dānaṃ samanuśāsti |
body.translated_text: 'I who constantly relinquish all the fruit of giving through compassion — from that very fact, it should be understood that I have no desire for the fruit of giving.' The <s>bodhisattva</s> instructs regarding giving.

body.text: dānābhirato na syāṃ prāptaṃ cettatphalaṃ na visṛjeyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'I would not delight in giving if I were to attain its fruit and not release it;

body.text: tathā hi |
body.translated_text: for indeed,

body.text: kṣaṇamapi dānena vinā dānābhirato bhavati naiva || Msa_17.57 ||
body.translated_text: one who delights in giving is never for even a moment without giving.' || Msa_17.57 ||

body.text: iti gatārthaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The verse is self-explanatory.

body.text: akṛtaṃ na phalasi yasmātpratikārāpekṣayā na me tulyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Since you do not bear fruit without action, you are not my equal in the expectation of reciprocation;

body.text: yastvā karoti tasya tvaṃ phalasi | tasmāttvaṃ pratikārapekṣayā na mattulyam |
body.translated_text: but you bear fruit for one who acts toward you — therefore, regarding the expectation of reciprocation, you are not my equal.

body.text: tathā hyahaṃ |
body.translated_text: For indeed, I

body.text: pratikāranirvyapekṣaḥ paratra phalado 'sya kāmaṃ te || Msa_17.58 ||
body.translated_text: am without any expectation of reciprocation, [yet] in the next world I am the giver of fruit — let this be as you wish.' || Msa_17.58 ||

body.text: gatārthametat |
body.translated_text: This is self-explanatory.

children.translated_text: Two verses on giving through compassion:

children.text: niravadyaṃ śuddhapadaṃ hitāvahaṃ caiva sānurakṣaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Blameless, of pure standing, beneficial, and with protection,
unsolicited, and untainted — such is the giving of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, [born] from compassion. || Msa_17.59 ||

body.text: tatra niravadyaṃ paramanupahṛtya dānāt | śuddhapadaṃ kalpikavasu[vastu]dānāt | viṣaśasramadyādivivarjanataḥ | hitāvahaṃ dānena saṃgṛhya kuśale niyojanāt | sānurakṣaṃ parijanasyāvighātaṃ kṛtvā anyasmai dānāt | nirmṛgyamayācamāne 'pyarthitvaṃ vighātaṃ vāvagamya svayameva dānāt dakṣiṇīyāparimārgaṇācca | nirlepaṃ pratikāravipākaniḥspṛhatvāt | aparaḥ prakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, blameless — because of giving without harming others. Of pure standing — because of giving permissible goods, through the avoidance of poison, weapons, intoxicants, and the like. Beneficial — because through giving, one gathers [beings] and establishes them in the wholesome. With protection — because of giving to another after having ensured no harm to one's retinue. Unsolicited — because of giving of one's own accord upon understanding the need or distress of one who does not ask, and also because of not seeking out worthy recipients. Untainted — because of being free from desire for reciprocation and fruition. Another mode:

children.text: sakalaṃ vipulaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ satataṃ muditaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ śuddhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Complete, vast, excellent, constant, joyful, free from material motivation, pure,
devoted to awakening, devoted to the wholesome — such is the giving of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, [born] from compassion. || Msa_17.60 ||

body.text: tatra sakalamādhyātmikabāhyavastudānāt | vipulaṃ prabhūtavastudānāt | śreṣṭhaṃ praṇītavastudānāt | satatamabhīkṣṇadānāt | mudītamapratisaṃkhyāya prahṛṣṭadānāt | nirāmiṣaṃ yathā nirlepaṃ | śuddhaṃ yathā śuddhapadaṃ | bodhinataṃ mahābodhipariṇāmanāt | kuśalanataṃ yathā hitāvahaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, complete — because of giving both internal and external goods. Vast — because of giving abundant goods. Excellent — because of giving superior goods. Constant — because of giving frequently. Joyful — because of giving joyfully without calculation. Free from material motivation — as [explained] regarding 'untainted.' Pure — as [explained] regarding 'of pure standing.' Devoted to awakening — because of dedication toward great awakening. Devoted to the wholesome — as [explained] regarding 'beneficial.'

body.text: upabhoagaviśeṣe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the distinction of enjoyment:

children.text: na tathopabhogatuṣṭiṃ labhate bhogī yathā parityāgāt |
children.translated_text: The enjoyer does not obtain as much satisfaction from enjoyment as
the compassionate one obtains from relinquishment, whose mind is nourished by the triple happiness. || Msa_17.61 ||

body.text: tatra sukhatrayaṃ dānaprītiḥ parānugrahaprītiḥ bodhisaṃbhārasaṃbharaṇaprītiśca | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the triple happiness is: the joy of giving, the joy of benefiting others, and the joy of accumulating the provisions for awakening. The rest is self-explanatory.

body.text: pāramitābhinirhārakaruṇāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the compassion that brings about the <s>pāramitās</s>:

children.translated_text: Compassion toward the wretched, compassion toward the violent, compassion toward the agitated, compassion toward the heedless,
compassion toward those enslaved to sense-objects, and compassion toward those who cling to wrong views. || Msa_17.62 ||

body.text: tatra kṛpaṇā matsariṇaḥ | raudrā duḥśīlāḥ paropatāpinaḥ | saṃkṣubdhāḥ krodhanāḥ | pramattāḥ kuśīdāḥ | viṣayaparatantrā kāmeṣu vikṣiptacittāḥ | mithyābhiniviṣṭāḥ duḥprajñāḥ tīrthikādayaḥ | eṣu pāramitāvipakṣadharmāvasthiteṣu yā karuṇā sā kṛpaṇādikaruṇā | sā ca tadvipakṣavidūṣaṇātpāramitābhinirhārāya saṃpadyate | tasmātpāramitābhinirhārakaruṇetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the wretched are the miserly. The violent are those of bad conduct who harm others. The agitated are the wrathful. The heedless are the indolent. Those enslaved to sense-objects are those with distracted minds toward sense-pleasures. Those who cling to wrong views are the unwise — sectarians and the like. The compassion toward those established in the dharmas that are the adverse factors of the <s>pāramitās</s> is the compassion toward the wretched and the rest. And that [compassion] leads to the bringing about of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the removal of their adverse factors. Therefore it is called 'the compassion that brings about the <s>pāramitās</s>.'

body.text: karuṇāpratyayasaṃdarśane ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on showing the conditions of compassion:

children.translated_text: Compassion of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — from happiness, from suffering, and from what follows from those;
compassion of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — from the cause, from the friend, and from its own nature. || Msa_17.63 ||

body.text: tatra pūrvārdhenālambanapratyayaṃ karuṇāyāḥ saṃdarśayati | trividhāṃ vedanāmālambya tisṛbhirduḥkhatābhiḥ karuṇāyanāt | aduḥkhāsukhā hi vedanā sukhaduḥkhayoranvayaḥ punastadāvāhanāt | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 127

With the second half, he shows the causal condition (<s>hetu</s>), dominant condition (<s>adhipati</s>), and immediately antecedent condition (<s>samanantara</s>) of compassion through [its] cause, friend, and intrinsic nature, respectively.

body.translated_text: Therein, with the first half, he shows the object-condition of compassion — because compassion arises toward the three types of feeling, through the three kinds of suffering (<s>duḥkhatā</s>). The feeling of neither-pleasure-nor-pain follows from [both] pleasure and pain, because it brings them about again.

body.text: mahākaruṇatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the greatness of compassion:

children.translated_text: The compassion of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be known as equal, from that [special] disposition,
from practice, from dispassion, from non-apprehension, and from purification. || Msa_17.64 ||

body.text: tatra samā trividhavedanāvastheṣu yatkiṃcidveditamidamatra duḥkhasyeti viditvā | sā punarāśayato 'pi cittena karuṇāyanāt | pratipattito 'pi tatparitrāṇāt | virāgato 'pi tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇāt | anupalambhato 'pyātmaparakaruṇānupalambhāt | viśuddhito 'pyaṣṭabhyāṃ bhūmāvanutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'equal' — toward those in the three states of feeling, knowing that 'whatever is felt here is suffering.' Furthermore, [it is great] from disposition — because of generating compassion through the mind; from practice — because of rescuing those [beings]; from dispassion — because of the abandonment of harm toward the adverse factor [of compassion]; from non-apprehension — because of the non-apprehension of self, other, and compassion; from purification — because of the attainment of the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) on the eighth stage.

children.translated_text: The foremost among the cultivations of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest: from one's own mind, from dharmas, from conviction,
from disposition also, from sovereignty, from non-conceptualization, and from unity. || Msa_17.65 ||

body.text: iti | pūrvanirdeśānusāreṇārtho 'nugantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The meaning should be followed according to the previous exposition.

children.translated_text: Thus, one who has generated supreme faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), who worships with great offerings and firm devotion,
who constantly serves a spiritual friend of many qualities and benevolence, and who has compassion for the world — attains all accomplishments. || Msa_17.66 ||

body.text: etena yathoktānāṃ pūjāsevāpramāṇānāmanukramaṃ guṇaṃ ca samāsena saṃdarśayati | mahopadhibhirdhruvaṃ satkriyā[yayā] cātyarthaṃ pūjanānmahadupadhidhruvasatkriyābhipūjī veditavyaḥ | satkriyā punaḥ samyakpratipattirveditavyā | evaṃ [lābha?]satkārapratipattipūjī bhavati | bahuguṇaṃ mitraṃ tadanyairguṇaiḥ | hitamanukampakatvena veditavyaṃ | eti sarvasiddhimiti svaparārthasiddhiṃ prāpnotīti |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows in order and in summary the qualities of the worship, service, and immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) as previously stated. 'With great offerings and firm devotion, worshipping intensely' — one should be understood as a worshipper with great offerings, firm practice, and worship. 'Firm practice,' furthermore, should be understood as correct practice. Thus one becomes a worshipper through acquisition, honor, and practice. 'A friend of many qualities' — possessing the other qualities. 'Benevolent' should be understood through [the quality of] compassion. 'Attains all accomplishments' means attains the accomplishment of the welfare of self and others.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre pūjāsevāpramāṇādhikāraḥ [saptadaśaḥ] samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the seventeenth chapter on worship, service, and the immeasurables (<s>pūjāsevāpramāṇādhikāra</s>) is completed ||

body.text: aṣṭādaśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Eighteenth chapter:

body.text: lajjāvibhāge ṣoḍaśaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Sixteen verses on the division of moral conscience (<s>lajjā</s>):

children.text: lajjā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Moral conscience (<s>lajjā</s>) is free from the adverse factor, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
having as its domain what is blameworthy and inferior, and ripening beings — for the resolute. || Msa_18.1 ||

body.text: etena svabhāvasahāyālambanakarmasaṃpadā caturvidhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bodhisattvalajjāyāḥ saṃdarśitaṃ | hīnānavadyaviṣayā | śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ [yānaṃ?] tadvi[ddhi]hīnaṃ ca mahāyānādanavadyaṃ ca | tena ca bodhisattvo lajjate | kathaṃ sattvānāṃ pācikā | tasyāmeva lajjā[yāṃ] paraprasthāpanāt |
body.translated_text: By this, the fourfold characteristic of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s moral conscience is shown through the perfection of intrinsic nature, accompaniment, object, and action. 'Having as its domain what is blameworthy and inferior' — the vehicle of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> is inferior compared to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, yet blameless. And the <s>bodhisattva</s> feels conscience regarding that. How does it ripen beings? By directing others toward that very [sense of] moral conscience.

body.text:
ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ vipakṣe vṛddhyā bodhisattvānāṃ |
pratipakṣe hānitaścāpyatīva saṃpadyate lajjā |
body.translated_text:
Through the increase of the adverse factors of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the decrease of their antidotes,
moral conscience is produced exceedingly in <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bṛddhyā parihānitaśca lajjā [?] pāramitāviṣakṣavṛddhyā tatpratipakṣaparihāṇyā cātyarthaṃ lajjotpādanāt |
body.translated_text: This is the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' moral conscience regarding increase and decrease — exceedingly producing moral conscience from the increase of the adverse factors of the <s>pāramitās</s> and the decrease of their antidotes.

children.translated_text: Moral conscience arises from laziness in cultivating the six <s>pāramitās</s>,
and also from engaging in dharmas that favor the afflictions — for the resolute. || Msa_18.2 ||

body.text: iyamaprayoga[prayoga?]lajjā pāramitābhāvanāyāmaprayogena | kleśānukūleṣu dharmeṣvindriyāguptadvāratvādiṣu ca prayogena lajjotpādanāt |
body.translated_text: This is the moral conscience of [non-]engagement — from non-engagement in the cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s>, and from engagement in dharmas that favor the afflictions such as not guarding the doors of the faculties and the like — moral conscience is produced.

children.translated_text: Moral conscience that is unconcentrated in nature, soft, middling, belonging to a lower stage,

children.text: hīnāśayā samānā hīnā hi tadanyathā tvadhikā || Msa_18.3 ||
children.translated_text: of inferior disposition, equal, inferior — but otherwise, it is superior. || Msa_18.3 ||

body.text: iyaṃ mṛdvadhimātrā lajjā | pūrvanirdeśānusāreṇāsya ślokasyārtho 'nugantavyaḥ | ataḥ paraṃ caturbhistribhiśca ślokairyathākramaṃ lajjāvipakṣe lajjāyāṃ ca doṣaguṇabhedaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: This is the moral conscience that is soft, middling, and intense. The meaning of this verse should be followed according to the previous exposition. From here onward, with four verses and three verses respectively, he shows the division of faults and qualities in the adverse [state] and in moral conscience:

children.translated_text: The wise one without moral conscience tolerates afflictions through improper mental attention;
one who harbors aversion and indifference harms beings and [violates] moral discipline. || Msa_18.4 ||

body.text: ityatra ātmavyābādhāya cetayate paravyābādhāyobhayavyābādhāya ceti saṃdarśitam | ayoniśata ityayoniśo manaskāreṇa | kathamupekṣayā sattvānupahanti | sattvārthapramādataḥ |
body.translated_text: Herein it is shown: one intends harm to oneself, harm to others, and harm to both. 'Through improper mental attention' — through improper mental engagement. How does one harm beings through indifference? Through heedlessness regarding the welfare of beings.

children.translated_text: From remorse, one becomes distressed; one suffers a loss of honor;
one is disregarded by assemblies of the faithful and the teacher. || Msa_18.5 ||

body.text:
sahadhārmi kairjinasutairvinindyate lokato 'yaśo labhate |
dṛṣṭe dharme
body.translated_text: One is blamed by fellow practitioners, the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>; in the world, one gains ill-repute;

body.text: ityanena dṛṣṭadhārmikamavadyaṃ prasavatīti darśitaṃ | yathākramamātmaparadevatāśāstṛbhirapavadanāt | vijñaiḥ sabrahmacāribhirdharmatayā vigarhaṇāt | digvidikṣu ca pāpakāvarṇaniścaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: by this, it is shown that one produces faults in the present life — through being condemned by self, others, deities, and the teacher, respectively; through being censured by the wise and fellow practitioners in accordance with the Dharma; and through the spread of evil reputation in the [cardinal and] intermediate directions.

body.text: 'nyatra kṣaṇarahito jāyate bhūyaḥ || Msa_18.6 ||
body.translated_text: in another [life], one is born deprived of [favorable] opportunities. || Msa_18.6 ||

body.text: ityanena sāṃparāyikamavadyaṃ prasavatīti saṃdarśitamakṣaṇeṣūpapatteḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, it is shown that one produces faults in future lives — from rebirth in unfavorable conditions.

body.text: prāptāprāptavihāniṃ śuklairdharmaiḥ samāpnute tena |
body.translated_text: One incurs the loss of both attained and unattained wholesome dharmas through that;

body.text: ityanena dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikamavadyaṃ prasavatīti saṃdarśitaṃ | prāptakuśaladharmaparihāṇitaḥ | aprāptaparihāṇitaśca yathākramam |
body.translated_text: by this, it is shown that one produces faults in both the present and future lives — from the loss of attained wholesome dharmas and from the loss of those not yet attained, respectively.

body.text: duḥkhaṃ viharati tasmānmanaso 'pyasvasthatāmeti || Msa_18.7 ||
body.translated_text: one dwells in suffering; therefore one's mind also reaches a state of unease. || Msa_18.7 ||

body.text: ityanena tajjaṃ caitasikaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyaṃ pratisaṃvedayata iti saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: By this, it is shown that one experiences the mental suffering born of that — namely, dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

body.text: ete sarve doṣā hīmatsu bhavanti no jinasuteṣu |
body.translated_text: All these faults occur in those without moral conscience, not in the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>;

body.text: ityata upādāya lajjāguṇo veditavyaḥ | yadete ca doṣā na bhavanti |
body.translated_text: from this point onward, the quality of moral conscience should be understood — namely, that these faults do not occur.

body.text: deveṣu ca manujeṣu ca nityaṃ saṃjāyate ca budhaḥ || Msa_18.8 ||
body.translated_text: and among gods and humans, one is constantly born wise. || Msa_18.8 ||

body.text: ityetadasya vipākaphalaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: This is the ripened fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>) of that [moral conscience].

body.text: saṃbhārāṃśca sa bodheḥ kṣipraṃ pūrayati lajjayā dhīmān |
body.translated_text: The wise one with moral conscience swiftly fulfills the provisions for awakening;

body.text: ityetadadhipatiphalaṃ |
body.translated_text: this is the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>).

body.text: sattvānāṃ pācanayā na khidyate caiva jinaputraḥ || Msa_18.9 ||
body.translated_text: and the son of the <s>Jinas</s> is never weary in the ripening of beings. || Msa_18.9 ||

body.text: ityetatpuruṣakāraphalam |
body.translated_text: This is the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>).

body.text: sa vipakṣapratipakṣai rahito 'rahitaśca jāyate satataṃ |
body.translated_text: One is constantly born free from the adverse factors and endowed with the antidotes;

body.text: ityete visaṃyoganiṣpandaphale | yaduta vipakṣarahitatvaṃ pratipakṣārahitatvaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: these are the fruits of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>) and outflow (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) — namely, being free from adverse factors and being endowed with antidotes.

body.text: ityetamānuśaṃsaṃ hīmānāpnoti jinaputraḥ || Msa_18.10 ||
body.translated_text: The son of the <s>Jinas</s> who possesses moral conscience attains these benefits. || Msa_18.10 ||

body.text: iti yathoktadoṣābhāvaṃ guṇayogaṃ ca prāpnotīti saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: Thus it is shown that one attains the absence of the aforementioned faults and the conjunction of qualities.

children.translated_text: For the foolish one, stained by faults, who lacks moral conscience, even though well-covered with fine garments —
the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, even though unclothed, is clothed in moral conscience, free from the stain of faults. || Msa_18.11 ||

body.text: etena vasraviśeṣaṇaṃ hriyaḥ | tadanyavasraprāvṛtasyāpi hrīrahitasya doṣamalinatvāt | nagnasyāpi na hrīmato nirmalatvāt | ākāśamiva na lipto hrīyukto jinasuto bhavati dharmaiḥ | dharmairiti lokadharmaiḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, [moral conscience is shown as] the distinguishing garment — because even one covered with other garments, if lacking moral conscience, is stained with faults; while even one who is naked, if possessing moral conscience, is pure. Like space, the son of the <s>Jinas</s> who possesses moral conscience is not stained by <s>dharmas</s> — 'by <s>dharmas</s>' means by worldly conditions.

body.text: hībhūṣitaśca śobhati saṃparkagato jinasutānām || Msa_18.12 ||
body.translated_text: And adorned with moral conscience, one shines in the company of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_18.12 ||

body.text: etena ślokena hriya ākāśabhūṣaṇasamatāṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this verse, he shows the equality of moral conscience with the adornment of space.

body.text: māturiva vatsalatvaṃ hriyo vineyeṣu bodhisatvānāṃ |
body.translated_text: The affection of moral conscience toward those to be trained is like a mother's [affection] toward her child, for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>,

body.text: trātavyasattvopekṣāyā lajjanāt |
body.translated_text: through the shame of neglecting beings who are to be rescued.

body.text: ārakṣā cāpi hrīḥ saṃsaratāṃ sarvadoṣebhyaḥ || Msa_18.13 ||
body.translated_text: And moral conscience is also the protection of those in <s>saṃsāra</s> from all faults. || Msa_18.13 ||

body.text: hastyaśvakāyādibhūtatvāt | ebhirvastrādidṛṣṭāntairvihāre kleśapratipakṣatāṃ cāre lokadharmapratipakṣatāṃ | sahadhārmikasaṃvāsānukūlatāṃ | sattvāparipākānukūlatām | akliṣṭasaṃsārānukūlatāṃ ca hriyo darśayati |
body.translated_text: Because it has the nature of elephants, horses, and bodily [protection]. By these similes of garment and so forth, he shows: in abiding, the nature of being the antidote to afflictions; in conduct, the nature of being the antidote to worldly conditions; the conduciveness to dwelling with fellow practitioners; the conduciveness to the ripening of beings; and the conduciveness to undefiled <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.translated_text: Not tolerating all [faults], and engaging in all [virtues] —

children.text: sarveṣu ca pravṛttirhrīvihitaṃ hīmato liṅgam || Msa_18.14 ||
children.translated_text: the non-engagement in all [faults] and the engagement in all [virtues] — this is the sign of one who possesses moral conscience, produced by moral conscience. || Msa_18.14 ||

body.text: etena caturvidhaṃ hrīkṛtaṃ liṅgaṃ hīmato darśayati | yaduta sarvadoṣeṣvanadhivāsanā cāpravṛttiśca | sarvaguṇeṣvadhivāsanā ca pravṛttiśca |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the fourfold sign of one who possesses moral conscience, produced by moral conscience: namely, non-tolerance and non-engagement in all faults, and tolerance and engagement in all virtues.

children.translated_text: The cultivation of moral conscience is foremost — from one's own mind, from <s>dharmas</s>, from conviction,
from disposition also, from sovereignty, from non-conceptualization, and from unity. || Msa_18.15 ||

body.text: ityasya nirdeśo yathāpūrvaṃ |
body.translated_text: Its exposition follows the previous [pattern].

body.text: dhṛtivibhāge sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the division of fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>):

children.translated_text: The fortitude of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by its characteristic and classification,
and by its firmness, is distinguished from all others. || Msa_18.16 ||

children.text: vīryaṃ samādhiḥ prajñā ca sattvaṃ dhairyaṃ dhṛtirmatā |
children.translated_text: Vigor, concentration, and wisdom, and courage and firmness are considered [synonyms of] fortitude;
for the <s>bodhisattva</s> is fearless because he proceeds from these three. || Msa_18.17 ||

body.text: etena dhṛtilakṣaṇaṃ saparyāyaṃ sasādhanaṃ coktaṃ | vīryādikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sattvādikaṃ paryāyaḥ | śeṣaṃ sādhanaṃ | katamasmāttrayānnirbhītaḥ pravartata ityāha |
body.translated_text: By this, the characteristic of fortitude has been stated, with its synonyms and with its means. Vigor and the rest are the characteristic. Courage and the rest are the synonyms. The remainder is the means. From which three is he fearless and proceeds? He says:

children.translated_text: From torpor, from instability, and from confusion, fear arises;

children.text: kṛtyeṣu tasmādvijñeyā dhṛtisaṃjñā nije traye || Msa_18.18 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the designation of fortitude in one's own three [qualities] should be known in [all] duties. || Msa_18.18 ||

body.text: sarvakāryeṣu hi līnacittatayā vā bhayamutpadyate tadanutsāhataḥ | calacittatayā vā cittānavasthānataḥ | saṃmohato vā tadupāyajñānataḥ | tatpratipakṣāśca yathākramaṃ vīryādayaḥ | tasmānnijavīryāditraye dhṛtisaṃjñā veditavyā nija ityapratisaṃkhyānakaraṇīye |
body.translated_text: For in all tasks, fear arises either from torpor of mind — due to lack of enthusiasm for that; or from instability of mind — due to the mind's non-abiding; or from confusion — due to the lack of knowledge of the means for that. And the antidotes to these are, respectively, vigor and the rest. Therefore, the designation of fortitude should be understood in one's own three [qualities] of vigor and the rest — 'one's own' meaning without analytical reflection.

children.text: prakṛtyā praṇidhāne ca nirapekṣatva eva ca |
children.translated_text: By nature, in aspiration, in indifference,
in the transgressions of beings, and in hearing what is profound and exalted; || Msa_18.19 ||
in the difficulty of training those to be trained, in the inconceivable [qualities] of the body of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: duṣkareṣu vicitreṣu saṃsārātyāga eva ca || Msa_18.20 ||
children.translated_text: in the manifold difficult deeds, and in the very non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s>; || Msa_18.20 ||
and in the non-defilement therein itself — fortitude arises in the courageous one,

children.text: asamā ca tadanyebhyaḥ so 'gre dhṛtimatāṃ yataḥ[mataḥ] || Msa_18.21 ||
children.translated_text: and it is unequalled compared to others — therefore one is considered foremost among those who possess fortitude. || Msa_18.21 ||

body.text: ebhistribhiḥ ślaukairdhṛtiprabhedaḥ darśayati | yathākramaṃ gotrataḥ | cittotpādataḥ | svārthataḥ | satvārthataḥ [parārthataḥ | tatvārthataḥ |] prabhāvataḥ | satvaparipācanataḥ | paramabodhitaśca | tatra nirapekṣatvaṃ svārthaprayuktasya kāyajīvitanirapekṣatvādveditavyaṃ | punarduṣkaracaryātaḥ | saṃcintyabhavopapattitaḥ | tadasaṃkleśato 'pi prabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: By these three verses, he shows the classification of fortitude. Respectively: from the lineage (<s>gotra</s>); from the generation of the mind; from self-interest; from the interest of beings; from the meaning of reality; from power; from the ripening of beings; and from supreme awakening. Therein, 'indifference' should be understood as indifference to body and life for one engaged in self-interest. Furthermore, the classification [includes]: from difficult conduct; from intentional rebirth in existence; and from the non-defilement therein as well.

children.translated_text: The courageous one is not shaken by bad friends, suffering, and hearing profound [teachings] —
like <s>Sumeru</s> by moths, by the winds of its wings, and by oceans. || Msa_18.22 ||

body.text: etena bodhisattvadhṛterdṛḍhatvaṃ darśayati | upamātrayaṃ trayeṇākampane[naṃ] yathākramaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the firmness of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s fortitude. The three similes should be understood for the three [causes of] non-shaking, respectively.

body.text: akhedavibhāge dvau ślaukau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of unweariness (<s>akheda</s>):

children.translated_text: The unweariness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is incomparable, regarding three things,
based on moral conscience and fortitude — insatiability in learning, great vigor, and suffering. || Msa_18.23 ||
The intense aspiration for great awakening is considered the unweariness of the wise;
and it is [either] unaccomplished, accomplished, or well-accomplished on the stages. || Msa_18.24 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ vastuto niśrayataḥ svabhāvataḥ prabhedataścākhedo nirdiṣṭaḥ | triṣu vastuṣu | śrutātṛptau | dīrghakālavīryārambhe | saṃsāraduḥkhe ca | hriyaṃ dhṛtiṃ ca niśritya | tābhyāṃ hi khedotpattito lajjayate na cotpādayati | tīvracchando mahābodhāviti svabhāvaḥ | chande hi vyāvṛtte khinno bhavati | aniṣpanno 'dhimukticaryābhūmau | niṣpannaḥ saptabhūmiṣu | suniṣpannaḥ pareṇa ityeṣa prabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: By these two [verses], unweariness has been taught in terms of object, basis, essential nature, and classification. Regarding three things: insatiability in learning, the undertaking of vigor over a long time, and the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Based on moral conscience and fortitude — for through these, one is ashamed when weariness arises and does not produce it. 'Intense aspiration for great awakening' — this is the essential nature, for when aspiration ceases, one becomes weary. Unaccomplished — on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>). Accomplished — on the seven stages. Well-accomplished — beyond those. This is the classification.

body.text: śāstrajñatāyāṃ dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on knowledge of treatises (<s>śāstrajñatā</s>):

children.translated_text: It is distinguished by its object, domain, function,
characteristic, imperishability, and the arising of its fruit. || Msa_18.25 ||
For the knowledge of treatises of the courageous ones is <s>samādhi</s>-door <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions);

children.text: gṛhītā sattvapākāya saddharmasya ca dhāraṇe || Msa_18.26 ||
children.translated_text: it is obtained for the ripening of beings and for the holding of the true Dharma. || Msa_18.26 ||

body.text: tatra śāstrajñatāyāḥ pañca vidyāsthānāni vastu | adhyātmavidyā hetuvidyā śabdavidyā cikitsāvidyā śilpakarmasthānavidyā ca | svaparārthakriyā adhikāraḥ | karma prathamavastuni (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 132

children.text: ) svayaṃ pratipattiḥ parebhyaśca tatsamākhyānaṃ | dvitīye taddoṣaparijñānaṃ paravādinigrahaśca | tṛtīye svayaṃ sunirūktābhidhānaṃ parasaṃpratyayaśca | caturthe pareṣāṃ vyādhiśamanaṃ | pañcame parebhyastatsaṃvibhāgaḥ | lakṣaṇaṃ śāstrajñatāyā etānyeva pañca vastūni śrutāni bhavanti | dhṛtāni | vacasā parijitāni | manasā anvīkṣitāni | dṛṣṭyā supratividdhāni | śrutvā yathākramaṃ tadudgrahaṇātaḥ | svādhyāyataḥ | prasannena manasārthacittanato yathāyogaṃ taddoṣaguṇāvagamāt svākhyātadurākhyātāvadhāraṇataśca | akṣayatvaṃ nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pyakṣayāt | phalasamudāgamaḥ sarvadharmasarvākārajñatā | sā punareṣā śāsrajñatā bodhisattvānāṃ samādhimukhairdhāraṇīmukhaiśca saṃgṛhītā | sattvaparipākāya ca bhavati | samādhimukhaistatkṛtyānuṣṭhānāt | saddharmapāraṇāya ca dhāraṇībhistaddhāraṇāt |
children.translated_text: ) one's own practice and the exposition thereof to others. Regarding the second, understanding the faults therein and the defeat of the doctrines of others. Regarding the third, one's own excellent articulation and the persuasion of others. Regarding the fourth, the curing of others' diseases. Regarding the fifth, the sharing thereof with others. The characteristic of knowledge of treatises is that these very five objects have been heard, retained, mastered verbally, examined mentally, and well-penetrated by insight — through hearing, by memorizing them, respectively; through study; through contemplation of meaning with a clear mind and, as appropriate, through the understanding of their faults and qualities, and through the ascertainment of well-spoken and ill-spoken [teachings]. Its imperishability — because of being imperishable even in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. The arising of the fruit is the omniscience of all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects. This knowledge of treatises of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is further comprehended by the doors of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>. It exists for the ripening of beings — through the accomplishment of their needs by the doors of <s>samādhi</s>. And for the holding of the true Dharma — through the holding of that by <s>dhāraṇīs</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, the five sites of knowledge are the object of knowledge of treatises: inner science (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and the science of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>). The accomplishment of the welfare of self and others is the domain. The function regarding the first object is (

body.text: lokajñatāyāṃ catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>):

children.translated_text: By body, by speech, and by the knowledge of truth — incomparable,

children.text: lokajñatā hi dhīrāṇāṃ tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate || Msa_18.27 ||
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the world of the courageous ones is distinguished from all others. || Msa_18.27 ||

body.text: kathaṃ kāyenetyāha | kṛtasmitamukhā nityaṃ | kathaṃ vācetyāha | dhīrāḥ pūrvābhibhāṣiṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: How by body? He says: 'With a constantly smiling face.' How by speech? He says: 'The courageous ones are the first to speak.'

body.text:
sā punaḥ kimarthamityāha | sattvānāṃ bhājanatvāya |
kasminnarthe bhājanatvāya | saddharmapratipattaye || Msa_18.28 ||
body.translated_text:
And for what purpose? He says: 'So that beings may become vessels.'
For what purpose becoming vessels? 'For the practice of the true Dharma.' || Msa_18.28 ||

body.text: kathaṃ satyajñānenetyāha |
body.translated_text: How by the knowledge of truth? He says:

children.translated_text: From the two truths, the repeated arising of the world is desired;
from the two [other truths], the cessation — therefore, the one who knows that is called a knower of the world. || Msa_18.29 ||

body.text: dvābhyāṃ satyābhyāṃ lokasyodayaḥ punaḥ punaḥ saṃsāro yaścodayo yena ceti kṛtvā | dvābhyāmastaṃgamo nirodhamārgasatyābhyāṃ | yaścāstaṃgamo yena ceti kṛtvā | tasmāttajjño lokajña ucyate | lokasyodayāstaṃgāminyā prajñayā samanvāgatatvāt |
body.translated_text: From the two truths [of suffering and origination], the arising of the world — that is, the repeated <s>saṃsāra</s> — considering what [constitutes] the arising and by what [it arises]. From the two [truths of cessation and path], the cessation — considering what the cessation is and by what [it is achieved]. Therefore, the one who knows that is called a knower of the world — because of being endowed with the wisdom that knows the arising and cessation of the world.

children.text: śamāya prāptaye teṣāṃ dhīmān satyeṣu yujyate |
children.translated_text: The wise one applies himself to the truths for the pacification and attainment of those [two];

children.text: satyajñānadyato dhīmān lokajño hi nirucyate || Msa_18.30 ||
children.translated_text: from the knowledge of truth, the wise one is thus etymologically called a knower of the world. || Msa_18.30 ||

body.text: anena lokajñatāyāḥ karma nirdiṣṭaṃ | tatra śamāya duḥkhasamudayasatyayoḥ prāptaye nirodhamārgasatyayoḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, the function of knowledge of the world is shown. Therein, for pacification — regarding the truths of suffering and origination; for attainment — regarding the truths of cessation and path.

body.text: pratisaraṇavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of the reliances (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>):

children.translated_text: The Dharma of teaching is what has come from the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages); the meaning is that which is intended;

children.text: prāmāṇikaśca nītārtho nirjalpā prāptirasya ca || Msa_18.31 ||
children.translated_text: the authoritative [meaning] is the definitive one; and the attainment thereof is beyond verbal designation. || Msa_18.31 ||

body.text: idaṃ pratisaraṇānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ | tatra prāmāṇiko 'rtho yaḥ pramāṇabhūtena nīto vibhaktaḥ śāstrā vā tatpramāṇīkṛtena vā | nirjalpā prāptiradhigamajñānaṃ lokottaraṃ | tasyānabhilāpyatvāt | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: This is the characteristic of the reliances. Therein, the authoritative meaning is that which has been determined and distinguished by the Teacher who is an authority, or by one authorized by him. The attainment that is beyond verbal designation is the supramundane knowledge of realization — because of its inexpressibility. The rest is self-evident.

children.translated_text: The prohibition taught here is against one who rejects what has been stated,

children.text: sābhilāṣa[pa]sya ca prāpteḥ pratiṣedho 'tra deśitaḥ || Msa_18.32 ||
children.translated_text: against what has been wrongly reflected upon, and against the attainment that is accompanied by desire. || Msa_18.32 ||

body.text: prathame pratisaraṇe ārṣadharmapratikṣeptuḥ pudnalasya pratiṣedho deśitaḥ | dvitīye yathārutārthasya vyañjanasya nābhiprāyikārthena | tṛtīye mithyā cintitārthasya viparītaṃ nīyamānasya | caturthe sābhilāṣa[pa]sya jñānasya[ā]pratyātmavedanīyasya |
body.translated_text: In the first reliance, the prohibition taught is against the person who rejects the Dharma coming from the <s>Ṛṣis</s>. In the second, [the prohibition is] against the meaning as literally understood, which is the letter, not the intended meaning. In the third, against the wrongly reflected meaning that is being taken in a perverted way. In the fourth, against the knowledge that is accompanied by desire and not to be individually realized.

children.translated_text: From conviction, from investigation, from hearing correctly from others,

children.text: nirjalpādapi ca jñānādapraṇāśo hi dhīmatāṃ || Msa_18.33 ||
children.translated_text: and from the knowledge beyond verbal designation — there is no destruction for the wise ones. || Msa_18.33 ||

body.text: ayaṃ pratisaraṇānuśaṃsaḥ | prathamena pratisaraṇenārṣadharmādhimuktito na praṇaśyati | dvitīyena svayamābhiprāyikārthavicāraṇāt | tṛtīyena paratastadaviparītārthanayaśravāt | caturthena lokottarajñānāt |
body.translated_text: This is the benefit of the reliances. Through the first reliance, one does not perish — from conviction in the Dharma that comes from the <s>Ṛṣis</s>. Through the second, from investigating the intended meaning by oneself. Through the third, from hearing from others the correct method of that meaning. Through the fourth, from supramundane knowledge.

body.text: pratisaṃvidvibhāge catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the division of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>):

children.translated_text: The incomparable four analytical knowledges of <s>bodhisattvas</s>

children.text: paryāye lakṣaṇe vākye jñāne jñānācca tā matāḥ || Msa_18.34 ||
children.translated_text: are held to be in synonyms, in characteristics, in speech, and in knowledge — and they arise from knowledge. || Msa_18.34 ||

body.text: prathamā paryāye jñānamekaikasyārthasya yāvanto nāmaparyāyāḥ | dvitīyā lakṣaṇe yasyārthasya tannāma | tṛtīyā vākye pratyekaṃ janapadeṣu yā bhāṣāḥ | caturthā jñāne svayaṃ yatpratibhānam | idaṃ pratisaṃvidāṃlakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: The first is knowledge in synonyms — however many synonymous names there are for each meaning. The second is in characteristics — of which meaning that is the name. The third is in speech — whichever languages exist in each region. The fourth is in knowledge — one's own spontaneous comprehension. This is the characteristic of the analytical knowledges.

children.text: deśanāyāṃ prayuktasya yasya yena ca deśanā |
children.translated_text: Of one engaged in teaching: for whom, and by what means the teaching [is given];
the teaching of both Dharma and meaning, by speech and by knowledge itself. || Msa_18.35 ||
From the synopsis and detailed exposition of the Dharma, from the complete conveying of both [Dharma and meaning],
and from the refutation of objections — the four analytical knowledges. || Msa_18.36 ||

body.text: iti catuṣṭve kāraṇaṃ | deśanāyāṃ hi prayuktasya yasya ca deśanā yena ca | tatra jñānena prayojanaṃ | kasya punardeśanā | dharmasyārthasya | kena deśanā vacanena jñānena ca | tatra dharmārthayordeśanā | dharmasyoddeśanirdeśāt | vākyena deśanā tayoreva dvayoḥ sarvathā prāpaṇāt |
body.translated_text: This is the reason for [there being] four. For one engaged in teaching: for whom the teaching [is given], and by what means. Therein, knowledge serves the purpose. For whom is the teaching? For the Dharma and its meaning. By what is it taught? By speech and by knowledge. Therein, the teaching of Dharma and meaning — from the synopsis and detailed exposition of the Dharma. The teaching by speech — from the complete conveying of both of those [Dharma and meaning] in all ways.

body.text: jñānena deśanā codyānāṃ pariharaṇāt | ato yacca yena ca deśyate tajjñānāt catasraḥ pratisaṃvido vyavasthāpitāḥ |
body.translated_text: The teaching by knowledge — from the refutation of objections. Therefore, from what is taught and by what it is taught, the four analytical knowledges have been established through knowledge.

children.translated_text: Having individually attained the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, the realization thereafter
is called analytical knowledge — for the destruction of all doubts. || Msa_18.37 ||

body.text: etena pratisaṃvidāṃ nirvacanaṃ karma ca darśitaṃ | pratyātmaṃ lokottareṇa jñānena sarvadharmasamatāṃ tathatāmavetya uttarakālaṃ tatpṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena pravedanā paryāyādīnāṃ pratisaṃviditi nirvacanaṃ | sarvasaṃśayanāśāya pareṣāmiti karma |
body.translated_text: By this, the etymology and function of the analytical knowledges are shown. Having individually attained the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — through supramundane knowledge, thereafter, the realization of synonyms and the rest through the subsequently-attained knowledge is the etymology of analytical knowledge. 'For the destruction of all doubts of others' — this is its function.

body.text: saṃbhāravibhāge catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the division of the accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>):

children.translated_text: The accumulation of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, consisting of merit and knowledge, is incomparable;
one [is for] prosperity in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the other for undefiled continuity in [<s>saṃsāra</s>]. || Msa_18.38 ||

body.text: yaśca saṃbhāro yadarthaṃ ca tatsaṃdarśitam | dvividhaḥ saṃbhāraḥ | tatra puṇyasaṃbhāraḥ saṃsāre 'bhyudayāya saṃvartate | jñānasaṃbhāro 'saṃkliṣṭasaṃsaraṇāya |
body.translated_text: What the accumulation is and for what purpose — that has been shown. The accumulation is twofold. Therein, the accumulation of merit leads to prosperity in <s>saṃsāra</s>. The accumulation of knowledge leads to undefiled continuity in [<s>saṃsāra</s>].

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ ca puṇyasya prajñā jñānasya saṃbhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Giving and moral discipline are the accumulation of merit; wisdom is the accumulation of knowledge;
and the other three [perfections] belong to both, and all five are also the accumulation of knowledge. || Msa_18.39 ||

body.text: etena pāramitābhistadubhayasaṃbhārasaṃgrahaṃ darśayati | kṣāntivīryadhyānabalena hyubhayaṃ kriyate | tasmāddvayasaṃbhārasrayaṃ bhavati | punaḥ prajñāyāṃ pariṇāmanātsarvāḥ pañca pāramitā jñānasaṃbhāro veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the comprehension of both accumulations by the <s>pāramitās</s>. For both [accumulations] are accomplished by the power of patience, vigor, and meditation.
