Therefore, the three belong to both accumulations. Furthermore, through the dedication of all five <s>pāramitās</s> to wisdom, they should be understood as the accumulation of knowledge.

children.text: saṃtatyā bhāvanāmetya bhūyo bhūyaḥ śubhasya hi |
children.translated_text: Encountering cultivation in continuity, repeatedly, the nourishment of the wholesome —

children.text: āhāro yaḥ sa saṃbhāro vī[dhī]re sarvārthasādhakaḥ || Msa_18.40 ||
children.translated_text: that is the accumulation, which accomplishes all purposes for the courageous one. || Msa_18.40 ||

body.text: etatsaṃbhāranirvacanaṃ karma ca | samiti saṃtatyā | bhā iti bhāvanāmāgamya | ra iti bhūyo bhūya āhāraḥ | sarvārthasādhaka iti karma | svaparārthayoḥ sādhanāt |
body.translated_text: This is the etymology and function of the accumulation. 'Sam' means in continuity. 'Bhā' means having arrived at cultivation. 'Ra' means repeated nourishment. 'Accomplishes all purposes' — this is the function, because of accomplishing the welfare of self and others.

children.translated_text: For entry, for the signless, for effortlessness, the accumulation
is amassed for consecration and for the final goal by the courageous ones. || Msa_18.41 ||

body.text: ayaṃ saṃbhāraprabhedaḥ | tatrādhimukticaryābhūmau saṃbhāro bhūmipraveśāya | ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣvanimittāya saptamībhūmisaṃgṛhītāya | tasyāṃ nimitta-[ā] samudācārāt | saptamyāṃ bhūmāvanābhogāya tadanyabhūmidvayasaṃgṛhītāyā | tayoḥ saṃbhārā[ro ']bhiṣekāya daśamībhūmisaṃgṛhītāya | tasyāṃ saṃbhāro niṣṭhāgamanāya buddhabhūmisaṃgṛhītāya |
body.translated_text: This is the classification of the accumulation. Therein, on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), the accumulation is for entry into the stages. On the six stages, for the signless, which is comprehended by the seventh stage — because of the non-arising of signs on that [stage]. On the seventh stage, for effortlessness, which is comprehended by the other two stages. On those [two stages], the accumulation is for consecration, which is comprehended by the tenth stage. On that [stage], the accumulation is for reaching the final goal, which is comprehended by the <s>Buddha</s>-stage.

body.text: smṛtyupasthānavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness is through fourteen aspects;
because of its incomparable nature for the wise, it is distinguished from all others. || Msa_18.42 ||

body.text: katamaiścaturdaśabhiḥ |
body.translated_text: What are the fourteen?

children.translated_text: Through basis, through antidote, and through entry, and likewise
through object, mental attention, and attainment, it is distinguished. || Msa_18.43 ||
Through conduciveness, through conformity, through full understanding, and through another — arising;
through the mere [degree], through the supreme, through cultivation, and through attainment. || Msa_18.44 ||

body.text: ityebhiścaturdaśabhirākārairbodhisatvānāṃ smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā viśiṣyate | kathamāśrayato mahāyāne śrutacintābhāvanāmayīṃ prajñāmāśritya | kathaṃ pratipakṣataḥ caturviparyāsapratipakṣāṇāmapyaśuciduḥkhānityānātmasaṃjñānāṃ pratipakṣatvātkāyādidharma nairātmyapraveśataḥ | kathamavatārataḥ | caturbhiḥ smṛtyupasthānairyathākramaṃ duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyāvatārātsvayaṃ pareṣāṃ cāvatāraṇāt | yathoktaṃ madhyāntavibhāge | kathamālambanataḥ sarvasattvakāyādyālambanāt | kathaṃ manaskārataḥ kāyādyanupalambhāt | kathaṃ prāptitaḥ kāyādīnāṃ na visaṃyogāya nāvisaṃyogāya | kathamānukūlyataḥ pāramitānukūlyena tadvipakṣapratipakṣatvāt | kathamanuvṛttitaḥ laukikānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ cānuvṛttyā tadupasaṃhitasmṛtyupasthānabhāvanāttebhyastadupadeśārthaṃ | kathaṃ parijñātaḥ kāyasya māyopamatvaparijñayā tathaivābhūtarūpasaṃprakhyānāt | vedanāyāḥ svapnopamatvaparijñayā tathaiva mithyānubhavāt | cittasya prakṛtiprabhāsvaratvaparijñayā ākāśavat | dharmāṇāmāgantukatvaparijñayā ākāśāganturajodhūmābhranīhāropakleśavat | kathamutpattitaḥ saṃcityabhavopapattau cakravartyādibhūtasya viśiṣṭakāyavedanādisaṃpattau tadasaṃkleśataḥ | kathaṃ mātrātaḥ mṛdvā api smṛtyupasthānabhāvanāyāstadanyebhyo 'dhimātratvāt | prakṛtitīkṣṇendriyatayā | kathaṃ paramatvena pariniṣpannānāmanābhogamiśropamiśrabhāvanāt | kathaṃ bhāvanātaḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 136

children.text: ) atyantaṃ tadbhāvanāt nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pi tadakṣayāt | kathaṃ samudāgamataḥ | daśasu bhūmiṣu buddhatve ca samudāgamāt |
children.translated_text: ) From the ultimate cultivation thereof — because of its imperishability even in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. How through attainment? From the attainment on the ten stages and in Buddhahood.

body.translated_text: By these fourteen aspects, the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is distinguished. How through basis? By relying on the wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and meditation in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. How through antidote? Because the perceptions of the impure, suffering, impermanent, and selfless, which are the antidotes to the four perversions, also serve as antidotes — from the entry into the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) through the body and the rest. How through entry? Because by the four foundations of mindfulness, one enters respectively the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and path, and causes others to enter them as well — as stated in the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>. How through object? From having as object the bodies and the rest of all beings. How through mental attention? From the non-apprehension of body and the rest. How through attainment? Because the body and the rest are neither for the purpose of disconnection nor for the purpose of non-disconnection. How through conduciveness? Because of being conducive to the <s>pāramitās</s>, by being the antidote to their opposing factors. How through conformity? From conformity with worldlings and with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — by cultivating the foundations of mindfulness connected with them, for the purpose of instructing them. How through full understanding? From the full understanding of the body as being like an illusion — through the manifestation of a non-real form; of feeling as being like a dream — through the experience of what is false; of the mind as being luminous by nature — like space; of phenomena as being adventitious — like the defilements of dust, smoke, clouds, and mist that are adventitious in space. How through arising? From arising in the intentional rebirth in existence of one who has become a universal monarch and the like — in the distinguished attainment of body, feeling, and the rest, without defilement therein. How through the mere [degree]? Because even the slightest cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness is of the highest degree compared to others — due to being by nature of keen faculties. How through the supreme? From the cultivation that is effortless, mixed, and quasi-mixed, of those who have attained perfection. How through cultivation? (

body.text: samyakprahāṇavibhāge pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the division of the right endeavors (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>):

children.translated_text: The right endeavor of the courageous ones is incomparable with all beings;
it is cultivated as the antidote to the faults [that are adverse] to the foundations of mindfulness. || Msa_18.45 ||

body.text: yāvatyaḥ smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā uktāḥ tadvipakṣāṇāṃ doṣāṇāṃ pratipakṣeṇa samyakprahāṇabhāvaneti samastaṃ samyakprahāṇalakṣaṇam | prabhedena punaḥ |
body.translated_text: For however many cultivations of the foundations of mindfulness have been stated, the cultivation of right endeavor is the antidote to the faults that are the opposing factors of those — this is the complete characteristic of right endeavor. In classification, furthermore:

children.translated_text: In the enjoyment of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and in the abandoning of the hindrances,

children.text: manaskārasya ca tyāge praveśe caiva bhūmiṣu || Msa_18.46 ||
children.translated_text: and in the abandoning of [wrong] mental attention, and in the very entry into the stages; || Msa_18.46 ||
in the abiding in the signless, and in the obtaining of the prediction,

children.text: sattvānāṃ paripāke ca abhiṣeke ca dhīmatāṃ || Msa_18.47 ||
children.translated_text: and in the ripening of beings, and in the consecration of the wise; || Msa_18.47 ||

children.text: kṣetrasya ca viśuddhyarthaṃ niṣṭhāgamana eva ca |
children.translated_text: and for the purpose of the purification of the field, and in the very reaching of the final goal —
[the right endeavor] of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is cultivated through the antidote to the opposing factor. || Msa_18.48 ||

body.text: ayaṃ samyakprahāṇabhāvanāprabhedaḥ | saṃsārasyāsaṃkliṣṭaparibhoge saṃpattiṣu | pañcanivāraṇatyāge | śrāvakapratyekabuddhamanaskāratyāge | bhūmipraveśe | animittavihāre saptamyāṃ bhūmau | vyākaraṇalābhe aṣṭamyāṃ | sattvānāṃ paripācane | navamyāṃ | abhiṣeke ca daśamyāṃ | kṣetraviśuddhyarthaṃ traye 'pi | niṣṭhāgamane ca buddhabhūmau | ye ca vipakṣāsteṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇa samyakprahāṇabhāvanā veditavyā | ayamasyāḥ prabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the classification of the cultivation of right endeavor: in the undefiled enjoyment of <s>saṃsāra</s>, in [its] prosperities; in the abandoning of the five hindrances; in the abandoning of the mental attention of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; in the entry into the stages; in the signless abiding on the seventh stage; in obtaining the prediction on the eighth stage; in the ripening of beings on the ninth; and in the consecration on the tenth; for the purpose of the purification of the field on the three [stages, i.e., eighth, ninth, and tenth]; and in the reaching of the final goal on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. And the cultivation of right endeavor should be understood as the antidote to whatever opposing factors there are. This is its classification.

children.translated_text: The cultivation of yoga, relying on aspiration, is accompanied by signs;
this is declared as the antidote in all the right endeavors. || Msa_18.49 ||

body.text: etena chandaṃ janayati | vyāyacchate vīryamārabhate | cittaṃ pragṛṇhāti | samyak pradadhātīti | eṣāṃ padānāmarthanirdeśaḥ | chandaṃ hi niśritya śamathavipaśyanākhyaṃ yogaṃ bhāvayatīti vyāyacchate | sā ca bhāvanā śamathapragrahopekṣānimittaiḥ saha bhāvyate | tasmātsā sanimittikā | kathaṃ ca punarbhāvyate | yacchamathapragrahopakleśayorlayauddhatyayoḥ pratipakṣeṇa vīryamārabhate | kathamārabhate | cittaṃ pragṛṇhāti pradadhāti ca | [tatra pragṛṇhātītiprajñayā | pradadhātīti?] śamathe [na?] samaprāpte co[ptaśco]pekṣāyāṃ pradadhāti | eṣā yogabhāvanā yathoktaprabhedeṣu sarvasamyakprahāṇeṣu pratipakṣa ucyate |
body.translated_text: By this: 'one generates aspiration, one exerts oneself, one initiates vigor, one uplifts the mind, one properly applies [the mind]' — this is the exposition of the meaning of these terms. For relying on aspiration, one cultivates the yoga called <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) — thus one exerts oneself. And that cultivation is cultivated together with the signs of calm, upliftment, and equanimity. Therefore it is 'accompanied by signs.' How then is it cultivated? One initiates vigor as the antidote to the defilements of torpor and excitement — the opposing factors of calm and upliftment. How does one initiate it? One uplifts the mind and applies it. [One uplifts it through wisdom.] When calm has been equally attained, one applies [the mind] to equanimity. This yoga-cultivation, in all the right endeavors of the classification stated, is called the antidote.

body.text: ṛddhipādavibhāge pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses on the division of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>):

children.translated_text: The four bases of supernatural power of the courageous ones, having the characteristics of preeminence,

children.text: sarvārthasiddhau jāyante ātmanaśca parasya ca || Msa_18.50 ||
children.translated_text: arise for the accomplishment of all purposes — both one's own and others'. || Msa_18.50 ||

body.text: sarvārthasiddhirlaukikī lokottarā ca veditavyā | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of all purposes should be understood as both worldly and supramundane. The rest is self-evident.

children.translated_text: Through the basis, classification, means, and production —
the establishment of the bases of supernatural power of the wise is accepted in every way. || Msa_18.51 ||

body.text: asyoddeśasya śeṣo nirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: The detailed exposition of this synopsis [follows]:

children.translated_text: Relying on the perfection of meditation, the classification is fourfold;
and the means and the production are established as sixfold. || Msa_18.52 ||

body.text: dhyānapāramitāniśrayaḥ prabhedaścaturvidhaśchandavīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhibhedāt | upāyaścaturvidha eva | abhinirhāraḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ | caturvidha upāyaḥ katamaḥ |
body.translated_text: The basis is the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). The classification is fourfold — through the distinction of <s>samādhis</s> of aspiration, vigor, mind, and investigation. And the means is fourfold as well. The production is sixfold. What is the fourfold means?

children.translated_text: The first is of the nature of resolve, the second is of the nature of support,
the third is of the nature of binding, and the fourth is of the nature of antidote. || Msa_18.53 ||

body.text: aṣṭānāṃ prahāṇasaṃskārāṇāṃ chando vyāyāmaḥ śraddhā vyāvasāyikaḥ upāyaḥ | śraddadhānasyārthino vyāyāmāt | praśrabdhiranugrāhakaḥ | smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ caupanibandhakaḥ | ekena cittasyālambanāvisārāt | dvitīyena visāraprajñānāt | cetanā copekṣā ca prātipakṣika upāyaḥ | layauddhatyopakleśayoḥ kleśānāṃ ca pratipakṣatvāt | ṣaḍvidho 'bhinirhāraḥ katamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among the eight abandonment-formations: aspiration, exertion, and faith are the means of the nature of resolve — from the exertion of one who has faith and aspires. Pliancy is [the means] of the nature of support. Mindfulness and clear comprehension are [the means] of the nature of binding — by the first, preventing the mind from straying from the object; by the second, knowing when it has strayed. Volition and equanimity are the antidotal means — because of being the antidote to the defilements of torpor and excitement, and to the afflictions. What is the sixfold production?

children.translated_text: The production of vision, of instruction, of abiding and play,
of aspiration, of mastery, and of the attainment of [special] <s>dharmas</s>. || Msa_18.54 ||

body.text: tatra darśanaṃ cakṣuḥ pañcavidhaṃ māṃsacakṣuḥ dīvyaṃ cakṣuḥ āryaṃ prajñācakṣuḥ dharmacakṣuḥ buddhacakṣuśca | avavādaḥ ṣaḍabhijñā yathākramaṃ | tābhirupasaṃkramya bhāṣāṃ cittaṃ cāgatiṃ ca gatiṃ ca viditvā niḥsaraṇāyāvavadanāt | sthitivikriḍitaṃ yasmāt bodhisattvānāṃ bahuvidhaṃ nirmāṇādibhiḥ samādhivikrīḍitaṃ | praṇidhiryena praṇidhijñānena praṇidhānabalikā bodhisattvāḥ praṇidhānavaiśeṣikatayā vikrīḍanti | yeṣāṃ na sukaraṃ saṃkhyā kartuṃ kāyasya vā prabhāyā vā svarasya veti vistareṇa yathā daśabhūmike sūtre | vaśitā yathā tatraiva daśa vaśitā nirdiṣṭāḥ | dharmaprāptirbalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmāṇāṃ prāptiḥ | ityeṣa darśanādīnāmabhinirhāraḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, vision is the fivefold eye: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the noble eye, the wisdom eye, the Dharma eye, and the <s>Buddha</s> eye. Instruction [consists of] the six supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), respectively — by approaching with those, knowing the language, the mind, the origin, and the destination [of beings], and then instructing for the purpose of escape. Abiding and play — because the <s>bodhisattvas</s> have manifold play of <s>samādhi</s> through emanation and the rest. Aspiration — by which <s>bodhisattvas</s>, endowed with the power of aspiration, who are distinguished by the special quality of aspiration, play through the knowledge of aspiration — those whose body, radiance, or voice cannot easily be enumerated, and so on in detail, as in the <s>Daśabhūmikasūtra</s>. Mastery — just as the ten masteries have been taught therein. The attainment of [special] <s>dharmas</s> — the attainment of the powers, the fearlessnesses, and the unique qualities of the <s>Buddhas</s>. This is the sixfold production of vision and the rest.

body.text: indriyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the faculties (<s>indriya</s>):

children.translated_text: Awakening, the bodhisattva-conduct, learning, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) —
these should be known as the domains of faith and the rest, from the standpoint of the accomplishment of their purposes. || Msa_18.55 ||

body.text: śraddhendriyasya bodhiḥ padamālambanamityarthaḥ | vīryendriyasya bodhisattvacaryā | smṛtīndriyasya mahāyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ śrutaṃ | samādhīndriyasya śamathaḥ | prajñendriyasya vipaśyanā padaṃ | tadarthādhikāreṇaiva caitāni śraddhādīni ādhipatyārthenendriyāṇyucyante |
body.translated_text: The domain of the faculty of faith is awakening — meaning it is its object. The domain of the faculty of vigor is the bodhisattva-conduct. The domain of the faculty of mindfulness is learning comprehended by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The domain of the faculty of <s>samādhi</s> is <s>śamatha</s>. The domain of the faculty of wisdom is <s>vipaśyanā</s>. And these — faith and the rest — are called faculties in the sense of sovereignty, precisely for the purpose of those [respective domains].

body.text: balavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the powers (<s>bala</s>):

children.translated_text: Faith and the rest, which were [described as] afflicted regarding entry into the stages,
are designated as powers due to the weakness of the opposing factors. || Msa_18.56 ||

body.text: gatārthaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The verse is self-evident.

body.text: bodhyaṅgavibhāge sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Seven verses on the division of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>):

children.translated_text: The establishment of the factors of awakening is prescribed for one who has entered the stages,
from the understanding of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and of all beings. || Msa_18.57 ||

body.text: etena yasyāmavasthāyāṃ yasyāvabodhāt bodhyaṅgāni vyavasthāpyante tadupadiṣṭaṃ | bhūmipraviṣṭāvasthāyāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca samatāvabodhādyathākramaṃ dharmanairātmyenātmaparasamatayā ca | ataḥ paraṃ cakrādisaptaratnasādharmyaṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this, it has been indicated at what stage and from what understanding the factors of awakening are established — at the stage of having entered [the bodhisattva stages], from the understanding of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and of all beings, respectively through the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and through the equality of self and other. Hereafter, he shows the similarity of the factors of awakening to the seven treasures such as the wheel and the rest:

body.text: smṛtiścarati sarvatra jñeyājitavinirjaye |
body.translated_text: Mindfulness moves everywhere, for the conquest of what is unconquered among the knowable —

body.text: ajitajñeyavinirjayāya | yathā cakravartinaścakraratnamajitadeśavinirjayāya |
body.translated_text: for the conquest of the unconquered among the knowable. Just as the wheel-treasure of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) [moves everywhere] for the conquest of unconquered territories.

body.text: sarvakalpanimittānāṃ bhaṅgāya vicayo 'sya ca || Msa_18.58 ||
body.translated_text: and the investigation [factor] is for the breaking of all conceptual signs. || Msa_18.58 ||

body.text: yathā hastiratnaṃ pratyarthikabhaṅgāya |
body.translated_text: Just as the elephant-treasure is for the breaking of adversaries.

body.text: āśu cāśeṣabodhāya vīryamasya pravartate |
body.translated_text: And vigor operates for swift and complete awakening —

body.text: kṣiprābhijñatotpādanāt | yathāśvaratnamāśu samudraparyantamahāpṛthivīgamanāya |
body.translated_text: because of producing swift supernatural knowledge. Just as the horse-treasure [operates] for swiftly traversing the great earth up to the ocean.

body.text: dharmālokavivṛddhyā ca prītyā āpūryate dhruvam || Msa_18.59 ||
body.translated_text: and one is surely filled with joy through the increase of the light of the Dharma. || Msa_18.59 ||

body.text: ārabdhavīryasya bodhisattvasya dharmālokā vivardhante | tataḥ prītiḥ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ[yaṃ] sadā prīṇayati | yathā maṇiratnamālokaviśeṣeṇa cakravartinaṃ prīṇayati |
body.translated_text: For a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has initiated vigor, the lights of the Dharma increase. From that [arises] joy — it always delights the entire task. Just as the jewel-gem delights the <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) through a special radiance.

body.text: sarvāvaraṇanirmokṣāt praśrabdhyā sukhameti ca |
body.translated_text: From the liberation from all obscurations, one attains happiness through <s>praśrabdhi</s> (pliancy),

body.text: sarvadauṣṭhulyasamutpāda[ṭa]nāt | yathā strīratnena cakravartī sukhamanubhavati |
body.translated_text: because of the eradication of all coarseness. Just as the <s>cakravartin</s> experiences happiness through the woman-jewel.

body.text: cintitārthasamṛddhiśca samādherūpajāyate || Msa_18.60 ||
body.translated_text: And the fulfillment of desired goals arises from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). || Msa_18.60 ||

body.text: yathā cakravartino gṛhapatiratnāt |
body.translated_text: Just as [the fulfillment arises] for the <s>cakravartin</s> from the householder-jewel.

children.translated_text: Through <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), one dwells as one wishes everywhere;
through the non-conceptual [mode] obtained subsequently, with conceptual [activity] — [such a one is] always the best. || Msa_18.61 ||

body.text: upekṣocyate nirvikalpaṃ jñānaṃ tayā bodhisattvaḥ sarvatra yathākāmaṃ viharati | tatpṛṣṭhalabdhena ca vihāreṇānyasyopagamāt | anyasyāpagamāt | nirvikalpena vihāreṇa tatra nirvyāpāratayā vāsakalpanāt | yathā cakravartinaḥ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ caturaṅgabalakāyamupanetavyaṃ copapraṇayati[gamayati] | apanetavyaṃ cāpanayati | tatra ca gatvā vāsaṃ kalpayati yatrākhinnaḥ caturaṅgo bālakāyaḥ paraiti |
body.translated_text: Equanimity is said to be non-conceptual knowledge. Through it, the <s>bodhisattva</s> dwells everywhere as one wishes. And through the subsequent attainment — by approaching one [realm] and departing from another; through the non-conceptual abiding — by dwelling there without activity. Just as the general-jewel of the <s>cakravartin</s> leads the fourfold army where it should be led, removes it where it should be removed, and, having gone there, establishes a camp where the fourfold army rests without fatigue.

children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with such qualities acts like a <s>cakravartin</s>,
always surrounded by the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), which are like the seven jewels. || Msa_18.62 ||

body.text: iti saptaratnopamatvaṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ nigamayati |
body.translated_text: Thus he concludes the comparison of the factors of awakening to the seven jewels.

children.translated_text: The factor of support, the factor of intrinsic nature, the factor of progress — these are the [first] three;
the fourth is the factor of benefit, and the factor of non-affliction is threefold. || Msa_18.63 ||

body.text: etena yabdodhyaṅgaṃ yathāṅgaṃ tadabhidyotitaṃ | smṛtirniśrayāṅgaṃ sarveṣāṃ tanniśrayeṇa pravṛtteḥ | dharmapravicayaḥ svabhāvāṅgaṃ bodhestatsvabhāvatvāt | vīryaṃ niryāṇāṅgaṃ tenāprāpyaniṣṭhā yāmadhiṣṭhānāt [vicchedāt] | prītiranuśaṃsāṅgaṃ cittasukhatvāt | praśrabdhisamādhyupekṣā asaṃkleśāṅgaṃ | yena yanniśritya yo 'saṃkleśa iti trividhamasaṃkleśāṅgaṃ veditavyam |
body.translated_text: By this, each factor of awakening is illuminated as to what kind of factor it is. <s>Smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is the factor of support — because all [other factors] operate depending on it. <s>Dharmapravicaya</s> (investigation of phenomena) is the factor of intrinsic nature — because it is the very nature of awakening. <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) is the factor of progress — because without it, the goal is not attained, due to interruption. <s>Prīti</s> (joy) is the factor of benefit — because of the happiness of mind. <s>Praśrabdhi</s> (pliancy), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) are the factor of non-affliction. Depending on what, from what, and what non-affliction — the threefold factor of non-affliction should be understood.

body.text: mārgāṅgavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of the path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>):

children.translated_text: The conformity to awakening as it truly is arises thereafter;
the determination of awakening as it truly is, and the entry into the established [teaching]. || Msa_18.64 ||
The purification of the threefold action, the antidote and cultivation
of the obscuration of the knowable, of the path, and of the special quality. || Msa_18.65 ||

body.text: bodhyaṅgakālādūrdhvaṃ yathābhūtāvabodhānuvṛttiḥ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | tasyaivāvabodhasya vyavasthānaṃ paricchedaḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ | tadvyavasthāne ca sūtrādike bhagavatā kṛte sa eva praveśastena tadarthāvabodhāt | karmatrayaviśuddhiḥ samyagvākkarmāntājīvāḥ | vākkāyobhayakarmasaṃgrahāt | pratipakṣasya bhāvanā samyagvyāyāmādayo yathākramaṃ jñeyāvaraṇasya mārgāvaraṇasya ca vaiśeṣikaguṇāvaraṇasya ca samyagvyāyāmena dīrghaṃ hi kālam akhidyamāno jñeyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣaṃ bhāvayati | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 140

children.text: ) samyaksmṛtyā śamathapragrahopekṣānimitteṣu layoddhatyābhāvānmārgasaṃmukhībhāvāyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣaṃ bhāvayati | samyaksamādhinā vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhārāyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣaṃ bhāvayatyevamaṣṭau mārgāṅgāni vyavasthāpyante |
children.translated_text: Through <s>samyaksmṛti</s> (right mindfulness), in the signs of calming, apprehension, and equanimity — from the absence of languor and agitation — one cultivates the antidote to the obscuration of the path, for the purpose of facing the path. Through <s>samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration), one cultivates the antidote to the obscuration for the purpose of producing the special qualities. Thus the eight path-factors are established.

body.translated_text: After the period of the factors of awakening, the conformity to awakening as it truly is — this is <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view). The determination, the delimitation, of that very awakening is <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention). And when that determination has been made by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in sūtras and the like, the entry into it — through the understanding of its meaning — [is what follows]. The purification of the threefold action is <s>samyagvāk</s> (right speech), <s>karmānta</s> (right action), and <s>ājīva</s> (right livelihood) — because they encompass the actions of speech, body, and both. The cultivation of the antidote is <s>samyagvyāyāma</s> (right effort) and the rest, for the obscurations of the knowable, of the path, and of the special quality, respectively. Through right effort, not wearying for a long time, one cultivates the antidote to the obscuration of the knowable.

body.text: śamathavipaśyanāvibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight):

children.translated_text: From the abiding of the mind in the mind, and from the investigation of phenomena,
relying on right concentration — <s>śamatha</s> and then <s>vipaśyanā</s>. || Msa_18.66 ||

body.text: samyaksamādhiṃ niśritya citte cittasyāvasthānāt | dharmāṇāṃ ca pravicayādyathākramaṃ śamatho vipaśyanā ca veditavyā | na tu vinā samyaksamādhinetyetacchamathavipaśyanālakṣaṇabhū |
body.translated_text: Relying on right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>), from the abiding of the mind in the mind, and from the investigation of phenomena, respectively, <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> should be understood. But not without right concentration — this is the characteristic ground of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>.

body.text: sarvatragā ca saikāṃśā naikāṃśopaniṣanmatā |
body.translated_text: It is universal, of one aspect, of two aspects, and considered a proximate cause.

body.text: sā ca śamathavipaśyanā sarvatragā yaṃ yaṃ guṇamākāṅkṣati tatra tatra tadbhāvanāt | yathoktaṃ sūtre | ākāṅkṣedbhikṣuraho vatāhaṃ viviktaṃ kāmairiti vistareṇa yāvat tena bhikṣuṇā imāveva dvau dharmau bhāvayitavyau | yaduta śamathaśca vipaśyanā cetyevamādi | ekāṃśā śamathavipaśyanā yadā śamathaṃ bhāvayati | vipaśyanāṃ vā | ubhayāṃśā yadā yugapadubhayaṃ bhāvayati | upaniṣatsaṃmatā śamathavipaśyanā bodhisattvānāmadhimukticaryābhūmau |
body.translated_text: And that <s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s> is universal — because wherever one desires a quality, one cultivates it there. As stated in the sūtra: 'A monk should wish, "May I indeed be secluded from sense-desires"' and so forth in detail, up to: 'That monk should cultivate these very two dharmas — namely, <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>.' And so forth. Of one aspect — <s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s> when one cultivates <s>śamatha</s> or <s>vipaśyanā</s> [separately]. Of two aspects — when one cultivates both simultaneously. Considered a proximate cause — <s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s> on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>).

body.text: prativedhe ca niryāṇe animitte hyasaṃskṛte || Msa_18.67 ||
body.translated_text: And in penetration, in progress, in the signless, in the unconditioned, || Msa_18.67 ||

children.translated_text: in purification, and in complete purification — <s>śamatha</s> and then <s>vipaśyanā</s>,

children.text: sarvabhūmigatā dhīre sa yogaḥ sarvasādhakaḥ || Msa_18.68 ||
children.translated_text: pervading all stages — for the steadfast, this is the yoga that accomplishes all. || Msa_18.68 ||

body.text: ityupaniṣanmatetyevamādinā śamathavipaśyanāyāḥ prabhedaḥ karma ca nirdiṣṭaṃ | yoga upāyo veditavyaḥ | tatra prativedhaḥ prathamabhūmipraveśaḥ | niryāṇaṃ yāvat ṣaṣṭhī bhūmiḥ | tābhiḥ sanimittaprayoganiryāṇāt | animittaṃ saptamī bhūmiḥ | asaṃskṛtamanyadbhūmitrayamanabhisaṃskāravāhitvāt | saṃskāro hi saṃskṛtaṃ tadatra nāstītyasaṃskṛtaṃ | tadeva ca bhūmitrayaṃ niśritya buddhakṣetraṃ ca pariśodhayitavyaṃ | buddhatvaṃ ca prāptavyaṃ | tadetadyathākramaṃ pariśuddhirviśuddhiśca |
body.translated_text: Thus, beginning with 'considered a proximate cause,' the division and function of <s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s> are indicated. 'Yoga' should be understood as 'method.' Therein, penetration is the entry into the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). Progress is up to the sixth stage — because through those [stages], progress is with signs and application. The signless is the seventh stage. The unconditioned is the other three stages — because they flow without [deliberate] conditioning; for conditioning is the conditioned, and that is absent here — thus 'unconditioned.' Relying on those same three stages, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) is to be purified and Buddhahood is to be attained — these are, respectively, purification and complete purification.

body.text: upāyakauśalyavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>):

children.translated_text: In the fulfillment of the <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, in the ripening of beings,

children.text: kṣipraprāptau kriyāśuddhau vartmācchede ca kauśalaṃ || Msa_18.69 ||
children.translated_text: in swift attainment, in the purification of activity, and in the non-cutting of the path — [there is] skill. || Msa_18.69 ||
In skillful means, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, on all stages, possess unequalled
skill, relying on which they accomplish all purposes. || Msa_18.70 ||

body.text: anenopāyakauśalyasya prabhedaḥ karma ca darśitaṃ | tatra buddhadharmaparipūraye nirvikalpaṃ jñānamupāyaḥ | sattvaparipācane catvāri saṃgrahavastūni | kṣiprābhisaṃbodhe sarvaṃ pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi yāvad bhavatu me jñānaṃ saṃbodhāyeti pratideśanānumodanādhyeṣaṇā pariṇāmanā | kriyāśuddhau samādhidhāraṇīmukhāni | taiḥ sarvārthakriyāsādhanāt | vartmānupacchede apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇe | asmin pañcavidha upāye sarvabhūmiṣu bodhisattvānāmasamaṃ tadanyaiḥ kauśalamityayaṃ prabhedaḥ | sarvasvaparārthasādhanaṃ karma |
body.translated_text: By this, the division and function of skillful means are shown. Therein, for the fulfillment of <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, non-conceptual knowledge is the skillful means. For the ripening of beings, the four means of attraction. For swift awakening — 'I confess all evil' up to 'may knowledge be mine for awakening' — [these are] confession, rejoicing, supplication, and dedication. For the purification of activity, <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateways — because through them, the accomplishment of all purposes and activities is achieved. For the non-cutting of the path, non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>). In these fivefold skillful means, the unequalled skill of <s>bodhisattvas</s> on all stages compared to others — this is the division. The accomplishment of all purposes of self and others is the function.

body.text: dhāraṇīvibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention):

children.translated_text: Through maturation, through the practice of hearing, and also through <s>samādhi</s> — <s>dhāraṇī</s> [arises];

children.text: parīttā mahatī sā ca mahatī trividhā punaḥ || Msa_18.71 ||
children.translated_text: it is small and great, and the great is again threefold. || Msa_18.71 ||
For those who have not entered and those who have entered [the stages], among the wise, it is soft and middling;
for those on the impure stages it is great, and [greater still] on the pure stages. || Msa_18.72 ||
Relying on that <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> again and again

children.text: prakāśayanti saddharmaṃ nityaṃ saṃdhārayanti ca || Msa_18.73 ||
children.translated_text: illuminate the true Dharma and constantly retain it. || Msa_18.73 ||

body.text: atrāpi prabhedaḥ karma ca dhāraṇyāḥ saṃdarśitaṃ | tatra trividhā dhāraṇī | pūrvakarmavipākena | śrutābhyāsena | dṛṣṭadharmabāhuśrutyena grahaṇadhāraṇasāmarthyaviśeṣaṇāt | samādhisaṃniśrayeṇa ca | sā punarvipākaśrutābhyāsābhyāṃ parīttā veditavyā | samādhinā mahatī | sāpi mahatī punastrividhā | abhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ mṛdvī bhūmipraviṣṭānām aśuddhabhūmikānāṃ madhyā saptasu bhūmiṣu | pariśuddhabhūmikā tvadhimātrā śeṣāsu bhūmiṣu ityayaṃ prabhedo dhāraṇyāḥ | saddharmasya prakāśanaṃ dhāraṇaṃ ca karma |
body.translated_text: Here also, the division and function of <s>dhāraṇī</s> are shown. Therein, <s>dhāraṇī</s> is threefold: through the maturation of previous <s>karma</s>; through the practice of hearing — from the special power of retention and holding through great learning in the present life; and through the support of <s>samādhi</s>. Furthermore, that [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] arising from maturation and the practice of hearing should be understood as small. That arising from <s>samādhi</s> is great. And that great one is again threefold: soft — for those who have not entered the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>). Middling — for those who have entered the impure stages, on the seven stages. Intense — on the pure stages, on the remaining stages. This is the division of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. The illumination and retention of the true Dharma is its function.

body.text: praṇidhānavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of <s>praṇidhāna</s> (aspiration):

children.text: cetanā chandasahitā jñānena preritā ca tat |
children.translated_text: Volition accompanied by desire, impelled by knowledge — that
is the aspiration of the steadfast, unequalled on all stages. || Msa_18.74 ||

children.text: hetubhūtaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ cittātsadyaḥ phalaṃ ca tat |
children.translated_text: And it should be known as being a cause, and its fruit arises immediately from the mind;
for the accomplishment of goals in the future, through the fulfillment from mind alone. || Msa_18.75 ||
It is varied, great, and pure, on successively higher stages,
up to awakening — for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, it accomplishes the welfare of self and others. || Msa_18.76 ||

body.text: atra praṇidhānaṃ svabhāvato nidānato bhūmitaḥ prabhedataḥ karmataśca paridīpitaṃ | cetanā chandasaṃprayuktā svabhāvaḥ | jñānaṃ nidānaṃ | sarvabhūmiṣviti bhūmiḥ | tacca praṇidhānaṃ hetubhūtaṃ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 142

children.text: ) cittādeva sadyaḥ phalatvāt | āyatyāṃ vā[cā]bhipretārthasiddhyarthaṃ cittātpunaḥ sadyaḥphalaṃ cittamātrāt yathābhipretārthasamṛddhitā[to] | veditavyā[vyaṃ] | yena praṇidhānena balikā bodhisattvā vikrīḍanti | yasya na sukarā saṃkhyā kartuṃ kāyasya veti vistaraḥ | citramadhimukticaryābhūmāvevaṃ caivaṃ ca syāmiti | mahadbhumipraviṣṭasya daśa mahāpraṇidhānāni | viśuddhamuttarottarāsu bhūmiṣu viśuddhiviśeṣādābodherityeṣa prabhedataḥ | svaparārthaprasādhanaṃ karma |
children.translated_text: because its fruit arises immediately from the mind. Or for the accomplishment of the intended goal in the future — its fruit again arises immediately from the mind, through the fulfillment in accordance with intention from mind alone. This should be understood — whereby young <s>bodhisattvas</s> play, and of which it is not easy to count the bodies, and so forth in detail. 'Varied' — on the stage of devoted conduct, thinking 'may I be thus and thus.' 'Great' — for one who has entered the stages, the ten great aspirations. 'Pure' — on successively higher stages, from the special purity, up to awakening — this is the division. The accomplishment of the welfare of self and others is the function.

body.translated_text: Here, aspiration is illuminated in terms of its intrinsic nature, origin, stages, division, and function. Volition conjoined with desire is its intrinsic nature. Knowledge is its origin. 'On all stages' refers to the stages. And that aspiration is a cause,

body.text: samādhitrayavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of the three <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations):

children.translated_text: The twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) should be known, as well as the basis of the grasping of self;
and the constant pacification of that — these are the domain of the three <s>samādhis</s>. || Msa_18.77 ||

body.text: trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ trividho gocaro jñeyaḥ | pudgaladharmanairātmyaṃ śūnyatāsamādheḥ | tadubhayātmagrāhasyāśrayaḥ pañcopādānaskandhā apraṇihitasamādheḥ | tasyāśrayasyātyantopaśama ānimittasamādhiḥ | sa eva |
body.translated_text: The threefold domain of the three <s>samādhis</s> should be known: the selflessness of person and phenomena is [the domain] of the <s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s> (concentration on emptiness). The basis of the grasping of self in both — the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) — is [the domain] of the <s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s> (concentration without aspiration). The complete pacification of that basis is the <s>ānimittasamādhi</s> (signless concentration). That very [threefold samādhi] —

body.text: samādhistrividho jñeyo grāhyagrāhakabhāvataḥ |
body.translated_text: The threefold <s>samādhi</s> should be known from the nature of the apprehended and the apprehender.

body.text: trividhaśca grāhyasya gocarasya grāhakā ye samādhayaḥ | te śūnyatādisamādhayaḥ iti grāhyagrāhakabhāvena trayaḥ samādhayo jñātavyāḥ | te punaryathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: And the threefold — the apprehended is the domain, and the apprehenders are the <s>samādhis</s>. Those <s>samādhis</s> beginning with <s>śūnyatā</s> — thus, through the nature of apprehended and apprehender, the three <s>samādhis</s> should be known. They, in order, are:

body.text: nirvikalpo 'pi vimukho ratiyuktaśca sarvadā || Msa_18.78 ||
body.translated_text: non-conceptual, turned away, and always connected with delight. || Msa_18.78 ||

body.text: śūnyatāsamādhirnirvikalpaḥ | pudgaladharmātmanoravikalpanāt | apraṇihito vimukhastasmādātmagrāhāśrayāt | ānimitto ratisaṃprayuktaḥ sarvakālaṃ tasmiṃstadāśrayopaśame |
body.translated_text: The <s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s> (emptiness concentration) is non-conceptual — because of the non-conceptualization of the self of persons and phenomena. The <s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s> (aspirationless concentration) is turned away — from that basis of the grasping of self. The <s>ānimittasamādhi</s> (signless concentration) is connected with delight at all times — in the pacification of that basis.

children.translated_text: For the purpose of full knowledge, for the purpose of abandonment,
and for the purpose of direct realization — the threefold meaning of the <s>samādhis</s> beginning with <s>śūnyatā</s> is proclaimed. || Msa_18.79 ||

body.text: pudgaladharma naierātmyayoḥ parijñārthaṃ śūnyatā | tadātmagrāhāśrayasya prahāṇārthamapraṇihitaḥ | tadupaśamasya sākṣātkriyārthamānimittaḥ samādhiḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness concentration) is for the purpose of the full knowledge of the selflessness of persons and phenomena. The <s>apraṇihita</s> (aspirationless concentration) is for the purpose of the abandonment of the basis of that self-grasping. The <s>ānimitta</s> (signless concentration) is for the purpose of the direct realization of the pacification of that.

body.text: dharmoddānavibhāge ślokau |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the Dharma-summaries (<s>dharmoddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The fourfold Dharma-summary, as the proximate cause of <s>samādhi</s>,
has been taught to <s>bodhisattvas</s>, out of the desire for the welfare of beings. || Msa_18.80 ||

body.text: tatra sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārā duḥkhāḥ ityapraṇihitasya samādherūpaniṣadbhāvena deśitaṃ | sarvadharmā anātmāna iti śūnyatāyāḥ | śāntaṃ nirvāṇamiti ānimittasya samādheḥ | kaḥ punaranityārtho yāvacchāntārthaḥ ityāha |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'all conditioned phenomena are impermanent' and 'all conditioned phenomena are suffering' — these are taught as the proximate cause of the <s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s> (aspirationless concentration). 'All phenomena are without self' — as [the proximate cause] of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness concentration). '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peace' — as [the proximate cause] of the <s>ānimittasamādhi</s> (signless concentration). What then is the meaning of impermanence, up to the meaning of peace? He says:

children.translated_text: The meaning of non-existence, the meaning of non-conceptualization, and the meaning of mere imagination —
and [meaning] the pacification of conceptualization — this is the fourfold [interpretation] for the wise. || Msa_18.81 ||

body.text: bodhisattvānāmasadartho 'nityārthaḥ | yannityaṃ nāsti tadanityaṃ teṣāṃ yatparikalpitalakṣaṇam | abhūtavikalpārtho duḥkhārtho yatparatantralakṣaṇaṃ | parikalpamātrārtho 'nātmārthaḥ | evaśabdenāvadhāraṇaṃ parikalpita ātmā nāsti parikalpamātraṃ tvastīti parikalpitalakṣaṇasyābhāvārtho 'nātmārtha ityuktaṃ bhavati | vikalpopaśamārthaḥ śāntārthaḥ pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ | kṣaṇabhaṅgārtho 'pyanityārtho veditavyaḥ paratantralakṣaṇasya | atastatprasādhanārthaṃ kṣaṇikatvavibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the meaning of 'non-existent' is the meaning of 'impermanent': what is permanent does not exist, that is impermanent — for them, this is the imagined characteristic (<s>parikalpitalakṣaṇa</s>). The meaning of 'unreal conceptualization' is the meaning of 'suffering' — that is the dependent characteristic (<s>paratantralakṣaṇa</s>). The meaning of 'mere conceptualization' is the meaning of 'non-self': the word 'merely' indicates delimitation — the imagined self does not exist, but mere conceptualization does exist — thus it is said that the meaning of the non-existence of the imagined characteristic is the meaning of 'non-self.' The meaning of 'pacification of conceptualization' is the meaning of 'peace' — the perfected characteristic (<s>pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa</s>) is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The meaning of 'momentary destruction' should also be understood as the meaning of 'impermanent,' pertaining to the dependent characteristic. Therefore, for the purpose of establishing that, ten verses on the division of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>):

children.translated_text: From the impossibility [of continuity] without [momentariness], from arising from causes, from [the] contradiction [between arising and ceasing], from the inability to abide by itself,
from the non-existence [of a cause of abiding], from the invariability of the characteristic [of impermanence], from continuity [through similarity], and from cessation; || Msa_18.82 ||
and from the perception of transformation, from its being a cause and an effect of that [which is momentary],
and from its being appropriated and dominated, and from its conformity with pure beings — || Msa_18.83 ||

body.text: tatra kṣaṇikaṃ sarvaṃ saṃskṛtamiti paścādvacanadiyaṃ pratijñā veditavyā | tatpunaḥ kathaṃ sidhyati | kṣaṇikatvamantareṇa saṃskārāṇāṃ pravṛtterayogāt | prabandhena hi vṛttiḥ pravṛttiḥ | sā cāntareṇa pratikṣaṇamutpādanirodhau na yujyate | atha kālāntaraṃ sthitvā pūrvottaranirodhotpādataḥ prabandheneṣyate vṛttiḥ | tadanantaraṃ pravṛttirna syāt prabandhābhāvāt | naiva cotpannasya vinā prabandhena kālāntaraṃ bhāvo yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ hetuta utpattiḥ | hetuto hi sarvaṃ saṃskṛtamutpadyate bhavatītyarthaḥ | tadyadi bhūtvā punaruttarakālaṃ bhavati tasyāvaśyaṃ hetunā bhavitavyaṃ | vinā hetunā ādita ivā[evā]bhāvāt | na ca tattenaiva hetunā bhavitumarhati tasyopayu[bhu]ktahetukatvāt | na cānyo heturupalambhate | tasmātpratikṣaṇamavaśyaṃ pūrvahetukamanyadbhavatīti veditavyaṃ | evaṃ vinā prabandhenotpannasya kālāntaraṃ bhāvo na yujyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the thesis to be stated below should be understood as: 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) are momentary.' How then is this established? Because the continuity of conditioned things is impossible without momentariness. For activity is operation through a continuum, and that is not possible without arising and ceasing at every moment. If one were to suppose that [something] abides for a period of time and then there is a continuum through the cessation of the earlier and the arising of the later — in that case, there would be no [immediate] activity, because of the absence of a continuum. Nor is it possible for something that has arisen to exist for a period of time without a continuum. For what reason? Because arising is from causes. For all conditioned things arise — that is, come into existence — from causes. If something, having come into being, were to exist again at a later time, it would necessarily need a cause [for that continued existence], since without a cause it would not exist, just as it did not exist at the beginning. And it cannot exist by that very same cause, since that cause has been consumed. Nor is another cause apprehended. Therefore, it should be understood that at every moment something different arises, caused by the previous [moment]. Thus, it is not possible for something that has arisen to exist for a period of time without a continuum.

body.text: athāpyevamiṣyeta notpannaṃ punarutpadyate yadarthaṃ hetunā bhavitavyaṃ syādutpannaṃ tu kālāntareṇa paścānnirudhyate notpannamātrameveti | tatpaścātkena nirudhyate | yadyutpādahetunaiva tadayuktaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇam | utpādanirodhayorvirodhāt | na hi virodhayostulyo heturupalabhyate | tadyathā chāyātapayoḥ śītoṣṇayośca | kālāntaranirodhasyaiva ca virodhāt | kena virodhāt | āgamena ca | yaduktaṃ bhagavatā | māyopamāste bhikṣo saṃskārā āpāyikāstāvatkālikā itvarapratyupasthāyina iti | manaskāreṇa ca yogināṃ | te hi saṃskārāṇāmudayavyayau manasikurvantaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ teṣāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyanti | anyathā hi teṣāmapi nirvidvirāgavimuktayo na syuryathānyeṣāṃ maraṇakālādiṣu nirodhaṃ paśyatāṃ | yadi cotpannaḥ saṃskāraḥ kālāntaraṃ tiṣṭhet sa svayameva vā tiṣṭhetsvayameva sthātuṃ samarthaḥ | sthitikāraṇena (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 144

children.text: ) vā kenacit | svayaṃ tāvadavasthānamayuktaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | paścātsvayamasthiteḥ | kena vā so 'nte punaḥ sthātuṃ na samarthaḥ | sthitikāraṇenāpi na yuktaṃ tasyābhāvāt | na hi tatkiṃcidupalabhyate | athāpi syādvināpi sthitikāraṇena vināśakāraṇābhāvāt avatiṣṭhate | labdhe tu vināśakāraṇe paścādvinaśyati agnimeva śyāmateti | tadayuktaṃ, tasyābhāvāt | na hi vināśakāraṇaṃ paścādapi kiṃcidasti | agnināpi śyāmatā vinasyatīti suprasiddhaṃ [na prasiddhaṃ,] | visadṛśotpattau tu tasya sāmarthyaṃ prasiddhaṃ | tathā hi tatsaṃbandhāt śyāmatāyāḥ saṃtatirvisadṛśī gṛhyate na tu sarvathaivāpravṛttiḥ | apāmapi kvāthyamānānāmagnisambandhādalpataratamotpattito 'timāndyādante punaranutpattirgṛhyate | na tu sakṛdevāgnisaṃbandhāttadabhāvaḥ | naiva cotpannasya kasyacid[ta] sthānaṃ yujyate | lakṣaṇaikāntyāt | aikāntikaṃ hyetatsaṃskṛtalakṣaṇamuktaṃ bhagavatā yaduta saṃskṛtasyānityatā | tadyadi notpannamātraṃ vinaśyet | kaṃcitkālamasyānityatā na syāditi anaikāntikamanityatālakṣaṇaṃ prasahya[jya]te | athāpi syātpratikṣaṇamapūrvotpattau tadevedamiti pratyabhijñānaṃ na syāditi | tadbhavatyeva sādṛśyasya anuvṛttermāyākāra pa[pha]lakavat | sādṛśyāttadbuddhirna tadbhāvāditi | kathaṃ gamyate | nirodhataḥ | na hi tathaivāvasthitasyānte nirodhaḥ syādādikṣaṇanirviśiṣṭatvāt | tasmānna tattadevetyavadhāryate ante pariṇāmopalabdheśca | pariṇāmo hi nāmānyathātvaṃ | tadyadi nādita evārabdhaṃ bhavedādhyātmikabāhyānāṃ bhāvānāmante pariṇāmo nopalabhyeta | tasmādādita evānyathātvamārabdhaṃ yatkrameṇābhivardhamānamante vyaktimāpadyate kṣīrasyeva dadyavasthāyāṃ | yāvattu tadanyathātvaṃ sūkṣmatvānna paricchidyate | tāvatsādṛśyānuvṛttestadevedamimi [ti]jñāyata iti siddhaṃ | tataśca pratikṣaṇamanyathātvāt | kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ | kutaśca prasiddhaṃ | taddhetutvaphalatvataḥ | kṣaṇikahetutvāt | kṣaṇikaphalatvāccetyarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) Now, self-persistence is unreasonable. For what reason? Because afterward it is unable to persist by itself. Why is it unable to persist by itself at the end? Persistence through a cause of persistence is also not reasonable, because of its non-existence — for no such [cause of persistence] is apprehended. Even if one were to suppose that it persists through the absence of a cause of destruction even without a cause of persistence, and that it is destroyed afterward when a cause of destruction is obtained — like a pot [destroyed] by fire — that is unreasonable, because of the non-existence of such [a cause of destruction]. For there is no cause of destruction afterward either. And that 'a pot is destroyed by fire' is well-known, [but not as complete annihilation]; rather, the capacity of fire for producing a dissimilar [effect] is what is well-known. For from the connection with fire, the continuum of the pot is apprehended as dissimilar, but not as the complete cessation of all activity. And with waters being heated, too, from the connection with fire, the arising of progressively less [water] is apprehended due to extreme diminishment, and finally non-arising — but not that from a single contact with fire there is complete non-existence. Nor is the persistence of anything that has arisen possible — because of the invariability of the characteristic [of impermanence]. For this characteristic of the conditioned has been declared invariable by the <s>Bhagavān</s> — namely, the impermanence of the conditioned. If something were not destroyed immediately upon arising, then for some period of time it would not have the characteristic of impermanence — thus the invariability of the characteristic of impermanence would be violated. And even if one were to object that with moment-by-moment novel arising, there would be no recognition that 'this is the same thing' — that [recognition] indeed occurs because of the continuity of similarity, like a magician's illusion or a reflection. The cognition 'this is the same' is from similarity, not from [actual] identity. How is this known? From cessation. For something that persists in the very same way would not cease at the end, being undifferentiated from the initial moment. Therefore, it is not ascertained that 'this is the very same thing' — also from the perception of transformation at the end. For transformation is indeed alteration. If alteration had not begun from the very start, the transformation of internal and external entities would not be perceived at the end. Therefore, alteration begins from the very start, and progressively increasing, it becomes manifest at the end — like milk in the stage of curds. As long as that alteration is not discerned because of its subtlety, for that long, due to the continuity of similarity, it is known as 'this is the same thing' — this is established. And from that, because of moment-by-moment alteration, momentariness is established. And from what else is it established? From being the cause and the effect of that [which is momentary] — meaning because of being the cause of what is momentary and the effect of what is momentary.

body.translated_text: Even if one were to accept the following: 'What has arisen does not arise again — for which purpose a cause would be needed — but what has arisen simply ceases after a period of time, not immediately upon arising' — then by what does it cease afterward? If by the very cause of arising itself, that is unreasonable. For what reason? Because of the contradiction between arising and ceasing. For a common cause for contradictory things is not found — just as for shade and sunshine, or for cold and heat. And because of the contradiction with ceasing after a period of time — with what contradiction? With scripture — as the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Conditioned things, O monk, are like an illusion, destined for the lower realms, so momentary, so quickly present [and gone].' And with the mental attention of <s>yogins</s> — for they, attending to the arising and passing of conditioned things, see their cessation at every moment. For otherwise, they too would not attain revulsion, dispassion, and liberation — just like others who see cessation only at the time of death and the like. And if a conditioned thing that has arisen were to persist for a period of time, it would either persist by itself — being capable of persisting by itself — or through some cause of persistence. (

body.text: kṣaṇikaṃ hi cittaṃ prasiddhaṃ tasya cānye saṃskārāścakṣurūpādayo hetutaḥ | tasmātte 'pi kṣaṇikā iti siddhaṃ | na tvakṣaṇikāt kṣaṇikaṃ bhavitumarhati yathā nityādanityamiti | cittasya khalvapi sarve saṃskārāḥ phalaṃ | kathamidaṃ gamyate | upāttatvādādhipatyācchuddhasattvānuvṛttitaśca | cittena hi sarve saṃskārāścakṣurādayaḥ sādhiṣṭhānā upāttāḥ sahasaṃmurchanāḥ tadanugrahānuvṛttitaḥ | tasmātte cittasya phalaṃ | cittasya cādhipatyaṃ saṃskāreṣu | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā | cittenāyaṃ loko nīyate cittena parikṛṣyate cittasyotpannasyotpannasya vaśe vartate iti | tathā vijñānapratyayaṃ nāma rūpamityuktaṃ | tasmāccittasya phalaṃ | śuddhacittānuvṛttitaśca | śuddhaṃ hi yogināṃ cittaṃ saṃskārā anuvartante | yathoktaṃ | dhyāyī bhikṣuḥ ṛddhimāṃścittavaśe prāpta imaṃ dāruskandhaṃ sacet suvarṇamadhimucyate tadapyasya tathaiva (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 145

children.text: ) syāditi | tasmādapi cittaphalaṃ saṃskārāḥ | sattvānuvṛttitaśca | tathā hi pāpakāriṣu sattveṣu bāhyā bhāvā hīnā bhavanti | puṇyakāriṣu ca praṇītāḥ | atastaccittānuvartanāt cittaphalatvaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ siddhaṃ | tataśca teṣāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ | na hi kṣaṇikasyākṣaṇikaṃ phalaṃ yujyate tadanuvidhāyitvāt | evaṃ tāvadaviśeṣeṇa saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ dvābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ sādhitam |
children.translated_text: ) Therefore too, conditioned things are the effect of mind. And because of the conformity with [the character of] beings — for when beings are evil-doers, external things become inferior; and when they are meritorious, [external things become] excellent. Thus, from the conformity with their minds, the status of conditioned things as effects of mind is established. And from that, their momentariness [is established] — for an effect of something momentary cannot reasonably be non-momentary, because of conforming to it. Thus far, the momentariness of conditioned things in general has been established by two verses.

body.translated_text: For it is well-established that mind (<s>citta</s>) is momentary, and other conditioned things such as the eye, form, and so forth are its causes. Therefore, they too are established as momentary — for something non-momentary cannot be the [cause of] something momentary, just as something permanent [cannot produce] something impermanent. Moreover, all conditioned things are the effect of mind. How is this known? Because of being appropriated, because of [mind's] dominance, and because of conformity with pure beings. For all conditioned things such as the eye and so forth are appropriated by mind — sustained together with it, depending on its maintenance and conformity. Therefore, they are the effect of mind. And mind has dominance over conditioned things, as was stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This world is led by mind, drawn by mind, and when mind arises, it is under the power of that arisen [mind].' And it is said: 'Name-and-form has consciousness as its condition.' Therefore, they are the effect of mind. And because of the conformity of conditioned things with pure mind — for the conditioned things of <s>yogins</s> whose minds are pure conform [to that purity]. As was stated: 'A meditating monk who possesses supernatural powers, having attained mastery of mind — if he resolves that this log of wood is gold, it becomes just so for him.' (

body.text: ādhyātmikānāṃ punaḥ sādhanārthaṃ pañca ślokā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, for the purpose of establishing [the momentariness] of internal [conditioned things], five verses should be understood:

children.translated_text: Through the initial [arising], through gradation, through accumulation, through being a basis,
through modification and ripening, and likewise through inferior and superior [states]; || Msa_18.84 ||
through luminous and non-luminous [states], through going to another place,
through the state of having seeds and being seedless, and through reflections — [these are] the types of arising. || Msa_18.85 ||
In the fourteen types of arising, from the distinction of having a cause,
from the impossibility of the purpose of accumulation and [impossibility] without [momentariness], from the impossibility of being a basis; || Msa_18.86 ||
from the impossibility of persistence at the end, from the non-transformation of the initial [moment],
and likewise regarding inferior and superior states, and luminous and non-luminous [states]; || Msa_18.87 ||
from the non-existence of [actual] going, from the impossibility of the persistence of what has gone, from the impossibility of the final [seedless state],
and from the conformity with mind — all conditioned things are momentary. || Msa_18.88 ||

body.text: ādyastaratamenāpi yāvatkṣaṇikaṃ sarvasaṃskṛtamiti | kathameṣāmebhiḥ kṣaṇikatvaṃ sidhyati | ādhyātmikānāṃ hi saṃskārāṇāṃ caturdaśavidha utpādaḥ | ādya utpādo yāvatprathamata ātmabhāvābhinirvṛttiḥ | taratamena yaḥ prathamajanmakṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ | cayena ya āhārasvapnabrahmacaryāsamāpattyupacayena | āśrayabhāvataḥ yaścakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ cakṣurādībhirāśrayaiḥ | vikāreṇa yo rāgādibhirvarṇādivipariṇāmataḥ | paripākena yo garbhabālakumārayuvamadhyamavṛddhāvasthāsu | hīnatvena viśiṣṭatvena ca yo durgatau [sugatau?] cotpadyamānānāṃ yathākramaṃ | bhāsvaratvena yo nirmitakāmeṣu paranirmitakāmeṣu rūpārūpyeṣu copapannānāṃ cittamātrādhīnatvāt | abhāsvaratvena yastadanyatropapannānāṃ | deśāntaragamanena yo 'nyadeśotpādanirodhe 'nyadeśotpādaḥ | sabījatvena yo 'hartaścaramān skandhānvarjayitvā | abījatvena yasteṣāmevārhataścarameṣāṃ | pratibimbatvena yo aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyināṃ samādhivaśena pratibimbānāṃ[khyānāṃ] saṃskārāṇāmutpādaḥ | etasyāṃ caturdaśavidhāyāmutpattāvādhyātmikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ hetumānaviśeṣādibhiḥ kāraṇairveditavyam | ādyotpāde tāvat hetutvaviśeṣāt | yadi hi tasya hetutvena viśeṣo na syāt taduttarāyāḥ saṃskārapravṛtteruttarottaraviśeṣo (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 146

children.text: ) nopalabhyeta hetvaviśeṣāt | viśeṣe ca sati taduttarebhyastasyānyatvāt kṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ | taratamotpāde mānaviśeṣāt | mānaṃ pramāṇamityarthaḥ | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ vinānyatvena parimāṇaviśeṣo bhavet | upacayotpāde cayāpārthyāt | upastambho hi cayaḥ | tasyāpārthyaṃ syādantareṇa kṣaṇikatvaṃ tathaivāvasthitatvāt | ayogāccopacayasyaiva | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ vinā puṣṭatarotpattyā yujyetopacayaḥ | āśrayabhāvenotpattāvāśritatvāsaṃbhavāt | na hi tiṣṭhatyāśraye ca tadāśritasyānavasthānaṃ yujyate | yāne tiṣṭhati tadārūḍhānavasthānavadanyathā hyāśrayatvaṃ na saṃbhavet | vikārotpattau paripākotpattau ca sthitasyāsaṃbhavāt | ādyanāśāvikārataḥ | na hi tathāsthitasyaiva rāgādibhirvikāraḥ saṃbhavati | na cāvasthāntareṣu paripāka ādāvavināśe satyante vikārābhāvāt | tathā hīnaviśiṣṭotpattau kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā vikāraparipākotpattau | na hi tathāsthiteṣveva saṃskāreṣu karmavāsanā vṛttiṃ labhate yato durgatau vā syādutpattiḥ sugatau vā | krameṇa hi saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣāt vṛttilābho yujyate | bhāsvarābhāsvare 'pi cotpāde tathaiva kṣaṇikatvaṃ yujyate | bhāsvare tāvat tathāsthitasyāsaṃbhavāt cittādhīnavṛttitāyāḥ | abhāsvare 'pi cādau vināśamantareṇānte vikārāyogāt |
children.translated_text: ) would not be observed, because of the non-distinction of the cause. And when there is distinction, because [the subsequent] is different from the preceding ones, momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) is established. In the production of degrees [of size], from the distinction of measure (<s>māna</s>). 'Measure' means means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). For without being different at each moment, there would be no distinction of measure. In the production of growth, because accumulation would be purposeless. For accumulation (<s>caya</s>) is support (<s>upastambha</s>). Its purposelessness would follow without momentariness, since [things] would remain in the same state. And of the accumulation itself there is no possibility. For without [change] at each moment, accumulation would not be possible through the production of a more nourished [state]. In production through the nature of a support (<s>āśraya</s>), because what is supported could not exist [otherwise]. For when the support is standing, it is not appropriate that what is supported thereon would not remain — just as when a vehicle stands still, its riders do not [fail to] remain. Otherwise the state of being a support would not be possible. In the production of transformation and in the production of ripening, because [these] are impossible for something that remains [unchanged]. [This is known] from there being no transformation without initial destruction. For transformation through redness and the like is not possible for something remaining in the same state. Nor is there ripening in successive states when there is no destruction at the beginning, because of the absence of transformation at the end. Similarly, in the production of what is inferior and superior, momentariness should be understood just as in the production of transformation and ripening. For the imprints of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmavāsanā</s>) do not gain operation in formations that remain in the same state, from which there would be birth in a bad destiny or a good destiny. For the gaining of operation is appropriate through a gradual particular transformation of the continuum (<s>saṃtati</s>). In the production of the luminous (<s>bhāsvara</s>) and the non-luminous (<s>abhāsvara</s>) [minds] too, momentariness is similarly appropriate. For the luminous [mind], because it is impossible for something remaining in the same state, since its operation depends on the mind (<s>citta</s>). For the non-luminous [mind] too, because of the impossibility of transformation at the end without destruction at the beginning.

body.translated_text: From 'through the initial [arising]' up to 'all conditioned things are momentary': how is the momentariness of these established by these [arguments]? For the arising of internal conditioned things is of fourteen kinds: the initial arising is the first production of an individual existence (<s>ātmabhāva</s>). Through gradation — that which follows from the first moment of birth onward. Through accumulation — that through the accumulation [of the body] by food, sleep, celibacy, and attainment. Through being a basis — that [arising] of eye-consciousness and the rest through their bases, the eye and so forth. Through modification — that through the transformation of complexion and the like due to passion and the rest. Through ripening — that in the stages of embryo, infant, youth, young adult, middle-age, and old age. Through inferior and superior states — that, respectively, of those being reborn in lower and higher destinies. Through luminosity — that of those reborn in the heavens of self-created enjoyment, the heavens of enjoyment created by others, and the form and formless realms, because of their dependence on mind alone. Through non-luminosity — that of those reborn elsewhere. Through going to another place — that arising in another place upon the cessation in one place. Through having seeds — that [arising] of the <s>Arhat</s> (one who has destroyed the defilements), excepting the final aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). Through being seedless — that of those very final [aggregates] of the <s>Arhat</s>. Through reflections — that arising of conditioned things that are reflections (<s>pratibimba</s>) by the power of <s>samādhi</s> for those who meditate on the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>). In these fourteen types of arising of internal conditioned things, momentariness should be understood through the reasons such as 'from the distinction of having a cause' and so forth. In the initial arising, first, from the distinction of causality — for if there were no distinction in its causality, there would be no progressive distinction in the subsequent activity of conditioned things. (

body.text: deśāntaragamanenotpattau gatyabhāvāt | na hi saṃskārāṇāṃ deśāntarasaṃkrāntilakṣaṇā gatirnāma kācit kriyā yujyate | sā hyutpannā vā saṃskāraṃ deśāntaraṃ gamayedanutpannā vā | yadyutpannā tena gatikāle na kaṃcidgata iti sthitasyaiva gamanaṃ nopapadyate | athānutpannā tenāsatyāṃ gatau gata iti na yujyate | sā ca kriyā yadi taddeśastha eva saṃskāre kāritraṃ karoti na yujyate | sthitasyānyadeśāprāpteḥ | athānyadeśasthe na yujyate | vinā kriyayānyadeśāprāpteḥ | na ca kriyā tatra vā anyatra vā deśe sthitā saṃskārādanyopalabhyate | tasmānnāsti saṃskārāṇāṃ deśāntarasaṃtatyutpādādanyā gatiḥ | tadabhāvācca siddhaṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ | deśāntaranirantarotpattilakṣaṇā gatirvibhavadbhiḥ kāraṇairveditavyā | asti cittavaśena yathā caṅkramaṇādyavasthāsu | asti pūrvakarmāvedhena yathāntarābhavaḥ | astyabhidhāta[astyākṣipta]vaśena yathā kṣiptasyeṣoḥ | asti saṃbandhavaśena yathā yānanadīplavārūḍhānāṃ | asti nodanavaśena yathā vāyupreritānāṃ tṛṇādīnām | asti svabhāvavaśena yathā vāyostiryaggamanamagnerūrdhvaṃ jvalanamapāṃ nimne syandanaṃ | astyanubhāvena yathā mantrauṣadhānubhāvena | keṣāṃcidayaskāntānubhāvenāyasāṃ | ṛddhyanubhāvena ṛddhimatāṃ | sabījābījabhāvenotpattau kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ sthitāyogāccaramāsaṃbhavācca | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ hetubhāvamantareṇa tathāsthitasyānyasminkāle punarbījabhāvo yujyate | nirbījatvaṃ vā carame kṣaṇe | na ca śakyaṃ (

children.translated_text: [page break: MSA Bagchi 147]

children.text: ) pūrvaṃ sabījatvaṃ carame kṣaṇe nirbījatvamabhyupagantuṃ | tadabhāve caramatvāsaṃbhavāt | tathā hi caramatvameva na saṃbhavati | pratibimbotpattau kṣaṇikatvaṃ cittānuvṛttito veditavyaṃ | pratikṣaṇaṃ cittavaśena tadutpādāt | ekāntāt[evaṃ tāvat]sādhitamādhyātmikaṃ sarvasaṃskṛtaṃ kṣaṇikamiti |
children.translated_text: ) that there is a seed-bearing state before and a seedless state in the final moment. Because in the absence of that [momentary change], the final character would not be possible. For indeed, the final character itself is not possible [without momentariness]. In the production of a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), momentariness should be understood from the conformity with mind (<s>cittānuvṛtti</s>). For at each moment, [the reflection] is produced through the power of the mind. Thus, it is established conclusively that all internal conditioned things (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) are momentary.

body.translated_text: In the production [of phenomena] through movement to another place, because movement (<s>gati</s>) [as real travel] does not exist. For no action called 'movement' — characterized by the transmigration of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) to another place — is appropriate. For it [movement] would either have arisen or not have arisen before making the formation go to another place. If it has arisen, then at the time of movement it has not gone anywhere — thus movement of what is standing still is not tenable. If it has not arisen, then when movement does not exist, [the thing is said to have] 'gone' — that is not appropriate. And if that action produces its effect in the formation situated in that very place — that is not appropriate, because what is stationary does not reach another place. And if [it produces its effect] in [the formation] situated in another place — that is not appropriate, because [it] does not reach another place without action. And no action situated in that place or in another place is observed as other than the formation. Therefore, there is no movement of formations other than the production of a continuum in another place. And from the absence of that [real movement], momentariness is established. Movement characterized by the production of an uninterrupted [continuum] in another place should be understood as [arising] from various causes: there is [movement] through the power of mind, as in the states of walking and the like; there is [movement] through the impetus of prior <s>karma</s>, as in the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>); there is [movement] through the power of being propelled, as with a shot arrow; there is [movement] through the power of connection, as with those mounted on a vehicle, boat, or river; there is [movement] through the power of propulsion, as with grasses and the like driven by the wind; there is [movement] through the power of inherent nature, as with the sideways movement of wind, the upward blazing of fire, and the downward flowing of water; there is [movement] through efficacy (<s>anubhāva</s>), as through the efficacy of mantras and medicines; for some, through the efficacy of a magnet upon iron; through the efficacy of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) for those who possess supernatural power. In the production [of phenomena] with or without a seed, momentariness should be understood from the impossibility of remaining [unchanged] and from the impossibility of the final [moment]. For without the state of being a cause at each moment, the seed-state at another time is not appropriate for something remaining in the same state. Nor [is there] seedlessness in the final moment. And it is not possible to accept (

body.text: bāhyasyedānīṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ tribhiḥ ślokaiḥ sādhayati |
body.translated_text: Now he establishes the momentariness of external [things] with three verses.

children.translated_text: The momentariness of the elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and of the sixfold object is established:

children.text: śoṣavṛddheḥ prakṛtyā ca calatvād vṛddhihānitaḥ || Msa_18.89 ||
children.translated_text: from the drying and growth [of water], from the natural mobility [of wind], from growth and decay, // Msa 18.89 //
from the arising of earth from those [elements], and from the fourfold transformation [of earth],
and from the equality of cause with color, smell, taste, and touch — likewise that [momentariness]. // Msa 18.90 //
From the dependence of [fire's] operation on fuel, from the observation of degrees [of sound],
from the conformity with mind [of mental objects], and from questioning — even the external is momentary. // Msa 18.91 //

body.text: kiṃ punastadbāhyaṃ | catvāri mahābhūtāni | ṣaḍivadhaścārthaḥ | varṇagandharasasparśaśabdā dharmāyatanikaṃ ca rūpam | ato bhūtānāṃ ṣaḍivadhārthasya ca kṣaṇikatvaṃ vidhīyate | kathaṃ vidhīyate | apāṃ tāvacchoṣavṛddheḥ | utsasarastaṭāgādiṣvapāṃ krameṇa vṛddhiḥ śoṣaścopalabhyate | taccobhayamantareṇa pratikṣaṇaṃ pariṇāmaṃ na syātpaścādviśeṣakāraṇābhāvāt | vāyoḥ prakṛtyā calatvād vṛddhihānitaśca | na hyavasthitasya calatvaṃ syāttatsvābhāvāditi[gatyabhāvāditi] prasādhitametat | na ca vṛddhihāsau tathaivāvasthitatvāt | pṛthivyāstatsaṃbhavāt pariṇāmacatuṣṭayācca | tacchabdenāpaśca gṛhyante vāyuśca | adbhyo hi vāyusahitābhyaḥ pṛthivī saṃbhūtā vivartakāle | tasmāttatphalatvāt sāpi kṣaṇikā veditavyā | caturvidhaśca pariṇāmaḥ pṛthivyā upalabhyate | karmakṛtaḥ sattvānāṃ karmaviśeṣāt | upakramakṛtaḥ prahādibhiḥ | bhūtakṛto 'gnyādibhiḥ | kālakṛtaḥ kālāntarapariṇāmataḥ[vāsataḥ] | sa cāntareṇa pratikṣaṇamanyotpattiṃ na yujyate vināśakāraṇābhāvāt | varṇagandharasasparśānāṃ pṛthivyādibhistulyakāraṇatvāt tathaiva kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ | tejasaḥ punaḥ kṣaṇikatvamindhanādhīnavṛttitvāt |
body.translated_text: What then is that 'external'? The four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>). And the 'sixfold object' is: color (<s>varṇa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), and the form belonging to the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental sense-base). Therefore, the momentariness of the elements and of the sixfold object is established. How is it established? First, for water, from drying and growth. In springs, lakes, ponds, and the like, the gradual growth and drying of water is observed. And both of these would not be possible without transformation at each moment, since there is no special cause afterward. For wind, from natural mobility and from growth and decay. For mobility is not possible for something that remains stationary — this has been established from the non-existence of movement as [the thing's] own nature. And there is no growth or decay, since [wind] would remain in the same state. For earth, from its arising from those [elements] and from the fourfold transformation. By the word 'those,' water and wind are also included. For earth arose from water combined with wind at the time of cosmic evolution (<s>vivartakāla</s>). Therefore, being the effect of those, it too should be understood as momentary. And a fourfold transformation of earth is observed: that produced by <s>karma</s>, from the particular <s>karma</s> of beings; that produced by effort (<s>upakrama</s>), through striking and the like; that produced by elements (<s>bhūta</s>), through fire and the like; and that produced by time (<s>kāla</s>), through transformation over time. And that [transformation] is not appropriate without the production of something different at each moment, because of the absence of a cause of destruction [at just one moment]. For color, smell, taste, and touch, because they share the same causes as earth and the like, momentariness should be understood in the same way. And the momentariness of fire (<s>tejas</s>) is [established] from the dependence of its operation on fuel.

body.text: na hi tejasyutpanne tejaḥ sahotpannamindhanaṃ tathaivāvatiṣṭhate | na ca dagdhendhanaṃ tejaḥ sthātuṃ samarthaṃ | mā bhūdante 'pyanindhanasyāvasthānamiti | ślokabandhānurodhādvarṇādīnāṃ pūrvamabhidhānaṃ paścāttejasaḥ | śabdaḥ punaryo 'pi kālāntaramupalabhyate ghaṇṭādīnāṃ tasyāpi kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ tāratamyopalabdheḥ | na hyasati kṣaṇikatve pratikṣaṇamandataratamopalabdhiḥ syāt | dharmāyatanikasyāpi rūpasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasiddhameva cittānuvṛtteryathā pūrvamuktaṃ | tasmādvāhyamapi kṣaṇikaṃ prasiddhaṃ | pṛcchrayate khalvapi sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ sidhyati (

children.translated_text: [page break: MSA Bagchi 148]

children.text: ) kathaṃ kṛtvā | idaṃ tāvadayamakṣaṇikavādī praṣṭavyaḥ | kasmādbhavānanityatvamicchati na [?] saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ necchatīti | yadyevaṃ vadet pratikṣaṇamanya[nitya]tvasyāgrahaṇāditi sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ | prasiddhakṣaṇikabhāveṣvapi pradīpādiṣu niścalāvasthāyāṃ tadagrahaṇādakṣaṇikatvaṃ kasmānneṣyate | yadyevaṃ vadet pūrvavatpaścādagrahaṇāditi | sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ | saṃskārāṇāmapi kasmādevaṃ neṣyate | yadyevaṃ vadet vilakṣaṇatvāt pradīpāditadanyasaṃskārāṇāmiti | sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ | dvividhaṃ hi vailakṣaṇyaṃ svabhāvavailakṣaṇyaṃ vṛttivailakṣaṇyaṃ ca | tadyadi tāvat svabhāvavailakṣaṇyamabhipretamata eva dṛṣṭāntatvaṃ yujyate | na hi tatsvabhāva eva tasya dṛṣṭānto bhavati yathā pradīpaḥ pradīpasya gaurvā goriti | atha vṛttivailakṣaṇyamata eva dṛṣṭāntatvaṃ pradīpādīnāṃ prasiddhatvāt | kṣaṇikatvānuvṛtteḥ punaḥ sa idaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ | kaccidicchasi yāne tiṣṭhati yānārūḍho gacchediti | yadi no hīti vadet | sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ | cakṣurādiṣu tiṣṭhatsu tadāśritaṃ vijñānaṃ prabandhena gacchatīti na yujyate | yadyevaṃ vadet nanu ca dṛṣṭaṃ vartisaṃniśrite pradīpe prabandhena gacchati vartyā avasthānamiti | sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ | na dṛṣṭaṃ tatprabandhena vartyāḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ vikārotpatteriti | yadyevaṃ vadet sati kṣaṇikattve saṃskārāṇāṃ kasmātpradīpādiva kṣaṇiakatvaṃ na siddhamiti | sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ viparyāsavastutvāt | sadṛśasaṃtatiprabandhavṛttyā hi kṣaṇikatvameṣāṃ na prajñāyate | yataḥ satyapyaparāparatve tadevedamiti viparyāso jāyate | itarathā hi anityanityaviparyāso na syāttadabhāve saṃkleśo na syāt kutaḥ punarvyavadānamityevaṃ paryanuyogato 'pi kṣaṇikatvaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ prasiddhaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) — how so? First, this proponent of non-momentariness should be asked: 'Why do you accept the impermanence of formations but not their momentariness?' If he says: 'Because at each moment one does not apprehend their difference' — he should be told: 'Even in the case of lamps and the like, whose momentary nature is well-known, when they remain motionless, their [momentary] difference is not apprehended. Why then do you not accept their non-momentariness?' If he says: 'Because one does not apprehend [their difference] afterward, as before' — he should be told: 'Why do you not accept the same for formations?' If he says: 'Because lamps and other such formations are dissimilar [from other formations]' — he should be told: 'There are two kinds of dissimilarity: dissimilarity of nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and dissimilarity of function (<s>vṛtti</s>). If dissimilarity of nature is intended, precisely for that reason the example is appropriate. For the example of a thing is never of that very same nature — just as a lamp is [not the example] of a lamp, or a cow of a cow. If dissimilarity of function is intended, precisely for that reason the example of lamps and the like is appropriate, because of being well-known, since momentariness is the common property [being illustrated].' Furthermore, he should be asked: 'Do you accept that when a vehicle is standing still, the one mounted on the vehicle moves?' If he says 'No' — he should be told: 'When the eye and the other [sense faculties] remain stationary, it is not appropriate that consciousness, which depends on them, should move in a continuum.' If he says: 'But it is observed that in a lamp that relies on a wick, [the flame] moves in a continuum while the wick remains' — he should be told: 'It is not observed that [the wick remains the same], because of the production of transformation of the wick at each moment.'
