If he says: 'Given the momentariness of formations, why is their momentariness not established just like that of lamps and the like?' — he should be told: 'Because it is a subject of perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>). For through the operation of a continuum of similar [moments], their momentariness is not recognized. Since even though there is succession, the perversion arises: "This is the very same." For otherwise, the perversion of [seeing] the impermanent as permanent would not arise; in the absence of that, defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) would not arise; whence then would purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) [be needed]?' Thus, even through this line of questioning, the momentariness of all formations is established.

body.translated_text: For when fire has arisen, the fuel that arose simultaneously with the fire does not remain in the same state. And fire cannot continue with burned fuel. Lest [one think] that even at the end there is no continuance without fuel — [the verse addresses fire before the others] following the metrical arrangement, [so] color and the like are mentioned first, and fire afterward. As for sound, even that which is perceived over a period of time, such as [the sound] of bells and the like — its momentariness should be understood from the observation of degrees [of intensity]. For without momentariness, there would not be the perception of gradually increasing dimness at each moment. The momentariness of the form belonging to the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental sense-base) is well-known, from its conformity with mind, as stated previously. Therefore, the momentariness of even the external is established. And indeed, the momentariness of all formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is established even through questioning (

body.text: pudgalanairātmyaprasādhanārthaṃ nairātmyavibhāge dvādaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of establishing the non-self of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>), twelve verses in the division on non-self.

children.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu |
children.translated_text: The person (<s>pudgala</s>) is to be spoken of as existing by way of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), but not as a substance (<s>dravya</s>);
because of non-apprehension, because of perversion, because of defilement, and because the cause [of defilement] is afflicted. // Msa 18.92 //
It is to be expressed as neither identical with nor different from [the aggregates]; therefore, from the twofold fault,
because of the absurd consequence of the aggregates being the self, and because of the absurd consequence of that [self] being a substance. // Msa 18.93 //
If it exists as a substance yet is inexpressible — the purpose [of asserting it] should be stated.
That it is inexpressible as identical or different is not appropriate, [and asserting it] is purposeless. // Msa 18.94 //
From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and from the <s>śāstras</s> too, it is not appropriate.
The inexpressibility of fuel and fire — because [identity or difference] is apprehended through both. // Msa 18.95 //

children.text: dvaye sati ca vijñānasaṃbhavātpratyayo na saḥ |
children.translated_text: And when both [conditions] are present, since consciousness can arise, it [a separate self] is not a condition (<s>pratyaya</s>).

children.text: nairarthakyādato draṣṭā yāvanmoktā na yujyate || Msa_18.96 ||
children.translated_text: Because of purposelessness, therefore the seer up to the liberator is not appropriate [as a separate entity]. // Msa 18.96 //
And if [the self] were the owner, it would not initiate what is impermanent and undesirable.

children.text: tatkarmalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyaṃ saṃbodho bādhyate tridhā || Msa_18.97 ||
children.translated_text: The defining characteristic of that <s>karma</s> to be accomplished — awakening is contradicted in three ways. // Msa 18.97 //
And in seeing and the like, that effort [would need to be explained]; [nor can the self be] self-existent (<s>svayaṃbhū</s>) — nor from the three either.
And the state of that effort being a condition — seeing and the like without effort [are also problematic]. // Msa 18.98 //
Because of non-agency, because of impermanence, and because of permanent and singular operation,

children.text: darśanādiṣu yatnasya svayaṃbhūtvaṃ na yujyate || Msa_18.99 ||
children.translated_text: the self-existence of effort in seeing and the like is not appropriate. // Msa 18.99 //
Similarly, because of the destruction of what remains, because of prior non-existence, because of impermanence,
and because of the absence of a third alternative — the state of being a condition is not appropriate. // Msa 18.100 //
All <s>dharmas</s> are without self; in the ultimate sense, [this is] emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaśca deśito yata eva ca || Msa_18.101 ||
children.translated_text: And the fault in the apprehension of a self has been taught by that very [principle]. // Msa 18.101 //
In defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>), distinguished by states and interruptions,
the difference of function and continuum is shown by [the concept of] 'person' (<s>pudgala</s>). // Msa 18.102 //
The view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) is not to be produced [anew]; the habituation is beginningless.

children.text: ayatnamokṣaḥ sarveṣāṃ na mokṣaḥ pudgalo 'sti vā || Msa_18.103 ||
children.translated_text: [If there were a real self,] liberation would be effortless for all, or there would be no liberation, or the person would [truly] exist. // Msa 18.103 //

body.text: pudgala kimastīti vaktavyo nāstīti vaktavyaḥ | āha |
body.translated_text: (Question) Should the person (<s>pudgala</s>) be said to exist or not to exist? He says:

body.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu |
body.translated_text: The person (<s>pudgala</s>) is to be spoken of as existing by way of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), but not as a substance (<s>dravya</s>).

body.text: yataśca prajñaptito 'stīti vaktavyo dravyato nāstīti vaktavyaḥ | evamanekāṃśavādaparigrahe naivāstitve doṣāvakāśo na nāstitve | sa punardravyato nāstīti kathaṃ veditavyaḥ | nopalambhāt | na hi sa dravyata upalabhyate rūpādivat | upalabdhirhi nāma buddhyā pratipattiḥ | na ca pudgalaṃ buddhyā na pratipadyante pudgalavādinaḥ | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā | dṛṣṭa eva dharme ātmānamupalabhate prajñāpayatīti kathaṃ nopalabdho bhavati | na sa evamupalabhyamāno dravyata upalabdho bhavati | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | viparyāsāt tathā hyanātmanyātmeti viparyāsa ukto bhagavatā | tasmādya evaṃ pudgalagrāho viparyāsaḥ saḥ | kathamidaṃ gamyate | saṃkleśāt | satkāyadṛṣṭikleśalakṣaṇo hyeṣa saṃkleśo yaduta ahaṃ mameti | na ca [cā] viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśo bhavitumarhati | na[sa] caiṣa saṃkleśa iti kathaṃ veditavyaṃ | kliṣṭahetutaḥ | tathāhi taddhetukāḥ kliṣṭā rāgādaya utpadyante | yatra punarvastuni rūpādisaṃjñakeprajñaptiḥ pudgala iti tasmātkimekatvena pudgalo vaktavya āhosvidanyetvena | āha |
body.translated_text: And since it exists nominally (<s>prajñaptitas</s>), it should be said [to exist]; substantially (<s>dravyatas</s>), it should be said not to exist. Thus, when accepting the non-one-sided position, there is no occasion for the fault of either existence or non-existence. But how should it be understood that it does not exist substantially? From non-apprehension — for it is not apprehended substantially, like form and the like. Apprehension means comprehension by the intellect. But the proponents of the person do indeed comprehend the person by the intellect. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said: 'One apprehends and designates the self in this very life.' How then is it not apprehended? Being apprehended in this way, it is not apprehended substantially. For what reason? Because of perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>) — for the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared the perversion of grasping the self in what is not-self. Therefore, this grasping at a person is a perversion. How is this understood? From affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) — for this affliction is characterized by the affliction of the view of the transitory collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), namely 'I' and 'mine.' And a perversion is indeed productive of affliction. But how is it known that this is an affliction? From its afflicted cause — for afflicted [states] such as passion and the like arise having that as their cause. Now, regarding the entity called form and the like, which is the basis for the designation 'person,' should the person be stated as identical or as different?

body.text: ekatvānyatvato 'vācyastasmādasau |
body.translated_text: It is inexpressible as either identical or different; therefore it is [inexpressible].

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | doṣadvayāt | katamasmāddoṣadvayāt |
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because of a twofold fault. What twofold fault?

body.text: skandhātmatvaprasaṅgācca taddravyatvaprasaṅgataḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of the consequence that the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) would be the self, and the consequence that it [the person] would be a substance.

body.text: ekatve hi skandhānāmātmatvaṃ prasajyate pudgalasya ca dravyasattvaṃ | athānyatve pudgalasya dravyasattvaṃ | evaṃ hi pudgalasya prajñaptito 'stitvādavaktavyatvaṃ yuktaṃ | tenāvyākṛtavastusiddhiḥ | ye punaḥ śāstuḥ śāsanamatikramya pudgalasya dravyato 'stitvamicchanti ta idaṃ syurvacanīyāḥ |
body.translated_text: For if identical, it would follow that the aggregates are the self; and the person would be a substantial entity. And if different, the person would [also] be a substantial entity. Thus, because the person exists only nominally, its inexpressibility is justified. Thereby, the establishment of the undeclared (<s>avyākṛta</s>) matter is [proven]. Now, those who transgress the teaching of the Teacher and hold that the person exists substantially should be addressed as follows:

body.text: dravyasanyadyavācyaśca vacanīyaṃ prayojanaṃ |
body.translated_text: If it is a substantial entity, yet inexpressible, the purpose [of declaring it inexpressible] should be stated.

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: For what reason?

body.text: ekatvānyatvato 'vācyo na yukto niṣprayojanaḥ |
body.translated_text: It is not justified that what is inexpressible as identical or different is without purpose.

body.text: atha dṛṣṭāntamātrāt pudgalasyāvaktavyatvamiccheyuḥ | yathāgnirindhanānnānyo nānanyo vaktavya iti | ta idaṃ syurvacanīyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, if they would hold the inexpressibility of the person merely from an example — just as fire should be stated as neither different nor non-different from fuel — they should be addressed thus:

body.text: lakṣaṇāllokadṛṣṭācca śāstrato 'pi na yujyate |
body.translated_text: From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and also from the teaching, it is not justified;

body.text: indhanāgnyoravācyatvamupalabdherdvayena hi |
body.translated_text: the inexpressibility of fire and fuel is [disproved] from the apprehension of both —

body.text: ekatvenānyatvena ca agnirhi nāma tejodhāturindhanaṃ śeṣāṇi bhūtāni | teṣāṃ ca bhinnaṃ lakṣaṇamityanya evāgnirindhanāt | loke ca vināpyagninā dṛṣṭamindhanaṃ kāṣṭhādi vināpi cendhanenāgniriti siddhamanyatvaṃ | śāstre ca bhagavatā na kvacidagnīndhanayoravācyatvamuktamityayuktametat | vina punarindhanenāgnirastīti kathamidaṃ vijñāyate | upalabdhestathā hi vāyunā vikṣiptaṃ dūramapi jvalatparaiti | athāpi syādvānustatrendhanamiti ata evāgnīndhanayoranyatvamiti siddhiḥ | kutaḥ | dvayena hi upalabdheriti prakṛtaṃ | dvayaṃ hi tatropalabhyate arcirvāyuścendhanatvena | astyeva pudgalo ya eṣa draṣṭā yāvadvijñātā kartā bhoktā jñātā moktā ca | na sa draṣṭā yujyate | nāpi yāvanmoktā | sa hi darśānādisaṃjñakānāṃ vijñānānāṃ pratyayabhāvena vā kartā bhavet svāmitvena vā | tatra tāvat |
body.translated_text: namely, in terms of identity and difference. For fire is the heat element; fuel is the remaining elements. And their characteristics are distinct; therefore fire is indeed different from fuel. In the world too, fuel such as wood and the like is seen without fire, and fire [is seen] without fuel; therefore difference is established. And in the teaching, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has nowhere stated the inexpressibility of fire and fuel; therefore this is unjustified. But how is it known that fire exists without fuel? From apprehension — for fire scattered far by the wind proceeds while burning. Even if one objects that 'the wind there is the fuel,' that itself is proof of the difference of fire and fuel. Why? 'From the apprehension of both' — this is the established [point]. For two things are apprehended there: the flame and the wind, as fuel. Suppose the person exists — the seer, up to the knower, the agent, the experiencer, the knower, and the liberator — that it is not justified as the seer, nor as [anything] up to the liberator. For it would be the agent of the cognitions designated as seeing and the rest, either as a condition or as an owner. Regarding the first:

body.text: dvayaṃ pratītya vijñānasaṃbhavātpratyayo na saḥ |
body.translated_text: It is not the condition, because consciousness arises dependent on two [conditions].

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | nairarthakyāt | na hi tasya tatra kiṃcitsāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ |
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because of purposelessness — for no capacity of it is seen therein.

body.text: svāmitve sati vānityamaniṣṭaṃ na pravartayet ||
body.translated_text: And if it were the owner, it would not produce undesired and impermanent [consciousness].

body.text: sa hi vijñānapravṛttau svāmībhavannani[bhavanni]ṣṭaṃ vijñānamanityaṃ na pravartayet | aniṣṭaṃ ca | naiva tasmādubhayathāpyasaṃbhavāt | asau draṣṭā yāvanmoktā na yujyate | api khalu yadi dravyataḥ pudgalo 'sti |
body.translated_text: For if it were the owner of the operation of consciousness, it would not produce undesired consciousness, nor impermanent [consciousness]. Yet [consciousness is] both undesired and [impermanent]. Therefore, from the impossibility of both [alternatives], it is not justified as the seer up to the liberator. Moreover, if the person exists substantially:

body.text: tatkarmalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyaṃ

children.text:
yadi dravyato 'stitasya karmāpyupalabhyate | yathā cakṣurādīnāṃ darśanādilakṣaṇaṃ ca rūpaprasādādi | na caivaṃ pudgalasya | tasmānna so 'sti dravyataḥ | tasmiṃśca dravyata iṣyamāṇe buddhasya bhagavataḥ |
saṃbodho bādhyate tridhā |
children.translated_text:
if it exists substantially, its action too should be apprehended, just as the eyes and the like have the characteristic of seeing and the like, and form, transparency, and so forth. But for the person, [this is] not so. Therefore it does not exist substantially. And if it were held to exist substantially, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>'s
awakening is obstructed in three ways.

body.translated_text: Its action-characteristic should be established —

body.text: gambhīrābhisaṃbodhaḥ | asādhāraṇābhisaṃbodhaḥ | lokottarābhisaṃbodhaśca | na hi pudgalābhisaṃbodhe kiṃcidgambhīramabhisaṃbuddhaṃ bhavati | na tīrthyāsādhāraṇaṃ | na lokānucittaṃ | tathā hyeṣa grāhaḥ sarvalokagamyaḥ | tīrthyābhiniviṣṭaḥ | dirghasaṃsārocittaśca | api khalu pudgalo draṣṭā bhavan yāvadvijñātā darśanādiṣu saprayatno vā bhavenniṣprayatno vā | saprayatnasya vā punarasau prayatnaḥ svayaṃbhūrvā bhavedākasmikaḥ | tatpratyayo [vā?]
body.translated_text: The profound awakening, the uncommon awakening, and the supramundane awakening [would be obstructed]. For in the realization of a person, nothing profound would have been realized; [it would] not [be] uncommon from the sectarians; and [it would] not [be] different from what the world [knows]. For this grasping is accessible to the entire world, is maintained by the sectarians, and has been cultivated through long <s>saṃsāra</s>. Moreover, the person, being the seer up to the knower, would be either with effort or without effort regarding seeing and the rest. And if with effort, that effort would be either self-originated, accidental, or conditioned by that [person].

body.text: darśanādau ca tadyatnaḥ svayaṃbhūrna trayādapi |
body.translated_text: And the effort for seeing and the rest is not self-originated, because of a threefold fault.

body.text: tasmādeva ca doṣatrayādvakṣyamāṇāt
body.translated_text: And therefore, because of the threefold fault to be stated:

body.text: tadyatnapratyayatvaṃ ca
body.translated_text: its being the condition of the effort

body.text: neti vartate | niṣprayatnasya vā punaḥ sataḥ siddhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: is not [possible] — this continues. And if without effort, then it would be established that:

body.text: niryatnaṃ darśanādikam |
body.translated_text: seeing and the rest are effortless.

body.text: ityasati vyāpāre pudgalasya darśanādau kathamasau draṣṭā bhavati | yāvadvijñātā | doṣatrayādityuktaṃ katamasmāddoṣatrayāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, in the absence of the person's activity regarding seeing and the rest, how is it the seer, up to the knower? The threefold fault was mentioned — what is that threefold fault?

children.translated_text: From non-agency, from impermanence, and from permanent and constant operation —
the self-originated nature of the effort regarding seeing and the rest is not justified.

body.text: yadi darśanādiṣu prayatna ākasmiko yato darśanādīni | na tarhi teṣāṃ pudgalaḥ karteti kathamasau draṣṭā bhavati yāvadvijñātā sati vākasmikatve nirapekṣatvāt na kadācitprayatno na syādanityo na syāt | nitye ca prayatne darśanādīnāṃ yugapacca nityaṃ ca pravṛttiḥ syāditi doṣaḥ | tasmānna yujyate darśanādiṣu prayatnasya svayaṃbhūtvaṃ |
body.translated_text: If the effort regarding seeing and the rest is accidental — from which seeing and the rest [arise] — then the person is not the agent of those; so how is it the seer up to the knower? And if [the effort is] accidental, being independent, the effort would never be absent and would never be impermanent. And if the effort were permanent, the fault would be the simultaneous and constant operation of seeing and the rest. Therefore, the self-originated nature of the effort regarding seeing and the rest is not justified.

children.translated_text: Likewise, for the existing [person] and for the destroyed [person], because of prior non-existence and impermanence —
and because of the absence of a third alternative — [its] being a condition is not justified.

body.text: atha pudgalapratyayaḥ prayatnaḥ syāt | tasya tathā sthitasya pratyayatvaṃ na yujyate | prāgabhāvāt | sati hi tatpratyayatve na kadācitpudgalo nāstīti | kimarthaṃ prāk prayatno na syādyadā notpannaḥ | vinaṣṭasyāpi pratyayatvaṃ na yujyate pudgalasyānityatvaprasaṅgāt | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 152

children.text: ) tṛtīyaśca kaścitpakṣo nāsti yanna sthito na vinaṣṭaḥ syāditi | tatpratyayo 'pi prayatno na yujyate | evaṃ tāvadyuktimāśritya dravyataḥ pudgalo nopalabhyate |
children.translated_text: And there is no third alternative — something that is neither existing nor destroyed. Therefore, the effort conditioned by that is also not justified. Thus, first relying on reasoning, the person is not apprehended substantially.

body.translated_text: Now, if the effort were conditioned by the person — for that [person] existing in such a way, its being a condition is not justified, because of prior non-existence. For if it were its condition, the person would never be non-existent. Why would the effort not exist prior [to the person], when [it] has not arisen? And the conditionality of the destroyed [person] is also not justified, because of the consequence that the person would be impermanent.

children.translated_text: All dharmas are selfless; ultimate emptiness [is taught];

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaśca deśito yata eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and the fault in the apprehension of self has been taught — from that very [teaching].

body.text: dharmoddāneṣu hi bhagavatā sarve dharmā anātmāna iti deśitaṃ paramārthaśūnyatāyāmasti karmāsti vipākaḥ kārakastu nopalabhyate ya imāṃśca skandhānnikṣipati anyāṃśca skandhānpratisaṃdadhāti | anyatra dharmasaṃketāditi deśitaṃ | pañcakeṣu pañcādīnavā ātmopalambha iti deśitā | ātmadṛṣṭirbhavati jīvadṛṣṭiḥ nirviśeṣo bhavati tīrthikaiḥ | unmārgapratipanno bhavati | śūnyatāyāmasya cittaṃ na praskandati na prasīdati na saṃtiṣṭhate nādhimucyate | āryadharmā asya na vyavadāyante | evamāgamato 'pi na yujyate | pudgalo 'pi hi bhagavatā tatra tatra deśitaḥ | parijñātāvī bhārahāraḥ śraddhānusāryādipudgalavyavasthānata ityasati dravyato 'stitve kasmāddeśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: For in the summaries of the Dharma, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught: 'All dharmas are selfless.' Regarding ultimate emptiness, [he taught]: 'There is action, there is fruition, but no agent is apprehended who discards these aggregates and takes up other aggregates — except in accordance with the convention of dharmas.' Five disadvantages of the apprehension of self have been taught: the view of self arises; the view of a living being arises; there is no difference from the sectarians; one has entered the wrong path; one's mind does not leap forward, does not gain confidence, does not become settled, and does not have conviction regarding emptiness; the noble dharmas do not lead one to purification. Thus from scripture too, [the substantial existence of the person] is not justified. But the <s>Bhagavān</s> has also taught the person here and there — 'the one who has fully understood,' 'the burden-bearer,' and the establishment of persons such as the faith-follower and so forth. If it does not exist substantially, why was it taught?

children.translated_text: In affliction and purification, differentiated by state and interruption,
the distinction of operation and continuum is shown by means of the 'person.'

body.text: avasthābhinne hi saṃkleśavyavadāne chedabhinne ca | pudgalaprajñaptimantareṇa tadvṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaśca deśayituṃ na śakyaḥ | tatra parijñāsūtre parijñeyā dharmāḥ saṃkleśaḥ parijñā vyavadānaṃ | bhārahārasūtre | bhāro bhārādānaṃ ca saṃkleśaḥ | bhāranikṣepaṇaṃ vyavadānaṃ | tayorvṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaścāntareṇa parijñātāvibhārahārapudgalaprajñaptiṃ na śakyeta deśayituṃ | bodhipakṣāśca dharmā bahudhāvasthāḥ prayogadarśanabhāvanāniṣṭhāmārga viśeṣabhedataḥ | teṣāṃ vṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaścāntareṇa śraddhānusāryādipudgalaprajñaptiṃ na śakyeta deśayituṃ | yenāsati dravyato 'stitve pudgalo deśita ityayamatra nayo veditavyaḥ | itarathā hi pudgaladeśanā niṣprayojanā prāpnoti | na hi tāvadasāvātmadṛṣṭyutpādanārthaṃ yujyate yasmāt
body.translated_text: For in affliction and purification, differentiated by state and by interruption, without the designation of 'person,' the distinction of operation and the distinction of continuum cannot be taught. Therein, in the Sūtra of Full Understanding: the dharmas to be fully understood are the affliction; full understanding is the purification. In the Sūtra of the Burden-Bearer: the burden and taking up the burden are the affliction; putting down the burden is the purification. The distinction of operation and the distinction of continuum of these two cannot be taught without the designation of the persons 'the one who has fully understood' and 'the burden-bearer.' And the dharmas conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) are differentiated in many states — through the distinctions of the paths of preparation, seeing, cultivation, and final completion. The distinction of their operation and the distinction of continuum cannot be taught without the designation of persons such as the faith-follower. This is the method to be understood here — that although [the person] does not exist substantially, the person was taught. Otherwise, the teaching of the person would be purposeless. For it is not justified [to say that it is taught] for the purpose of generating the view of self, since:

body.text: ātmadṛṣṭiranūtpādyā
body.translated_text: the view of self need not be produced,

body.text: pūrvamevotpannatvāt | nāpi tadabhyāsārthaṃ yasmādātmadṛṣṭer
body.translated_text: because it has already arisen. Nor for the purpose of its habituation, since the habituation of the view of self

body.text: abhyāso 'nādikālikaḥ |
body.translated_text: is beginningless.

body.text: yadi cātmadarśanena mokṣa ityasau deśyeta | evaṃ sati syāt
body.translated_text: And if it were taught that liberation [comes] through seeing the self, then it would follow that:

body.text: ayatnamokṣaḥ sarveṣāṃ
body.translated_text: liberation would [come] effortlessly for all.

body.text: tathā hi sarveṣāṃ na dṛṣṭasatyānāmātmadarśanaṃ vidyate | naiva vā mokṣo 'stīti prāpnoti | na hi pūrvamātmānamanātmato gṛhītvā satyābhisamayakāle kaścidātmato gṛhṇāti | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 153

children.text: ) yathā duḥkhaṃ duḥkhataḥ pūrvamagṛhītvā paścādgṛhṇātīti yathāpūrvaṃ tathā paścādapi mokṣo na syāt | sati cātmanyavaśyamahaṃkāramamakārābhyāmātmatṛṣṇayā cānyaiśca tannidānaiḥ kleśairbhavitavyamiti ato 'pi mokṣo na syāt | na vā pudgalo 'stīti abhyupagantavyaṃ | tasminhi sati niyatamete doṣāḥ prasajyante |
children.translated_text: Just as one who has not first grasped suffering as suffering [later] grasps it — as before, so afterward too, there would be no liberation. And if there were a self, inevitably there would be the conceits 'I' and 'mine,' self-craving, and other afflictions having that as their cause; therefore from this too, there would be no liberation. Or else, one must acknowledge that the person does not exist — for if it did, these faults would inevitably follow.

body.translated_text: For all who have not seen the truths have the view of self. Or else, it would follow that there is no liberation at all — for no one, having first grasped the self as non-self, at the time of the realization of the truths then grasps it as self.

children.translated_text: Thus, endowed with these qualities always, <s>bodhisattvas</s>

children.text: ātmārthaṃ ca na riñcanti parārthaṃ sādhayanti ca || Msa_18.104 ||
children.translated_text: do not neglect their own welfare, and accomplish the welfare of others. || Msa_18.104 ||

body.text: hīdhṛtiprabhṛtīnāṃ guṇānāṃ samāsena karma nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: The action of the qualities beginning with moral conscience and firmness has been stated in summary.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre bodhipakṣādhikāraḥ [aṣṭādaśaḥ] samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eighteenth chapter on the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣādhikāra</s>) is completed ||

body.text: ekonaviṃśatyadhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Nineteenth chapter:

body.text: āścaryavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of wonders (<s>āścarya</s>):

children.translated_text: Relinquishment of one's own body and of prosperity in the worldly state,

children.text: durbaleṣu kṣamā kāye jīvite nirapekṣiṇaḥ || Msa_19.1 ||
children.translated_text: patience toward the weak by one who has no regard for body and life, || Msa_19.1 ||

children.text: vīryārambho hyanāsvādo dhyāneṣu sukha eva ca |
children.translated_text: initiation of vigor without relishing, and happiness indeed in the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations),

children.text: niṣkalpanā ca prajñāyāmāścaryaṃ dhīmatāṃ ga[ma]taṃ || Msa_19.2 ||
children.translated_text: and non-conceptualization in wisdom — this is the wonder of the wise. || Msa_19.2 ||
Birth in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the attainment of prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>),
the attainment of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), and awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — these are held to be wonders. || Msa_19.3 ||

body.text: atra dvābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ pratipattyāścaryamuktaṃ ṣaṭpāramitā ārabhya | dānena hi svadehaparityāga āścaryaṃ śīlasaṃvaranimittamudārasaṃpattityāgaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | tṛtīyena ślokena phalāścaryamuktaṃ catvāri bodhisattvaphalānyārabhya prathamāyāmaṣṭamyāṃ daśamyāṃ trīṇi śaikṣāṇi phalāni | buddhabhūmau caturthamaśaikṣamatra phalaṃ |
body.translated_text: Herein, by the first two verses, the wonder of practice has been stated, beginning with the six <s>pāramitās</s>. For through giving, the relinquishment of one's own body is a wonder; the relinquishment of magnificent prosperity, which is a condition of the moral discipline of restraint, [is also a wonder]. The rest is self-explanatory. By the third verse, the wonder of the fruit has been stated, beginning with the four fruits of the <s>bodhisattva</s>: on the first, eighth, and tenth [stages], three learner-fruits; on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, the fourth, the non-learner-fruit.

body.text: anāścaryavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of non-wonder:

children.translated_text: Dispassion, compassion, and supreme cultivation,

children.text: tathaiva samacittatvaṃ nāścaryaṃ tāsu yuktatā || Msa_19.4 ||
children.translated_text: and likewise equal-mindedness — [their] engagement in these [perfections] is not wondrous. || Msa_19.4 ||

body.text: tāsviti pāramitāsu | vairāgyamāgamya dāne prayogo nāścaryaṃ | karuṇāmāgamya śīle kṣāntau ca | paramāṃ bhāvanāmāgamyāṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau nirabhisaṃskāranirvikalpo vīryādiprayogo nāścaryam | ātmaparasamacittatāmāgamya sarvāsveva pāramitāsu prayogo nāścaryamātmārtha iva parārthe khedābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: 'In these' means in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). Based on dispassion, the practice of giving is not wondrous. Based on compassion, [the practice] of moral discipline and patience [is not wondrous]. Based on supreme cultivation, on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), the effortless and non-conceptual practice of vigor and the rest is not wondrous. Based on the equal-mindedness of self and other, the practice of all the <s>pāramitās</s> is not wondrous — because of the absence of weariness in working for others just as for oneself.

body.text: samacittatāyāṃ trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on equal-mindedness:

children.translated_text: Not in the same way toward oneself, one's spouse, children, friends, and relatives

children.text: sattvānāṃ pragataḥ sneho yathā sattveṣu dhīmatāṃ || Msa_19.5 ||
children.translated_text: do beings extend their affection, as the wise ones [extend theirs] toward all beings. || Msa_19.5 ||
And impartiality toward supplicants, and the invariable non-violation of moral discipline,
patience everywhere, and great exertion of vigor for the welfare of beings; || Msa_19.6 ||

children.text: dhyānaṃ ca kuśalaṃ nityaṃ prajñā caivāvikalpikā |
children.translated_text: and wholesome <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) always, and non-conceptual <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) —
this should be known as the equal-mindedness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> in those very [perfections]. || Msa_19.7 ||

body.text: ekaḥ ślokaḥ sattveṣu samacittatāyāṃ | dvau pāramitāsu | na hi sattvānāmātmādiṣu snehaḥ samatayā anugato na cātyantaṃ | tathā hyātmānamapi kadācinmārayanti | bodhisattvānāṃ tu sarvasattveṣu samatayātyantaṃ ca pāramitāsu punardāne samacittatvamarthiṣvapakṣapātāt | śīle 'ṇumātrasyāpi nityamakhaṇḍanā | kṣāntiḥ sarvatreti deśakāle satveṣvabhedanā | vīrye sattvārthaṃ[sarvārthaṃ]vīryārambhātsvaparārthaṃ samaṃ prayogātsarvakuśalārthaṃ ca | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: One verse is on equal-mindedness toward beings; two are on [equal-mindedness in] the <s>pāramitās</s>. For the affection of beings toward self and the rest is not accompanied by equality, nor is it absolute — for indeed they sometimes even kill themselves. But for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, [their affection extends] toward all beings with equality and absolutely. Regarding the <s>pāramitās</s>, furthermore: in giving, equal-mindedness is due to impartiality toward supplicants. In moral discipline, it is the invariable non-violation of even the slightest [precept]. Patience is 'everywhere' — meaning non-discrimination with respect to place, time, and beings. In vigor, it is because of the exertion of vigor for the welfare of beings — equally for the welfare of self and others, and for all wholesome purposes. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: upakāritvavibhāge ṣoḍaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Sixteen verses on the division of beneficence:

children.text: sthāpanā bhājanatve ca śīleṣveva ca ropaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: Establishing [beings] in readiness, and the planting of moral disciplines,
and the forbearance of harm, and the engagement in purposeful activity; || Msa_19.8 ||
attracting [beings] to this teaching, and the cutting of doubt —
this is considered the beneficence of the wise ones toward beings. || Msa_19.9 ||

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiryathopakāritvaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ tatparidīpitaṃ | dānena hi sattvānāṃ bhājanatve sthāpayanti kuśalakriyāyāḥ | dhyānenāvarjayanti prabhāvaviśeṣayogāt | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | śeṣaiḥ ślokaiḥ mātrādisādharmyeṇopakāritvaṃ darśitam |
body.translated_text: Through these two verses, it is shown how <s>bodhisattvas</s> benefit [beings] through the six <s>pāramitās</s>. For through giving, they establish beings in readiness for wholesome activity. Through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), they attract [beings] because of the special power of [meditative] accomplishment. The rest is self-evident. In the remaining verses, beneficence is shown through the analogy of mother and the rest.

children.translated_text: Those who always sustain beings with a benevolent disposition,
generate [them] on the noble stage, and nurture [them] with wholesome [qualities]; || Msa_19.10 ||
protect [them] from wrongdoing, and instruct [them] in learning —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) are like mothers to beings. || Msa_19.11 ||

body.text: sattvānāṃ mātṛbhūtāḥ sattvamātṛkalpā | mātā hi putrasya pañcavidhamupakāraṃ karoti | garbheṇa dhārayati | janayati | āpāyayati poṣayati saṃvardhayati | apāyādrakṣate | abhilāpaṃ ca śikṣayati | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni pañcabodhisattvakarmāṇi veditavyāni | āryabhūmirāryadharmā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Like mothers to beings means they are like mothers of beings. For a mother performs fivefold benefit for her child: she carries [the child] in the womb; she gives birth; she nourishes, fosters, and nurtures; she protects from dangers; and she teaches speech. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. The noble stage should be understood as the noble <s>dharmas</s>.

children.translated_text: Because of always planting faith in all beings,
and because of engaging [them] in the training of higher moral discipline and the rest, and in liberation; || Msa_19.12 ||
and because of requesting the <s>Buddhas</s>, and because of removing obscurations of these [beings] —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like fathers to beings. || Msa_19.13 ||

body.text: pitā hi putrāṇāṃ pañcavidhamupakāraṃ karoti | bījaṃ teṣāmavaropayati | śilpaṃ śikṣayati | pratirūpairdārairniyojayati | sanmitreṣupanikṣipati | anṛṇaṃ karoti yathā na (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 156

children.text: ) paitṛkamṛṇaṃ dāpyate | tatsādharmyeṇa bodhisattvānāmetāni pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni | śraddhā hi sattvānāmāryātmabhāvapratilambhasya bījaṃ | śaikṣāḥ śilpaṃ | vimuktirbhāryā vimuktiprītisukhasaṃvedanā[t?]buddhāḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇi | avaraṇamṛṇasthānam |
children.translated_text: the paternal debt is not exacted. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. For faith is the seed for the attainment of a noble individual existence for beings. The trainings are the crafts. Liberation is the spouse — because of the experience of the bliss and joy of liberation. The <s>Buddhas</s> are the good friends. Obscuration is the place of debt.

body.translated_text: For a father performs fivefold benefit for his children: he plants the seed for them; he teaches them crafts; he engages them with suitable spouses; he entrusts them to good friends; and he frees them from debt so that

children.text: anarhadeśanāṃ ye ca sattvānāṃ gūhayanti hi |
children.translated_text: Those who conceal from beings the teaching [given to those] unworthy [of it],

children.text: śikṣāvipattiṃ nindanti śaṃsantyeva ca saṃpadam || Msa_19.14 ||
children.translated_text: who censure the failure of training and praise its accomplishment; || Msa_19.14 ||
who give admonition, and who announce [the attacks of] <s>Māra</s> —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like kinsmen to beings. || Msa_19.15 ||

body.text: bandhavo hi bandhūnāṃ pañcavidhamupakāraṃ kurvanti | guhyaṃ gūhayanti | kuceṣṭitaṃ vigarhanti | suceṣṭitaṃ praśaṃsanti | karaṇīyeṣu sāhāyyaṃ gacchanti | vyasanasthānebhyaśca nivārayanti | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni bodhisattvānāṃ pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni | anarhebhyo gambhīradharmedeśanāvinigūhanāt śikṣāvipattisaṃpattyoryathākramaṃ nindanātpraśaṃsanācca | adhigamāyāvavādāt mārakarmavedanācca |
body.translated_text: For kinsmen perform fivefold benefit for their kin: they conceal their secrets; they reproach their bad conduct; they praise their good conduct; they assist in [their] duties; and they prevent them from places of calamity. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood — from concealing the teaching of the profound Dharma from those unworthy, from censuring and praising the failure and accomplishment of training respectively, from giving admonition for the sake of realization, and from announcing the activities of <s>Māra</s>.

children.translated_text: Those who are themselves unwearied in understanding defilement and purification,

children.text: yacchanti laukikīṃ kṛtsnāṃ saṃpadaṃ cātilaukikīm || Msa_19.16 ||
children.translated_text: who bestow the entirety of worldly attainment and the supramundane [attainment]; || Msa_19.16 ||

children.text: sukhe hite cābhinnā[akheditvādabhinnā] ye sadā sukhahitaiṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: who are undivided in [seeking] happiness and benefit [for beings], and who always desire [their] happiness and benefit —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like friends to beings. || Msa_19.17 ||

body.text: taddhi mitraṃ yanmitrasya hite ca sukhe cāviparyastaṃ | sukhaṃ copasaṃharati hitaṃ cābhedyaṃ ca bhavati | hitasukhaiṣi ca nityaṃ | tathā bodhisattvāḥ sattvānāṃ pañcabhiḥ karmabhirmitrakalpā beditavyāḥ | laukikī hi saṃpat sukhaṃ | tayā sukhānubhavāt | lokottarā hitaṃ | kleśavyādhipratipakṣatvāt |
body.translated_text: For that is a [true] friend who is unconfused regarding both the benefit and the happiness of a friend, who brings happiness, who is unbreakable, and who always desires benefit and happiness. Likewise, <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as like friends to beings through five actions. For worldly attainment is happiness — because of experiencing happiness through it. The supramundane [attainment] is benefit — because it is the antidote to the disease of afflictions.

children.translated_text: Those who are always striving in the ripening of beings,
who correctly teach the way of departure [from suffering], who are patient in adversities; || Msa_19.18 ||
who bestow the twofold attainment, and who are skilled in the means for that —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like servants to beings. || Msa_19.19 ||

body.text: dāso hi pañcabhiḥ karmabhiḥ samyag vartate | utthānasaṃpanno bhavati | kṛtyeṣu avisaṃvādako bhavati | kṣamo bhavati paribhāṣaṇatāḍanādīnāṃ | nipuṇo bhavati sarvakāryakaraṇāt | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 157

children.text: ) vicakṣaṇaśca bhavati upāyajñaḥ | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni pañca karmāṇi bodhisattvānāṃ veditavyāni | dvayasaṃpattirlaukikī lokottarā ca veditavyā |
children.translated_text: he is discerning, knowing the means. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. The twofold attainment should be understood as the worldly and the supramundane.

body.translated_text: For a servant rightly conducts himself through five actions: he is endowed with diligence; he is not deceitful in duties; he is patient with reproach, beatings, and the like; he is skilled in all tasks; and

children.translated_text: Those who are considered to have attained patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>,
who teach all vehicles, and who engage [others] in accomplished <s>yoga</s>; || Msa_19.20 ||
who are gracious in response, and who have no regard for retribution —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like teachers to beings. || Msa_19.21 ||

body.text: pañcavidhena karmaṇā[cāryaḥ?]śiṣyāṇāmupakārī bhavati | svayaṃ suśikṣito bhavati | sarvaṃ śikṣayati | kṣipraṃ śikṣayati | sumukho bhavati suratajātīyaḥ | nirāmiṣacittaśca bhavati | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni bodhisattvānāṃ pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni |
body.translated_text: A [teacher] benefits his students through fivefold action: he himself is well-trained; he teaches everything; he teaches swiftly; he is gracious, being of a pleasant nature; and he is free from material motives. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.

children.translated_text: Those who, being devoted to the work of [benefiting] beings, complete the accumulations,
who swiftly liberate those who are accomplished, and who eliminate the opposing factors; || Msa_19.22 ||
and who engage [beings] with the various worldly attainments and with the supramundane [attainments] —
through five actions, the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are like preceptors to beings. || Msa_19.23 ||

body.text: upādhyāyaḥ pañcavidhena karmaṇā sārdhaṃ vihāriṇāmupakārī bhavati | pravrājayati upasaṃpādayati | anuśāsti doṣaparivarjane | āmiṣeṇa saṃgṛhṇāti dharmeṇa ca | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni bodhisattvānāṃ pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni |
body.translated_text: A preceptor benefits those who dwell with him through fivefold action: he ordains them; he gives them full ordination; he instructs them in the avoidance of faults; he supports them with material [provisions] and with the Dharma. By analogy with that, these five actions of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.

body.text: pratikāravibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of reciprocation:

children.text: asaktyā caiva bhogeṣu śīlasya ca na khaṇḍanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Through non-attachment to enjoyments, and through non-violation of moral discipline,
and through the pursuit of gratitude, and through engagement in practice; || Msa_19.24 ||
embodied beings who are engaged in the six <s>pāramitās</s> themselves
thereby become reciprocators to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || Msa_19.25 ||

body.text: tatheti yathā teṣāṃ bodhisattvā upakāriṇaḥ | tatra bhogeṣvanāsaktyā dāne vartante | śīlasyākhaṇḍanena śīle | kṛtajñatānuyogāt kṣāntau | upakāribodhisattvasya kṛtajñatayā te hi kṣāntipriyā iti | pratipattiyogato vīryadhyānaprajñāsu yena ca pratipadyante yatra ceti kṛtvā |
body.translated_text: 'Thereby' means in the same way that the <s>bodhisattvas</s> are benefactors to them. Therein, through non-attachment to enjoyments, they are engaged in giving. Through non-violation of moral discipline, [they are engaged] in moral discipline. Through the pursuit of gratitude, [they are engaged] in patience — because those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are benefactors are fond of patience through gratitude. Through engagement in practice, [they are engaged] in vigor, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>prajñā</s> — through what they practice and where they practice.

body.text: āśāstivibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of aspiration:

children.text: vṛddhiṃ hāniṃ ca kāṅkṣanti sattvānāṃ ca prapācanaṃ |
children.translated_text: They aspire for the increase and the decrease of beings, and for the ripening [of beings],

children.text: viśeṣagamanaṃ bhūmau bodhiṃ cānuttarāṃ sadā || Msa_19.26 ||
children.translated_text: for the attainment of distinction on the [bodhisattva] stages, and always for unsurpassed awakening. || Msa_19.26 ||

body.text: pañca sthānāni bodhisattvāḥ sadaivāśaṃsante | pāramitāvṛddhiṃ | tadvipakṣahāniṃ | sattvaparipācanaṃ | bhūmiviśeṣagamanaṃ | anuttarāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhim |
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> always aspire for five things: the increase of the <s>pāramitās</s>; the decrease of their opposing factors; the ripening of beings; the attainment of distinction on the [bodhisattva] stages; and unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: abandhyaprayogavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of unfailing effort:

children.translated_text: In the removal of terror, in the generation [of bodhicitta], in the cutting of doubt,
and in the admonition of practice — the children of the <s>Jinas</s> are always unfailing. || Msa_19.27 ||

body.text: caturvidhe sattvārthe bodhisattvānāmabandhyaḥ prayogo veditavyaḥ | gambhirodāradharmatrāsa[ā?]yoge | bodhicittasamutpāde | utpāditabodhicittānāṃ saṃśayopacchedane | pāramitāpratipattyavavāde ca |
body.translated_text: The unfailing effort of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be understood in four kinds of benefit to beings: in [removing] the terror of the profound and vast Dharma; in the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening); in the cutting of doubt for those who have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>; and in the admonition of the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.text: samyakprayogavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of correct practice:

children.translated_text: Giving for one who has no expectation of return, and for one who has no desire for rebirth,

children.text: śīlaṃ kṣāntiśca sarvatra vīryaṃ sarvaśubhodaye || Msa_19.28 ||
children.translated_text: moral discipline and patience everywhere, and vigor for the arising of all that is wholesome; || Msa_19.28 ||
and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) without [attachment to] the formless [realms], and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) conjoined with skillful means —
this is the correct practice of the steadfast ones in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. || Msa_19.29 ||

body.text: yathoktaṃ ratnakūṭe | vipāko 'pratikāṅikṣaṇo dāneneti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'Without expectation of retribution through giving' — and so on in detail.

body.text: parihāṇiviśeṣabhāgīyadharmavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of factors conducive to decline and distinction:

children.translated_text: Attachment to enjoyments, having gaps [in morality], pride, and devotion to pleasure,
relishing [of meditative states], and conceptualization — these are the causes of decline for the steadfast ones. || Msa_19.30 ||
For <s>bodhisattvas</s> who abide in the antidotes to those,
the factors conducive to distinction should be known — because they are the opposite of those. || Msa_19.31 ||

body.text: ṣaṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ vipakṣā hānabhāgīyāḥ | tatpratipakṣā viśeṣabhāgīyā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The opposing factors of the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the factors conducive to decline. Their antidotes should be understood as the factors conducive to distinction.

body.text: pratirūpakabhūtaguṇavibhāge dvau ślokau | ekaḥ paṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of counterfeit and genuine qualities — one is a six-footed [verse]:

children.translated_text: Deception even though bestowing, and the display of graciousness,

children.text: lobhatvena tathā vṛttiḥ śāntavākkāyatā tathā || Msa_19.32 ||
children.translated_text: and likewise conduct motivated by greed, and calmness of speech and body; || Msa_19.32 ||
and eloquence of speech devoid of practice —
these have been taught as leading to the inauthenticity of <s>bodhisattvas</s>;
when practiced in the opposite way, they are taught as leading to their authenticity. || Msa_19.33 ||

body.text: ṣaṇāṃpāramitānāṃ pratirūpakāḥ ṣaḍ bodhisattvaguṇāḥ pravā[tā]raṇādayo veditavyāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: The six counterfeit qualities of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, beginning with deception, should be understood. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: vinayavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of disciplining [beings]:

children.translated_text: Through the application of giving and the rest, they discipline beings

children.text: ṣaṭprakāraṃ vipakṣaṃ hi dhīmantaḥ sarvabhūmiṣu || Msa_19.34 ||
children.translated_text: from the sixfold opposing factor — the wise ones on all [bodhisattva] stages. || Msa_19.34 ||

body.text: ṣaṭprakāro vipakṣaḥ | ṣaṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ mātsaryadauḥśīlyakrodhakausīdyavikṣepadauṣprajñyāni yathāṃkramaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: The sixfold opposing factor [consists of]: miserliness, immorality, anger, laziness, distraction, and wrong understanding, corresponding respectively to the six <s>pāramitās</s>. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: vyākaraṇavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of prophecy:

children.translated_text: The prophecy of the wise is twofold, according to the distinction of time and person;
in [the prophecy of] awakening and in [the prophecy of] prophecy itself, it is stated that there is another [distinction] — the great. || Msa_19.35 ||
through obtaining the patience regarding the non-arising [of phenomena], through the abandonment of pride and purposeful effort,
and through going into oneness with all <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || Msa_19.36 ||

children.text: kṣetreṇa nāmnā kālena kalpanāmnā ca tatpunaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the field, by the name, by the time, by the name of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), and again
by the retinue and the continuity of the true Dharma — that [prediction] is accepted. || Msa_19.37 ||

body.text: tatra pudgalabhedena vyākaraṇaṃ gotrasthotpāditacittasaṃmukhāsamakṣapudgalavyākaraṇāt | kālabhedena parimitāparimitakālavyākaraṇāt | punarbodhau vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati | vyākaraṇe vā evaṃnāmā tathāgata evamamuṣminkāle vyākariṣyatīti | anyatpunarmahāvyākaraṇaṃ yadaṣṭamyāṃ bhūmāvanutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhataḥ | ahaṃ buddho bhaviṣyāmīti mānaprahāṇataḥ | sarvanimitta[ā?]bhogaprahāṇataḥ | sarvabuddhabodhisatvai[tva]śca sārdhamekībhāvopagamanataḥ | tadātmasaṃtānabhedādarśanāt | punaḥ kṣetrādibhirvyākaraṇamīdṛśe buddhakṣetre evaṃnāmā iyatā kālena buddho bhaviṣyati | evaṃnāmake kalpe īdṛśaścāsya parivāro bhaviṣyati | etāvadantaraṃ kālamasya saddharmānuvṛttirbhaviṣyatīti |
body.translated_text: Therein, prediction by the division of persons — from the prediction of persons [at different levels]: those abiding in the lineage (<s>gotra</s>), those who have generated the mind, those face-to-face, and those not present. By the division of time — from the prediction of limited and unlimited time. Again, there is prediction regarding awakening, or in the prediction [itself]: 'A <s>Tathāgata</s> of such-and-such a name will make a prediction at such-and-such a time.' But the other, the great prediction, is that on the eighth stage, through obtaining the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>); through the abandonment of the pride 'I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>'; through the abandonment of all sign-directed purposeful effort; and through going into oneness with all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> — because of not seeing any differentiation in their continua. Again, prediction by the field and the rest: 'In such-and-such a <s>Buddha</s>-field, one of such-and-such a name will become a <s>Buddha</s> in such-and-such a time, in such-and-such a named <s>kalpa</s>, and such-and-such will be one's retinue, and for this much time the continuity of one's true Dharma will endure.'

body.text: niyatipātavibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: A six-line verse on the division of determined attainment (<s>niyatipāta</s>):

children.translated_text: Determined attainment of prosperity and birth, and of unweariness for the wise,
and of continuity in cultivation, non-decline in concentration,
success in duty, effortlessness, and the attainment of patience in every way. || Msa_19.38 ||

body.text: ṣaṭpāramitādhikāreṇa ṣaḍvidho niyatipāta eṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ | saṃpattiniyatipāto nityamudārabhogasaṃpattilābhāt | upapattiniyatipāto nityaṃ yatheṣṭopapattiparigrahāt | akhedaniyatipāto n(

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 160

children.text: ) ityaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhairakhedāt | bhāvanāsātatyaniyatipāto nityaṃ bhāvanāsātatyāt | samādhānācyutau kṛtyasiddhau ca niyatipāto nityaṃ samādhyaparihāṇitaḥ sattvakṛtyasādhanataśca | anābhogānutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhe niyatipātaśca nityamanābhoganirvikalpajñānavihārāt |
children.translated_text: ) from constantly being unwearied by the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>; determined attainment of continuity in cultivation — from constant continuity of cultivation; determined attainment regarding non-decline in concentration and success in duty — from constant non-decline of <s>samādhi</s> and from accomplishing the duties toward beings; and determined attainment in the effortless obtaining of patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena — from constantly abiding in effortless non-conceptual knowledge.

body.translated_text: This sixfold determined attainment has been taught with reference to the six <s>pāramitās</s>: determined attainment of prosperity — from always obtaining magnificent prosperity of enjoyments; determined attainment of birth — from always obtaining birth as desired; determined attainment of unweariness — (

body.text: avaśyakaraṇīyavibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: A six-line verse on the division of what must necessarily be done:

children.translated_text: Worship, undertaking the trainings, compassion, cultivation of the wholesome,
diligence in solitude, and insatiability for the meaning of what has been heard —
on all stages, this is what must necessarily be done by the steadfast. || Msa_19.39 ||

body.text: ṣaṭpāramitā adhikṛtyeyaṃ ṣaḍvidhāvaśyakaraṇīyatā gatārthaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: This sixfold obligation, with reference to the six <s>pāramitās</s> — the verse has its meaning already explained.

body.text: sātatyakaraṇīyavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of what must constantly be done:

children.translated_text: Knowledge of the danger in sensual pleasures, examination of one's faults,

children.text: duḥkhādhivāsanā caiva kuśalasya ca bhāvanā || Msa_19.40 ||
children.translated_text: endurance of suffering, and the cultivation of the wholesome; || Msa_19.40 ||
non-savoring of pleasure, and the non-conceptualization of signs —
this is what must constantly be done by the wise on all stages. || Msa_19.41 ||

body.text: ṣaṭpāramitāpariniṣpādanārthaṃ ṣaṭ sātatyakaraṇīyāni | gatārthau ślokau | pradhānavastuvibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of accomplishing the six <s>pāramitās</s>, there are six things that must constantly be done. The verses have their meaning already explained. A six-line verse on the division of the principal matter (<s>pradhānavastu</s>):

children.translated_text: The giving of Dharma, the purity of moral discipline, and the patience regarding non-arising,
the undertaking of vigor in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the final abiding accompanied by compassion,

children.text: prajñā pāramitānāṃ ca pradhānaṃ dhīmatāṃ matam || Msa_19.42 ||
children.translated_text: and wisdom — these are regarded as the principal matters of the <s>pāramitās</s> for the wise. || Msa_19.42 ||

body.text: ṣaṭsu pāramitāsvetat ṣaḍvidhaṃ pradhānaṃ | tatra śīlaviśuddhirāryakāntaṃ śīlam | antyā sakaruṇā sthitiścaturthaṃ dhyānaṃ karuṇāpramāṇayuktaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: In the six <s>pāramitās</s>, these are the six principal matters. Therein, the purity of moral discipline is the morality beloved by the noble ones (<s>āryakāntaśīla</s>). The final abiding accompanied by compassion is the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) conjoined with the immeasurable of compassion. The rest has its meaning already explained.

body.text: prajñaptivyavasthānavibhāge catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Four verses on the division of designational establishment (<s>prajñaptivyavasthāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The establishment of the fields of knowledge, through the division of aspects such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest,
should be known as the establishment of dharmas for the wise on all stages. || Msa_19.43 ||
Again, the establishment of truths, through the sevenfold basis of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>);

children.text: caturdhā ca tridhā caiva yuktiyānavyavasthitiḥ || Msa_19.44 ||
children.translated_text: fourfold and threefold — the establishment of reasoning and vehicles. || Msa_19.44 ||
Proper mental engagement, right view endowed with fruit,
investigation through the means of valid cognition, and the inconceivable — the fourfold reasoning should be known. || Msa_19.45 ||
Through disposition, through teaching, through application, through accumulation,
and through the division of attainment — the vehicle is accepted as threefold. || Msa_19.46 ||

body.text: caturvidhaṃ prajñaptivyavasthānaṃ | dharmasatyayuktiyānaprajñaptivyavasthānabhedāt | tatra pañcavidyāsthānavyavasthānaṃ dharmavyavasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ sūtrageyādibhirākārabhedaiḥ | tadantarbhūtānyeva hi tadanyāni vidyāsthānāni mahāyāne bodhisattvebhyo deśyante | satyavyavasthānaṃ tu saptavidhāṃ tathatāmāśritya pravṛttitathatāṃ lakṣaṇatathatāṃ vijñaptitathatāṃ saṃniveśatathatāṃ mithyāpratipattitathatāṃ [viśuddhitathatāṃ?]samyakpratipattitathatāṃ ca | yuktiprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ caturvidham | apekṣāyuktiḥ | kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ | upapattisādhanayuktiḥ | dharmatāyuktiśca | yānaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ trividhaṃ | śrāvakayānaṃ | pratyekabuddhayānaṃ | mahāyānaṃ ca | tatrāpekṣāyuktistriṣvapi yāneṣu yoniśomanaskāraḥ | tamapekṣya tena pratyayena lokottarāyāḥ samyagdṛṣṭerutpādāt | kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ saphalā | upapattisādhanayuktiḥ pratyakṣādibhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ parīkṣā | dharmatāyuktiracintyaṃ sthānaṃ | siddhā hi dharmatā na punaścintyā | kasmād- yoniśomanaskārāt samyagdṛṣṭirbhavati | tato vā kleśaprahāṇaṃ phalamityevamādi | yānatrayavyavasthānaṃ pañcabhirākā rairveditavyaṃ | āśayato deśanātaḥ prayogataḥ saṃbhārataḥ samudāgamataśca | tatra hīnāmāśayadeśanāprayogasaṃbhārasamudāgamāḥ śrāvakayānaṃ madhyāḥ pratyekabuddhayānamuttamā mahāyānaṃ | yathāśayaṃ hi yathābhiprāyaṃ dharmadeśanābhibhavati | yathā deśanaṃ tathā prayogaḥ | yathāprayogaṃ saṃbhāraḥ | yathāsaṃbhāraṃ ca bodhisamudāgama iti |
body.translated_text: The designational establishment is fourfold — through the division of the establishment of dharmas, truths, reasoning, and vehicles. Therein, the establishment of the five fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>) should be understood as the establishment of dharmas, through the aspects of divisions such as <s>sūtras</s>, <s>geyas</s>, and the rest. For the other fields of knowledge included within those are taught to <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The establishment of truths, however, is based on sevenfold <s>tathatā</s> (suchness): the suchness of activity, the suchness of characteristics, the suchness of cognition, the suchness of arrangement, the suchness of wrong practice, the suchness of correct practice [possibly: the suchness of purification]. The designational establishment of reasoning is fourfold: the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>), the reasoning of proof and establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), and the reasoning of the nature of reality (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>). The designational establishment of vehicles is threefold: the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therein, the reasoning of dependence in all three vehicles is proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>) — because, depending on that condition, the supramundane right view arises. The reasoning of cause and effect is right view bearing fruit. The reasoning of proof and establishment is examination through the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) such as direct perception and the rest. The reasoning of the nature of reality is the inconceivable state — for the established nature of reality is not to be further investigated. Why does right view arise from proper mental engagement? And from that, the abandonment of afflictions is the result — and so forth. The establishment of the three vehicles should be understood through five aspects: through disposition, through teaching, through application, through accumulation, and through attainment. Therein, inferior disposition, teaching, application, accumulation, and attainment constitute the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle; middling — the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle; supreme — the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For in accordance with one's disposition, the Dharma-teaching prevails in accordance with one's intention. In accordance with the teaching, so is the application. In accordance with the application, the accumulation. And in accordance with the accumulation, the attainment of awakening.

children.translated_text: A verse on the division of investigation (<s>paryeṣaṇā</s>):
The investigation of the adventitious nature of name and object with respect to each other,
and the investigation of the mere-that-ness of the twofold designation herein. || Msa_19.47 ||

body.text: caturvidhā paryeṣaṇā dharmāṇāṃ | nāmaparyeṣaṇā vastuparyeṣaṇā | svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā | viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca | tatra nāmno vastunyāgantukatvaparyeṣaṇā nāmaparyeṣaṇā veditavyā | vastūno nāmnyāgantukatvaparyeṣaṇā vastuparyeṣaṇā veditavyā | tadubhayābhisaṃbandhe svabhāvaviśeṣaprajñaptyoḥ prajñaptimātratvaparyeṣaṇā svabhāvaviśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: The investigation of dharmas is fourfold: the investigation of name, the investigation of object, the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature, and the investigation of the designation of distinction. Therein, the investigation of name should be understood as the investigation of the adventitious nature of the name with respect to the object. The investigation of object should be understood as the investigation of the adventitious nature of the object with respect to the name. In the connection of both of those, the investigation of the designations of intrinsic nature and distinction as merely designations should be understood as the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature and distinction.

body.text: yathābhūtaparihāra[jñāna]vibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Ten verses on the division of knowledge as it truly is (<s>yathābhūtaparijñāna</s>):

children.translated_text: From the non-apprehension of everything, the fourfold true knowledge
arises for the steadfast on all stages, for the accomplishment of all purposes. || Msa_19.48 ||

body.text: caturvidhaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ dharmāṇāṃ nāmaparyeṣaṇāgataṃ | vastuparyeṣaṇāgataṃ | svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ | viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ ca | tacca sarvasyāsya nāmādikasyānupalambhādveditavyaṃ | uttarārdhena yathābhūtaparijñānasya karmaṇāṃ mahātmyaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: The fourfold knowledge as it truly is of dharmas: that arising from the investigation of name, that arising from the investigation of object, that arising from the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature, and that arising from the investigation of the designation of distinction. And it should be understood from the non-apprehension of all this — name and the rest. By the second half of the verse, he shows the greatness of the action of knowledge as it truly is.

children.translated_text: The basis, the enjoyment, and the seed — these indeed are the signs of bondage;
and mind and mental factors together with their supports are bound here, having seeds. || Msa_19.49 ||

body.text: tatra pratiṣṭhānimittaṃ bhājanalokaḥ | bhoganimittaṃ pañca rūpādayo viṣayāḥ | bījanimittaṃ yatteṣāṃ bījamālayavijñānaṃ | yatra[atra]trividhe nimitte sāśrayāścittacaittā vadhyante | yacca teṣāṃ bījamālayavijñānam | āśrayāḥ punaścakṣurādayo veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign of the basis is the vessel-world. The sign of enjoyment is the five sense-objects such as form and the rest. The sign of the seed is the seed of those — the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). In this threefold sign, mind and mental factors together with their supports are bound. And the seed of those is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. The supports should be understood as the eye and the rest.

children.text: purataḥ sthāpitaṃ yacca nimittaṃ yatsthitaṃ svayaṃ |
children.translated_text: Whatever sign has been placed before [by practice] and whatever abides by itself —
the wise one, having made all of that disappear, attains supreme awakening. || Msa_19.50 ||

body.text: tatra purataḥ sthāpitaṃ nimittaṃ yacchrutacintābhāvanāprayogenālambanīkṛtaṃ parikalpitaṃ | sthitaṃ svayameva yatprakṛtyālambanībhūtamayatnaparikalpitaṃ | tasya vibhāvanādhi[vi]gamo 'nālambanībhāvaḥ | akalpanā tadupāyo nimittapratipakṣaḥ | taccobhayaṃ kramādbhavati | pūrvaṃ hi sthāpitasya paścāt svayaṃsthitasya | tatra caturviparyāsānugataṃ pudgalanimittaṃ vibhāvayanyogī śrāvakabodhiṃ pratyekabodhiṃ vā labhate | sarvadharmanimittaṃ vibhāvayan mahābodhim | etena yathā tattvaṃ parijñāya mokṣāya saṃvartate yathābhūtaṃ parijñānaṃ | tatparidīpitam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the sign that has been placed before is that which has been made into an object-support through the application of hearing, reflection, and cultivation — the conceptualized [sign]. That which abides by itself is that which has by nature become an object-support, conceptualized without effort. The making of that disappear is its ceasing to be an object-support. Non-conceptualization is the means, the antidote to the sign. And both of these occur in sequence — first of the placed [sign], then of the self-abiding [sign]. Therein, the <s>yogin</s> who makes disappear the sign of person, which is followed by the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), attains the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> or a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>. One who makes disappear the sign of all dharmas attains great awakening. By this, it has been illuminated that knowledge as it truly is, having truly known reality, conduces to liberation.

children.translated_text: Knowledge that has <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as its object-support, free from the grasping of duality,
directly perceiving the body of dysfunction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) — for its destruction, [this is] considered [the knowledge] of the wise. || Msa_19.51 ||

body.text: etena yathāsvabhāvatrayaparijñānāt paratantrasvabhāvakṣayāya saṃvartate | tatparidīpitaṃ | tathatālambanatvena pariniṣpannaṃ svabhāvaṃ parijñāya | dvayagrāhavivarjitatvena kalpitaṃ | dauṣṭhulyakāyapratyakṣatvena paratantraṃ | tasyaiva kṣayāya saṃvartate dauṣṭhulyakāyasyālayavijñānasya tatkṣayārthaṃ tatkṣaye |
body.translated_text: By this, it is illuminated that through the knowledge as it truly is of the three natures respectively, it conduces to the destruction of the dependent nature (<s>paratantra svabhāva</s>). Having the perfected nature as its object-support through having <s>tathatā</s> as its object-support; the imagined [nature] through being free from the grasping of duality; the dependent [nature] through directly perceiving the body of dysfunction. It conduces to the very destruction of that body of dysfunction — the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> — for the purpose of its destruction, at the time of its destruction.

children.translated_text: Knowledge that has <s>tathatā</s> as its object-support, cultivated with non-diverse aspects,
directly perceiving the meaning of the existent and the non-existent — is said to be master of conceptualization. || Msa_19.52 ||

body.text: anānākārabhāvitaṃ nimittatathatayoranānātvadarśanāt | etena śrāvakānimittādvodhisattvānimittasya viśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ | te hi nimittānimittayornānātvaṃ paśyantu | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 163

children.text: ) sarvanimittānāmamanasikārādanimittasya ca dhātormanasikārādanimittaṃ samāpadyante | bodhisattvāstu tathatāvyatirekeṇa nimittapaśyanto nimittamevānimittaṃ paśyantyatasteṣāṃ tajjñānamanānākārabhāvitaṃ | sattārthe ca tathatāyāmasattārthe ca nimitte pratyakṣaṃ vikalpavibhu cocyate | vikalpavibhutvalābhādyathāvikalpaṃ sarvārthasamṛddhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) by not mentally attending to all signs and by mentally attending to the signless element — enter the signless [concentration]. But <s>bodhisattvas</s>, seeing the sign itself as signless without separating it from <s>tathatā</s> — therefore their knowledge is cultivated with non-diverse aspects. And it is said to be directly perceiving in the meaning of the existent — <s>tathatā</s> — and in the meaning of the non-existent — the sign — and to be master of conceptualization. Because of attaining mastery of conceptualization, [there is] the accomplishment of all purposes in accordance with conceptualization.

body.translated_text: 'Cultivated with non-diverse aspects' — from seeing the non-diversity of the sign and <s>tathatā</s>. By this, the distinction of the signlessness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> from the signlessness of <s>śrāvakas</s> has been illuminated. For they [śrāvakas], seeing diversity in the sign and signlessness, (

children.translated_text: For the childish, reality is concealed and unreality appears everywhere;

children.text: tattvaṃ tu bodhisattvānāṃ sarvataḥ khyātyapāsya tat || Msa_19.53 ||
children.translated_text: but for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, reality appears everywhere, having set aside that [unreality]. || Msa_19.53 ||

body.text: etena yathā bālānāṃ svarasenātattvameva khyāti nimittaṃ na tattvaṃ tathatā | evaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ svarasena tattvameva khyāti nātatvamityupadarśitam |
body.translated_text: By this, it has been shown that just as for the childish, unreality alone — the sign, not the reality of <s>tathatā</s> — appears spontaneously, so for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, reality alone appears spontaneously, not unreality.

children.translated_text: The non-appearance of the non-existent and the appearance of the existent —
this is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), and that is liberation, because of freedom of action. || Msa_19.54 ||

body.text: asadarthasya nimittasyākhyānatā sadarthasya tathatāyāḥ khyānatā āśrayaparāvṛttirveditavyā | tayā hi tadakhyānaṃ khyānaṃ ca | saiva ca mokṣo veditavyaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | kāmacārataḥ | tadā hi svatantro bhavati svacittavaśavartī prakṛtyaiva nimittāsamudācārāt |
body.translated_text: The non-appearance of the non-existent — the sign — and the appearance of the existent — <s>tathatā</s> — should be understood as the transformation of the basis. For through that [transformation], there is that non-appearance and appearance. And that very [transformation] should be understood as liberation. For what reason? Because of freedom of action — for then one becomes autonomous, under the power of one's own mind, because of the non-occurrence of signs by one's very nature.

children.translated_text: The meaning appears, mutually of the same kind, everywhere and great;
it creates an obstacle; therefore, having fully understood it, one should abandon it. || Msa_19.55 ||

body.text: idaṃ kṣetrapariśodhano[nau]pāye[ya]yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ | bhājanalokā[ko ']rtho mahānanyonyo vartamānastulyajātīyaḥ khyāti sa evāyamiti | sa caivaṃ khyānādantarāyakaro bhavati buddhakṣetrapariśuddhaye | tasmādantarāyakaraṃ parijñāyainamutsṛjedevaṃ khyātaṃ |
body.translated_text: This is the true understanding in the method of purifying the [Buddha-]field. The meaning of the container-world is great — [the perception that] what is present and of similar type is 'this very same thing.' And that perception thus creates an obstacle to the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field). Therefore, having fully understood it as an obstacle-creator, one should abandon such perception.

body.text: aprameyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the immeasurable (<s>aprameya</s>):

children.text: paripācyaṃ viśodhyaṃ ca prāpyaṃ yogyaṃ ca pācane |
children.translated_text: What is to be ripened, what is to be purified, what is to be attained, what is suitable for ripening,
and the substance of correct teaching — these are immeasurable for the wise. || Msa_19.56 ||

body.text: pañcavidhaṃ hi vastu bodhisattvānāmaprameyaṃ | paripācyaṃ vastu sattvadhāturaviśeṣeṇa viśodhyaṃ lokadhāturbhājanalokasaṃgṛhītaḥ | prāpyaṃ dharmadhātuḥ | paripācanayogyaṃ vineyadhātuḥ | samyagdeśanāvastu vinayopāyadhātuḥ |
body.translated_text: For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the substance is immeasurable in five ways: what is to be ripened is the <s>sattvadhātu</s> (realm of beings) without distinction; what is to be purified is the <s>lokadhātu</s> (world-realm), encompassed by the container-world; what is to be attained is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena); what is suitable for ripening is the <s>vineyadhātu</s> (realm of those to be disciplined); and the substance of correct teaching is the <s>vinayopāyadhātu</s> (realm of disciplinary methods).

body.text: deśanāphalavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of the fruits of teaching:

children.translated_text: The arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind), and the <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) of non-arising,

children.text: cakṣuśca nirmalaṃ hīnamāśravakṣaya eva ca || Msa_19.57 ||
children.translated_text: and the pure <s>dharmacakṣu</s> (Dharma-eye) pertaining to the lesser [vehicle], and the very destruction of the outflows (<s>āśravakṣaya</s>); || Msa_19.57 ||
the long duration of the true Dharma, comprehension, the cutting [of doubt], and the enjoyment [of the Dharma] —

children.text: deśanāyāḥ phalaṃ jñeyaṃ tatprayuktasya dhīmataḥ || Msa_19.58 ||
children.translated_text: these should be known as the fruits of teaching for the wise one engaged therein. || Msa_19.58 ||

body.text: deśanāyāṃ prayuktasya bodhisattvasyāṣṭavidhaṃ deśanāyāḥ phalaṃ veditavyaṃ | śrotṛṣu kecidbodhicittamutpādayanti | kecidanutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhante | kecidvirajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurutpādayanti hīnayānasaṃgṛhītaṃ | keccidāśravakṣayaṃ prāpnuvanti | saddharmaśca cirasthitiko bhavati paraṃparādhāraṇatayā | avyutpannānāmarthavyutpattirbhavati | saṃśayitānāṃ saṃśayacchedo bhavati | viniścitānāṃ saddharmasaṃbhogo bhavati anavadyo prītirasaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the <s>bodhisattva</s> engaged in teaching, the eightfold fruit of teaching should be understood: among the listeners, some generate <s>bodhicitta</s>; some attain <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena); some produce the stainless, immaculate <s>dharmacakṣu</s> (Dharma-eye) regarding phenomena, pertaining to the lesser vehicle; some attain the destruction of the outflows. The true Dharma endures for a long time through successive transmission and retention. For the uninstructed, there is comprehension of meaning. For the doubtful, there is the cutting of doubt. For the decided, there is the blameless enjoyment of the true Dharma, which is the taste of delight.

body.text: mahāyānamahattvavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of the greatness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>:

children.translated_text: Greatness of the object, and of the practice of both [self and other],

children.text: jñānasya vīryārambhasya upāye kauśalasya ca || Msa_19.59 ||
children.translated_text: of knowledge, of the initiation of vigor, of skillful means, || Msa_19.59 ||
greatness of attainment, and greatness of <s>buddhakarma</s> (Buddha-activity) —
because of the connection with this [sevenfold] greatness, it is described as '<s>Mahāyāna</s>' (Great Vehicle). || Msa_19.60 ||

body.text: saptavidhamahattvayogānmahāyānamityucyate | ālambanamahattvenāpramāṇavistīrṇasūtrādidharmayogāt | pratipattimahattvena dvayoḥ pratipatteḥ svārthe parārthe ca | jñānamahattvato dvayorjñānātpudgalanairātmyasya dharmanairātmyasya ca prativedhakāle | vīryārambhamahattvena trīṇi kalpāsaṃkhyeyāni sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogāt | upāyakauśalyamahattvena saṃsārāparityāgāsaṃkleśataḥ | samudāgamamahattvena balavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmasamudāgamāt | buddhakarmamahattvena ca punaḥ punarabhisaṃbodhimahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanataḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of the connection with sevenfold greatness, it is called '<s>Mahāyāna</s>': through greatness of object — from the practice of immeasurable, vast dharmas such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest. Through greatness of practice — from the practice of both self-interest and others' interest. Through greatness of knowledge — from the knowledge of both, the selflessness of persons and the selflessness of phenomena, at the time of penetration. Through greatness of the initiation of vigor — from the continuous and earnest endeavor through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). Through greatness of skillful means — from not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s> while remaining undefiled. Through greatness of attainment — from the attainment of the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and the special <s>buddhadharmas</s>. And through greatness of <s>buddhakarma</s> — from the repeated display of full awakening and great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: mahāyānasaṃgrahavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of the comprehensive scope of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>:

children.translated_text: <s>Gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), conviction in the Dharma, and the generation of the [awakening] mind,
the practice of giving and the rest, and the entry into the correct [path]; || Msa_19.61 ||
the ripening of beings and the purification of the [Buddha-]field,

children.text: apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ bodhiḥ śreṣṭhā ca darśanāt[darśanā] || Msa_19.62 ||
children.translated_text: non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and the supreme awakening — from [this] demonstration. || Msa_19.62 ||

body.text: etena daśavidhena vastuna kṛtsnaṃ mahāyānaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ | tatra satvānāṃ paripācanaṃ bhūmipratiṣṭha[praviṣṭa]sya yāvatsaptamyāṃ bhūmau veditavyaṃ | kṣetrapariśodhanamapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ cāvinivartanīyāyāṃ bhūmau trividhāyāṃ | śreṣṭhā bodhirbuddhabhūmau | tatraiva cābhisaṃbodhimahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanā veditavyā | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: By these ten aspects, the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> is encompassed. Therein, the ripening of beings should be understood from the entry into the stages up to the seventh stage. The purification of the field and non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> — on the threefold irreversible stage (<s>avinivartanīyabhūmi</s>). The supreme awakening — on the <s>Buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage). And therein too, the display of full awakening and great <s>parinirvāṇa</s> should be understood. The rest has its meaning already explained.

body.text: bodhisattvavibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Ten verses on the division of <s>bodhisattvas</s>:

children.translated_text: One is based on devoted conviction, and another is of purified superior intention;
and one who practices with signs, and one without signs, and also the noble one who is unconditioned —

children.text: bodhisattvā hi vijñeyāḥ pañcaite sarvabhūmiṣu || Msa_19.63 ||
children.translated_text: these five types of <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be known across all stages. || Msa_19.63 ||

body.text: tatra nimittacārī dvitīyāṃ bhūmimupādāya yāvat ṣaṣṭhayāṃ | animittacārī saptamyām | anabhisaṃskāracārī pareṇa | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, one who practices with signs — from the second stage up to the sixth. One who practices without signs — on the seventh. One who practices without conditioning — beyond that. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Unattached to sense-pleasures, of threefold pure action, unconquerable by anger, devoted to qualities,
