unwavering in the Dharma, of profound view of reality, aspiring to awakening — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.64 ||

body.text: etena ṣaṭpāramitāpratipattito mahābodhipraṇidhānataśca bodhisattvalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: By this, the characteristic of a <s>bodhisattva</s> is illuminated through the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening.

children.translated_text: Desiring to benefit, seeing non-harm, forbearing when harmed by others,

children.text: dhīro 'pramattaśca bahuśrutaśca parārthayuktaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.65 ||
children.translated_text: resolute, heedful, greatly learned, engaged in the welfare of others — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.65 ||

body.text: tatra dhīra ārabdhavīryo duḥkhairaviṣādāt | apramatto dhyānasukheṣvasaktaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'resolute' means one who has initiated vigor, because of not being dejected by sufferings. 'Heedful' means not attached to the pleasures of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Knowing the faults in one's own possessions, unattached to enjoyments, without concealed enmity,

children.text: yogī nimitte kuśalo 'kudṛṣṭiradhyātmasaṃsthaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.66 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>yogin</s>, skilled in signs, of correct views, established in the inner [Dharma] — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.66 ||

body.text: tatra bhogeṣvasakto yastānvihāya pravrajati | nimittakuśalaḥ śamathādinimittatrayakauśalyāt | adhyātmasaṃstho mahāyānāvikampanāt | mahāyānaṃ hi bodhisattvānāmadhyātmaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'unattached to enjoyments' — one who, having abandoned them, goes forth into homelessness. 'Skilled in signs' — from skill in the threefold signs of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and the rest. 'Established in the inner' — from being unshakeable in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; for the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the inner [Dharma] of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Endowed with compassion, established in the quality of moral conscience, not attached to one's own happiness due to the endurance of suffering,

children.text: smṛtipradhānaḥ susamāhitātmā yānāvikāryaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.67 ||
children.translated_text: preeminent in mindfulness, well-concentrated in mind, unchangeable regarding the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.67 ||

body.text: tatra smṛtipradhāno dhyānavān smṛtibalena cittasamādhānāt | susamāhitātmā nirvikalpajñānaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'preeminent in mindfulness' means meditative, because of the settling of the mind through the power of mindfulness. 'Well-concentrated in mind' means possessing non-conceptual knowledge. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.text: duḥkhāpaho duḥkhakaro na caiva duḥkhādhivāso na ca duḥkhabhītaḥ |
children.translated_text: A remover of suffering, yet not one who causes suffering; enduring suffering yet not fearing suffering;

children.text: duḥkhādvimukto na ca duḥkhakalpo duḥkhābhyupetaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.68 ||
children.translated_text: liberated from suffering yet not conceptualizing suffering; embracing suffering — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.68 ||

body.text: tatra duḥkhādvimukto dhyānavān kāmadhātuvairāgyād duḥkhaduḥkhatāmokṣataḥ | duḥkhābhyupetaḥ saṃsārābhyupagamāt | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'liberated from suffering' means meditative, from liberation from the suffering of suffering through dispassion toward the desire-realm. 'Embracing suffering' — from undertaking <s>saṃsāra</s>. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Delighting in the Dharma, not delighting in non-Dharma by nature; critical regarding the Dharma yet devoted to the Dharma;

children.text: dharme vaśī dharmanirandhakāro dharmapradhānaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.69 ||
children.translated_text: master of the Dharma, illuminating the Dharma without darkness, with the Dharma as primary — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.69 ||

body.text: atra dharme jugupsī akṣāntijugupsanāt | dharme vaśī samāpattau | dharmapradhāno mahābodhiparamaḥ | dharma evātra dharama ukto vṛttānuvṛttyā | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Here, 'critical regarding the Dharma' — from being critical of impatience. 'Master of the Dharma' — in meditative attainment. 'With the Dharma as primary' — having great awakening as the highest [goal]. 'Dharma' here is used in various senses through contextual variation. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Heedful regarding enjoyments, heedful regarding discipline, heedful regarding protection, heedful regarding the wholesome,

children.text: sukhāpramatto dharamāpramatto yānāpramatto khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.70 ||
children.translated_text: heedful regarding happiness, heedful regarding the Dharma, heedful regarding the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.70 ||

body.text: ratra rakṣāpramattaḥ kṣāntimān svaparacittānurakṣaṇāt | dharmāpramatto yathābhūtadharmaprajñānāt | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'heedful regarding protection' means patient, from guarding one's own and others' minds. 'Heedful regarding the Dharma' — from the true knowledge of phenomena as they really are. The rest has its meaning already explained.

children.translated_text: Having shame regarding disrespect, having shame regarding trivial faults, having shame regarding intolerance, having shame regarding decline,
having shame regarding vastness, having shame regarding subtle views, having shame regarding other vehicles — such indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_19.71 ||

body.text: tatra vimānalajjo yo 'rthino na vimānayati | tanudoṣalajjo 'ṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī tanudṛṣṭilajjo dharma nairātmyaprativedhī | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | sarvairebhiḥ ślokaiḥ paryāyāntareṇa ṣaṭpāramitāpratipattito mahābodhipraṇidhānataśca bodhisattvalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'having shame regarding disrespect' — one who does not disrespect those who are needy. 'Having shame regarding trivial faults' — one who sees danger in even the slightest transgression. 'Having shame regarding subtle views' — one who has penetrated the selflessness of phenomena. The rest has its meaning already explained. By all these verses, the characteristic of a <s>bodhisattva</s> is illuminated through an alternative formulation of the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening.

children.translated_text: Through equanimity here and hereafter, through the engagement with conditioned formations, through the attainment of sovereignty,

children.text: śamopa[samaupa]deśena mahāphalena anugrahe vartati bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.72 ||
children.translated_text: through the instruction of peace with great fruit — the <s>bodhisattva</s> engages in benefiting [beings]. || Msa_19.72 ||

body.text: ihaiva sattvānāmanugrahe vartate dānena | amutra śīlenopapattiviśeṣaṃ prāpya | saṃskārayogeneti vīryayogena | mahāphaleneti buddhatvena | śeṣaṃ gatārtham | etena ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhirmahābodhipraṇidhānena ca yathā sattvānugrahe bodhisattvo vartate tatparidīpitam |
body.translated_text: One engages in the benefit of beings here itself through giving. Hereafter — through moral discipline, by attaining a special rebirth. 'Through the engagement with conditioned formations' means through the engagement of vigor. 'With great fruit' means through Buddhahood. The rest has its meaning already explained. By this, it is illuminated how the <s>bodhisattva</s> engages in the benefit of beings through the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening.

body.text: bodhisattvasāmānyanāmavibhāge aṣṭau ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Eight verses on the division of the common names of <s>bodhisattvas</s>:

children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>mahāsattva</s>, wise one, one of supreme radiance,
child of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), support of the <s>Jinas</s>, conqueror, and sprout of the <s>Jinas</s>; || Msa_19.73 ||
heroic, supremely wondrous, caravan-leader, of great fame,
compassionate, of great merit, sovereign, and righteous — || Msa_19.74 ||

body.text: etāni ṣoḍaśa sarvabodhisattvānāmanvarthanāmāni sāmānyena |
body.translated_text: these sixteen are the common names of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, whose meanings correspond [to their qualities].

children.translated_text: Through the awakening to true reality, through the awakening to great purposes, through the awakening to all [goals], through constant awakening,

children.text: upāyabodhaiśca viśeṣaṇena tenocyate hetuna bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.75 ||
children.translated_text: and through the awakening to skillful means — by these specific reasons, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' || Msa_19.75 ||

body.text: pañcavidhena bodhaviśeṣeṇa bodhisattva ityucyate | pudgaladharma nairātmyabodhena | sarvākārasarvārthabodhena akṣayāvabodhena parinirvāṇasaṃdarśane 'pi | yathā vineyaṃ ca vinayopāyabodhena |
body.translated_text: Through fivefold distinctive awakening, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>': through the awakening to the selflessness of persons and phenomena; through the awakening to all aspects and all purposes; through inexhaustible awakening — even in the display of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; and through the awakening to the means of disciplining whomever is to be disciplined.

children.translated_text: Through the awakening to one's own [mind], through the awakening to subtle views, through the awakening to varied perceptions,
and through the awakening to the false conceptualization of everything — by these reasons, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' || Msa_19.76 ||

body.text: atra punaścaturvidhabodhaviśeṣaṃ darśayati cittamanovijñānabodhataḥ | teṣāṃ cābhūtaparikalpatvāvabodhataḥ | tatra cittamālayavijñānaṃ | manastadālambanamātmadṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktaṃ | vijñānaṃ ṣaḍvijñānakāyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here again he shows the fourfold distinctive awakening — from the awakening to <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and from the awakening to their nature as <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false conceptualization). Therein, <s>citta</s> is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). <s>Manas</s> is that which takes it as object, conjoined with <s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s> (self-view) and the like. <s>Vijñāna</s> is the six consciousness-groups.

children.translated_text: Through the awakening to non-awakening, through the awakening that follows awakening, through the awakening to non-existence, through the awakening that follows origination,
and through the counter-awakening to non-awakening — by these reasons, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' || Msa_19.77 ||

body.text: atra punaḥ pañcavidhaṃ bodhaviśeṣaṃ darśayati | avidyābodhāt | vidyābodhāt | parikalpitādisvabhāvatrayabodhācca | tatrābodhatvena bodhapratibodhāt pariniṣpannasvabhāvabodho veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here again he shows the fivefold distinctive awakening: from the awakening to ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); from the awakening to knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>); and from the awakening to the threefold nature — imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and the rest. Therein, the counter-awakening to what has the nature of non-awakening — the awakening to the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s>) should be understood.

children.translated_text: Through the awakening to non-purpose, through the awakening to ultimate reality, through the awakening to all [purposes], through the awakening to totality,
and through the awakening to the basis of what is to be awakened and the awakener — by these reasons, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' || Msa_19.78 ||

body.text: atra pañcavidhaṃ bodhaviśeṣaṃ darśayati | paratantralakṣaṇabodhāt | pariniṣpannalakṣaṇabodhāt | [parikalpitalakṣaṇabodhāt?] sarvajñeyasarvākārabodhāt | bodhyabodhakabodhi[dha]trimaṇḍalapariśuddhibodhācca |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the fivefold distinctive awakening: from the awakening to the dependent characteristic (<s>paratantralakṣaṇa</s>); from the awakening to the perfected characteristic (<s>pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa</s>); from the awakening to all aspects of all that is to be known; and from the awakening to the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>) of what is to be awakened, the awakener, and awakening.

children.translated_text: Through the awakening to accomplishment, through the awakening to the stages, through the awakening to the womb-[descent], through the awakening to the display of stages,

children.text: bodhādbhṛśaṃ saṃśayahānibodhāt tenocyate hetuna bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_19.79 ||
children.translated_text: and through the awakening to the intense removal of doubt — by these reasons, one is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' || Msa_19.79 ||

body.text: tatra niṣpannabodho buddhatvaṃ | padabodho yena tuṣitabhavane vasati | garbhānubodho yena mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati | kramadarśane bodho yena garbhānniṣkramaṇaṃ kāmaparibhogaṃ pravrajyāṃ duṣkaracaryāmabhisaṃbodhiṃ ca darśayati | bhṛśaṃ saṃśayahānibodho yena sarvasaṃśayacchedāya sattvānāṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, the awakening to accomplishment is Buddhahood. The awakening to the stages is that by which one dwells in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven. The awakening to the womb is that by which one descends into the mother's womb. The awakening to the display of stages is that by which one shows the departure from the womb, the enjoyment of sense-pleasures, the going forth, the practice of austerities, and full awakening. The awakening to the intense removal of doubt is that by which one turns the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma) for the cutting of all doubts of beings.

children.translated_text: A gainer yet a non-gainer, established in wisdom, one who awakens and follows up on awakening, one who confesses,
one whose understanding is free from discourse, one whose pride is destroyed, and one whose understanding is [both] unripe and ripe — such is the wise one. || Msa_19.80 ||

body.text: atraikādaśavidhenātītādinā bodhena bodhisattvaḥ paridīpitaḥ | tatra lābhī alābhī dhīsaṃsthitaścātītānāgatapratyutpannairbodhairyathākramaṃ | boddhā svayaṃbodhāt | anuboddhā parato bodhādetenādhyātmikabāhyaṃ bodhaṃ darśayati | pratideśako nirjalpabuddhirityaudārikasūkṣmaṃ | mānī hatamānīti hīnapraṇītam | apakvasaṃpakvamatiśceti dūrāntikaṃ bodhaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: Herein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> has been illuminated through the elevenfold awakening beginning with the past and the rest. Therein, one who has gained, one who has not gained, and one established in wisdom — through past, future, and present awakening, respectively. One who awakens — from self-awakening. One who subsequently awakens — from awakening through another. By this, he shows internal and external awakening. One who confesses — one whose understanding is without verbal discourse: this shows the coarse and subtle. One who has pride, one whose pride is destroyed: the inferior and excellent. One whose understanding is unripened and fully ripened: this shows the distant and near awakening.

body.text: || mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāre guṇādhikāraḥ [ekonaviṃśatitamaḥ?] samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the chapter on qualities (<s>guṇādhikāra</s>) is completed ||

body.text: viṃśatitamaekaviṃśatitamaścādhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Twentieth and twenty-first chapters:

body.text: liṅgavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of marks (<s>liṅga</s>):

children.translated_text: Compassion, kind speech, steadfastness, open-handedness,
and the release of the profound intention — these are the marks of the wise. || Msa_20.1 ||
Regarding embrace, the attainment of conviction, unweariness, the twofold gathering,
and from disposition and application — the fivefold mark should be known. || Msa_20.2 ||

body.text: tatraprathamena ślokena pañca bodhisattvaliṅgāni darśayati | dvitīyena teṣāṃ karma samāsa saṃgrahaṃ ca | tatrānukampā bodhicittena sattvaparigrahārthaṃ priyākhyānaṃ sattvānāṃ buddhaśāsanādhimuktilābhārthaṃ dhīratā duṣkaracaryādibhirakhedārthaṃ muktahastatā gambhīrasaṃdhinirmokṣaṇaṃ ca dvayena saṃgrahārthamāmiṣeṇa dharmeṇa ca yathākramam | eṣāṃ pañcānāṃ liṅgānām anukampā āśayato veditavyā | śeṣāṇi prayogataḥ |
body.translated_text: By the first verse, he shows the five marks of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. By the second, their function and summary. Therein: compassion is for the embrace of beings through <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). Kind speech is for the purpose of beings' attaining conviction in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. Steadfastness is for the purpose of unweariness in difficult practice and the like. Open-handedness and the release of the profound intention are for the purpose of the twofold gathering — by material means and by Dharma, respectively. Among these five marks, compassion should be understood as pertaining to disposition; the remaining [four] as pertaining to application.

body.text: gṛhipravrajitapakṣavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Three verses on the division of the householder and renunciant sides:

children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, being <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs) at all times,

children.text: prakurvanti hi sattvārthaṃ gṛhiṇaḥ sarvajanmasu || Msa_20.3 ||
children.translated_text: as householders accomplish the welfare of beings in all births. || Msa_20.3 ||
Renunciation obtained through undertaking, another obtained through the nature of reality,

children.text: nidarśikā ca pravrajyā dhīmatāṃ sarvabhūmiṣu || Msa_20.4 ||
children.translated_text: and demonstrative renunciation — [these are the types] of the wise on all stages. || Msa_20.4 ||
The side of the renunciant, endowed with immeasurable qualities,
is superior to the householder <s>bodhisattva</s>; therefore, the ascetic is more excellent. || Msa_20.5 ||

body.text: ekena ślokena yādṛśe gṛhipakṣe sthito bodhisattvaḥ sattvārthaṃ karoti tatparidīpitaṃ | dvitīyena yādṛśe pravrajitapakṣe | tatra trividhā pravrajyā veditavyā | samādānalabdhā | dharmatālabdhā | nidarśikā ca nirmāṇaiḥ | tṛtīyena gṛhipakṣāt pravrajitapakṣasya viśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ |
body.translated_text: By one verse, it has been illuminated in what kind of householder status the <s>bodhisattva</s> accomplishes the welfare of beings. By the second, in what kind of renunciant status. Therein, renunciation is of three kinds: obtained through [formal] undertaking; obtained through the nature of reality; and demonstrative — through emanations. By the third [verse], the superiority of the renunciant side over the householder side has been illuminated.

body.text: adhyāśayavibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: A six-line verse on the division of superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>):

children.translated_text: The desire for the wished-for fruit in the next life, and for wholesome conduct here in this [life],
and the desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is accepted as the disposition toward beings for the steadfast;
impure, purified, and supremely purified — on all stages. || Msa_20.6 ||

body.text: etena samāsataḥ pañcavidho 'dhyāśayaḥ paridīpitaḥ | sukhādhyāśayaḥ | paratreṣṭaphalecchāhitādhyāśayaḥ ihaiva kuśalapravṛttīcchā nirvāṇecchā tadubhayādhyāśaya eveti nānyo veditavyaḥ | aśuddhādikāstrayo 'dhyāśayā apraviṣṭānāṃ | bhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ | avinivartanīyabhūmiprāptānāṃ ca yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, fivefold superior intention has been illuminated in summary: the intention toward happiness — the desire for wished-for fruit in the next life; the intention toward benefit — the desire for wholesome conduct here in this life; the desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the intention toward both, and should be understood as not another [separate type]. The three [types] beginning with impure should be understood as [pertaining to] those who have not entered [the stages], those who have entered the stages, and those who have attained the stage of non-regression, respectively.

body.text: parigrahavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of embrace (<s>parigraha</s>):

children.translated_text: Through aspiration, through an equal mind, through sovereignty, [there is] embrace;
and through the attracting of the assembly — for the wise on all stages. || Msa_20.7 ||

body.text: caturvidhaḥ sattvaparigraho bodhisattvānāṃ praṇidhānaparigraho veditavyo bodhicittena sarvasattvaparigrahaṇāt | samacittatāparigraha ātmaparasamatālābhādabhisamayakāle | ādhipatyaparigrahaḥ svāmibhūtasya yeṣāmasau svāmī | gaṇaparikarṣaṇaparigrahaśca śiṣyagaṇopādanāt |
body.translated_text: The embrace of beings by <s>bodhisattvas</s> is fourfold: the embrace through aspiration should be understood from the embrace of all beings through <s>bodhicitta</s>. The embrace through equal mind — from the attainment of equality of self and other at the time of realization. The embrace through sovereignty — of those of whom one has become the lord, as the lord of those [beings]. And the embrace through the attracting of the assembly — from the taking in of the assembly of disciples.

body.text: upapattivibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>):

children.translated_text: Through the sovereignty of action, and another through aspiration,
and through <s>samādhi</s>, and through sovereignty — rebirth of the wise is considered [fourfold]. || Msa_20.8 ||

body.text: caturvidhā bodhisattvānāmupapattiḥ karmādhipatyena yādhimukticaryābhūmisthitānāṃ karmavaśenābhipretasthānopapattiḥ praṇidhānavaśena yā bhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ sarvasattvaparipācanārthaṃ tiryagādihīnasthānopapattiḥ | samādhyādhipatyena yā dhyānāni vyāvartya kāmadhātāvupapattiḥ | vibhutvādhipatyena yā nirmāṇaistuṣitabhavanādyupapattisaṃdarśanāt |
body.translated_text: The rebirth of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is fourfold: through the sovereignty of action — that of those abiding on the stage of devoted conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), rebirth in desired places through the power of action. Through the power of aspiration — that of those who have entered the stages, rebirth in low places such as the animal realm for the purpose of ripening all beings. Through the sovereignty of <s>samādhi</s> — that rebirth in the desire realm by turning away from the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations). Through the sovereignty of sovereign power — that through the display of rebirth from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and the like by means of emanations.

body.text: vihārabhūmivibhāge triṃśat [udāna] ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thirty verses on the division of abodes (<s>vihāra</s>) and stages (<s>bhūmi</s>):

children.translated_text: From characteristics, from persons, from the training aggregates (<s>śikṣāskandha</s>), accomplishment, and marks,

children.text: nirukteḥ prāptitaścaiva vihāro bhūmireva ca || Msa_20.9 ||
children.translated_text: from etymology, and from attainment — [there is both] the abode and the stage. || Msa_20.9 ||

body.text: lakṣaṇavibhāgamārabhya pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses beginning with the division of characteristics:

children.translated_text: Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is the supreme self; establishment in the non-destruction of actions;

children.text: vihṛtya sasukhairdhyānairjanma kāme tataḥ param || Msa_20.10 ||
children.translated_text: having abided in the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) accompanied by happiness, birth in the desire realm — and beyond that; || Msa_20.10 ||
then, the dedication of the factors conducive to awakening to <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: vinā ca cittasaṃkleśaṃ sattvānāṃ paripācanā || Msa_20.11 ||
children.translated_text: and without the defilement of one's own mind, the ripening of beings; || Msa_20.11 ||
and in rebirth, having deliberately guarded the defilement,
the path conjoined with the one-way path, exclusively signless; || Msa_20.12 ||
even in the signless, effortlessness, and the purification of the field,

children.text: sattvapākasya niṣpattirjāyate ca tataḥ param || Msa_20.13 ||
children.translated_text: and the accomplishment of the ripening of beings arises thereafter; || Msa_20.13 ||
and the purification of <s>samādhis</s>, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, and awakening itself —
from this establishment, the characteristic of the stages should be known. || Msa_20.14 ||

body.text: ekādaśa vihārā ekādaśa bhūmayaḥ | tepāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ | prathamāyāṃ bhūmau paramaśūnyatābhisamayo lakṣaṇaṃ pudgaladharma nairātmyābhisamayāt | dvitīyāyāṃ karmaṇāmavipraṇāśavyavasthānaṃ kuśalākuśalakarmapathatatphalavaicitryajñānāt | tṛtīyāyāṃ sātiśayasukhairbodhisattvadhyānairvihṛtyāparihīnasyaiva tebhyaḥ kāmadhātāvupapattiḥ | caturthyā bodhipakṣabahulavihāriṇo 'pi bodhipakṣāṇāṃ saṃsāre pariṇāmanā | pañcabhyāṃ caturāryasatyabahulavihāritayāvinātmanaścittasaṃkleśena sattvānāṃ paripācanāyāṃ nānāśāstraśilpapraṇayanāt | ṣaṣṭhyāṃ pratītyasamutpādabahulavihāritayā saṃcityabhavopapattau tatra saṃkleśasyānurakṣaṇā | saptamyāṃ miśropamiśratvenaikāyanapathasyāṣṭamasya vihārasya śliṣṭa ānimittikaikāntiko mārgaḥ | aṣṭabhyāmanimitte 'pyanābhogo nirabhisaṃskārānimittavihāritvād buddhakṣetrapariśodhanā ca | navamyāṃ pratisaṃvidvaśitayā sattvaparipākaniṣpattiḥ sarvākāraparipācanasāmarthyāt | daśamyāṃ samādhimukhānāṃ dhāraṇīmukhānāṃ ca viśuddhatā | ekādaśyāṃ buddhabhūmau bodhiviśuddhatā lakṣaṇāṃ [ṇaṃ]sarvajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt |
body.translated_text: There are eleven abodes and eleven stages. Their characteristics: on the first stage, the realization of supreme emptiness is the characteristic — from the realization of the selflessness of person and phenomena. On the second, the establishment in the non-destruction of actions — from the knowledge of the variety of wholesome and unwholesome paths of action and their fruits. On the third, having abided in the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>dhyānas</s> accompanied by superior happiness, rebirth in the desire realm without decline from those. On the fourth, although abiding abundantly in the factors conducive to awakening, the dedication of those factors to <s>saṃsāra</s>. On the fifth, through abiding abundantly in the four noble truths, without the defilement of one's own mind, the ripening of beings — from the composition of various treatises and crafts. On the sixth, through abiding abundantly in dependent origination, deliberately in rebirth in [worldly] existence, therein the guarding of defilement [from arising]. On the seventh, the path exclusively signless, conjoined through mixed and unmixed [application] with the one-way path of the eighth abode. On the eighth, even in the signless, effortlessness — from abiding in the signless without deliberate conditioning — and the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. On the ninth, the accomplishment of the ripening of beings — through the mastery of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), from the capacity for ripening in all ways. On the tenth, the purification of the gateways of <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>. On the eleventh, the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, the purification of awakening is the characteristic — from the abandonment of all obscurations of the knowable.

body.text: bhūmiṣṭhe ca [ṣvevaṃ] pudgalavibhāgamārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses beginning with the division of persons established on the stages:

children.translated_text: One of purified vision, one of supremely purified moral conduct, one concentrated, one of distinguished Dharma-mind,
one [skilled] in the distinction of defilement and purification of the continuum, an emanator, one who has attained wisdom in a single moment; || Msa_20.15 ||
one who is equanimous, one who purifies [Buddha-]fields, one skilled in the ripening of beings, one of great supernatural power,

children.text: saṃpūrṇakāyaśca nidarśane ca śakto 'bhiṣiktaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ || Msa_20.16 ||
children.translated_text: one of complete body and capable of demonstration — and one who is consecrated: indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s>. || Msa_20.16 ||

body.text: daśasu bhūmiṣu daśa bodhisattvā vyavasthāpyante | prathamāyāṃ viśuddhadṛṣṭiḥ pudgaladharmadṛṣṭipratipakṣajñānalābhāt | dvitīyāyāṃ suviśuddhaśīlaḥ sūkṣmāpattiskhalitasamudācārasyāpyabhāvāt | tṛtīyāyāṃ samāhito bhavatyacyutadhyānasamādhilābhāt | caturthyāṃ dharmavibhūtamānaḥ sūtrādidharmanānātvamānasya vibhūtatvāt | pañcamyāṃ saṃtānabhede nirmāṇo daśabhiścittāśayaviśuddhisamatābhiḥ sarvasaṃtānasamatāpraveśāt | ṣaṣṭhyāṃ saṃkleśavyavadānabhede nirmāṇaḥ pratītyasamutpādatathatābahulavihāritayā kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣābhyāṃ tathatāyāḥ saṃkleśavyavadānādarśanāt | prakṛtiviśuddhitāmupādāya | saptamyāmekacittakṣalabdhabuddhirnirnimittavihārasāmarthyāt pratikṣaṇaṃ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣabhāvanātaḥ | aṣṭamyāmupekṣakaḥ kṣetraviśodhakaścānābhoganirnimittavihāritvād miśropamiśraprayogataścāvinivartanīyabhūmipraviṣṭairbodhisattvaiḥ | navamyāṃ sattvaparipākakuśalaḥ (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 171

children.text: ) pūrvavat | daśamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau bodhisattvo maharddhikaśca vyavasthāpyate mahābhijñālābhāt | saṃpūrṇadharmakāyaścāpramāṇasamādhidhāraṇīmukhasphuraṇādāśrayasya nidarśane ca śakto vyavasthāpyate tuṣitabhavanavāsādinirmāṇanidarśanāt | abhiṣiktaśca buddhatve sarvabuddhebhyastatrābhiṣekalābhāt |
children.translated_text: ) as before. On the tenth, on the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is established as one of great supernatural power — from the attainment of great <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). And one of complete <s>Dharmakāya</s> — from the manifestation of immeasurable gateways of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>. And one capable of demonstration through the basis — from the demonstration through emanations of dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and the like. And one who is consecrated into Buddhahood — from obtaining the consecration by all <s>Buddhas</s> therein.

body.translated_text: On the ten stages, ten <s>bodhisattvas</s> are established: on the first, one of purified vision — from obtaining the knowledge that is the antidote to the view of person and phenomena. On the second, one of supremely purified moral conduct — from the absence even of subtle offenses and faults in conduct. On the third, one who is concentrated — from obtaining non-declining <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>. On the fourth, one of distinguished Dharma-mind — because the diversity of mind regarding the dharmas of <s>sūtras</s> and the rest has become sovereign. On the fifth, an emanator in the distinction of the continuum — from entering the equality of all continua through the ten purities of mental intention. On the sixth, an emanator in the distinction of defilement and purification — through abiding abundantly in dependent origination and <s>tathatā</s>, from seeing defilement and purification of <s>tathatā</s> through the dark and bright sides — taking into account its natural purity. On the seventh, one who has attained wisdom in a single moment — from the capacity of signless abiding, through the cultivation of the thirty-seven factors of awakening at every moment. On the eighth, one who is equanimous and one who purifies [Buddha-]fields — from the effortless signless abiding, and from the mixed and unmixed application, [established] by <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the stage of non-regression. On the ninth, one skilled in the ripening of beings — (

body.text: śikṣāvyavasthānamārabhya pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Five verses beginning with the establishment of the trainings:

children.translated_text: Having penetrated the nature of reality herein, one trains in the higher moral conduct;
in the higher mind as well, and in the higher wisdom — but wisdom has a twofold domain. || Msa_20.17 ||
The reality of dharmas and the mode of operation beginning with ignorance and knowledge of that —
this is the domain of wisdom; therefore its establishment is on two stages. || Msa_20.18 ||
The fruit of the trainings and their cultivation is another, fourfold:
the signless conditioned abiding is the first fruit. || Msa_20.19 ||
That very [signless abiding] without conditioning is accepted as the second fruit;
purification of the field and the accomplishment of the ripening of beings. || Msa_20.20 ||
The accomplishment of <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīs</s> is the supreme fruit —
this fourfold fruit is based on the four stages. || Msa_20.21 ||

body.text: prathamāyāṃ bhūmau dharmatāṃ pratividhya dvitiyāyāmadhiśīlaṃ śikṣate | tṛtīyāyāmadhicittaṃ | caturthīpañcamīṣaṣṭhīṣvadhiprajñaṃ | bodhipakṣasaṃgṛhītā hi prajñā caturthyāṃ bhūmau | sā punardvayagocarā bhūmidvaye | dvayaṃ punardharmatattvaṃ ca duḥkhādisatyaṃ | tadajñānajñānādikā ca vṛttiranulomaḥ [pratilomaḥ?] pratītyasamutpādaḥ | tadajñānādikā hi vṛttiravidyādikā | tajjñānādikā ca vṛttirvidyādikā | tasmādbhūmidvaye 'pyadhiprajñavyavasthānaṃ | ataḥ paraṃ caturvidhaṃ śikṣāphalaṃ caturbhūmisamāśritaṃ veditavyaṃ yathākramaṃ | tatra[prathamaṃ phalam animittovihāraḥ sasaṃskāraḥ?] dvitīyaṃ phalaṃ sa evānimitto vihāro 'nabhisaṃskāraḥ kṣetrapariśuddhiśca veditavyaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: Having penetrated the nature of reality on the first stage, one trains in the higher moral conduct on the second. In the higher mind on the third. In the higher wisdom on the fourth, fifth, and sixth. For the wisdom comprised by the factors conducive to awakening is on the fourth stage. And that [wisdom] has a twofold domain, on two stages: the twofold [domain] is the reality of dharmas — the truth of suffering and the rest — and the mode of operation beginning with ignorance and knowledge of that — the forward and reverse dependent origination. For the mode beginning with ignorance is the forward [sequence beginning with] ignorance and the rest; and the mode beginning with knowledge of that is the reverse [sequence beginning with] knowledge and the rest. Therefore, the establishment of the higher wisdom is also on two stages. Beyond that, the fourfold fruit of the trainings should be understood as based on the four stages, in order: therein, [the first fruit is the signless conditioned abiding;] the second fruit is that very signless abiding without conditioning, and the purification of the field should be understood. The rest has its meaning already explained.

body.text: skandhavyavasthānamārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses beginning with the establishment of the [training] aggregates (<s>skandha</s>):

children.translated_text: Having penetrated the nature of reality herein, the purification of the aggregate of moral conduct;
and the purification of the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom — beyond that, upward; || Msa_20.22 ||
the purification of the [aggregate of] liberation and knowledge-and-vision of liberation — on the other [stages],
from the fourfold obscuration, from the obstruction of non-covering [too]. || Msa_20.23 ||

body.text: tadanyāsviti saptamyāṃ yāvad buddhabhūmāvubhayorvimuktivimuktijñānayorviśodhanā | sā punarvimuktiścaturvidhaphalāvaraṇācca veditavyā | pratighātāvaraṇācca buddhabhūmau | yenānyeṣāṃ jñeye jñānaṃ pratihanyate | buddhānāṃ tu tadvimokṣāt sarvatrāpratihataṃ jñānaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārtham |
body.translated_text: In the other [stages] — on the seventh stage up to the <s>Buddha</s>-stage — there is the purification of both liberation and the knowledge of liberation. That liberation, moreover, should be understood from the fourfold fruit-obscuration. And on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, [there is purification] from the obscuration of obstruction — by which the knowledge of others regarding the knowable is obstructed. But for the <s>Buddhas</s>, because of liberation from that, knowledge is unobstructed everywhere. The rest is self-evident.

body.text: niṣpattivyavasthānamārabhya trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Beginning with the determination of completion, three verses:

children.translated_text: All the stages should be known as both incomplete and complete;
even the complete are [again] incomplete, and [then] again complete. || Msa_20.24 ||
Completion should be understood through the mental attention of determination as it has been established;
from the knowledge that that [determination] is mere conceptualization, and through the non-conceptualization of that very [conceptualization]. || Msa_20.25 ||
Even the cultivation is the completion — [this is] inconceivable on all stages,
because it is to be individually experienced, and because it is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. || Msa_20.26 ||

body.text: tatrādhimukticaryābhūmiraniṣpannā | śeṣā niṣpannā ityetāḥ sarvabhūmayaḥ | niṣpannā api punaḥ saptāniṣpannāḥ | śeṣā niṣpannā nirabhisaṃskāravāhitvāt | yatpunaḥ pramuditādibhūmirniṣpannā pūrvamuktā tatra niṣpattiryathāvyavasthāpitabhūmimanasikāreṇa | tasya bhūmivyavasthānasya kalpanāmātrajñānāt tadavikalpanā[nayā] ca veditavyā | yadā tadbhūmivyavasthānaṃ kalpanāmātraṃ jānīte | tadapi ca kalpanāmātraṃ na vikalpayatyevaṃ grāhyagrāhakāvikalpajñānalābhādbhūmipariniṣpattiruktā bhavati | api khalu bhūmīnāṃ bhāvanā ca niṣpattiścobhayamacintyaṃ sarvabhūmiṣu | tathā hi tadbodhisattvānāṃ pratyātmavedanīyaṃ buddhānāṃ ca viṣayo nānyeṣām |
body.translated_text: Therein, the stage of the conduct of aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>) is incomplete. The remaining [stages] are complete — thus all these stages [are both]. Even the complete [stages], again, the [first] seven are incomplete. The remaining [stages] are complete, because of proceeding spontaneously without effort. Now, the completion of the stages beginning with <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) that was stated earlier — therein, the completion should be understood through the mental attention of the established stage-determination, from the knowledge that that stage-determination is mere conceptualization, and through the non-conceptualization of that [conceptualization]. When one knows that the stage-determination is mere conceptualization, and does not even conceptualize that mere conceptualization — thus, from the attainment of the knowledge of non-conceptualization free from grasped and grasper, the completion of the stage is said [to occur]. Moreover, both the cultivation and the completion of the stages are inconceivable on all stages. For indeed, that is to be individually experienced by the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, not of others.

body.text: bhūmipratiṣṭha[viṣṭa]sya liṅgavibhāgamārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Beginning with the division of the signs of one who has entered the stages, two verses:

children.translated_text: Faith everywhere, accompanied by light, is considered the sign;
non-depression, non-dejection, and non-dependence on others; || Msa_20.27 ||
and penetration everywhere, and equal-mindedness everywhere,
and knowledge of means beyond attraction and persuasion, and birth in an [assembly] circle. || Msa_20.28 ||

body.text: etadbhūmipraviṣṭasya bodhisattvasya daśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvāsu bhūmiṣu veditavyaṃ | yāṃ bhūmiṃ praviṣṭastatra sāloko yāṃ na praviṣṭastatrādhimuktirityetadekaṃ liṅgam | alīnatvaṃ paramodāragambhīreṣu dharmeṣu | adīnatvaṃ duṣkaracaryāsu | aparapratyayatvaṃ svasyāṃ bhūmau | sarvabhūmiprativedhaśca tadabhinirhārakauśalyataḥ sarvasattveṣvātmasamacittatā | aneyā varṇāvarṇaśabdābhyāṃ | ananunayaścakravartītyādisaṃpattiṣu | upāyakauśalyamanupalambhastasya[lambhasya] buddhatvopāyajñānāt | buddhaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu cotpattiḥ sarvakālamityetāni aparāṇi liṅgāni bodhisattvasya |
body.translated_text: These are the tenfold signs of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered the stages, to be understood on all stages. Regarding the stage one has entered, there is illumination; regarding the stage one has not entered, there is faith — this is one sign. Non-depression is regarding the supremely vast and profound <s>dharmas</s>. Non-dejection is regarding the practices that are difficult to perform. Non-dependence on others is regarding one's own stage. And the penetration of all stages — from skill in their accomplishment. Equal-mindedness toward all beings as toward oneself. Being beyond attraction by words of praise and blame. Being beyond persuasion by the attainments of a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) and the like. Skill in means is from the knowledge of the means to Buddhahood through non-apprehension. And birth in the assembly circles of the <s>Buddhas</s> at all times — these are the remaining signs of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: bhūmiṣu pāramitālābhaliṅgavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of the signs of the attainment of the <s>pāramitās</s> on the stages:

children.text: nācchando na ca lubdhahrasvahṛdayo na krodhano nālaso
children.translated_text: Not lacking in desire [for the Dharma], not greedy nor narrow-hearted, not wrathful, not lazy,
not lacking in the disposition of loving-kindness and compassion, not of poor understanding, worthy of conceptualization and non-conceptualization;

children.text: no vikṣiptamatiḥ sukhairna ca hato duḥkharna vā [vyā]vartate
children.translated_text: not of scattered mind, not defeated by pleasures, not turning away from suffering,

children.text: satyaṃ mitramupāśritaḥ śrutaparaḥ pūjāparaḥ śāstari || Msa_20.29 ||
children.translated_text: relying on a true friend, devoted to learning, devoted to honoring the Teacher; || Msa_20.29 ||
making all accumulations of merit vast and extraordinary,
one who day after day dedicates [them] toward awakening — for he knows the supreme means;
born in his own domain, always doing what is auspicious, he plays with the qualities of supernatural knowledge,
standing above all, a treasury of qualities — he should be known as the child of the <s>Buddhas</s>. || Msa_20.30 ||

body.text: daśapāramitālābhino bodhisattvasya ṣoḍaśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ darśayati | ṣoḍaśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ | sadā pāramitāpratipatticchandenāvirahitatvaṃ | ṣaṭpāramitāvipakṣaiśca rahitatvaṃ pratyekam | anyayānamanasikāreṇāvikṣiptatā | saṃpattisukheṣvasaktatā | vipattiduṣkaracaryāduḥkhaiḥ prayogānirvartitā | kalyāṇamitrāśrayaḥ | śrutaparatvaṃ | śāstṛpūjāparatvaṃ | samyakpariṇāmanā upāyakauśalyapāramitayā | svāyatanopapattiḥ praṇidhānapāramitayā buddhabodhisattvāvirahitasthānopapatteḥ | sadāśubhakaratve[tvaṃ]balapāramitayā tadvipakṣadharmāvyavakiraṇāt | abhijñāguṇavikrīḍanaṃ ca jñānapāramitayā | tatra maitrī vyāpādapratipakṣaḥ sukhopasaṃhārāśayaḥ | karuṇā vihiṃsāpratipakṣo duḥkhāpagamāśayaḥ | svabhāvakalpanaṃ kalpaḥ | viśeṣakalpanaṃ vikalpo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the sixteen signs of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained the ten <s>pāramitās</s>. The sixteen signs [are]: always being endowed with the desire for the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>; being free from the opposing factors of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, each respectively; non-distraction by the mental attention of other vehicles; non-attachment to the pleasures of prosperity; non-turning away from the effort of difficult practices due to their suffering; reliance on good friends; devotion to learning; devotion to honoring the Teacher; correct dedication through the <s>pāramitā</s> of skill in means; birth in one's own domain through the <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration — because of being born in a place not separated from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>; always doing what is auspicious through the <s>pāramitā</s> of power — because of not being mixed with the opposing <s>dharmas</s>; and playing with the qualities of supernatural knowledge through the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge. Therein, loving-kindness is the antidote to ill-will, with the disposition to bring happiness. Compassion is the antidote to harmfulness, with the disposition to remove suffering. Conceptualization of intrinsic nature is 'conceptualization.' Conceptualization of distinction is 'non-conceptualization' — this should be understood.

body.text: tatraivānuśaṃsavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of benefits therein:

children.translated_text: The benefit in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is considered twofold and fivefold
for the wise, in every way, on all stages. || Msa_20.31 ||

body.text: tatraiva pāramitālābhe sarvabhūmiṣu bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaprakāro 'nuśaṃsaḥ pañcavidho veditavyaḥ | pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvadauṣṭhulyāśrayaṃ drāvayati | nānātvasaṃjñāvigatiṃ ca dharmārāmaratiḥ pratilabhate | aparicchinnākāraṃ ca sarvato 'pramāṇaṃ dharmāvabhāsaṃ saṃjānīte | avikalpitāni cāsya viśuddhibhāgīyāni nimittāni samudācaranti | dharmakāyaparipūripariniṣpattaye ca uttarāduttarataraṃ hetusaṃparigrahaṃ karoti | tatra prathamadvitīyau śamathapakṣe veditavyau | tṛtīyacaturthau vipaśyanāpakṣe | śeṣamubhayapakṣe |
body.translated_text: Therein, in the attainment of the <s>pāramitās</s> on all stages, the benefit of <s>bodhisattvas</s> of every kind should be understood as fivefold: at every moment, one melts away the basis of all dysfunction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>); and one obtains the delight of the Dharma-garden, the going beyond the perception of diversity; and one perceives the illumination of the Dharma, unlimited in all its aspects, in all directions, with unlimited features; and the signs conducive to purification arise for one without conceptualization; and for the complete perfection of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma body), one increasingly embraces the causes. Therein, the first two should be understood as belonging to the side of <s>śamatha</s>. The third and fourth to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. The rest to both sides.

body.text: bhūminiruktivibhāge nava ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Nine verses on the division of the etymologies of the stages:

children.translated_text: For those who see awakening as near and the accomplishment of the welfare of beings,

children.text: tīvra utpadyate modo muditā tena kathyate || Msa_20.32 ||
children.translated_text: intense joy arises — therefore it is called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful). || Msa_20.32 ||

body.text: atra na kiṃcidvyākhyeyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Here, nothing needs to be explained.

body.text: dauḥ śīlyābhogavaimalyādvimalā bhūmirucyate |
body.translated_text: Due to the purity of being free from the inclination toward immorality, the stage is called <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless);

body.text: dauḥ śīlyamalasyānyayānamanasikāramalasya cātikramādvimaletyucyate | tasmāttarhyasmābhistulyābhinirhāre sarvākārapariśodhanābhinirhāra eva yogaḥ karaṇīya iti vacanāt |
body.translated_text: because of going beyond the stain of immorality and the stain of the mental attention of other vehicles, it is called Stainless. Therefore, [the verse says] that at this level of equal accomplishment, effort should be made precisely in the accomplishment of the purification of all aspects — as stated.

body.text: mahādharmāvabhāsasya karaṇācca prabhākarī || Msa_20.33 ||
body.translated_text: and because of producing the great illumination of the Dharma, [it is called] <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous). || Msa_20.33 ||

body.text: tathā hi tasyāṃ samādhibalenāpramāṇadharmaparyeṣaṇadhāraṇāt mahāntaṃ dharmāvabhāsaṃ pareṣāṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: For on that [stage], through the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), because of retaining the unlimited investigation of the Dharma, one produces great illumination of the Dharma for others.

children.translated_text: Since the <s>dharmas</s> that are the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) have become flames that burn,
it is the <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant) stage — from that connection, because of the burning of the twofold [obscuration]. || Msa_20.34 ||

body.text: sā hi bodhipakṣātmikā prajñā dvayadahanapratyupasthānā tasyāṃ bāhulyena | dvyaṃ punaḥ kleśāvaraṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇaṃ cātra veditavyam |
body.translated_text: For the wisdom that has the nature of the factors of awakening, which is present in abundance on that [stage], is ready for the burning of the twofold [obscuration]. The twofold [obscuration] should be understood here as the afflictive obscuration (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the cognitive obscuration (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: The ripening of beings and the guarding of one's own mind —

children.text: dhīmadbhirjīyate duḥkhaṃ durjayā tena kathyate || Msa_20.35 ||
children.translated_text: the wise overcome the difficulty [of both]; therefore it is called <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Hard to Conquer). || Msa_20.35 ||

body.text: tatra sattvaparipākābhiyukto 'pi na saṃkliśyate | sattvavipratipattyā taccobhayaṃ duṣkaratvād durjayam |
body.translated_text: Therein, even though devoted to the ripening of beings, one is not defiled. And the adversity of beings [makes] both [tasks] difficult — therefore [it is called] Hard to Conquer.

children.translated_text: Because of facing both — <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — here,
the stage is called <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing) — from the support of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). || Msa_20.36 ||

body.text: sā hi prajñāpāramitāśrayeṇa nirvāṇasaṃsārayorapratiṣṭhānāt saṃsāranirvāṇayorabhimukhī |
body.translated_text: For that [stage], through the support of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, because of non-abiding in either <s>nirvāṇa</s> or <s>saṃsāra</s>, faces both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: ekāyanapathaśleṣādbhūmirdūraṃgamā matā |
body.translated_text: The stage is considered <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Going) because of its connection with the one-way path;

body.text: ekāyanapathaḥ pūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭastadupaśliṣṭatvāt dūraṃ gatā bhavati prayogaparyantagamanāt |
body.translated_text: the one-way path was taught previously; because of being connected with that, it has gone far — because of going to the end of practice.

body.text: dvayasaṃjñāvicalanādacalā ca nirucyate || Msa_20.37 ||
body.translated_text: And because of being unshaken by the twofold perception, it is etymologized as <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). || Msa_20.37 ||

body.text: dvābhyāṃ saṃjñābhyāṃ avicalanāt | nimittasaṃjñayā[nimittābhogasaṃjñayā]animittābhogasaṃjñayā ca |
body.translated_text: Because of being unshaken by the two perceptions — the perception of signs with effort and the perception of signlessness with effort.

body.text: pratisaṃvinmatisādhutvādbhūmiḥ sādhumatī matā |
body.translated_text: The stage is considered <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence) because of the excellence of the intelligence of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>);

body.text: pratisaṃvinmateḥ sādhutvāditi pradhānatvāt |
body.translated_text: because of the excellence of the intelligence of the analytical knowledges — meaning because of its predominance.

body.text: dharmameghā dvayavyāpterdharmākāśasya meghavat || Msa_20.38 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma) — because of pervading the twofold [object], like a cloud [pervading] the sky of Dharma. || Msa_20.38 ||

body.text: dvayavyāpteriti samādhimukhadhāraṇīmukhavyāpanānmeghenevākāśasthalīyasyāśrayasaṃniviṣṭasya śrutadharmasya dharmameghetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Because of pervading the twofold [object] — meaning because of the spread of the doors of <s>samādhi</s> and the doors of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — like a cloud [pervading] a region of the sky, regarding the Dharma that has been heard and is established in the basis, it is called <s>Dharmameghā</s>.

children.translated_text: Because of always dwelling with delight in the manifold accomplishment of what is wholesome,
the stages of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> are considered to be dwelling-places everywhere. || Msa_20.39 ||

body.text: vividhakuśalābhinirhāranimittaṃ sadā sarvatra ratyā viharaṇādvodhisattvānāṃ bhūmayo vihārā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: Because of always dwelling everywhere with delight, on account of the manifold accomplishment of the wholesome, the stages of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> are called dwelling-places.

children.translated_text: Again and again, through the practice of ascending in the immeasurable [stages],

children.text: bhūtāmitābhayārthāya ta eveṣṭā hi bhūmayaḥ || Msa_20.40 ||
children.translated_text: those very [dwelling-places] are desired as stages — for the purpose of [removing] the fear of the truly immeasurable [beings]. || Msa_20.40 ||

body.text: bhūyo bhūyo 'mitāsvāsūrdhvaṃgamanayogādbhūtāmitābhayārthāya ta eva vihārāḥ punarbhūmaya ucyante | amitāsviti daśasu bhūmiṣu ekaikasyāpramāṇatvāt | ūrdhvaṃgamanayogāditi uparibhūmigamanayogāt | bhūtāmitābhayārthamityamitānāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhayaprahāṇārtham |
body.translated_text: Through the practice of ascending again and again in the immeasurable [stages], for the purpose of eliminating the fear of the truly immeasurable beings, those very dwelling-places are again called stages. 'Immeasurable' — because each of the ten stages is unlimited. 'Through the practice of ascending' — because of the practice of going to the higher stages. 'For the purpose of [removing] the fear of the truly immeasurable beings' — for the purpose of eliminating the fear of immeasurable beings.

body.text: prāptivihāre[vibhāge]ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of attainment:

children.translated_text: The attainment of the stages is fourfold — from the aspiration,
from the conducts, from the penetration, and from the completion [of the stages]. || Msa_20.41 ||

body.text: caturvidho bhūmīnāṃ lābhaḥ | adhimuktilābho yathoktādhimuktito 'dhimukticaryābhūmau | caritalābho daśasu dharmacariteṣu vartanāttasyāmeva | paramārtha [prativedha] lābhaḥ paramārthaprativedhato bhūmipraveśe | niṣpatilābhaścāvinivartanīyabhūmipraveśe |
body.translated_text: The attainment of the stages is fourfold: the attainment through aspiration — on the stage of the conduct of aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), from the aspiration as described. The attainment through conduct — on that very [stage], from engaging in the ten Dharma-conducts. The attainment through ultimate penetration — at the entry into the stages through the penetration of ultimate reality. And the attainment through completion — at the entry into the irreversible stage.

body.text: caryāvibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaṭpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: A six-footed verse on the division of conduct:

children.translated_text: For those who have faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and for embodied beings in the lesser vehicle,
for the purpose of attracting and disciplining both,
the four conducts of the steadfast ones are taught, following the <s>sūtras</s>. || Msa_20.42 ||

body.text: tatra pāramitācaryā mahāyānādhimuktānāmarthe deśitā | bodhipakṣacaryā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānādhimuktānām | abhijñācaryā dvayorapi mahāyānahīnayānādhimuktayoḥ prabhāveṇāvarjanārthaṃ | sattvaparipākacaryā dvayoreva paripācanārthaṃ | paripācanaṃ hyatra vinayanam |
body.translated_text: Therein, the conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s> is taught for the purpose of those who have faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The conduct of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) is for those who have faith in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. The conduct of supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>) is for attracting both — those with faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and those with faith in the lesser vehicle — through the power of [spiritual] accomplishment. The conduct of ripening beings is for the disciplining of both. For the disciplining here is the ripening.

body.text: buddhaguṇavibhāge bahavaḥ ślokāḥ | apramāṇavibhāge tad buddhastotramārabhyaikaḥ |
body.translated_text: Many verses on the division of the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. Beginning with the division of the immeasurables — that praise of the <s>Buddha</s> — one [verse]:

children.translated_text: O compassionate one toward beings, with the disposition toward the joining of [beings with happiness]
and the separation [from suffering], with the disposition toward happiness and benefit — homage to you! || Msa_20.43 ||

body.text: atra
body.translated_text: Here, compassion toward beings is shown through the disposition toward happiness and benefit. The disposition toward happiness is shown through the disposition toward the joining with happiness, by means of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>); through the disposition toward the separation from suffering, by means of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>); and through the disposition toward the non-separation from happiness, by means of sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>). The disposition toward benefit is through equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). And that should be understood as characterized by the disposition toward the state of non-defilement.

body.text: anukampakatvaṃ sattveṣu hitasukhāśayatvena saṃdarśitaṃ | sukhāśayatvaṃ punaḥ sukhasaṃyogāśayatvena maitryā | duḥkhaviyogāśayatvena ca karuṇayā | sukhāviyogāśayatvena ca muditayā | hitāśayatvamupekṣayā | sā punarniḥ saṃkleśatāśayalakṣaṇā veditavyā |
vimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanavibhāge ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Verses on the division of the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), masteries (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), and totalities (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>):

children.translated_text: O sage, freed from all obscurations, master over all worlds,

children.text: jñānena jñeyaṃ vyāptaṃ te muktacitta namo 'stute || Msa_20.44 ||
children.translated_text: your knowledge pervades the knowable — O one of liberated mind, homage to you! || Msa_20.44 ||

body.text: atra vimokṣaviśeṣaṃ bhagavataḥ sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇanirmuktatayā darśayati | abhibhvāyatanaviśeṣaṃ sarvalokābhibhutvena svacittavaśavartanādyatheṣṭālambananirmāṇapariṇāmanatādhiṣṭhānataḥ | kṛtsnāyatanaviśeṣaṃ sarvajñeyajñānāvyāghātataḥ [jñānavyāptaḥ] | ata eva vimokṣādiguṇavipakṣamuktatvāt muktacittaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, he shows the special quality of liberation of the <s>Bhagavān</s> through being freed from all afflictive and cognitive obscurations. The special quality of the masteries through mastering all worlds — from the governance of one's own mind at will, through the creation, transformation, and empowerment of objects as desired. The special quality of the totalities through the unobstructedness of knowledge regarding all knowables. For this very reason — because of being liberated from the opposing factors such as the qualities of liberation and the rest — he is one of liberated mind.

body.text: araṇāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict):

children.translated_text: O destroyer of all afflictions of all beings without exception,
O striker of afflictions, compassionate toward the afflicted — homage to you! || Msa_20.45 ||

body.text: atrāraṇāviśeṣaṃ bhagavataḥ sarvasattvakleśavinayanādutpāditakleśeṣvapi ca tatkleśapratipakṣavidhānāt kliṣṭajanānukampayā saṃdarśayati | anye hyaraṇāvihāriṇaḥ sattvānāṃ kasyacideva tadālambanasya kleśasyotpattipratyayamātraṃ pratiharanti | na tu kleśasaṃtānādapanayanti |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the distinction of <s>araṇā</s> of the Blessed One through subduing the afflictions of all beings, and even toward those in whom afflictions have been produced, through providing the antidote to those afflictions, out of compassion for afflicted persons. For other dwellers in <s>araṇā</s> merely remove the condition for the arising of a particular affliction directed toward beings as its object-support, but they do not remove it from the continuum of afflictions.

body.text: praṇidhijñānaviśeṣe[vibhāge]ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the distinction of <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge):

children.translated_text: Without deliberate effort, without attachment, without obstruction, concentrated,

children.text: sadaiva sarvapraśnānāṃ visarjaka namo 'stu te || Msa_20.46 ||
children.translated_text: forever the answerer of all questions — homage to you! || Msa_20.46 ||

body.text: atra pañcabhirākāraiḥ praṇidhijñānaviśeṣaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃdarśayati | anābhogasaṃmukhībhāvataḥ | asaktisaṃmukhībhāvataḥ | sarvajñeyāvyāghātataḥ | sadā samāhitatvataḥ | sarvasaṃśayacchedanataśca sattvānāṃ | anye hi praṇidhijñānalābhino nānābhogān [bhogenā] praṇidhāya praṇidhījñānaṃ saṃmukhīkurvanti | na cāsaktaṃ samāpattipraveśāpekṣatvāt | na cāvyāhataṃ pradeśajñānāt | na ca sadā samāhitā bhavanti na ca sarvasaṃśayāṃśchindanti |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the distinction of <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> of the Blessed One through five aspects: through the presence of effortlessness (<s>anābhoga</s>); through the presence of non-attachment; through non-obstruction with regard to all knowables; through being always concentrated; and through cutting all doubts of beings. For other attainers of <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> make <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> present by making various deliberate resolutions — not without attachment, because of depending on attainment-entry; not without obstruction, because of partial knowledge; they are not always concentrated; and they do not cut all doubts.

body.text: pratisaṃvidvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge):

children.text: āśraye 'thāśrite deśye vākye jñāne ca deśike |
children.translated_text: In the basis, the content based thereon, the expression, the knowledge, and the teaching —
with unobstructed intellect, ever the supreme teacher — homage to you! || Msa_20.47 ||

body.text: atra samāsato yacca deśyate yena ca deśyate tatra nityamavyāhatamatitvena bhagavataścatasraḥ pratisaṃvido deśitāḥ | tatra dvayaṃ deśyate āśrayaśca dharmaḥ | tadāśritaścārthaḥ | dvayena deśyate vācā jñānena ca | sudeśikatvena tāsāṃ karma saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: Here, in summary, with regard to what is taught and by what means it is taught, the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) of the Blessed One have been taught through his being of unobstructed intellect at all times. Therein, two pertain to what is taught: the basis, which is <s>dharma</s>, and the content based thereon, which is meaning. Two pertain to the means of teaching: speech and knowledge. Through being the supreme teacher, the function of those is shown.

body.text: abhijñāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge):

children.translated_text: Having approached with words, O knower of their conduct, in their comings and goings,

children.text: niḥ sāre caiva sattvānāṃ svavavāda namo 'stu te || Msa_20.48 ||
children.translated_text: and in the essencelessness of beings — O admonisher, homage to you! || Msa_20.48 ||

body.text: atra ṣaḍbhirabhijñābhiḥ samyagavavādatvaṃ bhagavato darśitam | upetya vineyasakāśamṛdhdyabhijñayā | teṣāṃ bhāṣayā divyaśrotrābhijñayā cittacaritraṃ jñātvā cetaḥparyāyābhijñayā yathā pūrvāntādihagatiryathā cāparānte gatiryathā ca saṃsārānniḥ saraṇaṃ | tatrāvavādaṃ dadātyavaśiṣṭābhistisṛbhirabhijñābhiryathākramam |
body.translated_text: Here, the Blessed One's being the perfect admonisher is shown through the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges): by approaching those to be disciplined through the <s>ṛddhi-abhijñā</s> (superknowledge of magical power); by [understanding] their language through the <s>divyaśrotra-abhijñā</s> (superknowledge of divine hearing); having known their mental conduct through the <s>cetaḥparyāya-abhijñā</s> (superknowledge of others' minds); how their destiny was from the past, how their destiny will be in the future, and how they will escape from <s>saṃsāra</s> — therein he gives admonition through the remaining three <s>abhijñās</s> in sequence.

body.text: lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s> (marks and minor signs):

children.translated_text: All embodied beings, seeing you, recognize supreme manhood;
O producer of faith from the mere sight — homage to you! || Msa_20.49 ||

body.text: atra lakṣaṇānuvyañjanānāṃ bhagavati mahāpuruṣatvasaṃpratyayena darśanamātrātpareṣāṃ prasādajanakatvaṃ karma saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: Here, the function of the <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (marks) and <s>anuvyañjanas</s> (minor signs) of the Blessed One is shown as generating faith in others from the mere sight, through the conviction of great-person-hood (<s>mahāpuruṣatva</s>).

body.text: pariśuddhivibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>pariśuddhi</s> (purification):

children.translated_text: In taking up, abiding, relinquishing, and transformation through emanation —
O attainer of mastery over <s>samādhi</s> and knowledge — homage to you! || Msa_20.50 ||

body.text: atra bhagavataścaturvidhayā vaśitayā sarvākāraścatasraḥ pariśuddhayaḥ paridīpitāḥ | āśrayapariśuddhirātmabhāvasyādānasthānatyāgavaśitayā | ālambanapariśuddhirnirmāṇapariṇāmanavaśitayā | cittapariśuddhiḥ sarvākārasamādhivaśitayā | prajñāpariśuddhiḥ sarvākārajñānavaśitayā |
body.translated_text: Here, through the fourfold mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) of the Blessed One, the four purifications of all aspects are illuminated. The purification of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is through mastery over taking up, abiding in, and relinquishing the personal existence. The purification of the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) is through mastery over emanation and transformation. The purification of mind is through mastery over <s>samādhi</s> of all aspects. The purification of wisdom is through mastery over knowledge of all aspects.

body.text: balavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>bala</s> (powers):

children.translated_text: In the means, in refuge, in purity, and in the escape of beings —

children.text: mahāyāne ca niryāṇe mārabhañja namo 'stu te || Msa_20.51 ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, O crusher of <s>Māra</s> — homage to you! || Msa_20.51 ||

body.text: atra caturṣvartheṣu sattvānāṃ vipravādanāya māro yastadbhañjakatvena bhagavato daśānāṃ balānāṃ karma saṃdarśitaṃ | yaduta sugatidurgatigamanādyupāyavipravādane | aśaraṇe devādiṣu śaraṇavipravādane | sāśravaśuddhimātreṇa śuddhivipravādane | mahāyānaniryāṇavipravādane ca | (

children.translated_text: MSA_Bagchi 178

children.text: ) sthānāsthānajñānabalena hi bhagavānprathame 'rthe mārabhañjako veditavyaḥ | karmavipākajñānabalena dvitīye | dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena tṛtīye | indriyaparāparatvādijñānabalena caturthe | hīnānīndriyādīni varjayitvā śreṣṭhasaṃniyojanāt |
children.translated_text: ) The Blessed One should be understood as the crusher of <s>Māra</s> in the first matter through the <s>bala</s> of knowing what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>); in the second through the <s>bala</s> of knowing the ripening of <s>karma</s>; in the third through the <s>bala</s> of knowing <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, <s>samādhi</s>, and attainments; and in the fourth through the <s>bala</s> of knowing the superiority and inferiority of faculties and so forth — by directing toward the supreme, having set aside inferior faculties and the rest.

body.translated_text: Here, the function of the ten <s>balas</s> (powers) of the Blessed One is shown through being the crusher of <s>Māra</s> who leads beings astray in four matters: in leading astray regarding the means of going to good and bad destinies and so forth; in leading astray regarding refuge in gods and others; in leading astray regarding purity by mere tainted purity; and in leading astray regarding the escape through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. (

body.text: vaiśāradyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness):

children.translated_text: O teacher of knowledge, abandonment, the path of escape, and obstacles —
invincible by other sectarians in one's own and others' welfare — homage to you! || Msa_20.52 ||

body.text: atra jñānaprahāṇakārakatvena svārthe | niryāṇavighnadeśikatvena ca parārthe | nirādhṛṣyatvādanyatīrthyairbhagavato yathākramaṃ caturvidhaṃ vaiśāradyamudbhāvitam |
body.translated_text: Here, the fourfold <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness) of the Blessed One has been revealed in sequence: in one's own welfare through being the accomplisher of knowledge and abandonment; in others' welfare through being the teacher of the path and obstacles to escape; and through invincibility by other sectarians.

body.text: ārakṣasmṛtyupasthānavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>ārakṣā</s> (guards) and <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness):

children.translated_text: Speaking with censure in the assemblies, free from the two defilements,

children.text: nirārakṣa asaṃmoṣa gaṇakarṣa namo 'stu te || Msa_20.53 ||
children.translated_text: without need for guarding, unforgetting, O attractor of assemblies — homage to you! || Msa_20.53 ||

body.text: anena trīṇyarakṣāṇi trīṇi ca smṛtyupasthānāni bhagavataḥ paridīpitāni teṣāṃ ca karma gaṇaparipakarṣakatvaṃ | tairhi yathākramaṃ vi[ni]gṛhyavaktā ca bhavati parṣatsu nirārakṣatvāt | dvyasaṃkleśavarjitaścānunayapratighābhāvādasaṃmoṣatayā sadābhūya sthitasmṛtitvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, the three guards and three foundations of mindfulness of the Blessed One are illuminated, and their function is the attraction of assemblies. For through those, in sequence, he speaks with censure in assemblies because of being without need for guarding; he is free from the two defilements due to the absence of attachment and aversion; and because of unforgetting through always abiding with established mindfulness.

body.text: vāsanāsamuddhātavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s> (eradication of latent impressions):

children.translated_text: In conduct and in abiding, everywhere, there is no action that is not omniscient —

children.text: sarvadā tava sarvajña bhūtārthika namo 'stu te || Msa_20.54 ||
children.translated_text: at all times, O omniscient one, O speaker of truth — homage to you! || Msa_20.54 ||

body.text: anena cāre vihāre vā sarvatra sarvadā vāsarvajñaceṣṭitasyābhāvāt bhagavataḥ sarvakleśavāsanāsasuddhātaḥ paridīpitaḥ | asarvajño hi kṣīṇakleśo 'pyasamuddhātitatvād vāsanāyā ekadā bhrāntena hastinā sārdhaṃ samāgacchati bhrāntena rathenetyevamādikamasarvajñaceṣṭitaṃ karoti | yathoktaṃ māṇḍavyasūtre | tacca bhagavato bhūtārthasarvajñatvaṃ[jñatvena]nāsti |
body.translated_text: By this, through the absence of any action that is not omniscient, everywhere in conduct and abiding, at all times, the eradication of all latent impressions of afflictions of the Blessed One is illuminated. For even one with destroyed afflictions who is not omniscient, because of not having eradicated the latent impressions, sometimes encounters a mad elephant or a runaway chariot and performs such non-omniscient actions. As stated in the <s>Māṇḍavya-sūtra</s>. And that truthful omniscience of the Blessed One is free from such [non-omniscient actions].

body.text: asaṃmoṣatāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>asaṃmoṣatā</s> (non-forgetfulness):

children.translated_text: In all the beneficial activities for all beings, you never miss the right time;
with never-fruitless action, constantly unforgetting — homage to you! || Msa_20.55 ||

body.text: anena yasya sattvasya yo 'rthaḥ karaṇīyo yasminkāle tatkālānativartanāt abandhyaṃ kṛtyaṃ sadā bhagavata ityasaṃmoṣadharmatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ karmataśca saṃdarśitam |
body.translated_text: By this, because the Blessed One never misses the right time for what benefit needs to be done for which being at which time, his action is never fruitless — thus the nature and function of being of the nature of non-forgetfulness is shown.

body.text: mahākaruṇāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion):

children.translated_text: You survey the entire world six times day and night

children.text: mahākaruṇayā yukta hitāśaya namo 'stu te || Msa_20.56 ||
children.translated_text: with great compassion, O one of benevolent intention — homage to you! || Msa_20.56 ||

body.text: atra mahākaruṇā bhagavataḥ karmataḥ svabhāvataśca paridīpitā | mahākaruṇayā hi bhagavān ṣaṭkṛtvo rātrindivena lokaṃ pratyavekṣate ko hīyate ko vardhate ityevamādi | tadyogācca bhagavān sarvasattveṣu nityaṃ hitāśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the great compassion of the Blessed One is illuminated through its function and nature. For through great compassion, the Blessed One surveys the world six times day and night — who is declining, who is progressing, and so forth. And through that connection, the Blessed One is forever of benevolent intention toward all beings.

body.text: āveṇikaguṇavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>āveṇikaguṇa</s> (unique qualities):

children.translated_text: In conduct, in attainment, in knowledge, and in action —
O supreme among all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — homage to you! || Msa_20.57 ||

body.text: atra cārasaṃgṛhītaiḥ ṣaḍbhirāveṇikairbuddhadharmaiḥ | adhigamasaṃgṛhītaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ | jñānasaṃgṛhītaistribhiḥ | karmasaṃgṛhītaiśca tribhiḥ | tadanyasattvottamānāmapi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmantikāduttamatvena sarvasattvottamatvaṃ bhagavataḥ paridīpitaṃ | tatra nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitaṃ | nāsti ravitaṃ | nāsti muṣitā smṛtiḥ | nāstyasamāhitaṃ cittaṃ | nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā | nāstyapratisaṃkhyāyopekṣeti cārasaṃgṛhītāḥ ṣaḍāveṇikā buddhadharmā ye buddhasyaiva saṃvidyante nānyeṣāṃ | nāsti chandaparihāṇirnāsti vīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāvimuktiparihāṇirityadhigamasaṃgṛhītāḥ ṣaṭ | atīte 'dhvani tathāgatasyāsaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānam | anāgate pratyutpanne 'dhvani tathāgatasyāsaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānamiti jñānasaṃgṛhītāstrayaḥ | sarvaṃ tathāgatasya kāyakarma jñānapūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti | sarvaṃ vākkarma sarvaṃ manaskarmeti karmasaṃgahītāstrayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the six unique <s>Buddhadharmas</s> comprised in conduct, the six comprised in attainment, the three comprised in knowledge, and the three comprised in action — the Blessed One's supremacy among all beings is illuminated through his surpassing even the highest among others, the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Therein, the six unique <s>Buddhadharmas</s> comprised in conduct, which exist only in the <s>Buddha</s> and not in others, are: the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling; no idle chatter; no lapse of mindfulness; no unconcentrated mind; no perception of diversity; and no equanimity without discernment. The six comprised in attainment are: no decline of aspiration, no decline of vigor, no decline of mindfulness, no decline of <s>samādhi</s>, no decline of wisdom, and no decline of liberation. The three comprised in knowledge are: the <s>Tathāgata's</s> unobstructed and unhindered knowledge of the past, future, and present. The three comprised in action are: all bodily action of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is preceded by knowledge and follows knowledge; all verbal action; and all mental action.

body.text: sarvākārajñatāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects):

children.translated_text: Having attained great awakening of all aspects through the three bodies,

children.text: sarvatra sarvasattvānāṃ kāṅkṣāchida namo 'stu te || Msa_20.58 ||
children.translated_text: O cutter of doubts of all beings everywhere — homage to you! || Msa_20.58 ||

body.text: anena tribhiśca kāyaiḥ sarvākārabodhyupagamatvāt sarvajñeyasarvākārajñānācca sarvākārajñatā bhagavataḥ paridīpitā | trayaḥ kāyāḥ svābhāvikaḥ sāṃbhogiko nairmāṇikaśca | sarvajñeyasarvākārajñānaṃ punaratra sarvasattvānāṃ devamanuṣyādīnāṃ sarvasaṃśayacchedena karmaṇā nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: By this, the <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) of the Blessed One is illuminated through attaining awakening of all aspects through the three bodies, and through knowledge of all aspects of all knowables. The three bodies are: the <s>svābhāvikakāya</s> (essential body), the <s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body), and the <s>nairmāṇikakāya</s> (emanation body). The knowledge of all aspects of all knowables is further indicated here through its function of cutting all doubts of all beings — gods, humans, and the rest.

body.text: pāramitāparipurivibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: A verse on the division of the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s>:

children.translated_text: Without grasping, without fault, without impurity, without fixation,

children.text: āniṅkṣya sarvadharmeṣu niṣprapañca namo 'stu te || Msa_20.59 ||
children.translated_text: immovable with regard to all dharmas, free from conceptual elaboration — homage to you! || Msa_20.59 ||

body.text: anena sakalaṣaṭpāramitāvipakṣanirmuktatayā ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrirbhagavata udbhāvitā | tatrānavagrahatvaṃ bhoganirāgrahatvādveditavyaṃ | nirdoṣatvaṃ nirmalakāyādikarmatvāt | niṣkāluṣyatvaṃ lokadharmaduḥkhābhyāṃ cittākaluṣīkaraṇāt | anavasthitatvamalpāvaraṇa[vara]mātrādhigamānavasthānāt | āniṅkṣyatvamavikṣepāt | niṣprapañcatvaṃ sarvavikalpaprapañcāsamudācārāt |
body.translated_text: By this, the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> of the Blessed One is revealed through being completely free from the adversaries of all six <s>pāramitās</s>. Therein, non-grasping should be understood from non-attachment to enjoyments. Faultlessness from the purity of bodily and other actions. Freedom from impurity from the non-defilement of the mind by worldly conditions and suffering. Non-fixation from not resting content with the mere attainment of limited freedom from obscurations. Immovability from non-distraction. Freedom from conceptual elaboration from the non-arising of all conceptual proliferations.

body.text: buddhalakṣaṇavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Two verses on the division of <s>buddhalakṣaṇa</s> (characteristics of a Buddha):

children.translated_text: You have accomplished the ultimate truth, have emerged from all stages,
have attained supremacy among all beings, and are the liberator of all beings. || Msa_20.60 ||
Endowed with inexhaustible and incomparable qualities, you are seen in the worlds,
yet unseen even in assemblies, in every way, by gods and humans. || Msa_20.61 ||

body.text: atra ṣaḍbhiḥ svabhāvahetuphalakarmayogavṛttyarthairbuddhalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ | tatra viśuddhā tathatā niṣpannaḥ paramārthaḥ | sa ca buddhānāṃ svabhāvaḥ | sarvabodhisattvabhūminiryātatvaṃ hetuḥ | sarvasattvāgratāṃ prāptatvaṃ phalaṃ | sarvasattvavimocakatvaṃ karma | akṣayāsamaguṇayuktatvaṃ yogaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the characteristic of a <s>Buddha</s> is illuminated through six aspects: nature, cause, result, action, connection, and mode of activity. Therein, purified <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — the accomplished ultimate truth — is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>. Having emerged from all <s>bodhisattva</s> stages is the cause. Having attained supremacy among all beings is the result. Being the liberator of all beings is the action. Being endowed with inexhaustible and incomparable qualities is the connection.

body.text: nānālokadhātuṣu dṛśyamānatā nirmāṇakāyena parṣanmaṇḍaleṣvapi dṛśyamānatā sāṃbhogikena kāyena | sarvathā | cādṛśyamānatā dharmakāyeneti trividhā prabhedavṛttiriti |
body.translated_text: Being seen in various world-realms through the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), being seen in assemblies through the <s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body), and being unseen in every way through the <s>dharmakāya</s> — this is the threefold differentiated mode of activity.

body.text:
|| mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāreṣu vyavadātasamayamahābodhisattvabhāṣite caryāpratiṣṭhādhikāro
nāmaikaviṃśatitamo 'dhikāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: || In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, spoken by the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the pure assembly, the twenty-first chapter called 'Establishment of Practice' (<s>Caryāpratiṣṭhādhikāra</s>) ||

body.text: || samāptaśca mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra iti ||
body.translated_text: || Thus the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> is completed ||
